description: THE TTIMS LRCC PROJECT PURPOSE IS TO SERVE AS THE COORDINATING, LABORATORY, AND ANALYTICAL CENTER FOR ANALYSES RELEVANT TO THE EVALUATION AND MONITORING OF HIV (INCIDENT AND PREVALENT), HCV (INCIDENT) AND HBV (INCIDENT) POSITIVE BLOOD DONORS. SPECIFICALLY THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THIS CONTRACT ARE TO: Â€¢ COORDINATE THE COLLECTION OF RISK FACTOR DATA BY THE PARTICIPATING BLOOD CENTERS WHERE DONORS WITH INFECTIONS DONATED Â€¢ INTEGRATE RISK FACTOR DATA AND DISEASE MARKER SURVEILLANCE INFORMATION ACROSS DIFFERENT BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS Â€¢ EVALUATE AND MONITOR RISK FACTOR CHARACTERISTICS OF DONORS AND DONATIONS CONFIRMED POSITIVE FOR TIIS Â€¢ COMPARE/ANALYZE RISK FACTOR DATA TO THOSE OBTAINED IN THE REDS-II TTI MARKER PREVALENCE AND RISK FACTOR STUDY Â€¢ PROVIDE LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT AND FOR THE COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE MEETINGS, CONFERENCES, AND DONATION(S) TRANSFER/SHIPMENT Â€¢ SERVE AS THE BIOSPECIMEN REPOSITORY FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT Â€¢ PERFORM RECENCY TESTING ON HIV PLASMA SAMPLES FROM DONORS WITH SEROPOSITIVE INFECTION TO ESTABLISH ESTIMATES OF TIME OF HIV ACQUISITION. Â€¢ CONDUCT VIRAL GENETIC SEQUENCE ANALYSES ON PLASMA SAMPLES FROM HIV (INCIDENT AND PREVALENT), HCV (INCIDENT) AND HBV (INCIDENT) POSITIVE BLOOD DONORS TO DETERMINE GENOTYPES AND DRUG RESISTANCE (WHERE APPLICABLE) OF DONOR INFECTIONS. IN SUPPORT OF THESE OBJECTIVES, THE AMERICAN RED CROSS (ARC) WILL RECRUIT, ENROLL AND INTERVIEW ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDE DATA AS REQUIRED IN THE TTIMS LRCC STATEMENT OF WORK, PROVIDE CODED BIO-SPECIMENS FOR RESEARCH TESTING AT BSRI, AND WILL ACTIVELY COLLABORATE IN THE ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, AND REPORTING OF FINDINGS IN TTIMS.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, DAVIS (UCD) WILL PROVIDE ELEMENTS OF THE ANNUAL MANAGEMENT PLAN PERTINENT TO THEIR ORGANIZATION. THEY WILL WORK WITH THE AHRQ QI MAINTENANCE TEAM TO ENSURE THE ACCURACY, INTEGRITY AND CLINICAL VALIDITY OF THE AHRQ QI TOOLS, AS WELL AS IMPLEMENT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES TO MONITOR AND EVALUATE THE QUALITY OF THE PRODUCTS THAT SHALL BE DELIVERED. A NUMBER OF INPUTS NEED TO BE SUPPORTED AND REGULARLY CULLED TO CONTINUALLY STAY CONTEMPORARY AND IMPROVE THE MEASURES. UCD WILL PARTICIPATE IN A PROCESS THAT BOTH MANAGES THESE INPUTS AND DRAWS UPON THEM TO FOSTER REFINEMENTS, AND LEAD IN THE EFFORTS TO REVIEW CHANGES IN ADMINISTRATIVE DATA ELEMENTS, CODING, GUIDELINES, AND ICD-10 UPDATES. ANNUALLY, UCD WILL REVIEW STANFORD UNIVERSITYÂ€™S SUMMARY OF THE LATEST MEASURE RELATED METHODS, INNOVATIONS, ISSUES AND SOLUTIONS FOUND IN PUBLISHED LITERATURE, ACADEMIC AND PROFESSIONAL MEETINGS. THEY WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN THE DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION AND INTERPRETATION OF TESTING METHODOLOGIES, AND LEAD THE EFFORTS TO EVALUATE AND IMPROVE THE IQI AND PSI MODULES. UCD WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT ON APPLYING AHRQ QI SPECIFICATIONS/SOFTWARE TO THE MEDICARE POPULATION, SPECIFICALLY THE PSI AND IQI MODULES. THEY WILL REVIEW NATIONAL QUALITY FORUM MEASURE SUBMISSION FORMS FOR UP TO 4 INDICATORS, PREPARED BY STANFORD UNIVERSITY, AND WILL ASSIST IN THE RESPONSE TO TECHNICAL COMMENTS IN THE REVIEW AND COMMENT PHASE AND AD HOC FOLLOW UP REQUESTS. UCD WILL CONVENE AND SUPPORT TECHNICAL WORKGROUPS TO COLLECT EXPERT FEEDBACK ON INDICATORS. THEY WILL DEVELOP SPECIAL ANALYTIC REPORTS AND WHITE PAPERS AND DELIVER TECHNICAL AND TRAINING PRESENTATIONS. THEY WILL ALSO PROTECT THE SECURITY AND CONFIDENTIALITY OF ALL DATA AND SUPPORT THE PROJECT CLOSE-OUT PROCESS.

description: THE FELLOWSHIP FOR INTERPRETATION OF GENOMES (FIG) IS A NONPROFIT [501(C)(3)] ORGANIZATION INCORPORATED IN ILLINOIS. FIG PERSONNEL, WHO HAVE PROVIDED THE USER SUPPORT FOR RAST, WILL CARRY THIS ROLE FORWARD INTO THE SUPPORT OF THE PATRIC 3 ANNOTATION ENGINE. FIG WILL LEAD THE CURATION EFFORT, TO INCLUDE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE GENE ANNOTATION, CURATION OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE GENE COLLECTIONS, AND CURATE UPDATED COLLECTIONS OF AMR RELATED GENES AND GENOMIC VARIATIONS IN THE MICROBIAL GENOMES SUPPORTED BY PATRIC. THE STRUCTURED COLLECTIONS WILL BE USED IN SEVERAL WAYS THAT WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE AMR ANALYSIS FOR PATRIC USERS. FIG WILL INTEGRATE DATA FROM A NUMBER OF COMMUNITY RESOURCES, PROJECT KNOWN DETERMINANTS TO CLOSELY-Â­‐RELATED GENOMES IN THE PATRIC COLLECTION, ENCODE A FRAMEWORK FOR COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF VARIATION USING SUBSYSTEMS, AND CONNECT OUR ENCODINGS TO LITERATURE DESCRIBING THE MECHANISM OF ACTION, WHEN AVAILABLE. BY PROJECTING AMR-Â­‐RELEVANCE TO GENES IN ALL NEWLY-Â­‐ ACQUIRED GENOMES, CREATING AMR-Â­‐RELATED SUBSYSTEMS, AND OFFERING TOOLS TO SUPPORT CLASSIFICATION OF GENOMES (AS RESISTANT OR SUSCEPTIBLE), FIG WILL BUILD A CONTINUALLY IMPROVED TOOLKIT FOR RESEARCH IN AMR. THESE TOOLS WILL BE USED TO DRIVE DETAILED AMR RELATED ANNOTATIONS IN THE PATRIC ANNOTATION SYSTEM. FIG PERSONAL WILL WORK ON ESTABLISHING CLOSER CONNECTIONS WITH THE NIAID FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS CENTERS -Â­‐ THE HARVARD UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF PUBLIC HEALTH -Â­‐ FUNCTIONALIZING LISTS OF UNKNOWN TB ENTITIES (FLUTE), THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO -Â­‐ CHICAGO CENTER FOR FUNCTIONAL ANNOTATION (CCFA) AND THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON -Â­‐ GENES UNKNOWN IN ACINETOBACTER BAUMANNII (GUNK).

description: 1. TO RAPIDLY INITIATE AND COMPLETE LABORATORY-BASED PHASE II TRIALS EVALUATING THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS MY MAXIMIZING THE PATIENT AND SCIENTIFIC RESOURCES AND CLINICAL RESEARCH EXPERTISE OF AN ESTABLISHED CONSORTIUM WITH DEMONSTRATED EXPERTISE IN EARLY THERAPEUTICS DEVELOPMENT 2. TO EMPLOY A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO COLLECTION, PROCESSING, AND STORAGE OF BLOOD, NORMAL AND TUMOR TISSUE, AND OTHER RELEVANT BIOLOGIC SAMPLES FOR MOLECULAR AND CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGIC STUDIES. 3. TO EVALUATE THE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS ON THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS BY INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL LABORATORY, PHARMACOKINETIC AND PHARMACODYNAMIC CORRELATIONS, INCLUDING EVALUATION OF SPECIAL PATIENT POPULATIONS, SUCH AS THOSE WITH IMPAIRED END-ORGAN FUNCTION, THE ELDERLY, AND RACIAL AND/OR ETHNIC GROUPS IN WHOM DIFFERENCES ARE ANTICIPATED. 4. TO IDENTIFY NEW PREDICTIVE MARKERS OF RESPONSE AND/OR SURVIVAL TO NOVEL THERAPEUTICS, INCLUDING CYTOSTATIC AGENTS, TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE STUDY DESIGNS AND STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES TO ASSESS SURROGATE MOLECULAR AND BIOLOGIC ENDPOINTS, AND TO CORRELATE FINDINGS WITH CLINICALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES IN ASSOCIATED CLINICAL TRIALS. 5. TO UTILIZE SPECIAL SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE WITHIN THE CALIFORNIA CANCER CONSORTIUM IN THE AREAS OF A) DNA METHYLATION, B) DNA REPAIR, C) SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION AND CELL CYCLE REGULATION, D) TUMOR ANGIOGENESIS, AND E) FUNCTIONAL IMAGING TO ASSESS DRUG-TARGET INTERACTIONS, TO ESTABLISH POTENTIAL SURROGATE STUDY ENDPOINTS, AND TO OPTIMIZE DESIGN OF LABORATORY-CLINICAL CORRELATIVE STUDIES.

description: WORK SCOPE FOR FOLLOW-UP OF DES-EXPOSED COHORTS 2015 Â€“ 2020 AT THE MAYO CLINIC MOTHERSÂ€™ COHORT DEATH CERTIFICATE SEARCHES WILL BE CONDUCTED FOR REMAINING COHORT MEMBERS NOT KNOWN TO BE DECEASED. THIS INCLUDES SURVEILLANCE OF VITAL STATUS DATA BASES AND ACCOMPANYING REGISTRATION AND PROGRAMMING. DEATH CERTIFICATES OF THOSE COHORT MEMBERS FOUND TO BE DECEASED WILL BE OBTAINED AND TRANSMITTED TO THE NATIONAL CANCER INSTITUTE OR ITS CONTRACTORS. DAUGHTERSÂ€™ AND SONSÂ€™ COHORT FOLLOW-UP INFORMATIONAL NEWSLETTERS WILL BE SENT TO CURRENT COHORT MEMBERS VIA UNITED STATES POSTAL SERVICE. ADDRESSES OF COHORT MEMBERS WILL BE UPDATED FOR THOSE WHOSE NEWSLETTERS ARE RETURNED. INITIAL QUESTIONNAIRES WILL BE MAILED TO REMAINING DAUGHTERSÂ€™ AND SONSÂ€™ COHORT MEMBERS. SECOND REQUESTS AND QUESTIONNAIRES WILL BE SENT TO THOSE COHORT MEMBERS WHO DID NOT RESPOND TO THE FIRST REQUEST FOR SURVEY COMPLETION. PHONE INTERVIEWS WILL BE ATTEMPTED FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS WHO DID NOT COMPLETE A QUESTIONNAIRE BY MAIL. PARTICIPANTS WHO CAN NOT BE LOCATED BY TELEPHONE WILL HAVE THEIR ADDRESSES TRACED FOR RELOCATION AND THEIR VITAL STATUS ASCERTAINED. MEDICAL RECORD VERIFICATION Â€“ REPORTS OF CANCER AS WELL AS BREAST CERVICAL, VULVAL, AND VAGINAL BIOPSIES AMONG DAUGHTERSÂ€™ COHORT MEMBERS WILL BE VERIFIED. REPORTED CANCER DIAGNOSIS AMONG SONSÂ€™ COHORT MEMBERS WILL ALSO BE VERIFIED. VERIFICATION ENTAILS OBTAINING FROM THE REPORTED DIAGNOSING PHYSICIAN, THE MEDICAL RECORDS AND PATHOLOGY REPORTS PERTAINING TO THE REPORTED DIAGNOSIS. THESE RECORDS WILL BE DE-IDENTIFIED AND TRANSMITTED TO THE CONTRACTOR FOR REVIEW AND TRANSMISSION TO NCI OR ITS CONTRACTOR. BIOSPECIMEN ACQUISITION Â€“ PATHOLOGY SLIDES, OR THEIR FACSIMILE, FOR WOMEN WHOSE MEDICAL RECORDS INDICATE A DIAGNOSIS OF GRADE II CERVICAL NEOPLASIA OR HIGHER WILL BE OBTAINED AND FORWARDED TO THE STUDY PATHOLOGIST FOR REVIEW. LIKEWISE, SLIDES, OR THEIR FACSIMILE, VERIFYING PROSTATE OR TESTICULAR CANCER AMONG SONSÂ€™ COHORT MEMBERS WILL BE OBTAINED AND SENT TO THE STUDY PATHOLOGIST. SLIDES OF MEMBERS OF BOTH COHORTS WHOSE RECORDS INDICATE A DIAGNOSIS OF CARCINOID TUMORS WILL ALSO BE SENT TO THE STUDY PATHOLOGIST. THIRD GENERATION COHORT (GRANDDAUGHTERS) QUESTIONNAIRES WILL BE MAILED TO THE CURRENT COHORT MEMBERS AND ANY NEWLY IDENTIFIED ELIGIBLE THIRD GENERATION COHORT MEMBERS. AS IN THE FOLLOW-UP OF THE DAUGHTERSÂ€™ AND SONSÂ€™ COHORT MEMBERS, SECOND QUESTIONNAIRES WILL BE SENT TO COHORT MEMBERS WHO DID NOT RESPOND TO THE INITIAL REQUEST FOR QUESTIONNAIRE COMPLETION. ATTEMPTS WILL BE MADE TO INTERVIEW BY PHONE ALL COHORT MEMBERS WHO DID NOT RETURN A QUESTIONNAIRE BY MAIL. ALSO, PARTICIPANTS WHO CAN NOT BE LOCATED BY TELEPHONE WILL HAVE THEIR ADDRESSES TRACED FOR RELOCATION AND THEIR VITAL STATUS ASCERTAINED. REPORTED CANCER OR CARCINOID DIAGNOSIS AND CERVICAL, VULVAL, OR VAGINAL BIOPSIES WILL, AS WELL, BE VERIFIED USING THE SAME PROCEDURES AS THOSE IN PLACE FOR THE DAUGHTERSÂ€™ COHORT PARTICIPANTS. PATHOLOGY SLIDES OR THEIR FACSIMILES WILL ALSO BE OBTAINED AND TRANSMITTED FOR THIRD GENERATION COHORT MEMBERS WHOSE MEDICAL RECORDS OR PATHOLOGY REPORTS INDICATE A DIAGNOSIS OF GRADE II CERVICAL, VULVAL, OR VAGINAL NEOPLASIA OR HIGHER. NEWSLETTER MAILING NEWSLETTERS UPDATING DAUGHTERSÂ€™, SONSÂ€™ AND THIRD GENERATION COHORT MEMBERS WILL BE SENT TWICE DURING THE UPCOMING FOLLOW-UP CYCLE ONCE IN YEAR 3 AND AGAIN IN YEAR 5 OF THE CONTACT. WE ANTICIPATE MAILING THESE NEWSLETTERS TO APPROXIMATELY 2,200 COHORT MEMBERS. THE MAYO CLINIC WILL PROVIDE ALL NECESSARY OVERSIGHT AND STAFFING REQUIRED TO COMPLETE THE AFOREMENTIONED WORK SCOPE REQUIREMENTS. description: ATTACHMENT A SCOPE OF WORK Â€¢ KEY PERSONNEL SUBCONTRACTOR WILL HAVE THE FOLLOWING INDIVIDUAL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING ROLE AS KEY PERSONNEL UNDER THIS AGREEMENT: HEN LEAD AS OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE, UNLESS SUBSTITUTION APPROVED BY CONTRACTOR Â€¢ TASKS - SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DO AS FOLLOWS: 1. PROJECT PLANNING: PARTICIPATE IN INTERNAL PLANNING CALLS AND MEETINGS TO ENSURE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES ARE WELL COORDINATED, EFFECTIVE AND CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVING. 2. HOSPITAL-LEVEL SUPPORT: COACHING FOR IMPROVEMENT AT THE HOSPITAL LEVEL THROUGH AWARENESS AND SHARING OF BEST PRACTICES; SITE VISITS WITH EXPRESS PREPARATION AND UNDERSTANDING OF CURRENT DATA REPORTING AND CULTURAL CHALLENGES; ANY SOLICITED AD HOC IMPROVEMENT NEEDS MUST BE MET. 3. DATA COLLECTION: SUPPORT HOSPITAL-LEVEL DATA COLLECTION THROUGH INTEGRATION INTO TOPIC AND ROLE BASED EDUCATION; PROMOTION OF CDS; ALIGNMENT WITH MEASURE REPORTING REQUIREMENTS; STRIVE TO CUSTOMIZE SUPPORT FOR HOSPITALS BASED ON RELEVANT NATIONAL, STATE AND HOSPITAL DATA REPORTING LEVELS. 4. CLINICAL EDUCATION SUPPORT: SUPPORT TOPIC AND ROLE GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO LEADING AND DEVELOPING EDUCATIONAL TRAININGS AT THE STATE LEVEL. ALIGN WITH AND PROVIDE ANY NEEDED CLINICAL SUPPORT TO THE PROGRAMMING, LED BY AHA/HRET PARTNERS IHI, CYNOSURE AND UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL, INCLUDING IDENTIFYING HOSPITAL SPEAKERS. SUPPORT OVERALL ALIGNMENT TO FOUR STRATEGIC IMPROVEMENT DRIVERS FOR HEN 2.0 REFERENCED IN BACKGROUND, AND REINFORCE THROUGH EDUCATION AND TRAINING. 5. ENGAGEMENT: SUPPORT HEN LISTSERVS THROUGH SHARING QUESTIONS AND CONTRIBUTING TO CLINICAL CONVERSATIONS WHICH MATCH STAFF EXPERTISE; PROMOTE AHA/HRET HEN WEBSITE CONTENT BY CONTRIBUTING PEER-SHARED RESOURCES AND RELEVANT EDUCATION MATERIALS TO BE A STRONG RESOURCE AND ENCOURAGE SUSTAINABILITY FOR HEN HOSPITALS. 6. CMS DELIVERABLE SUPPORT: PROVIDE NECESSARY DOCUMENTATION AND SUFFICIENT DETAIL TO SUPPORT THE AHA/HRET DELIVERABLES TO THE FUNDER, CMS. THIS INCLUDES MONTHLY, MIDYEAR AND ANNUAL REPORTS, AND ALSO ANY AD HOC REQUESTS FROM CMS. 7. FINANCIAL: PROVIDE DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED BY AHA/HRET STAFF TO DOCUMENTS ACTIVITIES ENGAGED IN BY STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATION (SHA) STAFF AND SUBMIT INVOICES TO AHA/HRET IN THE PROVIDED FORMAT. PROVIDE TIMELY TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT TO HOSPITAL AND SHA STAFF AND RETAIN NECESSARY DOCUMENTATION AND ATTEST QUARTERLY TO THE ACCURACY TO AHA/HRET. 8. COMPLIANCE: ENSURE THAT ALL ASPECTS OF COMPLIANCE RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ARE ADHERED TO INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE FLOWDOWN PROVISIONS.   Â€¢ DELIVERABLES Â€“ SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE THE FOLLOWING DELIVERABLES WITHIN THE FOLLOWING TIMEFRAMES: SERVICE DELIVERABLE DELIVERY DATE SERVICE 1: PROJECT PLANNING 1. SUPPORT THE AHA/HRET HEN NETWORK ALIGNMENT BY PARTICIPATION IN THE WEEKLY SHA CALL; ONE, ONE-HOUR CALL PER WEEK. BIWEEKLY THROUGHOUT THE 52 WEEKS OF THE PROJECT 2. PROVIDE STAFF AND LEADERSHIP TO PARTICIPATE IN EACH OF THE BIWEEKLY, ONE-HOUR SHA CHECK-IN CALLS WITH AHA/HRET HEN STATE LEAD. EACH WEEK OF 52 WEEK PROJECT 3. SUPPORT PROJECT PLANNING AND SUCCESS THROUGH ATTENDANCE AND PARTICIPATION BY AT LEAST ONE SHA LEAD IN THE THRICE-ANNUAL SHA CONVENINGS. THREE TIMES ANNUALLY THROUGHOUT PROJECT SERVICE 2: HOSPITAL-LEVEL SUPPORT 1. THROUGH RECRUITMENT EFFORTS, APPROACH AND ENGAGE ALL ACUTE, CRITICAL ACCESS AND CHILDRENÂ€™S HOSPITALS DEDICATED TO THE HEN PROJECT GOALS; COLLECT AND DOCUMENT TO HRET THE RECEIPT OF HOSPITAL COMMITMENT LETTER; ENSURE THE COMPLETION OF THE NEEDS ASSESSMENT. WITHIN ONE MONTH OF CONTRACT AWARD 2. CONDUCT INFORMED SITE VISITS WITH EACH COMMITTED HOSPITAL, AT LEAST ONCE; COMPLETE POST-SITE VISIT FORM FOR EACH VISIT. WITHIN THREE MONTHS OF CONTRACT AWARD SERVICE 3: DATA COLLECTION 1. ENSURE 80% OF ELIGIBLE HOSPITALS ARE REPORTING ON 15 OF THE 17 CMS-REQUIRED MEASURES, MONTHLY. MONTHLY FOR EACH OF THE 12 MONTHS OF THE PROJECT 2. SUPPORT MONTHLY HOSPITAL SUBMISSION OF DATA INTO CDS: EITHER BY COACHING AND FACILITATION OR THROUGH SHELL UPLOAD OF STATE DATA TO CDS. 3. SUPPORT SUBMISSION OF HOSPITAL-LEVEL OPERATIONAL METRIC DATA; ENSURE ACCURACY OF HOSPITAL MEASURE SELECTION FOR ALL REQUIRED MEASURES. SERVICE 4: CLINICAL EDUCATION SUPPORT 1. DEVELOP CLINICAL EDUCATION ACTIVITY ACTION ITEMS BASED ON RELEVANT NATIONAL, STATE AND HOSPITAL DATA REPORTING LEVELS; SUPPORT HOSPITAL-LEVEL DATA COLLECTION, PROMOTION OF CDS, ALIGNMENT WITH MEASURE REPORTING REQUIREMENTS ON CALLS, MEETINGS AND WEBINARS. MONTHLY FOR EACH OF THE 12 MONTHS OF THE PROJECT SERVICE 5: ENGAGEMENT 1. SUBMIT DOCUMENTATION ABOUT HOSPITAL-LEVEL CONTACT, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: IN-PERSON MEETINGS, SITE VISITS AND COACHING CALLS. MONTHLY SERVICE 6: CMS DELIVERABLE SUPPORT 1. ENSURE TIMELY AND SUFFICIENT INFORMATION IS SUBMITTED FOR EACH CMS MONTHLY REPORT THROUGH THE SURVEY TOOL. QUICKLY RESPOND TO ANY FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONS FROM AHA/HRET STAFF TO FACILITATE A QUALITY AND TIMELY SUBMISSION TO CMS. MONTHLY FOR EACH OF THE 12 MONTHS OF THE PROJECT 2. SUPPORT AHA/HRET IN THE SUBMISSION OF THE MIDYEAR REPORT TO CMS. COORDINATE WITH AHA/HRET HEN STATE LEAD TO COMPLETE A STATE-LEVEL MIDYEAR REPORT TO BE SUBMITTED TO CMS. MIDPERIOD OF THE PROJECT 3. SUPPORT AHA/HRET IN THE SUBMISSION OF THE FINAL REPORT TO CMS. COORDINATE WITH AHA/HRET HEN STATE LEAD TO COMPLETE A STATE-LEVEL FINAL REPORT TO BE SUBMITTED TO CMS. WITHIN 60 DAYS OF CONTRACT COMPLETION SERVICE 7: FINANCIAL 1. QUARTERLY ATTESTATION TO AHA/HRET THAT REIMBURSEMENTS HAVE BEEN PROCESSED TO STATE HOSPITALS AND SHA STAFF ACCORDING TO AHA/HRET AND GSA GUIDELINES. QUARTERLY THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT 2. SUBMIT TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT FORMS AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION WITHIN FIVE BUSINESS DAYS OF TRAVEL COMPLETION, AS NECESSARY. MONTHLY FOR EACH OF THE 12 MONTHS OF THE PROJECT OTHER: CONTRACTUAL OBLIGATIONS 1. PROVIDE WRITTEN CONFIRMATION TO AHA/HRET STAFF REGARDING THE RESOLUTION OF NON-CONFORMING DELIVERABLES. AS REQUESTED BY AHA/HRET STAFF

description: 1. TO RAPIDLY INITIATE AND COMPLETE LABORATORY-BASED PHASE II TRIALS EVALUATING THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS MY MAXIMIZING THE PATIENT AND SCIENTIFIC RESOURCES AND CLINICAL RESEARCH EXPERTISE OF AN ESTABLISHED CONSORTIUM WITH DEMONSTRATED EXPERTISE IN EARLY THERAPEUTICS DEVELOPMENT. 2. TO EMPLOY A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO COLLECTION, PROCESSING, AND STORAGE OF BLOOD, NORMAL AND TUMOR TISSUE, AND OTHER RELEVANT BIOLOGIC SAMPLES FOR MOLECULAR AND CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGIC STUDIES. 3. TO EVALUATE THE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS ON THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS BY INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL LABORATORY, PHARMACOKINETIC AND PHARMACODYNAMIC CORRELATIONS, INCLUDING EVALUATION OF SPECIAL PATIENT POPULATIONS, SUCH AS THOSE WITH IMPAIRED END-ORGAN FUNCTION, THE ELDERLY, AND RACIAL AND/OR ETHNIC GROUPS IN WHOM DIFFERENCES ARE ANTICIPATED. 4. TO IDENTIFY NEW PREDICTIVE MARKERS OF RESPONSE AND/OR SURVIVAL TO NOVEL THERAPEUTICS, INCLUDING CYTOSTATIC AGENTS, TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE STUDY DESIGNS AND STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES TO ASSESS SURROGATE MOLECULAR AND BIOLOGIC ENDPOINTS, AND TO CORRELATE FINDINGS WITH CLINICALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES IN ASSOCIATED CLINICAL TRIALS. 5. TO UTILIZE SPECIAL SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE WITHIN THE CALIFORNIA CANCER CONSORTIUM IN THE AREAS OF A) DNA METHYLATION, B) DNA REPAIR, C) SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION AND CELL CYCLE REGULATION, D) TUMOR ANGIOGENESIS, AND E) FUNCTIONAL IMAGING TO ASSESS DRUG-TARGET INTERACTIONS, TO ESTABLISH POTENTIAL SURROGATE STUDY ENDPOINTS, AND TO OPTIMIZE DESIGN OF LABORATORY-CLINICAL CORRELATIVE STUDIES.

description: TEAM IS POSITIONED TO EXECUTE AN AMBITIOUS PROJECT THAT WILL FUNDAMENTALLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF NONHUMAN PRIMATE (NHP) MAJOR HISTOCOMPATIBILITY COMPLEX (MHC) GENETICS AND IMPROVE THE UTILITY OF THESE IMPORTANT ANIMAL MODELS FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH (FIGURE SOW.1). THE TEAM MEMBERS ARE UNIQUELY QUALIFIED FOR THIS PROJECT; TOGETHER WE HAVE ALREADY DEVELOPED THE LEADING NHP MHC ALLELE DISCOVERY, GENOTYPING, NOMENCLATURE, AND ANNOTATION RESOURCES FOR THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. IN THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL DEFINE MHC CLASS I AND MHC CLASS II -DRB CDNA SEQUENCES FROM 715 ANIMALS: CYNOMOLGUS MACAQUES OF Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒCHINESEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ (120)- AND VIETNAMESE (120)-ORIGINS; PIG-TAILED MACAQUES (120); AND CHINESE (120)- AND INDIAN (120)-ORIGIN RHESUS MACAQUES, PLUS 115 ANIMALS OF NIAIDÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CHOOSING. THE ADVENT OF ROCHE/454 DNA PYROSEQUENCING ENABLES NOVEL MHC CLASS I AND CLASS II -DRB ALLELES TO BE DETERMINED AT THE SAME TIME AS ANIMALS ARE GENOTYPED FOR PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED ALLELES, ESSENTIALLY UNIFYING THESE TWO PREVIOUSLY DISPARATE GOALS INTO A SINGLE HIGH-RESOLUTION AND COST-EFFECTIVE ASSAY. THIS STATE-OF-THE-ART ASSAY IS AVAILABLE TODAY AND WILL BE IMPROVED DURING THE CONTRACT. MHC CLASS II -DPA, -DPB, -DQA, -DQB, AND -DRA ALLELES WILL BE SANGER SEQUENCED FROM 415 OF THE 715 MACAQUES. CDNA LIBRARIES FROM 15 OF THE 715 ANIMALS WILL BE CONSTRUCTED FROM HIGH-PRIORITY ANIMALS TO FACILITATE IDENTIFICATION OF NON-CODING REGIONS OF MHC GENES AND TO PROVIDE A RESOURCE FOR OTHERS INTERESTED IN CHARACTERIZING GENES WITHIN THE EXTENDED MHC. ALLELES WILL BE CHARACTERIZED USING CRITERIA ESTABLISHED FOR HLA NOMENCLATURE, WHICH WILL RESULT IN CHARACTERIZATION OF BOTH FULL-LENGTH AND PARTIAL TRANSCRIPTS USING TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE TODAY. WE STRONGLY BELIEVE, HOWEVER, THAT FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT ALLELE DISCOVERY IS PREFERABLE AND ATTAINABLE AND WILL AGGRESSIVELY DEVELOP TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL ENABLE HIGH-THROUGHPUT, FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT SEQUENCING DURING THE CONTRACT PROPOSAL. 300 MHC CLASS I AND 300 MHC CLASS II PLASMID CLONES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. ALL 715 MACAQUES WILL BE EXAMINED WITH DNA MICROSATELLITE MARKERS TO DEFINE HAPLOTYPES, WHILE AT LEAST 20 NEW MHC MICROSATELLITE MARKERS WILL BE DEFINED. SUCH MARKERS WILL ENABLE ANY MOLECULAR BIOLOGY LABORATORY TO MHC HAPLOTYPE NHPS WITHOUT REQUIRING THE SOPHISTICATED SEQUENCING AND INFORMATICS SKILLS NECESSARY FOR HIGH-THROUGHPUT DNA SEQUENCING. IN ADDITION, IMMORTALIZED B CELL LINES FROM 250 OF THE 715 ANIMALS WILL BE PRODUCED AND MADE AVAILABLE TO THE COMMUNITY TO SERVE AS CONTROLS FOR LABORATORIES INTERESTED IN DEVELOPING GENOTYPING AND HAPLOTYPING EXPERTISE. THE COMMUNITY WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THE PRODUCTION OF 50 STABLE TRANSFERENT CELL LINES EXPRESSING INDIVIDUAL MHC CLASS I OR COMBINATIONS OF MHC CLASS II A AND B ALLELES, AS WELL AS 15 MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES SPECIFIC FOR INDIVIDUAL MHC ALLELES. ALLELE DISCOVERY, MHC GENOTYPING, AND MHC HAPLOTYPING PROTOCOLS, ALONG WITH QUALITY CONTROL PRECAUTIONS, AND BIOLOGICAL REAGENTS WILL BE PUBLISHED TO AN MHC CONTRACT WEB PORTAL BUILT ON THE LABKEY SERVER PLATFORM AND HOSTED BY THE PI. THE SAME SERVER WILL ALSO HOUSE A SECURE, WEBENABLED RESULTS DATABASE THAT WILL BE ACCESSIBLE BY TEAM MEMBERS AND NIAID CONTRACT STAFF. CURATED DATA FROM THE INTERNAL SYSTEM WILL BE VALIDATED AND PUBLISHED TO IPD-MHC-NHP, DBMHC, AND NBCI GENBANK. IPD-MHC-NHP WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR DEFINING THE NOMENCLATURE OF NEWLY DISCOVERED SEQUENCES AND ASCERTAINING THEIR VALIDITY. THE TEAM MEMBERSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ LABORATORIES WILL ALSO HOST ANNUAL TRAINING ON DATA ACQUISITION AND ANALYSIS FOR INTERESTED INVESTIGATORS.

description: THE SCOPE OF WORK MODIFIED TO DECREASE FUNDING FOR THE PROJECT YEAR. THIS VIDEO IS INTENDED TO HELP CLINICIANS UNDERTSTAND METHODS FOR COMMUNICATION WITH PATIENTS AFTER ADVERSE EVENTS, INCLUDING TIMELY REPORT TO PATIENTS AND ATTENTION TO THE NEEDS OF CAREGIVERS INVOLVED WITH AN ADVERSE EVENT AMONG OTHER MLCR ELEMENTS. description: TASK 1: RECEIVE AND REVIEW MATERIALS ABOUT THE NPSD - TRUVEN HEALTH WILL HAVE NO HOURS ALLOCATED TO THIS TASK. TASK 2: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PREPARE TO RECEIVE EVENT-LEVEL DATA AND CONSULT WITH THE PPC ON VARIABILITY ANALYSIS FOR NON-IDENTIFIABLE EVENTS. IN COLLABORATION WITH STANFORD UNIVERSITY, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW, REVISE OR DEVELOP NEW TABLE LAYOUTS FOR AGGREGATED DATA, AND DESIGN ANALYTIC PLANS FOR EVENT LEVEL ANALYSES (ESTIMATED 500 TABLES). TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW DISSEMINATION STRATEGY, DRAFT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CHANGES TO THE AHRQ COMMON FORMATS BASED ON ANALYSES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PARTICIPATE IN ONE HOUR INTERNAL WEEKLY CALLS AND ADDITIONAL CALLS AS REQUIRED. TASK 3: ANALYZE DATA ON TRENDS IN PATIENT SAFETY EVENTS AND PATTERNS OF HEALTH CARE ERROR - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DESIGN ANALYTIC PLAN FOR TASK 3, DEVELOP 160 PROVIDER TABLES, DEVELOP GRAPHICS FOR TABLES, AND CREATE BULLET TEXT FOR 160 TABLES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DEVELOP TRENDS FROM EXISTING EXTERNAL PATIENT SAFETY DATA, SUCH AS THE HCUP DATABASES, OASIS, MDS, NSQUIP, OR QSRS. FOR THESE SOURCES, THEY WILL DEVELOP APPROXIMATELY 70 TABLES, WITH BULLETS. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DEVELOP MULTIVARIATE TRENDS ANALYSES AND CREATE BULLETED TEXT FOR TABLES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW TABLES, GRAPHICS AND BULLETS CREATED BY OTHER SUBCONTRACTOR(S). TASK 4: REPORT ON PATIENT SAFETY EVENTS IN THE NATIONAL HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND DISPARITIES REPORTS - FOR THIS TASK TRUVEN HEALTH WILL LEAD WORK EFFORTS, AS STATED ABOVE, INCLUDING ANALYSES, PRESENTING FINDINGS TO THE INTERAGENCY WORK GROUP AS REQUESTED, AND CONDUCT FURTHER DISSEMINATION AS AGREED UPON WITH STANFORD AND AHRQ. TASK 5: MONITOR EFFECTIVE STRATEGIES FOR REDUCING MEDICAL ERRORS AND INCREASING PATIENT SAFETY - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CONSULT ON THE WORK PLAN AND REVIEW WORK MATERIALS. TASK 6: DISSEMINATE FINDINGS FROM ANALYSES - FOR THIS TASK TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CREATE THE DISSEMINATION PLAN. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PROVIDE TWO INDIVIDUALS TO ATTEND THE PSO ANNUAL MEETING, AND CREATE 2 EDUCATIONAL BRIEFS. TASK 7: ADMINISTER TASK ORDER - THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DELIVER A MONTHLY PROGRESS REPORT TO THE STANFORD. OPTIONAL TASK 8: ASSESS FEASIBILITY OF THE CREATION OF AN INTERACTIVE EVIDENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT RESOURCE FOR NETWORK OF PATIENT SAFETY DATABASES - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL LEAD ALL WORK DESCRIBED ABOVE AND CREATE THE FINAL FEASIBILITY REPORT. OPTIONAL TASK 9: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS - OPTIONAL TASK 9A: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 500 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 500 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. OPTIONAL TASK 9B: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 750 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 750 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. OPTIONAL TASK 9C: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 1000 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 1000 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. FOR EACH OF THE OPTION 9A-9C, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CREATE 50% OF THE TABLES AND ASSOCIATED DOCUMENTATION.

description: THIS PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE CRC SCREENING RATES WITHIN THE GREAT PLAINS QIN REGION. WE WILL IMPLEMENT THE INTERVENTION THAT SUPPORTS THE PRIMARY DETERMINANT OF INDIVIDUALS HAVING A COLORECTAL CANCER SCREENING TEST Â€“ A PHYSICIAN RECOMMENDATION Â€“ AND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A SYSTEMATIC PROCESS THAT ENSURES RECOMMENDATION AND FOLLOW UP FOR ALL PATIENTS. IMPLEMENTATION OF THIS INTERVENTION WILL INCLUDE A THREE-PART STRATEGY CONSISTING OF: 1) A REGIONAL LEARNING AND ACTION NETWORK; 2) DIRECT TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO RECRUITED CLINICS; AND 3) COORDINATION OF PUBLIC EDUCATION AND AWARENESS. THE POPULATION SERVED BY THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE THE PATIENTS AT PRIMARY CARE CLINICS IN THE FOUR STATE REGION. WE EXPECT THE OUTCOMES OF THE PROJECT WILL BE PRIMARY CARE CLINICS WITH BETTER SYSTEMS IN PLACE TO IDENTIFY NEEDS AND MANAGE CRC SCREENING (AS DEMONSTRATED BY THE PROCESS MEASURES), ALONG WITH AN IMPROVEMENT IN SCREENING RATES (AS DEMONSTRATED BY THE OUTCOMES MEASURES) AND EXPECT TO REACH A LARGER AUDIENCE THAN OUR RECRUITED CLINICS THROUGH OUR LEARNING AND ACTION NETWORK.

description: "NOVA PROPOSED KEY PERSONNEL SUPPORT PROJECT MANAGER/CORPORATE MONITOR: DANA M. YOUNG, JD. MS. YOUNG WILL OVERSEE AND MANAGE CONTRACTING MATTERS, PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNICATIONS WITH NCI DCCPS, ASSIST DR. MILLIKEN AS NEEDED IN PRIORITIZING AND PROVIDING CORPORATE RESOURCES, ATTEND CANCER CENTER MEETING IN HOUSTON, TX IN NOVEMBER TO ASSIST IN DOCUMENTING DISCUSSIONS AND NETWORKING WITH KEY CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES, AND PROVIDE INPUT ON AND PERFORM QC REVIEW OF DRAFT AND FINAL REPORTS. SENIOR SCIENCE WRITER: ERIN MILLIKEN, PHD. DR. MILLIKEN WILL BE THE LEAD WRITER PREPARING THE SYNTHESIS REPORT. SHE WILL COMMUNICATE WITH NCI DCCPS AS NEEDED, REVIEW CANCER CENTER SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS, ATTEND CANCER CENTER MEETING IN HOUSTON, TX IN NOVEMBER, IDENTIFY KEY QUESTIONS/ISSUES REQUIRING FOLLOW-UP, CONDUCT NECESSARY FOLLOW-UP DISCUSSIONS WITH CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES AND/OR GATHER ADDITIONAL INFORMATION, PREPARE SYNTHESIS REPORT OUTLINE, PREPARE DRAFT AND FINAL SYNTHESIS REPORTS FOR DELIVERY TO NCI DCCPS. NOVA TECHNICAL SUPPORT COMMUNICATE WITH NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD AS NEEDED THROUGHOUT THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE. PREPARE A WORK PLAN/TIMELINE FOR TASK PERFORMANCE, TO BE APPROVED BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. SUBMIT MONTHLY REPORTS ON PROGRESS TO NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. UPON RECEIPT, REVIEW EACH OF THE 18 CANCER CENTERS SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS (APPROXIMATELY 20 PP EACH) AND IDENTIFY COMMON THEMES, ISSUES, AND OTHER VARIABLES OF INTEREST. IDENTIFY ANY QUESTIONS AND/OR GAPS IN INFORMATION REQUIRING FOLLOWUP. ATTEND MEETING ON NOVEMBER 5-6, 2015 IN HOUSTON, TEXAS WHERE THE 18 CANCER CENTERS AWARDED SUPPLEMENTS WILL REPORT OUT ON FINDINGS. TAKE NOTES AT THE MEETING FOR PURPOSES OF ASSISTING IN PREPARATION OF THE SYNTHESIS REPORT. IDENTIFY ANY ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS OR INFORMATION REQUIRED TO PREPARE A SUBSTANTIVE SYNTHESIS OF THE CANCER CENTER SUPPLEMENTS AND APPROPRIATE PERSONS TO FOLLOW UP WITH AT CANCER CENTERS. OBTAIN APPROVAL FROM NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD TO INITIATE CONTACT WITH APPROPRIATE PERSONS AT CANCER CENTERS. DOCUMENT DISCUSSIONS. USING INFORMATION GATHERED FROM REVIEW OF SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS, ATTENDANCE AT HOUSTON MEETING, AND DISCUSSIONS WITH CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES, PREPARE AN OUTLINE OF REPORT FOR APPROVAL BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. FOLLOWING APPROVAL OF SYNTHESIS REPORT OUTLINE BEGIN WRITING OF DRAFT REPORT. DELIVER DRAFT REPORT TO NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD ON OR ABOUT JANUARY 15, 2016. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL NEVER HAVE ACCESS TO THE DATABASE CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES COVER CORRECTIONS (I.E., CORRECTED DATASETS) OF SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, WHICH WILL BE SENT BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC, AND THE BCSC-SCC STAFF WILL REPLACE THE ERRONEOUS DATA ELEMENTS WITH THE CORRECT DATA. description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. A CRITICAL ELEMENT OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THE GENERATION OF LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST FLAVIVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS TARGETS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN THE CROWE LAB. THE MABS FOR RVFV THAT WILL BE MAPPED IN THIS CONTRACT ARE BEING ISOLATED AS PART OF ONGOING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION OF TED ROSS, PHD OF VGTI IN FLORIDA. THE DENV-4 HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF SUBJECTS IMMUNIZED WITH A LIVE-ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE THAT HAS BEEN USED SUCCESSFULLY IN HUMAN TRIALS IN COLLABORATION WITH A. DURBIN AND S. WHITEHEAD. THE JEV HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED A LIVE-ATTENUATED OR INACTIVATED JEV VACCINE IN COLLABORATION WITH S. THOMAS AND FROM CONVALESCENT PBMCS FROM SUBJECTS INFECTED WITH JEV IN THE FIELD IN COLLABORATION WITH C. SIMMONS. FOR THIS CONTRACT, THE CROWE LABORATORY WILL SUPPLY HIGHLY PURIFIED IGG PREPARATIONS OF HUMAN MABS WITH KNOWN FUNCTIONAL ACTIVITY. THE TEXT BELOW DESCRIBES A PLAN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE MABS. SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. FOR SOME OF THE VIRUSES TARGETED FOR HUMAN MAB PRODUCTION (JEV, RVFV), SOME OF THE SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS OF OTHERWISE HEALTHY DONORS WHO SUFFERED ACUTE AND CONFIRMED VIRAL INFECTION. THIS WILL BE COORDINATED BY DR. CROWE AND COLLABORATORS (RVFV: DR. MARIETJIE VENTER, UNIVERSITY OF PRETORIA; JEV: DR. CAMERON SIMMONS, OXFORD UNIVERSITY CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, VIETNAM). CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM SEVERAL IMMUNE DONORS WILL BE TRANSFERRED IN A COMPLETELY DE-IDENTIFIED FASHION TO THE VANDERBILT VACCINE CENTER IN THE U.S. FOR THESE STUDIES. IMMUNIZATION. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS. MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION. SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE. HUMANS: DR. CROWE WILL BE CREATING HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. THERE WILL BE NO IDENTIFIERS LINKED TO THE DATA BEING TRANSFERRED TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY. VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. IN ADDITION, BERYLLIUM SHALL USE OPTION QUANTITY PERIOD 3 RESOURCES TO SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER FUNCTIONAL STUDIES (FUN) ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE.

description: UNIV OF KENTUCKY WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE HIGHLY COLLABORATIVE FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN_12) ENTITLED, Â€ŒTHE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) ASSEMBLY-LINES Â€“ TOOLS FOR BIOSYNTHESIS/ BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS.Â€? THE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) ASSEMBLY-LINES Â€“ TOOLS FOR BIOSYNTHESIS/BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS. MANY OF THE NATURALLY DERIVED ANTIBIOTICS IN CURRENT USE ARE COMPLEX SECONDARY METABOLITES BIOSYNTHESIZED ON NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) Â€ŒASSEMBLY-LINESÂ€? BY BACTERIA. UNIV OF KY HAS SHOWN THAT THREE SMALL PROTEINS (MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS) IN THE NPRS SYSTEM WERE ESSENTIAL FOR THE ACTIVATION OF CONGOCIDINE, KUTZNERIDE, AND THIOCORALINE NRPS SYSTEMS, RESPECTIVELY, IN S. COELICOLOR. FURTHERMORE, UNIV KY RECENTLY FOUND THAT CO-EXPRESSION OF ONE OF THESE SMALL PROTEINS (TIOT) WITH HOMOLOGUES FROM OTHER NRPS SYSTEMS RESULTED IN A DRASTIC CHANGE IN THE BIOCHEMICAL FUNCTION OF THE COMPLEX. BY COMBINING A VARIETY OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH DIFFERENT OTHER NRPS PARTNERS, IT MAY BE POSSIBLE TO CREATE A TOOLBOX FOR THE BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL PHARMACEUTICALS. THE AIM OF THIS FUNCTIONAL STUDY IS TO USE MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS FROM M. TUBERCULOSIS AND PURIFIED BY THE SSGCID TO EXPAND THE NRPS TOOLBOX AND DETERMINE THE STRUCTURAL BASIS DRIVING THE FUNCTIONAL VARIABILITY. SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE PROJECT ARE AS FOLLOWS: SPECIFIC AIM 1: CONSTRUCT HETEROLOGOUS NRPS CO-EXPRESSION SYSTEMS: GENES FOR THE MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS FROM SSGCID AND CSGID RELEVANT BACTERIAL PATHOGENS WILL BE CO-EXPRESSED WITH THE S. ALBUS NRPS PROTEINS TIOK AND TION AND THE CO-EXPRESSED COMPLEXES ASSAYED FOR A WIDE RANGE OF NRPS ACTIVITIES. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY. SPECIFIC AIM 2: DETERMINE CRYSTAL STRUCTURE OF TIOK AND TION IN COMPLEX WITH VARIOUS MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS: PURIFIED CO-EXPRESSED COMPLEXES OF PROTEINS WILL BE SHIPPED BY GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA TO SSGCID FOR PLACEMENT INTO CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS AT BERYLLIUM. IF NECESSARY, ADDITIONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION WILL BE DONE BY DR. BUCHKO AT PNNL. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED BY BOTH THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AND SSGCID. SPECIFIC AIM 3: DETERMINE A CRYSTAL STRUCTURE FOR A MBTH-MBTB COMPLEX AND ASSAY ACTIVITY: MBTH WILL ALSO BE CO-EXPRESSED WITH THE M. TUBERCULOSIS PROTEIN (MBTB) HOMOLOGOUS TO TION WITH THE AIM OF OBTAINING A STRUCTURE OF THE PROTEIN-PROTEIN COMPLEX. CLONING, PROTEIN PURIFICATION, AND ASSAY WORK WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY. CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS AND STRUCTURE DETERMINATION WILL BE PERFORMED AT BERYLLIUM AND ANY ADDITIONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION NEEDED WILL BE DONE BY DR. BUCHKO AT PNNL. OUTCOMES: THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT, A TOOLBOX FOR THE BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL PHARMACEUTICALS, ALIGNS WITH NIAIDÂ€™S MISSION OF USING STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TO ASSIST THE STRUCTURE-BASED DESIGN OF NOVEL ANTIMICROBIAL AGENTS. THE ACTIVITY ASSAYS WITH MULTIPLE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS AND TIOK AND TION WILL EXPAND THE AVAILABLE BIOENGINEERING TOOLBOX AND THE COMPLEMENTARY CRYSTAL STRUCTURES OF THE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH TIOK AND TION WILL PROVIDE A STRUCTURAL BASIS TO EXPLAIN THE MOLECULAR REACTIONS THESE COMPLEXES PERFORM AND THE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN INFLUENCING THE BIOCHEMISTRY. NOT ONLY WILL THE STRUCTURES OF THESE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH TIOK AND TION ASSIST THE STRUCTURE BASED DESIGN OF NOVEL BIOSYNTHESIZED ANTIBIOTICS, THE CO-EXPRESSION PROTOCOL WITH MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS MAY BE THE ONLY METHOD OF DETERMINING A STRUCTURE FOR M. TUBERCULOSIS MBTB AND SOME OF THE OTHER PROTEINS IN THE M. TUBERCULOSIS NRPS ASSEMBLY-LINE THAT ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR PRODUCING SIDEROPHORES. THE STRUCTURES OF THESE LATER COMPLEXES WILL ASSIST THE STRUCTURE-BASED DESIGN OF ANTIBIOTICS BASED ON COMPOUNDS THAT PREVENT THE FORMATION OF THESE COMPLEXES AND THE CONSEQUENTIAL IRON-STARVATION OF M. TUBERCULOSIS FOLLOWING INFECTION.

description: UWNMR SHALL PERFORM NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS TO DETERMINE AT LEAST THREE (3) SOLUTION STRUCTURES FROM TARGETS APPROVED BY NIAID FOR ENTRY INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE, FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CENTER FOR INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. UW NMR SHALL LEAD FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN_11) ENTITLED, "FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF PFHMGB2 AND DEVELOPMENT AS A DRUG TARGET FOR THE TREATMENT OF CEREBRAL MALARIA." THE AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DISCOVER AND LATER DEVELOP A LEAD INHIBITOR COMPOUND AGAINST PFHMGB2 THAT IS EFFECTIVE IN REDUCING BRAIN SWELLING AND INCREASING THE SURVIVAL OF CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL MALARIA.

description: BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM DATA RESOURCE INDEPENDENTLY AND NOT AS AN AGENT OF THE BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM (BCSC) DATA RESOURCE STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER (BCSC-SCC), THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO FURNISH ALL THE NECESSARY SERVICES, QUALIFIED PERSONNEL, MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES , NOT OTHERWISE PROVIDED BY THE BCSC-SCC, AS NEEDED TO PERFORM THE STATEMENT OF WORK. SCOPE: THE MAJOR OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO ASSIST IN THE SHARING OF EXISTING DATA STORED WITHIN THE CURRENT BCSC POOLED DATABASE AND IMPROVE ITS CAPACITY TO SUPPORT USE OF THIS POOLED DATA BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DO THIS BY PROVIDING APPROVAL FOR DATA SHARING, AND BY RESPONDING TO QUERIES FROM THE BCSC-SCC DATA RESOURCE TO HELP THEM CLEAN THE POOLED DATA. IF THE SUBCONTRACTOR IS COVERED UNDER HIPAA, IT WILL MAINTAIN DATA USE AGREEMENTS (DUAS) TO ENSURE VALID DATA INTERPRETATION WITH THE BCSC-SCC. THE DUAS ARE REQUIRED IN THE EVENT THAT THE SUBCONTRACTOR NEEDS TO ACCESS ITS SITE-SPECIFIC DATA IN ORDER TO SEND A CORRECTED DATASET BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC DATA RESOURCE IN ORDER TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF THE POOLED DATABASE. THERE ARE THREE DATA SOURCES FOR THIS CONTRACT: 1} THE POOLED DATA; 2) THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA; 3) THE CORRECTED SITE-SPECIFIC DATA. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL NEVER HAVE ACCESS TO THE DATABASE CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES COVER CORRECTIONS (I.E., CORRECTED DATASETS) OF SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, WHICH WILL BE SENT BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC, AND THE BCSC-SCC STAFF WILL REPLACE THE ERRONEOUS DATA ELEMENTS WITH THE CORRECT DATA. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: PROJECT AREA 1. PARTICIPATION IN MAINTAINING DATA QUALITY OF THE BCSC POOLED DATABASE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN IMPROVING THE DATA QUALITY OF THE BCSC- POOLED DATABASE THROUGH THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. ACCESSING SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO SUPPLY CORRECTIONS TO THE BCSC-SCC POOLED DATASET, AS NEEDED. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER COLLECTION OF ADDITIONAL SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES COVER SUBMISSION OF CORRECTED SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO THE BCSC-SCC. THE SUBCONTRACTOR ONLY WILL ACCESS SITE-SPECIFIC DATA THAT IS ALREADY IN THEIR POSSESSION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL NEVER ACCESS THE DATABASE CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA. B. ENSURE THAT PROPER ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS ARE IN PLACE WHICH MAY INCLUDE, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, IRB APPROVALS, HIPAA CERTIFICAT IONS, AND CERTIFICATIONS FOR RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. RECORDS OF THESE APPROVALS, CERTIFICATIONS, AND OR TRAININGS SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE BCSC-SCC UPON REQUEST. SUBCONTRACTORS WILL COOPERATE WITH THE CONTRACTOR IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERTIFICATES OF CONFIDENTIALITY , WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA ASSIST THE BCSC-SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO: CORRECTING DATA ELEMENTS THAT ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, CONTAIN IMPOSSIBLE VALUES, OR ARE MISSING. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SUBCONTRACTORS MAY NOT BE ABLE TO PROVIDE CORRECTIONS FOR APPARENTLY ERRONEOUS DATA, BUT THAT THEY WILL, TO THE BEST OF THEIR ABILITY, ATTEMPT TO DETERMINE NECESSARY MODIFICATIONS. PROJECT AREA 2. BCSC STEERING COMMITTEE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE WORK WITH THE BCSC STEERING COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF BCSC INVESTIGATORS THE BCSC-SCC, AND THE NCI COTR IN THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR 1.5 HOUR MONTHLY CONFERENCE CALLS FOR STEERING COMMITTEE MEMBERS AND PROVIDE MEETING MATERIALS AS REQUESTED BY THE BCSC-SCC FOR DOCUMENTATION OF THE POOLED DATA AT OR BEFORE THE MEETING. B. PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS REGARDING POOLED DATA REQUESTS, PROPOSED ANALYSES, SITE SPECIFIC DATA ISSUES AND MEETINGS, ON THE CONFERENCE CALLS. PROJECT AREA 3. CO

description: INDEPENDENTLY AND NOT AS AN AGENT OF THE CONTRACT BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM (BCSC) STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER (C-BCSC SCC), THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO FURNISH ALL THE NECESSARY SERVICES, QUALIFIED PERSONNEL, MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES, NOT OTHERWISE PROVIDED BY THE CONTRACT BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER AS NEEDED TO PERFORM THE STATEMENT OF WORK. SCOPE: THE MAJOR OBJECTIVE OF A SUBCONTRACT TO THE C-BCSC SCC DATA RESOURCE IS TO ASSIST IN THE SHARING OF DATA STORED WITHIN THE CURRENT BCSC DATABASE AND IMPROVE ITS CAPACITY TO SUPPORT USE OF THE DATA BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. TO ENSURE VALID DATA INTERPRETATION THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL MAINTAIN DATA USE AGREEMENTS WITH THE C-BCSC SCC TO AID IN CLARIFYING SITE SPECIFIC DATA IN THE POOLED DATABASE. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: PROJECT AREA 1. PARTICIPATION IN BCSC POOLED DATABASE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN THE SCSC POOLED DATABASE THROUGH THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. PROVIDE ACCESS TO THE EXISTING SITE-SPECIFIC DATA. B. ENSURE THAT PROPER ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS ARE IN PLACE WHICH MAY INCLUDE, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, IRS APPROVALS, CERTIFICATES OF CONFIDENTIALITY, HIPAA CERTIFICATIONS, AND CERTIFICATIONS FOR RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. RECORDS OF THESE APPROVALS, CERTIFICATIONS, AND OR TRAININGS SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE C-SCSC SCC UPON REQUEST. C. WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE DATA, ASSIST THE C-SCSC SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO: CORRECTING DATA ELEMENTS THAT ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, CONTAIN IMPOSSIBLE VALUES, OR ARE MISSING. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SUBCONTRACTORS MAY NOT BE ABLE TO COLLECT NEW DATA FROM THEIR RADIOLOGY FACILITIES TO ADDRESS PROBLEMS THAT MAY EXIST IN A VARIABLE, BUT THAT THEY WILL PURSUE THE BEST AVAILABLE REMEDY. PROJECT AREA 2. SCSC STEERING COMMITTEE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE WORK WITH THE SCSC STEERING COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF SCSC INVESTIGATORS THE C-BCSC SCC, AND THE NCI COTR IN THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR 1.5 HOUR MONTHLY CONFERENCE CALLS FOR STEERING COMMITTEE MEMBERS AND PROVIDE MEETING MATERIALS AS REQUESTED BY THE C-SCSC SCC FOR DOCUMENTATION OF THE DATA AT OR BEFORE THE MEETING. B. PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS REGARDING DATA REQUESTS, PROPOSED ANALYSES, DATA ISSUES AND MEETINGS, ON THE CONFERENCE CALLS. PROJECT AREA 3. COLLABORATION WITH THE STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER A. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE C-8CSC SCC TO ENSURE THAT EXTERNAL INVESTIGATORS ARE AWARE OF THIS RESEARCH RESOURCE AND ITS POTENTIAL TO AID THEM IN THEIR RESEARCH. B. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL COMPLY WITH THE REQUIREMENTS FOR TRANSITION-IN AND TRANSITION-OUT OF THE C-8CSC SCC. SUBCONTRACTORS SHALL PARTICIPATE IN TRANSITION-IN REQUIREMENTS BY PARTICIPATING IN THE C-BCSC SCC'S EVALUATION OF DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURES. PROJECT AREA 4. SECURITY AND PRIVACY THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST THE C-BCSC SCC'S IN MEETING THE SYSTEM SECURITY PROCEDURES TO ENSURE DETAILED PHYSICAL AND DATA SECURITY OF THE POOLED BCSC DATABASE AND PRIVATE WEBSITE, AS WELL AS TO ENSURE CONFIDENTIALITY OF PERSONAL INFORMATION OF LIMITED DATA SETS, INCLUDING LIMITS ON CELL SIZES IN ANALYSES. description: THE GOALS OF THE ATR PROGRAM CENTER ON THE PROVISION OF SUBSTANCE ABUSE CLINICAL AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES TO THOSE IN NEED. THIS GRANT PROGRAM IS DESIGNED TO BE A SYSTEMS- CHANGE INITIATIVE THROUGH THE INTRODUCTION OF A VOUCHER-BASED SYSTEM OF PAYMENT INTO THE CLINICAL TREATMENT DELIVERY SYSTEM, ENCOURAGING INDIVIDUAL CHOICE BY EMPOWERING THE INDIVIDUAL TO CHOOSE HIS/HER PROVIDER OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS CLINICAL TREATMENT AND/OR RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. THROUGH THIS CONTRACT, TA WILL BE PROVIDED TO STATE/T~IBES TO IMPLEMENT A LARGE-SCALE VOUCHERS SYSTEM THAT SUPPORTS THE CONTINUUM OF RECOVERY FROM SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS CONTRACT WILL SUPPORT PEER PROVIDERS WHO RECEIVE FEDERAL FUNDING TO BOTH PROVIDE PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES THROUGH RECOVERY CENTERS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, ETC. AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY-BUILDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STATEWIDE NETWORK OF RECOVERY COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE TO PROMOTE THE INVOLVEMENT OF INDIVIDUALS IN RECOVERY FROM ADDICTION, AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS AS PARTNERS IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND OTHER ALLIED HEALTH SYSTEMS. SUBCONTRACTOR HAS BEEN HIRED TO ASSIST THE GRANTEES WITH UNDERSTANDING AND IMPLEMENTING EMPOWERMENT EVALUATION INTO THEIR ATR PROGRAMS. THE TASKS ARE DESIGNED TO ENCOURAGE THE GRANTEES TO IDENTIFY THE IMPORTANCE OF EVALUATION FOR THEIR PROGRAMS AND HOW BY INCLUDING THEIR COALITIONS AND CLIENTS IN THE PROCESS, THE ATR PROJECT CAN BE ENHANCED. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE MOTIVATING THE ATR GRANTEES TO SEE HOW EVALUATION CAN ASSIST THEM WITH SUSTAINING THEIR PROJECTS. TASK 1: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP CONTENT FOR A TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (TA) PACKAGE FOR GRANTEES ON HOW TO UTILIZE EMPOWERMENT EVALUATION WITHIN THEIR ATR PROGRAMS AND/OR WITH THEIR PROVIDERS IN THEIR ATR PROGRAMS. TASK 2: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP CONTENT AND PRESENT THREE MINI WEBINARS/Â€?COFFEE BREAKSÂ€?. THE FIRST WEBINAR TITLED, Â€ŒEMPOWERMENT EVALUATION: A TOOL FOR PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITYÂ€? IS TAKING PLACE AUGUST 13, 2015. THE PURPOSE OF THIS WEBINAR IS TO HIGHLIGHT THE PURPOSE OF EMPOWERMENT EVALUATION, AS WELL AS THE PRINCIPLES AND CONCEPTS GUIDING THE APPROACH. IN ADDITION, SPECIFIC STEPS USED TO FACILITATE THE PROCESS WILL BE DISCUSSED. IMPLICATIONS FOR PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY WILL ALSO BE HIGHLIGHTED. TASK 3: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL INITIATE PLANNING FOR TWO TAÂ€™S FOR WASHINGTON ATR PROGRAM.

description: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL UNDERTAKE THE FOLLOWING TASKS IN COMPLETING THIS WORK: PROVIDE OVERALL LEADERSHIP AND ADMINISTRATIVE OVERSIGHT FOR THE PROPOSED PROJECT, INVOLVING CO-INVESTIGATORS RABIN AND DAVIES. PROVIDE EXPERT INPUT ON A LITERATURE REVIEW AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN AIMED AT DEVELOPING AN INVENTORY OF EXISTING CPMS FOR BOTH USE-CASES, AS WELL AS A SET OF PRELIMINARY CRITERIA FOR JUDGING THE QUALITY AND CLINICAL APPLICABILITY OF CPMS. THIS WORK WILL BE LED BY DR. RABIN, BUILDING ON PRIOR WORK BY HER TEAM AND OTHERS (EPROGNOSIS.ORG RESEARCH GROUP, CPM DEVELOPERS) TO PRODUCE CLINICAL TOOLS AIMED AT MAKING CPMS ACCESSIBLE TO CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL FOCUS ON CPMS FOR PROSTATE CANCER AND HEAD AND NECK CANCER TREATMENT OUTCOMES. OTHER CANDIDATE CPMS FOR BOTH USE CASES WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH FURTHER LITERATURE REVIEW. LEAD DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE MODEL OF USE FOR INCORPORATING CPMS RELEVANT TO TREATMENT DECISIONS FOR PROSTATE CANCER, AND REFINE THIS MODEL BASED ON ITERATIVE FEEDBACK OF EXPERT ADVISORY PANEL (EAP) MEMBERS, CONSISTING OF PRACTICING CLINICIANS (UROLOGISTS, MEDICAL ONCOLOGISTS), CANCER SURVIVORS WITH FOCUSED CONTENT EXPERTISE AND EXPERIENCE IN PROSTATE CANCER, AND CPM DEVELOPERS. THE MODEL OF USE WILL 1) IDENTIFY EXISTING CPMS OF SUFFICIENT QUALITY AND RELEVANCE TO THE TREATMENT DECISION, 2) CLARIFY THE VALUE AND LIMITATIONS OF EACH CPM, AND 3) SPECIFY THE APPROPRIATE MANNER AND SEQUENCE OF USE OF EACH CPM IN THE PATIENT COUNSELING AND DECISION-MAKING PROCESS. THE TEAMS WILL USE LOGIC MODELS AND STORYBOARDING TO DEPICT THE INFORMATION NEEDS OF CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS WHO ARE ENGAGING IN DECISION MAKING, AND TO REFINE THE PROTOTYPE MODELS OF USE. PROVIDE EXPERT INPUT ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE WEB-BASED CLINICAL META-TOOL THAT OPERATIONALIZES THE USE OF PROGNOSTIC MODELS IN CANCER CARE DECISIONS. THE META-TOOL PROTOTYPE WILL UTILIZE INTERACTIVITY AND INNOVATIVE VISUALIZATION TECHNIQUES TO ENHANCE THE UNDERSTANDABILITY AND USABILITY OF INFORMATION, AS WELL AS LANGUAGE SCRIPTS FOR EXPLAINING THE VALUE AND LIMITATIONS OF PROGNOSTIC ESTIMATES. THE TOOL WILL INCORPORATE EXPLANATORY LANGUAGE AND SCRIPTS DEVELOPED WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF EAP MEMBERS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT BE INVOLVED IN WRITING ANY SPECIFIC FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES THAT MIGHT DEVELOP FROM THIS WORK. HOWEVER, THE OUTPUT OF THIS CONTRACT IS EXPECTED TO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF POTENTIAL FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES IN THIS AREA, AND WILL BE USED. FOR EXAMPLE, PRESENTATIONS TO SENIOR NCI LEADERSHIP AND TO OTHER INTERESTED RESEARCHERS, TO CONTINUE THE DEVELOPMENT OF THIS AREA AS A RESEARCH PROGRAM FOR NCI.

description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO 1) APPLY HIGH THROUGHPUT GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES ON THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED WOMEN'S HEALTH INITIATIVE BIO RESOURCE AND TO 2) INTEGRATE THE DATA GENERATED WITH EXISTING CLINICAL, GENETIC, AND BIOMARKER DATA IN ORDER TO CONFIDENTLY IDENTIFY NOVEL DETERMINANTS OF CORONARY HEART DISEASE AND RELATED PHENOTYPES IN AGING POST-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN" WE PROPOSE TO CAREFULLY PROFILE THE DNA AND PLASMA OF CHD CASES AS WELL AS AN APPROPRIATE SET OF CONTROLS USING TWO COMPLEMENTARY BUT WELL-VALIDATED GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES AT BASELINE .. THESE GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES ARE EXPECTED TO GENERATE HIGH QUALITY AND HIGH-RESOLUTION GENOME WIDE DNA METHYLATION PROFILE AS WELL AS A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF CIRCULATING MICRORNA LEVELS. WE WILL THEN COMPREHENSIVELY ANALYZE AND INTEGRATE THIS GENOMIC DATA WITH EXISTING CLINICAL, GENETIC, AND BIOMARKER DATA USING STATE OF THE ART STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES DEVELOPED BY MEMBERS OF THE INVESTIGATIVE TEAM TO IDENTIFY GENOMIC SIGNATURES AND PATHWAYS RELEVANT TO CHD AND ITS RISK FACTORS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ALLOW US AND OTHERS 1) TO IDENTIFY GENOMIC BIOMARKERS OF CHD EVENTS, 2) TO INTEGRATE THESE BIOMARKERS INTO DIAGNOSTIC AND PROGNOSTIC PREDICTORS OF CHD AND RELATED PHENOTYPES, 3) TO ELUCIDATE THE BIOLOGY OF CHD AND RELATED PHENOTYPES, 4) TO TEST WHETHER AGING RELATED CPGS FOUND IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES MEDIATE THE RISK OF AGE ON CHD, AND 5) TO REVISIT THE GWAS STUDIES OF CHD BASED ON MOLECULARLY REFINED PHENOTYPES AND SNP SET ANALYSIS INFORMED BY OUR NEW GENOMIC DATA. THESE OBJECTIVES ARE ACHIEVABLE IN THE CONTEXT OF OUR PRIOR EXPERIENCE PRODUCING AND ANALYZING SIMILAR DATA IN OTHER SAMPLES SETS AS EXTENSIVELY DESCRIBED IN THE "TECHNICAL PLAN" SECTION OF THIS PROPOSAL. THESE OBJECTIVES ARE ALSO ACHIEVABLE IN THE CONTEXT OF THE NUMEROUS UNIQUE STATISTICAL TOOLS WE HAVE DEVELOPED SPECIFICALLY FOR INTEGRATING GENOMIC DATA GENERATED FROM VARIOUS SOURCES.

description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: ATTACHMENT A: SCOPE OF WORK & BUDGET BACKGROUND: AHRQ AS PART OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES HAL NATIONAL ACTION PLAN (NAP) HAS SUPPORTED THE IMPLEMENTATION AND ADOPTION OF THE COMPREHENSIVE UNIT-BASED SAFETY PROGRAM (CUSP) IN REDUCING CENTRAL LINE-ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTIONS (CLABSI) AND CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CAUTI). IN SEPTEMBER 2012, AHRQ SOUGHT TO APPLY THE PRINCIPLES AND CONCEPTS THAT HAVE BEEN LEARNED FROM THESE TWO HAL REDUCTION EFFORTS TO SURGICAL SITE INFECTIONS (SSI) AND OTHER SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS FOLLOWING WITHIN AMBULATORY SURGERY SETTINGS THROUGH EFFECTIVE NATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION OF A PROVEN SURGICAL SAFETY CHECKLIST AND DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AHRQ SAFETY PROGRAM FOR AMBULATORY SURGERY. THIS PROGRAM CAN BE APPLIED TO REDUCE SSI, OTHER HAIS, AND OTHER SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS IN AMBULATORY SURGERY CENTERS IN ALL STATES, THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, AND PUERTO RICO THROUGH STATE-BASED OR REGIONAL CONSORTIA/COLLABORATIVE IN A PHASED APPROACH. THE TOTAL FUNDING FOR SUBCONTRACTORÂ€™S EFFORT WITHIN THE AHRQ SAFETY PROGRAM FOR AMBULATORY SURGERY EXTENDED FACULTY NETWORK IN THE PERFORMANCE PERIOD IS ($34,921.05 U.S. DOLLARS). SUBCONTRACTOR IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR ANY COSTS FOR COMPLETION OF THE FOLLOWING TASKS AND DELIVERABLES IN EXCESS OF THIS AMOUNT. PERFORMANCE PERIOD MARCH 2,2015 Â€“ SEPTEMBER 29, 2015 ($34,921.05) OPTION YEAR THREE (TBD) (TBD) THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE THE FOLLOWING THROUGHOUT THIS CONTRACT PERIOD: DEVELOP AND FACILITATE THE CONTENT/RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY THROUGH PARTICIPATION IN THE FOLLOWING NATIONAL PROGRAM EVENTS: I. EDUCATIONAL SESSIONS, WORKSHOPS AND/OR TRAININGS II. MILESTONE MEETINGS AND SUPPLEMENTAL PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION EVENTS III. COACHING OPPORTUNITIES IV. NATIONAL PROGRAM OFFICE HOURS WE PROPOSE EDUCATIONAL CONTENT WITH A FOCUS ON IMPROVING PATIENT SAFETY AND QUALITY OF CARE IN THE AMBULATORY SURGERY CENTER SETTING. THESE TOPICS FOR THESE PROGRAMS COULD INCLUDE: SLEEP APNEA, PREVENTION OF FALLS, PREVENTION OF VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM (VTE), EMERGENCY DRILLS, SURGICAL AND PROCEDURAL SAFETY CHECKLISTS, ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS AND ANTIBIOTIC STEWARDSHIP, MALIGNANT HYPERTHERMIA, UPDATE ON 2015 AAAHC STANDARDS. description: DRS. MARK GLADWIN AND TAMIR KANIAS WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE STUDY DESIGN, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, HUMAN SUBJECT RESEARCH COMPLIANCE, PERFORM RATE OF HEMOLYSIS ASSAYS AND DATA ANALYSIS, SHIP REPOSITORY SAMPLES TO BLOOD SYSTEMS RESEARCH INSTITUTE (BSRI) AND REPORT RESULTS TO BSRI AND RESEARCH TRIANGLE INTERNATIONAL (RTI). TRAINING/MOP DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL PROVIDE TRAINING TO BSRI STAFF IN PERFORMING THE SELECTED HIGH-THROUGHPUT ASSAYS MEASURING UP TO 4 FORMS OF STRESS: OXIDANT-INDUCED STRESS, SHEAR OR MECHANICAL STRESS, OSMOTIC STRESS AND STORAGE HEMOLYSIS. DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL SHARE ALL PROTOCOLS RELATED TO ASSAYS AND INFORMATION REQUIRED TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE MANUAL OF PROCEDURES FOR THE STUDY WITH BSRI IN COLLABORATION WITH RTI, THE REDS-III DATA COORDINATING CENTER. PILOT/QC DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL PARTICIPATE IN A PILOT STUDY WITH BSRI TO COMPARE HEMOLYSIS PARAMETERS DURING STORAGE IN THE MANUFACTURED LEUKO-REDUCED PACKED RED BLOOD CELLS AND TRANSFER BAGS FROM EACH OF THE 4 HUBS, AND COMPARE THE REPRODUCIBILITY OF THE ASSAYS ACROSS THE TWO TESTING LABS (UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH (UP) AND BSRI). SCREENING FOR EXTREME HEMOLYSIS PHENOTYPES A TOTAL OF 14,000 RBC DONORS WILL BE ENROLLED ACROSS FOUR REDS-III HUBS IN A MULTI-CENTER STUDY TO IDENTIFY NOVEL POLYMORPHISMS IN HEMOGLOBIN AND IRON REGULATORY PROTEINS, TO DEFINE THE GENETIC AND METABOLIC BASES FOR DONOR SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES IN STORAGE HEMOLYSIS AND TO ESTABLISH A SHARABLE REPOSITORY OF RED BLOOD CELLS (RBC), PLASMA, WHITE BLOOD CELLS, AND DNA SAMPLES FROM DONORS WHO WERE CHARACTERIZED FOR HEMOGLOBIN PARAMETERS, IRON METABOLISM, RBC STORAGE HEMOLYSIS PROPENSITY, AND GENETIC AND METABOLOMIC PROFILES. DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB AT UP WILL RECEIVE LEUKOCYTE REDUCED-PACKED RED BLOOD CELL (LR-PRBC) SAMPLES IN SMALLER VOLUME BLOOD BAGS FROM THREE (3) OF THE REDS-III BLOOD CENTERS (APPROX.10,500 DONORS). DURING THE INITIAL SCREENING, THE BAGS WILL BE ACCESSED USING STERILE TECHNIQUES TO ACQUIRE SAMPLES CORRESPONDING TO LR-RBC COMPONENTS STORED FOR 42 DAYS OF STORAGE. SAMPLES (~120/WEEK) FROM EACH BAG AT THE 40-42 DAY STORAGE TIME POINT WILL BE TESTED WITH SELECTED HIGH-THROUGHPUT ASSAYS (SPONTANEOUS HEMOLYSIS AND OSMOTIC STRESS). THIS COHORT OF REDS-III DONORS WITH LINKED RBC DONATION-DERIVED SAMPLES WILL ENABLE ANALYSIS OF KEY RBC STORAGE PARAMETERS AS A FUNCTION OF DONOR CHARACTERISTICS INCLUDING DEMOGRAPHICS, SMOKING HISTORY, AND FIRST-TIME/REPEAT AND ABO BLOOD GROUP STATUS. THE DATA WILL BE ANALYZED AND REPORTED TO IDENTIFY 1000 DONORS WITH EXTREME RATES OF HEMOLYSIS PHENOTYPES TO BE RECALLED IN THE SECOND PHASE OF THE STUDY. IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT 800 WILL BE ENROLLED IN THE RECALL STUDY AND WILL PROVIDE DONATION OF ONE FULL LR-PRBC UNIT ALLOWING FOR AMPLE VOLUME TO TEST 3 OR MORE STORAGE TIME POINTS USING EXPANDED TESTING MEASURING UP TO 4 FORMS OF STRESS: OXIDANT-INDUCED STRESS, SHEAR OR MECHANICAL STRESS, OSMOTIC STRESS AND STORAGE HEMOLYSIS. UP WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOW UP TESTING ON Â¾ (600) OF THE RECALLED DONORS. BIOSPECIMEN REPOSITORY/BIOLINCC DOCUMENTATION DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE STORAGE (-86 DEGREE CELSIUS MECHANICAL FREEZER PROVIDED BY BSRI) OF MULTIPLE ALIQUOTS OF CONCENTRATED RED-BLOOD CELLS AND SUPERNATANT FLUID (ADDITIVE SOLUTION AND LEFT OVER PLASMA) AT EACH TIME POINT TESTED, DURING BOTH THE INITIAL SCREENING AND RECALL STUDY. THE LAB WILL USE VALIDATED SPECIMEN ACQUISITION AND STORAGE SOPS, AND WILL HAVE AN ACTIVE QA/QC PROGRAM TO ENSURE THAT THE SOPS ARE BEING FOLLOWED. SHIPMENT VMI WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SHIPMENT OF SPECIFIC ALIQUOTS TO DR. ZIMRINGÂ€™S LAB AT PUGET SOUND BLOOD CENTER (PSBC) FOR FURTHER METABOLOMIC TESTING AND QUARTERLY SHIPMENT OF FINAL REPOSITORY ALIQUOTS TO BSRI.

description: BIOSCIENCE WRITERS (BSW) WILL PROVIDE WRITERS/EDITORS TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLINICIAN SUMMARIES USING THE METHODS AND PROTOCOLS DEVELOPED BY THE EISENBERG CENTER. BSW WILL SERVE AS PART OF THE TRANSLATION TEAM BY CONTRIBUTING TO THE PREPARATION OF, AND WRITING AND EDITING OF, UP TO 10 CLINICIAN SUMMARIES, PROVIDING BETWEEN 60 AND 85 HOURS OF SERVICES FOR OUR COMPONENTS OF THE WORK ON EACH TOPIC AT $100 PER HOUR, TOTALING $85,000 IN DIRECT LABOR COSTS PER YEAR. BSW COSTS ALSO INCLUDE A FIXED FEE OF $1,500 PER TOPIC ($15,000 FOR 10 TOPICS ANNUALLY) FOR A TOTAL OF $100,000 PER YEAR FOR UP TO 5 YEARS. TASKS THAT BSW WILL ASSIST UNDER EISENBERG CENTER GUIDANCE AND PROTOCOLS INCLUDE ONE OR MORE OF THE FOLLOWING: 1) PRE-REVIEWING EPC DRAFTS USING THE EISENBERG CENTER CHECKLIST; 2) REVIEWING AND SUPPLEMENTING (AS NEEDED) FORMATIVE FINDINGS; 3) PREPARING PROJECT PLANS SPECIFIC TO CLINICIAN TARGET AUDIENCE(S), AND CONTRIBUTING TO DRAFTING THE KEY MESSAGE DOCUMENTS; 4) PREPARING, IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE MEDICAL CONTENT EXPERT (MCE) AND THE EISENBERG CENTER DIRECTOR OR HIS DESIGNEE, DRAFT CLINICIAN SUMMARIES; 5) CONTRIBUTING TO PREPARATION OF TESTING PROTOCOLS; 6) PARTICIPATING IN ANALYZING TESTING RESULTS; 7) MODIFYING SUMMARIES AS A RESULT OF TESTING AND REVIEWS BY EXPERTS, EXTERNAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND AHRQ; AND 8) PREPARING THE DISPOSITION REPORT AND THE CONTENT PROOF FOR FINAL INTERNAL EISENBERG CENTER REVIEW FOR SUBMISSION TO AHRQ.

description: PURPOSE: TO SERVE AS A DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARY FOR THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION OF THE NATIONAL NETWORK OF LIBRARIES OF MEDICINE. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: OUTREACH LIBRARIES AGREE TO PERFORM THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS ON BEHALF OF THE NETWORK: 1. DESIGNATE A LIBRARIAN TO SERVE AS OUTREACH LIBRARY LIAISON TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION; 2. PARTICIPATE IN OUTREACH LIBRARY WEBINARS AND OTHER COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES PROVIDED FOR OUTREACH LIBRARIANS; 3. ASSIST THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF UNDERSERVED GROUPS OF HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND CONSUMERS WITHIN THE STATE; 4. PROVIDE UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITHIN THE STATE WITH REFERENCE SERVICES AND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING ACCESS TO ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY" LICENSE AGREEMENTS; 5. PROVIDE DOCUMENT DELIVERY SERVICE TO UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, CONSUMERS AND NN/LM AFFILIATE MEMBERS IN THE STATE; 6. PROVIDE TRAINING IN NLM RESOURCES AND DATABASES TO HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARIANS AND CONSUMERS IN THE STATE. THIS MAY BE DONE AT THE LIBRARY'S OWN INITIATIVE OR IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY; 7. SUPPORT THE NLM AND NN/LM EXHIBIT PROGRAMS BY ASSISTING IN AND/OR SUPPORTING STAFFING AT STATE EXHIBITS COORDINATED BY THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY, BY INFORMING THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY ABOUT POSSIBLE EXHIBIT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE STATE, AND BY EXHIBITING AT LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENTS; 8. ENTER NLM AND NN/LM RELATED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES INTO THE APPROPRIATE DATABASE WITHIN 30 DAYS OF THE ACTIVITY *; 9. SUBMIT TALLY SHEETS TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER AN EXHIBIT EVENT ..; 10. SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION, SUMMARIZING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN BY THE OUTREACH LIBRARY DURING THE CONTRACT PREVIOUS YEAR*. *NOTE: IN THE FALL, NLM PLANS TO COMBINE THESE THREE REPORTING OPTIONS INTO THE "NLM OUTREACH APPLICATION AND ONLINE CONTACT REPORTING SYSTEM" WHICH WILL REPLACE THE OARF DATABASE. ALL OUTREACH ACTIVITIES, EXHIBITING EVENTS AND ANNUAL.REPORTS WILL BE ENTERED INTO THAT SYSTEM WHEN IT BECOMES AVAILABLE. MEASUREMENT OF PROGRESS: PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED BY MONITORING INPUT FROM THE DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARIAN DURING QUARTERLY WEBINARS AND OTHER MEETINGS, LEVEL OF ACTIVITY REPORTED IN THE NLM OUTREACH ACTIVITY DATABASE, AND CONTENT OF THE ANNUAL REPORT.

description: OPTION 1: 0258-0538-4609 OPTION 2: 0258-0570-4609 OPTION 3: 0258-0603-4609 OPTION 4: 0258-0632-4609 OPTION 5: 0258-0657-4609 OPTION 6: 0258-0676-4609 AS PART OF THE CENTER FOR RESEARCH ON INFLUENZA SURVEILLANCE AND PATHOGENESIS (CRIP) OUR MANDATE IS TO ADD TO THE CURRENT BODY OF KNOWLEDGE ON INFLUENZA VIRUS PATHOGENESIS, HOST RESTRICTION AND TRANSMISSION THROUGH CONDUCTING NOVEL RESEARCH AIMED AT PUBLICATION IN PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS. 1) TO DEFINE THE MOLECULAR SIGNATURES THAT LEAD TO MAMMALIAN TRANSMISSION OF H7 AND H9 SUBTYPE INFLUENZA VIRUSES USING THE MAMMALIAN AND AVIAN ANIMAL MODELS. 2) TO DEFINE THE ECOLOGY AND EVOLUTION OF AVIAN AND SWINE INFLUENZA VIRUSES IN GUATEMALA AND ARGENTINA. OPTION 15B - PATHOGENESIS PROJECT (0258-0517-4609) COLLABORATION BETWEEN UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA RESEARCH FOUNDATION, INC. - UNIVERSIDAD NACIONAL DE CORDOBA, ARGENTINA AS PART OF THE CENTER FOR RESEARCH ON INFLUENZA SURVEILLANCE AND PATHOGENESIS (CRIP) OUR MANDATE IS TO ADD TO THE CURRENT BODY OF KNOWLEDGE ON INFLUENZA VIRUS PATHOGENESIS, HOST RESTRICTION AND TRANSMISSION THROUGH CONDUCTING NOVEL RESEARCH AIMED AT PUBLICATION IN PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS. 1) TO INVESTIGATE WHETHER SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION SYSTEMS OF S. PNEUMONIAE SENSE IAV-INDUCED ALTERATIONS IN ALVEOLAR AND BRONCHIAL CELLS WE WILL. 2) TO DETERMINE WHICH VIRAL FACTORS ARE INVOLVED IN THE SYNERGISTIC MECHANISM BETWEEN IAV AND S. PNEUMONIAE CELLS WE WILL. 3) TO DEFINE THE SYNERGISM BETWEEN AVIAN/HUMAN INFLUENZA STRAINS AND S. PNEUMONIAE IN DIFFERENTIATED HUMAN AIRWAY CELLS (HAE). OPTION 11B - 400 ANIMAL SURVEILLANCE SAMPLES (0258-0572-4609) FERRETS (MUSTELA PUTORIUS FURO) ARE NATURALLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES A AND THEIR DISEASE RESPONSE TO INFECTION WIDELY RESEMBLES THAT OF HUMANS INCLUDING CLINICAL SIGNS, PATHOGENESIS AND IMMUNITY (1-6). FERRETS ARE ALSO SUSCEPTIBLE TO AVIAN, EQUINE AND SWINE INFLUENZA A VIRUSES, ALTHOUGH ONLY SWINE AND HUMAN A VIRUSES INDUCE FEBRILE ILLNESSES IN FERRETS (7, 8). THE FERRET ALSO DISPLAYS PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS THAT ALLOW EASY IDENTIFICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF CLINICAL SYMPTOMS. THE UNUSUALLY LONG TRACHEA ALLOWS EASY COMPARTMENTALIZATION OF THE UPPER AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACTS (9, 10). THE FERRET IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MONITOR CLINICAL PARAMETERS SUCH AS TEMPERATURE, PULSE AND RESPIRATORY RATE WHILE ALSO BEING THE ONLY SMALL ANIMAL TO DEVELOPS A FEBRILE RESPONSE TO NATURALLY OCCURRING INFLUENZA A VIRUSES (10). ANTIGENIC CHARACTERIZATION OF INFLUENZA VIRUSES IS TYPICALLY BASED ON HEMAGGLUTINATION INHIBITION (HI) ASSAY DATA FOR VIRAL ISOLATES TESTED AGAINST STRAIN-SPECIFIC POST-INFECTION FERRET ANTISERA. THE GOAL OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO PREPARE FERRET SERA AGAINST HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES. FERRETS WILL BE INOCULATED WITH A HIGH DOSE (≥106 TCID50) OF HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUS IN 1 ML INOCULUM (TABLE 1). TWO FERRETS/VIRUS WILL BE USED. FERRETS WILL BE MONITORED FOR CLINICAL SIGNS OF DISEASE. AT 14 DAYS-POST-INOCULATION (DPI), 2-3 ML OF BLOOD ARE COLLECTED TO TEST HI TITER AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS, IF THE ANTIBODY TITER HAS REACHED ≥ 640, THEN COLLECT FULL BLOOD. SACRIFICE. IF THE ANTIBODY TITER HAS NOT YET REACHED THE EXPECTED TITER, PERFORM ADDITIONAL IMMUNIZATION, FOOTPAD SQ INJECTION OF 0.4 ML (INACTIVATED VIRUS+ADJUVANT)*/FOOTPAD. AT 14 DAYS-POST-BOOST, BLEED OUT AND TEST HI TITERS AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS. OPTION 19B - 400 ANIMAL HUMAN/ANIMAL INTERFACE PROJECT (0258-0621-4609) AS PART OF THE CENTER FOR RESEARCH ON INFLUENZA SURVEILLANCE AND PATHOGENESIS (CRIP) OUR MANDATE IS TO ADD TO THE CURRENT BODY OF KNOWLEDGE ON INFLUENZA VIRUS PATHOGENESIS, HOST RESTRICTION AND TRANSMISSION THROUGH CONDUCTING NOVEL RESEARCH AIMED AT PUBLICATION IN PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS. OPTION 17E - CEIRS CROSS COLLABORATION PROJECT (0258-0635-4609) A GLOBAL CROSS-LABORATORY EXERCISE TO IMPROVE STANDARDIZATION OF FERRET TRANSMISSION STUDIES. description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. description: PURPOSE: TO SERVE AS A DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARY FOR THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION OF THE NATIONAL NETWORK OF LIBRARIES OF MEDICINE. DESIGNATE A LIBRARIAN TO SERVE AS OUTREACH LIBRARY LIAISON TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION; 2.
