ASSIST THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF UNDERSERVED GROUPS OF HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND CONSUMERS WITHIN THE STATE; 4. PROVIDE UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITHIN THE STATE WITH REFERENCE SERVICES AND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING ACCESS TO ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LICENSE AGREEMENTS; 5. PROVIDE DOCUMENT DELIVERY SERVICE TO UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, CONSUMERS AND NN/LM AFFILIATE MEMBERS IN THE STATE; 6. PROVIDE TRAINING IN NLM RESOURCES AND DATABASES TO HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARIANS AND CONSUMERS IN THE STATE. THIS MAY BE DONE AT THE LIBRARY'S OWN INITIATIVE OR IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY; 7. SUPPORT THE NLM AND NN/LM EXHIBIT PROGRAMS BY ASSISTING IN AND/OR SUPPORTING STAFFING AT STATE EXHIBITS COORDINATED BY THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY, BY INFORMING THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY ABOUT POSSIBLE EXHIBIT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE STATE, AND BY EXHIBITING AT LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENTS; 8. ENTER NLM AND NN/LM RELATED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES INTO THE APPROPRIATE DATABASE WITHIN 30 DAYS OF THE ACTIVITY*; 9. SUBMIT TALLY SHEETS TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER AN EXHIBIT EVENT*; 10. SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION, SUMMARIZING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN BY THE OUTREACH LIBRARY DURING THE CONTRACT PREVIOUS YEAR*. *NOTE: IN THE FALL, NLM PLANS TO COMBINE THESE THREE REPORTING OPTIONS INTO THE "NLM OUTREACH APPLICATION AND ONLINE CONTACT REPORTING SYSTEM" WHICH WILL REPLACE THE OARF DATABASE. ALL OUTREACH ACTIVITIES, EXHIBITING EVENTS AND ANNUAL REPORTS WILL BE ENTERED INTO THAT SYSTEM WHEN IT BECOMES AVAILABLE. MEASUREMENT OF PROGRESS: PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED BY MONITORING INPUT FROM THE DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARIAN DURING QUARTERLY WEBINARS AND OTHER MEETINGS, LEVEL OF ACTIVITY REPORTED IN THE NLM OUTREACH ACTIVITY DATABASE, AND CONTENT OF THE ANNUAL REPORT.

description: THE OVERARCHING LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNE MARKERS AND MECHANISMS IN THE ELDERLY THAT DETERMINE THEIR VULNERABILITY TO INFECTIONS AND BIOTERRORISM AGENTS, SPECIFICALLY WEST NILE VIRUS (WNV). ELDERLY HUMANS ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO WNV COMPARED TO IMMUNOCOMPETENT ADULTS, AND WNV READILY INFECTS MICE, WHERE THE DISEASE IS HIGHLY LETHAL TO OLD ANIMALS AND RECAPITULATES MANY ESSENTIAL FEATURES OF THE HUMAN DISEASE. PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR AT OREGON HEALTH AND SCIENCE UNIVERSITY (OHSU) WILL OVERSEE WNV MICRORNA EXPERIMENTS AND THE WORK COMPLETED BY THE CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS, POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER, SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT, AND RESEARCH ASSISTANT 2. OHSU WILL IDENTIFY MICRO RNAS WITHIN SPECIFIED CELL TYPES FROM ADULT AND OLD ORGANISMS USING MASSIVELY (“DEEP”) SEQUENCING-BASED TECHNIQUES. THESE METHODS ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE BOTH SEQUENCE AND QUALITY INFORMATION FOR EACH MIRNA, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE MIRNA HAS BEEN PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED. SPECIFICALLY, THE CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS WILL ANALYZE MIRNA EXPRESSION IN DCS AND T-CELLS FROM AND ADULT MICE AND HUMANS, WORK WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA LAB TO DETERMINE THE CONTRIBUTION OF THESE MIRNAS TO FUNCTIONAL DEFECTS OBSERVED IN THESE CELLS AND WORK WITH POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER TO DETERMINE MRNA TARGEST OF AGE-MISREGULATED MIRNAS AND THUS HELP PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC BASIS FOR AGE-RELATED MULTIFUNCTION OF CELLS OF THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AND PROVIDE STATISTICAL OVERSIGHT AND ASSIST WITH EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND OVERSEE ACTIVITIES OF SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT AND RESEARCH ASSISTANT. THE POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER WILL IDENTIFY TARGETS AFFECTED BY AGE-MISREGULATED MIRNAS AND DETERMINE THE ROLES THESE TARGETS PLAY IN AGE-RELATED DEFECTS IN IMMUNITY. THE SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT WILL LEAD THE MIRNA AND PATHWAY ANALYSIS. THE RESEARCH ASSISTANT 2 WILL OVERSEE ALL DATA DISSEMINATION FOLLOWING THE DATA SHARING PLAN. ADDITIONALLY, OHSU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA AS PROJECT PROGRESSES, INCLUDING TRAVELING TO UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. A CRITICAL ELEMENT OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THE GENERATION OF LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST FLAVIVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS TARGETS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN THE CROWE LAB. THE MABS FOR RVFV THAT WILL BE MAPPED IN THIS CONTRACT ARE BEING ISOLATED AS PART OF ONGOING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION OF TED ROSS, PHD OF VGTI IN FLORIDA. THE DENV-4 HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF SUBJECTS IMMUNIZED WITH A LIVE-ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE THAT HAS BEEN USED SUCCESSFULLY IN HUMAN TRIALS IN COLLABORATION WITH A. DURBIN AND S. WHITEHEAD. THE JEV HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED A LIVE-ATTENUATED OR INACTIVATED JEV VACCINE IN COLLABORATION WITH S. THOMAS AND FROM CONVALESCENT PBMCS FROM SUBJECTS INFECTED WITH JEV IN THE FIELD IN COLLABORATION WITH C. SIMMONS. FOR THIS CONTRACT, THE CROWE LABORATORY WILL SUPPLY HIGHLY PURIFIED IGG PREPARATIONS OF HUMAN MABS WITH KNOWN FUNCTIONAL ACTIVITY. THE TEXT BELOW DESCRIBES A PLAN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE MABS. SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. FOR SOME OF THE VIRUSES TARGETED FOR HUMAN MAB PRODUCTION (JEV, RVFV), SOME OF THE SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS OF OTHERWISE HEALTHY DONORS WHO SUFFERED ACUTE AND CONFIRMED VIRAL INFECTION. THIS WILL BE COORDINATED BY DR. CROWE AND COLLABORATORS (RVFV: DR. MARIETJIE VENTER, UNIVERSITY OF PRETORIA; JEV: DR. CAMERON SIMMONS, OXFORD UNIVERSITY CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, VIETNAM). CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM SEVERAL IMMUNE DONORS WILL BE TRANSFERRED IN A COMPLETELY DE-IDENTIFIED FASHION TO THE VANDERBILT VACCINE CENTER IN THE U.S. FOR THESE STUDIES. IMMUNIZATION. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS. MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION. SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. description: PURPOSE: TO SERVE AS A DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARY FOR THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION OF THE NATIONAL NETWORK OF LIBRARIES OF MEDICINE. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: OUTREACH LIBRARIES AGREE TO PERFORM THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS ON BEHALF OF THE NETWORK: 1. DESIGNATE A LIBRARIAN TO SERVE AS OUTREACH LIBRARY LIAISON TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION; 2. PARTICIPATE IN OUTREACH LIBRARY WEBINARS AND OTHER COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES PROVIDED FOR OUTREACH LIBRARIANS; 3. ASSIST THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF UNDERSERVED GROUPS OF HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND CONSUMERS WITHIN THE STATE; 4. PROVIDE UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITHIN THE STATE WITH REFERENCE SERVICES AND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING ACCESS TO ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LICENSE AGREEMENTS; 5. PROVIDE DOCUMENT DELIVERY SERVICE TO UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, CONSUMERS AND NN/LM AFFILIATE MEMBERS IN THE STATE; 6. PROVIDE TRAINING IN NLM RESOURCES AND DATABASES TO HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARIANS AND CONSUMERS IN THE STATE. THIS MAY BE DONE AT THE LIBRARY'S OWN INITIATIVE OR IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY; 7. SUPPORT THE NLM AND NN/LM EXHIBIT PROGRAMS BY ASSISTING IN AND/OR SUPPORTING STAFFING AT STATE EXHIBITS COORDINATED BY THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY, BY INFORMING THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY ABOUT POSSIBLE EXHIBIT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE STATE, AND BY EXHIBITING AT LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENTS; 8. ENTER NLM AND NN/LM RELATED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES INTO THE APPROPRIATE DATABASE WITHIN 30 DAYS OF THE ACTIVITY 9. SUBMIT TALLY SHEETS TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER AN EXHIBIT EVENT 10. SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION, SUMMARIZING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN BY THE OUTREACH LIBRARY DURING THE CONTRACT PREVIOUS YEAR *NOTE: IN THE FALL, NLM PLANS TO COMBINE THESE THREE REPORTING OPTIONS INTO THE "NLM OUTREACH APPLICATION AND ONLINE CONTACT REPORTING SYSTEM" WHICH WILL REPLACE THE OARF DATABASE. ALL OUTREACH ACTIVITIES, EXHIBITING EVENTS AND ANNUAL REPORTS WILL BE ENTERED INTO THAT SYSTEM WHEN IT BECOMES AVAILABLE. MEASUREMENT OF PROGREY: PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED BY MONITORING INPUT FROM THE DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARIAN DURING QUARTERLY WEBINARS AND OTHER MEETINGS, LEVEL OF ACTIVITY REPORTED IN THE NLM OUTREACH ACTIVITY DATABASE, AND CONTENT OF THE ANNUAL REPORT.

description: THIS STUDY SHALL PROVIDE A CLINICAL TRIAL COMPARING TWO APPROACHES FOR THE PREVENTION OF CMV I.E., PROPHYLAXIS VERSUS PREEMPTIVE THERAPY IN CMV RECIPIENT NEGATIVE/DONOR POSITIVE (R-/D+) LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. THE STUDY ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGIC CONCEPT, I.E. ALLOWING CONTROLLED ANTIGEN EXPOSURE TO OCCUR AS OPPOSED TO ITS COMPLETE SUPPRESSION MIGHT BETTER FACILITATE PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY NECESSARY FOR LONG-TERM PROTECTION AGAINST CMV. THUS, THE TARGETED APPROACH OF USING PREEMPTIVE THERAPY UPON DETECTION OF VIREMIA MAY INCUR A LOWER RISK OF CMV DISEASE AND LEADS TO GREATER DEVELOPMENT OF CMV-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSE COMPARED TO PROPHYLAXIS. OVER THE LIFE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT AGREEMENT, SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL RECRUIT AND RETAIN APPROXIMATELY THIRTY-SIX (36) CMV R-/D+ LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS TO COMPLETE THE FINAL PROTOCOL.

description: IMPROVE THE RATE OF INFLUENZA, PNEUMOCOCCAL, AND SHINGLES VACCINATIONS AMONG MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES. THIS TASK SUPPORTS ACHIEVEMENT OF THE HEALTHY PEOPLE 2020 IMMUNIZATION GOALS, AND HAS A SPECIFIC FOCUS ON IMPROVING THE IMMUNIZATION STATUS OF MINORITY AND UNDERSERVED BENEFICIARIES. GREAT PLAINS QIN IS COMMITTED TO ACHIEVING THESE GOALS VIA A MULTI-PART STRATEGY WHICH INCLUDES: Â€¢ WORKING WITH PROVIDERS, PRACTITIONERS, AND HHAS TO IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICES, POLICIES, AND PROCESSES TO ASSURE THAT ALL CURRENT AND FUTURE PATIENTS HAVE THEIR IMMUNIZATION STATUS ASSESSED AND ARE IMMUNIZED WHEN APPROPRIATE. Â€¢ ENGAGING, EDUCATING, AND ACTIVATING MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES ABOUT THE IMPORTANCE OF INFLUENZA, PNEUMOCOCCAL, AND SHINGLES VACCINE SO THAT THEY ARE PROACTIVE ABOUT ACQUIRING IMMUNIZATIONS FROM THEIR PROVIDER OR OTHER APPROPRIATE SOURCES INCLUDING PUBLIC HEALTH UNITS, PHARMACIES, ETC. Â€¢ PARTNERING WITH ORGANIZATIONS AND STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS STATE DEPARTMENTS OF HEALTH, THE STATE IMMUNIZATION ADVISORY COMMITTEES, COUNTY PUBLIC HEALTH UNITS, AND PHARMACIES, TO RAISE PUBLIC AWARENESS AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO IMMUNIZATIONS FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES WHO DO NOT REGULARLY ACCESS A PHYSICIANÂ€™S OFFICE. Â€¢ HELPING TO BUILD CAPACITY WITHIN THE STATE AND WITHIN INDIVIDUAL PRACTICES FOR COLLECTING AND REPORTING IMMUNIZATION DATA AND INFORMATION. Â€¢ LEVERAGING 11TH SOW COMMUNITY ORGANIZING AND COALITION BUILDING EFFORTS TO MAXIMIZE IMPACT OF THE TRIPLE AIM AT THE LOCAL LEVEL. Â€¢ UTILIZING DEMONSTRATED EXPERTISE IN QUALITY IMPROVEMENT METHODOLOGIES AND DATA ANALYSIS, DATA SOURCES INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO MEDICARE CLAIMS, CDC, AHRQ, AND HRSA. MAXIMIZING THE IMPACT OF THE SOW WITHIN THE GREAT PLAINS QIN REGION WILL REQUIRE SUCCESSFUL COORDINATION, RECRUITMENT AND ENGAGEMENT OF A BROAD GROUP OF STAKEHOLDERS, COMMUNITIES AND IDENTIFIED PARTICIPANTS. COORDINATION OF RECRUITMENT EFFORTS TO PRESENT A SINGLE, UNIFIED OPPORTUNITY TO PARTICIPATE IN ALL QIN-QIO PROJECTS. PROVIDERS THAT SERVE UNDERSERVED AND DISPARATE POPULATIONS IN AN EFFORT TO CLOSE GAPS IN QUALITY AND HEALTH STATUS WILL BE TARGETED. SPECIFIC TACTICS TO ACHIEVE RECRUITMENT GOALS INCLUDE UTILIZING EXISTING RELATIONSHIPS, PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, CONSUMER GROUPS AND AGENCIES, RECRUITMENT LETTERS, NEWSLETTERS, WEBSITES, DIRECT SOLICITATION, CONFERENCES AND THE MEDIA. ENGAGEMENT ACTUALLY BEGINS PRIOR TO RECRUITMENT BY RAISING AWARENESS AND BY IDENTIFYING AND PRIORITIZING THE ORGANIZATIONS/COMMUNITIES AND ASSESSING THEIR INTERESTS AND CONCERNS. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE TO ASSURE TIMELY RECRUITMENT OCCURS AT THE BEGINNING OF THE CONTRACT. description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. ADAMS WILL COORDINATE OBTAINING EXISTING MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A MINIMUM OF TEN MURINE ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS OR GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN SPOROZOITE OR MEROZOITE ASSAYS PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE AND SPOROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE EVALUATED BY DR. ADAMS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. ADAMS WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. ALTERNATE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES. IN ADDITION TO THE CORE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DRS. FREMONT, GROSS AND TOLIA, OUR COLLABORATIVE TEAM HAS EXPERTISE WITH A VARIETY OF COMPLEMENTARY METHODS THAT CAN BE USED AS NEEDED. B CELL EPITOPES MAY BE MAPPED BY PHAGE DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY, A TECHNIQUE SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED BY DR. ADAMS. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE. HUMAN SUBJECTS INVOLVEMENT, CHARACTERISTICS AND DESIGN HUMAN: THIS PROJECT WILL OBTAIN HUMAN BLOOD FOR: 1) IMMUNE SERUM ANTIBODIES TO IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE EPITOPES; 2) PLASMODIUM VIVAX FOR EX VIVO INVASION ASSAYS AND DNA TO ANALYZE GENETIC DIVERSITY OF DBP; AND 3) UNINFECTED RED BLOOD CELLS (NORMOCYTES, RETICULOCYTES) FOR IN VITRO BINDING ASSAYS AND EX VIVO INVASION ASSAYS. ANIMAL: USF COMPARATIVE MEDICINE MAINTAINS AN ANIMAL CARE AND USE PROGRAM IS FULLY AAALAC ACCREDITED, AS ACCREDITED UNIT #000434. VETERINARIANS AND STAFF PROVIDE OVERSIGHT OF ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, GUIDANCE AND ASSISTANCE AND EQUIPMENT AND ROOM SANITATION. ASSOCIATED WITH GHIDR VECTOR BORNE PATHOGEN LAB ARE BSL1 AND BSL2 ANIMAL FACILITIES WITHIN IDRB, COMBINED SPACE WITH PREP ROOM AND AUTOCLAVE IS APPROXIMATELY 800 SQ. FT., THAT ARE CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING MOST OF LABORATORY ANIMAL RESEARCH NEEDS OF THE ONGOING PROJECTS. ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.

description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: THIS STUDY SHALL PROVIDE A CLINICAL TRIAL COMPARING TWO APPROACHES FOR THE PREVENTION OF CMV I.E., PROPHYLAXIS VERSUS PREEMPTIVE THERAPY IN CMV RECIPIENT NEGATIVE/DONOR POSITIVE (R-/D+) LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. THE STUDY ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGIC CONCEPT, I.E. ALLOWING CONTROLLED ANTIGEN EXPOSURE TO OCCUR AS OPPOSED TO ITS COMPLETE SUPPRESSION MIGHT BETTER FACILITATE PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY NECESSARY FOR LONG-TERM PROTECTION AGAINST CMV. THUS, THE TARGETED APPROACH OF USING PREEMPTIVE THERAPY UPON DETECTION OF VIREMIA MAY INCUR A LOWER RISK OF CMV DISEASE AND LEADS TO GREATER DEVELOPMENT OF CMV-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSE COMPARED TO PROPHYLAXIS. OVER THE LIFE OF THE CONTRACT, SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL RECRUIT AND RETAIN APPROXIMATELY 67 CMV R-/D+ LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS TO COMPLETE THE FINAL PROTOCOL. description: 1. ENSURE THE RECRUITMENT OF AT LEAST 15 LONG TERM CARE FACILITIES THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF THE 12 MONTH PROJECT PARTICIPATION PERIOD. 2. OBTAIN AND MAINTAIN GENERAL KNOWLEDGE OF THE PROJECT (GOALS, EXPECTATIONS, INTERVENTIONS, TIMELINES, SCHEDULES, ETC.) AND SERVE AS A LIAISON BETWEEN THE NATIONAL PROGRAM TEAM AND THE LTCFS. 3. ENCOURAGE ALL LTCF TEAM MEMBERS TO COMPLETE THE TWO SAFETY CULTURE SURVEY ADMINISTRATIONS (BASELINE AND PROJECT CLOSE), AND ASSIST WITH SAFETY CULTURE IMPROVEMENTS AND OVERCOMING PROGRAM BARRIERS BY ADOPTING TECHNIQUES DISCUSSED ON NATIONAL CONTENT CALLS RELATED TO SAFETY CULTURE. 4. MONITOR LTCF'S MONTHLY DATA REPORTS PROVIDED BY HRET, AND ADVISE LTCFS WITH OUTLIER RESULTS OR LOW DATA SUBMISSION RATES TO PARTICIPATE IN OFFICE HOURS TO IMPROVE PERFORMANCE. 5. PARTICIPATE ALONG WITH AT LEAST ONE TEAM MEMBER FROM EACH LTCF ON ALL EDUCATIONAL WEBINARS AND CONFERENCE CALLS. 6. COMMIT TO THE AHRQ'S SAFETY PROGRAM FOR LONG TERM CARE CHANGE PACKAGE INTERVENTION, WHICH INCLUDES: EVIDENCE-BASED INFECTION AND COMPLICATION PREVENTION PRACTICES; IMPROVED SAFETY CULTURE THROUGH THE ADAPTATION OF THE PROVEN SAFETY PROGRAM KNOWN AS CUSP.

description: DR. DANZIGER-ISAKOV WILL SERVE AS THE CCHMC SITE-PI OVERSEEING IRS SUBMISSION AND IRS MAINTENANCE FOR THE STUD, AS WELL AS PATIENT SCREENING, ENROLLMENT, DATA ENTRY INTO THE CENTRAL REDCAP TM DATABASE, AND SPECIMEN COLLECTION AND SHIPMENT TO LOVELACE BIOMEDICAL AND ENVIRONMENT RESEARCH INSTITUTE (LBERI). THEY WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE CCHMC BONE MARROW TRANSPLANT TEAMÂ€™S STUDY CO-INVESTIGATOR. DR. MIKE GRIMLEY, TO IDENTIFY AND ENROLL ELIGIBLE PATIENTS. EACH OF THESE STUDY MEMBERS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, DATA CLEANING FOR THEIR SITEÂ€™S DATA, DISCUSSIONS ON DATA ANALYSES, AND MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION. STUDY COORDINATION THE CCHMC STUDY COORDINATOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DAY TO DAY ACTIVITIES OF THE PROJECT, INCLUDING STUDY SETUP, PATIENT CONSENT/ASSENT AND ENROLLMENT, IRS COMPLIANCE, MAINTENANCE OF THE LOCAL MANUAL OF PROCEDURES AND ENSURE THE COMPLETENESS/ACCURACY OF DATA FOR CCHMC PATIENTS. THE CCHMC STUDY COORDINATOR WILL WORK IN CONCERT WITH THE CHOP STUDY COORDINATOR TO MAINTAIN CONSTANT COMMUNICATION REGARDING STUDY EXECUTION THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRETY OF THE STUDY PERIOD. PATIENT ENROLLMENT, SAMPLE COLLECTION, AND DATA ENTRY PRIOR TO BEGINNING ANY STUDY RELATED ACTIVITIES, APPROVAL WILL BE OBTAINED FROM CCHMC IRS. CCHMC STUDY STAFF WILL PROSPECTIVELY IDENTIFY, SCREEN AND ENROLL CHILDREN PLANNED TO UNDERGO ALLOGENEIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT 120 TO 140 PATIENTS WILL BE ENROLLED DURING THE 40 MONTH ENROLLMENT PERIOD. AFTER PATIENTS ARE CONSENTED/ASSENTED THEY WILL HAVE A BLOOD SERUM AND STOOL SPECIMEN COLLECTED IN THE DAY 7 TO DAY 0 TIME PERIOD. THESE SPECIMENS WILL BE PROCESSED LOCALLY AND SHIPPED TO LBERI ACCORDING TO THE PROTOCOL DETAILS. ADDITIONALLY ANY REMAINING CLINICAL SPECIMEN THAT WAS FOUND TO BE POSITIVE BY ADENOVIRUS PCR DURING THE STUDY FOLLOW-UP PERIOD WILL BE PROCESSED AND SHIPPED TO LBERI FOR ADDITIONAL TESTING STUDY STAFF WILL PROSPECTIVELY COLLECT DATA FROM THE PATIENTÂ€™S MEDICAL RECORD AND ENTER INTO THE STUDYÂ€™S REDCAP TM DATABASE. PATIENTS WILL BE FOLLOWED FOR UP TO 180 DAYS FROM TRANSPLANTATION.

description: ATTACHMENT A SCOPE OF WORK Â€¢ KEY PERSONNEL SUBCONTRACTOR WILL HAVE THE FOLLOWING INDIVIDUAL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING ROLE AS KEY PERSONNEL UNDER THIS AGREEMENT: [INSERT] Â€¢ TASKS - SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DO AS FOLLOWS: 1. PROJECT PLANNING: PARTICIPATE IN INTERNAL PLANNING CALLS AND MEETINGS TO ENSURE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES ARE WELL COORDINATED, EFFECTIVE AND CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVING. 2. HOSPITAL-LEVEL SUPPORT: COACHING FOR IMPROVEMENT AT THE HOSPITAL LEVEL THROUGH AWARENESS AND SHARING OF BEST PRACTICES; SITE VISITS WITH EXPRESS PREPARATION AND UNDERSTANDING OF CURRENT DATA REPORTING AND CULTURAL CHALLENGES; ANY SOLICITED AD HOC IMPROVEMENT NEEDS MUST BE MET. 3. DATA COLLECTION: SUPPORT HOSPITAL-LEVEL DATA COLLECTION THROUGH INTEGRATION INTO TOPIC AND ROLE BASED EDUCATION; PROMOTION OF CDS; ALIGNMENT WITH MEASURE REPORTING REQUIREMENTS; STRIVE TO CUSTOMIZE SUPPORT FOR HOSPITALS BASED ON RELEVANT NATIONAL, STATE AND HOSPITAL DATA REPORTING LEVELS. 4. CLINICAL EDUCATION SUPPORT: SUPPORT TOPIC AND ROLE GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO LEADING AND DEVELOPING EDUCATIONAL TRAININGS AT THE STATE LEVEL. ALIGN WITH AND PROVIDE ANY NEEDED CLINICAL SUPPORT TO THE PROGRAMMING, LED BY HRET PARTNERS AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL, INCLUDING IDENTIFYING HOSPITAL SPEAKERS. SUPPORT OVERALL ALIGNMENT WITH STRATEGIC GOALS OF HIIN AND REINFORCE THROUGH EDUCATION AND TRAINING. 5. ENGAGEMENT: SUPPORT HIIN LISTSERVS THROUGH SHARING QUESTIONS AND CONTRIBUTING TO CONVERSATIONS WHICH MATCH STAFF EXPERTISE; PROMOTE HRET HIIN WEBSITE CONTENT BY CONTRIBUTING PEER-SHARED RESOURCES AND RELEVANT EDUCATION MATERIALS TO BE A STRONG RESOURCE AND ENCOURAGE SUSTAINABILITY FOR HIIN HOSPITALS. PROVIDE FEEDBACK TO NATIONAL TEAM ON NEEDED RESOURCES BASED ON HOSPITAL CONVERSATIONS. ENGAGE IN PARTNERSHIPS WITH QIN-QIOS, TCPI AND OTHER IDENTIFIED PARTNERS IN SUPPORT OF HOSPITAL IMPROVEMENT IN HIIN. 6. CMS DELIVERABLE SUPPORT: PROVIDE NECESSARY DOCUMENTATION AND SUFFICIENT DETAIL TO SUPPORT THE HRET DELIVERABLES TO THE FUNDER, CMS. THIS INCLUDES MONTHLY, MIDYEAR AND ANNUAL REPORTS, AND ALSO ANY AD HOC REQUESTS FROM CMS. 7. FINANCIAL: PROVIDE DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED BY HRET STAFF TO DOCUMENT ACTIVITIES ENGAGED IN BY STATE PARTNER STAFF AND SUBMIT INVOICES TO HRET IN THE PROVIDED FORMAT. IF PRE-APPROVED IN WRITING BY HRET FOR TRAVEL, SUBMIT TIMELY TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT FORMS AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION ABIDING BY THE HRET SUBCONTRACTOR EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT GUIDELINES AND SUBJECT TO FEDERAL RATES OF REIMBURSEMENT FOR STAFF AND CONTRACTORS. FOR MILESTONE 1, CMS STRONGLY DISCOURAGES THE USE OF MONETARY INCENTIVES FOR HOSPITALSÂ€™ PARTICIPATION. THE MILESTONE 1 PAYMENT IS FUNDS FOR DATA RELATED SUPPORT FOR THE HOSPITALS TO USE TO SUPPORT NEW DATA COLLECTION EFFORTS THAT ALIGN WITH THE HIIN TOPICS. THE MILESTONE 1 PAYMENT WILL NOT BE USED TO INCENT HOSPITALS TO PARTICIPATE, NOR WILL THE FUNDS BE UNDULY WITHHELD FROM THE HOSPITALS. 8. COMPLIANCE: ENSURE THAT ALL ASPECTS OF COMPLIANCE RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ARE ADHERED TO INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE FLOWDOWN PROVISIONS. AT LEAST TWO, TIMES ANNUALLY THROUGHOUT PROJECT SERVICE 2: HOSPITAL-LEVEL SUPPORT 1. COMMITMENT LETTER BY DECEMBER 16, 2016 NEEDS ASSESSMENT BY JANUARY 31, 2017 2. CONDUCT INFORMED SITE VISITS WITH EACH COMMITTED HOSPITAL, AT LEAST ONCE; COMPLETE POST-SITE VISIT FORM FOR EACH VISIT. INITIAL VISIT BY MARCH 31, 2017 AND AS NEEDED SERVICE 3: DATA COLLECTION 1. ENSURE AT LEAST 70% OF ELIGIBLE HOSPITALS ARE REPORTING ON APPLICABLE 15 OF THE 17 CMS-REQUIRED MEASURES, MONTHLY. MONTHLY FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT 2. SUPPORT MONTHLY HOSPITAL SUBMISSION OF DATA INTO CDS: EITHER BY COACHING AND FACILITATION OR THROUGH SHELL UPLOAD OF STATE DATA TO CDS. 3. SUPPORT SUBMISSION OF HOSPITAL-LEVEL OPERATIONAL METRIC DATA; ENSURE ACCURACY OF HOSPITAL MEASURE SELECTION FOR ALL REQUIRED MEASURES. SERVICE 4: CLINICAL EDUCATION SUPPORT 1. ENSURE TIMELY AND SUFFICIENT INFORMATION IS SUBMITTED FOR EACH CMS MONTHLY REPORT. MONTHLY FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT 2. SUPPORT HRET IN THE SUBMISSION OF THE MIDYEAR REPORT TO CMS. SUPPORT HRET IN THE SUBMISSION OF THE DRAFT FINAL TO CMS. PRIOR TO AUGUST 10, 2018 5. SUPPORT HRET IN THE SUBMISSION OF THE FINAL REPORT TO CMS. PRIOR TO SEPTEMBER 4, 2018 6. SUPPORT HRET IN THE SUBMISSION OF OTHER CONTRACT DELIVERABLES AS NECESSARY. HRET WILL PROVIDE THE INFORMATION FOR THE NECESSARY SUPPORT FOR THE DELIVERABLE AT LEAST TWO WEEKS IN ADVANCE OF THE DELIVERABLE DEADLINE. AS NEEDED FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT SERVICE 7: FINANCIAL 1. SUBMIT MONTHLY INVOICES ON THE 15TH DAY OF EACH CALENDAR MONTH FOR THE PRIOR MONTH TO HIINFINANCE@AHA.ORG DETAILING ACTIVITIES ENGAGED IN BY STATE PARTNER STAFF AND SUPPORT. IF THAT DATE FALLS ON A SATURDAY, SUNDAY OR HOLIDAY, THE NEXT BUSINESS DAY WILL SUBSTITUTE. MONTHLY FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT 2. SUBMIT TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT FORMS AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION FOR TRAVEL THAT WAS PRE-APPROVED IN WRITING BY THE HRET HIIN TEAM WITHIN FIVE BUSINESS DAYS OF TRAVEL COMPLETION, AS NECESSARY. MONTHLY FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT OTHER: CONTRACTUAL OBLIGATIONS 1. PROVIDE WRITTEN CONFIRMATION TO HRET STAFF REGARDING THE RESOLUTION OF NON-CONFORMING DELIVERABLES. description: THE CENTER FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID SERVICES (CMS) CENTER FOR CONSUMER INFORMATION AND INSURANCE OVERSIGHT (CCIIO) IS CHARGED WITH HELPING TO IMPLEMENT MANY REFORMS OF THE AFFORDABLE CARE ACT (ACA). CCIIO WORKS CLOSELY WITH STATE REGULATORS, CONSUMERS, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS TO ENSURE THAT THE AFFORDABLE CARE ACT SERVES THE AMERICAN PEOPLE. THE STATE EXCHANGE GROUP (SEG) WITHIN CCIIO OVERSEES GRANT FUNDING, POLICY AND IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND COORDINATION TO THE STATES AS THEY ESTABLISH AND IMPLEMENT THEIR MARKETPLACES. THESE ACTIVITIES REQUIRE TASKS IN THE AREAS OF HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY EXPERTISE, EXPERIENCE WITH PRIVATE HEALTH INSURERS, SOPHISTICATED DATA ANALYTICS AND MODELING TO DRIVE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS MISSION, MITRE / CAMH SEEKS OBJECTIVE AND INDEPENDENT PERSPECTIVE, IN-DEPTH INSTITUTIONAL KNOWLEDGE, AND ACCESS TO EXPERT-LEVEL UNDERSTANDING OF THE, SBMS AND THE PRIVATE HEALTH INSURANCE INDUSTRY. IN ADDITION TO THE DESIRED SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE, MITRE / CAMH IS SEEKING PARTNERS WHO HAVE THE FOLLOWING KEY TRAITS: OBJECTIVITY Â€“ INDEPENDENT ADVICE AND EXPERTISE, FREEDOM FROM CONFLICTS OF INTEREST, AND DEDICATION TO THE PUBLIC INTEREST.

description: AS PART OF A COLLABORATION WITH STANFORD UNIVERSITY TO UNDERSTAND IMMUNE SIGNATURES OF EBOLA VIRUS DISEASE (EVD) SEQUELAE IN SURVIVORS, UCLA WILL COLLECT AND PROVIDE BLOOD SAMPLES FROM 10 - 20 SURVIVORS AT VARIOUS TIME POINTS AFTER RECOVERY AND UP TO 30 CONTACTS IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO (DRC). OUR GROUP HAS MORE THAN A DECADE OF EXPERIENCE WORKING IN THE DRC WHERE WE RUN A FULL-TIME PROGRAM (UCLA DRC) CONDUCTING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS. IN A PREVIOUS STUDY WE SUCCESSFULLY COLLECTED PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC) WITH HIGH VIABILITY FROM EVD SURVIVORS AND CONTACTS IN THE DRC WITH COMPARABLE METHODS TO THOSE REQUIRED FOR THE PROPOSED PROJECT. WE HAVE ACCESS TO THE NECESSARY LABORATORY EQUIPMENT, RESOURCES AND LOCAL, TRAINED AND EXPERIENCED STAFF TO ACCOMPLISH SAMPLE COLLECTION TARGETS. WE WILL TRAVEL TO LOCATIONS WHERE EVD SURVIVORS ARE LOCATED, WHERE WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY ESTABLISHED TRUST WITH LOCAL POPULATIONS. WE WILL COLLECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD IN VACUTAINERS FROM EVD SURVIVORS AND CONTACTS AND PROCESS VIABLE PBMCS AND PLASMA FOR CRYOPRESERVATION ON-SITE. WE WILL MAKE USE OF COLD CHAIN PRACTICES THAT WE HAVE ESTABLISHED IN PREVIOUS STUDIES IN-COUNTRY, INCLUDING USE OF GENERATOR AND PORTABLE FREEZERS. WE WILL ALSO COLLECT DATA REGARDING THE DISEASE COURSE AND HEALTHY STATUS FOR INDIVIDUALS FOR USE IN THIS STUDY. DATA GENERATED BY BOTH STANFORD AND OURSELVES WILL BE SHARED FREELY IN SUPPORT OF COLLABORATIVE PUBLICATION.

THE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS ARE NEEDED TO PARTICIPATE IN PARTNERSHIP WITH MITRE AND CMS TO PERFORM A PORTFOLIO ASSESSMENT AND ASSOCIATED MARKET RESEARCH INTENDED TO COMMUNICATE THE STATUS OF THE CMMI PORTFOLIO AND PROVIDE APPROPRIATE CONTEXT FOR DECISION-MAKING AND COMMUNICATION AROUND THE CMMI PORTFOLIO.

description: THE RESEARCH TEAM AT ZHEJIANG CDC WILL WORK WITH DR. QIU (PLATTSBURGH) TO COLLECT DATA FROM DIFFERENT INDUSTRIES IN ZHEJIANG PROVINCE. A BRAND NEW MOBILE TEST VAN OWNED BY ZJCDC WILL BE USED TO CONDUCT AUDIOMETRIC TESTS FOR WORKERS ON-SITE. A TOTAL OF 1,000 NOISE-EXPOSED SUBJECTS AND 200 NON-EXPOSED SUBJECTS (CONTROL COHORT) WILL BE COLLECTED FROM ZHEJIANG AND GANSU PROVINCES. THE NOISE-EXPOSED DATABASE (N=L,000) WILL CONSIST OF THE FOLLOWING: A) DIGITAL RECORDINGS OF COMPLETE SHIFT-LONG (8-HOURS) TEMPORAL WAVEFORMS OF THE NOISE THAT INDIVIDUAL WORKERS ARE EXPOSED TO IN A VARIETY OF INDUSTRIES, AND B) AUDIOGRAMS FROM WORKERS EXPOSED TO EACH OF THE SPECIFIC INDUSTRIAL NOISE ENVIRONMENTS. THE NOISE EXPOSED DATABASE WILL BE TO INVESTIGATE THE USE OF KURTOSIS AS A MODIFIER OF THE CURRENT STANDARD MEASURE OF SOUND PRESSURE LEVEL OR NOISE ENERGY (LEQ), IN EVALUATING THE POTENTIAL FOR NIHL FOR OCCUPATIONAL NOISE STANDARDS AND CONTROL. THE NON-EXPOSED COHORT GROUP (N=200) WITH VARIOUS AGE DISTRIBUTIONS WILL BE COLLECTED FROM THE SAME INDUSTRIES WHERE NOISE-EXPOSED SUBJECTS WORK. BY EMPLOYING A NON-EXPOSED COHORT GROUP WITH VARIOUS AGE DISTRIBUTIONS THE IMPACT OF AGE AND GENDER ON HEARING THRESHOLDS INDEPENDENT OF NOISE EXPOSURE WILL BE FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR IN OUR ANALYSES.

description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO, 10/12/16 PRIOR TO START OF THE PROJECT FOR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 2 CREATE A STATE TRIAD ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS (STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATIONS, STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENTS AND QIN-QIO) THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE ENGAGING PARTNERS PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AND AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SHD AND QIN-QIO IS WORKING O ACUTE CARE HAI AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN IN-PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE FOUR HAIS; DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS; AND SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES, BARRIERS AND LESSONS LEARNED. 4. COMPLETE A STATE LEVEL REVIEW THAT FOCUSES ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE QIN-QIO, STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATION AND HOW THE THREE WORK TOGETHER TO PROMOTE QUALITY IMPROVEMENT IN HAI. 5. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE LEVEL NHSN DATE TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS INCLUDING CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA) BACTEREMIA, CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI), AND CENTRAL-LINE ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTION (CLASBI). 6. RECRUIT AT LEAST 5 HOSPITALS, AND AT A MINIMUM 60% TARGETED HOSPITALS AND/OR LONG-TERM HOSPITALS INTO THE PROJECT BY 10/14/16. 7. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 8. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS. 9. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON SATE LEVEL MEETING IN COLLABORATION WITH THE SHD AND THE QIN-QIO. 10. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISITS REPORTS TO HRET. 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR SHD, QIN-QIOS AND/OR OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATE IN MONTHLY STATE LEAD CALLS TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED 13. ATTEND ANNUAL WEBINAR FOCUSED ON WAYS TO ENHANCE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES BETWEEN KEY STATE STAKEHOLDERS.

TO EMPLOY A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO COLLECTION, PROCESSING, AND STORAGE OF BLOOD, NORMAL AND TUMOR TISSUE, AND OTHER RELEVANT BIOLOGIC SAMPLES FOR MOLECULAR AND CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGIC STUDIES. 3. TO EVALUATE THE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS ON THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS BY INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL LABORATORY, PHARMACOKINETIC AND PHARMACODYNAMIC CORRELATIONS, INCLUDING EVALUATION OF SPECIAL PATIENT POPULATIONS, SUCH AS THOSE WITH IMPAIRED END-ORGAN FUNCTION, THE ELDERLY, AND RACIAL AND/OR ETHNIC GROUPS IN WHOM DIFFERENCES ARE ANTICIPATED. 4. TO IDENTIFY NEW PREDICTIVE MARKERS OF RESPONSE AND/OR SURVIVAL TO NOVEL THERAPEUTICS, INCLUDING CYTOSTATIC AGENTS, TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE STUDY DESIGNS AND STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES TO ASSESS SURROGATE MOLECULAR AND BIOLOGIC ENDPOINTS, AND TO CORRELATE FINDINGS WITH CLINICALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES IN ASSOCIATED CLINICAL TRIALS. 5. TO UTILIZE SPECIAL SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE WITHIN THE CALIFORNIA CANCER CONSORTIUM IN THE AREAS OF A) DNA METHYLATION, B) DNA REPAIR, C) SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION AND CELL CYCLE REGULATION, D) TUMOR ANGIOGENESIS, AND E) FUNCTIONAL IMAGING TO ASSESS DRUG-TARGET INTERACTIONS, TO ESTABLISH POTENTIAL SURROGATE STUDY ENDPOINTS, AND TO OPTIMIZE DESIGN OF LABORATORY-CLINICAL CORRELATIVE STUDIES.

TO EVALUATE THE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS ON THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS BY INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL LABORATORY, PHARMACOKINETIC AND PHARMACODYNAMIC CORRELATIONS, INCLUDING EVALUATION OF SPECIAL PATIENT POPULATIONS, SUCH AS THOSE WITH IMPAIRED END-ORGAN FUNCTION, THE ELDERLY, AND RACIAL AND/OR ETHNIC GROUPS IN WHOM DIFFERENCES ARE ANTICIPATED. 4. TO IDENTIFY NEW PREDICTIVE MARKERS OF RESPONSE AND/OR SURVIVAL TO NOVEL THERAPEUTICS, INCLUDING CYTOSTATIC AGENTS, TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE STUDY DESIGNS AND STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES TO ASSESS SURROGATE MOLECULAR AND BIOLOGIC ENDPOINTS, AND TO CORRELATE FINDINGS WITH CLINICALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES IN ASSOCIATED CLINICAL TRIALS. 5. TO UTILIZE SPECIAL SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE WITHIN THE CALIFORNIA CANCER CONSORTIUM IN THE AREAS OF A) DNA METHYLATION, B) DNA REPAIR, C) SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION AND CELL CYCLE REGULATION, D) TUMOR ANGIOGENESIS, AND E) FUNCTIONAL IMAGING TO ASSESS DRUG-TARGET INTERACTIONS, TO ESTABLISH POTENTIAL SURROGATE STUDY ENDPOINTS, AND TO OPTIMIZE DESIGN OF LABORATORY-CLINICAL CORRELATIVE STUDIES.

description: THIS RESEARCH IS BEING CONDUCTED ON BEHALF OF THE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) TO EXPLORE THE FEASIBILITY OF ULTRAVIOLET DECONTAMINATION OF FILTERING FACE PIECE RESPIRATORS (FFRS). PANDEMICS ARE EXPECTED TO PLACE UNSUSTAINABLE DEMANDS ON SUPPLIES OF FFRS USED TO PROTECT INDIVIDUALS FROM INFLUENZA INFECTION. ULTRAVIOLET GERMICIDAL IRRADIATION (UVGI) PROMISES TO MITIGATE POTENTIAL SHORTAGES BY EXTENDING FFR SERVICE LIFE. THE FOCUS OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO UNDERSTAND NEEDS AND POTENTIAL BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTING THE FFR UVGI DEVICE IN HOSPITALS DURING A PANDEMIC. THIS SUBCONTRACT IS FOR SBUMC SUPPORT TO HELP ARA IDENTIFY THE NECESSARY LOGISTICS AND POSSIBLE BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTATION OF UVGI FFR-DECONTAMINATION/REUSE (UVDR) IN ORDER TO MITIGATE FFR SHORTAGES DURING A PANDEMIC EVENT.

description: DR. KULLER WAS ONE OF THE INITIAL INVESTIGATORS FOR THE WHI AND HELPED IN THE DESIGN OF THE STUDY. HE HAS REMAINED AN ACTIVE PITTSBURGH PI. HE HAS ALSO BEEN AN INVESTIGATOR ON TWO BAAS ON HORMONE METABOLISM AND BREAST CANCER AND ON RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). HE HAS BEEN A LONG TERM MEMBER OF THE ANCILLARY STUDY COMMITTEE. HE HAS CONTINUED HIS ACTIVE RESEARCH ON THE RELATIONSHIP OF HORMONE METABOLISM IN RELATIONSHIP TO CVD AND BREAST CANCER AND THE RELATIONSHIP OF AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE, ESPECIALLY RA, AND RISK OF CORONARY HEART DISEASE. HE ALSO HAS A MAJOR INTEREST IN VASCULAR DISEASE AND DEMENTIA AND ON CVD OLDER WOMEN. DR. CAULEY WAS ONE OF THE ORIGINAL INVESTIGATORS IN THE WHI AND PLAYED AN INSTRUMENTAL ROLE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE CALCIUM, VITAMIN D (CAD) ARM OF THE TRIAL, HAS CONTINUED TO PLAY A MAJOR ROLE IN THE STUDY OF FRACTURES IN RELATIONSHIP TO HORMONES AND CAD. SHE HAS REMAINED AN ACTIVE INVESTIGATOR IN THESE STUDIES AND HAS ALSO BEEN INVOLVED IN GENETIC STUDIES OF BONE METABOLISM. SHE HAS HAD A MAJOR RESEARCH INTEREST IN VITAMIN D, BOTH CIRCULATING 25-HYDROXYVLTAML N D LEVELS (25(0H)D) AND VITAMIN D SUPPLEMENTATION. AS PART OF THE WOMEN'S HEALTH INITIATIVE (WHI), SHE CHAIRED OR CO-CHAIRED THE CALCIUM, VITAMIN D (CAD) OSTEOPOROSIS COMMITTEE FOR THE ENTIRE DURATION OF THE TRIAL AND CURRENTLY SERVES ON THE OSTEOPOROSIS SIG. MORE RECENTLY, DR. CAULEY COMPLETED THE MANUSCRIPT DESCRIBING THE 5 YEAR CAD EXTENSION STUDY, MANUSCRIPT CURRENTLY IN PRESS, J WOMEN'S HEALTH. SHE PUBLISHED PAPERS DESCRIBING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN 25(0H)D AND HIP FRACTURE IN THE WHI, AND IN MEN ENROLLED IN THE OSTEOPOROTIC FRACTURES IN OLDER MEN STUDY (MR.OS). OF INTEREST, BOTH OF THESE MANUSCRIPTS SHOWED THAT THE INCREASE IN HIP FRACTURE WAS PRIMARILY CONFINED TO THOSE WITH 25(0H)D < 20NG/ML, CONSISTENT WITH THE IOM REPORT. SHE ALSO PUBLISHED THE FIRST PAPER DESCRIBING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN 25(0H)D AND FRACTURE IN NONÂ­ WHITE WOMEN ENROLLED IN WHI. OUR RESULTS SUGGESTED THAT THE "OPTIMAL" 25(0H)D LEVEL MAY DIFFER BY RACE. CURRENTLY, DR. CAULEY IS LEADING A PAPER EXAMINING THE RELATIONSHIP OF 25(0H)D MEASURED PRE-MENOPAUSALLY TO BONE LOSS AND FRACTURE IN WOMEN AS THEY TRANSITION THROUGH MENOPAUSE, (STUDY OF WOMEN'S HEALTH ACROSS THE NATION, SWAN). SHE HAS ALSO HAD EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN RECRUITING AND IN RETAINING OLDER SUBJECTS IN BOTH OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES AND RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIALS. SHE HAS BEEN ACTIVE IN MANY WHI WRITING GROUPS AS PART OF THIS CONTRACT AND WILL CONTINUE PARTICIPATING IN THE OSTEOPOROSIS SIG AND IN THE DEVELOPING OF NEW MANUSCRIPT PROPOSALS. DR. LOPEZ WORKS CLOSELY WITH DR. KULLER IN STUDIES OF DEMENTIA. HE IS A LEADING INVESTIGATOR IN POPULATION STUDIES OF THE DETERMINANTS OF DEMENTIA. HE HAS MAJOR EXPERTISE IN NEW TECHNOLOGIES RELATED TO THE DIAGNOSIS OF DEMENTIA, ESPECIALLY MRI, BLOOD FLOW STUDIES AND PET IMAGING OF AMYLOID AND TAU. HE IS THE PL OF THE ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE RESEARCH CENTER AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH. HE WILL HELP IN WHI IN REVIEWING STROKE AND DEMENTIA MANUSCRIPTS AND HELPING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROPOSALS IN RELATIONSHIP TO DEMENTIA AND PROVIDE AN IMPORTANT LINK BETWEEN WHI AND THE AD, DEMENTIA RESEARCH COMMUNITY. HE HAS ALSO PLAYED AN ACTIVE ROLE IN DEMENTIA RESEARCH IN OTHER LARGE NIH-FUNDED STUDIES, INCLUDING THE CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH STUDY, ATHEROSCLEROSIS RISK IN COMMUNITIES, THE AGES-REYKJAVIK STUDY AND HEALTH ABC AS WELL AS IN SEVERAL NHLBI-FUNDED CLINICAL TRIALS.

description: OUTCOMES OF HUMAN ADENOVIRUS (HADV) INFECTION AND DISEASE IN PEDIATRIC ALLOGENEIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS: A PROSPECTIVE MULTICENTER OBSERVATIONAL COHORT DR. ADRIANA KAJON DR. KAJON WILL SERVE AS THE LBERI SITE-PI AND THE STUDY CO-PI OVERSEEING SPECIMEN SHIPPING FROM CLINICAL SITES AS WELL AS PROCESSING OF ALL RESEARCH-DIRECTED SERUM AND STOOL SPECIMENS, AND SUBSEQUENTLY ALL CLINICAL SPECIMENS POSITIVE FOR ADENOVIRUS BY PCR. DR. KAJON WILL ALSO OVERSEE THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE REDCAPTM DATABASE AND ENSURE THAT THE DATA ARE MAINTAINED IN A MANNER THAT IS COMPLIANT WITH THE NIH REQUIREMENTS FOR THIS CONTRACT. THE DATABASE WILL BE DEVELOPED AND STORED AT LBERI. FINALLY, SHE WILL ASSIST IN PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT (INCLUDING STUDY DESIGN AND ANALYTIC PLAN), DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF THE MANUAL OF PROCEDURES, AND CONTRIBUTE TO MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION. DATABASE DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE HANS PETERSEN, SENIOR RESEARCH ASSOCIATE, WILL OVERSEE THE DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF THE REDCAPTM DATABASE. THE DATA ELEMENTS TO BE COLLECTED BY THE CLINICAL SITES WILL BE DETERMINED BY CHOP STUDY PERSONNEL AND SEQUENCED TO MR. PETERSEN FOR DATABASE DEVELOPMENT. THE DATABASE WILL BE DEVELOPED AND PILOTED BEFORE IT IS SHARED WITH CLINICAL SITES FOR ACTUAL DATA ENTRY. WHEN POSSIBLE, THE REDCAPTM DATABASE WILL BE DEVELOPED USING CDISC SDTM TERMINOLOGY. THE LBERI STAFF WILL ASSIST IN REGISTERING ALL LOCAL STUDY STAFF AT EACH OF THE PARTICIPATING CLINICAL SITES FOR REDCAPTM ACCESS. ON A PERIODIC BASIS MR. PETERSEN WILL DOWNLOAD THE DATA AND RUN A NUMBER OF AUTOMATED DATA CHECKS. ANY ERRORS OR MISSING DATA FROM THESE CHECKS WILL BE TRANSFERRED BACK TO THE CLINICAL SITE AND UPDATED. PROCESSING OF RESEARCH SPECIMENS AND CLINICAL SPECIMENS POSITIVE FOR ADENOVIRUS DR. KAJON WILL COMMUNICATE WITH EACH LOCAL SITEÂ€™S LABORATORY TO ENSURE APPROPRIATE PROCESSING AND SHIPMENT OF STUDY SPECIMENS. ALL TESTING DICTATED BY THE STUDY PROTOCOL WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. ADRIANA KAJON. THIS WILL INCLUDE SEROLOGY TESTING FOR ANTI-ADENOVIRUS IGG BY ELISA, PLAQUE REDUCTION ASSAYS TO DETECT TYPE-SPECIFIC NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES, VIRAL ISOLATION IN CELL CULTURE FROM STOOL SPECIMENS, MOLECULAR TYPING OF ADENOVIRUS ISOLATES DETECTED IN RESEARCH AND/OR CLINICAL SPECIMENS OF ENROLLED PATIENTS, AND RESISTANCE TESTING OF ADENOVIRUS TO CIDOFOVIR, AND OTHER ANTIVIRAL AGENTS. CONFERENCE CALLS AND STUDY MEETINGS DR. KAJON AND MR. PETERSEN WILL BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN MONTHLY CONFERENCE CALLS. ADDITIONALLY, DR. KAJON WILL BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN A STUDY KICK-OFF MEETING, AND IN YEARLY IN-PERSON STUDY MEETINGS.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.   B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. KING WILL GENERATE HUMAN ANTI-MALARIA MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. KING HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA MEROZOITES. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY DR. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. KING WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE. HUMANS: AS INDICATED IN HIS PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS/ASSURANCE IDENTIFICATION/IRB CERTIFICATION/DECLARATION OF EXEMPTION, DR. CHRISTOPHER KINGÂ€™S CURRENT PROPOSAL UTILIZES HUMAN SUBJECT MATTER THAT IS DE-IDENTIFIED AND DOES NOT QUALIFY AS HUMAN SUBJECTS RESEARCH ACCORDING TO FEDERAL REGULATIONS. ANY POTENTIAL CHANGES IN THE SCOPE OF WORK THAT WOULD REQUIRE HUMAN SUBJECTS MATERIAL WILL BE DISCUSSED AND APPROVED BY APPROPRIATE INSTITUTIONAL AND NIH OFFICIALS PRIOR TO THE START OF WORK. ANIMALS: NONE ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.

SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. RETRIEVE SAMPLES FROM THE BIOREPOSITORY, MAKE THE APPROPRIATE CHANGES TO THE JHS BIOREPOSITORY DATABASE, AND PROVIDE AS NEEDED: I. THAWING AND ALIQUOTING INTO SMALLER VOLUMES; J. ARRANGING INTO APPROPRIATE WORK SETS (E.G., PAIRING SAMPLES FROM THE SAME PERSON FROM TWO DIFFERENT EXAMS), BATCH SIZE (BASED ON THE NEEDS OF OUR LAB OR AN OUTSIDE LAB), ETC; K. RECEIVE RESIDUAL SAMPLES FROM OUTSIDE LABORATORIES, MAKE THE APPROPRIATE CHANGES TO THE JHS BIOREPOSITORY DATABASE, AND RE-STOCK THOSE SAMPLES TO THE JHS BIOREPOSITORY. M. description: STRUCTURAL STUDIES ARE CENTRAL TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL AND PROVIDE MODELS THAT GUIDE THE DESIGN OF TREATMENTS. WITHIN THE CENTER FOR STRUCTURAL GENOMICS OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES (CSGID), THE WORK AT THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS SOUTHWESTERN MEDICAL CENTER AT DALLAS WILL HAVE TWO MAIN COMPONENTS: (1) MAINTAINING THE SALVAGE PATHWAY FOR THE COMMUNITY AND CSGID MEMBERS AND (2) PERFORMING CRYO-EM STUDIES FOR SELECTED TARGETS FROM THE CSGID TARGET LIST. UTSW PLANS TO WORK ON 5 SALVAGE PATHWAY STRUCTURES PER YEAR, WITH AT LEAST 1 STRUCTURE SOLVED THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND AT LEAST 1 STRUCTURE SOLVED BY CRYO-EM. UTSW WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO THE OVERALL STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORT IF NEEDED TO ENSURE THAT THE CSGID MEETS ITS GOALS. THE NATURE OF THESE STUDIES REQUIRES THAT WE WORK WHEN OTHER MEMBERS OF THE CSGID DECIDE THAT A PROJECT IS TOO DIFFICULT TO COMPLETE BY MEANS OF STANDARD APPROACHES. WE PREDICT THAT THIS WILL RESULT IN PERIODS DURING WHICH NO SALVAGE TARGETS ARE AVAILABLE TO US AND PERIODS WHEN WE WILL BE WORKING WITH MULTIPLE PROTEINS SIMULTANEOUSLY. TO HANDLE THIS IN THE MOST EFFICIENT WAY POSSIBLE, WE WILL USE CORE FACILITIES FOR TECHNICAL TASKS THAT EITHER DO NOT REQUIRE OUR SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE OR WILL COMPLEMENT OUR STRENGTHS. FOR CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC EXPERIMENTS: THE EXPRESSION, PROTEIN PURIFICATION AND CRYSTALLIZATION, AS WELL AS INITIAL SOAKING AND DIFFRACTION EXPERIMENTS, WILL BE PERFORMED BY OTHER GROUPS. DEPENDING ON THE OUTCOME OF THE INITIAL DATA COLLECTION, THE UTSW GROUP WILL EITHER DESIGN MODIFIED PROTOCOLS TO DATA COLLECTION ON SINGLE OR MULTIPLE CRYSTALS OR FOCUS ON CUSTOM SOLUTIONS TO PHASING, DENSITY MODIFICATION AND MODEL BUILDING PROCEDURES. AFTER STRUCTURES ARE SOLVED AND REFINED, THEY WILL BE DEPOSITED AND STRUCTURAL RESULTS WILL BE USED TO DESIGN THE NEXT SET OF EXPERIMENTS. FOR CRYO-EM EXPERIMENTS: THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION WILL BE PERFORMED BY OTHER GROUPS, WHILE THE UTSW GROUP WILL PERFORM INITIAL NEGATIVE STAINING, NATIVE CRYO-EM GRID PREPARATION AS WELL AS DATA COLLECTION. THE DATA COLLECTION WILL BE FOLLOWED BY STRUCTURE SOLUTION AND REFINEMENT UP THROUGH THE FINAL STRUCTURE DEPOSITION. THE INITIAL CHARACTERIZATION WITH NEGATIVE STAINING AND QUICK LOWER RESOLUTION DATA COLLECTION WILL BE PERFORMED ON THE TALOS ARCTICA, AND THIS WILL BE FOLLOWED BY HIGH-RESOLUTION DATA COLLECTION USING THE KRIOS TITAN.

description: SHAPE LAN INITIATIVES WITH RECOGNIZED PAYMENT SME AND LEADERSHIP EXPERTISE/RECOMMENDATIONS, IN COLLABORATION WITH PUBLIC & PRIVATE SECTOR LEADERS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE TO SHAPE LAN INITIATIVES, WORK CLOSELY WITH OTHER HIGH-LEVEL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR LEADERS, AND FORMULATE TECHNICAL AND PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS TO DEVELOPING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EXPANDING ADVANCED ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS ON AN ENTERPRISE LEVEL. THIS REQUIRES MASTERY OF, AND EXPERIENCE WITH, METHODOLOGIES AND CHALLENGES RELATED TO HEALTHCARE PAYMENT MODELS, INCLUDING MODEL DEVELOPMENT, RISK ADJUSTMENT, AND IMPACT ANALYSIS, AND SMALL-SCALE TESTING. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HAVE A NATIONAL REPUTATION FOR EXPERTISE IN HEALTH CARE FINANCE AND ECONOMICS, INCLUDING MEDICARE PAYMENT SYSTEMS, RULES, AND REGULATIONS. DEEP EXPERTISE WITH OTHER CMS PROGRAMS, MOST NOTABLY MEDICAID, AS WELL AS PRIVATE PAYER FINANCIAL SYSTEMS AND RULES IS HIGHLY DESIRABLE. LEADERSHIP IN CONSULTING ON, AND/OR WORKING WITH, PAYERS DEVELOPING ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS AND THE GOVERNMENT AND/OR PRIVATE HEALTH CARE PROGRAMS TO DEVELOP ENTERPRISE-LEVEL SOLUTIONS TO SUPPORT MAJOR INITIATIVES IS HIGHLY DESIRABLE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HAVE A STRONG TRACK RECORD IN CONSULTING AND ENGAGING DIRECTLY WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR LEADERS TO UNDERSTAND ISSUES, RISKS, AND OBJECTIVES OF HEALTH CARE INITIATIVES, TO COLLABORATIVELY WORK WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR EXPERTS AND TEAM LEADERS TO DEFINE THE OPTIMAL PATH FORWARD, THE PLAN, AND THE STRATEGY FOR ACHIEVING THE DESIRED GOALS. description: OPTION YEAR 2 EXECUTED TO EXPAND THE SCOPE OF WORK AS FOLLOWS: 1. INFECTION CONTROL RISK ASSESSMENT 2. HAND HYGIENE INFRASTRUCTURE 3. REPROCESSING 4. CLEANING OF ENVIRONMENTAL SURFACES 5. WATER-RELATED ENVIRONMENTAL INFECTION CONTROL. 6. FLOW OF PATIENTS, PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT. AMERICAN SOCIETY OF HEALTHCARE ENGINEERING (ASHE) WILL USE A COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH-BASED APPROACH TO IDENTIFYING INFECTION CONTROL SOLUTIONS AND BEST PRACTICES FOR HEALTHCARE FACILITIES AND PERSONNEL. ASHE WILL PRODUCE REPORTS FOR BOTH EXISTING FACILITIES AND NEW CONSTRUCTION ON INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL TOPICS. EACH REPORT WILL ASSESS THE RISK, IMPACT AND MITIGATION STRATEGIES, FOCUSING ON DESIGN AND OPERATIONAL ELEMENTS IN THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT. SUCCESSFUL HOSPITAL PROGRAMS WILL BE PROFILED WITH PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT DATA AND PROCESS IMPROVEMENT STEPS CLEARLY IDENTIFIED AS WELL AS IMPLEMENTATION TOOLS UTILIZED TO ACHIEVE AND THEN HOLD THE GAIN. FACILITATE DISCUSSION ON THE SUBJECT AND GOALS OF THE REPORT BETWEEN PROJECT TEAM LEADERS AND THE CDC. CONDUCT AN IN-DEPTH LITERATURE REVIEW, AIDED BY THE AHA RESOURCE CENTER, THE POWERFUL RESEARCH ARM OF THE AHA.

description: STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CARRY OUT WORK DESIGNED TO SUPPORT STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS DRUG COSTS AND IMPROVE CARE FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES. SOME STRATEGY COMPONENTS WILL NEED TO BE DEVELOPED IN A COLLABORATIVE MANNER WITH THE MITRE TECHNICAL MANAGER, CAMH DELIVERY TEAM, AND THE CMMI MODEL TEAM. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL: 1. DEVELOP A LANDSCAPE ANALYSIS ON RECOMMENDED VALUE-BASED PAYMENT APPROACHES FOR MEDICARE PART B DRUGS 1.1 PROVIDE STRATEGIC ASSESSMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS ON VALUE-BASED PAYMENT APPROACHES FOR SPECIFIC CLASSES OF DRUGS RELEVANT TO MEDICARE PART B WITH INDICATION OR PATIENT-SPECIFIC APPROACHES WHERE APPLICABLE. 1.2 PROVIDE STRATEGIC ASSESSMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS ON POTENTIAL MODEL CONCEPTS THAT PROVIDE AN OVERARCHING FRAMEWORK AND STRATEGY FOR EXECUTING DRUG-FOCUSED VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS FOR MEDICARE PART B; AND COULD POTENTIALLY BE UTILIZED FOR ENTIRE THERAPEUTIC CLASSES VERSUS INDIVIDUAL DRUGS. 1.3 APPLY EXPERTISE AND EXPERIENCE, AND CONDUCT MARKET RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS OF TOOLS USED BY COMMERCIAL HEALTH PLANS TO MANAGE DRUG COSTS AND IMPROVE QUALITY. 1.4 (OPTIONAL) DEVELOP RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CHANGES TO THE PART B PROGRAMS TO SUPPORT IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW VALUE-BASED PROGRAMS FOR HIGH-COST DRUGS AND DEVELOP CONCEPT PAPERS AND/OR OPTION PAPERS THAT MAY INCLUDE DESIGN ALTERNATIVES FOR MEDICARE PART B. 2. DEVELOP AN OVERALL STRATEGY FOR SUCCESSFUL NEGOTIATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF DRUG-FOCUSED VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS WITH PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURERS FOR MEDICARE PART B: 2.1 PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF HOW VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS ARE NEGOTIATED BETWEEN PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURERS AND PAYERS - BOTH IN THE US AND GLOBALLY; PROVIDE DETAILS ON THE DIFFERENT STAGES OF NEGOTIATION, TIMELINES, DEAL NEGOTIATION APPROACHES, AGREEMENT STRUCTURES, PAYMENT MECHANISMS, MISALIGNED PRIORITIES, AND RECOMMENDED APPROACHES FOR PVM. 2.2 IDENTIFY CLINICAL QUALITY, PATIENT REPORTED OUTCOMES MEASURES OR OTHER REPORTING NEEDS FOR VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS, BASED ON THE NEGOTIATION APPROACHES RECOMMENDED, REGARDING DRUG-FOCUSED VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS FOR SPECIFIC DRUGS OR CLASSES THERAPIES. 2.3 IDENTIFY AND RECOMMEND KEY TECHNICAL DATA SHARING COMPONENTS FOR THE STRUCTURING OF VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS, INCLUDING HOW THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN A DRUGÂ€™S FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) APPROVED LABEL, AND THE SPECIFIC OUTCOMES MEASURED IN VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS. 2.4 IDENTIFY THE KEY INDUSTRY PRIORITIES FOR PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURERS, BASED ON CURRENT MARKET LANDSCAPE, AND IDENTIFY HOW VALUE-BASED PAYMENT APPROACHES FOR MEDICARE PART B CAN ALIGN WITH THOSE PRIORITIES, BASED ON VOLUNTARY MANUFACTURER PARTICIPATION IN PVM. 3. (OPTIONAL) BASED ON CMMI DIRECTION, PROVIDE STRATEGIC ASSESSMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS FOR NEGOTIATIONS WITH INDIVIDUAL PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURERS REGARDING DRUG-FOCUSED VALUE-BASED PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS FOR SPECIFIC DRUGS OR THERAPIES.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. ADAMS WILL COORDINATE OBTAINING EXISTING MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A MINIMUM OF TEN MURINE ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS OR GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN SPOROZOITE OR MEROZOITE ASSAYS PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE AND SPOROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE EVALUATED BY DR. ADAMS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. ADAMS WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. ALTERNATE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES. IN ADDITION TO THE CORE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DRS. FREMONT, GROSS AND TOLIA, OUR COLLABORATIVE TEAM HAS EXPERTISE WITH A VARIETY OF COMPLEMENTARY METHODS THAT CAN BE USED AS NEEDED. B CELL EPITOPES MAY BE MAPPED BY PHAGE DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY, A TECHNIQUE SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED BY DR. ADAMS. C. SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. description: SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND CAPACITY BUILDING THROUGH THE FOLLOWING PRODUCTS AND SERVICES: Â€¢ ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT AND END-STATE VISIONING Â€“ ENGAGING STATE LEADERSHIP AND PROJECT MANAGERS TO CREATE A SHARED UNDERSTANDING OF THE BUSINESS DRIVERS BEHIND THE TRANSFORMATION, FOLLOWED BY INTERVIEWING A BROAD CROSS SECTION OF STAKEHOLDERS, RANGING FROM SENIOR LEADERSHIP TO THE PEOPLE DOING THE DAY-TO-DAY WORK. THE INTERVIEWS HELP IDENTIFY WHAT ISNÂ€™T WORKING AS WELL AS IT COULD, AND WHERE AGILE WILL HELP IT IMPROVE. AN ASSESSMENT IS DEVELOPED TO INCLUDE A RECOMMENDATION ON STRUCTURAL CHANGES REQUIRED TO HELP THE STATE MEET ITS GOALS, ALONG WITH PORTFOLIO, PRODUCT, AND DELIVERY TEAM STRUCTURE. A WORKING STRUCTURE WOULD BE DRAFTED TO INCLUDE A GOVERNANCE MODEL, FRAMEWORK, METRICS FOR MEASURING PROGRESS ON THE ASSESSMENT AND AGAINST BUSINESS OUTCOMES, AND A MEANS TO INSTRUMENT THE PROCESS WITH TOOLING. Â€¢ COACHING STRATEGY - COACHING INVOLVES WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE TEAMS, IN ADDITION TO THE STANDARD SERIES OF TRAINING AND WORKSHOPS. COACHES CONDUCT A COMPETENCY ASSESSMENT TO BASELINE ADOPTION IN KEY COMPETENCY AREAS, WORK WITH THE TEAMS UNTIL THEY ARE AT A POINT OF SUSTAINABILITY, AND CORRELATE TEAM PERFORMANCE TO ORGANIZATION OUTCOMES IN THE WEEKLY (OR MONTHLY) STATUS REPORTS. Â€¢ TRANSFORMATION ROADMAP - THE TRANSFORMATION PLAN WILL DEFINE WHAT GROUPS OF TEAMS WILL MOVE TO AGILE, WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO WORK IN A MORE TRADITIONAL WATERFALL METHOD, WHAT ORDER THEYÂ€™LL DEPLOY, AND WHAT THE STEPS WILL LOOK LIKE AS THEY MAKE THEIR WAY ALONG THE TRANSFORMATION JOURNEY. Â€¢ CHANGE MANAGEMENT PLAN - WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE GOVERNING BODY LEADING THE TRANSITION, GOALS AND OBJECTIVES ARE SET, A 90-DAY ROLLING PLAN IS CREATED AND MAINTAINED Â€“ WITH WEEKLY STATUS REPORTS AND REVIEWS OCCURRING AT 30-DAY INTERVALS. A COMMUNICATION PLAN IS DEFINED AND EXECUTED, INCLUDING ESTABLISHING OFFICE HOURS, CONDUCTING LUNCH AND LEARNS, OR ANYTHING NECESSARY TO KEEP PEOPLE INFORMED AND CREATE SAFETY AND AWARENESS AROUND THE AGILE TRANSFORMATION INITIATIVE. Â€¢ AGILE ORGANIZATIONAL PILOT AND ENTERPRISE ROLLOUT Â€“ LEVERAGING THE DEFINED END-STATE, APPROPRIATE TEAMS (DELIVERY, PROGRAM, PORTFOLIO GOVERNANCE) ARE FORMED; GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORKS ARE ESTABLISHED, INCLUDING METRICS USED TO BASELINE PERFORMANCE OF THE NEW TEAMS AND MEASURE AND EVALUATE PERFORMANCE OVER TIME; AN EVALUATION AND REVIEW OF AGILE TOOLS MAY BE PERFORMED IF REQUESTED. THIS SHOULD PROVIDE A SOLID PERFORMANCE BASELINE CENTERED ON THE METRICS, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT. Â€¢ ADDITIONAL SERVICES INCLUDE: O AGILE BOOT CAMP O AGILE REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT COURSE O AGILE GOVERNANCE AND METRICS WORKSHOP O CONTINUED COACHING SERVICES O SPRINT PLANNING WORKSHOPS
