description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.   B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. KING WILL GENERATE HUMAN ANTI-MALARIA MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. KING HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA MEROZOITES. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY DR. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. KING WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE. HUMANS: AS INDICATED IN HIS PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS/ASSURANCE IDENTIFICATION/IRB CERTIFICATION/DECLARATION OF EXEMPTION, DR. CHRISTOPHER KINGÂ€™S CURRENT PROPOSAL UTILIZES HUMAN SUBJECT MATTER THAT IS DE-IDENTIFIED AND DOES NOT QUALIFY AS HUMAN SUBJECTS RESEARCH ACCORDING TO FEDERAL REGULATIONS. ANY POTENTIAL CHANGES IN THE SCOPE OF WORK THAT WOULD REQUIRE HUMAN SUBJECTS MATERIAL WILL BE DISCUSSED AND APPROVED BY APPROPRIATE INSTITUTIONAL AND NIH OFFICIALS PRIOR TO THE START OF WORK. ANIMALS: NONE ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.

description: STUDY PREPARATION AFTER THE CONFIRMATION OF THE STUDY SITES WITH MITRE, THE CONTRACTOR WILL WORK WITH THE FQHC PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS (PIS) TO DETERMINE THE DATA COLLECTION APPROACH FOR THE FQHC POPULATION. IN THIS DISCUSSION WITH THE PIS DURING A MITRE-HOSTED FQHC CALL SPECIFICALLY FOR THE PURPOSES OF THIS PROJECT, THE CONTRACTOR WILL PRESENT THE FOLLOWING DATA COLLECTION APPROACHES FOR DISCUSSION AND APPROVAL:  FOCUS GROUP 1. MINIMUM NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS: 10 PARTICIPANTS PER SITE IN ONE OR MORE FOCUS GROUPS 2. LENGTH OF TIME FOR DATA COLLECTION: 60-90 MINUTES PER FOCUS GROUP 3. STAFFING: 2-3 PERSON-MONTHS FOR TRAINING, PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT, AND DATA COLLECTION  ONE-ON-ONE 1. MINIMUM NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS: 10 PER SITE 2. LENGTH OF TIME FOR DATA COLLECTION: 15-30 MINUTES PER PERSON 3. STAFFING: 2-3 PERSON-MONTHS FOR TRAINING, PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT, AND DATA COLLECTION  EXISTING PATIENT PANEL 1. MINIMUM NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS: DEPENDING ON SIZE OF EXISTING PATIENT PANELS, 10 PARTICIPANTS PER SITE IN ONE OR MORE PANEL 2. LENGTH OF TIME FOR DATA COLLECTION: 60-90 MINUTES PER FOCUS GROUP 3. STAFFING: 2-3 PERSON-MONTHS FOR TRAINING, PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT, AND DATA COLLECTION FOLLOWING THE DETERMINATION OF RESEARCH APPROACH, THE CONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP APPROPRIATE INTERVIEW GUIDES WITH THE COLLABORATION OF INVOLVED FQHC PIS AND STUDY STAFF. ONCE THE APPROPRIATE DATA COLLECTION APPROACH(S) AND RELATED INTERVIEW GUIDES ARE DEVELOPED, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DRAFT AND SUBMIT THE STUDY PROTOCOL AND CORRESPONDING DOCUMENTS TO THE INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD FOR REVIEW. THE CONTRACTOR WILL SCHEDULE TRAINING SESSIONS FOR PERTINENT FQHC STAFF ON DATA COLLECTION AND VERIFICATION PROCEDURES PER STUDY PROTOCOL. DATA COLLECTION MITRE HAS ESTIMATED EACH SITE WILL NEED TO SPEND A MAXIMUM OF 40 HOURS TOTAL TO RECRUIT PARTICIPANTS FOR THIS STUDY. HEALTH LITERACY WILL BE ASSESSED (IDEALLY) BEFORE THE Â€ŒDATA GATHERINGÂ€? ACTIVITY DIRECTLY (RATHER THAN BY DEMOGRAPHIC PROXY) BY USING A VALIDATED INSTRUMENT, E.G., 1. RAPID ESTIMATE OF ADULT LITERACY IN MEDICINE- SHORT FORM OR REVISED (REALM-R/SF): BOTH VERSIONS OF THIS INSTRUMENT USE A WORD RECOGNITION TEST OF LESS THAN 10 WORDS TO ASSESS A PARTICIPANT'S HEALTH LITERACY LEVEL. NB: THIS INSTRUMENT COULD BE USED TO STRATIFY THE PARTICIPANT POPULATION IN REAL TIME, ALLOWING FOR DATA COLLECTION TO BE FOCUSED ON PARTICIPANTS WITH LOW LITERACY. 2. TEST OF FUNCTIONAL HEALTH LITERACY IN ADULTS- SHORT VERSION (S-TOFHLA). THIS INSTRUMENT TESTS NUMERACY AND READING COMPREHENSION BY UTILIZING HEALTH CARE MATERIALS TO ASSESS A PARTICIPANTÂ€™S FUNCTIONAL HEALTH LITERACY LEVEL. AIM 1: IDENTIFICATION OF INFORMATIONAL NEEDS THE OBJECTIVE OF AIM 1 IS TO IDENTIFY WHAT PERSONS WITH LOW HEALTH LITERACY FEEL ARE THE MOST ESSENTIAL PIECES OF INFORMATION FOR INFORMED DECISION MAKING ABOUT JOINING AOU. AIM 2: PRESENTATION FORMAT TO MAXIMIZE COMFORT, SATISFACTION, COMPREHENSIBILITY UTILIZING CURRENT AOU INFORMED CONSENT MATERIALS, WE WILL ASSESS IF THE VOCABULARY USED AND THE PRESENTATION FORMAT OF THE MATERIALS ASSISTS OR HAMPERS UNDERSTANDING OF THOSE WITH LOW HEALTH LITERACY. WE WILL ASSESS THE VOCABULARY EMPLOYED AND THE PRESENTATION OF MATERIALS. DATA ANALYSIS THE SECOND PHASE OF THE STUDY WILL INVOLVE CODING AND ANALYSIS USING THE APPROPRIATE QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS SOFTWARE (E.G.. DEDOOSE, NVIVO). THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED ENTIRELY BY THE CONTRACTOR AND MAY BE SUPPORTED BY THE FQHCS DEPENDING ON THEIR STAFF INTEREST AND CAPACITY. DATA WILL BE REVIEWED BY AT LEAST TWO RESEARCHERS, CODED INDEPENDENTLY, AND COMPARED. TOGETHER THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL DISCUSS CODING, RESOLVING DISAGREEMENT BY CONSENSUS. CODES WILL BE FURTHER CATEGORIZED AND THEMES WILL BE IDENTIFIED USING HEALTH LITERACY LEVEL AS A STRATIFICATION LENS; DUE TO FOCUS ON HEALTH LITERACY, THE SHORT DURATION OF THE STUDY, AND THE EXPECTED SAMPLE SIZE, DATA WILL NOT BE FURTHER STRATIFIED BASED ON ADDITIONAL DEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS.

description: 1.) PROTOCOL IMPLEMENTATION A. MANAGE AND OVERSEE THE CONDUCT OF THE CLINICAL TRIAL AT THE CLINICAL SITE. B. PARTICIPATE IN THE PRE-STUDY SITE QUALIFICATION AND INITIATION VISIT FOR THE STUDY. C. OBTAIN REGULATORY APPROVAL FOR THE PROTOCOL AND INFORMED CONSENT. INCLUDING ANY AMENDMENTS AND YEARLY CONTINUATION APPROVALS. D. RECRUIT AND ENROLL (ACCRUE) SUBJECTS. E. GENERATE ALL SPECIMENS REQUIRED BY THE PROTOCOL. F. PERFORM ALL LABORATORY TESTS REQUIRED BY THE PROTOCOL. G. TRAIN ALL PERSONNEL AS REQUIRED TO CONDUCT THE CLINICAL TRIAL IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROTOCOL. 2.) SITE MONITORING, MANAGEMENT AND PROCEDURES A. PARTICIPATE IN ROUTINE MONITORING VISITS AS DETAILED IN CLINICAL MONITORING PLAN. B. RESPOND TO OVERSIGHT MONITORING BY DMID OR DMIC CONTRACTOR AS NECESSARY. C. PARTICIPATE IN ONGOING SITE MANAGEMENT, INCLUDING REQUIRED TELEPHONE CONFERENCE CALLS WITH PROJECT DIRECTOR AND STUDY TEAM. D. PARTICIPATE IN THE INTERIM STUDY VISITS AND CLOSE OUT VISIT. E. REPORT SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENTS (SAES) PER THE PROTOCOL.

description: THE TULANE NATIONAL PRIMATE RESEARCH CENTER (TNPRC) WILL PROVIDE HIGHLY INTEGRATED CLINICAL MANAGEMENT AND LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS USING A RHESUS MACAQUE MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECTS OF ADJUVANTED VACCINE FORMULATIONS. TNPRC STAFF WILL HOUSE, TEND TO, CARE FOR AND PERFORM PROCEDURES ON RHESUS MACAQUES IN ACCORDANCE WITH AN IACUC-APPROVED PROTOCOL THAT WILL INCLUDE BOTH CLINICAL AND LABORATORY COMPONENTS. THE CLINICAL COMPONENT WILL ACQUIRE, HOUSE AND CARE FOR THE ADULT NONHUMAN PRIMATES AND PERFORM IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY STUDIES USING A TRIVALENT RECOMBINANT HEMAGGLUTIN INFLUENZA VACCINE WITH AND WITHOUT A NANOPARTICLE-BASED SMALL MOLECULE COMPOUND ADJUVANT FORMULATION. TNPRC WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DAILY CLINICAL CARE OF ANIMALS AND ANIMAL PROCEDURES SUCH AS IMMUNIZING THE ANIMALS, BLOOD DRAWS, URINE COLLECTION, MUSCLE AND LYMPH NODE BIOPSIES, SPLEEN ULTRASOUNDS, ETC. A TOTAL OF 15 ADULT RHESUS MACAQUES IN EFFICACY STUDIES WILL BE USED. SA":JPLES WILL BE COLLECTED FROM THE INDIVIDUAL ANIMALS ACROSS TIME AT UP TO 14 PHLEBOTOMY TIME-POINTS DURING 4 MONTHS VACCINATION STUDY PERIOD, ACCORDING TO THE RHESUS PROJECT SAMPLE COLLECTION TABLE (ATTACHED). SOME OF THE BIO-SAMPLES COLLECTED WILL BE SHIPPED TO THE LABORATORY OF DR. OFER LEVY AT BOSTON CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL (BCH) AND/OR RELEVANT SCIENTIFIC COLLABORATORS AS APPROVED AND REQUESTED BY DR. LEVY. THE LABORATORY COMPONENT PERFORMED AT TNPRC OR ITS DESIGNATED LOCAL AFFILIATED LABS WILL INCLUDE ROUTINE HEMATOLOGY, CLINICAL CHEMISTRY AND PATHOLOGIC EXAMINATION OF ALL BIOPSIES IN SUPPORT OF THE ANIMAL STUDIES. TNPRC WILL ALSO PROVIDE FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SPECIALIZED PATHOLOGY SERVICES INCLUDING IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION, IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY AND IMAGE ANALYSIS. TNPRC STAFF WILL ALSO HOLD REGULAR MONTHLY TELECONFERENCES WITH DR. LEVY AND HIS RESEARCH TEAM AT BCH TO REVIEW STUDY PROGRESS AND WILL FACILITATE HAVING DR. LEVY AND KEY MEMBERS OF HIS TEAM VISIT THE TNPRC FOR STUDY SITE VISITS AND SCIENTIFIC DISCUSSIONS.

description: SUPPORT REFINEMENTS TO THE ACO REGULATIONS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CARRY OUT WORK DESIGNED TO SUPPORT FUTURE REFINEMENTS TO ACO REGULATIONS AND RISK ADJUSTMENT. THE CENTRAL GOAL IS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND SAVINGS OPPORTUNITIES, PROFITABILITY OF ACO PARTICIPATION FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF PROVIDERS, AS WELL AS HOW TO DESIGN REGULATIONS TO PROMOTE ACO SUCCESS AND PROGRAM SAVINGS. FOR THE FIRST PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL: 1. PARTICIPATE IN PLANNING SESSIONS WITH THE SPONSOR AND THE MITRE MODEL TEAM, AS REQUESTED. 2. USE MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA TO UNDERSTAND VARIATION IN ACO SPENDING PATTERNS AND ASSESS WHAT SERVICES HIGH-SPENDING ACOS USE (AND FOR WHAT PATIENTS AND EPISODES) RELATIVE TO LOW SPENDING ACOS (AFTER RISK ADJUSTMENT), AND TO EXAMINE CHANGES IN RISK SCORES FOR DIFFERENT ORGANIZATIONS, SOME OF WHICH WILL BE ACOS, OTHERS WILL BE Â€˜PSEUDO ACOSÂ€™ MADE UP OF LARGE ORGANIZATIONS ELIGIBLE FOR ACO PARTICIPATION BUT NOT PART OF THE PROGRAM. 3. TO SUPPORT POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS, CONDUCT A QUALITATIVE ASSESSMENT TO UNDERSTAND HOW ACO LEADERS VIEW HOW CERTAIN ASPECTS OF POLICIES SUCH AS INTERNAL FINANCIAL MODELING AND RISK TOLERANCE INFLUENCE ACO PARTICIPATION AND PROFITABILITY. ADDITIONAL POLICY, RESEARCH AND OPERATIONAL ANALYSIS IN SUPPORT OF THE ACO MODEL OTHER TASKING MAY BE REQUIRED OF THE CONTRACTOR FOR THE ACO MODEL. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CARRY OUT THE FOLLOWING IN A TIMELY MANNER AS SPECIFIED BY MITRE: 1. TAKE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR PROVIDING EXPERT GUIDANCE TO CMMI, AND WORK CLOSELY WITH THE MITRE TEAM, IN PLANNING POLICY RESEARCH, OPERATIONAL APPROACHES, AND ADDITIONAL RESEARCH TO AID IN MODEL DESIGN, ROLL OUT, AND IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS. 2. TAKE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY, AND WORK CLOSELY WITH THE MITRE TEAM, TO CONDUCTING THE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPING OPTIONS FOR APPROACHES. 3. PROVIDE WRITTEN CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE DOCUMENTS OR DRAFT DOCUMENTS, SUCH AS AN STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP) OR ICIP MODIFICATION, AS NEEDED.

THE CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL OF PHILADELPHIA WILL CONDUCT THIS WORK AS A SUBCONTRACTOR OF VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER. THE TASK C-1 WORK WILL INCLUDE: Â€¢ CLINICAL TRIAL CONDUCT, INCLUDING ENROLLMENT OF SUBJECTS AND COMPLETION OF STUDY VISITS Â€¢ HOSTING OF CLINICAL MONITORS Â€¢ WORKING WITH THE CONTRACTOR TO REACH THE DELIVERABLES SPECIFIED IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. JASON G. NEWLAND MD, MED (CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR) WILL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF THIS CLINICAL TRIAL. SPECIFICALLY, HE WILL BE THE PRIMARY LIAISON TO THE COMMUNITY PRACTICES AND EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS PARTICLPATING IN THIS STUDY. HE WILL ALSO OVERSEE THE DEVELOPMENT OF TILE NECESSARY STRATEGIES TO IDENTIFY AND RECRUIT POTENTIAL PARTICIPANTS. STEPHANIE A. FRITZ MD, MSCI (CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR) WILL BE INVOLVED IN ALL ASPECTS OF THIS CLIN IC TRIAL. MOST IMPORTANTLY, SHE WILL OVERSEE THE PROCESSES AND PROCEDURES INVOLVED WITH CONDUCTING SAFE AND EFFECTIVE METHODS TO PERFORMING HOME VISITS FOR THIS CLINICAL TRIAL. MARY BOYLE, RN (NURSE COORDINATOR) WILL SCREEN POTENTIAL PATIENTS AND CONDUCT THE ENROLLMENT AND FOLLOW-UP VISITS IN THE HOME SETTING. DR. FRITZ'S RESEARCH TEAM WILL AID IN DEVELOPING THE PROCESS FOR THE BEST METHODS TO CONDUCT THESE VISITS. CINDY TERRILL (STUDY COORDINATOR) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR REGULATORY ISSUES AND SCREENING OF POTENTIAL PATIENTS. SHE WILL BE A LIA ISON TO THE CLINICS AND EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS PARTICIPATING IN THE STUDY. THE STUDY COORDINATOR WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN THE HOME VISITS TO HELP WITH DATA COLLECTION. POPULATIONS AND FACILITIES THIS STUDY WILL RECRUIT PATIENTS THAT ARE CARED FOR AT BOTH EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS AND PRIMARY CARE PEDIATRIC CLINICS WITHIN THE ST. LOUIS REGION. THREE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS (ED) WITHIN THE BJC HEALTHCARE SYSTEM THAT SERVE BOTH URBAN AND SUBURBAN AREAS WILL BE USED: ST. LOUIS CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL (SLCH), MEMORIAL HOSPITAL BELLEVILLE (MHB), AND MEMORIAL HOSPITAL EAST BELLEVILLE (MHE). ANNUALLY, SLCH ED EVALUATES OVER 51,000 PATIENTS WHILE THE EDS AT MHB AND MHE EVALUATE APPROXIMATELY 12,000 PEDIATRIC PATIENTS. 12. ADDITIONALLY, A GROUP OF 7 PRIMARY PEDIATRIC PRACTICES THAT FORM THE WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY CLINICAL ASSOCIATES (WUCA) NETWORK WILL BE USED. THESE 7 PRACTICES SERVE BOTH URBAN AND SUBURBAN AREAS AND SHARE THE SAME ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD SYSTEM. IN A PRELIMINARY ONE YEAR REVIEW OF PATIENTS 6 TO 71 MONTHS OF AGE WITH AN ICD10 CODE FOR PNEUMONIA AND RECEIVING ONE OF THE STUDY ANTIBIOTICS, 169 PATIENTS WERE IDENTIFIED. ENROLLMENT STRATEGIES THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS AND CLINICS BEING USED IN THIS STUDY HAVE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA THAT ARE IS EASILY OBTAINED ON A DAILY BASIS. A DAILY DATA REPORT WILL BE CONSTRUCTED FROM EACH ED AND THE WUCA NETWORK THAT COLLECTS INFORMATION FROM THE PREVIOUS DAY'S VISITS OF POTENTIALLY ELIGIBLE PATIENTS. THE PATIENTS IDENTIFIED FROM THE REPORTS WILL BE SCREENED BY REVIEWING ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA. THE PATIENTS DETERMINED TO BE POTENTIALLY ELIGIBLE WILL BE CONTACTED TO ASSESS FURTHER ELIGIBILITY AND INTEREST IN THE STUDY. IF A PATIENT IS DETERMINED TO BE LIKELY ELIGIBLE FOR THE STUDY, A HOME VISIT FOR ENROLLMENT WILL BE SCHEDULED. THE RESEARCH TEAM WE HAVE FORMED FOR THIS STUDY IS HIGHLY EXPERIENCED IN DEVELOPING DATA REPORTS AND ENROLLING PATIENTS IN CLINICAL TRIALS AND PERFORMING HOME VISITS. AS PREVIOUSLY MENTIONED, DR. description: DELIVERABLES: TCPH WILL FACILITATE UNTHSC'S SUCCESSFUL PERFORMANCE OF CDC'S TASK ORDER #1, "IMPROVING THE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF LATENT TB INFECTION." TO THAT END, TCPH WILL ACT AS UNTHSC'S TBESC ENROLLMENT AND PRIMARY WORK SITE; AND WILL IMPLEMENT AND PERFORM ACTIVITIES AS REQUIRED WITHIN ITS TB REFUGEE, AND OTHER APPROPRIATE CLINICS. METHODS: THESE TASKS WILL TAKE PLACE DURING THE COURSE OF ROUTINE PATIENT INTERACTIONS WITHIN THE EXISTING SETTING AND ACTIVITIES OF TCPH'S TB, REFUGEE, AND OTHER CLINICS. ACTIVITIES REQUIRED BY THE EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOL WILL REQUIRE ADDITIONAL LABOR AND OTHER RESOURCES WITHIN THE TCPH SETTING. SOME OF THESE ADDITIONAL RESOURCES WILL BE PROVIDED BY TCPH, TO INCLUDE SKILLED STAFF FOR NURSING, SUPERVISORY, PHYSICIAN, CLERICAL AND OTHER AS APPROPRIATE. STAFF WILL: 1. PARTICIPATE IN APPROPRIATE TRAINING PRIOR TO AND DURING THE COURSE OF THE STUDY ACTIVITIES; 2. ENROLL AND CONSENT RESEARCH SUBJECTS FROM AMONG POPULATIONS OF INTEREST; 3. description: OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND CMS HAS REQUESTED THE CMS ALLIANCE TO MODERNIZE HEALTHCARE (CAMH) FFRDC TO COLLABORATE ON A MEDICAID REGULATORY REVIEW AND PROVIDE ANALYSES AND RECOMMENDATIONS BASED ON A BROAD DESCRIPTION OF THEIR TARGET GOALS TO ALLEVIATE BURDEN AND INCREASE FLEXIBILITY FOR STATES. THE INTENT OF THE REGULATORY REVIEW IS TO TAKE A FRESH LOOK AT THE RELATIONSHIP OF THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TO THE STATES UNDER THE MEDICAID PROGRAM USING A NEW DECISION-MAKING MATRIX. CMS ANTICIPATES THE WORK BEING CONDUCTED IN FOUR PHASES. THE 4 PHASES ARE CURRENTLY UNDERSTOOD AS FOLLOWS: Â€¢ PHASE 1: WORK SHAPING, INCLUDING IDENTIFICATION OF END GOALS, TOPIC AREAS FOR REVIEW, DEVELOPMENT OF ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK AND DEFINED CRITERIA; Â€¢ PHASE 2: ANALYSES OF IDENTIFIED EXISTING REGULATIONS, SUB-REGULATORY GUIDANCE AND STAKEHOLDER PERSPECTIVES RELATED TO EACH ISSUE AREA IDENTIFIED IN PHASE 1; Â€¢ PHASE 3: DRAFTING REGULATORY AND SUB-REGULATORY DOCUMENTS, ASSISTING IN THE OSORA CLEARANCE PROCESS AND IMPLEMENTATION OF REGULATORY REVISIONS; Â€¢ PHASE 4: PROCESSING OF PUBLIC COMMENTS AND SUPPORT DRAFTING OF FINAL RULES. SCOPE Â€“ PHASE 2 THE NATIONAL OPINION RESEARCH CENTER AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO (HEREAFTER Â€ŒNORCÂ€?), DUE TO THEIR SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE IN MEDICAID POLICY AND FEDERAL REGULATORY ANALYSIS, HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED BY MITRE AS AN IMPORTANT PARTICIPANT IN THIS WORK. NORC WILL BE INVOLVED PRIMARILY IN PHASE 2 PROVIDING SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE, TO INCLUDE BUT NOT LIMITED TO POLICY AND FINANCIAL ANALYSES, REGARDING THE CURRENT MEDICAID MANAGED CARE REGULATIONS AND SUB-REGULATORY GUIDANCE. NORC WILL FUNCTION AS PART OF AN INTEGRATED TEAM THAT INVOLVES CMS, MITRE, AND SPEIRE LLC AND ADDITIONAL SUBCONTRACTORS THAT MITRE DEEMS NECESSARY TO ACCOMPLISH THIS WORK. THIS SCOPE OF WORK COVERS NORCÂ€™S ROLE IN PHASE 2 AND REQUIRES NORC TO ASSEMBLE A TEAM OF 4 Â€“ 5 STAFF MEMBERS WITH EXPERTISE IN MEDICAID POLICY, IN PARTICULAR, IN MEDICAID MANAGED CARE. Â€¢ WORK AS AN INTEGRATED TEAM WITH MITRE, ALLIANCE PARTNERS, AND SUBCONTRACTORS; Â€¢ PARTICIPATE IN WORK SESSIONS AND OTHER MEETINGS TO REVIEW RECOMMENDATIONS AND ARTICULATE POLICY GOALS; Â€¢ PARTNER WITH MITRE TO DEVELOP AND FINALIZE AN ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK TO PERFORM ANALYSES OF RECOMMENDATIONS; Â€¢ REVIEW RECOMMENDATIONS FROM PHASE ONE USING THE ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK ON MEDICAID POLICIES INCLUDED IN THE MAY 6, 2016 MEDICAID MANAGED CARE FINAL RULE; Â€¢ DRAFT ANALYSES OF POLICY AND FISCAL IMPLICATIONS OF RECOMMENDED CHANGES TO CURRENT MEDICAID POLICIES FOUND IN SPECIFIED REGULATIONS AND SUB-REGULATORY GUIDANCE; Â€¢ PREPARE ISSUE PAPERS, OPTIONS PAPERS, AND OTHER SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION THAT WILL HELP SHAPE RECOMMENDATIONS; AND Â€¢ PROVIDE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES AND POLICY EXPERTISE AS NEEDED.

description: DEVELOP THE BASIS FOR A MEDICARE STRATEGY THE FOLLOWING SUBTASKS PROVIDE THE BASIS FOR A STRATEGY FOR CONTINUING TO GROW MA, WHICH OFFERS THE POTENTIAL TO SLOW LONG-TERM MEDICARE COST GROWTH AND INCREASE COORDINATED CARE DELIVERY WITH HIGHER-VALUE PROVIDERS, THEREBY IMPROVING PATIENT OUTCOMES. MA ENROLLEES AS A PERCENT OF MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES CONTINUE TO GROW (31% OF ALL MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES IN 2016, UP FROM 25% IN 2011 AND 22% IN 2008) AND CURRENT PROJECTIONS BY THE CBO SUGGEST THAT WITHOUT ANY OTHER CHANGES, BY 2026 41% OF MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES WILL BE ENROLLED IN AN MA PLAN. UNDER CURRENT POLICY, PRIVATE MA PLANS TYPICALLY DELIVER BASIC MEDICARE BENEFITS AT A LOWER COST THAN FFS DOES. INCREASING MA PENETRATION WOULD POTENTIALLY LOWER MEDICARE COSTS AND PROVIDE CMS WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO WORK WITH MA PLANS ON VALUE-BASED CAPITATION ARRANGEMENTS. SUBTASK 2.1: ANALYZE CURRENT STATE AND POTENTIAL LEVERS TO DRIVE GROWTH OBJECTIVES ■ DEVELOP A FACT BASE OF MEDICARE GROWTH AND FINANCING TRENDS ■ DEVELOP HYPOTHESES ABOUT POTENTIAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN MA PROGRAM CHANGES AND GROWTH ELEMENTS ■ UNDERSTAND CONSUMER DECISION-MAKING IN MA PLAN SELECTION ■ UNDERSTAND KEY INDICATORS OF MA COST AND SPENDING RELATIVE TO OTHER CARE OPTIONS (E.G., FFS) ■ ASSESS REGULATORY STREAMLINING OPTIONS AND SHARE BEST PRACTICES TO RESTRUCTURE BUSINESS PROCESSES ■ DEVELOP SPECTRUM OF LEVERS/OPTIONS AVAILABLE TO INCREASE MA PENETRATION (E.G., AGE-IN FACILITATION) ■ CREATE ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK WITH RELEVANT METRICS (E.G., PENETRATION RATE, CONSUMER SATISFACTION, CHURN RATES) AGAINST WHICH TO ASSESS LEVERS/OPTIONS PRIORITIZE THE BASIS FOR A MEDICARE PRODUCT COMPETITIVE BIDDING STRATEGY THE FOLLOWING SUBTASKS PROVIDE THE BASIS FOR A STRATEGY FOR CONTINUING TO FOSTER INNOVATION IN MA. OVER THE PAST FEW YEARS, MEDICARE ADVANTAGE PLANS HAVE PURSUED INNOVATIONS IN PROVIDER PAYMENT THROUGH OUTCOME AND RISK BASED ARRANGEMENTS ACCELERATING SUPPLY SIDE INNOVATION. MEDICARE COULD ALSO ENCOURAGE DEMAND-SIDE INNOVATION, WHICH COULD BE OF VALUE BUT ALSO PROVIDE A COMPOUNDING BENEFIT COUPLED WITH PAYMENT INNOVATIONS ALREADY UNDERWAY. CMS HAS TAKEN SOME INITIAL STEPS, FOR EXAMPLE THROUGH THE CENTERS FOR MEDICARE AND MEDICAID INNOVATION (CMMI) LAUNCHING A PILOT IN VALUE-BASED INSURANCE DESIGN (VBID) FOR A LIMITED SET OF QUALIFYING MA PLANS AS OF JANUARY 2017. INITIAL PILOTS FOCUSED ON SPECIFIC BANDS OF MEDICAL CONDITIONS AND STATES AND CARRIERS HAVE BEEN RESTRICTED IN TERMS OF THEIR ABILITY TO MARKET TO AND COMMUNICATE WITH BENEFICIARIES. SUBTASK 3.1: ANALYZE CURRENT STATE AND CODIFY POTENTIAL LEVERS TO DRIVE INNOVATION OBJECTIVES ■ CONDUCT CURRENT STATE ANALYSIS TO UNDERSTAND THE RANGE OF PRODUCT OFFERING OPTIONS ■ IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES TO ENABLE PRODUCT DIFFERENTIATION FOR MA (E.G., HEALTH SAVINGS ACCOUNTS (HSAS) WITH SECONDARY PREVENTION, VALUE-BASED INSURANCE DESIGN (VBID) OFFERINGS, INTEGRATED DELIVERY PLAN OFFERINGS) ■ CREATE FRAMEWORK WITH WHICH TO EVALUATE SUCCESS OF MA INNOVATION OPPORTUNITIES AGAINST STATED GOALS (E.G., % PENETRATION, OVERALL UTILIZATION, OVERALL PREMIUMS), INCLUDING THE SCALABILITY OF EXISTING INNOVATION PROGRAMS SUCH AS THE CMMI VBID PILOT

description: THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO DETERMINE WHETHER THREE DIFFERENT MICRO-ENGINEERED Â€˜ORGAN-ON-CHIPÂ€™ MICROPHYSIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS (GUT CHIP, BONE MARROW CHIP AND LUNG CHIP) CAN SERVE AS IN VITRO ALTERNATIVES TO IN VIVO SCREENING OF MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES (MCMS) FOR ACUTE RADIATION SYNDROME. IN PHASE 1 (24 MONTHS) OF THE BASE PERIOD (42 MONTHS), WE WILL BEGIN STUDIES WITH A HUMAN GUT CHIP THAT CONTAINS LIVING HUMAN INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL CELLS CULTURED WITHIN MICROFLUIDIC DEVICES THAT RECAPITULATE THE THREE- DIMENSIONAL (3D) VILLUS ARCHITECTURE AND MECHANICALLY ACTIVE MICROENVIRONMENT OF THE LIVING INTESTINE. RADIATION SENSITIVITY AND MCM STUDIES WILL BE CARRIED OUT USING THE GUT CHIP IN THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF A LIVING MICROBIOME. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CARRY OUT EXPERIMENTS USING A BONE MARROW CHIP THAT IS FORMED BY ENGINEERING WHOLE ARTIFICIAL BONE IN A LIVING MOUSE, AND THEN REMOVING IT AND CULTURING IT WITHIN A MICROFLUIDIC DEVICE. ALTHOUGH WE WILL BEGIN WITH MOUSE MARROW, WE ALSO WILL CARRY OUT STUDIES TO EXPLORE IF WE CAN REPLACE THE MOUSE MARROW CELLS WITH CELLS FROM HUMAN CORD BLOOD TO CREATE A HUMAN BONE MARROW CHIP.

THROUGH THE LCS, THE CENTER FOR MEDICAID AND CHIP SERVICES (CMCS) IS ABLE TO QUICKLY PUSH OUT HIGHPRIORITY POLICY AND OPERATIONAL INFORMATION TO STATES; INFORMALLY DISCUSS ISSUES RELATED TO HEALTH CARE REFORM WITH STATE MEDICAID AND CHIP OFFICIALS; DEVELOP TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TOOLS AND MATERIALS FOR STATES TO SUPPORT HEALTH REFORM IMPLEMENTATION AND MONITORING; AND TO RECEIVE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FROM MATHEMATICA AND MANATT STAFF.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL MAINTAIN A DATA MANAGEMENT SYSTEM WHICH SHALL ALLOW PROCESSING OF ALL INCOMING DATA, PERFORM BASIC DATA EDITS, AND UPDATE CASE AND TUMOR SPECIFIC INFORMATION. 6. Â€¢ RESPONDING TO LOCAL DATA REQUESTS FROM THE HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND THE LAY PUBLIC FOR NON-CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. Â€¢ MAINTAINING A COLLABORATIVE RELATIONSHIP WITH LOCAL INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARDS. Â€¢ ACTING AS LIAISON TO MAINTAIN THE COOPERATION OF HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS IN SPECIAL STUDIES. description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO 5/7/17 2. CREATE A STATE PARTNER ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE STRIVE PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AND AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SDH, QIN-QIO (IF YOUR QIN-QIO IS WORKING ON ACUTE CARE HAI), AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: A. ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE 4 HAIS; B. DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS C. SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES BARRIERS AND LESSONS LEARNED. 4. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE-LEVEL NHSN DATA TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS, INCLUDING CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), MRSA BACTEREMIA, CAUT, AND CLABSI. FOR THIS INITIATIVE, PRIORITY WILL BE PLACED ON CDI FOR TARGETING PURPOSES. METHODOLOGY FOR TARGETING WILL BE DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH CDC AND HRET. 5. RECRUIT AT LEAST 5 HOSPITALS BY 6/30/2017. 6. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS WITH ALL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS AND INTERVENE AS SOON AS CHALLENGES BECOME APPARENT. THESE ARE: A. EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS B. DATA REQUIREMENTS C. SUBMISSION OF PRE- AND POST IMPLEMENTATION PRACTICE CHANGE ASSESSMENT OF AT LEAST 90% OF ALL PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS BY THE DEADLINE SPECIFIED BY HRET; ICAR RESULTS MAY BE USED FOR THE PRE-IMPLEMENTATION INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL PRACTICE CHANGE ASSESSMENT. 7. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS; THIS APPLIES TO ALL UNITS, INCLUDING THOSE MAKING GOOD PROGRESS. 8. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON STATE-LEVEL MEETING FOR THE PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS PLANNED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE STATE PARTNERS AND TO BE ATTENDED BY THE STATE PARTNERS. 9. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISIT REPORT TO HRET. 10. COMPLETE A QUARTERLY QUESTIONNAIRE THAT ADDRESSES SHA CHECK-INS WITH HOSPITALS, MONITORING OF HOSPITAL PROGRESS AND HOW WELL ALL THE STATE PARTNERS ARE COORDINATING AND ALIGNING STATE-WIDE HAI PREVENTION AND ADDRESSING INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL GAPS 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT, QIN-QIOS AND/OR OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATING IN MONTHLY STATE PARTNER CALLS LED BY HRET TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED.

description: HE MACSQUANTÂ® ANALYZER 10 IS A 3-LASER, 8 COLOR, 10 PARAMETER FLOW CYTOMETER DESIGNED TO PHENOTYPICALLY CHARACTERIZE SAMPLES THAT ARE LABELED WITH FLUORESCENT DYES OR ANTIBODIES CONJUGATED TO FLUORESCENT MOLECULES. THE RELATIVELY SMALL FOOTPRINT OF THE UNIT, AND INTEGRATED COMPUTER, (24IN X 18IN X 20IN) IN COMPARISON TO OTHER COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE FLOW CYTOMETERS MAKES IT IDEALLY SUITED FOR BENCH TOP OPERATION WITHIN ANY LABORATORY, OR INSIDE A STANDARD CLASS II HOOD. ALTHOUGH CATEGORIZED IN THE Â€ŒBENCH-TOPÂ€? SEGMENT DUE TO ITS SIZE, THE GOLD STANDARD TECHNOLOGIES OF HIGH END ANALYZERS ARE INCLUDED IN THE MACSQUANT INSTRUMENT LINE, UNLIKE ANY OTHER CYTOMETER IN THIS SEGMENT. THE INSTRUMENT HAS A PRE-CONFIGURED OPTICAL BENCH CONSISTING OF THREE SPATIALLY SEPARATED LASERS (405 NM, 488 NM, 635 NM), RESULTING IN HIGHLY STABLE AND CONSISTENT LIGHT DETECTION. ALSO, THE MACSQUANT ANALYZER 10 HAS SEVERAL DESIGN FEATURES THAT PERMIT THE FULLY AUTOMATED PROCESSING OF CELL SAMPLES Â€“ FROM SAMPLE PREPARATION AND LABELING, THROUGH SAMPLE MIXING, UPTAKE TO FLUORESCENCE ANALYSIS, INCLUDING MAGNETIC PRE-ENRICHMENT FOR RARE CELLS PRIOR TO ANALYSIS. THE MACSQUANT ANALYZER 10 CAN BE EASILY FITTED WITH THE MACS MINISAMPLER TO PROVIDE HIGH FLEXIBLY FOR MULTISAMPLING FROM TUBES OR 96-WELL PLATE FORMATS. THE MACS MINISAMPLER IS A MOTORIZED SAMPLE RACK HOLDER THAT CAN HOLD CHILLABLE RACKS (4 DEGREES C) OF VARYING FORMATS TO MEET MANY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEEDS. FULLY AUTOMATED MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES, SUCH AS PMT CALIBRATION AND INSTRUMENT SHUTDOWN, ARE ALSO A DESIGN FEATURE OF THE INSTRUMENT. UNDER THE CONTROL OF THE MACSQUANTIFY SOFTWARE, THE FULLY AUTOMATED UPTAKE AND PROCESSING OF MULTIPLE SAMPLES IS POSSIBLE THUS PERMITTING THE USER A HANDS-FREE, HIGH-THROUGHPUT OPERATION. IN ADDITION, THE INSTRUMENT CAN BE MONITORED REMOTELY. AFTER SAMPLE UPTAKE, THE INSTRUMENT CAN ANALYZE FLUORESCENTLY-LABELED CELLS USING UP TO TEN OPTICAL PARAMETERS Â€“ EIGHT FLUORESCENCE AND TWO SCATTER CHANNELS. ALL CHANNELS UTILIZE PMTS FOR OPTIMAL SENSITIVITY, INCLUDING SCATTER PARAMETERS. WITH EVERY SAMPLE ACQUIRED, THE MACSQUANTÂ® ANALYZER 10 PROVIDES ABSOLUTE CELL COUNTS IN THE FORM OF CELLS/L OR CELLS/ML. THE MACSQUANTIFYÂ„¢ SOFTWARE CAN PERFORM ALL STANDARD FLOW CYTOMETRIC DATA ANALYSES AND VISUALIZATIONS, INCLUDING HISTOGRAMS, DOT PLOTS, DENSITY PLOTS, GATING, AND STATISTICAL VIEWS. DATA ARE ALSO AMENABLE TO DEEPER ANALYSIS IN TERMS OF AREA, HEIGHT, AND WIDTH. UPON ACQUISITION, DATA ARE AUTOMATICALLY STORED IN PREDESIGNATED DIRECTORIES FOR LATER ANALYSIS WITH AN INTUITIVE SYSTEM BACK-UP PROCESS. THE MACSQUANT ANALYZER 10 CAN ALSO PERFORM PRE-ENRICHMENT OF MAGNETICALLY LABELED CELLS BEFORE FLOW CYTOMETRIC ANALYSIS. THE MACSQUANT INSTRUMENTS ARE THE ONLY COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE FLOW CYTOMETERS TO OFFER A MAGNETIC, COLUMN-BASED CELL ENRICHMENT MODULE. THIS FEATURE IS BASED ON THE RENOWNED MACS TECHNOLOGY, UTILIZING THE MACSQUANT COLUMN AND MACS CELL ENRICHMENT UNIT. THE MACS CELL ENRICHMENT UNIT IS PARTICULARLY USEFUL FOR THE ANALYSIS OF RARE CELLS LABELED WITH MACS MICROBEADS. IN ONE PROGRAMMED STEP, THE RARE CELLS ARE ENRICHED AND THEN SENT TO THE FLOW CELL FOR DIRECT FLOW ANALYSIS. OPERATION OF THE INSTRUMENT IS EXTREMELY SIMPLE THROUGH THE USE OF THE THIN-FILM TRANSISTOR (TFT) COLOR TOUCHSCREEN AND INTUITIVE SCREEN MENUS BUILT INTO THE MACSQUANTIFY SOFTWARE. THE USER HAS THE OPTION OF PERFORMING PRE-PROGRAMMED ANALYSES USING THE MACS CONTROL APPLICATIONS IN THE EXPRESS MODE OR OF CUSTOMIZING SAMPLE ANALYSIS PROTOCOLS OR AUTOMATION USING THE CUSTOM MODE. ALL USER-DEFINED PROGRAMS CAN BE SAVED FOR FUTURE RECALL TO STREAMLINE THE DATA ACQUISITION PROCESS. DATA ANALYSIS USING A VARIETY OF DISPLAY OPTIONS AND FUNCTIONS CAN BE PERFORMED ON THE INSTRUMENT AND THE SOFTWARE HAS BEEN CONFIGURED TO BE USER-FRIENDLY WITH A HIGHLY FLEXIBLE FUNCTIONALITY.

description: COMMENT PERIOD SUPPORT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE STAFF TO CODE AND ORGANIZE COMMENTS. THE COMMENT PERIOD SUPPORT WILL BE COORDINATED BY MITRE AND WILL BE PERFORMED IN A WEB-BASED TOOL PROVIDED BY MITRE. MITRE WILL PROVIDE TRAINING FOR STAFF AND THE FIRST SEVERAL WEEKS OF THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE ARE EXPECTED TO BE SPENT ON TRAINING. STAFF ARE EXPECTED TO BE AVAILABLE 25-50% TIME FOR TRAINING DURING THE TRAINING PERIOD. TRAINING WILL INCLUDE THE PROCESSES REQUIRED TO DO PUBLIC COMMENT WORK, AND THE TOOLS USED TO CODE AND ORGANIZE COMMENTS. PART OF THE TRAINING WILL BE CENTERED ON THE TAXONOMY MITRE HAS DEVELOPED. THE TAXONOMY IS A CODING SCHEMA BASED UPON THE STRUCTURE OF THE NPRM. ONCE COMMENTS ARE RECEIVED, MITRE WILL LOAD THEM IN THE WEB-BASED TOOL. THE CONTRACTOR STAFF SHALL ANALYZE AND PARSE EACH COMMENT INTO INDIVIDUAL THOUGHTS/THEME USING THE APPROVED TAXONOMY. EACH INDIVIDUAL THOUGHT IS STORED SEPARATELY IN THE TOOL WITH A LINK TO THE ORIGINAL COMMENT. THE CONTRACTOR STAFF SHALL THEN CATEGORIZE (CODE) THESE INDIVIDUAL THOUGHTS USING THE TAXONOMY. EACH STAFF MEMBER WILL BE ASSIGNED A NUMBER OF SUBMISSIONS TO ANALYZE, CODE, AND SUMMARIZE IN THE WEB-BASED TOOL. EACH SUBMISSION MAY RANGE ANYWHERE FROM A PARAGRAPH TO MANY PAGES. THE CONTRACTOR WILL ALSO PROVIDE STAFF TO PERFORM TASKING COORDINATION AND A QUALITY REVIEW AND WILL ASSIST IN PROVIDING ADDITIONAL TRAINING OR REMEDIATION IF QUALITY PROBLEMS ARE FOUND. THE QUALITY REVIEW WILL INCLUDE AN ASSESSMENT OF INTERCODER RELIABILITY. THE TASK COORDINATOR WILL WORK WITH THE MITRE PROJECT LEADER TO ASSIGN SUBMISSIONS FOR PROCESSING. TASK 2 ASSUMPTIONS: Â€¢ A MAXIMUM OF 250 COMMENTS ARE EXPECTED. Â€¢ THE EXACT TIMELINE FOR THIS EFFORT WILL BE DEFINED ONCE THE NPRM IS RELEASED. TRAINING WILL BEGIN NO LATER THAN 30 DAYS BEFORE THE CLOSE OF THE COMMENT PERIOD. Â€¢ ALL COMMENT PROCESSING MUST BE COMPLETED WITHIN TWO (2) WEEKS OF THE CLOSURE OF THE COMMENT PERIOD. Â€¢ TRAINING, INCLUDING TIME FOR READING THE RULE, WILL BE FOUR (4) WEEKS AT 25-50% OF STAFF TIME. Â€¢ MITRE WILL DO ALL STATUS REPORTING FROM THE WEB-BASED TOOL. TASK 3: COMMENT SUMMARIZATION (OPTIONAL) UPON EXERCISE OF THIS OPTIONAL TASK, THE CONTRACTOR STAFF SHALL SUMMARIZE EACH COMMENT IN ADDITION TO IDENTIFYING ADDITIONAL THOUGHTS, EXTRACTING EACH COMPONENT OF THE COMMENT IN THE TOOL, AND CODING THE THOUGHT. THE SUMMARIZATION SHALL DESCRIBE THE COMMENT IN GENERAL TERMS AND SHALL ADHERE TO THE STYLE GUIDE PROVIDED BY MITRE. THE CONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE A CONSISTENT QUALITY REVIEW OF THE ACCURACY OF THE SUMMARIZATION AND WILL PROVIDE ADDITIONAL TRAINING OR REMEDIATION IF QUALITY PROBLEMS ARE FOUND.

JOHNSON AND HARRIS HAVE A COHORT OF PATIENTS ADMITTED TO THE MICU OR SICU FROM JANUARY 1 , 2001 TO PRESENT. PATIENTS IN THE MICU AND SICU HAVE ADMISSION, WEEKLY AND DISCHARGE PERI-RECTAL CULTURES PERFORMED AS PART OF A VANCOMYCIN-RESISTANT ENTEROCOCCI INFECTION PREVENTION ACTIVE SURVEILLANCE PROGRAM. THESE SWABS ARE FROZEN IN 1 5% GLYCEROL AND FROZEN AT - 80Â°C FOLLOWING A FREEZING METHOD THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND PUBLISHED AS PART OF A PREVIOUSLY FUNDED NIH R01. THE COHORT CONSISTS OF > 23,000 PATIENTS, >50,000 FROZEN PERI-RECTAL SAMPLES, AND > 5,000 FROZEN SPUTUM SAMPLES. THE ACCESSION NUMBERS OF THE SWABS CAN BE LINKED TO THE UMMC CLINICAL DATA REPOSITORY (CDR); A RELATIONAL DATABASE WITH MICROBIOLOGY, PHARMACY, ADMISSION DISCHARGE TRANSFER, PATHOLOGY AND RADIOLOGY DATA. DRS. JOHNSON AND HARRIS WILL PROVIDE THE PATIENT SPECIMENS TO YALE UNIVERSITY AS WELL AS LINKING PATIENT METADATA FOR THE FINAL ANALYSIS. DR. JOHNSON WILL SERVE AS THE CO-PRIMARY INVESTIGATOR FOR THIS AWARD, PROVIDING INPUT IN STUDY DESIGN AND ANALYSIS, AS WELL AS PREPARATION OF RESULTING MANUSCRIPTS. DR. HARRIS WILL SERVE AS A CO-INVESTIGATOR PROVIDING DATA EXTRACTION AND ANALYSIS.

description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO 3/8/17 2. CREATE A STATE PARTNER ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE STRIVE PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AND AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SDH, QIN-QIO (IF YOUR QIN-QIO IS WORKING ON ACUTE CARE HAI), AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: A. ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE 4 HAIS; B. DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS C. SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES BARRIERS AND LESSONS LEARNED. 4. COMPLETE A QUARTERLY QUESTIONNAIRES THAT ADDRESSES SHA CHECK-INS WITH HOSPITALS MONITORING OF HOSPITAL PROGRESS AND HOW WELL ALL THE STATE PARTNERS ARE COORDINATING AND ALIGNING STATE-WIDE HAI PREVENTION AND ADDRESSING INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL GAPS. 5. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE-LEVEL NHSN DATA TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS, INCLUDING CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), AND A HIGH BURDEN OF METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MSRA) BACTEREMIA, CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI) AND/OR CENTRAL LINE-ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTION (CLASBI). 6. RECRUIT AT LEAST 4 HOSPITALS AND, AT A MINIMUM, 60% OF TARGETED HOSPITALS AND/OR LONG-TERM ACUTE CARE HOSPITALS (LTACHS) INTO THE PROJECT BY 4/10/17. 7. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS WITH ALL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS AND INTERVENE AS SOON AS CHALLENGES BECOME APPARENT. 8. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS; THIS APPLIES TO ALL UNITS, INCLUDING THOSE MAKING GOOD PROGRESS. 9. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON STATE-LEVEL MEETING FOR THE PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS PLANNED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE STATE PARTNERS AND TO BE ATTENDED BY THE STATE PARTNERS. 10. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISIT REPORT TO HRET. 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT, QIN-QIOS AND/OR OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATING IN MONTHLY STATE PARTNER CALLS LED BY HRET TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED.

WHAT CHANGES WOULD BRING STABILITY TO THE RISK POOL, PROMOTE CONTINUOUS COVERAGE, INCREASE THE NUMBER OF YOUNGER AND HEALTHIER CONSUMERS PURCHASING PLANS, REDUCE UNCERTAINTY AND VOLATILITY, AND ENCOURAGE UNINSURED INDIVIDUALS TO BUY COVERAGE? 3. description: QUALITY PAYMENT PROGRAM RESOURCE CENTER FOR THE MIDWEST THE QUALITY PAYMENT PROGRAM RESOURCE CENTER FOR THE MIDWEST (QPP RESOURCE CENTER) IS DEDICATED TO PROVIDING INNOVATIVE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO CLINICIAN PRACTICES IN RURAL, HPSA, AND UNDERSERVED AREAS, TOGETHER EXPANDING THE VALUE, IMPACT, AND REACH OF EACH PARTNER ORGANIZATION. THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER THROUGH THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL WILL SUPPORT CLINICIANS IN THEIR TRANSITION FROM FEE-FOR-SERVICE TO AN ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODEL (APM) OR MERIT BASED INCENTIVE PAYMENT SYSTEM (MIPS). THE FOLLOWING SCOPE OF WORK PERTAINS TO THE CMS APPROVED QPP-SURS CONTRACT, ADDITIONAL QPP SUPPORT MAY BE OFFERED BY SUBCONTRACTORS TO PROVIDERS ON A FEE-FOR-SERVICE OR COMMERCIAL BASIS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER COMMERCIAL SERVICES POLICY. ADDITIONALLY, USE OF THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM AND MIPSCASTTM WITH PROVIDERS THAT ARE NOT ENROLLED IN QPP-SURS SUPPORT MAY BE ALLOWED SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE COMMERCIAL SERVICES POLICY. IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROPOSAL APPROVED BY CMS FOR THE QPP-SURS INITIATIVE, MICHIGAN PEER REVIEW ORGANIZATION (MPRO) WILL SUPPORT ALTARUM INSTITUTE (ALTARUM) AS FOLLOWS. WORKING UNDER THE DIRECTION OF ALTARUMÂ€™S QPP RESOURCE CENTER PROJECT MANAGER, MPRO WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES AND ACTIVITIES: TASK 1: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT TASK 2: OUTREACH ACTIVITIES TASK 3: RESOURCE CENTER CONTENT TASK 4: CLINICAL PRACTICE IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES TASK 5: LEARNING ACTION NETWORKS (LAN)

description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO 5/17/17 PRIOR TO THE START OF THE PROJECT FOR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 2. CREATE A STATE PARTNER ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS (STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATION, STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS) THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE STRIVE PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AN AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. THE PLAN SHOULD ADDRESS CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), CENTRAL LINE-ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTION (CLASBI), CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI) AND METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MSRA) BACTEREMIA PREVENTION. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SDH, QIN-QIO (IF YOUR QIN-QIO IS WORKING ON ACUTE HAI), AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN IN-PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: A. ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE 4 HAIS B. DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS C. SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES, BARRIERS AN LESSONS LEARNED 4. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE-LEVEL NHSN DATA TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS, INCLUDING CDI, MRSA BACTEREMIA, CAUTI AND CLASBI. FOR THIS INITIATIVE, PRIORITY WILL BE PLACED ON CDI FOR TARGETING PURPOSES. METHODOLOGY FOR TARGETING WILL BE DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH CDC AND HRET. 5. RECRUIT AT LEAST 5 HOSPITAL BY 5/26/17. 6. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS WITH ALL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS AND INTERVENE AS SOON AS CHALLENGES BECOME APPARENT. 7. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS; THIS APPLIES TO ALL UNITS, INCLUDING THOSE MAKING GOOD PROGRESS. 8. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON STATE-LEVEL FOR THE PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS PLANNED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE STATE PARTNERS AND TO BE ATTENDED BY STATE PARTNERS. 9. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISIT REPORT TO HRET. 10. COMPLETE A QUARTERLY QUESTIONNAIRE THAT ADDRESSES SHA CHECK-INS WITH HOSPITALS, MONITORING OF HOSPITAL PROGRESS AND HOW WELL ALL THE STATE PARTNERS ARE COORDINATING AD ALIGNING STATE-WIDE HAI PREVENTION AN ADDRESSING INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL GAPS. 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATING IN MONTHLY STATE PARTNER CALLS LED BY HRET TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED.

description: THE CONTRACTOR WILL WORK WITH MITRE TO HELP THE FDA OHR ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING: Â€¢ AN ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN THAT CAPTURES FDA'S CURRENT HUMAN CAPITAL MANAGEMENT AND COMPENSATION PROCESS, RELATIVE TO HIRING AND RETAINING SCIENTIFIC, TECHNICAL, OR PROFESSIONAL POSITIONS THAT SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT, REVIEW, AND REGULATION OF MEDICAL PRODUCTS. AN ANALYSIS OF HIRING SOLUTIONS AND PAY PRACTICES FOR COMPARABLE PRIVATE, PUBLIC, ACADEMIC, COMPARABLE FEDERAL SCIENTIFIC AGENCIES AND OTHER FEDERAL AGENCIES. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE IDENTIFYING RELEVANT BENCHMARKS AND CORRELATING THOSE TO EXISTING AND FUTURE FDA POSITIONS AND PAY SYSTEMS. Â€¢ FDA WILL HAVE AN INFORMED GOVERNANCE AND DECISION-MAKING BOARD, TO DELIBERATE AND MAKE DECISIONS ON THE WAY FORWARD FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE HIRING AUTHORITIES UNDER THE CURES ACT. (THE MAJORITY OF THE WORK DONE HERE WILL BE PERFORMED BY MITRE, BUT MITRE WILL RELY ON PRM FOR ADVISORY SUPPORT TO INCLUDE SHARING LESSONS LEARNED FROM OTHER EFFORTS, UNDERSTANDING PRECONDITIONS FOR SUCCESS, ARTICULATING THE ADVANTAGES AND DISADVANTAGES OF CERTAIN APPROACHES, AND HELPING MITRE/FDA UNDERSTAND WHAT TO EXPECT AS THE APS IS CONSTRUCTED AND ROLLED OUT.) Â€¢ FDA WILL HAVE AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN THAT WILL ENABLE THE FDA TO ESTABLISH AN HCM AND PAY SOLUTIONS THAT ALIGN WITH THE 21ST CENTURY CURES LEGISLATION.

description: OBJECTIVES 1.1 PRIMARY OBJECTIVES Â€“ THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY WILL BE TO DEMONSTRATE THAT ONCE DAILY, TOPICAL APPLICATION OF A GEL FORMULATION OF 4-OHT TO THE BREASTS RESULTS IN A REDUCTION IN THE KI-67 LABELING INDEX OF DCIS LESIONS THAT IS NOT INFERIOR TO THAT SEEN WITH ORAL TAM 20 MG DAILY FOR 26Â±2 WEEKS, WHEN COMPARING THE BASE-LINE DIAGNOSTIC CORE BIOPSY TO THE THERAPEUTIC SURGICAL EXCISION SAMPLE. 1.2 SECONDARY OBJECTIVES Â€“ 1. TO COMPARE POST-THERAPY CHANGES IN THE ONCOTYPE DCIS-SCORE BETWEEN ARMS (THIS IS A VALIDATED RT-PCR ASSAY FOR KI67, STK15, SURVIVIN, CYCLIN B1, MYBL2, PR, GSTM1). 2. description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO 3/8/17 PRIOR TO THE START OF THE PROJECT FOR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 2. CREATE A STATE PARTNER ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS (STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATION, STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS) THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE STRIVE PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AN AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. THE PLAN SHOULD ADDRESS CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), CENTRAL LINE-ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTION (CLASBI), CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI) AND METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MSRA) BACTEREMIA PREVENTION. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SDH, QIN-QIO (IF YOUR QIN-QIO IS WORKING ON ACUTE HAI), AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN IN-PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: A. ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE 4 HAIS B. DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS C. SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES, BARRIERS AN LESSONS LEARNED 4. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE-LEVEL NHSN DATA TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS, INCLUDING CDI, MRSA BACTEREMIA, CAUTI AND CLASBI. FOR THIS INITIATIVE, PRIORITY WILL BE PLACED ON CDI FOR TARGETING PURPOSES. METHODOLOGY FOR TARGETING WILL BE DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH CDC AND HRET. 5. RECRUIT AT LEAST 5 HOSPITAL BY 4/1/17. 6. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS WITH ALL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS AND INTERVENE AS SOON AS CHALLENGES BECOME APPARENT. 7. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS; THIS APPLIES TO ALL UNITS, INCLUDING THOSE MAKING GOOD PROGRESS. 8. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON STATE-LEVEL FOR THE PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS PLANNED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE STATE PARTNERS AND TO BE ATTENDED BY STATE PARTNERS. 9. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISIT REPORT TO HRET. 10. COMPLETE A QUARTERLY QUESTIONNAIRE THAT ADDRESSES SHA CHECK-INS WITH HOSPITALS, MONITORING OF HOSPITAL PROGRESS AND HOW WELL ALL THE STATE PARTNERS ARE COORDINATING AD ALIGNING STATE-WIDE HAI PREVENTION AN ADDRESSING INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL GAPS. 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATING IN MONTHLY STATE PARTNER CALLS LED BY HRET TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED.

description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO, 3/8/17 PRIOR TO START OF THE PROJECT FOR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 2 CREATE A STATE PARTNER ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS (STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATIONS, STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS) THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE STRIVE PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AND AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. THE PLAN SHOULD ADDRESS CDI, CLABSI, CAUTI AND MRSA BACTEREMIA PREVENTION. HRET WILL PROVIDE A TEMPLATE FOR STATE TRIADS TO USE. IDEALLY, THE STATE TRIAD PLAN WILL BE COMPLETED PRIOR TO THE START OF THE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING FOR PARTICIPATING FACILITIES, OR NO LATER THAN MONTH TWO OF THE 12 MONTH HOSPITAL INTERVENTION. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SDH,QIN-QIO (IF YOUR QIN-QIO IS WORKING ON ACUTE CARE HAI) AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN IN-PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE FOUR HAIS; DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS; AND SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES, BARRIERS AND LESSONS LEARNED. 4. COMPLETE A QUARTERLY QUESTIONNAIRE THAT ADDRESSES SHA CHECK-INS WITH HOSPITALS, MONITORING OF HOSPITAL PROGRESS AND HOW WELL ALL THE STATE PARTNERS ARE COORDINATING AND ALIGNING STATE-WIDE HAI PREVENTION AD ADDRESSING INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL GAPS. 5. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE LEVEL NHSN DATE TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS INCLUDING CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA) BACTEREMIA, CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI), AND CENTRAL-LINE ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTION (CLASBI). 6. RECRUIT AT LEAST 5 HOSPITALS, AND AT A MINIMUM 60% TARGETED HOSPITALS AND/OR LONG-TERM HOSPITALS INTO THE PROJECT BY 4/1/2017. 7. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS WITH ALL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS AND INTERVENE AS SOON AS CHALLENGES BECOME APPARENT. 8. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS. 9. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON STATE LEVEL MEETING FOR THE PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS PLANNED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE STATE PARTNERS AND TO BE ATTENDED BY STATE PARTNERS. 10. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISITS REPORTS TO HRET. 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATE IN MONTHLY STATE PARTNER CALLS LED BY HRET TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED.

description: THE MITRE CORPORATION (MITRE) REQUIRES ASSISTANCE IN THE DELIVERY OF FEDERALLY FUNDED RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CENTER (FFRDC) SERVICES TO THE CENTERS FOR MEDICARE &MEDICAID SERVICES (CMS) FOR A PROJECT TO ESTABLISH AND SUPPORT THE HEALTH CARE PAYMENT LEARNING AND ACTION NETWORK (LAN). THE OBJECTIVE OF THE LAN IS TO ALIGN CMS AND PRIVATE PAYERS IN MOVING PAYMENT FROM TRADITIONAL FEE FOR SERVICE (FFS) METHODS TO FFS-LINKED TO QUALITY, ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS, AND POPULATION-BASED PAYMENT TO ACHIEVE THE STATED GOALS OF DELIVERY SYSTEM REFORM. BY SHARING INFORMATION ABOUT SUCCESSFUL MODELS AND ENCOURAGING PRIVATE ENTITIES TO SHARE THEIR BEST PRACTICES, THE CENTER FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID INNOVATION (CMMI) INTENDS TO MINIMIZE BARRIERS TO ADOPTION OF ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS. SPECIFICALLY, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ONE (1) GUIDING COMMITTEE CO-CHAIR AS DEFINED IN THE FOLLOWING TASK DESCRIPTION. WORKING CLOSELY WITH ANOTHER CO-CHAIR, THIS INDIVIDUAL WILL PROVIDE LEADERSHIP TO THE LAN GUIDING COMMITTEE. THE GUIDING COMMITTEE WILL PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE SUCCESS OF THE NETWORK. THE PURPOSE OF THE LAN GUIDING COMMITTEE IS TO GUIDE THE LAN TOWARD ACHIEVING ITS GOALS. IT IS THE PRIMARY COLLABORATIVE BODY OF THE LAN, SERVING IN AN ADVISORY ROLE TO CAMH. THE GUIDING COMMITTEE WILL PROVIDE EXECUTIVE OVERSIGHT WITH THE FOLLOWING RESPONSIBILITIES: A) COLLABORATE WITH CAMH TO DEVELOP A STRATEGY FOR ACHIEVING THE GOALS OF THE LAN. THE LAN IS INTENDED TO ACCELERATE A CHANGE PROCESS (PAYMENT REFORM) THAT EXTENDS BEYOND THE OPERATING TERM OF THE GUIDING COMMITTEE. THEREFORE, THE COMMITTEE WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING NEAR-TERM RESULTS (ACTIONS THAT CAN BE DELIVERED WITHIN THE TERM OF THE GUIDING COMMITTEE) AND LONGER TERM STRATEGY THAT COULD INFORM FUTURE OUTCOMES. B) IDENTIFY AND PRIORITIZE ACTION COLLABORATIVES, WORK GROUPS, AND AFFINITY GROUPS; COLLABORATE WITH CAMH TO SELECT MEMBERS; PROVIDE ON-GOING GUIDANCE AND DIRECTION TO THE GROUPS; AND REVIEW AND ENDORSE THE WORK PRODUCTS AND OTHER OUTPUTS. C) DEVELOP AND OVERSEE THE EXECUTION OF PLANS TO ACTIVELY ENGAGE STAKEHOLDERS, SHARE AND DISSEMINATE RESULTS, ACCELERATE LEARNING, AND ENCOURAGE STAKEHOLDERS TO TAKE ACTION IN ALIGNMENT WITH LAN GOALS.

FOR A PROJECT TO ESTABLISH AND SUPPORT THE HEALTH CARE PAYMENT LEARNING AND ACTION NETWORK (Â€ŒLANÂ€?). THE OBJECTIVE OF THE LAN IS TO ALIGN CMS AND PRIVATE PAYERS IN MOVING PAYMENT FROM TRADITIONAL FEE FOR SERVICE (Â€ŒFFSÂ€?) METHODS TO FFS-LINKED TO QUALITY, ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS, AND POPULATION-BASED PAYMENT TO ACHIEVE THE STATED GOALS OF DELIVERY SYSTEM REFORM. BY SHARING INFORMATION ABOUT SUCCESSFUL MODELS AND ENCOURAGING PRIVATE ENTITIES TO SHARE THEIR BEST PRACTICES, THE CENTER FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID INNOVATION (Â€ŒCMMIÂ€?) INTENDS TO MINIMIZE BARRIERS TO ADOPTION OF ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS. THE LAN HAS DEFINED PROGRESS IN TERMS OF REBALANCING HEALTH CARE SPENDING FLOWING THROUGH FOUR CATEGORIES OF HEALTH CARE PAYMENTS, WHICH ARE: Â€¢ CATEGORY 1: FFS WITH NO LINK TO QUALITY AND VALUE Â€¢ CATEGORY 2: FFS LINKED TO QUALITY AND VALUE Â€¢ CATEGORY 3: APMS BUILT ON FFS ARCHITECTURE Â€¢ CATEGORY 4: POPULATION-BASED PAYMENT TO HELP MOVE THE FIELD TOWARD CATEGORIES 3 AND 4, THE LAN INDEPENDENTLY CONVENES ACTION COLLABORATIVES (ACS) COMPRISED OF STAKEHOLDERS THAT HAVE PRIORITIZED A COMMITMENT TO ADOPTING ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODELS. THE ACTION COLLABORATIVES ARE FOCUSED ON SPECIFIC ACTIONABLE GOALS Â€“ SUCH AS IMPLEMENTATION OF THE LANÂ€™S MATERNITY EPISODE PAYMENT MODEL RECOMMENDATIONS IN SELECT REGIONS ACROSS THE U.S., AND PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR PRIMARY CARE PAYMENT TRANSFORMATION WITH AN INITIAL FOCUS ON THE CMS INNOVATION CENTERÂ€™S (CMMI) COMPREHENSIVE PRIMARY CARE PLUS (CPC+) MODEL. A FUTURE ACTION COLLABORATIVE WILL BE FOCUSED ON ACCOUNTABLE CARE ORGANIZATIONS (ACOS.) THIS SOW IS WRITTEN TO BE GENERALIZABLE TO ANY ACTION COLLABORATIVE, REGARDLESS OF SUBJECT MATTER. MITRE IS THE INDEPENDENT CONVENER OF LAN ACS, BUT OPERATES IN CLOSE PARTNERSHIP WITH CMMI AND WITH GUIDANCE FROM THE LAN GUIDING COMMITTEE. THE AIM IS TO ENSURE THAT THE VIRTUAL EVENTS ORCHESTRATED FOR AC PARTICIPANTS CREATE VALUE FOR THEM, AND MOVE THEM CLOSER TO ACTION BY MEETING THEIR APM IMPLEMENTATION GOALS AND THE AGREED-UPON, MEASURABLE GOALS.

BACKGROUND SECRETARY PRICE HAS LAID OUT THE GOAL OF CREATING A PATIENT-CENTERED HEALTH CARE SYSTEM THAT ADHERES TO THE KEY PRINCIPLES OF AFFORDABILITY, ACCESSIBILITY, QUALITY, INNOVATION, AND EMPOWERMENT. IN ADDITION TO A RIGOROUS REVIEW OF REGULATIONS IMPACT ON PATIENTS, THE ANALYSIS ALSO NEEDS TO CONSIDER AND BE GUIDED BY THE FOLLOWING PRIMARY GOALS: 1. ENHANCE AFFORDABILITYÂ€”PURSUE POLICIES THAT REDUCE PREMIUMS AND PROVIDE A RANGE OF AFFORDABLE, QUALITY OPTIONS TO CONSUMERS. 4. description: 1. ATTEND ONE IN PERSON MEETING IN CHICAGO, 3/8/2017 PRIOR TO START OF THE PROJECT FOR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 2 CREATE A STATE TRIAD ACTION PLAN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OTHER STATE PARTNERS (STATE HOSPITAL ASSOCIATIONS, STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENTS AND QIN-QIO) THAT EVALUATES CURRENT HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS AND ADDRESS HOW THE STRIVE PROGRAM CAN COMPLEMENT, ADDRESS GAPS THAT MAY EXIST AND AVOID DUPLICATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES. THE PLAN SHOULD ADDRESS CDI, CLABSI, CAUTI AND BACTEREMIA PREVENTION. IDEALLY, THE STATE TRIAD PLAN WILL BE COMPLETED PRIOR TO THE START OF THE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING FOR PARTICIPATING FACILITIES, OR NO LATER THAN MONTH TWO OF THE 12 MONTH HOSPITAL INTERVENTION. 3. PARTICIPATE WITH SHD,QIN-QIO (IF YOUR QIN-QIO IS WORKING ON ACUTE CARE HAI) AND OTHER STATE PARTNERS AT LEAST QUARTERLY IN IN-PERSON OR VIRTUAL MEETINGS TO: ADDRESS PROGRESS ON THE FOUR HAIS; DISCUSS WAYS TO COORDINATE AND ALIGN HAI PREVENTION EFFORTS; AND SHARE SUCCESSES, BEST PRACTICES, BARRIERS AND LESSONS LEARNED. 4. COMPLETE A QUARTERLY QUESTIONNAIRE THAT ADDRESSES SHA CHECK-INS WITH HOSPITALS, MONITORING OF HOSPITAL PROGRESS AND HOW WELL ALL THE STATE PARTNERS ARE COORDINATING AND ALIGNING STATE-WIDE HAI PREVENTION AD ADDRESSING INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL GAPS. 5. TARGET HOSPITALS USING STATE LEVEL NHSN DATE TO IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH HIGH BURDEN OF HAIS INCLUDING CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI), METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA) BACTEREMIA, CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI), AND CENTRAL-LINE ASSOCIATED BLOODSTREAM INFECTION (CLASBI). 6. RECRUIT AT LEAST 5 HOSPITALS, AND AT A MINIMUM 60% TARGETED HOSPITALS AND/OR LONG-TERM HOSPITALS INTO THE PROJECT BY 4/1/2017. 7. PROMOTE AND MONITOR COMPLIANCE OF PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS. 8. CHECK IN MONTHLY WITH HOSPITALS. 9. HOLD AT LEAST ONE IN-PERSON SATE LEVEL MEETING FOR THE PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS PLANNED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE STATE PARTNERS AND TO BE ATTENDED BY STATE PARTNERS. 10. COORDINATE AND ATTEND SITE VISITS TO 50% OF YOUR PARTICIPATING HOSPITALS AND PROVIDE SHORT SITE VISITS REPORTS TO HRET. 11. REPORT QUARTERLY ON THE COLLABORATIVE HAI PREVENTION ACTIVITIES YOUR ASSOCIATION ENGAGES IN WITH YOUR SHD, QIN-QIOS AND/OR OTHER RELEVANT STATE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. 12. PARTICIPATE IN MONTHLY STATE PARTNER CALLS LED BY HRET TO DISCUSS PROJECT CHALLENGES AND SUCCESSES AND TO PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK TO HRET ON WAYS THE PROJECT MAY BE REFINED AND ENHANCED.

description: PRIMARY OBJECTIVES TO ASSESS HPV VACCINE-TYPE-SPECIFIC SEROCONVERSION RATES AT 12-MONTHS POST-TRANSPLANTATION AMONG FEMALE LIVING DONOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS WHO RECEIVE ≥ 1 DOSES OF THE GARDASIL 9 HPV VACCINE ≥ 30 DAYS PRIOR TO TRANSPLANTATION. 1.2 SECONDARY OBJECTIVES TO EVALUATE THE FOLLOWING IN FEMALE LIVING DONOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS WHO RECEIVE ≥ 1 DOSES OF THE GARDASIL 9 HPV VACCINE ≥ 30 DAYS PRIOR TO TRANSPLANTATION: 1) HPV VACCINE-TYPE-SPECIFIC SEROCONVERSION RATES AT 12-MONTHS POST-TRANSPLANTATION STRATIFIED BY: A) NUMBER OF DOSES (1 VS. 2) OF THE VACCINE GIVEN PRE-TRANSPLANT; B) TIME ELAPSED BETWEEN LAST VACCINE DOSE AND THE TRANSPLANT PROCEDURE; C) VARIATIONS IN DOSING AND TYPES OF POST-TRANSPLANT IMMUNOSUPPRESSANT MEDICATIONS; D) DIFFERENCES IN HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGEN (HLA) HISTOCOMPATIBILITY BETWEEN DONOR AND RECIPIENT. 2) PERSISTENCE AND STABILITY OF HPV VACCINE-TYPE-SPECIFIC GEOMETRIC MEAN TITERS (GMT) AT 6 AND 12-MONTHS POSTTRANSPLANTATION, AND RISE IN HPV VACCINE-TYPE-SPECIFIC GMT AT THE 13-MONTHS POST-TRANSPLANTATION VISIT (1-MONTH AFTER THE THIRD/BOOSTER VACCINE DOSE). 3) VACCINE SAFETY PROFILE AND ALLOGRAFT REJECTION/OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS STRATIFIED BY NUMBER OF VACCINE DOSES AND TIME BETWEEN THE LAST VACCINE DOSE AND THE TRANSPLANT PROCEDURE. 4) HPV DETECTION IN SAMPLES FROM THE CERVIX/VAGINA, AND ORAL CAVITY AT BASELINE (PRE-VACCINATION) AND AT 6- AND 12- MONTHS POST-VACCINATION, OVERALL AND BY NUMBER OF VACCINE DOSES (1 VS. 2) AND TIME ELAPSED BETWEEN THE LAST VACCINE DOSE AND THE TRANSPLANT PROCEDURE.

description: WHI ARIZONA 2015-2020 THE ARIZONA SITE WILL BE ACTIVELY PARTICIPATING IN WHI 2015-2020 AS BOTH AN ANCILLARY SITE FOR OUTCOMES COLLECTION AND AS A SATELLITE RESEARCH CENTER. ARIZONA IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO ENHANCE THE IMPACT OF WHI 2015-2020 PARTICULARLY SINCE THIS SITE IS BOTH A WHI MINORITY RECRUITMENT SITE AND A BONE DENSITY SITE. AS DESCRIBED BELOW WE HAVE RECRUITED OUR STRONGEST STAFF AND FACULTY TO SUPPORT THIS EFFORT FOR THE NEXT FIVE YEARS. IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT INVOLVEMENT OF THE ARIZONA SITE WILL SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACT OUTCOMES ASCERTAINMENT, JUNIOR INVESTIGATOR TRAINING AND AS A RESULT WHI SCIENCE. OUTCOMES ASCERTAINMENT THE ARIZONA SITE WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE COLLECTION OF OUTCOMES FOR THE HT AND MINORITY WHI COHORTS AS WELL AS THE FOLLOW-UP ON THE SELF-REPORT COHORT FOR CONSENTS AND F33/33D NON-RESPONDERS UNDER THE WHI CONTRACT. WE ESTIMATE COLLECTION OF APPROXIMATELY 300 OUTCOME CASES PER YEAR WITH AN ESTIMATED INCREASE IN OUTCOMES OF BETWEEN 50-75 CASES ANNUALLY, PARTICULARLY IN THE AREA OF CANCER AND MORTALITY. TO PROMOTE EFFICIENT AND THOROUGH OUTCOMES ASCERTAINMENT WE HAVE ENGAGED DR. CYNTHIA THOMSON, PI OF WHI AZ SITE FOR THE PAST 12 YEARS, AND AMELIA LOBOS, OUTCOMES COORDINATOR FOR AZ FOR OVER 16 YEARS, AND WITH THE STUDY FOR OVER 18 YEARS. AZ WHI SCIENCE A MAJOR FOCUS OF WHI 2015-2020 IS THE EXPANSION OF THE IMPACT OF WHI THROUGH NOVEL, HIGH-IMPACT SCIENCE. THE GOAL IS TO TEST HYPOTHESES THAT CAN BE TRANSLATED INTO IMPROVED CLINICAL CARE FOR AGING WOMEN. TO THIS END THE AZ SITE HAS SELECTED STRONG SENIOR LEADERSHIP WHO IS EXPERIENCED IN WHI AND PARTNERED THESE INDIVIDUAL SCIENTISTS WITH EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS AT ALL LEVELS TO PROMOTE NEW IDEAS, EXPERTISE AND EXPANDED PUBLICATION AND PRESENTATION OF WHI SCIENCE. LISTED BELOW IS A BRIEF SUMMARY OF EACH INVESTIGATOR AND THE EXPERTISE THEY BRING TO THE TABLE. AZ PLANS TO ACTIVELY EXPAND ON ITS SCIENTIFIC NICHE IN THE AREA OF BODY COMPOSITION, BONE HEALTH, OBESITY AND DISEASE RISK.

description: TWO FEATHERS NATIVE AMERICAN FAMILY SERVICES WILL 1) MEET WITH CALIFORNIA TRIBES AND STATE AND COUNTY LEADERS IN THE HUMBOLDT/DEL NORTE COUNTIES TO EXPLORE THE VALUE AND POTENTIAL OF LINKING EFFORTS TO BUILD ON CULTURAL TRADITIONS IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF YOUTH RESILIENCY AND SELF-ESTEEM WITHIN SEVERAL LOCAL COMMUNITIES. THIS AREA OF FOCUS WILL BUILD ON LINKAGES ACROSS COMMUNITIES TO SUPPORT COORDINATED EFFORTS ACROSS TRIBAL AND GEOGRAPHIC DIFFERENCES, BRINGING TOGETHER MODELS OF SUPPORT FOR LOCAL YOUNG PEOPLE. SPECIFIC ATTENTION WILL BE DEVOTED TO SUPPORT COORDINATION BETWEEN THE COMMUNITIES OF WEITCHPEC AND HOOPA IN THEIR YOUTH PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. 2) MEET WITH CALIFORNIA TRIBES TO COORDINATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICE SYSTEMS EFFORTS BETWEEN TRIBES, IHS, AND COUNTY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ACT (MHSA) FUNDS AND PROGRAMS, TO STRENGTHEN THE WEB OF SUPPORTS AND SERVICES FOR YOUTH PEOPLE AND THEIR FAMILIES ACROSS THE REGION, WHILE DECREASING DUPLICATION OF SERVICES. 3) MEET WITH TRIBES ACROSS THE STATE THAT HAVE RECENTLY FACED ISSUES OF YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH CHALLENGES, INCLUDING SUICIDE, IN AN EFFORT TO LEARN FROM LOCAL EXPERIENCES OF EFFECTIVE RESPONSES TO THESE SITUATIONS AND CONSIDER THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STATEWIDE COORDINATED EFFORT TO DEVELOP SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACROSS TRIBES WITHIN THE STATE. 4) PRESENT ON LESSONS LEARNED FROM THE COMMUNITIES WHO HAVE RECENTLY FACED ISSUES OF YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH CHALLENGES, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, AND CULTURAL RESILIENCY. 5) DEVELOP A CULTURALLY-BASED BEHAVIORAL WELLNESS CURRICULUM FOR TRIBES ACROSS THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. A CRITICAL ELEMENT OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THE GENERATION OF LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST FLAVIVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS TARGETS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN THE CROWE LAB. THE MABS FOR RVFV THAT WILL BE MAPPED IN THIS CONTRACT ARE BEING ISOLATED AS PART OF ONGOING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION OF TED ROSS, PHD OF VGTI IN FLORIDA. THE DENV-4 HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF SUBJECTS IMMUNIZED WITH A LIVE-ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE THAT HAS BEEN USED SUCCESSFULLY IN HUMAN TRIALS IN COLLABORATION WITH A. DURBIN AND S. WHITEHEAD. THE JEV HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED A LIVE-ATTENUATED OR INACTIVATED JEV VACCINE IN COLLABORATION WITH S. THOMAS AND FROM CONVALESCENT PBMCS FROM SUBJECTS INFECTED WITH JEV IN THE FIELD IN COLLABORATION WITH C. SIMMONS. FOR THIS CONTRACT, THE CROWE LABORATORY WILL SUPPLY HIGHLY PURIFIED IGG PREPARATIONS OF HUMAN MABS WITH KNOWN FUNCTIONAL ACTIVITY. THE TEXT BELOW DESCRIBES A PLAN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE MABS. SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. FOR SOME OF THE VIRUSES TARGETED FOR HUMAN MAB PRODUCTION (JEV, RVFV), SOME OF THE SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS OF OTHERWISE HEALTHY DONORS WHO SUFFERED ACUTE AND CONFIRMED VIRAL INFECTION. THIS WILL BE COORDINATED BY DR. CROWE AND COLLABORATORS (RVFV: DR. MARIETJIE VENTER, UNIVERSITY OF PRETORIA; JEV: DR. CAMERON SIMMONS, OXFORD UNIVERSITY CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, VIETNAM). CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM SEVERAL IMMUNE DONORS WILL BE TRANSFERRED IN A COMPLETELY DE-IDENTIFIED FASHION TO THE VANDERBILT VACCINE CENTER IN THE U.S. FOR THESE STUDIES. IMMUNIZATION. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS. MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION. SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE. HUMANS: DR. CROWE WILL BE CREATING HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. THERE WILL BE NO IDENTIFIERS LINKED TO THE DATA BEING TRANSFERRED TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY. PLEASE NOTE: ANY CHANGES TO THIS PROPOSAL THAT MAY ALTER ITS "NON-HUMAN"STATUS SHOULD BE PRESENTED TO THE IRB FOR APPROVAL PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CHANGES. IN ACCORDANCE WITH IRB POLICY III.J, AMENDMENTS WILL BE ACCEPTED UP TO ONE YEAR FROM THE DATE OF APPROVAL. IF SUCH CHANGES ARE REQUESTED BEYOND THIS TIME FRAME, SUBMISSION OF A NEW PROPOSAL IS REQUIRED. ANIMALS: NONE ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.

VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A MINIMUM OF TEN MURINE ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS OR GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN SPOROZOITE OR MEROZOITE ASSAYS PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE AND SPOROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE EVALUATED BY DR. ADAMS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. DR. ADAMS WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. ALTERNATE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES. IN ADDITION TO THE CORE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DRS. FREMONT, GROSS AND TOLIA, OUR COLLABORATIVE TEAM HAS EXPERTISE WITH A VARIETY OF COMPLEMENTARY METHODS THAT CAN BE USED AS NEEDED. B CELL EPITOPES MAY BE MAPPED BY PHAGE DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY, A TECHNIQUE SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED BY DR. ADAMS. C. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.   B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. KING WILL GENERATE HUMAN ANTI-MALARIA MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. KING HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA MEROZOITES. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY DR. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. FOCUS WILL CONTINUE ON PREPARING, INITIATING, IMPLEMENTING, AND SUSTAINING VALUE STREAM IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES WITH AN EMPHASIS ON DELIVERING MEASURABLE OUTCOMES THAT WILL SUPPORT THE AGENCY IN THE EFFORT TO TRANSITION FROM A LEARNING ORGANIZATION TO A MATURE TARGET STATE WHERE PRACTICING CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT, INCLUDING STRATEGIC THINKING, IS PART OF DAY-TO-DAY PLANNING AND OPERATIONS.
