description: FEDERAL FUNDING FOR MEDICAID INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) TAKES UP A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE OVERALL FEDERAL SPENDING ON MEDICAID. THE CURRENT PROCESS FOR STATES TO REQUEST ENHANCED FUNDING (90/10 FOR DDI AND 75/25 FOR O&M) IS COSTLY, BURDENSOME, AND MAY NOT RESULT IN SYSTEMS THAT EFFECTUATE DESIRED STATE OUTCOMES OR MEET FEDERAL POLICY REQUIREMENTS. THE DATA AND SYSTEMS GROUP (DSG) WITHIN THE CENTER FOR MEDICAID AND CHIP SERVICES (CMCS) AT THE CENTERS FOR MEDICARE AND MEDICAID SERVICES (CMS) IS REIMAGINING THE PROCESS USED TO APPROVE AND FUND STATE MEDICAID TECHNOLOGY REQUESTS AND TESTING NEW APPROACHES TO BETTER ACHIEVE DESIRED BUSINESS OUTCOMES, ENSURING COMPLIANCE WITH FEDERAL REQUIREMENTS, AND IMPROVING THE EXPERIENCE FOR ALL END-USERS. DSG IS LOOKING TO TRANSFORM ITS ROLE, FUNCTION, AND PROCESSES SO THAT STATES AND CMS ACHIEVE PROGRAM AND BUSINESS GOALS EFFICIENTLY AND EFFECTIVELY AND THAT STATES GET A CONSISTENT, TRANSPARENT, AND TIMELY EXPERIENCE FROM CMS. AMONG THE STATE-FACING ACTIVITIES BEING EXPLORED TO ACHIEVE THESE OBJECTIVES ARE TRANSITIONING TO OUTCOMES-BASED FUNDING REQUESTS AND RFPS, OUTCOMES-BASED ASSESSMENTS OF TECHNOLOGY IMPLEMENTATION AND ONGOING OPERATIONS, STATE ENGAGEMENTS BASED ON QUANTITATIVE RISK ASSESSMENT FINDINGS, AND ENHANCED TOOLS TO MONITOR STATE FUNDING AND PROGRAM OPERATIONS. DSG IS CURRENTLY OPERATING AN EXPERIMENT PROGRAM WHERE IMPROVEMENT IDEAS FOR BOTH SMA, DSG AND CMS REGIONAL ANALYST THAT SUPPORT SMAS ARE EVALUATED, APPROVED, TRACKED AND IMPLEMENTED. DSG WILL BE UNDERTAKING RAPID EXPERIMENTS TO IDENTIFY BEST WAYS TO ACHIEVE ITS OBJECTIVES, WHICH WILL INVOLVE THE CAREFUL TESTING OF NEW APPROACHES AND ANALYSIS OF DATA PRIOR TO SCALING. THE EXPERIMENT PROGRAM IS SEEKING ADDITIONAL SUPPORT FOR ONE KEY EXPERIMENT THAT IS BEING CONSIDERED. SCOPE THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE EXPECTED TO CONSULT WITH MITRE ON THE PROPOSED APD PLANNING EXPERIMENT. SPECIFICALLY, THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE ASKED TO WORK WITH MITRE ON HOW TO INCORPORATE AN OUTCOMES-BASED APPROACH INTO THE GOALS MATRIX FOR STATE PLANNING AND FUNDING REQUESTS PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED BY THE CONTRACTOR FOR CMS. THE CONTRACTOR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO IDENTIFY NEW EXPERIMENT OPPORTUNITIES THAT LEVERAGE THE CONTRACTORÂ€™S CURRENT AND PAST STATE ENGAGEMENT INITIATIVES. THE CONTRACTOR WILL ADHERE TO THE MITRE DEVELOPED AND DGS APPROVE EXPERIMENT PROTOCOL.

description: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ADVISORY SUPPORT TO PROVIDE CRITICAL CONTEXT AND INSIGHTS IN SUPPORT OF MITREÂ€™S ROLE IN ASSESSING PRICE TRANSPARENCY LANDSCAPES IN THE HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY AND NON-HEALTHCARE INDUSTRIES, UNDERSTANDING KEY DRIVERS OF CONSUMER ENGAGEMENT ON HEALTH CARE DECISIONS AND DEVELOPING HIGH IMPACT INITIATIVES TO ADVANCE HEALTHCARE PRICE TRANSPARENCY EFFORTS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF THE CURRENT LANDSCAPE OF THE HEALTHCARE PRICE TRANSPARENCY INITIATIVES (WHAT HAS BEEN TRIED, WHAT HAS WORKED, WHAT HAS NOT WORKED, WHAT HAS FAILED, PRICE DISPERSIONS, AND INCENTIVES/DISINCENTIVES). TO ACCOMPLISH THIS, THE CONTRACTOR WILL CONDUCT THE ACTIVITIES OUTLINED IN TASKS 2-6, BELOW. THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE INVOLVED IN PROVIDING SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE, TO INCLUDE BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PRICE TRANSPARENCY STUDIES IN HEALTHCARE AND OTHER INDUSTRIES, IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES, AND DECISION-MAKING SUPPORT TOOLS NEEDS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH MITRE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT DELIVER ANY DOCUMENTS TO THE SPONSOR DIRECTLY AND SHALL NOT ENGAGE WITH THE SPONSOR DIRECTLY, WITHOUT MITRE KNOWLEDGE AND CONSENT, FOR ANY REASON. TASK 2: OVERVIEW OF HEALTHCARE PRICE TRANSPARENCY LANDSCAPE THE CONTRACTOR WILL CONDUCT 10-15 MARKET EXPERT INTERVIEWS, CODIFY SOLUTIONS DEPLOYED BY PRIVATE SECTOR PAYORS AND PROVIDERS IN THE COMMERCIAL INDIVIDUAL MARKET. TO THE DEGREE THERE IS INFORMATION TO BE GAINED FROM THE MEDICARE MARKET, THE CONTRACTOR MAY INCLUDE INFORMATION FROM THOSE ORGANIZATIONS AS WELL. IN ADDITION, THE CONTRACTOR WILL INCORPORATE LESSONS LEARNED FROM STAKEHOLDER SESSIONS ALREADY CONDUCTED BY EXISTING PROJECT (TO BE PROVIDED BY MTIRE) TO DEVELOP AN INVENTORY OF CURRENT, EXISTING SOLUTIONS EMPLOYED IN THE MARKETPLACE TODAY. TASK 3: RESEARCH CONSUMER DECISION POINTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT RESEARCH ON THE CURRENT PRICE DECISION PROCESS FLOW ACROSS A SERIES OF CARE CONDITION AND SETTINGS, TO BE IDENTIFIED, INCLUDING KEY DECISION POINTS AND CURRENTLY AVAILABLE PRICING DATA WITH A FOCUS ON CONSUMER PRICING DECISION JOURNEYS IN MEDICARE AND INDIVIDUAL MARKET SEGMENTS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL CONDUCT STAKEHOLDER ACTION SIMULATIONS USING THE CONTRACTORS SIMULATION METHODOLOGY TO DETERMINE WHAT INFORMATION DRIVES A CONSUMER TO MAKE THE DECISIONS IN QUESTION. AS A RESULT OF THIS ACTIVITY, THE CONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE THE INFORMATION AVAILABLE TO FACILITATE THE DECISION, WHAT ENTITY POSSESSES THE INFORMATION, AND HOW THAT INFORMATION IS COMMUNICATED TO THE PATIENT. TASK 4: INITIATIVES TO ADVANCE PRICE TRANSPARENCY IN HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP A PRIORITIZED SET OF HIGH IMPACT INITIATIVES TO ADVANCE PRICE TRANSPARENCY INCLUDING QUALITATIVE IMPLICATIONS, POTENTIAL RISKS AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATION. THE CONTRACTOR WILL ALSO INDICATE THESE SELECT INITIATIVES MAY BE TAILORED TO PRIORITIZED COVERAGE SEGMENT(S) (E.G., MARKETPLACE). AS PART OF THIS PROCESS, THE CONTRACTOR WILL DETERMINE OPTIONS AND ASSOCIATED QUALITATIVE IMPLICATIONS FOR DEFINING Â€ŒPRICEÂ€? (E.G., PROVIDER-DETERMINED CHARGES, MEDICARE RATES, NET NEGOTIATED PRICES, ETC.), BASED ON INTERVIEWS WITH 2-3 GENERAL COUNSELS ACROSS THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT AND CONVENE AN IDEATION SESSION(S) WITH HEALTHCARE EXPERTS TO IDENTIFY THE KEY LEVERS CMS COULD USE TO ADVANCE PRICE TRANSPARENCY, INCLUDING OPPORTUNITIES FOR HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS TO BUNDLE AND PUBLISH PRICING FOR SERVICES THE CONTRACTOR WILL INTERVIEW 3-5 PRIVATE SECTOR PAYORS AND PROVIDERS TO IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES FOR CMS TO FACILITATE PRIVATE SECTOR PRICE TRANSPARENCY EFFORTS (E.G., ADDRESS REGULATORY BARRIERS) AND DEVELOP HIGH-LEVEL QUALITATIVE IMPLICATIONS OF EACH INITIATIVE FOR STAKEHOLDERS (E.G., HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS AND CONSUMERS) THE RESULT WILL BE A PRIORITIZED SET OF STRATEGIC INITIATIVES AGAINST A CMS-DETERMINED FRAMEWORK, BASED ON AVAILABLE EVIDENCE (E.G., RELATIVE QUANTITATIVE IMPACT BASED ON AVAILABLE EVIDENCE, TIME TO IMPLEMENT, OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINTS, AND POTENTIAL STAKEHOLDER RISKS)

description: OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND CMS LEADERSHIP IS PURSUING OPPORTUNITIES TO INCORPORATE PRICE TRANSPARENCY DATA AND TOOLS TO INFORM DECISION-MAKING IN THE MEDICARE PROGRAM. BENEFICIARIES, FEE FOR SERVICE (FFS) PRACTITIONERS, AND THE MEDICARE PROGRAM AS PAYER COULD BENEFIT FROM REDUCED SPENDING DERIVED FROM COMPARISON SHOPPING FOR SERVICES AND PROVIDERS. HOWEVER, PRIOR TO DECIDING HOW TO IMPLEMENT PRICE TRANSPARENCY INTERVENTIONS OR TOOLS FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES, THE ADMINISTRATION SHOULD CAREFULLY CONSIDER WHICH SERVICES, PROVIDERS, AND BENEFICIARIES IN THE MEDICARE PROGRAM COULD BENEFIT FROM MORE TRANSPARENT PRICES. EVEN IN THE COMMERCIAL SECTOR, THERE ARE SERVICES, SUCH AS EMERGENCY CARE, FOR WHICH A CONSUMER CANNOT BE EXPECTED TO SHOP PRIOR TO RECEIVING THE SERVICE. MEDICARE HAS SEVERAL ADDITIONAL BARRIERS THAT FURTHER REDUCE THE INCENTIVES OF BENEFICIARIES AND PRACTITIONERS TO COMPARISON SHOP FOR CARE: Â€¢ MEDICARE SETS PRICES, THUS, THERE IS LITTLE PRICE COMPETITION AMONG PROVIDERS Â€¢ MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES ARE LARGELY PROTECTED FROM COST SHARING SINCE MOST BENEFICIARIES HAVE SUPPLEMENTAL COVERAGE THROUGH THEIR EMPLOYER, MEDIGAP, OR MEDICAID Â€¢ LEGAL LIMITATIONS ON MEDICAREÂ€™S ABILITY TO INCENTIVIZE OR REQUIRE ACTIVITIES RELATED TO IMPROVING TRANSPARENCY IN PRICING INFORMATION WHILE THESE LIMITATIONS MAY PREVENT PRICE TRANSPARENCY INITIATIVES FROM HAVING A BROAD IMPACT ON SPENDING, THERE ARE SOME MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES, FFS PRACTITIONERS, AND SERVICES AND PROVIDERS WHERE INCREASED TRANSPARENCY COULD HAVE AN IMPACT ON SPENDING. MITRE WOULD LIKE TO ENGAGE RAND TO: 1.) DESCRIBE BENEFICIARY SUBPOPULATIONS, FFS PRACTITIONERS, AND SERVICES THAT MIGHT BE CANDIDATES FOR A PRICE TRANSPARENCY INITIATIVE, AND 2.) TO THE EXTENT POSSIBLE, QUANTIFY THE NUMBER OF BENEFICIARIES, FFS PRACTITIONERS, AND SERVICES ASSOCIATED WITH A SUBSET OF HIGH-PRIORITY CANDIDATES SUCH AS BENEFICIARIES WITHOUT SUPPLEMENTAL COVERAGE. SCOPE THE CONTRACTOR WILL PRODUCE A SHORT SCOPING MEMO DESCRIBING BENEFICIARY SUBPOPULATIONS, FFS PRACTITIONERS, AND SERVICES THAT ARE PROMISING CANDIDATES FOR PRICE TRANSPARENCY TOOLS OR INTERVENTIONS. THE REPORT WILL INCLUDE A RATIONALE FOR SELECTION, CONTEXT, EXPECTED IMPACTS, AND UNANTICIPATED CONSEQUENCES FOR EACH BENEFICIARY, FFS PRACTITIONER, OR SERVICE CATEGORY. THE REPORT WILL DESCRIBE HOW EACH CATEGORY COULD BE IDENTIFIED AND STUDIED USING DATA SUCH AS CLAIMS DATA ACCESSED THROUGH CMSÂ€™S INTEGRATED DATA REPOSITORY (IDR).

description: ELECTRONIC PRESCRIBING (ERX) IS A PRESCRIBER'S ABILITY TO ELECTRONICALLY SEND AN ACCURATE, ERROR-FREE AND UNDERSTANDABLE PRESCRIPTION DIRECTLY TO A PHARMACY FROM THE POINT-OF-CARE. IT IS AN IMPORTANT ELEMENT IN IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF PATIENT CARE. THE INCLUSION OF ELECTRONIC PRESCRIBING IN THE MEDICARE MODERNIZATION ACT (MMA) OF 2003 GAVE MOMENTUM TO THE MOVEMENT, AND THE JULY 2006 INSTITUTE OF MEDICINE REPORT ON THE ROLE OF E-PRESCRIBING IN REDUCING MEDICATION ERRORS RECEIVED WIDESPREAD PUBLICITY, HELPING TO BUILD AWARENESS OF ERXÂ€™S ROLE IN ENHANCING PATIENT SAFETY. ADOPTING THE STANDARDS TO FACILITATE ERX WAS ONE OF THE KEY ACTION ITEMS IN EXPEDITING THE ADOPTION OF ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS AND BUILDING A NATIONAL ELECTRONIC HEALTH INFORMATION INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE UNITED STATES. AS PART OF ITS PLAN TO ESTABLISH AN IMPROPER PAYMENT OUTREACH AND EDUCATION IN THE MEDICARE FFS PROGRAM, THE CENTER FOR PROGRAM INTEGRITY (CPI) IS SPEARHEADING THE DME ERX INITIATIVE, WITH THE PURPOSE OF OBTAINING A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT FOR DME ERX, AND ENCOURAGING INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS TO USE DATA INTEROPERABILITY STANDARDS AND DOCUMENTATION LOOKUP SERVICES BEING DEVELOPED THROUGH THE HEALTH LEVEL SEVEN (HL7) DA VINCI PROJECT. UNDER THIS INITIATIVE, CENTERS FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID SERVICES (CMS) WILL WORK WITH THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) INDUSTRY, AS WELL AS OTHER HEALTH INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) VENDORS, TO ENCOURAGE THE USE OF DME ERX.

description: SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND CAPACITY BUILDING THROUGH THE FOLLOWING PRODUCTS AND SERVICES: Â€¢ ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT AND END-STATE VISIONING Â€“ ENGAGING STATE LEADERSHIP AND PROJECT MANAGERS TO CREATE A SHARED UNDERSTANDING OF THE BUSINESS DRIVERS BEHIND THE TRANSFORMATION, FOLLOWED BY INTERVIEWING A BROAD CROSS SECTION OF STAKEHOLDERS, RANGING FROM SENIOR LEADERSHIP TO THE PEOPLE DOING THE DAY-TO-DAY WORK. THE INTERVIEWS HELP IDENTIFY WHAT ISNÂ€™T WORKING AS WELL AS IT COULD, AND WHERE AGILE WILL HELP IT IMPROVE. AN ASSESSMENT IS DEVELOPED TO INCLUDE A RECOMMENDATION ON STRUCTURAL CHANGES REQUIRED TO HELP THE STATE MEET ITS GOALS, ALONG WITH PORTFOLIO, PRODUCT, AND DELIVERY TEAM STRUCTURE. A WORKING STRUCTURE WOULD BE DRAFTED TO INCLUDE A GOVERNANCE MODEL, FRAMEWORK, METRICS FOR MEASURING PROGRESS ON THE ASSESSMENT AND AGAINST BUSINESS OUTCOMES, AND A MEANS TO INSTRUMENT THE PROCESS WITH TOOLING. Â€¢ COACHING STRATEGY - COACHING INVOLVES WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE TEAMS, IN ADDITION TO THE STANDARD SERIES OF TRAINING AND WORKSHOPS. COACHES CONDUCT A COMPETENCY ASSESSMENT TO BASELINE ADOPTION IN KEY COMPETENCY AREAS, WORK WITH THE TEAMS UNTIL THEY ARE AT A POINT OF SUSTAINABILITY, AND CORRELATE TEAM PERFORMANCE TO ORGANIZATION OUTCOMES IN THE WEEKLY (OR MONTHLY) STATUS REPORTS. Â€¢ TRANSFORMATION ROADMAP - THE TRANSFORMATION PLAN WILL DEFINE WHAT GROUPS OF TEAMS WILL MOVE TO AGILE, WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO WORK IN A MORE TRADITIONAL WATERFALL METHOD, WHAT ORDER THEYÂ€™LL DEPLOY, AND WHAT THE STEPS WILL LOOK LIKE AS THEY MAKE THEIR WAY ALONG THE TRANSFORMATION JOURNEY. Â€¢ CHANGE MANAGEMENT PLAN - WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE GOVERNING BODY LEADING THE TRANSITION, GOALS AND OBJECTIVES ARE SET, A 90-DAY ROLLING PLAN IS CREATED AND MAINTAINED Â€“ WITH WEEKLY STATUS REPORTS AND REVIEWS OCCURRING AT 30-DAY INTERVALS. A COMMUNICATION PLAN IS DEFINED AND EXECUTED, INCLUDING ESTABLISHING OFFICE HOURS, CONDUCTING LUNCH AND LEARNS, OR ANYTHING NECESSARY TO KEEP PEOPLE INFORMED AND CREATE SAFETY AND AWARENESS AROUND THE AGILE TRANSFORMATION INITIATIVE. Â€¢ AGILE ORGANIZATIONAL PILOT AND ENTERPRISE ROLLOUT Â€“ LEVERAGING THE DEFINED END-STATE, APPROPRIATE TEAMS (DELIVERY, PROGRAM, PORTFOLIO GOVERNANCE) ARE FORMED; GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORKS ARE ESTABLISHED, INCLUDING METRICS USED TO BASELINE PERFORMANCE OF THE NEW TEAMS AND MEASURE AND EVALUATE PERFORMANCE OVER TIME; AN EVALUATION AND REVIEW OF AGILE TOOLS MAY BE PERFORMED IF REQUESTED. THIS SHOULD PROVIDE A SOLID PERFORMANCE BASELINE CENTERED ON THE METRICS, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT. Â€¢ ADDITIONAL SERVICES INCLUDE: O AGILE BOOT CAMP O AGILE REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT COURSE O AGILE GOVERNANCE AND METRICS WORKSHOP O CONTINUED COACHING SERVICES O SPRINT PLANNING WORKSHOPS

IN ADDITION TO DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN PLANNED WORKING SESSIONS WITH CMS PERSONNEL AND OTHER MEMBERS OF THE MITRE DELIVERY TEAM TO ASSIST IN CREATING IMPACTFUL AND ACCURATE MATERIALS TO COMMUNICATE STRATEGY AND METHODOLOGY, AND TO CREATE TEMPLATES WHICH MAY BE USED BY THE TEAM FOR ONGOING ACTIVITIES AND COMMUNICATIONS. WORKING SESSIONS MAY BE BY PHONE OR IN PERSON AS NEEDED. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT ONGOING AND ITERATIVE CREATION OF DESIGNS THAT, AT A HIGH LEVEL, ARTICULATE THE RECOMMENDED DESIGN PATTERNS TO BEST REPRESENT THE INTEROPERABILITY INITIATIVE STRATEGY AND METHODOLOGY. THESE CONCEPT DESIGNS SHALL BE DEVELOPED AT THE DIRECTION OF THE MITRE PROJECT LEADER OR DESIGNEE. AFTER MITRE HAS REVIEWED THE CONCEPT DESIGNS, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL GENERATE MOCKUPS/DRAFTS, DELIVERED IN THE FORMAT DEFINED BY THE MITRE, VIA EMAIL TO THE MITRE PROJECT LEADER OR DESIGNEE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL: 1) WORK AS AN INTEGRATED TEAM WITH MITRE, ALLIANCE PARTNERS, AND SUBCONTRACTORS. 2) PARTICIPATE IN WORK SESSIONS AND OTHER MEETINGS TO REVIEW RECOMMENDATIONS AND DEVELOP PRESENTATION MATERIALS, INCLUDING UPDATES TO THE CMS INTEROPERABILITY ROAD MAP. 3) DESIGN A COMMUNICATIONS AND BRANDING STRATEGY RELATED TO THE MYHEALTHEDATA INITIATIVE AND THE INTEROPERABILITY PROPOSED RULE. 4) AT THE DISCRETION OF THE PROJECT LEADER, ASSIST IN DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNICATIONS MATERIALS, GRAPHICS DESIGNS, BRANDING, AND COORDINATING WITH CMS ON AD HOC BASIS. 5) ENSURE ALL MATERIALS DELIVERED UNDER CONTRACT MEET FEDERAL GOVERNMENT 508 COMPLIANCE STANDARDS, CONSISTENT WITH CMS STYLE GUIDES. 6) ENSURE ALL MATERIALS AND METHODS USED ARE FREE FROM LICENSING/FEE PAYMENTS, COPYRIGHTS, AND TRADEMARKS.

description: SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND CAPACITY BUILDING THROUGH THE FOLLOWING PRODUCTS AND SERVICES: Â€¢ ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT AND END-STATE VISIONING Â€“ ENGAGING STATE LEADERSHIP AND PROJECT MANAGERS TO CREATE A SHARED UNDERSTANDING OF THE BUSINESS DRIVERS BEHIND THE TRANSFORMATION, FOLLOWED BY INTERVIEWING A BROAD CROSS SECTION OF STAKEHOLDERS, RANGING FROM SENIOR LEADERSHIP TO THE PEOPLE DOING THE DAY-TO-DAY WORK. THE INTERVIEWS HELP IDENTIFY WHAT ISNÂ€™T WORKING AS WELL AS IT COULD, AND WHERE AGILE WILL HELP IT IMPROVE. AN ASSESSMENT IS DEVELOPED TO INCLUDE A RECOMMENDATION ON STRUCTURAL CHANGES REQUIRED TO HELP THE STATE MEET ITS GOALS, ALONG WITH PORTFOLIO, PRODUCT, AND DELIVERY TEAM STRUCTURE. A WORKING STRUCTURE WOULD BE DRAFTED TO INCLUDE A GOVERNANCE MODEL, FRAMEWORK, METRICS FOR MEASURING PROGRESS ON THE ASSESSMENT AND AGAINST BUSINESS OUTCOMES, AND A MEANS TO INSTRUMENT THE PROCESS WITH TOOLING. Â€¢ COACHING STRATEGY - COACHING INVOLVES WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE TEAMS, IN ADDITION TO THE STANDARD SERIES OF TRAINING AND WORKSHOPS. COACHES CONDUCT A COMPETENCY ASSESSMENT TO BASELINE ADOPTION IN KEY COMPETENCY AREAS, WORK WITH THE TEAMS UNTIL THEY ARE AT A POINT OF SUSTAINABILITY, AND CORRELATE TEAM PERFORMANCE TO ORGANIZATION OUTCOMES IN THE WEEKLY (OR MONTHLY) STATUS REPORTS. Â€¢ TRANSFORMATION ROADMAP - THE TRANSFORMATION PLAN WILL DEFINE WHAT GROUPS OF TEAMS WILL MOVE TO AGILE, WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO WORK IN A MORE TRADITIONAL WATERFALL METHOD, WHAT ORDER THEYÂ€™LL DEPLOY, AND WHAT THE STEPS WILL LOOK LIKE AS THEY MAKE THEIR WAY ALONG THE TRANSFORMATION JOURNEY. Â€¢ CHANGE MANAGEMENT PLAN - WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE GOVERNING BODY LEADING THE TRANSITION, GOALS AND OBJECTIVES ARE SET, A 90-DAY ROLLING PLAN IS CREATED AND MAINTAINED Â€“ WITH WEEKLY STATUS REPORTS AND REVIEWS OCCURRING AT 30-DAY INTERVALS. A COMMUNICATION PLAN IS DEFINED AND EXECUTED, INCLUDING ESTABLISHING OFFICE HOURS, CONDUCTING LUNCH AND LEARNS, OR ANYTHING NECESSARY TO KEEP PEOPLE INFORMED AND CREATE SAFETY AND AWARENESS AROUND THE AGILE TRANSFORMATION INITIATIVE. Â€¢ AGILE ORGANIZATIONAL PILOT AND ENTERPRISE ROLLOUT Â€“ LEVERAGING THE DEFINED END-STATE, APPROPRIATE TEAMS (DELIVERY, PROGRAM, PORTFOLIO GOVERNANCE) ARE FORMED; GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORKS ARE ESTABLISHED, INCLUDING METRICS USED TO BASELINE PERFORMANCE OF THE NEW TEAMS AND MEASURE AND EVALUATE PERFORMANCE OVER TIME; AN EVALUATION AND REVIEW OF AGILE TOOLS MAY BE PERFORMED IF REQUESTED. THIS SHOULD PROVIDE A SOLID PERFORMANCE BASELINE CENTERED ON THE METRICS, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT. Â€¢ ADDITIONAL SERVICES INCLUDE: O AGILE BOOT CAMP O AGILE REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT COURSE O AGILE GOVERNANCE AND METRICS WORKSHOP O CONTINUED COACHING SERVICES O SPRINT PLANNING WORKSHOPS

description: MCS MEASURE IDENTIFICATION AND DEFINITION WORKING WITH AND UNDER THE DIRECTION OF MITRE, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL IDENTIFY EXISTING QUALITY MEASURES DEVELOPED FROM THE MDS AND OASIS BASED ON DATA ELEMENTS AVAILABLE IN THE MDS AND OASIS MOST APPROPRIATE FOR POSSIBLE INCLUSION IN THE MEDICAID CORE SETS BASED ON CMCS POLICY PRIORITIES (IMPROVING CARE FOR VULNERABLE POPULATIONS, FOCUSING ON OUTCOMES) AND CORE SETS TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS (I.E. DATA MUST BE REPORTABLE AT THE STATE-LEVEL FOR JUST THE MEDICAID BENEFICIARY POPULATIONS, AND ABLE TO BE AGGREGATED UP TO A NATIONAL LEVEL.) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PARTNER WITH MITRE AND CMCS TO IDENTIFY MEASURES DRAWN FROM THE MDS AND OASIS SETS BEST SUITED FOR MEDICAID. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DETERMINE, IN CONJUNCTION WITH MITRE AND CMCS AND IN IN CONSULTATION WITH CCSQ/DCPAC, A SET OF PROPOSED MEASURED FOR INCLUSION IN THE MCS AND DETERMINE IF IT IS POSSIBLE TO CALCULATE THESE PROPOSED MEASURES, AS WELL AS TRACK PERFORMANCE ON THESE MEASURES LONGITUDINALLY AT THE STATE LEVEL FOR TWO YEARS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CALCULATE THE MEASURES FOR STATES IN WHICH THE DATA IS DETERMINED TO BE RELIABLE AND COMPLETE. FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT OF USING MDS/OASIS DATA FOR MCS MEASURES THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS TASK IS TO ASSESS WHETHER AND IF SO HOW THE MINIMUM DATA SET (MDS) AND OUTCOME AND ASSESSMENT INFORMATION SET (OASIS) DATA CAN BE USED TO CREATE MEASURES FOR THE CMCS MEDICAID CORE SETS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH MITRE TO DETERMINE THE TECHNICAL, DATA QUALITY FEASIBILITY AND POTENTIAL LIMITATIONS OF USING THE MDS AND OASIS DATA FOR CREATING MCS QUALITY MEASURES FOR EACH STATE WITH A MINIMUM OF TWO YEARS OF DATA. SUB-TASK 3.1: TECHNICAL FEASIBILITY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH MITRE TO DETERMINE THE MDS/OASIS DATA ELEMENTS NEEDED FOR THE CALCULATION OF QUALITY MEASURES AND ASSESS THE TECHNICAL VIABILITY OF USING THESE DATA ELEMENTS FOR THE CALCULATION OF QUALITY MEASURES. SOME OF THE FEASIBILITY FACTORS TO ASSESS THE USABILITY OF THE DATA ELEMENTS INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: Â€¢ GRANULARITY OF DATA Â€“ DETERMINE IF THE NEEDED DATA IS AVAILABLE AT THE RIGHT GRANULARITY LEVEL E.G. MEDICAID BENEFICIARY POPULATIONS AT THE STATE-LEVEL THAT CAN AGGREGATE UP TO A NATIONAL LEVEL OR AT THE PLAN, PROVIDER, FACILITY LEVEL Â€¢ TIMELINESS OF DATA Â€“ DETERMINE IF THE TIMELINESS OF THE DATA AND UPDATE FREQUENCY IS ADEQUATE FOR QUALITY MEASURES CALCULATION/REPORTING Â€¢ TIMEFRAME Â€“ DETERMINE THE FEASIBILITY OF PULLING DATA FOR MEASURES DRAWN FROM MDS AND OASIS THAT ALLOWS FOR A LONGITUDINAL VIEW AT THE STATE LEVEL (I.E. THE ABILITY TO PULL MEASURE DATA FOR A GIVEN STATE YEAR OVER YEAR) Â€¢ DATA ACCESS Â€“ DETERMINE THE LEVEL OF TECHNICAL CHALLENGE TO ACCESS AND COMPLEXITY TO PREPARE THE NEEDED DATA ELEMENTS FOR QUALITY MEASURE CALCULATION SUB-TASK 3.2: DATA QUALITY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH MITRE TO DOCUMENT THE INFORMATION FLOW, ENTITIES THAT PERFORM THE REVIEW AND VALIDATION FUNCTIONS AS WELL AND ACTIONS (OR BUSINESS RULES) TAKEN THAT COULD HAVE IMPACT TO THE QUALITY OF THE SURVEY DATA/INFORMATION. IDENTIFY THE SYSTEMS AND ORGANIZATIONAL (E.G. STATE SURVEY AND CERTIFICATION AGENCIES) FUNCTIONS THAT EXTRACT, TRANSFORM AND LOAD (ETL) THE OASIS ASSESSMENT SUBMISSIONS AND MDS DATA AS WELL AS METHODS AND ALGORITHMS USED TO CALCULATE MEASURES. TOGETHER WITH MITRE, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HELP DETERMINE THE COMPLETENESS AND ACCURACY OF THE DATA BEING CONSIDERED AS DATA SOURCE FOR MCS QUALITY MEASURES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PROVIDE INSIGHTS AND POSSIBLE OPTIONS TO IMPROVE DATA QUALITY IF/WHERE APPLICABLE. THE APPROACH TO DETERMINE THE LEVEL OF DATA QUALITY ACCEPTABILITY SHOULD FOCUS ON IDENTIFYING AND ADDRESSING SOLVABLE ISSUES TO IMPROVE THE DATA IN QUESTION TO AN ACCEPTABLE LEVEL FOR THE NATURE OF THE WORK BEFORE DISQUALIFYING THE USE OF THE DATA SOURCES, INCLUDING IDENTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL MISSING DATA ELEMENTS THAT MAY IMPACT POSSIBLE INTEGRATION INTO THE CMCS MEDICAID CORE SETS.

description: IN THIS STUDY, WE WILL RANDOMIZE 30 PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH RECURRENT PANCREATITIS WHO ARE UNDERGOING TREATMENT AT THE CEDARS-SINAI MEDICAL CENTER (CSMC) OR KAISER PERMANENTE LOS ANGELES MEDICAL CENTER (KPMC) TO SIMVASTATIN OR PLACEBO (20 IN THE SIMVASTATIN ARM, 10 IN THE CONTROL). ASSUMING THAT ~20% OF THE STUDY PARTICIPANTS DROP-OUT, WE EXPECT TO HAVE DATA ON A FINAL SAMPLE OF 24 MEN AND WOMEN (16 SIMVASTATIN, 8 CONTROL) COMPLETING THE 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UP PERIOD. CLINICAL AND RESEARCH MEASUREMENTS WILL BE TAKEN AT BASELINE (STUDY VISIT 1), MONTH 3 (STUDY VISIT 2), AND MONTH 6 (STUDY VISIT 3). THREE AND 6 MONTHS WERE CHOSEN, GIVEN THAT PATIENTS HAVE VARIABLE RECOVERY TIMES IN THE ORDER OF MONTHS AFTER AN ACUTE PANCREATITIS EVENT [46]. THEREFORE, THE REPEATED MEASURES AT 3 AND 6 MONTHS WILL BE ESSENTIAL FOR DETERMINING THE TRAJECTORY OF CHANGE IN THE CLINICAL AND RESEARCH MEASUREMENTS DURING THE RECOVERY PERIOD. PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED FOR ACUTE OR CHRONIC PANCREATITIS WILL BE RECRUITED FOR THE STUDY. ALL PATIENTS WILL RECEIVE THEIR USUAL CARE UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF THEIR GASTROENTEROLOGIST. THE TRIAL GASTROENTEROLOGISTS, DRS. PANDOL (CSMC) AND WU (KPMC) WILL BE ALERTED THAT A PATIENT WITH PANCREATITIS IS IN THE HOSPITAL. THE LIPASE LAB VALUES AND DIAGNOSIS CODES FOR ADMITTED PATIENTS WILL BE CHECKED ON A DAILY BASIS BY THE CSMC RESEARCH NURSE, WHO WILL NOTIFY DR. PANDOL THAT A PATIENT WITH PANCREATITIS HAS BEEN HOSPITALIZED. THE KPMC LAB WILL SEND DR. WU AN AUTOMATIC PAGE ALERT FOR HOSPITALIZED PATIENTS WITH AN ABNORMALLY HIGH SERUM LIPASE LEVEL.

description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS TASK ORDER IS TO ALLOW THE NIH TO ACQUIRE THE SCIENTIFIC, TECHNICAL, BUSINESS, AND STRATEGIC SERVICES NEEDED TO CONDUCT A PILOT OF THE Â€ŒCOMMONSÂ€? CONCEPT, WHICH IS INTENDED TO HELP ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY AND IMPACT OF CHANGING THE WAY THAT THE STORAGE OF AND ACCESS TO NIH OWNED SCIENTIFIC DATA IS FUNDED. THROUGH THE MITRE TASK ORDER, THE NIH WILL TEST, ASSESS, AND REFINE AN APPROACH WHICH MOVES AWAY FROM INDIVIDUAL IC PURCHASE OF DATA STORAGE TO THE USE OF SHARED (COMMODITY CLOUD) RESOURCES. SHOULD THE PROPOSED VALUE PROPOSITION BE REALIZED IN THE PILOT PHASE, THE MITRE TASK ORDER WILL FACILITATE THE MOVEMENT OF THE COMMONS OUT OF THE PILOT PHASE AND INTO THE OPERATIONAL (PRODUCTION) PHASE THROUGH PROVISION OF APPROPRIATE TRANSITION AND ACQUISITION SUPPORT. WORK DESCRIPTIONS OVERALL MANAGEMENT AND COORDINATION TASK ADMINISTRATION ACTIVITIES WILL BE COORDINATED BY THE MITRE PROJECT LEADER OR DESIGNEE, WITH INPUT FROM CONTRACTOR. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL: 1. PARTICIPATE IN A FORMAL KICK-OFF MEETING WITH MITRE TO REVIEW THE WORK TO BE ACCOMPLISHED UNDER THIS SOW AND ENSURE THAT ALL PARTIES HAVE A COMMON UNDERSTANDING OF THE WORK TO BE PERFORMED AND OF THE RESPECTIVE RESPONSIBILITIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE PARTIES TO THAT END. 2. DETERMINE WITH MITRE THE AGREED-UPON METHOD TO RESOLVE, TRACK, AND REPORT ON ISSUES. 3. DETERMINE WITH MITRE THE AGREED-UPON QUALITY ASSURANCE METHODS THAT WILL BE USED FOR PROJECT DELIVERABLES. 4. PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS AND CONTRIBUTE TO PROGRESS REPORTS THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF THIS PROJECT, AS NEEDED, TO COMMUNICATE STATUS, KEY ISSUES, AND FINDINGS. 5. CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOPING AND MAINTAINING A CURRENT PROJECT WORK PLAN (PWP), INCLUDING A DETAILED TIMELINE OF PROJECT MILESTONES AND DELIVERABLES. 6. PROVIDE A MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT THAT INCLUDES, (1) INCEPTION TO DATE (ITD) ACTUAL COSTS FOR WORK PERFORMED (ACWP) FOR THE PROJECT, (2) AND THE CONTRACTORÂ€™S BEST ESTIMATE OF THE TIME-PHASED RESOURCES REQUIRED TO COMPLETE THEIR REMAINING AUTHORIZED WORK Â€“ THE ESTIMATE AT COMPLETE (EAC). 7. INVOICE MITRE MONTHLY FOR ALLOWABLE INCURRED COSTS. 8. PARTICIPATE IN AN INTERNAL CLOSEOUT BRIEFING AT THE CONCLUSION OF THE PROJECT. MITRE PROJECT LEADER OR DESIGNEE AND THE CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL WILL PARTICIPATE IN A SESSION DESIGNED TO TRANSFER DOMAIN AND TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE LEVERAGED AND/OR GAINED DURING THE PROJECT WITH THE PURPOSE OF ENSURING THAT MITRE, AS THE FFRDC OPERATOR, MAINTAINS INSTITUTIONAL MEMORY AND PROGRAM CONTINUITY. CONTENT PRESENTED MAY BE PULLED FROM FORMAL AND INFORMAL DELIVERABLES PRESENTED TO THE SPONSOR. NOTE THAT TASKING IS DESCRIBED IN THE CONTEXT OF THE OVERALL PWP ISSUED BY NIH TO MITRE AND REFERENCES PWP TASK AND SUBTASK NUMBERS. TASK 5: MULTI-PILOT EVALUATION SUPPORT CONTRACTOR PERFORM THE WORK NECESSARY TO HELP DRIVE THE EVALUATION OF THE PROPOSED BUSINESS MODELS (STRIDES PILOT, DATA COMMONS PILOT, SDDP) AT THE ENTERPRISE LEVEL. THIS EFFORT, WHICH BEGINS SIMPLY AS DATA COLLECTION AND AGGREGATION, BUILDS TOWARDS A COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS, TO INCLUDE BOTH DIFFERENTIAL USAGE AND COMPARATIVE VALUE OF SERVICES PROVIDED. IT IS NOTED THAT THE LIST OF ATTRIBUTES FOR THIS ANALYSIS WILL BE INFORMED THROUGH ITERATIVE CYCLES OF STAKEHOLDER INPUT, AS OVERSEEN BY NIH. THIS WORK IS EVOLVING TO ADDRESS, TO A DEGREE AND DEPTH MUTUALLY AGREED FOR EACH THEME, THE ENTIRE PILOT ECOSYSTEM. OVER THE COURSE OF OPTION YEAR 1, MITRE WILL DOCUMENT AND DELIVER ANALYSIS CRITERIA AND ANALYSIS RESULTS IN AN ITERATIVE FASHION TO ENABLE APPROPRIATE STAKEHOLDER INPUT. BOTH HIGHLY TACTICAL (REPORTING) AND MORE STRATEGIC (BUSINESS PROCESS COMPARISON) WORK IS ANTICIPATED UNDER THIS TASK, WITH SPECIFIC TYPES OF SUPPORT TO BE REFINED DURING THE COURSE OF THE POP. THREE BASE EFFORT SUBTASKS ARE EXPLICITLY CALLED OUT IN THIS SOW, ALONG WITH TWO OPTIONAL SUBTASKS. NOTE THAT UPDATES TO THE REPORTING CAPABILITY TOOLS ARE EXPLICITLY COVERED IN AN OPTIONAL TASK. description: IN THIS STUDY, WE WILL RANDOMIZE 30 PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH RECURRENT PANCREATITIS WHO ARE UNDERGOING TREATMENT AT THE CEDARS-SINAI MEDICAL CENTER (CSMC) OR KAISER PERMANENTE LOS ANGELES MEDICAL CENTER (KPMC) TO SIMVASTATIN OR PLACEBO (20 IN THE SIMVASTATIN ARM, 10 IN THE CONTROL). ASSUMING THAT ~20% OF THE STUDY PARTICIPANTS DROP-OUT, WE EXPECT TO HAVE DATA ON A FINAL SAMPLE OF 24 MEN AND WOMEN (16 SIMVASTATIN, 8 CONTROL) COMPLETING THE 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UP PERIOD. CLINICAL AND RESEARCH MEASUREMENTS WILL BE TAKEN AT BASELINE (STUDY VISIT 1), MONTH 3 (STUDY VISIT 2), AND MONTH 6 (STUDY VISIT 3). THREE AND 6 MONTHS WERE CHOSEN, GIVEN THAT PATIENTS HAVE VARIABLE RECOVERY TIMES IN THE ORDER OF MONTHS AFTER AN ACUTE PANCREATITIS EVENT [46]. THEREFORE, THE REPEATED MEASURES AT 3 AND 6 MONTHS WILL BE ESSENTIAL FOR DETERMINING THE TRAJECTORY OF CHANGE IN THE CLINICAL AND RESEARCH MEASUREMENTS DURING THE RECOVERY PERIOD.

description: CONDUCT PRICE TRANSPARENCY ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN THE FOLLOWING SUBTASKS DETAIL THE PROCESS, DELIVERABLES, AND DELIVERABLE DUE DATES BY WHICH THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONTRIBUTE TO THE SPECIAL ANALYSIS OF MEDICARE PRICE TRANSPARENCY. SUBTASK 2.1 CONDUCT PRICE TRANSPARENCY ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN UNDER THIS SUBTASK, IN COLLABORATION WITH MITRE, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT AN ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN AND LITERATURE REVIEWS TO IDENTIFY DATA-DRIVEN, HIGH-YIELD OPPORTUNITIES AND PRACTICES THAT HAVE SUCCEEDED IN PROVIDING HEALTHCARE COST INFORMATION TO BENEFICIARY FOR HEALTH DECISIONS, THUS REDUCING OVERALL HEALTH CARE COSTS. THIS INCLUDES EXISTING HEALTHCARE PRICE TRANSPARENCY EFFORTS BASED ON RESEARCH OF PEER-REVIEWED LITERATURE, GOVERNMENT REPORTS, AND GREY LITERATURE INCLUDING PAPERS, FOUNDATION REPORTS, SYNTHESES, AND OTHER PUBLICATIONS. IT SHALL ALSO INCLUDE A REVIEW OF CURRENT PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR INITIATIVES, PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR WEBSITES, AND PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR DIGITAL TOOLS THAT ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF PRICE TRANSPARENCY IN HEALTH CARE. THESE PUBLIC SECTOR REVIEWS SHOULD INCLUDE STATE, FEDERAL, AND CMS ACTIVITIES. THE SCAN SHALL HIGHLIGHT BEST PRACTICES AND PROMISING INNOVATIONS IN AREAS SUCH AS CONTENT, FEATURES, AND OTHER FACTORS THAT ENHANCE ACCESS AND EASE OF USE; INCREASE USE RATES; REDUCE COSTS; ENABLE TIMELY CHOICE OF LOW COST/HIGH VALUE OPTIONS. IN ADDITION, THE SCAN SHALL REVIEW RESEARCH, PROGRAMS, AND INITIATIVES FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING SPECIFICS: Â€¢ MEDICARE AUDIENCE INTEREST IN AND USE OF PRICE TRANSPARENCY INFORMATION, SUCH AS USE OF TRANSPARENCY WEBSITES, PRINT SOURCES, AND OTHER COMMUNICATION CHANNELS; THE TYPES OF INFORMATION (E.G., NONEMERGENT OR SHOPPABLE SERVICES, EQUIPMENT) IN WHICH THEY ARE MOST INTERESTED; AND HOW THE STRUCTURE OF MEDICARE BENEFITS (E.G., COVERED AND UNCOVERED SERVICES AND EQUIPMENT, DEDUCTIBLES, CO-PAYS, MEDIGAP INSURANCE) AFFECTS THEIR USAGE OF AND INTEREST IN PRICING INFORMATION. Â€¢ OTHER FACTORS THAT MIGHT INFLUENCE BENEFICIARY INTEREST IN AND USE OF PRICE TRANSPARENCY INFORMATION, SUCH AS CHARACTERISTICS OF PARTICULAR BENEFICIARY SUBPOPULATIONS (E.G., GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION, HEALTH STATUS, FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS, AGE-BASED COHORTS); LITERACY AND NUMERACY LEVELS; DIGITAL ACCESS ISSUES; USE OF COMPUTERS AND SMARTPHONES; AND USE OF PUBLIC REPORTING SITES SUCH AS THE CMS COMPARE SITES. Â€¢ PRIVATE AND PUBLIC EFFORTS. UNDERSTAND HOW PRIVATE AND PUBLIC INSURERS SEEK TO EMPOWER CONSUMERS THROUGH PRICE TRANSPARENCY. THIS INCLUDES UNDERSTANDING WHAT EFFORTS (E.G., EOBS, WEBSITES, COST SHARING) HAVE BEEN MADE OR ARE BEING MADE WITHIN THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT AND WITHIN THE PRIVATE SECTOR TO IMPROVE PRICE TRANSPARENCY, ALONG WITH AN ASSESSMENT OF WHAT EFFORTS ARE MOST EFFECTIVE. Â€¢ UNDERSTAND HOW AND WHEN CONSUMERS ARE MOST LIKELY TO USE PRICE TOOLS WHEN SEEKING HEALTH CARE SERVICES. THIS INCLUDES AN EXPLORATION OF HOW MEDICARE CAN BEST PROMOTE AND DISPLAY PRICING INFORMATION, UNDERSTANDING CONSUMER MOTIVATIONS TO USE PRICING INFORMATION, AND IDENTIFYING SPECIFIC HIGH COST SETTINGS/SERVICES/PROCEDURES FOR WHICH CONSUMERS ARE LIKELY TO PRICE SHOP. Â€¢ IDENTIFY INNOVATIVE AND PROMISING SOLUTIONS TO IMPROVING USE OF PRICE TRANSPARENCY TOOLS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PRESENT DEVELOP A SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN RESULTS. THE SUMMARY SHALL INCLUDE A WRITTEN REPORT WITH DETAILED FINDINGS OF RESULTS AND A POWERPOINT PRESENTATION. BOTH THE WRITTEN REPORT AND POWERPOINT PRESENTATION SHALL FOCUS ON FINDINGS FOR PRICE TRANSPARENCY PARTICULARLY RELEVANT TO THE MEDICARE POPULATION. description: COMMENT PERIOD SUPPORT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE STAFF TO CODE AND ORGANIZE COMMENTS. THE STAFF SHOULD HOLD OR BE PURSUING A J.D. OR M.P.H. DEGREE OR HAVE EXPERIENCE SUCCESSFULLY AND EFFECTIVELY CATEGORIZING SIMILAR COMMENTS. THE COMMENT PERIOD SUPPORT WILL BE COORDINATED BY MITRE AND WILL BE PERFORMED IN A WEB-BASED TOOL PROVIDED BY MITRE. MITRE WILL PROVIDE TRAINING FOR STAFF AND THE FIRST WEEK OF THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE ARE EXPECTED TO BE SPENT ON TRAINING. STAFF ARE EXPECTED TO BE AVAILABLE 25-50% TIME FOR TRAINING DURING THE TRAINING PERIOD, UP TO 10 HOURS. TRAINING WILL INCLUDE THE PROCESSES REQUIRED TO DO PUBLIC COMMENT WORK, AND THE TOOLS USED TO CODE AND ORGANIZE COMMENTS. PART OF THE TRAINING WILL BE CENTERED ON THE TAXONOMY MITRE HAS DEVELOPED. THE TAXONOMY IS A CODING SCHEMA BASED UPON THE STRUCTURE OF THE FINAL RULE WITH COMMENT AND INTERIM FINAL RULE WITH COMMENT. ONCE COMMENTS ARE RECEIVED, MITRE WILL LOAD THEM IN THE WEB-BASED TOOL. THE CONTRACTOR STAFF SHALL ANALYZE AND PARSE EACH COMMENT INTO INDIVIDUAL THOUGHTS/THEME USING THE APPROVED TAXONOMY. EACH INDIVIDUAL THOUGHT IS STORED SEPARATELY IN THE TOOL WITH A LINK TO THE ORIGINAL COMMENT. THE CONTRACTOR STAFF SHALL THEN CATEGORIZE (CODE) THESE INDIVIDUAL THOUGHTS USING THE TAXONOMY. EACH STAFF MEMBER WILL BE ASSIGNED A NUMBER OF SUBMISSIONS TO ANALYZE, CODE, AND SUMMARIZE IN THE WEB-BASED TOOL. EACH SUBMISSION MAY RANGE ANYWHERE FROM A PARAGRAPH TO MANY PAGES. THE CONTRACTOR WILL ALSO PROVIDE STAFF TO PERFORM TASKING COORDINATION AND A QUALITY REVIEW AND WILL ASSIST IN PROVIDING ADDITIONAL TRAINING OR REMEDIATION IF QUALITY PROBLEMS ARE FOUND. THE QUALITY REVIEW WILL INCLUDE AN ASSESSMENT OF INTERCODER RELIABILITY, AND WILL ENSURE THAT ALL UNIQUE THOUGHTS IN EACH LETTER ARE CAPTURED AND EACH COMMENT IS DISCRETE. THE TASK COORDINATOR WILL WORK WITH THE MITRE PROJECT LEADER TO ASSIGN SUBMISSIONS FOR PROCESSING. TASK 2 ASSUMPTIONS: Â€¢ A MAXIMUM OF 1500 COMMENTS ARE EXPECTED. Â€¢ TRAINING WILL BEGIN NO LATER THAN 10 BUSINESS DAYS BEFORE THE CLOSE OF THE COMMENT PERIOD. Â€¢ ALL HIGH-PRIORITY COMMENT PROCESSING (UP TO 25 COMMENT LETTERS DESIGNATED HIGH-PRIORITY) MUST BE COMPLETED WITHIN (1) WEEK OF THE CLOSURE OF THE COMMENT PERIOD, AND ALL COMMENT PROCESSING MUST BE COMPLETED WITHIN TWO (2) WEEKS OF THE CLOSURE OF THE COMMENT PERIOD. Â€¢ TRAINING, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO TIME FOR READING THE RULE, WILL BE ONE (1) WEEK AT 25-50% OF STAFF TIME, UP TO 10 HOURS. Â€¢ MITRE WILL DO ALL STATUS REPORTING FROM THE WEB-BASED TOOL. THE CONTRACTOR IS REQUESTED TO EXPLICITLY ESTIMATE IN ADVANCE ANY OVERTIME PAY NEEDED TO MEET THESE REQUIREMENTS.

description: RESEARCH SUPPORT- DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS SIMPLIFICATION (DRS) AND IMPROPER PAYMENTS (IP) THE CONTRACTOR IS TO CONDUCT RESEARCH IN SUPPORT OF THE DRS INTEGRATED PROJECT TEAMÂ€™S (IPT) CONSIDERATION OF ISSUES PERTINENT TO DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS SIMPLIFICATION AND PROVIDE DATA ANALYSIS FOR THE IP IPT. DRS IPT THE DRS IPT MAINTAINS A PIPELINE OF ISSUES TO CONSIDER AND REQUIRES THE CONTRACTOR TO CONDUCT IN-DEPTH RESEARCH TO ASCERTAIN THE IMPACT OF ISSUES AND THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF ADDRESSING THEM. THE RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE SUFFICIENT DETAIL TO ALLOW THE IPT TO DETERMINE IF THERE IS VALUE IN ADDRESSING THE ISSUE AND TO PRIORITIZE THE PIPELINE OF ISSUES. FURTHERMORE, RESEARCH IS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION NEEDED FOR THE IPT TO DEFINE THE IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH. THE CONTRACTOR WILL RECEIVE RESEARCH ASSIGNMENTS FROM THE MITRE TASK LEAD AND MAY BE TASKED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH MITRE ANALYSTS. DURING TASK ASSIGNMENT, THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE ABLE TO INTERFACE DIRECTLY WITH IPT PARTICIPANTS TO CLARIFY UNDERSTANDING OF THE REQUEST AS NEEDED. THE SCHEDULING AND CONDUCTING OF MEETINGS WITH CMS STAFF IN SUPPORT OF RESEARCH EFFORTS WILL BE COORDINATED WITH THE MITRE TASK LEAD. THE CONTRACTOR IN COORDINATION WITH THE MITRE TASK LEAD WILL APPLY A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO RESEARCHING EACH ISSUE. FOLLOWING INITIAL DIRECT DISCUSSIONS WITH CMS AND AFTER CONDUCTING AN INITIAL ASSESSMENT, THE CONTRACTOR, IN COLLABORATION WITH MITRE, IS TO DRAFT A RESEARCH PLAN THAT INCLUDES, A PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT OF THE SCOPE OF THE ISSUE, IDENTIFICATION OF THE CMS PROGRAMS IMPACTED, IDENTIFICATION OF THE INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL STAKEHOLDERS INVOLVED AND POTENTIALLY IMPACTED, AN INITIAL LIST OF AREAS THAT WILL NEED TO BE REVIEWED, IDENTIFICATION OF CMS PERSONNEL OR OTHER STAKEHOLDERS THAT MAY NEED TO BE INTERVIEWED, A PROPOSED STAFFING PLAN, AND A DRAFT TIMELINE FOR COMPLETING THE RESEARCH AND DELIVERING THE FINAL RESULTS REPORT. THE RESEARCH PLAN WILL IDENTIFY A RESEARCH TEAM ALLOCATING SPECIFIC RESOURCES FROM THE CONTRACTOR AND MITRE AS APPROPRIATE; THERE WILL BE A POINT PERSON FOR EACH TOPIC IDENTIFIED AS THE RESEARCH LEAD. THE CONTRACTOR AND THE MITRE TASK LEAD WILL REVIEW THE RESEARCH PLAN WITH CMS, AND OBTAIN CMS SIGNOFF PRIOR TO INITIATING RESEARCH WORK. USING THE RESEARCH PLAN AGREED UPON WITH CMS, THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL PERFORM RESEARCH FOR EACH PROJECT. IN-DEPTH RESEARCH MAY ENTAIL, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, THE FOLLOWING: Â€¢ CONDUCTING A THOROUGH LANDSCAPE ANALYSIS, VALIDATING THE DOCUMENTATION AND ARTIFACTS TO BE CONSIDERED. Â€¢ IDENTIFYING AND SECURING INTERVIEWS WITH ANY CMS PERSONNEL THAT MAY BE REQUIRED. Â€¢ IDENTIFYING, AND REVIEWING POTENTIAL IMPACT OF THE PROJECT BY APPLYING A DEEP KNOWLEDGE OF CMS PROGRAMS AND OF MEDICARE PROVIDERS, BENEFICIARIES, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS TOGETHER WITH EXTENSIVE ANALYTICAL SKILL ACROSS THE SPECTRUM OF RELEVANT OF STATUTES, REGULATION, REGULATORY GUIDANCE, SUB-REGULATORY GUIDANCE, MANUALS (PROGRAM INTEGRITY, SUPPLIER, CLAIMS PROCESSING, ETC.), POLICY (NCDS, LCDS, ETC.), CMS OPERATIONS, AND CMS SYSTEMS. Â€¢ REVIEWING PUBLICLY-AVAILABLE DATA AND INFORMATION, AND CMS DATA AS PROVIDED, TO GAUGE THE SCOPE OF AN ISSUEÂ€”FOR EXAMPLE, BY DETERMINING THE NUMBER AND TYPE OF CLAIMS INVOLVED, AND THE RESULTANT NUMBER OF DENIALS AND APPEALS. Â€¢ DEVELOPING HIGH-LEVEL COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS, WHICH MAY INCLUDE DATA SIMULATION, MODELING ETC., AS REQUIRED, PROVIDED SUFFICIENT DATA ARE AVAILABLE AND PROVIDED, SUCH AS FOR CHANGES TO CURRENT CMS BUSINESS OPERATIONS (INTERNAL OPERATIONS / PROCEDURES) AND CHANGES TO CURRENT IT SYSTEMS (BOTH FEDERAL SYSTEMS AND CONTRACTOR SYSTEMS). Â€¢ ASSESSING THE Â€ŒREAL-WORLDÂ€? IMPACT OF IMPLEMENTING BASED ON AN UNDERSTANDING OF CURRENT PROVIDER SENTIMENT AND OPERATIONS. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL DOCUMENT AND DELIVER RESEARCH FINDINGS TO DETAIL THE BREADTH OF THE ISSUE, ITS IMPACT, THE BENEFIT OF RESOLVING THE ISSUE (E.G., REDUCING PROVIDER BURDEN), AND THE NEEDED CHANGES.

description: SPECIAL ANALYSIS FOR AMBULANCE SERVICES THE FOLLOWING SUBTASKS DETAIL THE PROCESS, DELIVERABLES, AND DELIVERABLE DUE DATES BY WHICH THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT THE SPECIAL ANALYSIS OF MEDICARE AMBULANCE SERVICES. SUBTASK 2.1 - CONDUCT RESEARCH ON THE UNIVERSE OF AMBULANCE SUPPLIERS/PROVIDERS AND COST UTILIZATION USING CMS ENROLLMENT DATA, CLAIMS DATA, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCANNING 2.1.1 - ANALYSIS OF CMS PROVIDER AND SUPPLIER DATA: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL GAIN ACCESS TO AND ANALYZE CMS DATA ON AMBULANCE PROVIDERS AND SUPPLIERS SUCH AS THE PECOS DATA. THE GOAL OF THE ANALYSIS WILL BE TO UNDERSTAND THE NUMBER OF PROVIDERS AND SUPPLIERS AND THEIR CHARACTERISTICS (INCLUDING GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION, SERVICE AREA, SERVICES OFFERED, OWNERSHIP STATUS, ETC.). THIS ANALYSIS WILL HELP INFORM DECISIONS ON SURVEY AND SAMPLING DESIGN PARTICULARLY WITH RESPECT TO WHICH SAMPLING STRATA CAN BE IMPLEMENTED GIVEN AVAILABLE CMS DATA. THIS ANALYSIS WILL ALSO INFORM DECISIONS ON WHICH ITEMS NEED NOT BE INCLUDED IN THE DATA COLLECTION SURVEY QUESTIONNAIRE DUE TO THEIR AVAILABILITY IN EXTANT CMS DATA. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUMMARIZE MAIN FINDINGS FROM THIS ANALYSIS IN A MEMO AND TABLES AND PROVIDE PROVIDER AND SUPPLIER ANALYSIS SUMMARY AND TABLES IN A FORMAT AGREED TO BY THE CMS AND MITRE. THIS INFORMATION WILL ALSO BE INCLUDED IN THE TARGETED ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN. 2.1.2 - CLAIMS DATA-BASED ANALYSIS OF UTILIZATION AND PAYMENTS: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL GAIN ACCESS AND ANALYZE PART B CLAIMS DATA TO ESTIMATE THE UTILIZATION OF AND MEDICARE SPENDING ON AMBULANCE SERVICES IN ONE OR MORE RECENT YEARS. THE ANALYSES WILL REPORT UTILIZATION AND SPENDING SEPARATELY FOR EACH SERVICE (BY HCPCS CODES A0425 Â€“ A0429, A0432-A0434, A0999) AND LEVEL OF SERVICE, BY BILLED MODIFIERS (ORIGIN AND DESTINATIONS, QL), BY GEOGRAPHIC AREA, AND, TO THE EXTENT POSSIBLE GIVEN LINKAGES USING NATIONAL PROVIDER IDS OR OTHER IDENTIFIERS TO PECOS DATA, BY DIFFERENT CHARACTERISTICS OF AMBULANCE SERVICE SUPPLIERS AND PROVIDERS. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INFORM CMS TO BETTER TARGET ITEMS IN THE DATA COLLECTION SURVEY QUESTIONNAIRE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUMMARIZE MAIN FINDINGS FROM THIS ANALYSIS AND PROVIDE THE UTILIZATION AND PAYMENT ANALYSIS SUMMARY AND TABLES IN A MEMO AND TABLES FORMAT (INCLUDED IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN). THIS ANALYSIS WILL INFORM THE SAMPLING STRATIFICATION IN SUBTASK 2.3. (I.E., PROVIDERS THAT HAVE A SUFFICIENT PATIENT LOAD TO BE INCLUDED IN THE SAMPLING FRAME). 2.1.3 - ENVIRONMENTAL SCANNING: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT AN ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN TO INFORM THE UNIVERSE OF GROUND AMBULANCE SUPPLIERS AND PROVIDERS AND THEIR CHARACTERISTICS AS NECESSARY TO FILL IN ANY GAPS IN INFORMATION NOT AVAILABLE IN THE CLAIMS AND ENROLLMENT DATA. THIS INFORMATION SHALL BE INCLUDED IN THE DELIVERABLE TABLE BELOW. SUBTASK 2.2 - CONDUCT STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN TO INFORM SURVEY AND SAMPLING PLAN DESIGN 2.2.1 - TARGETED ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN: UNDER THIS SUBTASK, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT MITRE IN CONDUCTING A TARGETED ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN ON THE AMBULANCE FEE SCHEDULE (AFS). IT WILL ALSO SUPPORT AN EXAMINATION OF STUDIES ON AMBULANCE COST DATA REQUIRED BY THE AMERICAN TAXPAYER RELIEF ACT OF 2012 (ATRA), RELATED STUDIES ON COST DATA BY THE AMERICAN AMBULANCE ASSOCIATION (AAA) AND OTHER INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS, AND REPORTS ISSUED BY OTHER GOVERNMENTAL AND PRIVATE SECTOR ORGANIZATIONS. 2.2.2 - STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO MITRE TO ASSIST CM IN CONDUCTING UP TO 15 STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENTS RELATED TO AMBULANCE SERVICES. THESE ENGAGEMENTS MAY BE IN MULTIPLE FORUMS, SUCH AS INTERVIEWS, FOCUS GROUPS, TECHNICAL EXPERT PANELS (TEP), OR LISTENING SESSIONS, SUCH AS OPEN-DOOR FORUM, ETC. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COLLABORATE WITH CM ON THE GROUPS AND REPRESENTATIVES TO BE CONTACTED FOR THESE ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES, AND THROUGH THE FACILITATION OF CM CONSULT REPORTS OBTAINED WITH PERMISSION FROM THE AMERICAN AMBULANCE ASSOCIATION TO INFORM THE SELECTION.

description: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE RURAL HEALTH STRATEGY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST MITRE IN WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE CMS RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL TO IMPLEMENT THE CMS RURAL HEALTH STRATEGY, APPLYING THE APPROACH TO BE OUTLINED IN THE CMS RURAL HEALTH STRATEGY IMPLEMENTATION WORK PLAN. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST MITRE WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE CMS RURAL HEALTH STRATEGY IMPLEMENTATION WORK PLAN. THIS WORK PLAN WILL OUTLINE THE ACTIVITIES MAY INCLUDE IDENTIFYING ADDITIONAL SHORT, MID AND LONG-TERM MILESTONES AND OPPORTUNITIES TO SUPPORT THE STRATEGIC OBJECTIVES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK CLOSELY WITH MITRE, THE COR, CMS OMH LEADERSHIP, AND CMS RHC CO-CHAIRS TO COMPLETE THE WORK PLAN. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST MITRE IN PARTNERING WITH THE CMS RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL TO DEVELOP AND PRODUCE AN ANNUAL REPORT THAT DETAILS COUNCIL ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING STRATEGIC COORDINATION ACROSS CMS CENTERS, OFFICES, AND REGIONAL OFFICES; STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT STRATEGY AND ACTIVITIES; STRATEGIC PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES; AND MAJOR ACHIEVEMENTS AND MILESTONES. NOTE: THE INTENTION IN TASK 2 IS THAT THE CONTRACTOR CONTRIBUTE SUBSTANTIALLY TO THE COMBINED MITRE-CONTRACTOR EFFORT IN SUPPORTING CMS IN ITS IMPLEMENTATION OF THE RURAL HEALTH STRATEGY TASK 2 DELIVERABLES SEE DELIVERABLES TABLE BELOW TASK 3: DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF COMMUNICATIONS PLAN (OPTIONAL TASK) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST MITRE IN WORKING CLOSELY WITH THE CMS RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS PLAN THAT SUPPORTS THE CMS RURAL HEALTH STRATEGY. THE RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL COMMUNICATION PLAN IS INTENDED TO PROVIDE A FRAMEWORK FOR SELECTING, MANAGING, AND COORDINATING A WIDE VARIETY OF COMMUNICATION TO ADDRESS RURAL HEALTH NEEDS FOR ENGAGEMENT, AWARENESS, AND COMMITMENT OF INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL AUDIENCES AND STAKEHOLDERS AS WELL AS TO BUILD EXTERNAL VISIBILITY OF THE COUNCIL AND ITS EFFORTS. THE COMMUNICATION FRAMEWORK WILL ARTICULATE GOALS, OBJECTIVES, AND RELATED ACTIVITIES TO ACHIEVE THE COMMUNICATION OUTCOMES. THE FRAMEWORKÂ€™S PURPOSE IS TO PRIORITIZE COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES THAT SUPPORT THE OUTCOMES OF THE STRATEGY. THE COMMUNICATIONS PLAN WILL OUTLINE MULTIPLE DIRECT, PRINT AND ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION CHANNELS. THESE CHANNELS MAY INCLUDE OVERVIEW BRIEFINGS, SEMINARS/WORKSHOPS, CONFERENCE PARTICIPATION, PRINT MATERIALS AND WEBSITE CONTENT. THE COMMUNICATIONS PLAN WILL ALSO INCLUDE TACTICS FOR STRATEGIC COORDINATION BY THE RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL ACROSS CMS CENTERS AND OFFICES, AS WELL AS ENGAGEMENT WITH KEY RURAL HEALTH STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS THE COUNTRY, AS OUTLINED IN TASK 4. STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT & PARTNERSHIPS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSUME THE LEAD ROLE IN SUPPORTING STRATEGIC COORDINATION BY THE RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL ACROSS CMS, AND SUPPORT STRATEGIC RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL ENGAGEMENT WITH KEY STAKEHOLDERS, WHICH MAY INCLUDE RURAL HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS AND THEIR REPRESENTATIVES, SUCH AS PHYSICIANS AND OTHER PROVIDERS AND PHYSICIAN ORGANIZATIONS AND OTHER PROVIDER ORGANIZATIONS. KEY STAKEHOLDERS MAY ALSO INCLUDE HEALTH CARE ORGANIZATIONS SUCH AS HOSPITALS, CLINICS, HOSPICES, AND DIALYSIS FACILITIES, AS WELL AS RELATED ASSOCIATIONS SUCH AS HOSPITAL ASSOCIATIONS. IN ADDITION, KEY STAKEHOLDERS MAY INCLUDE CONSUMERS, STATES; NATIONAL, STATE, AND LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS WITH A FOCUS ON RURAL HEALTH; AS WELL AS RESEARCHERS AND OTHER THOUGHT LEADERS. STRATEGIC COORDINATION THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSUME THE LEAD ROLE IN PARTNERING WITH THE CMS RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL AND CMS OMH TO ENSURE THE SMOOTH INTERFACE OF THE RURAL HEALTH COUNCIL AS IT WORKS ACROSS THE BREADTH OF CMS CENTERS, SPECIFIC OFFICES, AND REGIONAL OFFICES TO ACHIEVE ITS VISION OF ENSURING ACCESS TO HIGH QUALITY HEALTH CARE FOR ALL AMERICANS LIVING IN RURAL SETTINGS; ADDRESSING THE UNIQUE ECONOMICS OF PROVIDING HEALTH CARE IN RURAL AMERICA; AND BRINGING THE RURAL HEALTH CARE FOCUS TO CMSÂ€™ HEALTH CARE DELIVERY AND PAYMENT REFORM INITIATIVES. O WORKING WITH THE LTR IT LEAD TO MAKE SURE THAT ALL DESKTOPS/LAPTOPS USED BY THE REGISTRY STAFF MEMBERS ARE ENCRYPTED IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE FEDERAL INFORMATION PROCESSING STANDARD (FIPS) 140-2 O SETTING UP A SITE-TO-SITE VPN BETWEEN THE HOST INSTITUTION AND THE LSU HEALTH SCIENCES CENTER IN NEW ORLEANS. O AUDIT THE REGIONAL REGISTRY TO ENSURE SUFFICIENT PHYSICAL SECURITY PROCEDURES IN PLACE O AUDIT STAFF WHO WORK FROM HOME OFFICE TO MAKE SURE ALL PHYSICAL SECURITY REQUIREMENTS ARE MET. O INSTALL COMPUTER VIRUS DETECTION SOFTWARE AND VIRUS DETECTION SIGNATURES AS WELL PATCHES AND UPGRADES ON ALL DESKTOPS/LAPTOPS FOR REGIONAL REGISTRY STAFF AND ENSURE THEY ARE CURRENT. 2. EDIT AND CONSOLIDATE ALL SEER REPORTABLE CANCER CASES FROM THE CATCHMENT AREA AND PROVIDE HIGH-QUALITY, TIMELINESS, AND COMPLETE DATA THAT MEET ALL THE BENCHMARKS IN THE SEER DATA QUALITY PROFILES. 3. CONDUCT COMPLETE CASE ASCERTAINMENT FOR CANCER CASES FROM NOT ONLY HOSPITALS (BOTH ANALYTIC AND NON-ANALYTIC) BUT ALSO NON-HOSPITAL SETTINGS, SUCH AS TREATMENT CENTERS, UROLOGY, DERMATOLOGY, AND HEMATOLOGY-ONCOLOGY OFFICES. 4. CONTINUE TO FOLLOW-UP PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER IN 2000 AND AFTER TO OBTAIN CURRENT FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION FOR THOSE THAT THE LTR CANNOT OBTAIN FROM VARIOUS LINKAGES TO MEET THE SEER-REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP RATES. 5. PARTICIPATE IN THE NCI-SEER QUALITY CONTROL AND TRAINING ACTIVITIES 6. MAKE EFFORTS TO HELP REVIEW AND TEST NEW SEER CODING SOFTWARE TOOLS AND TRAINING MODULES, AS WELL AS ANSWER OR REVIEW QUESTIONS FOR SINQ OR ASK A SEER REGISTRAR. 7. ENSURE THAT THE ESTABLISHED DATA SECURITY PROCEDURES, PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROLS, AND STAFF TRAINING MEET THE NATIONAL STANDARDS AND NCI'S REQUIREMENTS.

description: DTU IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MAINTAINING, ENHANCING, AND UPDATING THE EXISTING SET OF T CELL PREDICTION TOOLS. DTU WILL MAINTAIN THE EXISTING B CELL TOOLS DEVELOPED BY DTU, AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS FOR THE ANALYSIS RESOURCE. DTU WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIOD TELECONFERENCES AND MEETINGS, AND PROVIDE TASK STATUS FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. ANALYSIS RESOURCE TASKS SPECIFICALLY, DTU WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS: 1. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE THE MHC CLASS I AND II BINDING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 2. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE MHC PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 3. IDENTIFY AND INCORPORATE NEW MHC CLASS I AND II PREDICTION TOOLS 4. MAINTAIN EXISTING B CELL TOOLS DEVELOPED BY DTU 5. UPDATE EVALUATIONS OF THE MHC BINDING AND T CELL PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS 6. ESTABLISH AN AUTOMATED BENCHMARKING SYSTEM FOR PREDICTION TOOLS NOT HOSTED IN THE IEDB 7. DEVELOP NEW B CELL EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS WITH RESPECT TO THESE TASKS, DTU WILL DELIVER UPDATED EXECUTABLES FOR THOSE TOOLS DEVELOPED UNDER SEPARATE FUNDING THAT ARE BEING MADE AVAILABLE TO THE IEDB FOR INTEGRATION, SUCH AS NETCHOP, NETCTL, BEPIPRED, AND DISCOTOPE, AS RETRAINING, BUG FIXES, AND FEATURE ENHANCEMENTS OCCUR. FOR TOOLS DEVELOPED UNDER THE CURRENT CONTRACT, DTU WILL DELIVER EXECUTABLES, SOURCE CODE, AND DOCUMENTATION. MEETINGS AND REPORTS 1. MONTHLY MEETINGS/TELECONFERENCES/VIDEOCONFERENCES DTU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH LIL AT A MINIMUM OF MONTHLY INTERVALS, EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA TELECONFERENCE/VIDEOCONFERENCE. THE PURPOSE OF THESE MEETINGS WILL BE TO COORDINATE EFFORTS AND REPORT PROGRESS. 2. QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS DTU WILL PROVIDE INPUT FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS ON A TIMELY BASIS SO THEIR CONTENT CAN BE INCORPORATED IN ADVANCE OF THE SPECIFIED DELIVERY DATE TO NIAID.

description: PHASE 3 (3.5 YEARS) - IN PHASE 3 THE SUBRECIPIENT SHALL: EXHIBIT A SCOPE OF WORK A. FINALIZE NCH PROTOCOL, CONSENT AND DATA FORMS, DATA MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR PHASE 3, FOR NIMH REVIEW AND APPROVAL; GET LOCAL IRB APPROVALS. B. TEST THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE TREATMENT ALGORITHM INCLUDING EACH OF THE CORE ALGORITHM COMPONENTS: (I) REVIEW OF ANTIPSYCHOTIC MEDICATION ORDERS BY A CHILD PSYCHIATRIST, (II) BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NAVIGATION, (III) EXPEDITED ACCESS TO SHORT-TERM, FACE-TO-FACE PSYCHOTHERAPY, AND (IV) PSYCHOTHERAPY DELIVERED VIA TELEVIDEO CONFERENCE IN A PRAGMATIC CLINICAL TRIAL WITH A TARGET RECRUITMENT OF 200 SUBJECTS AT NCH. C. PREPARE AND SECURELY TRANSFER A LIMITED DATA SET FOR THE PRACTICAL CLINICAL TRIAL TO THE DATA COORDINATING CENTER AT KAISER PERMANENTE. D. CONTRIBUTE TO THE PREPARATION OF REQUIRED REPORTS TO NIMH AS WELL AS SCHOLARLY PRESENTATIONS AND MANUSCRIPTS ADDRESSING THE RESEARCH QUESTIONS OF THE STUDY. E. REGULARLY ATTEND TEAM MEETINGS AND ASSIST WITH SCIENTIFIC DISSEMINATION.PHASE 2 (12 MONTHS) IN PHASE 2 THE SUBRECIPIENT SHALL:A. FINALIZE THE PHASE 2 NCH PROTOCOL, CONSENT AND DATA FORMS, DATA MANAGEMENT PLAN, GET IRB APPROVALS, AND RECEIVE NIMH APPROVAL TO BEGIN PILOT RECRUITMENT. B. IMPLEMENT STUDY INFRASTRUCTURE AND PROCESSES TO CARRY OUT THE PILOT STUDY. C. CONDUCT A PILOT STUDY IN APPROXIMATELY 20-40 SUBJECTS. D. THE PILOT STUDY WILL TEST THE ACCEPTABILITY OF AND ADHERENCE TO THE ALGORITHM(S) BY CLINICIANS, PATIENTS, AND THEIR FAMILIES, THE VALIDITY OF THE CLINICAL INSTRUMENTS TO MEASURE TREATMENT OUTCOMES AND MODERATORS AND MEDIATORS OF RESPONSE, AND THE FEASIBILITY, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REPRODUCIBILITY OF THE ALGORITHM(S). E. PREPARE AND SECURELY TRANSMIT A LIMITED DATA SET FOR THE PILOT STUDY TO GROUP HEALTH. F. CONTRIBUTE TO A STATISTICAL REPORT ADDRESSING THE KEY AIMS OF THE STUDY. G. COLLECT STAKEHOLDER FEEDBACK TO INFORM CHANGES TO THE MAIN TRIAL IN PHASE 3. H. THE NCH SITE INVESTIGATOR WILL REGULARLY ATTEND TEAM AND STEERING COMMITTEE MEETINGS. I. ASSUMPTIONS: 1. IT IS ANTICIPATEDÂ· THAT PHASE 2 WILL BE 12 MONTHS IN DURATION.PHASE1 (8 MONTHS)Â· THE SUBRECIPIENTSHALL: A. DEFINE THE TARGET NCH PATIENT POPULATION WITH RESPECT TO DEMOGRAPHIC AND CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS. THIS POPULATION WILL CONSIST OF CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS AGE 5-17 WITH NONPSYCHOTIC MOOD AND BEHAVIORAL DISTURBANCES. B. ASSIST WITH RECRUITMENT OF CONSENSUS PANEL EXPERTS. C. CONDUCT 1 FOCUS GROUP WITH EACH OF 3 STAKEHOLDER GROUPS (PARENTS/GUARDIANS, YOUTH, PRESCRIBING CLINICIANS). D. IDENTIFY LOCAL PROVIDERS AND HEALTH PLAN LEADERS FOR CLINICAL DECISION DESIGN SESSIONS AND INFORMATION GATHERING MEETINGS WITH GROUP HEALTH STAFF. E. CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF TREATMENT ALGORITHMS TO BE USED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF THE DEFINED TARGET PATIENT POPULATION, WITH ESTIMATED OUTCOMES FOR EACH STEP OF THE ALGORITHM. F. CONTRIBUTE TO A DRAFT PROTOCOL AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CONDUCTING THE FEASIBILITY TRIAL IN PHASE 2. G. THE NCH SITE INVESTIGATOR WILL REGULARLY ATTEND TEAM AND STEERING COMMITTEE MEETINGS.

description: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO BEST ENABLE NIH OVERSIGHT OF THE DATA COMMONS CONSORTIUM MEMBERSHIP AS THEY PERFORM THEIR RESPONSIBILITIES AS DEFINED THROUGH THE OTHER TRANSACTIONAL AUTHORITY (OTA) NEGOTIATION PROCESS. THIS INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: 1. WITHIN 15 BUSINESS DAYS OF EXECUTION, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE A STRATEGY FOR ESTABLISHING PROGRAM MANAGEMENT CONTROLS FOR THE DATA COMMONS, AND THE ONGOING EFFORTS CONSORTIUM THAT UNDERLIES IS. THIS WILL BE VETTED WITH KEY NIH STAKEHOLDERS, MODIFIED AS NEEDED, AND THEN FINALIZED. KEY ATTRIBUTES OF THE STRATEGY WILL INCLUDE SOME OR ALL OF THE FOLLOWING (TO INCLUDE MECHANISMS OF ACHIEVING THESE GOALS): A. RISK ENUMERATION B. MITIGATION ENUMERATION (BASED ON A.) C. INTEGRATION OF CONSORTIUM ACTIVITIES D. CROSS-TEAM COORDINATION E. DEPENDENCY ENUMERATION F. PROGRAM GOVERNANCE G. DATA GOVERNANCE H. STANDARDS ASSURANCE I. ACCOUNTABILITY MANAGEMENT J. FINANCIAL TRACKING (COST, VALUE) K. INFRASTRUCTURE PLANNING L. ENUMERATION OF CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT OPPORTUNITIES THE REQUIRED CONTENTS OF THE STRATEGY DOCUMENT WILL BE ENUMERATED BY MITRE WITHIN THE FIRST 5 BUSINESS DAYS OF THIS CONTRACT, EXCEPT BY MUTUAL AGREEMENT OF MITRE, NIH, AND CONTRACTOR. IT IS EXPECTED THAT A 1-PAGE DOCUMENT WILL SUFFICE FOR THESE PURPOSES. 2. THROUGH THIS EFFORT, INCLUDING DURING FINALIZATION OF THE STRATEGY FOR PROGRAM MANAGEMENT CONTROLS, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BEGIN EXECUTION OF PORTIONS THAT HAVE BEEN MUTUALLY AGREED. THIS MEANS THAT SUPPORTING THE OVERALL MANAGEMENT OF THIS EFFORT BY ENSURING THE TIMELY COMPLETION AND COORDINATION OF OBJECTIVES, REFINING NIH-DERIVED METRICS OF SUCCESS, AND ENHANCING OVERALL REPORTING AND COMMUNICATION ON THE PROGRAM CAN BEGIN IMMEDIATELY. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES TO BE UNDERTAKEN IMMEDIATELY INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: A. COORDINATE WITH CONSORTIUM PROJECT MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL B. MONITOR GENERAL PROJECT HEALTH C. MAINTAIN MASTER SCHEDULE OF MILESTONES AND DEPENDENCIES FOR ALL DATA COMMONS ACTIVITIES BASED ON THE SCHEDULE PROVIDED INITIALLY BY NIH D. FACILITATE INTERDEPENDENT ISSUES AND RISKS MITIGATION E. FACILITATE CRITICAL PROGRAM MEETINGS (NO MORE THAN 12) F. CREATE EXECUTIVE-LEVEL PRESENTATIONS (NO MORE THAN 6) G. SUPPORT AND ENFORCE ADHERENCE TO PROJECT COMMUNICATIONS PLAN (MECHANISM TBD) H. MANAGE STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT METRICS (NO MORE THAN MONTHLY) I. PROVIDE OTHER SUPPORT TO PROGRAM LEAD, AS REQUIRED AND AS APPROPRIATE FOR THE POSITION CONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE REPORTS ON THE ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN AND OUTCOMES EVERY 20 BUSINESS DAYS, IN A FORMAT MUTUALLY AGREEABLE TO CONTRACTOR, NIH, AND MITRE. IT IS EXPECTED THAT A 1-3-PAGE DOCUMENT WILL SUFFICE FOR THESE PURPOSES. TASK 3: DATA MANAGEMENT SUPPORT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO BEST ENABLE NIH DATA MANAGEMENT FOR THE DATA COMMONS CONSORTIUM MEMBERSHIP AS THEY PERFORM THEIR RESPONSIBILITIES AS DEFINED THROUGH THE OTHER TRANSACTIONAL AUTHORITY (OTA) NEGOTIATION PROCESS. THIS INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: 1. WITHIN 15 BUSINESS DAYS OF EXECUTION, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE A STRATEGY FOR ESTABLISHING DATA MANAGEMENT CONTROLS FOR THE DATA COMMONS, INCLUDING (BUT NOT EXCLUSIVE TO) TOPMED AND GTEX DATA AND METADATA, AND THE ONGOING CONSORTIUM EFFORTS THAT UNDERLIES THIS. THIS WILL BE VETTED WITH KEY NIH STAKEHOLDERS, MODIFIED AS NEEDED, AND THEN FINALIZED. KEY ATTRIBUTES OF THE STRATEGY WILL INCLUDE SOME OR ALL OF THE FOLLOWING (TO INCLUDE MECHANISMS OF ACHIEVING THESE GOALS): A. DATA MIGRATION (TO CLOUD, INTER-CLOUD, DOWNLOAD FROM CLOUD) B. DATA CURRENCY MAINTENANCE C. METADATA MANAGEMENT D. METADATA CONFIGURATION AND MANAGEMENT IN SRA/SDDP/FUSERA OR OTHER NIH-PRESCRIBED ACCESS CONTROL MECHANISMS E. DATA ACCESS CONTROL AND USER AUTHENTICATION F. CLOUD DATA STORAGE CONFIGURATION AND ADMINISTRATION G. DATA USE MEASUREMENT H. DATA STORAGE COST FORECASTS I. DATA STORAGE USE FORECASTS J. DATA GOVERNANCE K. DATA AVAILABILITY COMMUNICATIONS

description: BASE: 0258-A406-4609 OPTION 1: 0258-A428-4609 OPTION 2: 0258-A443-4609 OPTION 3: 0258-A457-4609 OPTION 4: 0258-B457-4609 OPTION 5: 0258-C457-4609 OPTION 6: IF300302155-940002 THE COBEY GROUP WILL TAKE THE LEAD ON ASSESSING THE HYPOTHETICAL AND ACTUAL IMPACT OF IMMUNE HISTORY ON THE EFFECTIVENESS OF VACCINE CANDIDATES AND MEASURING THE POTENTIAL FOR EVOLUTIONARY ESCAPE FROM VACCINES. THEY WILL ALSO PROVIDE EXTENSIVE MODELING AND STATISTICAL SUPPORT FOR OTHER ACTIVITIES, ESPECIALLY THOSE RELATING TO IMMUNE HISTORY AND EVOLUTION. FINALLY, THE COBEY GROUP WILL PROVIDE ADDITIONAL STATISTICAL AND MODELING EXPERTISE AS DEMANDED BY THE EVOLVING RESEARCH RESULTS, INCLUDING ESTIMATING THE NECESSARY VACCINATION COVERAGE REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE ERADICATION OF TARGETED TYPES AND/OR SUBTYPES. THESE ACTIVITIES ARE PART OF RESEARCH AREA 2. OPTION 23A: 0258-A431-4609 UNDERSTANDING HOW IMMUNITY IS ACQUIRED TO SARS-COV-2 IS ESSENTIAL FOR PREDICTING THE COURSE OF THE EPIDEMIC AND INTERPRETING RESPONSES TO VACCINATION. RECENTLY, TWO MULTI-SITE STUDIES, PARIS/PARIS-2 AND SPARTA, HAVE ESTABLISHED ADULT COHORTS IN WHOM IMMUNE RESPONSES AND RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS WILL BE TRACKED FOR 12 MONTHS. THE OVERARCHING AIM OF THESE STUDIES IS TO UNDERSTAND THE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION AGAINST SARS-COV-2 INFECTION. SECONDARILY, THEY WILL INVESTIGATE THE DURABILITY OF RESPONSES AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MILD VERSUS SEVERE INFECTIONS. THERE ARE TWO MAJOR STATISTICAL CHALLENGES IN THIS WORK. THE FIRST IS THAT, AS IN ALL OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES, CONFOUNDING CAN CREATE MISLEADING CORRELATIONS (KAHN ET AL., AM J EPIDEMIOL (IN PRESS); DOI: 10.1101/2020.05.02.20088765). THE SECOND IS THAT IMMUNE RESPONSES ARE COMPLICATED AND VARY EXTENSIVELY BETWEEN PEOPLE FOR REASONS THAT REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THE INCLUSION OF EIGHT SITES WITH DIFFERENT POPULATIONS (STUDENTS, HEALTHCARE WORKERS, ETC.), WHICH WILL EXPERIENCE DIFFERENT RISKS OF INFECTION AT DIFFERENT TIMES, AND HIGH-DIMENSIONAL IMMUNE OBSERVATIONS FROM UP TO 12,000 PARTICIPANTS SHOULD REDUCE BIAS AND INCREASE THE PRECISION AND RANGE OF BIOLOGICAL HYPOTHESES THAT CAN BE TESTED. WE THUS PROPOSE TO PERFORM, IN CLOSE COORDINATION WITH THE PARIS AND SPARTA PIS, SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS TO UNDERSTAND IN GREATER QUANTITATIVE DETAIL HOW IMMUNE RESPONSES TO SARS-COV-2 EVOLVE OVER TIME AND PROTECT AGAINST INFECTION. OUR ULTIMATE AIM IS TO DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS OF THESE RESPONSES SO THAT WE CAN UNDERSTAND HOW IMMUNITY AND RISK EVOLVE IN INDIVIDUALS AND POPULATIONS OVER TIME. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL 1. QUANTIFY VARIATION IN IMMUNE RESPONSES AFTER SEVERE AND MILD SARS-COV-2 INFECTIONS AND DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS OF HOW THESE RESPONSES VARY OVER TIME. 2. ESTIMATE THE RATE OF ASYMPTOMATIC INFECTIONS. 3. MEASURE CORRELATES AND MEDIATORS OF PROTECTION. 4. ANALYZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SARS-COV-2 TO RESPIRATORY PATHOGEN DYNAMICS AND RESPIRATORY ILLNESS.

description: THE ECONOMETRIC METHODS TO BE USED WILL INCLUDE WEB SCRAPING, TEXTUAL SENTIMENT ANALYSIS, AND SEVERAL FORMS OF ADVANCED REGRESSION PREDICTIVE MODELING TO INCLUDE LOGISTIC, TIME-SERIES, AND HAZARD MODELING. FOR EXAMPLE, WE WOULD DEVELOP SENTIMENT SCORES USING TEXT FROM FDA QUALITY MANAGEMENT DOCUMENTS SUCH AS WARNING LETTERS, TO DETERMINE HOW VARIATION IN LANGUAGE USED IN WARNING LETTERS INFLUENCES FUTURE FIRM QUALITY LEARNING, AS MEASURED BY FUTURE PRODUCT QUALITY RISK. WE WOULD COMBINE THIS WITH PUBLIC DATA OBTAINED BY WEB SCRAPING WEBSITES SUCH AS LINKEDLN AND GLASSDOOR, TO MEASURE HOW ASPECTS OF FIRM LEADERSHIP AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT MAY ACCENTUATE OR ATTENUATE FDA QUALITY MANAGEMENT ACTIONS IN INFLUENCING FIRM QUALITY LEARNING AND REDUCING FUTURE DRUG QUALITY RISK. AS A FURTHER EXAMPLE, WE WOULD ALSO EXPLORE HOW THE EXPERIENCES AND BIASES OF FIRM LEADERSHIP, SUCH AS EDUCATION, TRAINING AND POLITICAL AFFILIATION MAY MODERATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN FDA QUALITY MANAGEMENT ACTIONS AND FUTURE QUALITY RISK. THE PROJECT DELIVERABLE WILL BE A PREDICTIVE MODEL THAT CAN INFORM FDA AS TO WHICH QUALITY MANAGEMENT TECHNIQUES ARE MOST EFFECTIVE AT REDUCING QUALITY RISKS FOR EACH UNIQUE MANAGEMENT TEAM, FIRM, FACILITY OR PRODUCT. THIS INCLUDES THE MOST INFLUENTIAL OR HARMFUL LANGUAGE TO USE IN QUALITY MANAGEMENT TEXT DOCUMENTS FROM THE FDA, OR THE APPROPRIATE FREQUENCY OF FACILITY INSPECTIONS, OR THE LEVEL OF DEPTH OF SCRUTINY OF NEW PRODUCT APPROVALS, THAT MAY BE NECESSARY AND MAY BE DEPENDENT ON FIRM IDIOSYNCRATIC CHARACTERISTICS SUCH AS SENIOR LEADERSHIP OR EMPLOYEE MEASURES WE COLLECT FOR THIS STUDY. THE DEPENDENT VARIABLES IN OUR STUDY WILL BE OBSERVABLES, SUCH AS ADVERSE EVENT REPORTS OR DRUG RECALLS. FURTHER, WE WILL ESTIMATE THE LATENT QUALITY RISK OF A PLANT, BASED ON SIMILAR OBSERVABLES. SUCH A LATENT RISK MODEL WILL BE BASED ON EITHER A HIDDEN MARKOV MODEL OR A DENSITYÂ­ SMOOTHING APPLICATION. LATENT QUALITY RISK WOULD EFFECTIVELY AGGREGATE THE MULTI-DIMENSIONAL QUALITY RISK DATA AVAILABLE INTO A SINGLE QUALITY RISK METRIC FOR USE IN THE ANALYSIS.

description: THE WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY GROUP (WSU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GARRY BUCHKO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD TWO). WSU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST 2 NMR STRUCTURES PER YEAR, WHICH MAY SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR). WSU MAY ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY NMR: WSU (DR. BUCHKO) WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST TWO (2) PROTEINS USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CID RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15NLABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY WSU/PNNL. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION, AND REPORTING: WSU WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. description: THE FELLOWSHIP FOR INTERPRETATION OF GENOMES (FIG) IS A NONPROFIT [501(C)(3)] ORGANIZATION INCORPORATED IN ILLINOIS. FIGÂ€™S OVERALL GOAL IS TO DEVELOP AND SUPPORT THE COMPUTATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED TO INTERPRET GENOMES. FIGÂ€™S PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY WILL BE TO SUPPORT ACCURATE, FULLY AUTOMATED ANNOTATION OF MANY THOUSANDS OF MICROBIAL AND PHAGE GENOMES AVAILABLE IN PATRIC AND THROUGH PATRIC SERVICES. THIS WORK WILL FOCUS ON THE AUTOMATION OF FORMERLY MANUAL STEPS IN THE CURATION PROCESS, LIKE THE CONSTRUCTION OF NEW SUBSYSTEMS AND PROTEIN FAMILIES WITH AN EMPHASIS ON GENES RELATING TO AMR, BACTERIOPHAGE RESEARCH AND OTHER DETERMINANTS OF NIAID INTEREST. WE WILL ALSO ENGAGE IN THE CURATION AND UNIFICATION OF THE MANY METADATA TYPES OF HIGHTHROUGHPUT OMICS DATASETS FOR PATRIC. THIS BECOMES HIGHLY RELEVANT AS MORE AND MORE RESEARCH GROUPS RELEASE THEIR DATA, BUT NO STANDARDIZED PROTOCOLS AND FORMATS ARE IN PLACE. FOR AN INTEGRATED RESOURCE LIKE PATRIC THE DATA STANDARDIZATION AND UNIFICATION IS IMPERATIVE. AND THIRDLY WE WILL BE INVOLVED IN THE PRODUCTION OF FULL WORKFLOW TRAINING COURSES AND MOOCS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON THEIR USABILITY FOR TEACHING PURPOSES. WE BELIEVE THIS TO BE OF GREAT IMPORTANCE AS THE STUDENTS OF TODAY WILL BE THE PATRIC USERS OF TOMORROW.

description: DR. KONG FROM NYU HAS DESIGNED A PANEL OF IMMUNOGENS ENGRAFTING THE V1V2 DOMAIN INTO TRIMERIC AND PENTAMERIC SCAFFOLDS IN STRUCTURALLY CONSTRAINED CONFORMATIONS. THEY ALSO FUSED V1V2 TO AN FC FRAGMENT TO MIMIC THE UNCONSTRAINED V1V2 CONFORMATION. THEY HAVE TESTED THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF 12 V1V2-SCAFFOLD PROTEIN IMMUNOGENS. THE RESULTS SHOW THE INDUCTION OF V2-SPECIÃ¯Â¬Ï¿½C ABS THAT ARE REACTIVE WITH V1V2 AND WITH GP120 ENVS FROM DIVERSE STRAINS AND CLADES (ZOLLA-PAZNER, ET AL., 2016). BASED ON THESE STUDIES, NYU WILL SUGGEST LUNA TO CHOOSE THE IMMUNOGENS FOR CNT LOADING AND CO-DELIVERY WITH THE ENCODING MRNA IN PHASE II. THE SEQUENCE OF THE MRNA THAT TARGETS HIV WILL BE SELECTED PER THE SUBCONTRACTORÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RECOMMENDATION FOR BEST INDICATION OF ABS PRODUCTION IN RABBIT STUDIES. THE GLYCOPROTEIN V1V2 WILL BE PRODUCED (TOTALLY 30 MG) AND PROVIDED BY NYU AND NYU WILL PROVIDE LUNA A REPORT FOR THE PROTEIN PURIFICATION (GEL ANALYSIS) AND CHARACTERIZATION (WESTERN BLOT) REPORT. LUNA WILL WORK WITH PROF. KONG FROM THE NYU SCHOOL OF MEDICINE TO EVALUATE THE CNT FORMULATION IMMUNOGENICITY IN RABBITS. DURING THE PHASE II, LUNA WILL PERFORM TESTING UNDER TWO DIFFERENT EXPERIMENTAL SETS. THE FIRST GOAL OF THE SET A TESTING WILL BE TO DOWN-SELECT ONE BEST PERFORMING CNT-MRNA FORMULATION (FROM THREE) FOR CONTINUED USE WITH PROTEIN (ANTIGEN) CO-DELIVERY IN THE SET B EXPERIMENTS. THE ENVISIONED TEST SETUP IS SHOWN IN FIGURE 1. THREE GROUPS OF RABBIT (5 ANIMALS FOR EACH GROUP) WILL BE USED FOR EACH SET. 30 RABBITS (15 IN PERIOD A AND ANOTHER 15 IN PERIOD B) WILL BE USED. WE WILL USE FEMALE NEW ZEALAND WHITE RABBITS 6-8 WEEKS OLD (~2KG). RABBITS WILL BE PURCHASED FROM COMMERCIAL VENDORS AND HOUSED IN THE ANIMAL FACILITY AT NYU SCHOOL OF MEDICINE IN ACCORDANCE WITH AN IACUC-APPROVED PROTOCOL.

VIRUS WILL ALSO BE CULTURED FROM EACH SAMPLE BY AMPLIFICATION IN MDCK CELLS, AND VIRAL STOCKS WILL BE PRODUCED. THE ANTIGENIC RELATEDNESS TO VIRUSES IN THE CURRENT VACCINE WILL ALSO BE INVESTIGATED. FINALLY, WE WILL COMPARE THE BASELINE SEQUENCE DATA OBTAINED FROM THE INITIAL SAMPLE WITH THE SEQUENCE OF THE CULTURED VIRUS, AND ASSESS THE INTRINSIC SEQUENCE DIVERSITY OF THE INFLUENZA VIRUS POPULATION IN EACH CLINICAL SAMPLE. ALL SEQUENCE DATA WILL BE SENT TO THE CEIRS DATA PROCESSING AND COORDINATING CENTER FOR DISSEMINATION TO PUBLIC DATABASES.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON PROTEIN PRODUCTION GROUP (UW-PPG), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF WESLEY C. VAN VOORHIS, M.D., PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK (OPTION PERIOD TWO OPTION QUANTITIES 3, 4, 5 &6) TO ADDITIONALLY SUPPORT THE BASIC REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD TWO TERM) OF THE SSGCID CONTRACT (CONTRACT NR HHSN272201700059C). UW-PPG WILL SUPPORT ONE OPTION QUANTITY EFFORT (OQS 3 & 4) TO PROVIDE PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND LEAD ONE OPTION QUANTITY EFFORT (OQS 5 & 6) TO SUPPORT AMR DRUG DEVELOPMENT FOR ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE AND SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS. A. OPTION QUANTITY EFFORTS UW-PPG WILL USE OPTION QUANTITY RESOURCES (OQS 3 & 4) TO SUPPORT A PROJECT LED BY UW-CRYOEM FOCUSING ON PROVIDING PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS THROUGH STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY STUDIES OF PROTEINS FROM FLAVIVIRUS, ALPHAVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS FAMILIES. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS OPTION QUANTITY PROPOSAL IS TO INCREASE STRUCTURAL COVERAGE OF THE GN-GC GLYCOPROTEINS AND RDRP FROM THESE VIRUSES, PRIMARILY TO FACILITATE VACCINE AND DRUG DEVELOPMENT, RESPECTIVELY. STAFF FROM UW-PPG WILL DESIGN, EXPRESS AND PURIFY FULL-LENGTH AND SINGLE-DOMAIN CONSTRUCTS OF RDRP, FOR SUBSEQUENT STRUCTURE SOLUTION AT UCB. ADDITIONALLY, UW-PPG WILL LEAD OPTION QUANTITY EFFORTS (OQS 5 & 6) TO SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF NEW DRUGS AGAINST ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT (AMR) BACTERIA, INCLUDING THOSE CAUSING SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS OPTION QUANTITY PROPOSAL WILL BE FULFILLED BY PERFORMING STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION OF OUTER MEMBRANE PROTEIN OMPA AND FROM A. BAUMANNII AND OTHER GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIAL AS WELL AS FROM TARGETS NOMINATED BY INDUSTRY AND ACADEMIA AS WELL AS BY PERFORMING STRUCTURE SOLUTION OF PROTEINS FROM N. GONORRHOEAE AND M. GENITALIUM WITH THE GOAL OF IDENTIFYING AND OPTIMIZING NOVEL LEAD COMPOUNDS AGAINST THESE TARGETS. IN ADDITION TO LEADING THE PROJECT, UW-PPG WILL CLONE, EXPRESSION TEST AND PURIFY TARGET PROTEINS FOR SUBSEQUENT STRUCTURE SOLUTION AT UCB.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON PROTEIN PRODUCTION GROUP (UW-PPG), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF WESLEY C. VAN VOORHIS, M.D., PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD TWO). UW-PPG WILL GENERATE TARGET CLONES, PERFORM SMALL- AND LARGE-SCALE SCREENING, UPSCALE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION OF THE CLONES AND LEAD TWO STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY (SVTD) STUDIES (SVTD_08 AND SVTD_09). UW-PPG WILL MANAGE (SHEPHERD) OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. CLONING, EXPRESSION TESTING, UPSCALE AND PURIFICATION OF SSGCID TARGETS: UW-PPG WILL PERFORM CLONING MAINLY USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PCR-BASED LIGATION INDEPENDENT CLONING INTO E. COLI EXPRESSION VECTORS. UW-PPG WILL SCREEN THEIR EXPRESSION AND SOLUBILITY PROPERTIES USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PROTOCOLS, INCLUDING, AS NEEDED, MULTIPLE EXPRESSION SYSTEMS AND CLEAVAGE SYSTEMS. UW-PPG WILL GENERATE LARGE SCALE EXPRESSIONS OF TARGETS FOR HIGHLY PURIFIED TARGET PROTEINS OR PROTEIN FRAGMENTS AND PRODUCE THEM IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY FOR STRUCTURE DETERMINATION THROUGH STANDARDIZATION AND AUTOMATION OF PROTOCOLS. UW-PPG WILL EVALUATE THE PURITY, CONCENTRATION AND BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES (E.G. PROTEIN FOLDING, AGGREGATION, AND/OR STABILITY) OF THE PURIFIED SAMPLES TO ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORTS. UW-PPG WILL LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDIES: UW-PPG WILL USE OPTION PERIOD TWO TERM RESOURCES TO LEAD TWO STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDIES: SVTD_08 IS ENTITLED, Â€ŒTARGET SCREENING USING THE J&J JUMPSTARTER COMPOUND LIBRARYÂ€?, THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO DEVELOP HIGH QUALITY HITS FROM A LIBRARY SCREEN, WITH STRUCTURAL INFORMATION, TO ALLOW RATIONAL STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DEVELOPMENT FOR LEISHMANIASIS AND CRYPTOCOCCOSIS. SVTD_09 IS ENTITLED Â€ŒFACILITATION OF STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DEVELOPMENT ON NAEGLERIA FOWLERI GLUCOKINASEÂ€?, THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO USE STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DEVELOPMENT TO IMPROVE HITS FOUND BY AFFINITY PROCEDURE. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-PPG WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-PPG WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY UW-PPG STAFF WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. UW-PPG WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. UW-PPG WILL CONDUCT THEIR WORK WITH THE AIM TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS IN HIGH IMPACT PUBLICATIONS.

description: I. SUBTASK 1: EFFICACY TESTING OF CANDIDATE THERAPEUTICS FOR USE AGAINST MOUSE MODELS OF FUNGAL INFECTION THE CONTRACTOR SHALL EVALUATE THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF CANDIDATE THERAPEUTICS BY EXAMINING A SINGLE FUNGAL SPECIES IN A MOUSE MODEL AS DICTATED BY THE SRF. THERE ARE TWO GROUPS OF MOUSE MODELS, AND THE SPECIES THAT MAY BE USED FOR TESTING IN THOSE MODELS ARE LISTED IN TABLE 1 BELOW. THE NUMBER OF EVALUATIONS TO BE PERFORMED BY THE CONTRACTOR FOR EACH OF THE TWO GROUPS OF MOUSE MODELS ARE LISTED IN TABLE 1 BELOW. FOR EACH EVALUATION, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL: A. INCLUDE UNTREATED AND POSITIVE CONTROL GROUPS. B. PERFORM A FUNGAL BURDEN STUDY EVALUATING FUNGAL BURDEN IN TREATED ANIMALS AND CONTROLS. C. PERFORM A SURVIVAL STUDY EVALUATING FUNGAL BURDEN, CLINICAL SIGNS, AND SURVIVAL IN CONTROL AND TREATED ANIMALS. D. ALL ANIMALS SHALL BE OBSERVED FOR UP TO 30 DAYS POST CHALLENGE. E. USE A NUMBER OF ANIMALS NEEDED TO ACHIEVE STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE II. SUBTASK 2: MAXIMUM TOLERATED DOSE ASSESSMENT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL TEST THE TOXICITY OF CANDIDATE THERAPEUTIC IN IMMUNOCOMPETENT MICE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT THREE (3) TOXICITY EVALUATIONS, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FOLLOWING: A. ADMINISTER INCREASING DOSES OF CANDIDATE THERAPEUTIC. B. EVALUATE MICE FOR WEIGHT LOSS, CLINICAL SIGNS, AND MORTALITY. C. INCLUDE UNTREATED CONTROLS. D. HOLD MICE FOR UP TO 30 DAYS. ILL. SUBTASK 3: PHARMACOKINETIC AND TOLERABILITY ASSESSMENT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL TEST THE TOLERABILITY AND PHARMACOKINETICS OF CANDIDATE THERAPEUTICS IN MICE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT FOUR (4) TOLERABILITY AND PHARMACOKINETIC EVALUATIONS, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FOLLOWING: A. EVALUATE MICE FOR WEIGHT LOSS AND MORTALITY. B. INCLUDE UNTREATED CONTROLS. C. INCLUDE NUMBER OF MICE NEEDED TO ACHIEVE STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE. D. INCLUDE NUMBER OF MICE NEEDED TO DEVELOP A PHARMACOKINETIC CURVE AFTER THE FINAL DOSE. E. SHIP SAMPLES OF PLASMA AND UP TO TWO TISSUES TO THE SPONSOR, OR A LAB OF THEIR CHOICE, FOR ANALYSIS. F. HOLD MICE FOR UP TO 30 DAYS FOR OBSERVATION.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK (OPTION PERIOD TWO OPTION QUANTITIES 1,2,3&4) TO ADDITIONALLY SUPPORT THE BASIC REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD TWO TERM) OF THE SSGCID CONTRACT (CONTRACT NR HHSN272201700059C). UW-CRYOEM WILL SUPPORT ONE OPTION QUANTITY EFFORT (OQS 1 & 2) TO DEVELOP NANOPARTICLE HCV VACCINES AND WILL LEAD ONE OPTION QUANTITY EFFORT (OQS 3 & 4) FOCUSING ON PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS. A. OPTION QUANTITY EFFORTS UW-CROEM WILL USE OPTION QUANTITY RESOURCES (OQS 1 & 2) TO SUPPORT A PROJECT LED BY UW-IPD FOCUSING ON DESIGN AND CHARACTERIZATION OF SELF-ASSEMBLING NANOPARTICLE VACCINES AGAINST HCV. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS OPTION QUANTITY PROPOSAL IS TO DESIGN A NOVEL MULTI-COMPONENT SELF-ASSEMBLING NANOPARTICLE HCV E1/E2 VACCINE THAT CAN DISPLAY A Â€ŒMOSAICÂ€? FORMAT OF MULTIPLE E1/E2 VARIANTS ON THEIR SURFACE. SPECIFICALLY, MIXING OF TWO OR MORE DIFFERENT E1/E2 HETERODIMERS WITH A SECOND COMPONENT OF A SELF-ASSEMBLING NANOCAGE SYSTEM WILL RESULT IN A SPECTRUM OF CO-DISPLAYED HCV E1/E2 VARIANTS. STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL ANALYZE THE VARIOUS SAMPLES USING HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN EM TO ASSESS THEIR QUALITY AND WILL BE THE LEAD PERSON ON ALL ASPECTS OF STRUCTURE DETERMINATION INCLUDING DATA COLLECTION/PROCESSING AND STRUCTURE ANALYSIS/DATA INTERPRETATION. IT IS EXPECTED THAT AT LEAST ONE CRYOEM STRUCTURE WILL BE SOLVED AS A PART OF THIS PROJECT. UW-CROEM WILL USE OPTION QUANTITY RESOURCES (OQS 3 & 4) TO LEAD A PROJECT FOCUSING ON PROVIDING PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS THROUGH STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY STUDIES OF PROTEINS FROM FLAVIVIRUS, ALPHAVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS FAMILIES. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS OPTION QUANTITY PROPOSAL IS TO INCREASE STRUCTURAL COVERAGE OF THE GN-GC GLYCOPROTEINS AND RDRP FROM THESE VIRUSES, PRIMARILY TO FACILITATE VACCINE AND DRUG DEVELOPMENT, RESPECTIVELY. STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE PURIFICATION OF GLYCOPROTEIN ECTODOMAINS AND LEAD THE CRYOEM STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORT OF GN-GC IN COMPLEX WITH NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODY FAB FRAGMENTS. IT IS EXPECTED THAT AT LEAST ONE CRYOEM STRUCTURE WILL BE SOLVED AS A PART OF THIS PROJECT.
