description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD TWO). UW-NMR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 3 NMR STRUCTURES DURING THIS SIX-MONTH SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, WHICH INCLUDES FULFILMENT OF THE EXPECTED STRUCTURE GOAL FROM THIS PERIOD (1 STRUCTURE, 9/1/2019 Â€“ 2/29/2020) IN ADDITION TO THE COMPLETION OF THE UNFULFILLED GOAL FROM THE PREVIOUS SUBCONTRACT PERIOD (2 STRUCTURES, PERIOD 9/1/2018-8/31/2019). UW-NMR WILL ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A.STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF 3 PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES BY NMR:UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF THREE (3) PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CID RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITY ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB;HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD TWO). UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST FOUR CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR. UCB MAY ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST FOUR PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEX USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. FINALLY, WE WILL USE RECENTLY DEVELOPED ROSETTA TOOLS, WHICH ALLOWED US TO DETERMINE THE FIRST HIGH-RESOLUTION STRUCTURE OF A CORONAVIRUS SPIKE GLYCOPROTEIN TRIMER. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-CRYOEM WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND CAPACITY BUILDING THROUGH THE FOLLOWING PRODUCTS AND SERVICES: Â€¢ ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT AND END-STATE VISIONING Â€“ ENGAGING STATE LEADERSHIP AND PROJECT MANAGERS TO CREATE A SHARED UNDERSTANDING OF THE BUSINESS DRIVERS BEHIND THE TRANSFORMATION, FOLLOWED BY INTERVIEWING A BROAD CROSS SECTION OF STAKEHOLDERS, RANGING FROM SENIOR LEADERSHIP TO THE PEOPLE DOING THE DAY-TO-DAY WORK. THE INTERVIEWS HELP IDENTIFY WHAT ISNÂ€™T WORKING AS WELL AS IT COULD, AND WHERE AGILE WILL HELP IT IMPROVE. AN ASSESSMENT IS DEVELOPED TO INCLUDE A RECOMMENDATION ON STRUCTURAL CHANGES REQUIRED TO HELP THE STATE MEET ITS GOALS, ALONG WITH PORTFOLIO, PRODUCT, AND DELIVERY TEAM STRUCTURE. A WORKING STRUCTURE WOULD BE DRAFTED TO INCLUDE A GOVERNANCE MODEL, FRAMEWORK, METRICS FOR MEASURING PROGRESS ON THE ASSESSMENT AND AGAINST BUSINESS OUTCOMES, AND A MEANS TO INSTRUMENT THE PROCESS WITH TOOLING. Â€¢ COACHING STRATEGY - COACHING INVOLVES WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE TEAMS, IN ADDITION TO THE STANDARD SERIES OF TRAINING AND WORKSHOPS. COACHES CONDUCT A COMPETENCY ASSESSMENT TO BASELINE ADOPTION IN KEY COMPETENCY AREAS, WORK WITH THE TEAMS UNTIL THEY ARE AT A POINT OF SUSTAINABILITY, AND CORRELATE TEAM PERFORMANCE TO ORGANIZATION OUTCOMES IN THE WEEKLY (OR MONTHLY) STATUS REPORTS. Â€¢ TRANSFORMATION ROADMAP - THE TRANSFORMATION PLAN WILL DEFINE WHAT GROUPS OF TEAMS WILL MOVE TO AGILE, WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO WORK IN A MORE TRADITIONAL WATERFALL METHOD, WHAT ORDER THEYÂ€™LL DEPLOY, AND WHAT THE STEPS WILL LOOK LIKE AS THEY MAKE THEIR WAY ALONG THE TRANSFORMATION JOURNEY. Â€¢ CHANGE MANAGEMENT PLAN - WORKING SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH THE GOVERNING BODY LEADING THE TRANSITION, GOALS AND OBJECTIVES ARE SET, A 90-DAY ROLLING PLAN IS CREATED AND MAINTAINED Â€“ WITH WEEKLY STATUS REPORTS AND REVIEWS OCCURRING AT 30-DAY INTERVALS. A COMMUNICATION PLAN IS DEFINED AND EXECUTED, INCLUDING ESTABLISHING OFFICE HOURS, CONDUCTING LUNCH AND LEARNS, OR ANYTHING NECESSARY TO KEEP PEOPLE INFORMED AND CREATE SAFETY AND AWARENESS AROUND THE AGILE TRANSFORMATION INITIATIVE. Â€¢ AGILE ORGANIZATIONAL PILOT AND ENTERPRISE ROLLOUT Â€“ LEVERAGING THE DEFINED END-STATE, APPROPRIATE TEAMS (DELIVERY, PROGRAM, PORTFOLIO GOVERNANCE) ARE FORMED; GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORKS ARE ESTABLISHED, INCLUDING METRICS USED TO BASELINE PERFORMANCE OF THE NEW TEAMS AND MEASURE AND EVALUATE PERFORMANCE OVER TIME; AN EVALUATION AND REVIEW OF AGILE TOOLS MAY BE PERFORMED IF REQUESTED. THIS SHOULD PROVIDE A SOLID PERFORMANCE BASELINE CENTERED ON THE METRICS, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT. Â€¢ ADDITIONAL SERVICES INCLUDE: O AGILE BOOT CAMP O AGILE REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT COURSE O AGILE GOVERNANCE AND METRICS WORKSHOP O CONTINUED COACHING SERVICES O SPRINT PLANNING WORKSHOPS

description: AMEND 1 241,211 AGREEMENT 3,133,362 THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE FIELD TRIAL AND THE RESEARCH LABORATORY TO PERFORM ASSAY WORK FOR A NATURAL HISTORY STUDY TO DESCRIBE THE CLINICAL OUTCOMES (PARTICULARLY THE NEUROLOGIC AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES) OF POSTNATALLY ACQUIRED ZIKA VIRUS INFECTION IN INFANTS AND CHILDREN IN GUATEMALA. UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO (CU) WILL IMPLEMENT THE PROTOCOL AND CONDUCT OF ALL STUDY ACTIVITIES PERFORMED BY THE SUBCONTRACTED SITES (CHCO AND FSIG), IN ACCORDANCE WITH ALL FEDERAL, STATE, AND LOCAL REGULATIONS, REQUIREMENTS AND GUIDELINES, INCLUDING DHHS AND NIH POLICIES, THE MOP, AND SOP. CU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SATISFYING ALL INTERNATIONAL, LOCAL AND COMMUNITY BASED GUIDELINES, CUSTOMS, AND REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS TO CONDUCT THIS STUDY IN GUATEMALA. CU PI WILL ENSURE THAT THE APPROPRIATE FACILITY RESOURCES ARE AVAILABLE AT THE SITE IN GUATEMALA FOR THE CONDUCT OF THE STUDY, AND THAT APPROPRIATE PERSONNEL IS APPOINTED AND TRAINED FOR THE RECRUITMENT, ENROLLMENT, EVALUATION AND RETENTION OF STUDY VOLUNTEERS. A LABORATORY MOP AND SOP WILL BE DEVELOPED OR ADAPTED BY BCM AND CU PIS TO ENSURE THE PROPER SPECIMEN COLLECTION, PROCESSING, AND SHIPMENT BY THE FIELD SITE TO THE DMID REPOSITORY. ALL PERSONNEL INVOLVED IN PROTOCOL IMPLEMENTATION WILL FOLLOW FEDERAL AND STATE REGULATIONS PERTAINING TO GCP IN THE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. CU WILL ORGANIZE AND PARTICIPATE, ALONG WITH BCM AND SUBCONTRACTED SITES, THE TASK ORDER SITE ASSESSMENT VISIT AND INITIATION MEETINGS, ATTEND ALL TASK ORDER-SPECIFIC TELECONFERENCES AND MEETINGS, AND ALL ADDITIONAL AD-HOC MEETINGS AND TELECONFERENCES. CU WILL ENSURE THE DEVELOPMENT OF ALL DOCUMENTS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE SUBCONTRACT INSTITUTIONS, THAT PERTAIN TO THE PROTOCOL IMPLEMENTATION PROCESS (PROTOCOL AMENDMENTS, ICF, STUDY MATERIALS, SOURCE DOCUMENTS, MEETING MINUTES, ACTION ITEMS LIST) WHICH WILL BE REVIEWED BY BCM FOR CLARITY, CONSISTENCY AND ADHERENCE TO APPLICABLE LOCAL AND FEDERAL REGULATIONS PRIOR TO DISTRIBUTION TO DMID AND SUBCONTRACTED SITES. STUDY IMPLEMENTATION WILL BE CONDUCTED AS PER FOUR TASK ORDER OPTIONS, BASE AND OPTIONS 1 Â€“ 4. FROM THE STUDY START ON JANUARY 23, 2017, A ONE YEAR ENROLLMENT PERIOD AND ONE YEAR FOLLOW UP IS EXPECTED. CU AND SUBCONTRACT SITES WILL PERFORM PERIODIC ASSESSMENTS OF THE STUDY PROCEDURES, GOALS, AND TIMELINES, TO ENSURE THAT MILESTONES ARE BEING MET. IF CONCERNS OR ISSUES ARE IDENTIFIED, THE PIS WILL MODIFY THE PROJECT MANAGEMENT PLAN TO ADDRESS ALL ISSUES AND IMPROVE THE CONDUCT OF THE STUDY. FINALLY, CU AND SUBCONTRACTING INSTITUTIONS (FSIG AND CHCO) IN COORDINATION WITH BCM WILL MAKE ARRANGEMENTS FOR THE STUDY CLOSE OUT VISIT TO TAKE PLACE BASED ON GUIDANCE FROM DMID, ONCE ALL STUDY PROCEDURES HAVE BEEN COMPLETED, DATA CLEANING HAS BEEN COMPLETED, DATABASE HAS BEEN LOCKED, AND LABORATORY ANALYSIS HAS BEEN FINALIZED.

description: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH HAS THREE MAJOR TASKS: 1. SAMPLE COLLECTION AT MINE SITES; 2. POST COLLECTION CHARACTERIZATION (SIZE, SHAPE, COMPOSITION); 3.EVALUATION OF THE SOURCE CONTRIBUTION TO RCMD. TASKS 1 AND 3 WILL BE PERFORMED BY THE TEAM AT MICHIGAN TECH. TASK 2 WILL BE DIVIDED BY BOTH TEAMS. THE TEAM AT MICHIGAN TECH WILL CHARACTERIZE THE COLLECTED SAMPLES USING CONVENTIONAL TECHNIQUES SUCH AS THERMOGRAVIMETRIC ANALYSIS (TGA), SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPE-ENERGY DISPERSIVE X-RAY SPECTROSCOPY (SEM-EDS), AND X-RAY DIFFRACTION. THE TEAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL EVALUATE THREE STATE-OF-THE-ART TECHNIQUES (FIELD-FLOW FRACTIONATION, X-RAY MICRO, AND NANO CT AND MICRO XRF) USING ADVANCED INSTRUMENTATION FOR RCMD CHARACTERIZATION, FOR THE FIRST TIME. THE RESULTS OBTAINED FROM TASKS 1,2, AND 3, WILL HELP IN EVALUATION OF THE FEASIBILITY OF FFF, NANO AND MACRO X-CT AND MICRO XRF FOR THE ANALYSIS OF NANO AND MICRON-SIZED COAL MINE DUST PARTICLES. THE PARTICLE CHARACTERIZATION RESULTS OBTAINED FROM THESE ADVANCED TECHNIQUES WILL BE COMBINED WITH THE RESULTS OBTAINED BY THE MICHIGAN TECH TEAM TO GENERATE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL MAP OF SPECIFIC RCMD METRICS, SUCH AS RESPIRABLE DUST PARTICLE COMPOSITION, SIZE, AND SHAPE OF PARTICLES COLLECTED ON A FILTER, AND ACROSS THE THICKNESS DIMENSION OF THE PARTICLE BED FOR SELECTED SAMPLES. THE RESULTS OBTAINED FROM THIS WORK SHOULD YIELD INFORMATION ON TEMPORAL CHANGE OF DUST COMPOSITION AND PARTICLE SIZE ASSOCIATED WITH THE MINE OPERATIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. THE COLLECTIVE INFORMATION WILL BE USED TO EVALUATE THE SOURCE CONTRIBUTION TO RCMD FOR EACH MINE. FEASIBILITY OF ADVANCED PARTICLE CHARACTERIZATION INSTRUMENTS SUCH AS FFF, MICRO/NANO X-CT, AND MICRO XRF WILL BE EVALUATED. PROTOCOLS WILL BE ESTABLISHED FOR THESE INSTRUMENTS FOR FACILE ANALYSES OF COAL MINE DUST PARTICLES. THE RESULTS OBTAINED FROM TASK 2 (FIELD-FLOW FRACTIONATION) WILL PROVIDE INFORMATION ON THE SIZE DISTRIBUTION AND ELEMENTAL COMPOSITION OF NANOPARTICLES IN COAL MINE DUST FOR THE FIRST TIME. CONSIDERING THE FACT THAT NANOPARTICLES ARE MUCH MORE TOXIC TO HUMANS THAN LARGER PARTICLES, THIS TASK WILL PROVIDE VITAL INFORMATION FOR THE SAFETY OF COAL MINE WORKERS.

description: SUBK 2 OF 2 FOR CHEROKEE HEALTH SYSTEMS SUBK 130533 THE NIH ALL OF US RESEARCH PROGRAM (ALSO REFERRED TO AS AOURP OR THE PROGRAM) IS INTENDED TO REFLECT THE RICH DIVERSITY OF AMERICA, ENSURING THAT ENROLLMENT IS OPEN AND ACCESSIBLE TO ALL GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO SOCIOECONOMIC, RACIAL/ETHNIC, ANCESTRAL BACKGROUNDS, AGE, SEX AND GENDER, GEOGRAPHIC, ABILITY/DISABILITY, ETC. AS SUCH, ONE OF THE KEY POINTS OF CONSIDERATION DURAING PROGRAM ENROLLMENT IS ENSURING THAT THE MAJORITY OF THE PARTICIPANT DATA AVAILABLE TO RESEARCHERS COMES FROM MEMBERS OF COMMUNITIES WHICH HAVE BEEN HISTORICALLY UNDERREPRESENTED IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH (UBR), INCLUDING ENROLLED PARTICIPANTS RESULTING FROM THE DURABLE AND STABLE RELATIONSHIPS WITH VULNERABLE COMMUNITIES SERVED BY FQHC ENROLLMENT CENTERS ACROSS THE NATION. THE GOAL OF THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) IS TO CONTINUE AOURP EFFORTS WITH SELECTED FQHCS INTO THE NEXT PHASE OF AOURP HEALTHCARE PROVIDER ORGANIZATION (HPO) ACTIVITIES AIMED TO INCREASE THE TASK ORDER SUBCONTRACT AGREEMENT NO. 130532 PARTICIPATION OF UBR COMMUNITIES. SINCE THE BEGINNING OF THIS EFFORT, FQHCS HAVE ENROLLED MORE THAN 12,0001 PARTICIPANTS FROM THEIR UNDERSERVED OR UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES. THEY HAVE INCREASED THEIR CAPACITY TO SUPPORT THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM, SCALING FQHC OPERATIONS, PARTNERING WITH FELLOW FQHCS, WHILE UNDER MITREÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CENTRAL COORDINATION, OR MONITORING AND MANAGEMENT MODEL. FQHCS HAVE CONSISTENTLY SOUGHT TO CONTINUE THIS WORK BY USING LESSONS LEARNED TO INFORM PROCESS IMPROVEMENT OPPORTUNITIES WITHIN THE CENTRAL COORDINATION MODEL. THIS SOW DELINEATES THE TASKS AND ASSOCIATED ACTIVITIES REQUIRED OF THE FQHC IN SUPPORT OF THE AOURP FQHC PROJECT. THE SCOPE OF THIS SOW IS TO CONTINUE TO PLAN AND IMPLEMENT PROGRAM ACTIVITIES, TO REFINE AND HONE PROCESSES FOR ENGAGEMENT, ENROLLMENT, RETENTION, AND TO CONTRIBUTE EXPERTISE AND EVIDENCE-BASED LEARNINGS THAT LEAD TO THE EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROGRAM EFFORT.

description: WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY THE WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY SUBCONTRACT WILL HAVE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR TARGET PROTEINS THAT ARE NOT SUITABLE FOR HIGH THROUGHPUT EXPRESSION IN E. COLI AS SOLUBLE PROTEINS. THIS MAY INCLUDE GLYCOSYLATED PROTEINS AND EXTRACELLULAR PROTEINS AS WELL AS ANY TARGET PROTEINS THAT MAY REASONABLY BE EXPECTED TO BE MORE EFFECTIVELY PRODUCED, PURIFIED AND CRYSTALLIZED USING MAMMALIAN OR INSECT CELL EXPRESSION SYSTEMS. WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY WILL PROVIDE THE PROTEINS AND DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS NECESSARY TO DETERMINE THE STRUCTURES OF AT LEAST 3 TARGET PROTEINS PER YEAR A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION PIPELINE 1. TARGET SELECTION A. TARGETS OF BIOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: SELECT HUMAN PATHOGEN TARGETS THAT ARE EXPECTED TO HAVE AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGICAL ROLE; AND FOR WHICH KNOWLEDGE OF THE 3D STRUCTURE AND, IF APPROPRIATE, OF ITS INTERACTING MOLECULES/COMPOUNDS, IS EXPECTED TO HAVE AN IMPACT ON BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH. EXAMPLES OF TARGETS OF INTEREST INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: Â· PROTEINS INVOLVED IN PATHOGENESIS, SUCH AS INVASINS, ADHESINS, TOXINS; Â· PROTEINS ESSENTIAL TO THE PATHOGENÂ€™S LIFE AND REPRODUCTIVE CYCLE; Â· PROTEINS INVOLVED IN EVASION OR SABOTAGE OF HOST IMMUNITY; Â· PROTEIN MARKERS OF ACUTE OR CHRONIC INFECTION; Â· COMPLEXES WITH NATURAL SUBSTRATES/COFACTORS, RECEPTORS, OR MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES; Â· PROTEIN SPLICE VARIANTS, POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS AND OTHER FUNCTIONALLY CHARACTERIZED VARIANTS. B. MICROBIAL ORGANISMS OF INTEREST: SELECT TARGETS FOR 3D STRUCTURE DETERMINATION MUST BE SELECTED PRIMARILY FROM ORGANISMS IN THE NIAID CATEGORY A-C PRIORITY PATHOGENS LIST (HTTP://WWW.NIAID.NIH.GOV/TOPICS/BIODEFENSERELATED/BIODEFENSE/RESEARCH/PAGES/CAT A.ASPX), AS WELL AS ORGANISMS CAUSING EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES (HTTP://WWW.NIAID.NIH.GOV/TOPICS/EMERGING/PAGES/LIST.ASPX), AND THEIR PHYLOGENETICALLY RELATED SPECIES. TARGETS CAN ALSO BE SELECTED FROM OTHER HUMAN PATHOGENS (WITH THE EXCEPTION OF HIV) AND THEIR PHYLOGENETICALLY RELATED ORGANISMS. C. TARGETS REVIEW AND APPROVAL: CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT TO THE TARGET SELECTION BOARD (SECTION E.2 BELOW) FOR REVIEW, PROPOSALS FOR PATHOGEN TARGETS SELECTED BY THE CONTRACTOR. PROPOSALS MUST ULTIMATELY BE APPROVED BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER TECHNICAL REPRESENTATIVE (COTR) PRIOR TO INITIATION OF ANY ACTIVITY ASSOCIATED WITH THE DETERMINATION OF THEIR STRUCTURE. PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT 2, REPORTING REQUIREMENTS AND DELIVERABLES FOR SPECIFIC GUIDANCE ON SUBMISSION. D. TARGET STATUS MONITORING: CONTRACTOR MUST CHECK ON THE STATUS OF THE PROPOSED AND APPROVED TARGETS AT OTHER DOMESTIC OR INTERNATIONAL STRUCTURAL GENOMICS CENTERS OR CONSORTIA TO ENSURE THERE IS NO DUPLICATION OF EFFORTS. 2. TARGET CLONING, EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION: A. GENERATE TARGET CLONES AND SCREEN THEIR EXPRESSION AND SOLUBILITY PROPERTIES USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PROTOCOLS. PRODUCE HIGH YIELDS OF THE EXPRESSION CLONES USING A VARIETY OF APPROACHES INCLUDING, FOR EXAMPLE, MULTIPLE EXPRESSION SYSTEMS, CLEAVAGE SYSTEMS, OPTIMIZATION OF CODON USAGE AND CHANGES TO THE ENCODED AMINO ACID SEQUENCE. VERIFY SEQUENCE ACCURACY OF EXPRESSION CLONES. B. CONFIDENTIALITY: ENSURE THAT THE SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION ABOUT THE COMMUNITY TARGETS (E.G. ALTERNATIVE A A. IN ADDITION TO PRESENTING TARGET DATA ON THE SCGID'S PUBLIC WEBSITE, REGISTER THE SGCID'S TARGETS AT PUBLIC DATABASE RESOURCES AS DIRECTED BY THE COTR. B. MAKE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE MEASURES TO INTERPRET THE VALIDATION CRITERIA OF THE STRUCTURAL MODEL AND TO ALLOW THE EVALUATION OF ITS QUALITY. C. PHYSICAL CLONES, EXPRESSION CONSTRUCTS, PEPTIDES) INTO PUBLIC REPOSITORIES, SUCH AS THE NIAID BIODEFENSE AND EMERGING INFECTIONS RESEARCH RESOURCES REPOSITORY (HTTP://WWW.BEIRESOURCES.ORG/), OR DNASU MATERIAL REPOSITORY (HTTPS://DNASU.ORG/DNASU/) OR AS DIRECTED BY THE COTR, FOR DISTRIBUTION TO THE BROAD SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. PROVIDE THROUGH THE PUBLIC WEB PORTAL AND VIA A FTP-SITE MIRRORING MECHANISM WITH BIOINFORMATICS RESOURCE CENTERS SUCH AS PATRIC (HTTPS://WWW.PATRICBRC.ORG), OR AS DIRECTED BY THE COTR, THE INFORMATION GENERATED BY THE EXPERIMENTAL PROJECTS AIMED AT BETTER CHARACTERIZING THE FUNCTIONAL ROLE OF THE SELECTED TARGETS, WITHIN TWO MONTHS FROM THE COMPLETION OF EACH PROJECT. description: STRUCTURAL STUDIES ARE CENTRAL TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL AND PROVIDE MODELS THAT GUIDE THE DESIGN OF TREATMENTS. WITHIN THE CENTER FOR STRUCTURAL GENOMICS OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES (CSGID), THE WORK AT THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS SOUTHWESTERN MEDICAL CENTER AT DALLAS WILL HAVE TWO MAIN COMPONENTS: (1) MAINTAINING THE SALVAGE PATHWAY FOR THE COMMUNITY AND CSGID MEMBERS AND (2) PERFORMING CRYO-EM STUDIES FOR SELECTED TARGETS FROM THE CSGID TARGET LIST. UTSW PLANS TO WORK ON 5 SALVAGE PATHWAY STRUCTURES PER YEAR, WITH AT LEAST 1 STRUCTURE SOLVED THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND AT LEAST 1 STRUCTURE SOLVED BY CRYO-EM. UTSW WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO THE OVERALL STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORT IF NEEDED TO ENSURE THAT THE CSGID MEETS ITS GOALS. THE NATURE OF THESE STUDIES REQUIRES THAT WE WORK WHEN OTHER MEMBERS OF THE CSGID DECIDE THAT A PROJECT IS TOO DIFFICULT TO COMPLETE BY MEANS OF STANDARD APPROACHES. WE PREDICT THAT THIS WILL RESULT IN PERIODS DURING WHICH NO SALVAGE TARGETS ARE AVAILABLE TO US AND PERIODS WHEN WE WILL BE WORKING WITH MULTIPLE PROTEINS SIMULTANEOUSLY. TO HANDLE THIS IN THE MOST EFFICIENT WAY POSSIBLE, WE WILL USE CORE FACILITIES FOR TECHNICAL TASKS THAT EITHER DO NOT REQUIRE OUR SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE OR WILL COMPLEMENT OUR STRENGTHS. FOR CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC EXPERIMENTS: THE EXPRESSION, PROTEIN PURIFICATION AND CRYSTALLIZATION, AS WELL AS INITIAL SOAKING AND DIFFRACTION EXPERIMENTS, WILL BE PERFORMED BY OTHER GROUPS. DEPENDING ON THE OUTCOME OF THE INITIAL DATA COLLECTION, THE UTSW GROUP WILL EITHER DESIGN MODIFIED PROTOCOLS TO DATA COLLECTION ON SINGLE OR MULTIPLE CRYSTALS OR FOCUS ON CUSTOM SOLUTIONS TO PHASING, DENSITY MODIFICATION AND MODEL BUILDING PROCEDURES. AFTER STRUCTURES ARE SOLVED AND REFINED, THEY WILL BE DEPOSITED AND STRUCTURAL RESULTS WILL BE USED TO DESIGN THE NEXT SET OF EXPERIMENTS. FOR CRYO-EM EXPERIMENTS: THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION WILL BE PERFORMED BY OTHER GROUPS, WHILE THE UTSW GROUP WILL PERFORM INITIAL NEGATIVE STAINING, NATIVE CRYO-EM GRID PREPARATION AS WELL AS DATA COLLECTION. THE DATA COLLECTION WILL BE FOLLOWED BY STRUCTURE SOLUTION AND REFINEMENT UP THROUGH THE FINAL STRUCTURE DEPOSITION. THE INITIAL CHARACTERIZATION WITH NEGATIVE STAINING AND QUICK LOWER RESOLUTION DATA COLLECTION WILL BE PERFORMED ON THE TALOS ARCTICA, AND THIS WILL BE FOLLOWED BY HIGH-RESOLUTION DATA COLLECTION USING THE KRIOS TITAN.

description: NATURAL DISASTERS, DISEASE OUTBREAKS, INFRASTRUCUTRE FAILURES AND OTHER HAZARDOUS EVENTS CREATE HEALTH RISKS FOR LARGE SEGMENTS OF THE U.S. POPULATION. MANY DIFFERENT ORGANIZATIONS AND SECTORS HAVE ROLES TO PLAY IN PREVENTING, PREPARING FOR, RESPONDING TO AND RECOVERING FROM THE HEALTH EFFECTS OF DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES. THIS COMPLEXITY POSTS CHALLENGES FOR UNDERSTANDING THE COLLECTIVE STRENGTH OF THE HEALTH SECURITY SYSTEM AS A WHOLE AND FOR MANAGING AND IMPROVING THIS SYSTEM OVERTIME. THE NATIONAL HEALTH SECURITY PREPAREDNESS INDEX PROVIDES A MECHANISM FOR MEASURING HOW HEALTH SECURITY CAPABILITIES VARY ACROSS THE U.S. HOW THEY CHANGE OVER TIME AND HOW THEY CAN BE STRENGTHENED TO PROTECT EVERYONE. STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS FUNCTION AS CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF THE NATION'S HEALTH SECURITY SYSTEM. RELATIVELY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW ACCURATELY AND COMPLETELY THE INDEX MEASURES PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS AND ABOUT HOW PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS CAN BEST USE THE INDEX.

description: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF A LARGE (N=6,012), WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF AFRICAN AMERICAN WOMEN WITH LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENTS OF CERVICAL LENGTH BEGINNING IN THE MID- TRIMESTER AND THE COLLECTION OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL TO PERMIT GENOTYPING OF MOTHERS FOR THIS PROPOSAL. FOR FUTURE STUDIES, BIOBANKED SAMPLES OF OFFSPRING DNA, CERVICO-VAGINAL FLUID FOR THE MICROBIOME, AND OTHER BIOMARKERS INCLUDING CYTOKINES ARE AVAILABLE. THE COHORT ALSO INCLUDES 83 WOMEN TREATED WITH VAGINAL PROGESTERONE DUE TO A PREGNANCY COMPLICATED BY A SHORT CERVIX. THE KEY COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE A GENOME- WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (GWAS) OF MATERNAL DNA FOR LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF ULTRASOUND-MEASURED CERVICAL LENGTH AS A QUANTITATIVE TRAIT. THE FINDINGS OF THE DISCOVERY GWAS WILL BE VALIDATED BY TARGETED GENOTYPING OF AN INDEPENDENT AFRICAN-AMERICAN COHORT. THE VALIDATED LOCI WILL THEN BE USED TO ASSESS HOW SELECT GENOTYPES CAN MODIFY PROGESTERONE RESPONSIVENESS. DR. WOLEN'S DUTIES ON THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE: DESIGNING AND BUILDING A REPRODUCIBLE DATA PIPELINE IN WHICH THE PLANNED ANALYSES CAN BE IMPLEMENTED, STARTING WITH THE CERVICAL LENGTH GROWTH MODELS AND QC FOR THE SNP MICROARRAYS. THE WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED AT UTHSC IN THE TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCES RESEARCH BUILDING AND WILL UTILIZE LOCAL HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING RESOURCES.

description: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF A LARGE (N=6,012), WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF AFRICAN AMERICAN WOMEN WITH LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENTS OF CERVICAL LENGTH BEGINNING IN THE MIDTRIMESTER AND THE COLLECTION OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL TO PERMIT GENOTYPING OF MOTHERS FOR THIS PROPOSAL. FOR FUTURE STUDIES, BIOBANKED SAMPLES OF OFFSPRING DNA, CERVICO-VAGINAL FLUID FOR THE MICROBIOME, AND OTHER BIOMARKERS INCLUDING CYTOKINES ARE AVAILABLE. THE COHORT ALSO INCLUDES 83 WOMEN TREATED WITH VAGINAL PROGESTERONE DUE TO A PREGNANCY COMPLICATED BY A SHORT CERVIX. THE KEY COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE A GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (GWAS) OF MATERNAL DNA FOR LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF ULTRASOUND-MEASURED CERVICAL LENGTH AS A QUANTITATIVE TRAIT. THE FINDINGS OF THE DISCOVERY GWAS WILL BE VALIDATED BY TARGETED GENOTYPING OF AN INDEPENDENT AFRICAN-AMERICAN COHORT. THE VALIDATED LOCI WILL THEN BE USED TO ASSESS HOW SELECT GENOTYPES CAN MODIFY PROGESTERONE RESPONSIVENESS. TIMOTHY YORK, PH.D. (PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR). DR. YORK, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF HUMAN & MOLECULAR GENETICS AND OB/GYN AT VCU, WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE OVERALL ADMINISTRATION AND DIRECTION OF THIS SUB-CONTRACT. HE IS A FULL MEMBER OF THE VCU CENTER FOR HEALTH DISPARITIES AND ALSO THE DIRECTOR OF THE VCU DATA SCIENCE LAB COMMITTED TO BEST PRACTICES IN REPRODUCIBLE RESEARCH AND OPEN SCIENCE METHODOLOGY. HE WILL OVERSEE ASPECTS OF SPECIMEN PROCESSING, DATA MANAGEMENT, STATISTICAL AND QUANTITATIVE GENETIC ANALYSES, AND MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION. DR. YORK WILL ENSURE THAT DEFINED QUALITY CONTROL MEASURES ARE FOLLOWED IN THE DATA GENERATION, DATA ENTRY AND ANALYSIS PORTIONS OF THIS STUDY. ALONG WITH OTHER CO-I'S HE WILL WORK TO SELECT THE APPROPRIATE STATISTICAL-GENETIC MODELS TO COMPLETE THE STATISTICAL GENETIC ANALYSES FOR EACH AIM. HE WILL INTERACT WITH DR. STRAUSS TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL DATA FOR ANALYSIS AND INTERPRET RESULTS. BRADLEY TODD WEBB, PH.D. (CO-INVESTIGATOR). DR. WEBB IS AN ASSISTANT PROFESSOR OF PSYCHIATRY AT VCU AND IS TRAINED IN STATISTICAL GENETICS AND BIOINFORMATICS AND HAS A BACKGROUND IN MOLECULAR BIOLOGY. HE WILL WORK CLOSELY IN THIS GRANT WITH DR. YORK, DR. WOLEN, AND THE GRADUATE STUDENT TO ANALYZE AND INTERPRET THE GWAS ARRAY DATA FOR CERVICAL LENGTH GENETIC ARCHITECTURE STUDIES AND TEST FOR PUTATIVE MQTL LOCI WITH DNA METHYLATION MEASURES. HE WILL PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN DATA ANALYTIC SUPPORT FOR THIS MULTI-PLATFORM DATA AND CONTRIBUTE TO MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION. JEROME STRAUSS, M.D., PH.D., (CO-INVESTIGATOR). DR. STRAUSS IS A PROFESSOR OF OB/GYN AT VCU AND AN EMERITUS PROFESSOR OF OB/GYN AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA WHERE HIS RESEARCH LAB IS CURRENTLY LOCATED. HE WILL SERVE AS THE PHENOTYPIC EXPERT ON BIRTH OUTCOME MEASURES AND THE MOLECULAR GENETICS OF GESTATION AND PARTURITION. . IN THE LATER STAGES OF THE PROJECT HE WILL PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON INTERPRETATION OF FINDINGS, ADVISE ON THE PRIORITIZATION OF GENOMIC FINDINGS AND, ALONG WITH DR. YORK AND THE STUDY TEAM, WILL CONSTRUCT HYPOTHESES REGARDING GENOMIC MECHANISMS TO BE TESTED FOR PGX STUDIES.

description: THE OVERALL PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING 4 OBJECTIVES: [I] WE WILL CALCULATE INFLUENZA VACCINE EFFECTIVENESS FOR PREVENTING SEVERE INFLUENZA-ASSOCIATED DISEASE AMONG ADULTS IN THE UNITED STATES, INCLUDING VACCINE EFFECTIVENESS FOR SPECIFIC SUBTYPES OF PATIENTS (BASED ON AGE, COMORBIDITIES, AND RISK FACTORS) AND SPECIFIC VACCINES (INCLUDING THOSE WITH ADJUVANT AND HIGHER ANTIGEN OR CELL CULTURE-BASED PRODUCTION). [2] WE WILL PROVIDE A DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF BOTH ACUTE RESPIRATORY AND NON-RESPIRATORY MANIFESTATIONS OF INFLUENZA INFECTION. [3] WE WILL COLLECT BIOLOGICAL SAMPLES TO INVESTIGATE SEPSIS AND OTHER 25 MECHANISMS BEHIND FULMINANT AND RAPIDLY PROGRESSIVE INFLUENZA ILLNESS IN OTHERWISE HEALTHY HOSTS. [ 4] WE WILL DOCUMENT INFLUENZA VACCINATION STATUS AMONG CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS IN THE HOSPITAL WITH ACUTE RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS USING VALIDATED REGISTRIES AND OTHER METHODS.

agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
naics_title: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHYSICAL, ENGINEERING, AND LIFE SCIENCES (EXCEPT NANOTECHNOLOGY AND BIOTECHNOLOGY)
psc_title: HEALTH R&D SERVICES; HEALTH CARE SERVICES; APPLIED RESEARCH
description: STUDY OVERVIEW: INFLUENZA VACCINE EFFECTIVENESS IN THE CRITICALLY ILL (IVY) IS A MULTICENTER PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY OF INFLUENZA INFECTION AMONG HOSPITALIZED ADULTS IN THE US, WITH A FOCUS ON CRITICALLY- ILL PATIENTS IN THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU). IVY IS FUNDED BY THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC) VIA A CONTRACT TO VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER (VUMC). VUMC WILL SERVE AS THE CLINICAL COORDINATING CENTER (CCC), DATA COORDINATING CENTER (DCC), CENTRAL VIRAL LABORATORY, AND SINGLE INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD (SIRB). PATIENTS WILL BE ENROLLED IN HOSPITALS PARTICIPATING IN THE PREVENTION AND EARLY TREATMENT OF ACUTE LUNG INJURY (PETAL) CLINICAL TRIALS NETWORK, BUT THE PETAL NETWORK AND THE NATIONAL HEART, LUNG, AND BLOOD INSTITUTE (NHLBI) HAVE NO ROLE IN THE STUDY. ENROLLMENT EXPECTATIONS: PARTICIPATING SITES ARE EXPECTED TO SCREEN AND ENROLL PATIENTS IN THE STUDY DURING THE 2019-2020 INFLUENZA SEASON (DEFINITION OF INFLUENZA SEASON IS PROVIDED IN IVY PROTOCOL). ADULTS WITH SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS OF SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY INFECTION ARE ELIGIBLE FOR ENROLLMENT (SPECIFIC ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA ARE OUTLINED IN THE IVY PROTOCOL). GOAL ENROLLMENT AT EACH SITE IS 70 PATIENTS DURING THE 2019-2020 INFLUENZA SEASON, INCLUDING 50 PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED IN AN ICU AND 20 PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED OUTSIDE THE ICU (I.E. A FLOOR OR STEP-DOWN AREA). FOR THE ENTIRE STUDY ACROSS ALL SITES, TARGET ENROLLMENT IS 700 PATIENTS WITH APPROXIMATELY 20% INFLUENZA PREVALENCE AMONG ENROLLED PATIENTS. BECAUSE INFLUENZA SEASONS ARE VARIABLE BY YEAR AND BY LOCATION, THE ENROLLMENT PLAN REQUIRES FLEXIBILITY. THE IVY PROTOCOL COMMITTEE WILL REVIEW ENROLLMENT DATA WEEKLY THROUGHOUT THE STUDY. ADJUSTMENTS IN THE NUMBER OF PATIENTS ENROLLED AT INDIVIDUAL SITES MAY BE MADE BY THE PROTOCOL COMMITTEE TO MAXIMIZE THE PROBABILITY OF ENROLLING 700 TOTAL PATIENTS. THUS, DEPENDING ON THE PACE OF ENROLLMENT AND INFLUENZA PREVALENCE AT INDIVIDUAL SITES, SOME SITES MAY BE INVITED TO ENROLL MORE THAN 70 PATIENTS AND SOME SITES MAY BE CAPPED AT FEWER THAN 70 PATIENTS.

description: STUDY OVERVIEW: INFLUENZA VACCINE EFFECTIVENESS IN THE CRITICALLY ILL (IVY) IS A MULTICENTER PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY OF INFLUENZA INFECTION AMONG HOSPITALIZED ADULTS IN THE US, WITH A FOCUS ON CRITICALLY- ILL PATIENTS IN THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU). IVY IS FUNDED BY THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC) VIA A CONTRACT TO VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER (VUMC). VUMC WILL SERVE AS THE CLINICAL COORDINATING CENTER (CCC), DATA COORDINATING CENTER (DCC), CENTRAL VIRAL LABORATORY, AND SINGLE INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD (SIRB). PATIENTS WILL BE ENROLLED IN HOSPITALS PARTICIPATING IN THE PREVENTION AND EARLY TREATMENT OF ACUTE LUNG INJURY (PETAL) CLINICAL TRIALS NETWORK, BUT THE PETAL NETWORK AND THE NATIONAL HEART, LUNG, AND BLOOD INSTITUTE (NHLBI) HAVE NO ROLE IN THE STUDY. ENROLLMENT EXPECTATIONS: PARTICIPATING SITES ARE EXPECTEDWILL USE BEST EFFORTS TO SCREEN AND ENROLL PATIENTS IN THE STUDY DURING THE 2019-2020 INFLUENZA SEASON (DEFINITION OF INFLUENZA SEASON IS PROVIDED IN IVY PROTOCOL). ADULTS WITH SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS OF SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY INFECTION ARE ELIGIBLE FOR ENROLLMENT (SPECIFIC ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA ARE OUTLINED IN THE IVY PROTOCOL). GOAL ENROLLMENT AT EACH SITE IS 70 PATIENTS DURING THE 2019-2020 INFLUENZA SEASON, INCLUDING 50 PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED IN AN ICU AND 20 PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED OUTSIDE THE ICU (I.E. A FLOOR OR STEP-DOWN AREA). FOR THE ENTIRE STUDY ACROSS ALL SITES, TARGET ENROLLMENT IS 700 PATIENTS WITH APPROXIMATELY 20% INFLUENZA PREVALENCE AMONG ENROLLED PATIENTS. BECAUSE INFLUENZA SEASONS ARE VARIABLE BY YEAR AND BY LOCATION, THE ENROLLMENT PLAN REQUIRES FLEXIBILITY. THE IVY PROTOCOL COMMITTEE WILL REVIEW ENROLLMENT DATA WEEKLY THROUGHOUT THE STUDY. ADJUSTMENTS IN THE NUMBER OF PATIENTS ENROLLED AT INDIVIDUAL SITES MAY BE MADE BY THE PROTOCOL COMMITTEE TO MAXIMIZE THE PROBABILITY OF ENROLLING 700 TOTAL PATIENTS. THUS, DEPENDING ON THE PACE OF ENROLLMENT AND INFLUENZA PREVALENCE AT INDIVIDUAL SITES, SOME SITES MAY BE INVITED TO ENROLL MORE THAN 70 PATIENTS AND SOME SITES MAY BE CAPPED AT FEWER THAN 70 PATIENTS. ENROLLING SITE STUDY PROCEDURES: ENROLLED PATIENTS WILL UNDERGO THE FOLLOWING, AS DESCRIBED IN THE IVY PROTOCOL: - CONSENT FOR STUDY PARTICIPATION VIA THE PATIENT OR A SURROGATE. - COLLECTION OF A MID-TURBINATE/ORO-PHARYNGEAL SPECIMEN AND SHIPMENT TO VUMC FOR VIRAL TESTING. - FOR PATIENTS WHO ARE INTUBATED ONLY: COLLECTION OF A TRACHEAL ASPIRATE SPECIMEN AND SHIPMENT TO VUMC FOR VIRAL TESTING. - FOR PATIENTS AGED 18 Â€“ 65 YEARS WITHOUT MAJOR CO-MORBIDITIES ONLY (YOUNG HEALTHY HOST POPULATION, AS DEFINED IN THE IVY PROTOCOL): COLLECTION OF BLOOD FOR STORAGE IN THE IVY BIOSPECIMEN REPOSITORY. - FOR PATIENTS WHO TEST POSITIVE FOR INFLUENZA ONLY: CLINICIAN SURVEY REGARDING PERCEPTIONS OF THE ROLE INFLUENZA INFECTION PLAYED IN THE PATIENTÂ€™S CLINICAL COURSE. - INTERVIEW AT THE TIME OF ENROLLMENT WITH PATIENT AND/OR SURROGATE TO COLLECT DATA ABOUT DEMOGRAPHICS, REASONS FOR RECEIVING OR NOT RECEIVING INFLUENZA VACCINATION, COMORBIDITIES, ACUTE PRESENTATION, HISTORY OF HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION, AND RECENT OUTPATIENT TREATMENT. - MEDICAL RECORD REVIEW FOR INFORMATION ON RISK FACTORS, COMORBIDITIES, AND IN-HOSPITAL OUTCOMES. - INFLUENZA VACCINE VERIFICATION USING A STANDARDIZED APPROACH. - ECRFÂ€™S SHALL BE COMPLETED WITHIN THIRTY (30) DAYS OF HOSPITAL DISCHARGE

psc_title: R&D- OTHER RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT (APPLIED RESEARCH/EXPLORATORY DEVELOPMENT)
description: NATURAL DISASTERS, DISEASE OUTBREAKS, INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURES AND OTHER HAZARDOUS EVENTS CREATE HEALTH RISKS FOR LARGE SEGMENTS OF THE U.S. POPULATION. MANY DIFFERENT ORGANIZATIONS AND SECTORS HAVE ROLES TO PLAY IN PREVENTING, PREPARING FOR, RESPONDING TO, AND RECOVERING FROM THE HEALTH EFFECTS OF DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES.1 THIS COMPLEXITY POSES CHALLENGES FOR UNDERSTANDING THE COLLECTIVE STRENGTH OF THE HEALTH SECURITY SYSTEM AS A WHOLE, AND FOR MANAGING AND IMPROVING THIS SYSTEM OVER TIME. THE NATIONAL HEALTH SECURITY PREPAREDNESS INDEX PROVIDES A MECHANISM FOR MEASURING HOW HEALTH SECURITY CAPABILITIES VARY ACROSS THE U.S. HOW THEY CHANGE OVER TIME, AND HOW THEY CAN BE STRENGTHENED TO PROTECT EVERYONE.1,2 STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS FUNCTION AS CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF THE NATIONÂ€™S HEALTH SECURITY SYSTEM. RELATIVELY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW ACCURATELY AND COMPLETELY THE INDEX MEASURES PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS, AND ABOUT HOW PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS CAN BEST USE THE INDEX. SCIENTIFIC APPROACH, DATA AND METHODS: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECT WILL ACCOMPLISH 4 RELATED AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ASSESS HOW THE INDEX PERFORMS IN MEASURING STATE AND LOCAL PREPAREDNESS CAPABILITIES AND THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO NATIONAL HEALTH SECURITY, USING BOTH QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE TESTS OF VALIDITY AND RELIABILITY. WE WILL LINK STATE AND LOCAL INDEX DATA WITH A VARIETY OF OTHER DATA SOURCES RELATED TO PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS CAPABILITIES, INCLUDING PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT (PHEP) PERFORMANCE MEASURES AND OPERATIONAL READINESS REVIEWS (ORRS), NACCHOÂ€™S PROJECT PUBLIC HEALTH READY CERTIFICATION PROGRAM, AND THE SPATIAL HAZARDS, EVENTS AND LOSSES (SHELDUS) DATABASE. QUANTITATIVE VALIDITY AND RELIABILITY ANALYSES WILL EXAMINE THE INDEXÂ€™S PERFORMANCE IN ACCURATELY REFLECTING PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS CAPABILITIES AND OUTCOMES. A DELPHI SURVEY FIELDED WITH A NATIONAL SAMPLE OF STATE, TERRITORIAL AND LOCAL PREPAREDNESS OFFICIALS WILL ASSESS THE FACE VALIDITY OF INDEX MEASURES AND CONSTRUCT WEIGHTS OF RELATIVE IMPORTANCE. SITE VISITS, INTERVIEWS AND DOCUMENT REVIEWS WILL BE COMPLETED WITH STATE, TERRITORIAL AND LOCAL PREPAREDNESS STAKEHOLDERS IN A DIVERSE COHORT OF TEST SITES TO SUPPORT DETAILED QUALITATIVE ASSESSMENTS OF INDEX VALIDITY AND RELIABILITY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY A CORE SET OF METRICS THAT ACCURATELY REFLECT STATE AND LOCAL PREPAREDNESS CAPABILITIES AND THAT ARE FEASIBLE FOR USE WITHIN THE INDEX AND IN OTHER MEASUREMENT TOOLS. WE WILL USE FACTOR ANALYSIS, CLUSTER ANALYSIS, AND LATENT CLASS ANALYSIS METHODS WITH THE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DATA SOURCES ABOVE, ALONG WITH QUALITATIVE DATA FROM THE TEST SITES, TO IDENTIFY THIS MEASUREMENT SET. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THE CURRENT USE AND UTILITY OF THE INDEX FOR PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS BY FIELDING A NATIONAL SURVEY OF STATE AND LOCAL PREPAREDNESS OFFICIALS AND CONDUCTING COMPARATIVE CASE STUDIES WITH DIVERSE PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS. IN AIM 4, WE WILL SYNTHESIZE STUDY FINDINGS AND PRODUCE AND TEST GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS AND TOOLS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS INDICATING HOW THEY CAN USE CURRENT AND FUTURE EDITIONS OF THE INDEX TO STRENGTHEN HEALTH SECURITY IN THEIR STATES AND COMMUNITIES. DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE INCLUDE A SCIENTIFIC MANUSCRIPT DESCRIBING INDEX VALIDITY AND RELIABILITY (PRODUCED AT MONTH 12), A SUMMARY REPORT DESCRIBING THE CORE SET OF PREPAREDNESS METRICS (PRODUCED AT MONTH 24), TWO MANUSCRIPTS DESCRIBING INDEX USE AND UTILITY (PRODUCED AT MONTHS 24 AND 30), AND A SET OF GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS AND ELECTRONIC TOOLS SUPPORTING INDEX USE BY STATE, TERRITORIAL, AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS STAKEHOLDERS (FINALIZED AT MONTH 36).

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON INSTITUTE FOR PROTEIN DESIGN GROUP (UW-IPD), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID BAKER, PH.D. AND WITH SUPPORTING CO-INVESTIGATORS LANCE STEWART, PH.D. AND NEIL KING, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK (OPTION PERIOD ONE OPTION QUANTITY 6) TO ADDITIONALLY SUPPORT THE BASIC REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD ONE TERM) OF THE SSGCID CONTRACT (CONTRACT NR HHSN272201700059C). UW-IPD WILL LEAD THE OPTION QUANTITY EFFORT TO CONTINUE THE NANOPARTICLE FLU STUDY DESCRIBED BELOW. A. OPTION QUANTITY 6: NANOP/FLU: UW-IPD WILL USE OPTION QUANTITY 6 RESOURCES TO LEAD CONTINUE THE STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDY (SVTD-02) STUDY WHICH ENDED 8/31/18 AND WAS ENTITLED, Â€ŒDESIGN AND CHARACTERIZATION OF A SELF-ASSEMBLING NANOPARTICLE VACCINEÂ€?. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS SVTD WAS TO DESIGN, PRODUCE, AND CHARACTERIZE THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF COMPUTATIONALLY DESIGNED SELF-ASSEMBLING PROTEIN NANOPARTICLES THAT MULTIVALENTLY DISPLAY HA ANTIGENS IN COMBINATION WITH C3D. USING OQ 6 FUNDS, AIM 1 WILL BE EXPANDED - PRODUCE SELF-ASSEMBLING IMMUNOGENS THAT CO-DISPLAY FULL-LENGTH HA AND C3D AT VARIOUS RATIOS AND CHARACTERIZE THEM BIOCHEMICALLY AND BIOPHYSICALLY. ADDITIONAL AIM 2 WILL BE EXPANDED AND PERFORMED TOGETHER WITH UW-CRYOEM - EXAMINE THE STRUCTURE OF THE SELF-ASSEMBLING HA/C3D BY CRYOEM. AND FINALLY AIM 3 WILL BE COMPLETED AT NO COST BY UW-IPD COLLABORATORS, THE NIAID VACCINE RESEARCH CENTER - CHARACTERIZE THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF THESE SELF-ADJUVANTING HA NANOPARTICLES IN MICE.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON INSTITUTE FOR PROTEIN DESIGN GROUP (UW-IPD), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID BAKER, PH.D. AND WITH SUPPORTING CO-INVESTIGATORS LANCE STEWART, PH.D. AND NEIL KING, PH.D., WILL GENERATE COMPUTATIONAL PROTEIN STRUCTURE MODELS FOR HIGH PRIORITY SSGCID PROTEIN TARGETS AND ALSO LEAD A STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY (SVTD) STUDY. A. STRUCTURE MODELING OF AT LEAST 100 SSGCID TARGETS: UW-IPD WILL GENERATE COMPUTATIONAL MODELS USING BOTH ROSETTA METHODS ALONG WITH GREMLIN (CO-EVOLUTION AMINO ACID CONTACT RESTRAINTS). THE ROSETTA MODELS OF ~100 SSGCID TARGETS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY VIA THE WEB SITES OF SSGCID AND THE INSTITUTE FOR PROTEIN DESIGN (IPD). THE ROSETTA MODELS WILL AID CONSTRUCT DESIGN FOR THE SSGCID GENE-TO-PROTEIN PIPELINE, AND WILL SERVE AS ATOMIC MODELS TO SUPPORT X-RAY CRYSTAL STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF SSGCID TARGETS BY MOLECULAR REPLACEMENT. THESE EFFORTS WILL PARTIALLY SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-IPD WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA. UW-IPD WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY UW-IPD STAFF WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. UW-IPD WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. UW-IPD WILL CONDUCT THEIR WORK WITH THE AIM TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS IN HIGH IMPACT PUBLICATIONS.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON PROTEIN PRODUCTION GROUP (UW-PPG), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF WESLEY C. VAN VOORHIS, M.D., PH.D., WILL GENERATE TARGET CLONES, PERFORM SMALL AND LARGE SCALE SCREENING, UPSCALE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION OF THE CLONES; MANAGE ONE FUNCTIONAL (FUN) STUDY (FUN_21); MANAGE ONE STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY (SVTD) STUDY (SVTD_06) AND CONTRIBUTE TO ONE SVTD PROJECT (SVTD_04). UW-PPG WILL LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). A. CLONING, EXPRESSION TESTING, UPSCALE AND PURIFICATION OF SSGCID TARGETS: UW-PPG WILL PERFORM CLONING MAINLY USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PCR-BASED LIGATION INDEPENDENT CLONING INTO E. COLI EXPRESSION VECTORS. UW-PPG WILL SCREEN THEIR EXPRESSION AND SOLUBILITY PROPERTIES USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PROTOCOLS, INCLUDING, AS NEEDED, MULTIPLE EXPRESSION SYSTEMS AND CLEAVAGE SYSTEMS. UW-PPG WILL GENERATE LARGE SCALE EXPRESSIONS OF TARGETS FOR HIGHLY PURIFIED TARGET PROTEINS OR PROTEIN FRAGMENTS AND PRODUCE THEM IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY FOR STRUCTURE DETERMINATION THROUGH STANDARDIZATION AND AUTOMATION OF PROTOCOLS. UW-PPG WILL EVALUATE THE PURITY, CONCENTRATION AND BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES (E.G. PROTEIN FOLDING, AGGREGATION, AND/OR STABILITY) OF THE PURIFIED SAMPLES TO ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORTS. B. IT IS EXPECTED THAT UW-PPG WILL INITIATE EFFORTS TO CLONE, EXPRESSION TEST AND PURIFY 5 COMPLEXES, WITH THE AIM OF OBTAINING ~2 STRUCTURES (TIER 17). IT IS EXPECTED THAT UW-PPG MAY SUPPORT BERYLLIUMÂ€™S MEMBRANE PROTEIN EFFORTS (TIER 18) BY CLONING 10 TARGETS, POSSIBLY WITH MULTIPLE TRUNCATIONS OF EACH. C. FOWLERIÂ€?, THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO USE PHYSICOCHEMICAL AND CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC METHODS TO EXPLORE G PROTEIN COUPLED INTERACTIONS IN NAEGLERIA FOWLERI. D. STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDIES: UW-PPG WILL USE OPTION PERIOD ONE TERM RESOURCES TO LEAD A TRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDY (SVTD_06) ENTITLED, Â€ŒNOVEL DRUG CANDIDATES FOR FREE-LIVING AMOEBAÂ€?, THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO PURSUE A PILOT STRUCTURE-GUIDED DRUG DEVELOPMENT APPROACH TO DEVELOP LEAD COMPOUNDS FOR 3 PROTEINS SHOWN TO BE PRESENT IN 3 FREE LIVING AMOEBA (N. FOWLERI, A. CASTELLANII AND B. MANDRILLARIS) AND FOR WHICH STRUCTURES OF 2 ARE ALREADY SOLVED BY THE SSGCID. ADDITIONALLY, UW-PPG WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE STRUCTURE-GUIDED INFLUENZA VACCINE INITIATIVE (STRIVE) PROJECT (SVTD_04). E. description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST ONE CRYOEM STRUCTURE DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR. THE WORK DESCRIBED BELOW COVERS THE ENTIRE AWARD YEAR, PERIOD 9/1/2018 Â€“ 8/31/2019. THE AMOUNT OF WORK TO BE PERFORMED DURING THE PERIOD OF THIS SUBCONTRACT SHOULD ROUGHLY EQUAL THE PROPORTION OF MONTHS THIS SUBCONTRACT COVERS DIVIDED BY THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MONTHS AWARDED TO THIS SUBCONTRACT SITE. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST ONE PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEX USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. FINALLY, WE WILL USE RECENTLY DEVELOPED ROSETTA TOOLS, WHICH ALLOWED US TO DETERMINE THE FIRST HIGH-RESOLUTION STRUCTURE OF A CORONAVIRUS SPIKE GLYCOPROTEIN TRIMER. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA. UW-CRYOEM WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: NATURAL DISASTERS, DISEASE OUTBREAKS, INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURES AND OTHER HAZARDOUS EVENTS CREATE HEALTH RISKS FOR LARGE SEGMENTS OF THE U.S. POPULATION. MANY DIFFERENT ORGANIZATIONS AND SECTORS HAVE ROLES TO PLAY IN PREVENTING, PREPARING FOR, RESPONDING TO, AND RECOVERING FROM THE HEALTH EFFECTS OF DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES.1 THIS COMPLEXITY POSES CHALLENGES FOR UNDERSTANDING THE COLLECTIVE STRENGTH OF THE HEALTH SECURITY SYSTEM AS A WHOLE, AND FOR MANAGING AND IMPROVING THIS SYSTEM OVER TIME. THE NATIONAL HEALTH SECURITY PREPAREDNESS INDEX PROVIDES A MECHANISM FOR MEASURING HOW HEALTH SECURITY CAPABILITIES VARY ACROSS THE U.S. HOW THEY CHANGE OVER TIME, AND HOW THEY CAN BE STRENGTHENED TO PROTECT EVERYONE.1,2 STATE AND LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS FUNCTION AS CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF THE NATIONÂ€™S HEALTH SECURITY SYSTEM. RELATIVELY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW ACCURATELY AND COMPLETELY THE INDEX MEASURES PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS, AND ABOUT HOW PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS CAN BEST USE THE INDEX.

THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CID RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU-NMR MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM. MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. DR. BUCHKO WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. description: THE QUALITY PAYMENT PROGRAM RESOURCE CENTER FOR THE MIDWEST (QPP RESOURCE CENTER) REMAINS DEDICATED PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO SMALL CLINICIAN PRACTICES WITH 15 OR FEWER CLINICIANS UNDER ONE TIN WHO ARE ALSO ELIGIBLE FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE MERIT-BASED INCENTIVE PAYMENT SYSTEM (MIPS). THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER, THROUGH THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL, WILL SUPPORT CLINICIANS IN THEIR TRANSITION FROM A FEE-FOR-SERVICE MODEL TO AN ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODEL (APM) OR THE MERIT BASED INCENTIVE PAYMENT SYSTEM (MIPS). WORKING UNDER THE DIRECTION OF ALTARUMÂ€™S QPP RESOURCE CENTER PROJECT MANAGER, NIU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOWING TASKS AND ACTIVITIES: TASK 1: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) ASSIGN QPP ADVISOR STAFF AND ENSURE THEIR AVAILABILITY FOR ONBOARDING/TRAINING SESSIONS ON PROGRAM OBJECTIVES, VIRTUAL SUPPORT SERVICES, QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL WORKFLOWS AND TOOLS, AND CMS TOOLS, AND (2) DESIGNATE STAFF MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE IN APPROPRIATE WORKGROUPS TASK 2: RESOURCE CENTER CONTENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IDENTIFY AND PROVIDE EXISTING QPP RELATED RESOURCES AND TOOLS WITHIN YOUR ORGANIZATION IN A FORMAT APPROPRIATE FOR UPLOAD TO THE WEBSITE AND USE BY CLINICIANS, AND (2) ASSIST WITH RESEARCH FOR PUBLICLY AVAILABLE TOOLS AND RESOURCES TO BE LINKED TO OR UPLOADED ONTO THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM TASK 3: OUTREACH ACTIVITIES - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) PROVIDE INFORMATION AS REQUIRED TO DOCUMENT IN THE CMS CRM THE UNILATERAL ENGAGEMENT OF CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS IN THE QPP-SURS PROGRAM, (2) IDENTIFY A STAFF PERSON TO PARTICIPATE IN THE MARKETING & OUTREACH WORKGROUP, (3) IDENTIFY NEW, AND USE EXISTING, COMMUNICATION AVENUES TO PROMOTE THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER, QPP TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND CMS/CMS QPP-SURS CENTRAL SUPPORT CONTRACTOR SPONSORED EVENTS, (4) REACH OUT TO LOCAL AND STATE CLINICIAN ORGANIZATIONS, PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, AND OTHER RELEVANT GROUPS TO HAVE THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER ADVERTISED ON THEIR WEBSITES, IN NEWSLETTERS, E-NEWSLETTERS, AND OTHER CLINICIAN COMMUNICATIONS, (5) CONTINUE UNILATERAL ENGAGEMENT (I.E. OUTREACH) UNTIL 100% OF SURS ELIGIBLE CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS HAVE BEEN UNILATERALLY ENGAGED FOR THE 2019 PROGRAM YEAR AND THIS UNILATERAL ENGAGEMENT HAS BEEN DOCUMENTED AT THE TAX IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (TIN) AND/OR INDIVIDUAL NATIONAL PHYSICIAN IDENTIFIER (NPI) LEVEL TASK 4: CLINICIAN ENGAGEMENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) PROVIDE INFORMATION IN THE CMS CRM AS REQUIRED TO DOCUMENT THE ENGAGEMENT OF ILLINOIS CLINICIANS, AS WELL AS UNREACHABLE CLINICIANS, (2) PROVIDE UPDATES ON CLINICIAN ELIGIBILITY OR ELIGIBLE CLINICIAN FILE ERRORS TO CMS BY SUBMITTING CASES VIA THE CMS CRM, (3) ASSIGN QPP ADVISORS TO ASSIST ALL ENROLLED PRACTICES IN THE STATE OF ILLINOIS THAT ARE ASSIGNED TO NIU FOR VIRTUAL TA SERVICE, (4) CONTINUE BI-LATERAL ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES UNTIL 100% OF SURS ELIGIBLE CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS HAVE BEEN BI-LATERALLY ENGAGED FOR THE PROGRAM YEAR AND THIS BILATERAL ENGAGEMENT HAS BEEN DOCUMENTED AT THE TIN AND/OR INDIVIDUAL NPI LEVEL. TASK 5: DELIVER VIRTUAL SUPPORT AND TA TASK 6: CUSTOMER SATISFACTION ASSESSMENT TASK 7: DATA CAPTURE AND REPORTING - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE A SELF-SELECTED PROGRAM/METHOD TO TRACK ALL OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT EVENTS (INCLUDING DATE, ENGAGEMENT TYPE, AND AFFILIATED NPIS/TINS). PROVIDE COUNTS BY EVENT TYPE MONTHLY AND MAINTAIN DATA IN SUPPORT OF UNREACHABLE CLINICIAN DOCUMENTATION, (2) SUPPORT COMPLETE DOCUMENTATION OF AND RECORD PRACTICE AND CLINICIAN DEMOGRAPHIC INFORMATION, (3) RECORD INFORMATION ON PARTICIPATING PRACTICESÂ€™ PARTICIPATION IN OTHER CMS MODELS AND PROGRAMS AS REQUIRED BY CMS AND WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH LOCAL MIPS/APM OUTREACH AND EDUCATION ACTIVITIES TO PREVENT DUPLICATION OF EFFORT, (4) DOCUMENT PROGRAM MILESTONES.

description: PURDUE UNIVERSITY WILL HAVE THE RESPONSIBILITY FOR PERFORMING LIGAND SCREENING, DESIGN AND SYNTHESIS AS WELL AS CRYO-EM STRUCTURES OF HIGH-PRIORITY PROTEIN TARGETS FOR THE CENTER FOR STRUCTURAL GENOMICS OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES (CSGID). PURDUE WILL UTILIZE DIFFERENT APPROACHES IN THE DISCOVERY, DESIGN AND SYNTHESIS OF LIGANDS THAT BIND TO THEIR TARGETS. FOR EXAMPLE, PURDUE WILL UTILIZED BIOCHEMICAL-BASED ASSAYS TO SCREEN COMPOUND LIBRARIES TO IDENTIFIY INHIBITORS (OR ACTIVATORS) THAT WILL SERVE AS LEAD LIGANDS FOR DESIGN, CRYSTALLOGRAPHY ETC. AS ANOTHER EXAMPLE, PURDUE WILL UTILIZE X-RAY STRUCTURE-BASED SCREENING AGAINST SMALL COMPOUND LIBRARIES OR COMPUTATIONALLY SELECTED COMPOUNDS TO IDENTIFY LEAD LIGANDS. OTHER APPORACHES WILL BE UTLIZED TO IDENTIFY LIGANDS AND THESE APPROACHES WILL DEPEND ON THE IDENTIFIED OR PROPOSED FUNCTION OF THE TARGET PROTEIN. FINALLY, LEAD COMPOUND AND ANALOG SYNTHESIS WILL ALSO BE PERFORMED AT PURDUE TO GENERATE LIGANDS AND INCREASE POTENCY OF WEAKER LEAD MOLECULES. PURDUE WILL ALSO UTILIZE THEIR STATE-OF-THE-ART CRYO-EM FACILITY AND EXPERTISE TO DETERMINE THE CRYO-EM STRUCTURES FOR VIRUSES AND VIRUSES IN COMPLEX WITH ANTIBODIES. VIRUS TARGETS WILL BE SELECTED BY THE CSGID. PURDUE UNIVERSITY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE TARGET SELECTION AND STRUCTURE DETERMINATION PROCESSES AS PART OF THE OVERALL CSGID STATEMENT OF WORK.

THE OVERALL GOALS OF THIS OPTION QUANTITY PROPOSAL ARE TO CHARACTERIZE NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES ELICITED BY HOST HUMORAL RESPONSE TO ANTIGENS DERIVED FROM HENIPAVIRUS FUSION MACHINERY AND TO CHARACTERIZE THE FUSION MACHINERY OF EMERGING HENIPA-LIKE VIRUSES. STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL PERFORM WORK FOCUSED ON PROTEIN PRODUCTION, CRYO-EM, AND BIOLOGICAL CHARACTERIZATION STUDIES FOR THIS PROJECT.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE). UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST FOUR CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR. UW-CRYOEM WILL LEAD ONE FUNCTION STUDY (FUN) AND MAY ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST FOUR PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. B. FUNCTION STUDIES: UW-CRYOEM WILL USE OPTION PERIOD THREE TERM RESOURCES TO LEAD ONE FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN). THIS FUN IS ENTITLED Â€ŒSTRUCTURAL STUDY OF THE SARS-COV-2 MULTIFUNCTIONAL REPLICATION MACHINERY,Â€? THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO STRUCTURALLY CHARACTERIZE THE SARS-COV-2 CORE RNA-DEPENDENT RNA POLYMERASE (RDRP) PROTEIN NSP12 AND ENDONUCLEASE NSP15 IN COMPLEX WITH AUXILIARY NON-STRUCTURAL PROTEINS (NSPS) TO ELUCIDATE THEIR ROLES AND SYNERGISM IN VIRAL GENOME REPLICATION. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. description: SUSAN STRAMER, PHD, AMERICAN RED CROSS PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR DR. STRAMER HAS PROVIDED SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TO THE ARC FOR OVER 20 YEARS IN THE AREA OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES, TESTING AND DONOR AND RECIPIENT SAFETY. SHE IS WIDELY PUBLISHED (>150 PUBLICATIONS AND 200 ABSTRACTS) AND HAS PRESENTED IN SUPPORT OF PRODUCTS FOR FDA LICENSURE AT NUMEROUS ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETINGS. SHE HAS BEEN INVOLVED IN NEARLY 20 CLINICAL TRIALS AS THE STUDY PI WHILE AT THE RED CROSS FROM NUCLEIC ACID TESTING FOR HIV, HCV, HBV, WNV, ZIKV AND BABESIA. SHE IS WELL VERSED IN STUDY DESIGN, DATA ANALYSES AND PREPARING AND REVIEWING MANUSCRIPTS FOR PUBLICATION. SHE HAS BEEN A REPRESENTATIVE ON NUMEROUS COMMITTEES OF THE AABB AND ISBT INCLUDING SERVING AS THE AABB PRESIDENT FROM 2012-2013. SHE IS A NEW YORK STATE ACCREDITED LABORATORY DIRECTOR. PRIOR TO THE ARC, DR. STRAMER WORKED IN THE DIAGNOSTIC DIVISION OF ABBOTT LABORATORIES AND PRIOR TO THAT IN THE HEPATITIS BRANCH OF THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION. DR. STRAMER WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE OVERALL LEADERSHIP FOR THE PROJECT AND WILL BE THE PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT AT THE COLLABORATING ARC BLOOD CENTERS. WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF THE PROJECT TEAM, SHE WILL BE THE POINT OF CONTACT FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF STUDY SUBJECTS AND COLLECTION OF DATA. SHE WILL PARTICIPATE WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS IN THE ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION AND REPORTING OF THE DATA. DR. STRAMER WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVERALL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS FOR DATA COLLECTION AS REQUIRED UNDER THE TERMS OF THE SUBCONTRACT TO ARC. SHE WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR OBTAINING THE NECESSARY INVESTIGATIONAL REVIEW BOARD APPROVALS FOR THE PROJECT. ROGER DODD, PHD, CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR DR. DODDÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RESPONSIBILITIES WILL INCLUDE PARTICIPATION IN STUDY DESIGN, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, STATISTICAL ANALYSIS, MANUSCRIPT DEVELOPMENT AND INPUT ON REPORTS TO THE FDA, AND OVERALL SCIENTIFIC GUIDANCE OF THE PROJECT. HE HAS >200 SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS AND HAD SERVED NUMEROUS ROLES OF INCREASING RESPONSIBILITY AT THE ARC, AND UNTIL 2014 AS THE VICE PRESIDENT OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OF BIOMEDICAL SERVICES. THE STUDY PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI) (DR. SUSAN STRAMER) AND STUDY CO-PI (DR. ROGER DODD) WILL WORK TOGETHER WITH THE VRI STUDY PI AND CO-PI ON ALL STUDY-RELATED TASKS. THEY WILL ALSO WORK WITH THE OTHER STUDY PIS AND STUDY STAFF TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. BOTH DRS. STRAMER AND DODD ARE EXPERIENCED RESEARCHERS IN BOTH BLOOD CENTER INTERVENTION RESEARCH, BIOTECHNOLOGY CLINICAL TRIALS AND FEDERAL CONTRACTS RELATED TO POLICY AND BLOOD SAFETY (REDS, TTIMS) AS WELL AS OTHER RESEARCH/SCIENCE EXPERIENCE IN INFECTIOUS DISEASES. THE ARC COLLECTS ABOUT 40% OF THE US BLOOD SUPPLY AND HAS DEVELOPED AND MAINTAINED A COMPREHENSIVE DATABASE WITH DETAILED INFORMATION ON EVERY DONATION SINCE 1995. USING THIS TOOL, THE ORGANIZATION HAS ROUTINELY PUBLISHED, IN THE PEER-REVIEWED LITERATURE, INFORMATION ON THE INCIDENCE, PREVALENCE, AND DEMOGRAPHIC AND RISK FACTORS, AND MITIGATION STRATEGIES INCLUDING DONOR SELECTION, TESTING AND PATHOGEN REDUCTION FOR ALL MAJOR INFECTIOUS MARKERS, INCLUDING THOSE FOR HBV, HCV, HIV, HTLV, WEST NILE, ZIKA, DENGUE AND CHIKUNGUNYA VIRUSES, TRYPANOSOMA CRUZI AND BABESIA MICROTI. RESEARCH IN THESE AREAS, AS CONDUCTED BY THE ARC, INCLUDING THE PI AND CO-PI HAVE PROVIDED THE MAJORITY OF DATA TOWARDS PROTECTING THE BLOOD SUPPLY FROM THESE AGENTS IN THE US. AS MENTIONED, THE ARC HAS BEEN INVOLVED IN TTIMS LEADING THE DATA AND DONATION COORDINATING CENTER (DDCC) WHERE DATA ARE COLLECTED IN A SECURE AND QUALITY-CONTROLLED DATABASE FROM EACH OF FOUR BLOOD SYSTEMS COMPRISING APPROXIMATELY 60% OF BLOOD COLLECTED IN THE US. THROUGH CALCULATIONS OF INCIDENCE AND PREVALENCE, AS WELL AS A CO- INVESTIGATOR IN THE LABORATORY AND RISK FACTOR COORDINATING CENTER (LRCC) PORTION OF TTIMS, THE IMPACT OF POLICY CHANGES (E.G., MSM DEFERRAL CHANGES) CAN BE ASSESSED.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY OF LEIDOS AS PART OF THE IEDB & AR PROGRAM IS TO MAINTAIN AND IMPROVE THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE AND CURATION SYSTEMS. IN ADDITION, LEIDOS SHALL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC MEETINGS, PROVIDE PROGRESS REPORTS ON THE WORK AND RESPOND TO IEDB HELP DESK TICKETS IF REQUIRED. AN OVERVIEW OF TASKS TO BE ACCOMPLISHED BY LEIDOS ARE LISTED BELOW: A. IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE SYSTEM AND MAKING IT AVAILABLE TO END USERS. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, STORAGE, ANALYSIS, ARCHIVE AND EXCHANGE OF IMMUNE EPITOPE DATA AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. 2. ASSIST LJI IN MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF THE IEDB WEB PORTAL INCLUDING: A. FURTHER OPTIMIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF UNIFORM, INTELLIGENT WEB-BASED INTERFACES FOR MAKING DATA ACCESSIBLE TO END USERS. THE INTERFACE SHALL MINIMALLY INCLUDE COMPLEX QUERY; SEMANTIC QUERY; DOWNLOAD; EPITOPE SUBMISSION; LINKS TO RELATED RESOURCES; AND REPORTS, MANUSCRIPTS, NEWSLETTERS, AND COMPENDIA. B. UPDATE EXISTING FEATURES AND IMPLEMENT NEW FEATURES IN THE IEDB WEB PORTAL AS NEEDED. C. ASSIST IN ESTABLISHING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE METRICS TO DETERMINE UTILIZATION AND UTILITY OF THE WEB PORTAL WITHIN THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. RELEVANT METRICS SHALL FREQUENCY OF DATA DOWNLOADS, CHARACTERIZATION OF USERS AND USER QUERY STATISTICS. AT A MINIMUM, THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE CONDUCTED BIANNUALLY (EVERY 2 YEARS). 3. UPON REQUEST, ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE AND UPDATING OF SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION INCLUDING: A. DOCUMENT ALL SYSTEM COMPONENTS, SOFTWARE AND DATABASES IN ACCORDANCE WITH INDUSTRY BEST PRACTICES AND IN A MANNER THAT WILL ALLOW ANOTHER CONTRACTOR OR USER TO UNDERSTAND AND UTILIZE THE SYSTEM. B. PROVIDE A HIGH LEVEL OVERVIEW OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES OF THE SYSTEM, INCLUDING SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DESIGN, DATABASE DESIGN AND DATA MODELS. THIS COMPENDIUM OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES SHALL BE UPDATED SEMI-ANNUALLY OR AS REQUESTED BY THE COTR OR CONTRACTING OFFICER. C. WORK WITH LJI TO ESTABLISH AND DOCUMENT A SCHEDULE OF SYSTEM UPDATES AND RELEASES. 4. COMPLY WITH SECTION 508 OF THE REHABILITATION ACT (29 U.S.C. 794D), (SEE HTTP://WWW.SECTION508.GOV/) IN TERMS OF DATABASE/WEBSITE USE AND DIRECT EPITOPE/DATA SUBMISSION BY THE BROADER RESEARCH COMMUNITY. B. CURATION SYSTEM TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB CURATION SYSTEM. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, TRACKING, AND ASSIGNMENT OF PUBLISHED MANUSCRIPTS AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. C. MEETINGS AND REPORTS PARTICIPATE IN WEEKLY MEETINGS TO COORDINATE SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS. ADDITIONALLY, PROVIDE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS SUMMARIZING WORK PERFORMED. D. COMMUNITY OUTREACH 1. IF REQUESTED, ASSIST WITH ADDRESSING ANY HELP DESK TICKETS RELATED TO ANY IEDB SYSTEMS INFRASTRUCTURE. 2. ASSIST LJI WITH PREPARING A COMPENDIUM OF THE DATA IN THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

description: THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO DELINEATE THE B-CELL AND SEROLOGICAL ANTIBODY REPERTOIRES ELICITED BY INFLUENZA VIRUS, INCLUDING A MOLECULAR-LEVEL ASSESSMENT OF INFLUENZA VACCINE CANDIDATES THROUGH PRECLINICAL ANIMAL STUDIES, EARLY PHASE CLINICAL TRIALS, AND HEALTHY VOLUNTEER HUMAN CHALLENGE STUDIES. ALL SPECIMENS FOR ANALYSIS SHALL BE PROVIDED BY THE NIH CIVICS CONTRACT PRIME, NAMELY, DUKE HUMAN VACCINE INSTITUTE. THE GEORGIOU AND IPPOLITO LABS AT UT AUSTIN SHALL PERFORM HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING OF RESPONDING B CELLS AND PROVIDE AN ANALYSIS OF THEIR KEY REPERTOIRE FEATURES (E.G., IGHV GENE USE, CDR-H3 LENGTH DISTRIBUTIONS, MUTATIONAL PATTERNS). DRS. GEORGIOU, IPPOLITO, AND THE DUKE HUMAN VACCINE INSTITUTE COMMUNICATE REGULARLY VIA TELEPHONE AND E-MAIL TO ACHIEVE OUR COLLABORATIVE GOALS. SPECIFIC TASKS TO BE PERFORMED AT UT AUSTIN INCLUDE (I) HEAVY-CHAIN-ONLY VH SEQUENCING OF B-CELL SPECIMENS, (II) PAIRED VH:VL SEQUENCING OF B-CELL SPECIMENS, AND (III) PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS OF INFLUENZA-SPECIFIC SEROLOGICAL IMMUNOGLOBULINS. THE TASKS LISTED ABOVE SHALL BE PERFORMED EVERY YEAR FOR THE ENTIRETY OF THIS CIVICS SUBCONTRACT.

description: DR. KUZNIEWICZ, WILL BE THE SITE PI AT KPNC, AND WILL PROVIDE CLINICAL EXPERTISE TO PROJECT STAFF THAT WILL BE USED FOR DEVELOPING AND TESTING PROGRAMMING ALGORITHMS FOR DATASET CREATION AND ANALYSIS. DR. MICHAEL KUZNIEWICZ WILL OVERSEE THE ACCESS, ABSTRACTION, CLEANING, PREPARATION OF THE KAISER PERMANENTE DATASET FOR ANALYSIS. HE WILL PERFORM REVIEW OF ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS TO RETRIEVE RELEVANT CLINICAL INFORMATION TO VALIDATE CLINICAL DIAGNOSES. HE WILL COLLABORATE ON DATA ANALYSES AND PREPARATION OF MANUSCRIPTS FOR PUBLICATION. CYNTHIA CAMPBELL, PHD, MPH, CO-INVESTIGATOR. DR. CAMPBELL IS HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCHER IN SUBSTANCE USE WITH A FOCUS ON PRESCRIPTION OPIOID USE AND MISUSE, CO-OCCURRING PSYCHIATRIC AND MEDICAL CONDITIONS, AND THE USE OF ELECTRONIC HEALTH CARE (EHR) DATA AND INTERVENTIONS TO STUDY THIS ISSUE. SHE HAS DEVELOPED A PRESCRIPTION OPIOID REGISTRY USING EHR DATA. SHE HAS BEEN CONDUCTING RESEARCH RELATED TO OPIOIDS AND OTHER SUBSTANCE USE FOR OVER 15 YEARS, USING PRAGMATIC TRIALS, PATIENT SURVEYS, AND THE HER. SHE WILL CONTRIBUTE HER LONG STANDING EXPERIENCE WORKING WITH MONIQUE HEDDERSON, PHD IS AN EPIDEMIOLOGIST AT THE DIVISION OF RESEARCH, KAISER PERMANENTE NORTHERN CALIFORNIA WHO FOCUSES ON THE FIELD OF MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH. HER RESEARCH PORTFOLIO INVESTIGATES THE INFLUENCE OF PRECONCEPTION, PRENATAL AND EARLY CHILDHOOD EXPOSURES ON MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH. SHE WILL PROVIDE EXPERTISE ON THE IMPACT OF MATERNAL EXPOSURES ON CHILD NEURODEVELOPMENT FOR THE PROJECT. SHE HAS EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE USING THE KPNC DATABASES TO CHARACTERIZE MATERNAL FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE INFANT AND CHILD HEALTH. SHE WILL PROVIDE EXPERTISE RELATED TO IDENTIFICATION OF IMPORTANT MATERNAL AND INFANT VARIABLES TO BE USED FOR MATCHING IN THE MULTIVARIATE MATCHED ANALYSIS PLANNED FOR THE PROJECT. DR. LISA CROEN, CO-INVESTIGATOR. AS A SENIOR RESEARCH SCIENTIST AT THE DIVISION OF RESEARCH (DOR), KAISER PERMANENTE NORTHERN CALIFORNIA (KPNC), AND THE DIRECTOR OF THE KAISER PERMANENTE AUTISM RESEARCH PROGRAM. DR. CROEN OVERSEES THE KP AUTISM REGISTRY AS WELL. SHE WILL PROVIDE EXPERTISE ON AUTISM AND COLLABORATE ON DATA ANALYSES AND PREPARATION OF MANUSCRIPTS FOR PUBLICATION. PROGRAMMER WILL WORK UNDER THE DIRECT SUPERVISION OF DR. KUZNIEWICZ, WILL TEST AND VERIFY CODES TO EXTRACT DATA FROM KPHC. PROGRAMMER WILL ALSO CREATE AND FORMAT ANALYTIC DATASETS AND FORMAT ANALYTIC DATASETS AND PERFORM ANALYSES IN SUPPORT OF ALL STUDY AIMS. RESEARCH ASSOCIATE WILL WORK UNDER THE DIRECT SUPERVISION OF DR. KUZNIEWICZ TO SUPPORT PROJECT PREPARATION, PLANNING, MANAGE SCHEDULING WITH DR. PIMENTEL AT BERKELEY TO CONDUCT REQUIRED WORK FOR PRE-ANALYSIS ON SITE AT KPNC, AND IN COORDINATION WITH THE RESEARCH COORDINATOR AT COLUMBIA IN PROJECT MONITORING AND TEAM COMMUNICATION. WILL PARTICIPATE IN ALL ACTIVITIES RELATED TO RESULTS DISSEMINATION.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON INSTITUTE FOR PROTEIN DESIGN GROUP (UW-IPD), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID BAKER, PH.D. AND WITH SUPPORTING CO-INVESTIGATOR LANCE STEWART, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE). UW-IPD WILL GENERATE COMPUTATIONAL PROTEIN STRUCTURE MODELS FOR HIGH PRIORITY SSGCID PROTEIN TARGETS AND LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY (SVTD) STUDY. A. STRUCTURE MODELING OF AT LEAST 100 SSGCID TARGETS: UW-IPD WILL GENERATE COMPUTATIONAL MODELS USING BOTH ROSETTA METHODS ALONG WITH GREMLIN (CO-EVOLUTION AMINO ACID CONTACT RESTRAINTS). THE ROSETTA MODELS OF ~100 SSGCID TARGETS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY VIA THE WEB SITES OF SSGCID AND THE INSTITUTE FOR PROTEIN DESIGN (IPD). THE ROSETTA MODELS WILL AID CONSTRUCT DESIGN FOR THE SSGCID GENE-TO-PROTEIN PIPELINE AND WILL SERVE AS ATOMIC MODELS TO SUPPORT X-RAY CRYSTAL STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF SSGCID TARGETS BY MOLECULAR REPLACEMENT. THESE EFFORTS WILL PARTIALLY SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. B. STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDIES: UW-IPD WILL USE OPTION PERIOD THREE TERM RESOURCES TO LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDY (SVTD). THIS SVTD IS ENTITLED Â€ŒFACILITATION OF STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DESIGN OF PEPTIDE MACROCYCLES TARGETING MTB DNAN,Â€? THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO USE COMPUTATIONAL PREDICTION AND DESIGN OF PEPTIDE MACROCYLES TO GENERATE CYCLIC PEPTIDE ANALOGS OF NATURAL PRODUCT GRESILMYCIN, THAT TARGETS MTB DNAN. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-IPD WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-IPD WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY UW-IPD STAFF WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. UW-IPD WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. UW-IPD WILL CONDUCT THEIR WORK WITH THE AIM TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS IN HIGH IMPACT PUBLICATIONS.

description: UCB, UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THOMAS EDWARDS, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE). UCB WILL PREPARE SAMPLES FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY STRUCTURE DETERMINATION STUDIES, CONDUCT HIGH THROUGHPUT (HTP) CRYSTALLIZATION EXPERIMENTS, COLLECT DIFFRACTION DATA AND PERFORM STRUCTURE SOLUTION. UCB WILL MANAGE AND MAINTAIN THE TIER 3/22 (CODON-ENGINEERED/MUTAGENESIS), TIER 11 (LIGANDS), TIER 12 (FOL SCREEN) AND TIER 18 (MEMBRANE PROTEINS) PORTIONS OF THE PIPELINE. PETER HORANYI, PH.D. WILL MANAGE THE MEMBRANE PROTEINS PORTION OF THE SSGCID PIPELINE. UCB WILL ALSO LEAD A FUNCTIONAL STUDY. UCB WILL MANAGE (SHEPHERD) OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF SSGCID TARGETS: UCB WILL PREPARE PROTEIN SAMPLES PRODUCED IN-HOUSE AND RECEIVED FROM THE OTHER TEAM SITES FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY STRUCTURE DETERMINATION STUDIES AND CONDUCT HIGH THROUGHPUT (HTP) CRYSTALLIZATION EXPERIMENTS, IN WHICH CRYSTALLIZATION TRIALS, OPTIMIZATION, DATA COLLECTION AND INTERPRETATION MUST BE AUTOMATED, WITH LIMITED HUMAN INTERVENTION. WHEN NECESSARY, UCB WILL CONDUCT CO-CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS OF THE TARGET IN COMPLEX WITH SMALL MOLECULES AND LIGANDS. UCB WILL IDENTIFY AND HARVEST CRYSTALS THAT ARE SUITABLE FOR DIFFRACTION SCREENING AND CONDUCT LARGE SCALE CRYSTAL DIFFRACTION SCREENS, COLLECT DIFFRACTION DATA AND MONITOR QUALITY METRICS OF THE SUITABLE CRYSTALS. UCB WILL PERFORM STRUCTURE SOLUTION, MODEL REFINEMENT AND VALIDATION FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. A STRUCTURE DETERMINATION PROJECT WILL BE CONSIDERED COMPLETE WHEN THE REFINEMENT AND VALIDATION OF THE FINAL STRUCTURE MODELS DO NOT PROVIDE ANY CLEAR SIGNAL OF WHERE THE MODEL CAN BE IMPROVED OR WHEN 3D STRUCTURE QUALITY PARAMETERS SATISFY THE MINIMUM QUALITY REQUIREMENTS ESTABLISHED AND AGREED UPON IN COORDINATION WITH THE CENTER FOR STRUCTURAL GENOMICS OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT AT LEAST 45 TARGET STRUCTURES WILL BE SOLVED AS A PART OF THE TERM (CORE) EFFORTS. APPROXIMATELY 18 STRUCTURES ARE ANTICIPATED TO BE SOLVED THROUGH PIPELINE PROTEIN SAMPLES (TIERS 1/6), AND AN ADDITIONAL 27 STRUCTURES AS OUTLINED IN SECTION B BELOW FROM TIERS 3/22, 8, 11, 12, AND 18. UCB WILL LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. TIERS 3/22 (SYNTHETIC GENES/MUTAGENESIS), 8 (BACULOVIRUS EXPRESSION), 11 (LIGANDS), 12 (FRAGMENT SCREENS) AND 18 (MEMBRANE PROTEINS): UCB WILL DESIGN AND SOURCE CODON-ENGINEERED SYNTHETIC GENE CONSTRUCTS FOR TARGETS ENTERING TIER 3/22 AS NEEDED. UCB WILL SCREEN THE CLONES FOR SOLUBLE EXPRESSION IN E. COLI USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PROTOCOLS. UCB WILL PRODUCE HIGHLY PURIFIED TARGET PROTEINS OR PROTEIN FRAGMENTS IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY FOR CRYSTALLIZATION AND STRUCTURE DETERMINATION. UCB WILL SCREEN FOR PURITY AND CONCENTRATION AND EVALUATE BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF THE PURIFIED SAMPLES (E.G. PROTEIN FOLDING, AGGREGATION, STABILITY AS NEEDED) TO ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS FOR THE STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORTS. IT IS EXPECTED THAT AT LEAST 36 TARGETS WILL ENTER THESE TIERS AND ~1 STRUCTURE WILL BE SOLVED (INCLUDING PROJECTS DESCRIBED BELOW). IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT UCB WILL INITIATE CLONING, BV OR HEK EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION EFFORTS FOR 5-6 TARGETS (OUTSIDE OF THE FUN) WORK DESCRIBED BELOW. IT IS EXPECTED THAT PURIFIED PROTEIN FROM THESE CONSTRUCTS, ALONG WITH ANY BV OR HEK EXPRESSED PROTEINS FROM SCRI WILL ENTER CRYSTALLIZATION TRIALS AT UCB, WITH THE AIM TO OBTAIN 1-2 STRUCTURES (TIER 8/9). UCB WILL CARRY OUT LIGAND CO-CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENING FOR SELECTED TARGETS WITH THE GOAL OF ELUCIDATING TARGET LIGAND CO-CRYSTAL STRUCTURES. THE LIGANDS FOR THIS EFFORT WILL BE CHOSEN BASED ON THE ANTICIPATED BIOCHEMISTRY OF THE TIER 11 TARGETS. IT IS EXPECTED THAT AT LEAST 40 TARGETS WILL ENTER THIS TIER
