description: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF A LARGE (N=6,012), WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF AFRICAN AMERICAN WOMEN WITH LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENTS OF CERVICAL LENGTH BEGINNING IN THE MID-TRIMESTER AND THE COLLECTION OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL TO PERMIT GENOTYPING OF MOTHERS FOR THIS PROPOSAL. FOR FUTURE STUDIES, BIOBANKED SAMPLES OF OFFSPRING DNA, CERVICO-VAGINAL FLUID FOR THE MICROBIOME, AND OTHER BIOMARKERS INCLUDING CYTOKINES ARE AVAILABLE. THE COHORT ALSO INCLUDES 83 WOMEN TREATED WITH VAGINAL PROGESTERONE DUE TO A PREGNANCY COMPLICATED BY A SHORT CERVIX. THE KEY COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE A GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (GWAS) OF MATERNAL DNA FOR LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF ULTRASOUND-MEASURED CERVICAL LENGTH AS A QUANTITATIVE TRAIT. THE FINDINGS OF THE DISCOVERY GWAS WILL BE VALIDATED BY TARGETED GENOTYPING OF AN INDEPENDENT AFRICAN-AMERICAN COHORT. THE VALIDATED LOCI WILL THEN BE USED TO ASSESS HOW SELECT GENOTYPES CAN MODIFY PROGESTERONE RESPONSIVENESS.

description: THE WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY GROUP (WSU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GARRY BUCHKO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE). WSU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST 2 NMR STRUCTURES PER YEAR, WHICH MAY SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR). WSU MAY ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY NMR: WSU (DR. BUCHKO) WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST TWO (2) PROTEINS USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CID RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY WSU/PNNL. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION, AND REPORTING: WSU WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. WSU WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. THE MAJOR AIM OF THE PROJECT WORK WILL BE IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: UCB, UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THOMAS EDWARDS, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK (OPTION PERIOD THREE OPTION QUANTITIES 3 & 4) TO ADDITIONALLY SUPPORT THE BASIC REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE TERM) OF THE SSGCID CONTRACT (CONTRACT NR HHSN272201700059C). UCB WILL SUPPORT ONE OPTION QUANTITY EFFORT (OQS 3 & 4) AMR DRUG DEVELOPMENT FOR ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE AND SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS. A. OPTION QUANTITY EFFORTS UCB WILL USE OPTION QUANTITY RESOURCES (OQS 3 & 4) TO SUPPORT A PROJECT FOCUSED ON STRUCTURE-GUIDED DRUG DEVELOPMENT FOR ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE AND SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS. THE AIMS OF THIS WORK ARE TO STRUCTURALLY CHARACTERIZE INTEGRAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN MSBA, CO-CRYSTALLIZE PENICILLIN BINDING PROTEIN 1A FROM N. GONORRHEA AND C. TRACHOMATIS, AND TO STUDY PREDICTED LIGANDS OF NGTRPRS AS BIOCHEMICAL INHIBITORS, THEIR STRUCTURE BINDING NGTRPRS, AND THEIR ABILITY TO INHIBIT N. GONORRHOEAE GROWTH IN VITRO. STAFF FROM UCB WILL SUPPORT PROTEIN PRODUCTION OF MSBA FOLLOWED BY STRUCTURE DETERMINATION VIA CRYOEM PROTEIN PRODUCTION OF PTP1B FOLLOWED BY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY, AND CRYSTALLOGRAPHY SUPPORT FOR THE STI TRPRS PROJECT. IT IS EXPECTED THAT 5 STRUCTURES WILL BE DETERMINED FROM THESE EFFORTS.

description: O 5.4.4.2.1 SUBTASK 2-A Â€“ PROJECT-LEVEL SOLUTION ENGINEERING SERVICES THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SOLUTION ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR PROJECTS EXECUTED BY THE OCIO. THESE SERVICES MAY INCLUDE END-TO-END SOLUTION ENGINEERING SUPPORT SO THAT IT PROJECTS ACHIEVE THEIR GOALS THROUGH A SYSTEMATIC APPLICATION OF TECHNICAL AND OPERATIONAL EXPERTISE. IN GENERAL, SOLUTION ENGINEERING MUST CONSIDER TECHNICAL, OPERATIONAL, AND BUSINESS PERSPECTIVES IN ENVISIONING HOW THE PROJECT FITS THE OVERALL GOALS OF ACF. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL BRING SUCH A CONTEXT TO BEAR DURING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF SOLUTIONS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE PERSONNEL WITH THE SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE TO ENGINEER SOLUTIONS FOR ON-PREMISE ENVIRONMENTS AND CLOUD ENVIRONMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL INCLUDE EXPERTS WHO HAVE EXPERIENCE IN DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING IN THE PRIMARY CLOUD SERVICE MODELS: INFRASTRUCTURE-AS-A-SERVICE (IAAS), PLATFORM-AS-A-SERVICE (PAAS), AND SOFTWARE-AS-A-SERVICE (SAAS). THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL HELP FULFILL THIS ROLE BY PROVIDING SERVICES RELATED TO THREE ACTIVITY AREAS ALIGNED TO THE EA FUNCTION: ▪ ACTIVITY AREA 1: SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE ▪ ACTIVITY AREA 2: REQUIREMENTS ELABORATION ▪ ACTIVITY AREA 3: ASSESSMENT, EVALUATION, AND RECOMMENDATION OF SOLUTIONS TO TECHNICAL PROBLEMS THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE A TEAM OF TECHNICALLY-MINDED SYSTEM ENGINEERSÂ€”NOT BUSINESS ANALYSTS OR BUSINESS ARCHITECTS. O SUBTASK 2-A, ACTIVITY AREA 1: SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE TO DELIVER SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE SUPPORT SUCCESSFULLY, THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ADVANCE AND SUPPORT ACTIVITIES INCLUDING (BUT NOT LIMITED TO): 1. COORDINATE WITH VENDORS OR WITH THE PROJECT MANAGER TO DEVISE A SOLUTION; THIS SOLUTION WOULD BE IMPLEMENTED WITHIN OPERATIONS (HANDOFF TO SSD SERVICE DELIVERY BRANCH). 2. ENGINEER SOLUTIONS (E.G., NETWORK, VTC, COMPONENTS) THAT RESOLVE EXISTING ACF PROBLEMS. 3. PROVIDE OPERATIONS-ORIENTED SOLUTIONS (EXPANDING ON CONCEPTUAL ARCHITECTURES PROVIDED BY PSP EA) THAT ENCOMPASS ALL LAYERS OF THE TECHNICAL SOLUTION (INFRASTRUCTURE, DATA, APPLICATION, AND INTERFACE). 4. IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES FOR LEVERAGING FEDRAMP-APPROVED CLOUD SOLUTIONS AS PART OF THE OVERALL DESIGN; UPON APPROVAL, COMPLETE SYSTEM DESIGNS, INCORPORATING CLOUD SOLUTIONS APPROPRIATELY. 5. DEVELOP PROJECT-LEVEL SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE VIEWS. 6. PERFORM FUNCTIONAL AND TECHNICAL INTEGRATION DURING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOFTWARE. THIS SHALL INCLUDE FUNCTIONAL INTEGRATION THAT PROVIDES THE APPROPRIATE BUSINESS ORCHESTRATION REQUIRED TO MEET THE NEEDS AND REQUIREMENTS OF THE ACF IT PROJECT. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL INCLUDE A CONCEPTUAL PLAN FOR INTEGRATION REGARDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, COMPONENTS, SERVICES, AND DATA ACROSS THE SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE. 7. IDENTIFY DATA REQUIREMENTS, PREPARE DATA MODELS, AND CREATE DATA VIEWS AS NECESSARY TO SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION ACTIVITIES. 8. ENSURE PROJECT-SPECIFIC EA ADMINISTRATION. IMPLEMENTATION APPROACHES SHOULD BE DESIGNED TO ACHIEVE TO-BE STATES. THIS WOULD INCLUDE: (A) PROJECT-SPECIFIC EA ARTIFACTS IN SUPPORT OF ACF GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK GATE REVIEWS (B) MAINTAINING PROJECT EA DOCUMENTATION AS PROJECTS PROGRESS TOWARD THE TO- BE STATE (C) CONTRIBUTING DETAILED DESIGNS AND ARTIFACTS TO PROJECTS AS NEEDED, TO ENSURE SOLUTIONS ARE CLEAR AND WELL DOCUMENTED. 9. ENSURE DETAILED SYSTEM-LEVEL CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT, TRACKING OF CHANGES, AND PROJECT RELEASES AND REPORTING OF THESE CHANGES AT THE MOST RECENT TRB. O SUBTASK 2-A, ACTIVITY AREA 2: REQUIREMENTS ELABORATION TO EXECUTE REQUIREMENTS ELABORATION SUCCESSFULLY, THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ADVANCE AND SUPPORT ACTIVITIES INCLUDING (BUT NOT LIMITED TO): 1. PROVIDE EXPERTISE IN THE ANALYSIS OF BOTH FUNCTIONAL AND NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS. description: STUDY OUTLINE AND FURTHER DETAILS: THE FDA HAS PROPOSED A STUDY TO CONSIDER CHANGES IN POLICY FROM THE CURRENT DEFERRAL INTERVAL FOR MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN (MSM). THE GOAL OF THE STUDY IS TO GIVE THE FDA ENOUGH DATA TO DETERMINE IF THE MSM DEFERRAL CAN BE LOWERED EVEN FURTHER TO THREE MONTHS AS IS BEING DONE IN CANADA AND OTHER COUNTRIES. THE STUDY WILL NEED A SAMPLE OF 2000 INDIVIDUALS POTENTIALLY INTERESTED IN DONATING BLOOD WHO HAVE HAD SEX WITH MEN AT LEAST ONCE DURING THE PAST THREE MONTHS. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE CONTACTED TWICE OVER THE COURSE OF THE STUDY. THE FIRST VISIT WILL INVOLVE AN IN-PERSON QUESTIONNAIRE AND A COLLECTION OF 7 ML BLOOD SAMPLE. THE SECOND VISIT IS A SECOND INTERVIEW ON RISK FACTORS FOR HIV INFECTION. ONEBLOOD WILL HAVE TWO ENROLLMENT CITIES AND PLAN TO RECRUIT 250 PARTICIPANTS IN EACH CITY TO EQUAL 500 OUT OF THE 2000 PARTICIPANTS. THE NUMBERS HAVE BEEN REACHED IN THE ASSUMPTION THAT EIGHT CITIES WILL BE PARTICIPATING IN THE STUDY. FOR THOSE PARTICIPANTS WHOSE BLOOD TESTS HIV POSITIVE, NOTIFICATION AND COUNSELING MUST BE PROVIDED.

description: SUBCONTRACT TO UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN (DR. ADAM LAURING, CO-INVESTIGATOR) WE WILL USE GENOMIC EPIDEMIOLOGY TO UNDERSTAND PATTERNS OF SARS-COV-2 TRANSMISSION WITHIN COLLEGE STUDENT POPULATIONS, AND BETWEEN STUDENTS AND THE COMMUNITIES IN WHICH THEIR SCHOOLS ARE LOCATED. OUR STUDY WILL FOCUS ON STUDENTS FROM 4 INSTITUTIONS: UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN-MADISON, UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN-MILWAUKEE, UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, AND WAYNE STATE UNIVERSITY. THESE INSTITUTIONS REPRESENT 2 MEDIUM-SIZED Â€ŒCOLLEGE TOWNSÂ€? (MADISON AND ANN ARBOR) AND 2 LARGER CITIES (MILWAUKEE AND DETROIT). THIS SUBCONTRACT TO THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN WILL BE FOR SAMPLING, SEQUENCING, AND ANALYSIS OF VIRUSES FROM INDIVIDUALS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN AND WAYNE STATE UNIVERSITY. SEQUENCING WILL BE PERFORMED DURING THREE SAMPLING INTERVALS. THE FIRST WILL BE IN SEPTEMBER 2020, FOLLOWING THE RESUMPTION OF IN-PERSON INSTRUCTION AT ALL FOUR SCHOOLS. THE SECOND WILL BE IN JANUARY, 2021 WHEN STUDENTS RETURN FOR THE SECOND SEMESTER OF THE ACADEMIC YEAR AND INFLUENZA AND OTHER UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS ARE COMMON. THE THIRD WILL BE IN SEPTEMBER, 2021 WHEN WE ASSUME AN EFFECTIVE SARS-COV-2 VACCINE WILL BE AVAILABLE, BUT PROBABLY NOT YET UNIVERSALLY ADMINISTERED. THUS, INTERVALS 1 AND 2 ARE DURING THE FIRST YEAR OF THE PROJECT, AND INTERNAL 3 IS DURING THE SECOND YEAR OF THE PROJECT. THIS SUBCONTRACT WILL COVER 400 SAMPLES/VIRUSES PER INTERVAL (100 FROM UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, 100 FROM WAYNE STATE UNIVERSITY, 200 FROM THE WAYNE COUNTY COMMUNITY). THEREFORE, WE HAVE BUDGETED FOR 800 SAMPLES/VIRUSES IN THE FIRST YEAR, AND 400 SAMPLES/VIRUSES IN THE SECOND YEAR. VIRUSES WILL BE COLLECTED FROM STUDENTS WHO PRESENT TO CAMPUS HEALTH SERVICES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN OR WAYNE STATE UNIVERSITY AND TEST POSITIVE FOR SARS-COV-2. POST-TESTING, RESIDUAL SPECIMENS WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH TESTING RECORDS AT EACH SITE AND TRANSPORTED TO DR. LAURINGÂ€™S LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN MEDICAL SCHOOL. MEMBERS OF DR. LAURINGÂ€™S LABORATORY WILL EXTRACT VIRAL NUCLEIC ACID AND PREPARE SAMPLES FOR SEQUENCING, USING EITHER THE OXFORD NANOPORE OR ILLUMINA PLATFORM. DR. LAURING AND HIS TEAM WILL ANALYZE THE SEQUENCE DATA TOGETHER WITH THE PROJECT TEAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN (LABORATORIES OF DR. DAVID OÂ€™CONNOR AND DR. THOMAS FRIEDRICH).

description: IN THIS PROJECT, WE BUILD ON PAST FDA FUNDED WORK THAT HAS LED TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW ORGAN-ON-A-CHIP (ORGAN CHIP) MICROFLUIDIC CULTURE DEVICES AS PRECLINICAL TOOLS FOR EVALUATION OF EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF RADIATION MEDICAL COUNTER MEASURES (MCMS), INCLUDING THOSE FOR ACUTE RADIATION SYNDROME.THE MAJOR TASKS ARE TO: 1) TEST THE EFFECTS OF RADIATION MCMS IN THE HUMAN BONE MARROW CHIP RADIOTOXICITY MODEL, 2) EVALUATE THE ROLE OF GUT MICROBIOME IN HUMAN RADIATION INJURY, 3) RECAPITULATE RADIATION-INDUCED PNEUMONITIS IN HUMAN LUNG ALVEOLUS CHIP, AND 4) LEVERAGE THESE IN VITRO MODELS TO DISCOVER NEW RADIATION MCMS. ALL ORGAN CHIPS (BONE MARROW, INTESTINE, AND LUNG) WILL BE EXPOSED TO -RADIATION AT BOSTON CHILDRENÂ€™S HOSPITAL (BCH), AND EXPERIMENTAL HANDLING OF CHIPS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR AND AFTER EXPOSURE WILL BE CARRIED OUT IN OUR BCH LABORATORY TO ENSURE WE ANALYZE IMMEDIATE AND RAPID RESPONSES AS WELL AS LONGER-TERM BIOLOGICAL EFFECTS AFTER EXPOSURE. THE RADIATION-PNEUMONITIS MODEL IN HUMAN LUNG ALVEOLUS CHIP WILL ALSO BE DEVELOPED, OPTIMIZED, AND STUDIED IN THE BCH LABORATORY WHERE CLINICAL EXPERTS IN LUNG INJURY ARE LOCATED.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE). UW-NMR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 3 NMR STRUCTURES DURING THIS ONE YEAR SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, 9/1/2020 Â€“ 8/31/2021). UW-NMR WILL ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF 3 PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES BY NMR: UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF THREE (3) PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CID RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITIES ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON PROTEIN PRODUCTION GROUP (UW-PPG), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF WESLEY C. VAN VOORHIS, M.D., PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (OPTION PERIOD THREE). UW-PPG WILL GENERATE TARGET CLONES, PERFORM SMALL- AND LARGE-SCALE SCREENING, UPSCALE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION OF THE CLONES AND LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY (SVTD) STUDY. UW-PPG WILL MANAGE (SHEPHERD) OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. CLONING, EXPRESSION TESTING, UPSCALE AND PURIFICATION OF SSGCID TARGETS: UW-PPG WILL PERFORM CLONING MAINLY USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PCR-BASED LIGATION INDEPENDENT CLONING INTO E. COLI EXPRESSION VECTORS. UW-PPG WILL SCREEN THEIR EXPRESSION AND SOLUBILITY PROPERTIES USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PROTOCOLS, INCLUDING, AS NEEDED, MULTIPLE EXPRESSION SYSTEMS AND CLEAVAGE SYSTEMS. UW-PPG WILL GENERATE LARGE SCALE EXPRESSIONS OF TARGETS FOR HIGHLY PURIFIED TARGET PROTEINS OR PROTEIN FRAGMENTS AND PRODUCE THEM IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY FOR STRUCTURE DETERMINATION THROUGH STANDARDIZATION AND AUTOMATION OF PROTOCOLS. UW-PPG WILL EVALUATE THE PURITY, CONCENTRATION AND BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES (E.G. PROTEIN FOLDING, AGGREGATION, AND/OR STABILITY) OF THE PURIFIED SAMPLES TO ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORTS. UW-PPG WILL LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDIES: UW-PPG WILL USE OPTION PERIOD THREE TERM RESOURCES TO LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY STUDY (SVTD). THIS SVTD IS ENTITLED Â€ŒTARGET SCREENING USING JOHNSON & JOHNSON JUMPSTARTER COMPOUND LIBRARIES,Â€? THE AIM OF WHICH IS TO DEVELOP HIGH QUALITY HITS FROM A LIBRARY SCREEN, WITH STRUCTURAL INFORMATION, TO ALLOW RATIONAL STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DEVELOPMENT FOR LEISHMANIASIS. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-PPG WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-PPG WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY UW-PPG STAFF WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. UW-PPG WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. UW-PPG WILL CONDUCT THEIR WORK WITH THE AIM TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS IN HIGH IMPACT PUBLICATIONS.

TRACHOMATIS, AND TO STUDY PREDICTED LIGANDS OF NGTRPRS AS BIOCHEMICAL INHIBITORS, THEIR STRUCTURE BINDING NGTRPRS, AND THEIR ABILITY TO INHIBIT N. GONORRHOEAE GROWTH IN VITRO. STAFF FROM UW-PPG WILL PERFORM PROTEIN PRODUCTION, BIOCHEMICAL ASSAYS, AND CHARACTERIZATION STUDIES FOR THIS PROJECT.

ELAINE REED FOCUSES ON PROFILING THE IMMUNE RESPONSE BEFORE AND AFTER HUMAN INFLUENZA VACCINATION TO DETERMINE THE HOST SIGNATURES IN HEALTHY ADULTS AND HIGH-RISK POPULATIONS USING PARALLEL DISCOVERY-BASED AND HYPOTHESIS-BASED APPROACHES. THE IMMUNE PROFILING DATA OBTAINED IN HUMANS IMMUNIZED WITH COMMERCIAL FLU VACCINES WILL BE INTEGRATED WITH PRECLINICAL ANIMAL VACCINATION MODELS USING CANDIDATE UNIVERSAL VACCINES TO DEVELOP INNOVATIVE MODELING FRAMEWORKS TO INFORM ON VACCINE DESIGN AND EFFICACY. PROJECT 2, LED BY DR. REN SUN, WILL CHARACTERIZE AND DEVELOP A HYPER INTERFERON SENSITIVE (HIS) VIRUS, WHICH DISPLAYS SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER IFN PRODUCTION AND SENSITIVITY TO IFN TREATMENT THAN WILD TYPE VIRUS AND ELICITS POTENT T CELL IMMUNITY AND ANTIBODY PRODUCTION. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROPOSAL IS TO FURTHER CHARACTERIZE HIS VACCINE CANDIDATE AS WELL AS USING THIS GENOMIC TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM TO IDENTIFY MORE VACCINE CANDIDATE VIRUSES WITH DESIRED INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES, AND CHARACTERIZE THE VACCINE CANDIDATES IN MULTIPLE IN VIVO MODELS TO IDENTIFY MARKERS ASSOCIATED WITH PROTECTION, WHICH CAN LEAD TO FURTHER INCREASE OF IMMUNOGENICITY AND VACCINE SAFETY.

description: APPLIED RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THE CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) EMERGING PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY TO SUPPORT THE CONCURRENT MACRI, ELECTRONIC AND COMMUNITY BASED COHORT STUDIES OF INCIDENCE AND BURDEN OF COVID-19 AMONG PREGNANT WOMEN. I OFFER THIS LETTER ON BEHALF OF LEIGH MATHIAS AS THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR TO THE ABT TEAM, AND OUR TEAM AT BAYLOR COLLEGE OF MEDICINE. WE HAVE A WELL-ESTABLISHED PARTNERSHIP WITH ABT ASSOCIATES THROUGH PREVIOUS TASK ORDERS RELATED TO THIS WORK, AND HAVE A STRONG COMMITMENT TO CONTINUING OUR PARTNERSHIP. WE ARE PREPARED TO IMPLEMENT A PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY OF PREGNANT WOMEN RECEIVING PRENATAL CARE AND ENROLLED ELECTRONICALLY (ELECTRONIC COHORT) OR IN PERSON (COMMUNITY COHORT) PRIOR TO 28 WEEKS OF GESTATION TO ASSESS TRANSMISSIBILITY OF INFECTION WITH SARS COV-2, RATES OF INFECTION AND ILLNESS, CLINICAL EPIDEMIOLOGY OF COVID-19 DISEASE AND CHARACTERISTICS OF MEDICALLY AND NON-MEDICALLY ATTENDED COVID-19 CASES. IN ADDITION, WE ARE ALSO PREPARED TO IMPLEMENT THE MACRI STUDY TO EVALUATE THE INCIDENCE AND CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS OF COVID-19 IN PREGNANT WOMEN AT THE TIME OF ADMISSION FOR DELIVERY. TO ACCOMPLISH THESE STUDY OBJECTIVES, OUR WORK WILL INCLUDE CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE FINALIZATION OF RESEARCH PROTOCOLS AND DATA COLLECTION FORM, STUDY IMPLEMENTATION AND LOGISTICS AT OUR SITE, SUBJECT RECRUITMENT AND ENROLLMENT, AND COLLECTION OF DATA AND BIOSPECIMEN AMONG COHORT AND PERIPARTUM STUDY PARTICIPANTS, LEVERAGING OUR EXISTING STUDY INFRASTRUCTURE FROM PRIOR INFLUENZA RESEARCH CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ABT AND CDC.

description: THE OBJECTIVE IS TO ADDRESS UNMET NEEDS IN SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGICAL TESTING: 1) STANDARDIZATION, 2) ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, AND 3) AVAILABILITY OF LARGE-SCALE TESTING TO IDENTIFY THOSE WHO MAY HAVE BEEN INFECTED OR EXPOSED TO THE VIRUS. SCALING UP OF VALIDATED SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGICAL ASSAYS WITH EMERGENCY USE AUTHORIZATION (EUA) WITH EVIDENCE OF HIGH SPECIFICITY, SENSITIVITY AND REPRODUCIBILITY, WILL INCREASE NOT ONLY THE NATIONAL TESTING CAPACITY, BUT ALSO ENABLE COMPARISONS OF DATA ACROSS DIFFERENT SITES AND STUDIES. THEREFORE, IT WILL FACILITATE AN UNDERSTANDING OF NATURAL HISTORY OF THE SARS-COV-2 INFECTION, VACCINE DEVELOPMENT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW VACCINE CANDIDATES. THIS WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SERONET (ACADEMIC AND COMMERCIAL SEROLOGY LABORATORIES), INCLUDING THE FNLCR SEROLOGY LABORATORY, SSNCC AND THE SSC, TO DEVELOP AND MAKE AVAILABLE REAGENTS AND STANDARDS TO THE SEROLOGY COMMUNITY ONCE GENERATED AND QUALIFIED

description: THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO DELINEATE THE B-CELL AND SEROLOGICAL ANTIBODY REPERTOIRES ELICITED BY INFLUENZA VIRUS, INCLUDING A MOLECULAR-LEVEL ASSESSMENT OF INFLUENZA VACCINE CANDIDATES THROUGH PRECLINICAL ANIMAL STUDIES, EARLY PHASE CLINICAL TRIALS, AND HEALTHY VOLUNTEER HUMAN CHALLENGE STUDIES. ALL SPECIMENS FOR ANALYSIS SHALL BE PROVIDED BY THE NIH CIVICS CONTRACT PRIME, NAMELY, DUKE HUMAN VACCINE INSTITUTE. THE GEORGIOU AND IPPOLITO LABS AT UT AUSTIN SHALL PERFORM HIGH- THROUGHPUT NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING OF RESPONDING B CELLS AND PROVIDE AN ANALYSIS OF THEIR KEY REPERTOIRE FEATURES (E.G., IGHV GENE USE, CDR-H3 LENGTH DISTRIBUTIONS, MUTATIONAL PATTERNS). DRS. GEORGIOU, IPPOLITO, AND THE DUKE HUMAN VACCINE INSTITUTE COMMUNICATE REGULARLY VIA TELEPHONE AND E-MAIL TO ACHIEVE OUR COLLABORATIVE GOALS. SPECIFIC TASKS TO BE PERFORMED AT UT AUSTIN INCLUDE (I) HEAVY-CHAIN-ONLY VH SEQUENCING OF B-CELL SPECIMENS, (II) PAIRED VH:VL SEQUENCING OF B-CELL SPECIMENS, AND (III) PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS OF INFLUENZA-SPECIFIC SEROLOGICAL IMMUNOGLOBULINS. THE TASKS LISTED ABOVE SHALL BE PERFORMED EVERY YEAR FOR THE ENTIRETY OF THIS CIVICS SUBCONTRACT.

description: THE OBJECTIVE IS TO ADDRESS UNMET NEEDS IN SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGICAL TESTING: 1) STANDARDIZATION, 2) ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, AND 3) AVAILABILITY OF LARGE-SCALE TESTING TO IDENTIFY THOSE WHO MAY HAVE BEEN INFECTED OR EXPOSED TO THE VIRUS. SCALING UP OF VALIDATED SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGICAL ASSAYS WITH EMERGENCY USE AUTHORIZATION (EUA) WITH EVIDENCE OF HIGH SPECIFICITY, SENSITIVITY AND REPRODUCIBILITY, WILL INCREASE NOT ONLY THE NATIONAL TESTING CAPACITY, BUT ALSO ENABLE COMPARISONS OF DATA ACROSS DIFFERENT SITES AND STUDIES. THEREFORE, IT WILL FACILITATE AN UNDERSTANDING OF NATURAL HISTORY OF THE SARS-COV-2 INFECTION, VACCINE DEVELOPMENT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW VACCINE CANDIDATES. THIS WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SERONET (ACADEMIC AND COMMERCIAL SEROLOGY LABORATORIES), INCLUDING THE FNLCR SEROLOGY LABORATORY, SSNCC AND THE SSC, TO DEVELOP AND MAKE AVAILABLE REAGENTS AND STANDARDS TO THE SEROLOGY COMMUNITY ONCE GENERATED AND QUALIFIED.

RESEARCH STUDIES ARE DEVELOPED COLLABORATIVELY BY NIAID AND INRB AND MAY INCLUDE OTHER RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS ACCORDING TO THE PALM MULTILATERAL GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE AND STRATEGIC PLAN. THE SCOPE OF WORK FOR FUTURE RESEARCH WILL INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: STRATEGIC AND OPERATIONAL PLANNING AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT; INFRASTRUCTURE OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE; LOGISTICS AND PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT; SITE DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE ALL CLINICAL SITES REMAIN IN A STATE OF PREPAREDNESS AND COMPLIANCE WITH PROTOCOL REQUIREMENTS; INITIATING AND COMPLETING ENROLLMENT AND FOLLOW-UP FOR THE CLINICAL RESEARCH PROTOCOL; OVERALL MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF THE CONDUCT OF THE MOBILIZATION, PSYCHOSOCIAL SUPPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS EFFORTS; AND OTHER ACTIVITIES SUCH AS LABORATORY SERVICES AND PHARMACY SUPPORT. THE END OF EBOLA OUTBREAK #11 IN THE DRC WAS DECLARED ON 11/18/2020 AND THEREFORE ALL SUPPORT OF THE OUTBREAK IS IN THE PROCESS OF BEING WITHDRAWN OVER THE COMING MONTH. SUPPORT OF THE INRB BIOREPOSITORY STAFFING WILL CONTINUE UNDER THIS SUBCONTRACT THROUGH 3/31/2021 AT WHICH TIME THESE HUMAN RESOURCES WILL BE SUPPORTED BY WAY OF PARTNER INSTITUTIONS. BIOSPECIMENS COLLECTED DURING THE EBOLA OUTBREAK WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE INRB BIOREPOSITORY AND MAY BE USED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH STUDIES.

description: OPTION 23A: 0258-A431-4609 MIAMI DADE COUNTY IN FLORIDA HAS CONSTITUTED A COVID 19 HOTSPOT IN RECENT MONTHS. THE MIAMI CITY OPTION WILL EXPAND THE CIVICS PARIS STUDY AND REFERS TO THE INVESTIGATION OF A MIAMI COHORT THAT WILL BE ENRICHED IN PEOPLE OF AFRICAN AMERICAN AND HISPANIC RACIAL/ETHNICITY. WE WILL BE FOCUSING ON PEOPLE WITH GREATER RISK FOR COVID 19 BECAUSE OF PROFESSION (E.G. HEALTH CARE WORKERS, FIRE FIGHTERS) AND TAKE INTO CONSIDERATION RACE, AGE AND COEXISTING COMORBIDITIES SUCH AS DIABETES, CORONARY HEART DISEASE AND CHRONIC RESPIRATORY DISEASE IN THE DATA ANALYSIS. THE MAJOR GOAL OF IS TO FOLLOW THIS Ã¯Â¿Â½AT-RISKÃ¯Â¿Â½ CATEGORY OF PARTICIPANTS (WITH AND WITHOUT DOCUMENTED SARS COV2 INFECTION) TO DETERMINE THE INCIDENCE, MAGNITUDE, AND DURABILITY OF ANTIBODY AGAINST SARS COV-2 VIRUS AND ITS RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER RESPIRATORY PATHOGENS. THE PARTICIPANTS ARE DIVIDED INTO TWO STUDY GROUPS IN A 1:1 RATIO. GROUP 1 WILL HAVE PREVIOUS OR CURRENT DOCUMENTED PCR-CONFIRMED SARS-COV-2 VIRUS INFECTION (SYMPTOMATIC OR ASYMPTOMATIC) AND GROUP 2 WILL BE COMPRISED OF PARTICIPANTS DEMOGRAPHICALLY MATCHED WITH GROUP 1 BUT CONFIRMED PCR NEGATIVE FOR SARS-COV-2 INFECTION AT THE TIME OF ENTRY INTO THE STUDY. FAMILY MEMBERS OF INFECTED PERSONS WILL BE INVITED TO PARTICIPATE IN ORDER TO INCLUDE ADDITIONAL HIGH RISK PARTICIPANTS AND ALSO DETERMINE POTENTIALLY ASYMPTOMATIC CASES. ALL PARTICIPANTS WILL BE EVALUATED LONGITUDINALLY ONCE A MONTH FOR AT LEAST THREE VISITS UPTO A MAXIMUM OF 12 VISITS. AT EACH VISIT, QUESTIONNAIRES WILL BE USED TO SURVEY RISK, EXPOSURE AND CLINICAL SIGNS OF RESPIRATORY DISEASE/INFECTION. RESPIRATORY PATHOGEN TESTING WILL BE PERFORMED AT ENTRY INTO THE STUDY ON NASOPHARYNGEAL SWABS (CAN BE SUBSTITUTED WITH NASAL OR SALIVARY SAMPLE). WE WILL USE THE BIOFIREÃ¯Â¿Â½ RESPIRATORY 2.1 (RP2.1) PANEL WHICH DETECTS 18 VIRAL AND 3 BACTERIAL TARGETS WITH A RAPID RESULT, AND THE RESULTS WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PARTICIPANTS. REPEAT BIOFIRE TESTING WILL BE PERFORMED IF RESPIRATORY SYMPTOMS OCCUR AT ANY TIME OVER THE COURSE OF THE STUDY FOR INCIDENCE OF INFECTION AND RE-INFECTION. ON FOLLOW-UP MONTHLY VISITS, WE WILL STORE NP SAMPLES REGARDLESS OF SYMPTOMS FOR FUTURE RESEARCH. FOR EXAMPLE, SYSTEMATIC MOLECULAR TESTING OF RESPIRATORY PATHOGENS COULD BE PERFORMED FOR CAPTURING ACCURATE DATA, SUCH AS THAT NEEDED TO CALCULATE INFECTION RATES (AND INCIDENCE OF PROLONGED VIRAL SHEDDING) OF COMMONLY CIRCULATING RESPIRATORY VIRUSES BESIDES SARS-COV-2. SUCH ANALYSES COULD IN ADDITION FILL THE KNOWLEDGE GAP ON INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTION RATES IN VACCINATED AGING PERSONS. VENOUS BLOOD (~60-80 ML) WILL BE COLLECTED MONTHLY AT EACH FOLLOW-UP VISIT AND PROCESSED FOR STORAGE OF SERUM AT -800 C AND CRYOPRESERVATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC) IN LIQUID NITROGEN. SERUM SAMPLES WILL BE BATCH SHIPPED MONTHLY TO DR FLORIAN KRAMMER IN NEW YORK FOR ANTIBODY PROFILING FOR ASSESSMENT OF FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERISTICS, AND ANTIBODY DECAY. SEROCONVERSION INCIDENCE WILL BE MONITORED IN THE CONTROL GROUP. THE PBMC WILL SERVE AS A BIOREPOSITORY FOR FUTURE RESEARCH. IDENTIFY WITHIN-PERSON VIRAL VARIANTS IN NASOPHARYNGEAL SWABS (NPS), OROPHARYNGEAL SWABS (OPS) AND COARSE AND FINE PARTICLE AEROSOLS USING INFLUENZA-SPECIFIC DEEP SEQUENCING TO A) TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT INFLUENZA VIRUS VARIANTS FOUND IN NPS, OPS, AND COARSE AND FINE PARTICLE EXHALED BREATH AEROSOLS REPRESENT INDEPENDENT SETS OF VARIANTS, AND B) IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE NON-SYNONYMOUS VARIANTS, AND VARIANT STABILITY OVER THE COURSE OF UP TO THREE DAYS POST ONSET OF SYMPTOMS, AND C) CHARACTERIZE THE FREQUENCY OF SNPS DIFFERENTIATING CONSENSUS SEQUENCES IN THE UPPER AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT AND THE POTENTIAL OF SEQUENCE ANALYSIS FOR IDENTIFYING NOT ONLY CHAINS OF TRANSMISSION BUT ALSO WHETHER TRANSMISSION WAS FROM THE UPPER OR LOWER AIRWAYS OF THE INDEX CASE; 2. CHARACTERIZE HOST MUCOSAL IMMUNITY IN THROAT SWAB SAMPLES USING HIGHLY SENSITIVE HA- AND NA-PROTEIN ARRAYS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESES THAT SHEDDING IN EXHALED FINE PARTICLE AEROSOLS IS NEGATIVELY ASSOCIATED WITH MUCOSAL ANTIBODY AGAINST THE INFLUENZA VIRUS WITH WHICH THE SUBJECT IS INFECTED, BUT POSITIVELY ASSOCIATED WITH IMMUNITY TO RELATED STRAINS IN THE ABSENCE OF SPECIFIC HIGH-LEVEL IMMUNITY TO THE INFECTING STRAIN, AND THAT DIVERGENCE OF UPPER AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT VIRAL SEQUENCES IS ASSOCIATED WITH A HIGH RATIO OF IGG TO IGA IMMUNITY TO CLOSELY RELATED VIRUSES; 3. IDENTIFY CO-INFECTION USING A TAQMANÂ® ARRAY CARD ASSAY TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AEROSOL SHEDDING IS ASSOCIATED WITH CO-INFECTION, CONTROLLED FOR OTHER HOST FACTORS (INCLUDING BMI, SEX, COUGH FREQUENCY, VACCINATION, MUCOSAL IMMUNITY, SYMPTOMS, ASTHMA, SMOKING, AND VIRAL LOAD AS MEASURED IN NP SWABS). INTEGRATE THE ANALYSIS OF SEQUENCE DATA, MUCOSAL IMMUNITY, AND CO-INFECTION AND INCORPORATE DATA FROM THE DARPA-BARDA PROMETHEUS YEARS 1-3 (2017-19). NON-SEVERABLE OPTION 20E Â€“ EMERGING PATHOGEN PROJECT: 0258-0686-4609 THIS OPTION REPRESENTS PARTIAL FUNDING OF A CONTINUING COVID-19 SURVEILLANCE AND EXHALED BREATH AEROSOL ASSESSMENT STUDY, DESIGNED TO BE CARRIED OUT OVER A PERIOD OF 3 MONTHS. THE RECIPIENT SHALL: 1. RECRUIT COVID-19 CASES THROUGH THREE MECHANISMS: 1) SURVEILLANCE OF AN AT-RISK COHORT VIA DAILY SYMPTOM CHECKS AND WEEKLY PCR TESTING; 2) DIRECT RECRUITING OF CASES THROUGH THE PRINCE GEORGE'S COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT AND LOCAL PROVIDERS INCLUDING THE UMD UNIVERSITY HEALTH CENTER; AND 3) INTENSIVE SURVEILLANCE OF HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS OF CASES IDENTIFIED FROM THE ATRISK COHORT AND REFERRED CASES. THE RECIPIENT SHALL AIM TO RECRUIT AT LEAST 12 CASES PER MONTH (36 OR MORE TOTAL OVER THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE) AND AT LEAST 44 OR MORE TOTAL HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS. 2. OBTAIN MUCOSAL SWABS, BLOOD (SERA AND PBMCS), SALIVA FROM COVID-19 CASES. 3. OBTAIN EXHALED BREATH SAMPLES FROM COVID-19 CASES, VIA THE GESUNDHEIT-II BIOAEROSOL SAMPLER INCLUDING PAIRED BACK-TO-BACK SAMPLES FROM EACH CASE WEARING A) A FACE MASK OR FACE SHIELD, AND B) NO FACE MASK OR SHIELD, AND/OR A) WITHOUT LOUD TALKING OR SINGING AND B) WITH LOUD TALKING OR SINGING, ON AT LEAST TWO SEPARATE DAYS. 4. TEST SALIVA, SWABS, AND EXHALED BREATH SAMPLES FOR SARS-COV-2 USING THE THERMO-FISHER TAQPATH ASSAY IN A 96-WELL FORMAT IN A QUANTSTUDIO 7, AND QUANTITATE RNA COPY NUMBERS IN POSITIVE SAMPLES. 5. CULTURE POSITIVE SAMPLES FOR VIRUS THROUGH THE SERVICES OF MATTHEW FRIEMAN'S BSL-3 LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND SCHOOL OF MEDICINE IN BALTIMORE. 6. ANALYZE QRT-PCR AND CULTURE ANALYSIS RESULTS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESES A) THAT ASYMPTOMATIC AND MINIMALLY SYMPTOMATIC INFECTIONS SHED INFECTIOUS AEROSOLS; B) THAT A SMALL FRACTION OF CASES SHED THE VAST MAJORITY OF VIRAL AEROSOLS; AND C) THAT SURGICAL AND HOMEMADE FACE MASKS BUT NOT FACE SHIELDS ARE EFFECTIVE SOURCE CONTROL. 7. MAINTAIN A BIOREPOSITORY OF THESE SAMPLES.

description: WHILE MANY MINE HEALTH AND SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS HAVE BEEN MADE IN RECENT DECADES, THE UNDERGROUND COALMINE ENVIRONMENT STILL PRESENTS NUMEROUS HEALTH AND SAFETY HAZARDS. IN PARTICULAR, THE COALMINE WORKING SECTION IS AN EXTREMELY HAZARDOUS LOCATION. IN 2017 AND 2018, THERE WERE 14 FATALITIES IN US UNDERGROUND COALMINES. OF THESE, NINE (64%) HAD THE ACCIDENT CLASSIFICATION OF POWERED HAULAGE. FOR EXAMPLE, ON JANUARY 14, 2019, A SURVEYOR IN A KENTUCKY COALMINE WAS STRUCK AND KILLED BY A SHUTTLE CAR TRAMMING TO A FEEDER. CONSIDERING THESE HAZARDS, AS WELL AS THOSE ASSOCIATED WITH RESPIRABLE DUST (E.G. COAL AND SILICA DUST), ROOF AND RIB FALLS, FIRE, ETC., REMOVING MINERS FROM HAZARDOUS LOCATIONS TO SAFER ONES WOULD GREATLY BENEFIT MINERS. description: DOGS WITH NATURALLY OCCURRING CANCERS CAN SERVE AS A BETTER MODEL SYSTEM FOR EVALUATING NOVEL CANCER IMMUNO-THERAPEUTICS THAN THE TRADITIONAL MOUSE MODEL SYSTEMS, AND ALSO PROVIDE A TARGET PATIENT GROUP. HOWEVER, USE OF CANINE CANCER PATIENTS IS CURRENTLY LIMITED BY THE AVAILABILITY OF SUITABLE REAGENTS TO MONITOR CANINE IMMUNE RESPONSES. THE MAJORITY OF COMMERCIALLY-AVAILABLE REAGENTS FOR CANINE BIOMARKERS ARE RABBIT POLYCLONAL REAGENTS, WHICH ARE NOT RENEWABLE AND SUFFER FROM LOT-TO-LOT VARIABILITY. FOLLOWING OUR SUCCESS IN PHASE I, HERE WE PROPOSE TO USE OUR NOVEL YEAST RABBIT ANTIBODY DISPLAY PLATFORM TO DISCOVER HIGH AFFINITY, HIGHLY SPECIFIC RABBIT MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES AGAINST AN EXPANDED PANEL OF 26 CANINE BIOMARKERS. IN PARALLEL, WE PLAN TO OPTIMIZE THE CANINIZED ANTI-CANINE-PD-1 ANTIBODY ISOLATED IN PHASE I AS A CANINE IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC, THEN PERFORM A PILOT STUDY IN PET DOGS WITH LYMPHOMA TO ASSESS ITS SAFETY AND EFFICACY AS CONCURRENT THERAPY WITH STANDARD OF CARE CHEMOTHERAPY USING THE BIOMARKER REAGENTS GENERATED DURING THIS PROJECT TO ASSESS IN VIVO IMMUNE RESPONSES TO TREATMENT. A SUCCESSFUL OUTCOME WILL RESULT IN A PANEL OF HIGH QUALITY, WELL CHARACTERIZED, RENEWABLE REAGENTS FOR CANINE BIOMARKERS THAT WILL FACILITATE FUTURE DEVELOPMENT OF IMMUNOTHERAPEUTICS PLUS PROVIDE A NOVEL TREATMENT FOR CANINE LYMPHOMA.

description: THE NIAID DIVISION OF MICROBIOLOGY AND INFECTIOUS DISEASES (DMID) SUPPORTS EARLY PHASE DEVELOPMENT OF VACCINES AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. UNDER THE CONTRACT PROPOSAL TO THE NIAID SUBMITTED IN OCTOBER 2013, IDRI HAS SUCCESSFULLY FORMULATED AND MANUFACTURED THE PROPHYLACTIC TUBERCULOSIS (TB) VACCINE (ID93) CO-LYOPHILIZED WITH AN OIL-IN-WATER EMULSION ADJUVANT TO PRODUCE A THERMOSTABLE, SINGLE VIAL CANDIDATE PRODUCT WITH AN ONGOING CLINICAL TRIAL. IN THIS CONTRACT EXTENSION, WE FURTHER PROPOSED TO PRODUCE THE SAME VACCINE AS A SPRAY-DRIED MATERIAL FOR BULK STORAGE AND MUCOSAL DELIVERY. TO DETERMINE WHETHER SPRAY-DRYING OF THE ID93+GLA-SE VACCINE ALTERS ITS BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY WE WILL EMPLOY THE MOUSE MODEL OF IMMUNOGENICITY AND PROTECTIVE EFFICACY THAT HAS BEEN USED THROUGHOUT THIS CONTRACT. WE WILL COMPARE THE BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITIES OF THE SPRAY-DRIED ID93+GLA-SE MATERIALS TO THE RECONSTITUTED SPRAY-DRIED ID93+GLA-SE FOR THEIR H1/TH2 RESPONSES VIA AEROSOL, INTRANASAL AND INTRAMUSCULAR IMMUNIZATIONS.

description: DR. HARRIS WILL COLLABORATE WITH DRS. DANIELA WEISKOPF AND ALESSANDRO SETTE WITH CONTRIBUTION OF HER EXPERTISE ON ZIKA, CHIKUNGUNYA, AND DENGUE AND ARBOVIRAL IMMUNOLOGY. SHE WILL ALSO COORDINATE WITH THE SUSTAINABLE SCIENCES INSTITUTE AND THE NICARAGUAN MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND HELP SUPERVISE THE SELECTION, SEROLOGICAL ANALYSIS, CODING AND SHIPPING OF HUMAN PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC) FROM NICARAGUAN INDIVIDUALS WHO PARTICIPATE IN BLOOD DONATIONS AT THE NICARAGUAN NATIONAL BLOOD BANK. THESE SAMPLES ARE PRE-COLLECTED AND DE-IDENTIFIED. SHE WILL ALSO HELP SUPERVISE THE SELECTION, CODING AND SHIPPING OF HUMAN PBMCS FROM NICARAGUAN INDIVIDUALS WHO PARTICIPATED IN NICARAGUAN STUDIES OF CHIKUNGUNYA AND DENGUE AS PART OF THE RETROSPECTIVE PORTION OF THE CONTRACT; THESE SAMPLES ARE ALSO PRE-COLLECTED AND DE-IDENTIFIED. HER LABORATORY WILL PERFORM NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS IN 80-100 ZIKA POSITIVE DONOR PBMC OVER THE FIRST THREE YEARS. SHE WILL PARTICIPATE IN ANNUAL MEETINGS AND PLANNED TELECONFERENCES AS APPROPRIATE AS WELL IN PREPARATION OF PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS. SHE WILL VISIT THE FIELD SITE ONCE PER YEAR.

TABLE 1 IDENTIFIES THE CLINICAL ASSAYS THAT WILL BE USED TO EVALUATE TBVPX-120 VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNOGENICITY. TO ACHIEVE THIS STUDY OUTCOME, CELLULAR RESPONSES WILL BE ASSESSED BY INTRACELLULAR CYTOKINE STAINING (ICS) AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC CYTOKINE (IFNÃŽÂ³, IL-10) ELISPOTS. IN ADDITION, HUMORAL RESPONSES WILL BE EVALUATED BY ELISA FOR TOTAL ID93 AND ID93-COMPONENT (RV1813, RV2608, RV3619, RV3620) IGG ANTIBODIES AND FOR ID93-SPECIFIC IGG SUBCLASSES (IGG1, IGG2, IGG3, IGG4). description: COLLECT MOST RECENT DEMOGRAPHIC DATA FROM US CENSUS ON OVERALL POPULATION BY SEX, AGE, & RACE/ETHNICITY FOR EACH PARTICIPATING METROPOLITAN AREA. COLLECT, CLEAN, & COLLATE FROM BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS FOR EACH PARTICIPATING METROPOLITAN AREA, INCLUDING TOTAL NUMBER OF BLOOD DONATIONS STRATIFIED BY FIRST-TIME OR REPEAT DONATIONS, SEX OF DONOR, AGE IN YEARS, RACE/ETHNICITY, BLOOD TYPE, & ZIP CODE OF RESIDENCE. COLLECT DEMOGRAPHIC & OTHER SELECTED DATA FOR EACH BLOOD DONATION SPECIMEN SELECTED TO UNDERGO SARS- COV-2 ANTIBODY TESTING, INCLUDING STUDY ID, DONOR SEX, AGE IN YEARS, RACE/ETHNICITY, ZIP CODE OF RESIDENCE, WHETHER DONATION WAS FIRST-TIME OR REPEAT, & DATE OF BLOOD DONATION. WE ASSUME DEIDENTIFIED DATA FROM BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS ON SELECTED SPECIMENS WILL BE COMPILED & CLEANED BY VRI & TRANSMITTED TO WESTAT FOR FURTHER PROCESSING. COLLECT RESULTS DATA FOR EACH BLOOD DONOR SPECIMEN SELECTED TO UNDERGO SARS-COV-2 ANTIBODY TESTING, INCLUDING STUDY ID, SARS-COV-2 ANTIBODY TESTING RESULTS, ABO BLOOD GROUP, & IF APPLICABLE, CONFIRMATORY TESTING RESULTS. WE ASSUME TESTING DATA FROM BLOOD TESTING LABORATORIES WILL BE CLEANED & COLLATED BY VRI & TRANSMITTED TO WESTAT FOR FURTHER PROCESSING. PERFORM TRIANGULATION/COMPARISON BETWEEN BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS, DEMOGRAPHIC DATA FROM SPECIMENS SELECTED TO UNDERGO SARS-COV-2 ANTIBODY TESTING, & US CENSUS DATA FOR EACH PARTICIPATING METROPOLITAN AREA TO DETERMINE APPROPRIATE POST-STRATIFICATION OR CALIBRATION-TYPE WEIGHTING DETERMINATIONS THAT SHOULD BE USED TO EXTRAPOLATE SEROPREVALENCE RESULTS FROM BLOOD DONATION SPECIMENS TO GENERAL POPULATION IN EACH METROPOLITAN AREA. USE WEIGHTING DETERMINATIONS TO APPROPRIATELY EXTRAPOLATE SEROPREVALENCE DATA FROM BLOOD DONOR SAMPLES TO DETERMINE OVERALL SEROPREVALENCE FOR EACH ONE-MONTH FOR 13 CONSECUTIVE MONTHS, & ONCE AT 18-MONTHS, IN EACH METROPOLITAN AREA (OR LARGER GEOGRAPHIC REGION IF DETERMINED TO BE STATISTICALLY APPROPRIATE) STRATIFIED BY AGE & SEX, AT A MINIMUM, & RACE/ETHNICITY IF POSSIBLE GIVEN SAMPLE SIZE STATISTICAL LIMITATIONS. UTILIZE AVAILABLE DATA THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH ACADEMIC, CDC, & OTHER PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEAGUES WHO ARE RUNNING COMMUNITY & COMMERCIAL LABORATORY-BASED SARS-COV-2 SEROSTUDIES WITHIN PARTICIPATING METROPOLITAN REGIONS TO PERFORM SENSITIVITY ANALYSES FOR BLOOD DONATION SEROPREVALENCE ESTIMATES FOR GENERAL POPULATION. DATA SHARING MECHANISMS WILL BE DETERMINED THROUGH DISCUSSIONS WITH CDC PROJECT STAFF. WE ASSUME CDC WILL PROVIDE WESTAT ACCESS TO CLEAN ANALYTIC DATASETS. CALCULATE CHANGES IN OVERALL, GEOGRAPHIC REGION, AGE- GENDER- & RACE- ETHNICITY-SPECIFIC SEROINCIDENCE OF SARS-COV-2 IN DONATION POPULATIONS & EXTRAPOLATED GENERAL POPULATIONS FOR DESIGNATED METROPOLITAN AREA BY DETERMINED TIME INTERVALS OVER COURSE OF PROJECT & RELATE THOSE RESULTS TO CLINICAL CASES, DEATHS, & COMMUNITY SEROSURVEY DATA. PRESENT FINAL RESULTS IN AGGREGATE, STRATIFIED BY APPROPRIATE INTERVALS & GEOGRAPHIC AREAS (POTENTIAL GEOGRAPHIC AREAS COULD INCLUDE CITY, CORE-BASED STATISTICAL AREA, STATE, CENSUS REGION, & NATIONWIDE), AGE, GENDER, & RACE/ETHNICITY. TRANSMIT CLEANED/COLLATED DATA ELECTRONICALLY TO CDC MONTHLY AT DAY & TIME REQUIRED BY CDC. ALL DATA TRANSMITTED TO CDC WILL BE SECURELY STORED ACCORDING TO EXISTING DATA STORAGE RULES & REQUIREMENTS. THESE DATA WILL BE TRANSFERRED SECURELY IN A MANNER TO BE DESCRIBED BY CDC. STORE DATA ELECTRONICALLY IN AN ENCRYPTED MANNER TO ENSURE REAL-TIME, USER-LEVEL ACCESS TO APPROVED PROJECT PERSONNEL. ACCESS TO THESE DATA WILL BE PROVIDED THROUGH A WEB INTERFACE & AN API. WESTAT ASSUMES DATA MODEL IS ALREADY DEFINED & NO VISUALIZATIONS ARE REQUIRED. WESTAT WILL PROVIDE ACCESS TO THREE PRE-DEFINED DATA VIEWS (I.E. NO SEARCHING). API WILL BE PROVIDED ACCESS TO SAME THREE VIEWS AS USER INTERFACE. ADJUST EXISTING REDS-IV-P RESPONSE STUDY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM/QUESTIONNAIRE, DEPLOY, & HOST SITE FOR VRI. WE ASSUME NO CHANGES WILL BE MADE TO RESPONSE SYMPTOM QUESTIONNAIRE.

EXTRACTING AND PREPARING DH DATA IN STANDARDIZED VSD STRUCTURE AND FORMAT (ALL VSD FILES) FOR ALL COVID-19 RELATED ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING ACCESS TO DH DDM TO CDC AND RUNNING SAS PROGRAMS USING A DDM, AND REVIEWING AND APPROVING SAS PROGRAMS BY DEADLINES SET BY CDC, 2. CONDUCTING DATA QUALITY ASSESSMENTS OF DH DATA FOR COVID-19 RELATED ACTIVITIES, 3. UPLOADING COVID-19 DH DATA DIRECTLY TO THE VSD HUB, 4. COMPLETING NECESSARY REGULATORY ELEMENTS INCLUDING IRB APPROVAL AND DUA EXECUTION FOR COVID-19 ACTIVITIES, 5. TIMELY AND ONGOING INVOICING FOR THE COVID-19 ACTIVITIES, 6. description: DR. ANTONINO CATANZARO AND HIS TEAM AT UCSD WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS: OVERSEEING THE ENROLLMENT OF THREE COHORTS OF CLINICAL PATIENTS; COLLECTING, PROCESSING, AND SHIPPING CLINICAL SAMPLES AND ASSOCIATED CLINICAL DATA; AND COLLECTING AND SHARING LABORATORY DATA AND SUPPORTING ANALYSES, AND PUBLICATION OF RESULTS. THE THREE PATIENT COHORTS WE WILL RECRUIT FOR THE PROJECT INCLUDE: NOTE: STOOL AND SPUTUM SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED AND PROCESSED AT THE RECRUITMENT SITE FOR SHIPMENT TO LJI FOR ALL LISTED COHORTS. 1. PHERESIS COHORT SIZE: 20 PATIENTS WHO ARE BCG-POSITIVE AND IGRA-NEGATIVE; AT LEAST 5 OF WHICH TO BE RECRUITED DURING YEAR 1 (9/30/2019-9/29/2020) AND THE REMAINING DONORS TO BE RECRUITED DURING YEAR 2 (9/30/2020-9/29/2021). IGRA-NEGATIVE PATIENTS WILL BE THE PRIORITY FOR RECRUITMENT DURING YEAR 1; HOWEVER, SHOULD IGRA-POSITIVE PATIENTS BE IDENTIFIED DURING THIS WAVE OF RECRUITMENT, THEY WILL BE INCLUDED IN THIS COHORT, WITH A TARGET OF 20 TOTAL PATIENTS TO BE COMPLETED IN YEAR 2 (9/30/2020-9/29/2021). 2. LONGITUDINAL COHORT SIZE: 40 PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH ACTIVE TB INFECTION UNDERGOING TB TREATMENT, TO BE RECRUITED STARTING IN YEAR 2 (9/30/2020-9/29/2021), WITH FOLLOW-UP COLLECTIONS TO BE CONCLUDE IN YEAR 3 (9/30/2021-9/29/2022). TB DIAGNOSIS TO BE DEFINED AS: DIAGNOSED ACTIVE TB CONFIRMED BY POSITIVE CULTURE FOR SPUTUM TIMEPOINTS/VOLUMES: 20-40 ML AT DIAGNOSIS, END OF TREATMENT, AND 1-YEAR POST-DIAGNOSIS; 250-450 ML AT 3 MONTHS POST-DIAGNOSIS (MID-TREATMENT). PROGRESSION COHORT SIZE: 100 PATIENTS AT RISK FOR PROGRESSION TO ACTIVE TB FROM THE HIGH-RISK COHORTS WITH ACTIVE TB CONTACTS TO BE RECRUITED STARTING IN YEAR 2 (9/30/2020-9/29/2021), WITH FOLLOW-UP COLLECTIONS TO CONTINUE IN YEAR 3 (9/30/2021- 9/29/2022) TIMEPOINTS/VOLUMES: 40 ML AT 0-, 3-, AND 6-MONTHS.

description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS ACQUISITION IS TO OBTAIN SURVEY DATA, SPECIMEN COLLECTION, TRANSPORTATION, AND TESTING FROM THE PROSPECT STUDY. THIS PROJECT WILL BE THE FIRST REPRESENTATIVE ARBOVIRUS SEROSURVEY IN PUERTO RICO. IT WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO RISK FACTORS AND TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS ACROSS THE ISLAND. THESE COMPONENTS ARE CRITICAL FOR ONGOING AND FUTURE EFFORTS TO PREVENT AND CONTROL DENGUE ON THE ISLAND THROUGH INTERVENTIONS (E.G. VECTOR CONTROL, VACCINATION). THE PROJECTS AIMS ARE TO: 1) IMPLEMENT SENTINEL ENHANCED AFI SURVEILLANCE AT ONE SITE IN THE SAN JUAN METROPOLITAN AREA; 2) ESTABLISH BASELINE INCIDENCE OF ARBOVIRUSES, INFLUENZA AND LEPTOSPIROSIS AND MEASURE TRENDS AFTER AN ATMOSPHERIC EVENT; 3) COMPARE OBSERVED EPIDEMIOLOGIC TRENDS IN PATHOGENS DETECTED AT SENTINEL ENHANCED SURVEILLANCE SITE IN SAN JUAN WITH THOSE OF PASSIVE SURVEILLANCE FROM SAN JUAN AND ENHANCED SURVEILLANCE FROM PONCE. FDI CLINICAL RESEARCH WILL FURNISH THE NECESSARY MANAGEMENT AND PERSONNEL FOR THE EFFICIENT PERFORMANCE OF THESE DUTIES: SPECIMEN COLLECTION FOR RECRUITED PROSPECT PARTICIPANTS; SPECIMEN PREPARATION, STORAGE, AND PERIODIC TRANSPORT TO DENGUE BRANCH; AND PROVIDE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PARTICIPANT DATA FOR RISK ANALYSES.

description: THIS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT (R&D) CONTRACT WAS AWARDED AS PART OF THE MULTIPLE-AWARD INDEFINITE DELIVERY, INDEFINITE QUANTITY (IDIQ) CONTRACTS FOR THE CONTRACEPTIVE CLINICAL TRIALS NETWORK (CCTN) FEMALE SITES. THE PURPOSE OF THESE CONTRACTS IS TO ESTABLISH A NETWORK OF CLINICAL RESEARCH SITES COLLABORATING TO EVALUATE NEW FEMALE CONTRACEPTIVE DRUGS AND DEVICES FOR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN PHASE I, II, III AND IV CLINICAL TRIALS. THIS CONTRACT SHALL PROVIDE THE REQUISITE PERSONNEL, FACILITIES AND SERVICES TO CONDUCT AND SUPPORT THESE CLINICAL TRIALS. THE DATA COLLECTED FROM THE CCTN THROUGH CLINICAL TRIALS ON NEW ENTITIES ARE THE BASIS FOR ADVANCING CANDIDATE DRUGS AND DEVICES THROUGH DEVELOPMENT WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF SUBMISSION TO THE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) IN SUPPORT OF REGULATORY APPROVAL. PRODUCTS EVALUATED IN THE CCTN ARE SELECTED TO ADDRESS GAPS IN AVAILABLE CONTRACEPTIVE TECHNOLOGY, INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SAFER, MORE ACCEPTABLE, AND MORE ACCESSIBLE CONTRACEPTIVE METHODS FOR WOMEN, INCLUDING WOMEN WHO ARE OBESE OR HAVE OTHER RISK FACTORS THAT LIMIT THEIR USE OF EXISTING METHODS.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK SARS-COV-2 B CELL EPITOPE MAPPING SUPPLEMENT (WILSON) SUBCONTRACT TO THE SUPPLEMENT FOR: NIAID CONTRACT 75N93019C00062 (FREEMONT, PI, PD) B CELL MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF PROTECTION FROM SARS-COV-2 PATRICK C. WILSON, SUBCONTRACT PI DEPARTMENT OF MEDICINE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO CHICAGO IL 60637 E-MAIL: WILSONP@UCHICAGO.EDU Ã¢Â‚¬Æ’ STATEMENT OF WORK CORONAVIRUSES ARE ENVELOPED NON-SEGMENTED POSITIVE-SENSE RNA VIRUSES BELONGING TO THE FAMILY CORONAVIRIDAE AND CIRCULATE BROADLY AMONGST AND BETWEEN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS. OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, TWO BETACORONAVIRUSES, SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (SARS-COV) AND MIDDLE EAST RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (MERS-COV), WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVER 10,000 CASES OF INFECTION. THE MORTALITY RATE OF SARS-COV WAS 10% WITH 29 COUNTRIES AFFECTED, AND THE MORTALITY RATE OF MERS WAS 35% WITH 27 COUNTRIES AFFECTED GLOBALLY. IN DECEMBER OF 2019, A NOVEL CORONAVIRUS (2019-NCOV) WAS DISCOVERED THROUGH DEEP SEQUENCING ANALYSIS AFTER A SERIES OF PNEUMONIA CASES WERE REPORTED IN WUHAN, HUBEI, CHINA WITH UNKNOWN VIRAL ORIGIN. SEVERAL INDEPENDENT STUDIES HAVE SINCE CONFIRMED THAT THE NOVEL VIRUS ORIGINATED FROM EXPOSURES IN A WUHAN SEAFOOD MARKET. BY ONLY MARCH 16, 2020, 2019-NCOV CAUSED A PANDEMIC SPANNING MOST COUNTRIES ON EARTH WITH A REPORTED 167,000 PEOPLE INFECTED WORLDWIDE, AND ALMOST 7000 CONFIRMED DEATHS. CASE AND MORTALITY RATES ARE CONTINUING TO RISE AND THE LACK OF ADEQUATE TESTING IN MAJOR POPULATION CENTERS PLUS CLEAR EVIDENCE OF COMMUNITY TRANSMISSIONS SUGGESTS THAT THE NUMBER OF INFECTED IS LIKELY SIGNIFICANTLY GREATER. MOREOVER, AS THE VIRUS CONTINUES TO SPREAD, ITS HIGH MUTATION RATE INTRODUCES THE THREAT OF INFECTIONS WITH NEW VARIANTS WHICH COULD HAVE ALTERED SEVERITY AND TRANSMISSIBILITY. THESE OCCURRENCES NECESSITATE THE URGENCY OF NOVEL PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC MEASURES TO HELP PREVENT THE SPREAD OF NCOV-2019, WHICH POSES ONE OF THE GREATEST GLOBAL HEALTH THREATS IN MODERN HISTORY. MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MAB) ARE MONOVALENT PROTEINS EXPRESSED BY B CELLS THAT CAN SPECIFICALLY TARGET 3-DIMENSIONAL VIRAL EPITOPES, LEADING TO POTENT VIRAL NEUTRALIZATION. MABS HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED MODERN MEDICINE BY PROVIDING PRECISION MEDICINE AGAINST MANY DISEASES, WITH OVER 70 MAB-BASED DRUGS APPROVED BY THE FDA. THE ISOLATION OF HUMAN MABS SPECIFIC FOR HIGHLY IMMUNOGENIC NCOV-2019 PROTEINS CAN BE RAPIDLY USED AS THERAPEUTIC AGENTS, FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS, AND FOR TEMPLATING THE GENERATION OF VACCINES THAT CAN PROTECT AGAINST NCOV-2019. OUR LABORATORY IS HIGHLY SPECIALIZED IN THE RAPID GENERATION OF NEUTRALIZING MABS FROM HUMAN B CELLS. WE AIM TO APPLY THIS EXPERTISE TO GENERATE HUMAN NCOV-2019-SPECIFIC MABS, WHICH HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RAPIDLY ALLEVIATE THE GLOBAL HEALTH BURDEN IMPOSED BY NCOV-2019 THROUGH THREE CRITICAL MEASURES: PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC. BY INVESTIGATING THE HUMAN ANTIBODY RESPONSE TO NCOV-2019, WE WILL GAIN IMPORTANT INSIGHT INTO THE IMMUNOGENICITY AND IMMUNODOMINANCE OF NCOV-2019 VIRAL PROTEINS, WHICH WILL IN TURN INFORM WHICH VIRAL TARGETS WILL BE MOST IMPORTANT TO PURSUE WITH THERAPEUTICS AND VACCINES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROPOSED SUPPLEMENT ARE AS FOLLOWS: A) GENERATE PANELS OF HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS. COVID-19 PATIENT BLOOD WILL BE OBTAINED FROM SEVERAL SOURCES INCLUDING VERIFIED INFECTED SAMPLES FROM TOKYO THROUGH COLLABORATOR YOSHI KAWAOKA, THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO OR OTHER HOSPITALS FROM COVID-19 ADMITTED PATIENTS, OR THROUGH OTHER COLLABORATING LABS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 SPIKE PROTEIN, SPIKE RBD AND ORF7 FROM DAVED FREEMONTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, VERSIONS OF THE SPIKE PROTEIN AND RBD FROM FLORIAN KRAMMERS LABORATORY, PLUS NSP3, NSP5, NSP9, NSP10, NSP15, NSP16, AND N PROTEIN FROM ANDRJEZ JOACHIMIACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, OR TO UNBIASED OTHER EPITOPES TARGETED BY ACTIVATED B CELLS AND PLASMABLASTS WILL BE DEVELOPED BY PATRICK WILSONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE RICKETTS BIOCONTAINMENT LABORATORY ON THE ARGONNE NATIONAL LABS CAMPUS AND AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO. B) EVALUATE THE B CELL RESPONSE OF COVID-19 PATIENTS: THE WILSON LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO WILL CHARACTERIZE PERIPHERAL BLOOD B CELLS REACTIVE TO SARS-COV-2 ENCODED PROTEINS OR ACTIVATED DURING INFECTION PLUS TFH CELLS USING SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOME AND CITE-SEQ ANALYSIS ON THE 10XGENOMICS PLATFORM. FROM THIS WE WILL LEARN ABOUT THE UNDERLYING IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THIS NOVEL CORONAVIRUS AND CORRELATE IMMUNE ACTIVITIES TO SERUM AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY PROTECTION, INFORMING FUTURE VACCINE-DESIGN AND EVALUATION EFFORTS. C) EVALUATE SERUM REACTIVITY TO A PANEL OF SARS-COV-2 PROTEINS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL BE VALUABLE AS POSSIBLE THERAPEUTIC AGENTS OR FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL ALSO GUIDE AND TEMPLATE THE GENERATION OF VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST COVID-19. THIS CONTRACT SUPPLEMENT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. WE WILL DEVELOP A DATABASE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO AND AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY THAT CATALOGS THE DATA GENERATED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY VARIOUS MAPPING STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. FREMONT AND COLLEAGUES AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY WILL MIRROR THIS DATA AS WELL AS PROGRESS OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY EXPERIMENTS OF THE ANTIBODY-ANTIGEN COMPLEXES. THE TEAMS OF INVESTIGATORS AND COLLABORATING LABORATORIES WILL DEPOSIT ALL VALIDATED EPITOPE DATA WITH THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE (IEDB) WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF IDENTIFICATION. THEY ALSO WILL SUBMIT ALL STRUCTURAL DATA FOR DEPOSITION IN THE RCSB PROTEIN DATABASE (PDB). ADDITIONAL RESOURCE SHARING, INCLUDING PUBLICATION UPLOADING FOR PMC FREE-ACCESS, WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY ALL INVESTIGATORS. ALL MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE GREATER RESEARCH COMMUNITY IN PUBLIC DEPOSITORIES SUCH AS BEI OR UPON REQUEST.

THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER, THROUGH THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL, WILL SUPPORT CLINICIANS IN THEIR TRANSITION FROM A FEE-FOR-SERVICE MODEL TO AN ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODEL (APM) OR THE MERIT BASED INCENTIVE PAYMENT SYSTEM (MIPS). WORKING UNDER THE DIRECTION OF ALTARUMÂ€™S QPP RESOURCE CENTER PROJECT MANAGER, NIU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOWING TASKS AND ACTIVITIES: TASK 1: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) ASSIGN QPP ADVISOR STAFF AND ENSURE THEIR AVAILABILITY FOR ONBOARDING/TRAINING SESSIONS ON PROGRAM OBJECTIVES, VIRTUAL SUPPORT SERVICES, QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL WORKFLOWS AND TOOLS, AND CMS TOOLS, AND (2) DESIGNATE STAFF MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE IN APPROPRIATE WORKGROUPS TASK 2: RESOURCE CENTER CONTENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IDENTIFY AND PROVIDE EXISTING QPP RELATED RESOURCES AND TOOLS WITHIN YOUR ORGANIZATION IN A FORMAT APPROPRIATE FOR UPLOAD TO THE WEBSITE AND USE BY CLINICIANS, AND (2) ASSIST WITH RESEARCH FOR PUBLICLY AVAILABLE TOOLS AND RESOURCES TO BE LINKED TO OR UPLOADED ONTO THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM TASK 3: OUTREACH ACTIVITIES - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) PROVIDE INFORMATION AS REQUIRED TO DOCUMENT IN THE CMS CRM THE UNILATERAL ENGAGEMENT OF CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS IN THE QPP-SURS PROGRAM, (2) IDENTIFY A STAFF PERSON TO PARTICIPATE IN THE MARKETING & OUTREACH WORKGROUP, (3) IDENTIFY NEW, AND USE EXISTING, COMMUNICATION AVENUES TO PROMOTE THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER, QPP TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND CMS/CMS QPP-SURS CENTRAL SUPPORT CONTRACTOR SPONSORED EVENTS, (4) REACH OUT TO LOCAL AND STATE CLINICIAN ORGANIZATIONS, PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, AND OTHER RELEVANT GROUPS TO HAVE THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER ADVERTISED ON THEIR WEBSITES, IN NEWSLETTERS, E-NEWSLETTERS, AND OTHER CLINICIAN COMMUNICATIONS, (5) CONTINUE UNILATERAL ENGAGEMENT (I.E. OUTREACH) UNTIL 100% OF SURS ELIGIBLE CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS HAVE BEEN UNILATERALLY ENGAGED FOR THE 2020 PROGRAM YEAR AND THIS UNILATERAL ENGAGEMENT HAS BEEN DOCUMENTED AT THE TAX IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (TIN) AND/OR INDIVIDUAL NATIONAL PHYSICIAN IDENTIFIER (NPI) LEVEL TASK 4: CLINICIAN ENGAGEMENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) PROVIDE INFORMATION IN THE CMS CRM AS REQUIRED TO DOCUMENT THE ENGAGEMENT OF ILLINOIS CLINICIANS, AS WELL AS UNREACHABLE CLINICIANS, (2) PROVIDE UPDATES ON CLINICIAN ELIGIBILITY OR ELIGIBLE CLINICIAN FILE ERRORS TO CMS BY SUBMITTING CASES VIA THE CMS CRM, (3) ASSIGN QPP ADVISORS TO ASSIST ALL ENROLLED PRACTICES IN THE STATE OF ILLINOIS THAT ARE ASSIGNED TO NIU FOR VIRTUAL TA SERVICE, (4) CONTINUE BI-LATERAL ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES UNTIL 100% OF SURS ELIGIBLE CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS HAVE BEEN BI-LATERALLY ENGAGED FOR THE PROGRAM YEAR AND THIS BILATERAL ENGAGEMENT HAS BEEN DOCUMENTED AT THE TIN AND/OR INDIVIDUAL NPI LEVEL. TASK 5: DELIVER VIRTUAL SUPPORT AND TA TASK 6: CUSTOMER SATISFACTION ASSESSMENT TASK 7: DATA CAPTURE AND REPORTING - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE A SELF-SELECTED PROGRAM/METHOD TO TRACK ALL OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT EVENTS (INCLUDING DATE, ENGAGEMENT TYPE, AND AFFILIATED NPIS/TINS). PROVIDE COUNTS BY EVENT TYPE MONTHLY AND MAINTAIN DATA IN SUPPORT OF UNREACHABLE CLINICIAN DOCUMENTATION, (2) SUPPORT COMPLETE DOCUMENTATION OF AND RECORD PRACTICE AND CLINICIAN DEMOGRAPHIC INFORMATION, (3) RECORD INFORMATION ON PARTICIPATING PRACTICESÂ€™ PARTICIPATION IN OTHER CMS MODELS AND PROGRAMS AS REQUIRED BY CMS AND WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH LOCAL MIPS/APM OUTREACH AND EDUCATION ACTIVITIES TO PREVENT DUPLICATION OF EFFORT, (4) DOCUMENT PROGRAM MILESTONES.

description: EVALUATION OF NOVEL ENGINEERED LIPID A-BASED ADJUVANTS WITH BROADLY PROTECTIVE NEURAMINIDASE ANTIGENS THIS STUDY IS FOCUSED ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW RECOMBINANT NEURAMINIDASE (NA) BASED VACCINE IN COMBINATION WITH NOVEL ADJUVANTS (BECC438 AND BECC470) IN AN INFLUENZA VIRUS VACCINE MODEL. FOR NEXT GENERATION VACCINES TO BE DEVELOPED, IT IS CRITICAL THAT HIGH QUALITY ANTIGENIC TARGETS, SUCH AS INFLUENZA VIRUS NEURAMINIDASE (NA) PROTEIN, BE USED IN COMBINATION WITH AN ADJUVANT TO INCREASE THEIR IMMUNOGENIC CAPACITIES. TO DATE, VACCINE ADJUVANTS HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED USING A TRIAL-AND-ERROR APPROACH. ADJUVANTS LICENSED FOR USE IN HUMAN VACCINES, SUCH AS ALUM (ALHYDROGEL) AND OIL-IN-WATER EMULSIONS (PHAD), CANNOT BE USED UNIVERSALLY AND HAVE DRAWBACKS INCLUDING THE REQUIREMENT FOR REPEATED APPLICATIONS AND THE INAPPROPRIATE SKEWING OF CERTAIN INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES. NEXT-GENERATION VACCINE ADJUVANTS CAN BE EFFICIENTLY MANUFACTURED USING A SIMPLE BIOSYNTHESIS MECHANISM THAT TARGETS SPECIFIC COMPONENTS OF AN IMMUNE RESPONSE. OUR PROVEN BIOSYNTHETIC METHOD, BACTERIAL ENZYMATIC COMBINATORIAL CHEMISTRY (BECC) CAN PRODUCE LIPID A MIMETICS QUICKLY AND EFFICIENTLY AND OFFERS THE ADVANTAGE OF EASE OF MANIPULATION OF IMMUNOSTIMULATORY PROPERTIES OF A FINAL ADJUVANT MOLECULE. THE IMMUNOSTIMULATORY PROPERTIES OF OVER 70 BECC MOLECULES HAVE BEEN CHARACTERIZED AND THE TOP TWO ADJUVANT CANDIDATES, BECC348 AND BECC470 WILL BE FORMULATED WITH THE INFLUENZA VIRUS NEURAMINIDASE PROTEIN, RECENTLY SHOWN TO BE PROTECTIVE IN MOUSE MODELS OF INFLUENZA VIRUS BY DR. KRAMMER. DR. FRIEMAN WILL STUDY WHETHER FORMULATION OF AN NA ANTIGEN-BASED VACCINE WITH BECC438 OR BECC470 CAN ENHANCE THE PROTECTIVE EFFECTS OF THE VACCINE IN BOTH MICE AND FERRETS.

WILSON, SUBCONTRACT PI DEPARTMENT OF MEDICINE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO CHICAGO IL 60637 E-MAIL: WILSONP@UCHICAGO.EDU Ã¢Â‚¬Æ’ STATEMENT OF WORK CORONAVIRUSES ARE ENVELOPED NON-SEGMENTED POSITIVE-SENSE RNA VIRUSES BELONGING TO THE FAMILY CORONAVIRIDAE AND CIRCULATE BROADLY AMONGST AND BETWEEN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS. OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, TWO BETACORONAVIRUSES, SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (SARS-COV) AND MIDDLE EAST RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (MERS-COV), WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVER 10,000 CASES OF INFECTION. THE MORTALITY RATE OF SARS-COV WAS 10% WITH 29 COUNTRIES AFFECTED, AND THE MORTALITY RATE OF MERS WAS 35% WITH 27 COUNTRIES AFFECTED GLOBALLY. IN DECEMBER OF 2019, A NOVEL CORONAVIRUS (2019-NCOV) WAS DISCOVERED THROUGH DEEP SEQUENCING ANALYSIS AFTER A SERIES OF PNEUMONIA CASES WERE REPORTED IN WUHAN, HUBEI, CHINA WITH UNKNOWN VIRAL ORIGIN. SEVERAL INDEPENDENT STUDIES HAVE SINCE CONFIRMED THAT THE NOVEL VIRUS ORIGINATED FROM EXPOSURES IN A WUHAN SEAFOOD MARKET. BY ONLY MARCH 16, 2020, 2019-NCOV CAUSED A PANDEMIC SPANNING MOST COUNTRIES ON EARTH WITH A REPORTED 167,000 PEOPLE INFECTED WORLDWIDE, AND ALMOST 7000 CONFIRMED DEATHS. CASE AND MORTALITY RATES ARE CONTINUING TO RISE AND THE LACK OF ADEQUATE TESTING IN MAJOR POPULATION CENTERS PLUS CLEAR EVIDENCE OF COMMUNITY TRANSMISSIONS SUGGESTS THAT THE NUMBER OF INFECTED IS LIKELY SIGNIFICANTLY GREATER. MOREOVER, AS THE VIRUS CONTINUES TO SPREAD, ITS HIGH MUTATION RATE INTRODUCES THE THREAT OF INFECTIONS WITH NEW VARIANTS WHICH COULD HAVE ALTERED SEVERITY AND TRANSMISSIBILITY. THESE OCCURRENCES NECESSITATE THE URGENCY OF NOVEL PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC MEASURES TO HELP PREVENT THE SPREAD OF NCOV-2019, WHICH POSES ONE OF THE GREATEST GLOBAL HEALTH THREATS IN MODERN HISTORY. MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MAB) ARE MONOVALENT PROTEINS EXPRESSED BY B CELLS THAT CAN SPECIFICALLY TARGET 3-DIMENSIONAL VIRAL EPITOPES, LEADING TO POTENT VIRAL NEUTRALIZATION. MABS HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED MODERN MEDICINE BY PROVIDING PRECISION MEDICINE AGAINST MANY DISEASES, WITH OVER 70 MAB-BASED DRUGS APPROVED BY THE FDA. THE ISOLATION OF HUMAN MABS SPECIFIC FOR HIGHLY IMMUNOGENIC NCOV-2019 PROTEINS CAN BE RAPIDLY USED AS THERAPEUTIC AGENTS, FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS, AND FOR TEMPLATING THE GENERATION OF VACCINES THAT CAN PROTECT AGAINST NCOV-2019. OUR LABORATORY IS HIGHLY SPECIALIZED IN THE RAPID GENERATION OF NEUTRALIZING MABS FROM HUMAN B CELLS. WE AIM TO APPLY THIS EXPERTISE TO GENERATE HUMAN NCOV-2019-SPECIFIC MABS, WHICH HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RAPIDLY ALLEVIATE THE GLOBAL HEALTH BURDEN IMPOSED BY NCOV-2019 THROUGH THREE CRITICAL MEASURES: PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC. BY INVESTIGATING THE HUMAN ANTIBODY RESPONSE TO NCOV-2019, WE WILL GAIN IMPORTANT INSIGHT INTO THE IMMUNOGENICITY AND IMMUNODOMINANCE OF NCOV-2019 VIRAL PROTEINS, WHICH WILL IN TURN INFORM WHICH VIRAL TARGETS WILL BE MOST IMPORTANT TO PURSUE WITH THERAPEUTICS AND VACCINES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROPOSED SUPPLEMENT ARE AS FOLLOWS: A) GENERATE PANELS OF HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS. COVID-19 PATIENT BLOOD WILL BE OBTAINED FROM SEVERAL SOURCES INCLUDING VERIFIED INFECTED SAMPLES FROM TOKYO THROUGH COLLABORATOR YOSHI KAWAOKA, THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO OR OTHER HOSPITALS FROM COVID-19 ADMITTED PATIENTS, OR THROUGH OTHER COLLABORATING LABS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 SPIKE PROTEIN, SPIKE RBD AND ORF7 FROM DAVED FREEMONTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, VERSIONS OF THE SPIKE PROTEIN AND RBD FROM FLORIAN KRAMMERS LABORATORY, PLUS NSP3, NSP5, NSP9, NSP10, NSP15, NSP16, AND N PROTEIN FROM ANDRJEZ JOACHIMIACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, OR TO UNBIASED OTHER EPITOPES TARGETED BY ACTIVATED B CELLS AND PLASMABLASTS WILL BE DEVELOPED BY PATRICK WILSONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE RICKETTS BIOCONTAINMENT LABORATORY ON THE ARGONNE NATIONAL LABS CAMPUS AND AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO. B) EVALUATE THE B CELL RESPONSE OF COVID-19 PATIENTS: THE WILSON LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO WILL CHARACTERIZE PERIPHERAL BLOOD B CELLS REACTIVE TO SARS-COV-2 ENCODED PROTEINS OR ACTIVATED DURING INFECTION PLUS TFH CELLS USING SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOME AND CITE-SEQ ANALYSIS ON THE 10XGENOMICS PLATFORM. FROM THIS WE WILL LEARN ABOUT THE UNDERLYING IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THIS NOVEL CORONAVIRUS AND CORRELATE IMMUNE ACTIVITIES TO SERUM AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY PROTECTION, INFORMING FUTURE VACCINE-DESIGN AND EVALUATION EFFORTS. C) EVALUATE SERUM REACTIVITY TO A PANEL OF SARS-COV-2 PROTEINS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL BE VALUABLE AS POSSIBLE THERAPEUTIC AGENTS OR FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL ALSO GUIDE AND TEMPLATE THE GENERATION OF VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST COVID-19. THIS CONTRACT SUPPLEMENT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. WE WILL DEVELOP A DATABASE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO AND AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY THAT CATALOGS THE DATA GENERATED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY VARIOUS MAPPING STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. FREMONT AND COLLEAGUES AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY WILL MIRROR THIS DATA AS WELL AS PROGRESS OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY EXPERIMENTS OF THE ANTIBODY-ANTIGEN COMPLEXES. THE TEAMS OF INVESTIGATORS AND COLLABORATING LABORATORIES WILL DEPOSIT ALL VALIDATED EPITOPE DATA WITH THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE (IEDB) WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF IDENTIFICATION. THEY ALSO WILL SUBMIT ALL STRUCTURAL DATA FOR DEPOSITION IN THE RCSB PROTEIN DATABASE (PDB). ADDITIONAL RESOURCE SHARING, INCLUDING PUBLICATION UPLOADING FOR PMC FREE-ACCESS, WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY ALL INVESTIGATORS. ALL MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE GREATER RESEARCH COMMUNITY IN PUBLIC DEPOSITORIES SUCH AS BEI OR UPON REQUEST.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES OF DTU AS PART OF IEDB & AR PROGRAM ARE TO MAINTAIN, ENHANCE AND UPDATE THE EXISTING SET OF EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS, AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS FOR THE ANALYSIS RESOURCE. DTU WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC TELECONFERENCES AND MEETINGS, AND PROVIDE TASK STATUS FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. SPECIFICALLY , DTU WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS: A. ANALYSIS RESOURCE TASKS 1. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE THE EXISTING MHC CLASS I AND II BINDING PREDICTION TOOLS.THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 2. DEVELOP NEW MHC CLASS I AND II EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF TCR BASED EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING THE TCR SEQUENCE AND STRUCTURE INFORMATION. 3. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE MHC PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 4. UPDATE EVALUATIONS OF THE MHC BINDING AND T CELL PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. 5. MAINTAIN EXISTING B CELL TOOLS DEVELOPED BY DTU. 6. DEVELOP NEW B CELL EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODY SPECIFIC EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING BCR SEQUENCE INFORMATION. 7. ESTABLISH AUTOMATED BENCHMARKING SYSTEMS FOR PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS AS WELL AS PREDICTION TOOLS NOT HOSTED IN THE IEDB. 8. PROVIDE UPDATED BENCHMARK DATASETS WITH RESPECT TO THESE TASKS, DTU WILL DEVELOP CODE IN THEIR LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND ENSURE THAT IT CAN BE EXECUTED APPROPRIATELY IN THE IEDB PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT AND WORK WITH THE LJI TEAM TO UPDATE WEB SERVERS EXECUTING THE CODE AS NECESSARY. THIS INCLUDES RETRAINING, BUG FIXES, AND FEATURE ENHANCEMENTS AS THEY OCCUR. FOR ANY NEW TOOL OR SUBSTANTIAL TOOL UPDATE DEVELOPED WITH FUNDING FROM THE IEDB BY DTU, THE PRIMARY PUBLICATION WILL INCLUDE A LINK TO THE WORKING TOOL ON THE IEDB WEBSITE. B. MEETINGS AND REPORTS 1. MEETINGS/TELECONFERENCESNIDEOCONFERENCES DTU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH LJI AT A MINIMUM OF TWICE PER MONTH, EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA TELECONFERENCE/VIDEOCONFERENCE. THE PURPOSE OF THESE MEETINGS WILL BE TO COORDINATE EFFORTS AND REPORT PROGRESS . DTU WILL ALSO BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN 1-2 US BASED PROGRAM MEETINGS PER CONTRACT YEAR FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING FEEDBACK TO NIH AND FURTHER PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. 2. QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS DTU WILL PROVIDE INPUT FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS ON A TIMELY BASIS SO THEIR CONTENT CAN BE INCORPORATED IN ADVANCE OF THE SPECIFIED DELIVERY DATE TO NIAID. 3. ADMINISTRATIVE REPORTS DTU WILL COOPERATE WITH AND PROVIDE ALL ADMINISTRATIVE REPORTING DESCRIBED IN ATTACHMENT 1, "REPRESENTATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS," ATTACHMENT 2, "GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS ," AND ATTACHMENT 6, "PRIME CONTRACT TERMS AND CONDITIONS."

description: THE DE SILVA AND HEISE LABORATORIES WILL TEST HUMAN BLOOD SAMPLES FOR THE PRESENCE OF DENGUE (DENV), ZIKA (ZIKV) AND CHIKUNGUNYA (CHIKV) SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES. ALL SAMPLES WILL BE TESTED IN DUPLICATE AT MULTIPLE DILUTIONS BY ELISA TO DETECT SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES TO DENV, ZIKV AND CHIKV. SAMPLES THAT TEST POSITIVE FOR CHIKV BY ELISA WILL BE DESIGNATED AS CHIKV IMMUNE SAMPLES. SAMPLES THAT POSITIVE FOR DENV AND/OR ZIKV BY ELISA WILL BE TESTED FOR DENV1, DENV2, DENV3, DENV4 AND ZIKV NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES. THE NEUTRALIZATION DATA WILL BE ANALYZED TO DETERMINE THE PREVIOUS DENV AND ZIKV EXPOSURE HISTORY OF EACH SUBJECT. FOR BUDGETING PURPOSES, WE ESTIMATE A FLAVIVIRUS SEROPREVALENCE OF 50% AND HAVE BUDGETED FOR TESTING HALF THE SAMPLES RECEIVED EACH YEAR FOR NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODY. THE NUMBER OF SAMPLES TO BE TESTED EACH YEAR ARE AS FOLLOWS: 1) YEAR 1: 75 SAMPLES TO BE TESTED BY ELISA FOR CHIKV, DENV AND ZIKV ANTIBODIES 38 SAMPLES TO BE TESTED FOR DENV1, 2, 3, 4 AND ZIKV NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES 2) YEAR 2: 75 SAMPLES TO BE TESTED BY ELISA FOR CHIKV, DENV AND ZIKV ANTIBODIES 38 SAMPLES TO BE TESTED FOR DENV1, 2, 3, 4 AND ZIKV NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES 3) YEAR 3 50 SAMPLES TO BE TESTED BY ELISA FOR CHIKV, DENV AND ZIKV ANTIBODIES 25 SAMPLES TO BE TESTED FOR DENV1, 2, 3, 4 AND ZIKV NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES

description: 1. PROVIDE ONSITE SUPPORT FOR THE AHRQ DATA CENTER INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT OF AND UPDATES TO POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUALS, INVENTORY CONTROL, TRAINING, TECHNICAL SUPPORT, DATA MIGRATION, ANALYSIS PROGRAM EXECUTION, AND OTHER FUNCTIONS THAT PERTAIN TO THE SUPPORT AND OPERATIONS OF THE AHRQ DATA CENTER AND SECURE LOCAL AREA NETWORK (LAN) DATA ENVIRONMENT. 2. PROVIDE CONTINUOUS ONSITE TECHNICAL SERVICES FOR MEPS DATA; PROVIDE ASSISTANCE REGARDING MEPS DATA TO AHRQ DATA CENTER USERS IN-PERSON OR REMOTELY, AS NEEDED. 3. RECEIVE AND REVIEW APPLICATIONS REGARDING ACCESSING CONFIDENTIAL DATA AND ANSWERING ANY QUESTIONS FROM PROSPECTIVE DATA CENTER USERS. 4. MONITOR AND PROVIDE ASSISTANCE TO ONSITE AND REMOTE (E.G., CENSUS RESEARCH DATA CENTERS) DATA USERS. 1. MONITOR ONSITE USERS TO ENSURE APPROPRIATE ONSITE BEHAVIOR AND USE OF DATA CENTER RESOURCES. 2. ENSURE REMOTE USERS ARE ACTIVELY WORKING ON PROJECTS. REGULARLY CHECK IN WITH INACTIVE USERS TO SEE IF THEY STILL REQUIRE AN ACTIVE ACCOUNT SEAT ON AHRQ AWS. 5. SERVE AS THE GATEKEEPER FOR CONFIDENTIAL DATA MAINTAINED ONSITE IN THE AHRQ DATA CENTER. 6. MONITOR PC AND LAN USE AND STORAGE AND COORDINATE EQUIPMENT UPGRADES AND LICENSE RENEWALS WITH AHRQ SECURE LAN ADMINISTRATOR. 7. INSTALL MEPS AND SECONDARY DATA FIELDS, EXECUTE AND LOG DATA TRANSFERS TO AND FROM AHRQ NETWORK TO OTHER CONTRACTORS AND USERS. 8. COORDINATE WITH IMPAQ STAFF TO INCREASE EFFICIENCY AND TRANSPARENCY OF AHRQ DATA CENTER OPERATIONS (E.G., AUTOMATE APPLICATIONS). 9. SUPPORT NEW ONSITE TASKS AS AGREED UPON WITH AHRQ, IMPAQ AND AQUAS. 10. REVIEW OUTPUT FROM DATA CENTER USERS TO COMPLY WITH CONFIDENTIALITY GUIDELINES. 11. FACILITATE PROCESSING OF EXTERNAL MIPS RESEARCH APPLICATIONS; INFORM APPLICANTS OF THE PROCESS, SHARE APPLICATIONS WITH APPLICABLE AHRQ STAFF. 12. MAINTAIN INVENTORIES FOR DATA CENTER USAGE, INCLUDING APPLICATIONS FOR ACCESSING CONFIDENTIAL DATA, DATA RECEIPT, AND FILE TRANSFERS. PRODUCE AD HOC USAGE AND OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE REPORTS AS NEEDED. 13. BACKUP ONSITE SUPPORT STAFF PERFORMING SIMILAR DUTIES FOR HCUP. 14. AS NEEDED, PROVIDE HCUP DATA LIBRARIAN AND ANALYTIC SERVICES TO ONSITE AND REMOTE AHRQ STAFF. 15. AS NEEDED, PROVIDE ONSITE FILE AND DATA TRANSFER SERVICES, MONITOR AND SERVE AS GATEKEEPER FOR HCUP DATA ACCESS ACCOUNTS AND CONFIDENTIAL DATA MAINTAINED IN THE SECURE LAN, MAINTAIN A LOG OF DATA FILES, AND ENSURE ARRANGEMENTS MADE WITH THIRD PARTIES TO ACCESS DATASETS OR ANALYTIC FILES ARE ACCOMPLISHED IN ACCORDANCE WITH AHRQ DATA USE GUIDELINES. 16. PROVIDE MONTHLY REPORT OF DATA CENTER ACTIVITIES

description: IN THE FIRST EXPERIMENT, 10 INITIALLY SELECTED CANDIDATES WILL BE TESTED IN VACCINATION WITH FLU AND DENGUE ANTIGENS IN CONJUNCTION. MICE WILL BE PRIME VACCINATED WITH TEST OR CONTROL ARTICLE VIA INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION ON DAY 0 AND BOOSTED ON DAY 21. MICE WILL BE CHALLENGED WITH A LETHAL DOSE OF VIRUS BY THE INTRANASAL ROUTE ON DAY 42. THE GOAL OF THIS INITIAL PILOT WILL BE TO DETERMINE IF THE IN VITRO AND IN VIVO MECHANISTIC EFFECTS OBSERVED TRANSLATE TO VACCINATION. THE TOTAL COST OF EXPERIMENT ONE IS $141,932 IN THE SECOND EXPERIMENT, MICE WILL BE VACCINATED INTRAMUSCULARLY (IM) WITH THE TARGET ANTIGEN IN COMBINATION WITH THE TOP 3 IMMUNO-MODULATOR COMBINATIONS (E.G. HA + PRR-AGONIST + HONOKIOL) SELECTED AND VALIDATED PREVIOUSLY. INFLUENZA HA WILL BE USED AS A VACCINE UNLESS THE ANTIGEN PROVES TO BE POORLY IMMUNOGENIC. THE CONTROL ANIMALS WILL BE IMMUNIZED WITH THE HA+ IMMUNE-POTENTIATOR WITHOUT A PRR-L (HA + I-M), OR A COMBINATION OF HA AND PRR-L (HA + CPG) AT THE SAME RATIOS OF THE ANTIGEN AND ADJUVANTS AS IN THE HA+ CPG + I-POTENTIATOR VACCINE. ADDAVAX-FORMULATED HA WILL BE USED AS A VACCINE STANDARD FOR OUR PLATFORM. MICE WILL BE IMMUNIZED ON DAY 0 (PRIME) AND WEEK 3 (BOOST). AT WEEKS 1, 2, AND 3 POST PRIME, AND 1, 2, 3 WEEKS AFTER BOOST (W4, 5, 6) WE WILL EVALUATE THE KINETICS OF TOTAL IGG, IGG1, IGG2A AND IGM IN SERUM BY AN HA-SPECIFIC ELISA TO DETERMINE THE MAGNITUDE OF AB RESPONSE AND DEFINE TH1/TH2 POLARIZATION OF THE RESPONSE USING RATIOS OF IGG2A TO IGG1. THE NEUTRALIZING CAPACITY OF THE AB WILL BE TESTED BY THE HI ASSAY AT WEEK 3 AND 6. THE TOTAL COST OF EXPERIMENT TWO IS $122,919

description: - BASED ON THE CONCEPT SELECTED BY CLIENT IN PHASE 1, CONTINUE DEVELOPMENT WITH ANTICIPATED SCOPE AS FOLLOWS. - HOLD WEEKLY CONFERENCE CALL WITH CLIENT TO DISCUSS PROJECT PROGRESS, CHALLENGES AND PLANNING (TYPICALLY CONTINUES THROUGHOUT DEVELOPMENT). - INDIVIDUALLY PROTOTYPE CRITICAL FUNCTIONS. SYMBIENT DEFINES CRITICAL FUNCTIONS AS THOSE CONCEPT FEATURES WHICH ENTAIL TECHNICAL RISK AND ARE ANTICIPATED TO REQUIRE ITERATION IN ORDER TO MEET PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS. FOR THE PURPOSES OF THIS ESTIMATE IT IS ASSUMED THAT THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL FUNCTIONS WILL REQUIRE DEVELOPMENT: - FABRICATE 2 LOW COMPLEXITY PROTOTYPE MOLDS FOR THE SLIDING VALVE AND ROTARY VALVE (EACH INCLUDING A SUBSTRATE AND OVERMOLD), ASSUMES ALL FOUR CAVITIES FIT ON ONE MOLD BASE. - DESIGN AND FABRICATE RAPID PROTOTYPES FOR EACH CRITICAL FUNCTION. - TEST RAPID PROTOTYPES AGAINST DEFINED PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS. AT CLIENT REQUEST, SEND PROTOTYPES TO CLIENT FOR ADDITIONAL TESTING. - ITERATE AND FABRICATE RAPID PROTOTYPES FOR EACH CRITICAL FUNCTION UNTIL RESULTS INDICATE THAT PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS ARE MET. ESTIMATED COSTS AND DURATION ASSUMES THAT UP TO TWO ITERATIONS WILL BE SUFFICIENT (UP TO THREE SETS OF PROTOTYPES TOTAL PER CRITICAL FUNCTION). - FABRICATE AN INTEGRATED RAPID PROTOTYPE. THE INTEGRATED PROTOTYPE IS A FUNCTIONAL PROTOTYPE THAT WILL BE TESTED AGAINST ALL PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS. TYPICAL TESTING PERFORMED IS FOR MECHANICAL FUNCTION (INCLUDING LIQUID HANDLING). SEND PROTOTYPE TO CLIENT FOR ADDITIONAL TESTING. - ITERATE AND FABRICATE INTEGRATED RAPID PROTOTYPES UNTIL RESULTS INDICATE THAT ALL PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS ARE MET, SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATIONS OF THE PROTOTYPING METHODS. ESTIMATED COSTS AND DURATION ASSUMES THAT UP TO TWO ITERATIONS WILL BE SUFFICIENT (UP TO THREE SETS OF PROTOTYPES TOTAL PER CRITICAL FUNCTION). - ESTIMATE BUDGET AND SCHEDULE FOR PHASE 3: PROTOTYPE MOLDS, MOLDING, AND ASSEMBLY METHODS.
