description: THE UCI VACCINE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT TEAM WILL PROVIDE VACCINE FORMULATIONS IN EMULSIONS FOR TESTING OF IMMUNE MODULATORS OF T-CELL ACTIVITY, EPITOPE/ANTIGEN DIVERSITY, AND IMMUNOLOGICAL OUTPUTS UPON VACCINATION. RESEARCHERS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, IRVINE HAVE EXPERTISE IN SCREENING, VACCINE FORMULATIONS, AND NOVEL ADJUVANT DEVELOPMENT AND THEY HAVE PREVIOUSLY WORKED CLOSELY WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO TO DEVELOP ADJUVANTS FOR Q-FEVER VACCINES. AFTER THE INITIAL SCREEN HAS BEEN COMPLETED, WE WILL FOCUS ON 10 COMPOUNDS WITH THE MOST DISTINCTIVE PROFILE OF ANTIGEN PRESENTATION TO INFLAMMATION PRODUCTION. THE GOAL WILL BE TO DETERMINE THE BIOCHEMICAL AND CELLULAR MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH THESE COMPOUNDS ACT TO INFLUENCE ANTIBODY SELECTION AND MATURATION. WE WILL TEST 3 HYPOTHESES ABOUT HOW THE IMMUNE POTENTIATORS ARE OPERATING. FIRST, THAT THEY ARE ACTING, AS IN CULTURE, TO DIRECTLY REDUCE INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES AND IMPROVE ANTIGEN PRESENTATION. SECOND, THAT THE INCREASED ANTIBODY RESPONSES ARE DUE TO SECONDARY PROCESSES OCCURRING FROM THE REDUCED INFLAMMATION. THIRD, THAT THE IN VIVO EFFECTS RESULT NOT FROM THE ANTIGEN PRESENTING CELLS DIRECTLY, BUT THAT SUPPRESSION OF INFLAMMATION IN THE INJECTION SITE RESULTS IN THE IMPROVED ANTIGEN PRESENTATION SEEN IN IN VIVO EXPERIMENTS. THE GOAL WILL BE TO IDENTIFY KEY IMMUNE CELLS AND A BIOCHEMICAL/IMMUNOLOGICAL MECHANISM TARGETED BY ADJUVANTS, AND NARROW CANDIDATE SELECTION. THE NFKB INHIBITORS UNDERSTUDY IN THIS PROJECT ARE PREDICTED TO STRONGLY ALTER THE ANTIBODY RESPONSE AND SHIFT THE RESPONSE FROM IGG2C TO IGG1 ANTIBODIES AS WELL AS CHANGE THE EPITOPE SELECTION. TO DETERMINE ANTIBODY SPECIFICITY AND MECHANISM WE WILL VACCINATE WITH GP120, FLU H1N1, AND DENV. WE CAN EXAMINE BOTH THE ANTIBODY RESPONSE IN TERMS OF SUBTYPE AND THE EPITOPE SPECIFICITY. WE WILL PLAN TO MAP THE EPITOPES SPECIFICITY FOR 5 OPTIMIZED CANDIDATES WITH VACCINATION IN MICE AS OUR MODEL SYSTEM. WE WILL ALSO CHARACTERIZE THE SHIFT IN ANTIBODY SUBTYPE FOR EACH OF THESE EXPERIMENTS ACROSS ANTIGENS TO DETERMINE IF WHAT WE HAVE OBSERVED IS A GENERAL PHENOMENON OR SPECIFIC TO OVA. OUR LABORATORY HAS DEVELOPED PROTEIN MICROARRAY TECHNOLOGY THAT WE HAVE USES EXTENSIVELY FOR Q FEVER, INFLUENZA AND DENGUE VIRUS PROJECTS WHICH WILL BE APPLIED HERE. WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW CHANGING IN VIVO VACCINE YIELDS NOVEL EPITOPE TARGETS AGAINST HIV, FLU AND DENGUE. WE WILL USE A HA PROTEIN/PEPTIDE MICROARRAY TO DETERMINE THE BREADTH OF THE AB RESPONSE. THIS WILL EVALUATE QUANTITY OF AB-BINDING SEQUENCES IN THE HA PROTEIN FOR ALL EXPERIMENTAL CATEGORIES. WE WILL ESTABLISH B CELL ACTIVATION SPECIFIC FOR HA. WE WILL TEST THE TOTAL AND HA-SPECIFIC IGG-SECRETING ASC PLASMABLASTS/PLASMA CELLS IN BLOOD, DRAINING LN (DLN), SPLEEN AND BONE MARROW (BM) BY B CELL ELISPOT. THE PHENOTYPE OF DLN- AND SPLEENRESIDENT GERMINAL CENTER B CELLS (GCB) AND CIRCULATING PLASMABLASTS/PLASMA CELLS WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY FLOW CYTOMETRY USING MARKERS SPECIFIC FOR PLASMABLASTS/PLASMA CELLS AND GCB. description: TITLE: EVALUATING HOSPITAL-ONSET BACTEREMIA (HOB) AND FUNGEMIA AS PREVENTABLE HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS 1. BACKGROUND AND NEED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (BSIS) ARE A SERIOUS AND LIFE THREATENING INFECTION. FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRACKING HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS (HAIS), MOST ATTENTION HAS BEEN PAID TO CENTRAL-LINE ASSOCIATED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (CLABSIS). PREVENTION OF CLABSIS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE FEASIBLE VIA WELL-STUDIED BUNDLES OF CARE RELATED TO CATHETER INSERTION AND MAINTENANCE. HOWEVER, TRACKING CLABSIS IS DIFFICULT, TIME CONSUMING AND HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE SUBJECTIVE WITH SUBSTANTIAL INTERRATER VARIABILITY. RESEARCHERS IN THE UNITED STATES HAVE BEGUN TO EVALUATE THE UTILITY OF TRACKING HOSPITAL-ONSET BACTEREMIA AND FUNGEMIA (HOB) AS A RELEVANT HAI OUTCOME IN LIEU OF CLABSI. HOB COMPRISES ALL POSITIVE BLOOD CULTURES TAKEN AT LEAST 48 HOURS POST ADMISSION TO THE HOSPITAL. THUS, IT INCLUDES CLABSIS AND NON-CENTRAL LINE ASSOCIATED BSIS THAT PRESUMABLY OCCURRED WITHIN THE HOSPITAL INITIAL HOB STUDIES IN THE UNITED STATES HAVE SHOWN THAT CLABSIS COMPRISE LESS THAN 20% OF TOTAL HOBS LEADING TO QUESTIONS OF WHETHER THESE NON-CLABSI HOBS REPRESENT PREVENTABLE INFECTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT HOB MAY ALSO BE A REASONABLE PROXY FOR CLABSI RATES. SEVERAL STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT HOB RATES TRACKED WELL WITH CLABSI RATES WHEN BOTH WERE MEASURED SIMULTANEOUSLY AND IN ONE STUDY HOB RATES TRENDED DOWNWARDS PROPORTIONALLY WITH CLABSI RATE DECREASES AFTER A CLABSI INTERVENTION WAS IMPLEMENTED. THESE DATA SUGGEST THAT A HEALTHCARE FACILITY MAY BE ABLE TO EXPEND LESS RESOURCES FOLLOWING HOB AND STILL DETECT CLABSI DECREASES WHEN IMPLEMENTING TARGETED PREVENTION BUNDLES. ONGOING WORK TO DETERMINE THE ETIOLOGY AND PREVENTABILITY OF HOB IS UNDERWAY AS WELL; PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGESTS THAT POTENTIALLY HALF OF HOB EVENTS MIGHT BE AVOIDABLE WITH KNOWN INTERVENTIONS. IN LOW AND MIDDLE-INCOME (LMIC) COUNTRIES WHERE BOTH HUMAN AND MONETARY RESOURCES ARE LIMITED AND EPIDEMIOLOGY OF HAI INFECTIONS HAVE BEEN STUDIED LESS ROBUSTLY, USING HOB AS A HAI METRIC HAS SEVERAL POTENTIAL ADVANTAGES. IT CAN OFTEN BE COLLECTED FROM MICROBIOLOGY DATA ALONE, RATHER THAN REQUIRING A LARGE REVIEW OF A PATIENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CHART OR MEDICAL RECORDS. ADDITIONALLY, IT IS OBJECTIVE AND LIKELY REQUIRES LESS INTENSIVE TRAINING FOR STAFF THAN CLABSI SURVEILLANCE. FINALLY, IN LMICS WHERE PROMPT TREATMENT AND PREVENTION OF SEPSIS IS OFTEN INADEQUATE, THERE ARE LIKELY A POOL OF NON-CLABSI HOB THAT ARE PREVENTABLE WITH SIMPLE, KNOWN INTERVENTIONS. CURRENTLY, ALL STUDIES ON HOB HAVE BEEN IN HIGH-INCOME COUNTRIES. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO DETERMINE WHETHER HOB IS A FEASIBLE, USEFUL, AND ACCEPTABLE METRIC FOR HAI SURVEILLANCE IN HOSPITALS IN LMIC. 2. SCOPE OF WORK THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO EVALUATE HOB IN HOSPITALS IN LMICS AS A FEASIBLE, USEFUL AND ACCEPTABLE METRIC FOR HAI SURVEILLANCE. THE SPECIFIC GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO: X SET UP HOB SURVEILLANCE IN ONE OR MORE SITES WITHIN A LOW OR MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRY (ACCORDING TO WORLD BANK CLASSIFICATIONS) AND DESCRIBE THE FOLLOWING: O THE ETIOLOGIES AND SYNDROMES ASSOCIATED WITH HOB O THE EPIDEMIOLOGY OF HOB IN TERMS OF PERSON, PLACE AND TIME X DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK FOR DETERMINING WHICH HOB EVENTS ARE LIKELY TO BE PREVENTABLE WITH INFECTION CONTROL MEASURES AND QUALITY HOSPITAL CARE AND COLLECT CLINICAL DATA TO DETERMINE THE PROPORTION OF HOB EVENTS OBSERVED THAT MEET THE CRITERIA OUTLINED IN THE FRAMEWORK. THIS SHOULD BE DONE VIA PROSPECTIVE DATA COLLECTION THAT CAPTURES RELEVANT CLINICAL DATA AND SHALL NOT RELY SOLELY ON DATA FROM MEDICAL CHARTS WHICH LIKELY WILL NOT HAVE SUFFICIENT DETAIL TO MAKE DETERMINATIONS. X EVALUATE THE COST, FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF IMPLEMENTING AN HOB SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM IN 200-2016-91804 75D30119F00003 PAGE 5 OF 28 LMIC. THIS WILL INCLUDE COLLECTION OF QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE DATA ON ACCEPTABILITY OF THE SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM FROM STAFF AND HOSPITAL ADMINISTRATION AS WELL AS COLLECTION OF DIRECT AND INDIRECT COSTS OF IMPLEMENTING THE SURVEILLANCE OUTSIDE A RESEARCH STUDY. X DETERMINE WHAT DATA MIGHT BE NEEDED TO BE INCLUDED IN AN HOB SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM TO ADEQUATELY TARGET PREVENTION EFFORTS. 3. TASKS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ALL LABOR, EXPERTISE, MATERIALS, AND SUPPLIES AND PERFORM ALL SERVICES REQUIRED TO CARRY OUT THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT. TASK 1: START UP MEETING X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ARRANGE AND CONDUCT AN INITIAL MEETING (BY TELECONFERENCE) WITH THE COR AND OTHER RELEVANT STAFF WITHIN 2 WEEKS OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE TASK ORDER. THE PURPOSE OF THE MEETING WILL BE TO REVIEW AND CLARIFY THE SCOPE OF WORK AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE FOR TASKS, TO DELINEATE ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES, AND TO ESTABLISH COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS. EACH TASK AND DELIVERABLE WILL BE REVIEWED. X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT AN AGENDA FOR THE ABOVE MEETING WITHIN 1 WEEK OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE TASK ORDER. TASK 2: MAINTAIN COMMUNICATION WITH THE SCIENCE OFFICER X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH THE COR FOR ALL PROJECT RELATED COMMUNICATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL MAINTAIN REGULAR COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE SCIENCE OFFICER AND COR INVOLVED WITH THE PROJECT. THE CHIEF MEANS OF COMMUNICATION WILL BE VIA CONFERENCE CALLS THAT WILL BE SCHEDULED EVERY MONTH THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT PERIOD AND ONE IN-PERSON MEETING. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE AN AGENDA AND MEETING MINUTES FOR EACH CALL. ALL CONFERENCE CALLS SHALL BE SCHEDULED AND ADMINISTERED BY THE CONTRACTOR. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL RESPOND TO ALL EMAILS AND TELEPHONE COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE SCIENCE OFFICER WITHIN 2-3 WORKING DAYS. X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH THE COR FOR AN IN-PERSON MEETING ASSOCIATED WITH TASK 5 & 6 (FRAMEWORK AND PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT MEETING) WHERE THEY WILL MEET WITH THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER AND OTHER RELEVANT CDC STAFF. THE IN-PERSON MEETING MAY BE AT THE CONTRACTORÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SITE OR AT CDCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ATLANTA, GA LOCATION. TASK 3: QUARTERLY PROGRESS REPORTS X ON THE 10TH DAY FOLLOWING THE 3 MONTHS BEING REPORTED, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE AND SUBMIT A QUARTERLY PROGRESS REPORT CONTAINING THE CURRENT STATUS OF WORK AND PROJECT SPENDING. THE REPORT SHALL CONTAIN, AT A MINIMUM, THE CURRENT PROGRESS ON EACH OF THE REQUIREMENTS SET FORTH BELOW, THE FINANCIAL STATUS OF THE PROJECT, PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED DURING THE MONTH, SOLUTIONS IMPLEMENTED, PLANNED ACTIVITY FOR THE UPCOMING MONTH AND ANY OTHER INFORMATION MUTUALLY AGREED UPON BETWEEN THE CONTRACTOR AND THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER. TASK 4: FINALIZE WORK PLAN AND TIMELINE X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL FINALIZE THE DETAILED PLAN AND TIMELINE, SUBMITTED IN THEIR PROPOSAL, FOR DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A STUDY EVALUATING THE USE OF HOB AS AN HAI METRIC THAT ADDRESSES THE SPECIFIC AIMS OUTLINED ABOVE IN THE STATEMENT OF WORK. THE WORK PLAN SHALL SPECIFY THE APPROACH TO DEVELOPING A STUDY PROTOCOL AND IMPLEMENTING ACTIVITIES OUTLINED IN THE PROTOCOL. A FINALIZED TIMELINE FOR THE COMPLETION OF THESE TASKS INCLUDING THE IDENTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL FACTORS THAT MAY HASTEN OR IMPEDE THE ACCOMPLISHMENT OF STATED OBJECTIVES WILL BE PRESENTED TO THE COR AND SCIENCE OFFICER FOR APPROVAL. TASK 5: DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK AND GUIDE FOR DETERMINING HOB PREVENTABILITY X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK AND SET OF CRITERIA TO DETERMINE THE PREVENTABILITY OF HOB EVENTS IN THIS STUDY AS WELL AS THE DATA THAT NEEDS TO BE COLLECTED TO PROVIDE A PREVENTABLE/NOT PREVENTABLE DETERMINATION FOR EACH HOB EVENT. THE FINAL FRAMEWORK AND CRITERIA SHOULD BE APPROVED BY THE CDC PROJECT OFFICER PRIOR TO USE. 200-2016-91804 75D30119F00003 PAGE 6 OF 28 X THIS FRAMEWORK SHALL BE DEVELOPED USING INPUT FROM AN EXPERT PANEL OF PHYSICIANS WITH BACKGROUNDS IN CRITICAL CARE, INFECTIOUS DISEASE, AND HOSPITAL EPIDEMIOLOGY. USING DELPHI METHODOLOGY, THE EXPERT PANEL SHALL BE CONVENED TO DEVELOP AND DEFINE THE FRAMEWORK AND GUIDE. THE GUIDING QUESTION FOR PREVENTABILITY SHALL BE Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒWAS THIS BACTEREMIA OR FUNGEMIA PREVENTABLE IN AN IDEAL HOSPITAL SETTING, PRACTICING PERFECT CLINICAL CARE AND INFECTION PREVENTION (EVEN IF THAT DOESNÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢TEXIST)Ã¢Â‚¬Â„¢. X THE GOAL OF THE FRAMEWORK IS TO THEN DEVELOP A GUIDE TO OPERATIONALIZE THE FRAMEWORK WITHIN THE SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM AND DETERMINE THE DATA THAT NEEDS TO BE COLLECTED FOR HOB EVENTS TO MAKE THE DETERMINATION. X THE GUIDE AND FRAMEWORK SHALL ALSO INCLUDE CONTINGENCY PLANS FOR HOW TO DEAL WITH DIFFICULT CASES OR CASES WHERE THE DETERMINATION CANNOT BE MADE WITH THE EXISTING FRAMEWORK (E.G., REFERRAL TO A TWOPERSON EVALUATION TEAM TO MAKE A DETERMINATION). X AN IN-PERSON MEETING OF THE CONTRACTOR, SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS AND CDC REPRESENTATIVES TO DEVELOP AND APPROVE THE DRAFT FRAMEWORK SHALL BE PLANNED AS OUTLINED IN TASK 2. DUE TO PRA LIMITATIONS, THE EXPERT PANEL SHOULD INCLUDE NOT MORE THAN 9 EXTERNAL EXPERTS. TASK 6: DEVELOP A PROTOCOL X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE PROJECT OFFICER ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOCOL THAT SPECIFICALLY LAYS OUT THE STUDY QUESTION, METHODOLOGY, DATA SOURCES, LABORATORY METHODS, STUDY POPULATION, ANALYTIC STRATEGY AND RELATED TASKS. X IN ORDER TO IMPROVE GENERALIZABILITY IT WOULD BE FAVORED FOR THE PROTOCOL TO INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION AT SEVERAL SITES, THOUGH THE AREAS OF DATA COLLECTION COULD BE SUBSETS OF THE LARGER HOSPITAL POPULATION (E.G., WITHIN THE ICUS OF SEVERAL HOSPITALS). X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP A PROTOCOL THAT OUTLINES THE FOLLOWING: O HOW HOB RATE DATA WILL BE COLLECTED AND COMPARED AT THE GIVEN FACILITY/FACILITIES OR WARD/WARDS. O HOW THE DATA REQUIRED TO DETERMINE THE PREVENTABILITY OF HOB INFECTIONS (AS DEFINED IN TASK 5) WILL BE COLLECTED, HOW DIFFICULT DETERMINATIONS WILL BE ADJUDICATED, AND WHEN DETERMINATIONS WILL BE MADE. THIS DATA WILL NEED TO BE COLLECTED PROSPECTIVELY AND SHALL MAKE USE OF ALL AVAILABLE DATA INCLUDING MEDICAL CHART DATA (THOUGH SHALL NOT SOLELY RELY ON THIS), INTERVIEWS WITH CLINICAL STAFF, REVIEW OF LABORATORY DATA AND OTHER RELEVANT MEDICAL INFORMATION. O HOW FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF HOB SURVEILLANCE WILL BE ASSESSED, INCLUDING POTENTIALLY QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE DATA AS APPROPRIATE. O HOW COSTS OF HOB SURVEILLANCE WILL BE CAPTURED X IN ADDITION THE PROTOCOL SHALL INCLUDE: O DEFINITIONS TO BE USED FOR HOB NUMERATORS O DENOMINATOR TO BE USED TO CALCULATE RATES O SAMPLE SIZE, POWER CALCULATIONS AS APPROPRIATE AND NEEDED TASK 7: OBTAIN INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB) AND OTHER SCIENCE OR ADMINISTRATIVE APPROVALS X THE CONTRACTOR WILL PREPARE AND SUBMIT THE RESEARCH PROTOCOL TO ALL RELEVANT AND NEEDED IRB BODIES AS WELL AS ANY ADDITIONAL SCIENTIFIC OR ADMINISTRATIVE APPROVALS THAT MAY EXIST IN COUNTRY. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF PACKAGE DEVELOPMENT AND SUBMISSION AS REQUIRED PRIOR TO COLLECTION OF ANY DATA. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE THE PACKAGES INCLUDING ALL FORMS AND ATTACHMENTS FOR CDC SCIENCE OFFICER APPROVAL AS NEEDED. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT THE IRB PACKAGE TO THE RELEVANT IRB(S) AND SHALL ENSURE THAT CLINICAL SITES INVOLVED IN THE STUDY APPLY FOR AND RECEIVE IRB APPROVAL. COPIES OF IRB APPROVALS FROM THE CONTRACTOR AND ALL CLINICAL SITES SHALL BE PROVIDED TO THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER. TASK 8: COLLECT DATA X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HAVE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR COLLECTING AND MANAGING RELEVANT MICROBIOLOGY, CLINICAL AND OTHER DATA TO FULFILL THE OBJECTIVES OF THE STUDY. THE DATA COLLECTED SHALL INCLUDE, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO, THE FOLLOWING: O NUMBER OF HOB EVENTS AND MICROBIOLOGIC DESCRIPTION INCLUDING RESISTANCE DATA IF AVAILABLE O CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGIC DATA AS WELL AS ANY OTHER DATA Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ DETERMINED VIA TASKS 5 AND 6 - TO DETERMINE PREVENTABILITY OF INFECTIONS 200-2016-91804 75D30119F00003 PAGE 7 OF 28 O APPROPRIATE DENOMINATOR DATA (E.G. PATIENT-DAYS) O QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY DATA O COST DATA ON IMPLEMENTATION X FACILITY-WIDE DATA ON IPC PRACTICES, KNOWLEDGE GAPS OR OTHER METRICS MAY NEED TO BE COLLECTED IF RELEVANT TO THE STUDY. X DATA COLLECTION SHALL BEGIN ON OR BEFORE THE DUE DATE AS NOTED IN THE DELIVERABLE SCHEDULE AND CONTINUE FOR A MINIMUM OF 6 MONTHS. DATA COLLECTED SHALL BE PRESENTED IN AGGREGATE DURING TWO QUARTERLY REPORTS ALONG WITH DESCRIPTION OF CHALLENGES AND PROPOSED SOLUTIONS TO ANY DATA COLLECTION ISSUES. ANY DATA COLLECTION ISSUES SHALL BE REPORTED IN A TIMELY MANNER, BY PHONE OR EMAIL, NO LATER THAN 2 WEEKS AFTER ONSET. X PILOTING OF DATA COLLECTION SHALL BE CARRIED OUT TO VALIDATE DATA ELEMENTS, QUESTIONS, COLLECTION LOGISTICS AND MAKE ADJUSTMENTS AS NEEDED TO ENSURE HIGH QUALITY DATA COLLECTION DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. TASK 9: DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYSIS X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COLLECT, MANAGE, ANALYZE AND SECURELY STORE ALL RELEVANT DATA AND SHALL DESIGN AND MAINTAIN A DATA MANAGEMENT STRUCTURE AND PROCEDURES THAT WILL ENSURE CONSISTENT DATA COLLECTION FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT. X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REVISE THEIR PROPOSED DATA ANALYTIC PLAN IN LINE WITH THE DEVELOPED PROTOCOL. THE DATA ANALYTIC PLAN SHALL DESCRIBE THE DATA ELEMENTS, DATA ARCHITECTURE, AND DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PLANNED ANALYSES. THIS DATA ANALYTIC PLAN SHALL BE SUBMITTED TO AND APPROVED BY THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER BEFORE DATA ANALYSES CAN PROCEED. THE PLAN SHALL OUTLINE HOW THE FOLLOWING OUTCOMES WILL BE OUTPUT FROM THE PROPOSED ANALYSIS: O DESCRIPTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGY OF HOB EVENTS O PROPORTION OF PREVENTABLE EVENTS O MEASURES OF FEASIBILITY AND COST X ONCE DATA ANALYSIS HAS BEGUN, UPDATES ON DATA ANALYTICS SHALL BE INCLUDED IN QUARTERLY REPORTS GIVEN TO COR AND CDC SCIENCE OFFICER. POTENTIAL DATA ANALYSIS ISSUES SHALL BE REPORTED, BY PHONE OR BY EMAIL, IN A TIMELY MANNER, NO LATER THAN 2 WEEKS AFTER ONSET. X RESULTS OF THE FINAL DATA ANALYSIS SHALL BE INCLUDED IN THE DRAFT FINAL REPORT AND SHALL BE REVIEWED AND APPROVED BY THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER PRIOR TO INCLUSION IN THE FINAL REPORT. TASK 10: FINAL REPORT X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PRESENT A DRAFT FINAL REPORT OF THE PROJECT OUTCOMES TO THE COR FOR REVIEW. THE REPORT SHALL INCLUDE, IN ADDITION TO FINAL ANALYSES ON HOB EPIDEMIOLOGY, PREVENTABLE EVENTS AND COST/FEASIBILITY DATA, SUGGESTIONS FOR ANY HOB PREVENTION EFFORTS THAT MIGHT BE EFFECTIVE BASED ON DATA COLLECTED. AFTER RECEIVING COMMENTS AND RECOMMENDATIONS ON THE DRAFT FINAL REPORT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT THE FINAL REPORT, INCORPORATING CDCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S COMMENTS AND RECOMMENDATIONS WITHIN 1 MONTH OF RECEIVING CDC FEEDBACK. BOTH REPORTS SHALL INCLUDE WITH IT ALL MATERIALS THAT WERE DEVELOPED AND TRANSMITTED TO CDC ELECTRONICALLY. X WRITING MANUSCRIPTS FOR PUBLICATION WILL BE THE SHARED RESPONSIBILITY OF CDC TEAM AND CONTRACTOR, AND AUTHORSHIP WILL BE GRANTED BASED ON SCIENTIFIC CONTRIBUTION IN ACCORDANCE WITH CDC AUTHORSHIP POLICY (HTTP://WWW.CDC.GOV/MASO/POLICY/AUTHORSHIP.PDF). description: HOSPITAL ACQUIRED INFECTIONS (HAIS) ARE SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO PATIENTSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ SAFETY WORLDWIDE. LOW AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRIES (LMICS) HAVE HIGHER PREVALENCE OF HAIS AND SURGICAL SITE INFECTIONS (SSIS) WHEN COMPARED TO THE UNITED STATES (US) AND EUROPE. THE OVERALL OCCURRENCE OF HAIS IN ADULTS IN INTENSIVE CARE UNITS (ICUS) IS AT LEAST 3 TIMES HIGHER IN LMICS VERSUS THE UNITED STATES. ALTHOUGH COUNTRY-WIDE HAI RATES ARE NOT AVAILABLE FOR INDIA, A RECENT STUDY OF ICUS IN 40 INDIAN HOSPITALS REPORTED HAI RATES TO BE SUBSTANTIALLY HIGHER THAN THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION'S NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY NETWORK (CDC-NHSN) MEDIAN RATES, DESPITE INDIAN ICUS HAVING LOWER UTILIZATION OF DEVICES. CENTRAL LINE ASSOCIATED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (CLABSI) RATES IN INDIAN ICUS WERE AT LEAST 5 TIMES HIGHER THAN RATES IN US ICUS. HOWEVER, RECENT US STUDIES FOUND THAT CLABSIS COMPRISE LESS THAN 20% OF TOTAL HOSPITAL ONSET BACTEREMIA AND FUNGEMIA (HOB). IMPORTANTLY, TWO-THIRDS OF THE HOB EVENTS WERE JUDGED TO BE PREVENTABLE. SUB-OPTIMAL INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES IN INDIA, AS EVIDENCED BY HIGH CLABSI AND OTHER HAI RATES, INDICATE THAT NON-CLABSI HOB EVENTS MAY ACCOUNT FOR SIGNIFICANT PROPORTION OF POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE INFECTIONS IN INDIAN HOSPITALS. THESE DATA SUGGEST THAT EVALUATING THE LARGER GROUP OF HOB EVENTS MAY ALLOW US TO EXPAND THE TARGETS FOR HAI DETECTION, AND MORE APPROPRIATELY DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO REDUCE ADDITIONAL SIGNIFICANT HAI EVENTS NOT BEING CURRENTLY ADDRESSED IN A SYSTEMATIC MANNER IN RESOURCE LIMITED SETTINGS. IN THIS STUDY WE WILL IDENTIFY AND VALIDATE NEW STRATEGIES FOR HAI PREVENTION IN RESOURCE LIMITED SETTINGS SUCH AS INDIAN HOSPITALS WITH AN AIM TO ADVANCE SURVEILLANCE OF HAI AND GUIDE INFECTION PREVENTION ACTIVITIES TO IMPROVE HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND PATIENT SAFETY. SCOPE OF WORK HOSPITAL-ONSET BACTEREMIA AND FUNGEMIA (HOB) IS BEING EVALUATED IN THE UNITED STATES AS AN OBJECTIVE METRIC FOR SURVEILLANCE OF HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS (HAI). GIVEN THE HIGH BURDEN OF HAI AND ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN LOW AND MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRIES, IT IS APPROPRIATE TO EXPAND THE STUDY OF HOB TO THOSE COUNTRIES. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, THE FRAMEWORK FOR THE STUDY OF HOB DEVELOPED FOR US HOSPITALS WILL BE ADAPTED AND EVALUATED IN INDIA TO UNDERSTAND THE EPIDEMIOLOGY, SOURCES, PREVENTABILITY, AND FEASIBILITY OF HOB SURVEILLANCE IN THE INDIAN HOSPITAL SETTING. AIM 1: ASSESS THE INCIDENCE OF HOB THROUGH BLOOD CULTURE DATA COLLECTION PROSPECTIVELY FOR 6 MONTHS IN TWO STUDY HOSPITALS IN INDIA WE WILL CONDUCT A PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY TO EXAMINE HOB INCIDENCE AMONG PATIENTS ADMITTED TO THE TWO HOSPITALS FROM MARCH 1, 2020 TO AUGUST 31, 2020. EVERY BLOOD CULTURE PROCESSED BETWEEN MARCH 1, 2020 AND AUGUST 31, 2020 IN MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORIES OF TWO HOSPITALS WILL BE INCLUDED IN THE STUDY. FOR EACH BLOOD CULTURE, INFORMATION WILL BE COLLECTED BY INFECTION CONTROL NURSES. AIM 2: ASSESS THE SOURCES AND PREVENTABILITY OF HOB THROUGH A DETAILED REVIEW OF SPECIFIED NUMBER OF HOB EVENTS IN TWO STUDY HOSPITALS IN INDIA TO ASSESS THE SOURCE AND PREVENTABILITY OF HOB CASES, 300 CONSECUTIVE HOB CASES FROM AMRITA HOSPITAL AND 150 HOB CASES FROM FORTIS HOSPITAL WILL BE EXAMINED IN SELECTED UNITS (MICU, SICU, BMTU, NCU, PICU, NEURO ICU, INPATIENT MEDICAL AND SURGICAL WARDS INCLUDING LABOR AND DELIVERY WARDS) PROSPECTIVELY FROM APRIL 1, 2020 TO AUGUST 31, 2020. AT THE TWO HOSPITALS, A STANDARDIZED DATA COLLECTION FORM WILL BE USED TO CAPTURE KEY CLINICAL, MICROBIOLOGIC, AND DEMOGRAPHIC DATA, TO DETERMINE THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE OR SOURCE OF HOB, AND DETERMINE DEGREE OF PREVENTABILITY USING THE EXPERT-CONSENSUS BASED LIKERT SCALE PREVENTABILITY ASSESSMENT TOOL DEVELOPED FOR US HOSPITALS IN AN ONGOING STUDY. AIM 3: ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY AND COST FOR CONDUCTING HOB SURVEILLANCE IN THE TWO STUDY HOSPITALS IN INDIA TO ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY, INFORMATION ON FACTORS AFFECTING HOB SURVEILLANCE IMPLEMENTATION WILL BE COLLECTED AT THE TWO HOSPITALS BY CONDUCTING QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH STUDY INFECTION CONTROL NURSES, 3-5 CLINICIANS, THE HEAD OF INFECTION CONTROL PROGRAM AND THE STUDY STAFF. THESE INTERVIEWS WILL BE CONDUCTED BY PIS EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA SKYPE. CO-I: SURBHI LEEKHA (8% EFFORT) DR. LEEKHA WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. GANDRA IN PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC INPUT INTO THE DESIGN AND CONDUCT OF ALL ASPECTS OF THIS PROPOSAL. SPECIFICALLY, SHE WILL USE HER EXPERTISE IN DEVELOPING THE PREVENTABILITY FRAMEWORK INCLUDING THE DELPHI CONSENSUS METHODOLOGY USED FOR THE ONGOING US STUDY OF HOB, AS WELL AS EVALUATION OF SOURCES OF HOB. SHE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE START-UP MEETING, REGULAR COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE STUDY TEAM AND CDC, DEVELOPMENT OF THE PREVENTABILITY FRAMEWORK, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, DATA COLLECTION, AND DATA ANALYSIS.

ACCORDINGLY, COLLECTION OF FINE NEEDLE ASPIRATES (FNA) OF LYMPH NODES ARE INCREASINGLY BECOMING THE PREFERRED METHOD FOR MONITORING THE VACCINE-INDUCED GC-TFH AND GC-B CELLS IN THE LN OF NON-HUMAN PRIMATE AND HUMAN STUDIES. THE USE OF FNAS PROVIDES THE UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO LONGITUDINALLY SAMPLE THE SAME LN WITHOUT EXCISING THE ENTIRE LN THROUGH BIOPSY. HOWEVER, THE FNAS SAMPLE VERY TINY FRACTION OF THE LN AND IT IS NOT CLEAR IF THEY REPRESENT THE GC-TFH AND GC-B CELL RESPONSE OF THE ENTIRE LN. HENCE IT IS IMPERATIVE THAT WE KNOW THAT WHAT WE ARE MEASURING VIA FNA IS SIMILAR TO WHAT IS HAPPENING IN THE LN. THEREFORE, IN THIS STUDY WE AIM TO MEASURE AND TRACK ANTIGEN SPECIFIC RESPONSES POST INFLUENZA VACCINATION BY TAKING FNAS JUST PRIOR TO COLLECTION OF LN BIOPSY. IN ADDITION, WE WILL COMPARE THE GC-TFH AND GC-B CELL RESPONSE INDUCED BY TWO ADJUVANTS I.E., AS03 AND ALUM-3M-052. AS03 HAS BEEN APPROVED FOR USE IN HUMANS AND ALUM-3M-052 IS CURRENTLY BEING TESTED IN HUMANS FOR A HIV VACCINE. USING THE RESULTS FROM THIS STUDY WE WOULD BE ABLE TO DETERMINE IF FNA SAMPLES TAKEN POST VACCINATION CAN CORRECTLY PREDICT THE ANTIGEN SPECIFIC RESPONSE IN THE LN AND IF HOW IMMUNE RESPONSES INDUCED BY TWO PROMISING AND CLINICALLY RELEVANT ADJUVANTS COMPARE FOR INDUCTION AND PERSISTENCE OF GC T AND B CELL RESPONSES, AND HOW THESE INFLUENCE PLASMA CELLS IN BM AND PERSISTENCE OF ANTIBODY RESPONSE IN SERUM. OPTION 18C: IF300302076-940002 HERE WE PROPOSE CONDUCT A NHP STUDY TO ADDRESS TWO OBJECTIVES. THE OBJECTIVE OF AIM 1 IS TO TEST IF INTRANASAL BOOST WITH JN.1 SPIKE MRNA VACCINATION IS SUPERIOR TO INTRAMUSCULAR BOOST WITH THE SAME MRNA VACCINE IN INDUCING HUMORAL AND CELLULAR IMMUNITY IN THE UPPER AND LOWER AIRWAY. THE OBJECTIVE OF AIM 2 IS TO COMPARE THE ABILITY OF JN.1 SPIKE MRNA VACCINATION TO INDUCE NEUTRALIZING ACTIVITY AGAINST JN.1 IN THE PRESENCE AND ABSENCE OF PRE-EXISTING IMMUNITY TO SARS-COV2 AGAINST ANCESTRAL WA-1 SPIKE. THIS WILL ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF B CELL IMPRINTING IN THE CONTEXT OF THE CURRENT COVID-19 VACCINE. THESE DATA WILL BE VERY IMPORTANT FOR DEVELOPING IMPROVED VACCINES AGAINST COVID-19. THESE MEASUREMENTS ARE VERY DIFFICULT IN VACCINATED HUMANS AND NHP STUDIES ARE IDEAL. AS INDICATED BELOW, WE PROPOSE TO STUDY 3 GROUPS OF RHESUS MACAQUES WITH 5 ANIMALS/GROUP. THIS ACCOUNTS FOR A TOTAL OF 15 ANIMALS.

description: THE BRIGHAM AND WOMEN'S HOSPITAL, INC. (BWH), IN COLLABORATION WITH RUTGERS UNIVERSITY, PROPOSES TO CONDUCT A STUDY TO COMPARE THE RISK OF NEWLY DIAGNOSED DEMENTIA/ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) BETWEEN PATIENTS TREATED WITH SELECTED MEDICATIONS (A MAXIMUM OF 20), TARGETING SPECIFIC MOLECULAR PATHWAYS ASSOCIATED WITH THE SEVERITY OF AD PATHOLOGY OR THE EXPRESSION OF CLINICAL SYMPTOMS, AND PATIENTS TREATED WITH ALTERNATIVE MEDICATIONS FOR THE SAME INDICATION. THE STUDY, DESCRIBED IN DETAIL IN THE RESEARCH PLAN, WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARALLEL IN US MEDICARE DATA AND UK CLINICAL PRACTICE RESEARCH DATALINK (CPRD) DATA. US MEDICARE ANALYSES WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AT BWH; UK CPRD ANALYSES WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AT RUTGERS UNIVERSITY AT THE CENTER FOR PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGY AND TREATMENT SCIENCE (PETS) LED BY DR. GERHARD, THE PI OF THE RUTGERS SUBCONTRACT. THE TEAM AT RUTGERS WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE TEAM AT BWH AND DR. THAMBISETTY'S TEAM AT NIA ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE ANALYTIC PROTOCOLS, WITH PARTICULAR RESPONSIBILITY FOR ALL ASPECTS OF THE CPRD ANALYSES. IN ADDITION, RUTGERS WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR DATA CLEANING, CONSTRUCTION OF ANALYTIC DATASETS, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF DESCRIPTIVE AND INFERENTIAL STATISTICAL ANALYSES FOR ALL CPRD STUDIES. DR. GERHARD WILL CLOSELY COLLABORATE WITH DRS. DESAI, SCHNEEWEISS, THAMBISETTY, AND OTHER STUDY INVESTIGATORS ON THE INTERPRETATION OF THE DATA, DEVELOPMENT OF REPORTS AND MANUSCRIPTS, AND DISSEMINATION OF FINDINGS.

description: THE TTIMS LRCC PROJECT PURPOSE IS TO SERVE AS THE BIOSTATISTICAL AND ANALYTICAL CENTER FOR SPECIFIC ANALYSES RELEVANT TO THE EVALUATION AND MONITORING OF HIV (INCIDENT AND PREVALENT INFECTIONS), HCV (INCIDENT) AND HBV (INCIDENT), AND SYPHILIS POSITIVE BLOOD DONORS. SPECIFICALLY, THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THIS CONTRACT ARE TO: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE AND MONITOR RISK FACTOR CHARACTERISTICS OF DONATIONS CONFIRMED POSITIVE FOR TTIS AND COMPARISON UNINFECTED (CONTROL) DONORS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ COMPARE/ANALYZE RISK FACTOR DATA TO THAT OBTAINED IN THE EARLIER TTIMS STUDY PERIOD AND THE REDS-II TTVI MARKER PREVALENCE AND RISK FACTOR STUDY. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ INTEGRATE RISK FACTOR DATA AND DISEASE MARKER SURVEILLANCE INFORMATION ACROSS DIFFERENT BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ MONITOR ARV AND PREP/PEP USE IN US ALLOGENEIC BLOOD DONOR POPULATION BASED ON TESTING OF BOTH HIV- POSITIVE AND INFECTION NEGATIVE DONATIONS FOR THE PRESENCE OF ARV DRUGS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EXPLORE THE CHARACTERISTICS OF BLOOD DONORS WHO USE ARV/PREP/PEP TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THEIR RISKS, KNOWLEDGE, AND MOTIVATIONS FOR DONATING WHILE USING THESE THERAPIES. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE WELL-CHARACTERIZED US BLOOD DONOR SAMPLES FROM TTIMS AND OTHER SOURCES FOR THE REFINEMENT OF EXISTING ANALYTICAL METHODS SUCH AS THE SEDIA LAG AVIDITY ASSAY TO DERIVE ESTIMATES OF RECENT INFECTION WITH HIV WITH A GOAL OF RAPIDLY OBTAINING MORE ACCURATE AND TIMELY RESULTS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ PROVIDE LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT AND FOR THE COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE MEETINGS, CONFERENCES, AND DONATION(S) TRANSFER/SHIPMENT. IN SUPPORT OF THESE OBJECTIVES, NYBC WILL RECRUIT, ENROLL AND INTERVIEW ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDE DATA AS REQUIRED IN THE TTIMS LRCC STATEMENT OF WORK, PROVIDE BIOSPECIMENS FOR RESEARCH TESTING AT VRI, AND WILL ACTIVELY COLLABORATE IN THE ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, AND REPORTING OF FINDINGS IN TTIMS. DEBRA KESSLER, WILL SERVE AS THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI) AT NYBC. SHE WILL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF NYBCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PARTICIPATION IN THE LRCC PORTION OF TTIMS INCLUDING ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA AND BIOSPECIMENS AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT. IN ADDITION, CARLOS DEL VALLE, WILL SERVE AS THE STUDY MANAGER AT NYBC. HE WILL ASSIST IN THE OVERSIGHT OF THE ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA, AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT WHEN NECESSARY. NYBC WILL RECRUIT DONORS WITH QUALIFYING TEST RESULTS; ADMINISTER THE WEB-BASED QUESTIONNAIRE AND ENTER RISK FACTOR DATA INTO AN ELECTRONIC DATABASE; PERFORM QUALITY CONTROL (QC) ON ALL DATA ENTERED INTO THE DATABASE; RESPOND TO REQUESTS FROM THE LRCC REGARDING DATA QUALITY ASSURANCE AND QC; DEVELOP AND SUBMIT TO THE LOCAL IRB DOCUMENTS AND AMENDMENTS FOR APPROVAL. NYBC STAFF WILL FORWARD PLASMA BAGS AND/OR PILOT TUBES TO CREATIVE TESTING SOLUTIONS (CTS) SO THAT CTS CAN CREATE UP TO 5 X 2 ML PLASMA CYROVIALS AND A SINGLE 15 ML PLASMA CRYOVIAL FOR EACH PARTICIPANT AND PREPARE ALIQUOTS FOR SHIPMENT TO THE REPOSITORY AND ADDITIONAL TESTING AT VRI FOR ALL INFECTIONS OF INTEREST AS DEFINED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE. IN COLLABORATION WITH THE LRCC, NYBC WILL COORDINATE SAMPLE SHIPMENT WITH DESIGNATED CTS STAFF. IN ADDITION, NYBC WILL WORK WITH THE LRCC AND CTS TO SOURCE SPECIMENS FOR ARV/PEP/PREP TESTING. NYBC WILL ALSO WORK THE LRCC TO FACILITATE SURVEYS AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS OF ARV/PEP/PREP REACTIVE BLOOD DONORS. NYBC WILL NOT BE EXPECTED TO LEAD THE COLLECTION OF THESE SURVEY AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW DATA BUT WILL ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING AND RECRUITING PARTICIPANTS FOR THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDENDUMS TO THIS SOW WILL BE DEVELOPED AFTER THE RESEARCH PROTOCOLS TO SUPPORT EXPANDED ART/PEP/PREP STUDIES ARE FULLY DEFINED AND APPROVED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE. A PROTOCOL FOR EXPANDED DONOR SAMPLE COLLECTION FOR PREP/PEP TESTING IS UNDER DEVELOPMENT AND WILL TRIGGER AN ADDENDUM TO THIS SOW.

description: IN COLLABORATION WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN-MADISON AND ESTABLISHED COMMUNITY PARTNERS, THE CITY OF MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY (MHDL) WILL UTILIZE VIRAL GENOME SEQUENCING FOR SARS-COV-2 TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE EMERGENCE AND SPREAD OF NEW SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS ARISING AS A RESULT OF IMMUNE FAILURE. MHDLÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON THE FOLLOWING KEY POPULATIONS IN MILWAUKEE COUNTY: PATIENTS AND PROVIDERS IN HEALTHCARE SETTINGS, INCLUDING VACCINATED AND/OR IMMUNE COMPROMISED INDIVIDUALS; STUDENT POPULATIONS; AND CONGREGATE SETTINGS OF HIGH SOCIOECONOMIC VULNERABILITY, SUCH AS HOMELESS SHELTERS AND PRISONS. AS STATED IN THE FULL PROJECT STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW), PRIMARY DELIVERABLE FROM THIS PROJECT WILL BE ATTEMPTING TO UNFOLD 6,000 SARS-COV-2 GENOME SEQUENCES FROM DANE COUNTY AND MILWAUKEE COUNTY COMBINED. MHDL WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SEQUENCING APPROXIMATELY 1,000 SPECIMENS PER YEAR IN MILWAUKEE COUNTY. MHDL WILL OBTAIN CLINICAL SPECIMENS THROUGH THE WISCONSIN DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SERVICES Ã¢Â‚¬Å“COVID-19 HEALTH ALERT # 25: SURVEILLANCE FOR NEW GENETIC VARIANTS OF SARS-COV-2: INFORMATION FOR CLINICIANS,Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ WHICH AUTHORIZES SARS-COV-2 TESTING PROVIDERS TO SHARE RESIDUAL SAMPLES FROM INDIVIDUALS WITH IMMUNE FAILURE, AS WELL AS FROM ITS HIGH-RISK COVID-19 SURVEILLANCE SITES, INCLUDING MILWAUKEE COUNTY JAILS, DETENTION CENTERS, CORRECTIONAL FACILITIES, HOMELESS SHELTERS, GROUP HOMES, AND OTHER COMMUNITY SETTINGS. ALL THOSE SITES ARE CURRENTLY MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY COVID-19 SURVEILLANCE SITES. IN ORDER TO FULFILL THE PROJECT OBJECTIVES OF SEQUENCING VIRAL GENOMES AND ASSESSING ANTIBODY TITERS FROM THE SPECIFIED POPULATIONS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ SARS-COV-2 INFECTED, VACCINATED HEALTHCARE WORKERS, PERSISTENTLY INFECTED INDIVIDUALS WITH MEDICALLY MANAGED CO-MORBIDITIES, AND HOMELESS AND INCARCERATED INDIVIDUALS WITH PERSISTENT INFECTIONS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ MHDL WILL GENERATE UP TO 500 SARS-COV-2 SEQUENCES PER YEAR FROM EACH OF THOSE POPULATION GROUPS. ADDITIONALLY, IN ORDER TO FULFILL THE GOAL OF CONDUCTING COMMUNITY SURVEILLANCE SEQUENCING FOR SARS-COV-2, MHDL WILL SEQUENCE UP TO 500 SPECIMENS FROM CITY OF MILWAUKEE PER YEAR IF SPECIMEN ACCRUAL FROM THE OTHER SPECIFIED POPULATIONS DOES NOT MEET ENROLLMENT TARGETS. MHDL WILL ALSO ASSESS ANTIBODY TITERS FOR ABOUT 100 SPECIMENS PER YEAR AS PART OF THIS PROJECT. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL, CLINICAL, AND DEMOGRAPHIC DATA (DE-IDENTIFIED) WILL BE SHARED BETWEEN UW-MADISON, MHDL AND OTHER GRANT AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS AS NEEDED, TO SUPPORT MORE EFFICIENT FLOW OF INFORMATION, ENHANCED UNDERSTANDING OF TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS INCLUDING DIVERSITY AND ORIGINATION OF VIRUS VARIANTS, AS WELL AS IMPACT OF IMMUNE FAILURE DUE TO SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS IN BOTH MILWAUKEE AND DANE COUNTIES, AND ANY NECESSARY FOLLOW-UP. DR. SANJIB BHATTACHARYYA, DIRECTOR OF THE CITY OF MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY, WILL LEAD PROJECT AND COLLABORATION EFFORTS WITH DRS. OÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢CONNOR AND FRIEDRICH AT UW-MADISON.

description: SECTION 1 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ BACKGROUND DURING CRITICAL PPE SHORTAGES, SUCH AS THOSE ASSOCIATED WITH THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, CDC RECOMMENDS N95 EXTENDED USE (WEARING THE SAME N95 FOR MULTIPLE PATIENT ENCOUNTERS) AND LIMITED REUSE (STORING AN N95 BETWEEN SHIFTS FOR USE OVER MULTIPLE SHIFTS WITH OR WITHOUT DECONTAMINATION). MANY HEALTHCARE WORKERS ARE EMPLOYING THESE STRATEGIES OUT OF NECESSITY. THE SUSTAINED PERFORMANCE OF THESE RESPIRATORS DEPENDS ON THE RESPIRATOR MAINTAINING ITS FILTRATION EFFICIENCY AND ITS ABILITY TO PROVIDE AN ADEQUATE SEAL (FIT) TO THE USERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S FACE. FIT TESTING IS TYPICALLY PERFORMED WHEN A RESPIRATOR IS ISSUED TO THE USER AND ON AN ANNUAL BASIS. A USER-SEAL CHECK IS THEN PERFORMED WHENEVER A RESPIRATOR IS DONNED. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE FOUND REPEATED DONNINGS/DOFFINGS TO SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASE THE RESPIRATORÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S FIT. A RECENT PILOT CROSSSECTIONAL CLINICAL STUDY ADMINISTERED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, SAN FRANCISCO FOUND FIT FAILURES OF RESPIRATORS AFTER BEING WORN FOR 2 SHIFTS. CLINICAL STUDIES PROVIDE A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO MEASURE RESPIRATOR PERFORMANCE UNDER ACTUAL USE SCENARIOS. MANY RESEARCH QUESTIONS RELATED TO N95S BEING USED DURING THE CURRENT COVID-19 PANDEMIC CAN BE ANSWERED BY ASSESSING FIT OF N95S WHILE IN USE, EXAMINING USED N95S FOR FILTRATION AND CONTAMINATION, AND SURVEYING THOSE WHO WEAR THESE N95S FOR EXTENDED PERIODS OR WHO REUSE N95S OR WEAR DECONTAMINATED N95S. SECTION 2 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ PURPOSE THE PURPOSE OF THIS AGREEMENT IS TO SUPPORT THE COMPLETION OF THE STUDY TITLED A CLINICAL EXAMINATION OF N95 REUSE AND EXTENDED. A CLINICAL INVESTIGATION OF N95 EXTENDED USE AND REUSE (WITH AND WITHOUT DECONTAMINATION) WILL PROVIDE KEY INFORMATION RELATED TO 1) HOW LONG N95S MAINTAIN THEIR FIT DURING EXTENDED USE, 2) HOW MANY TIMES AN N95 CAN BE DONNED/DOFFED AND MAINTAIN THEIR FIT, 3) THE ABILITY OF A USER SEAL CHECK TO INDICATE FIT IN THE FIELD, 4) WHAT ADVERSE HEALTH EFFECTS OR SYMPTOMS ARE EXPERIENCED BY USERS DURING EXTENDED USE AND REUSE, 5) WHAT EFFECT DOES EXTENDED USE AND REUSE HAVE ON N95 FILTRATION PERFORMANCE AND 6) THE LEVEL OF CONTAMINATION OF N95S WHEN SUBJECTED TO EXTENDED USE AND REUSE. SECTION 3 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ SCOPE OF WORK UCSF WILL COORDINATE AND CONDUCT A PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY EXAMINING THE EFFECTS OF N95 EXTENDED USE AND REUSE (WITH AND WITHOUT DECONTAMINATION) ON USER DISCOMFORT AND RESPIRATOR FIT, FILTRATION, AND CONTAMINATION AT SIX PARTICIPATING SITES. UCSF IS THE PRIME SITE, RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CREATION OF THE STUDY PROTOCOL, IRB PROPOSAL, DATA COLLECTION, MANAGEMENT, AND ANALYSIS AS WELL AS DISSEMINATION OF RESULTS. THE STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED AT UCSF AND FIVE OTHER SITES (BELOW), WHERE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES, WHO CURRENTLY WEAR N95S UNDER EXTENDED USE AND REUSE STRATEGIES WILL PARTICIPATE IN THIS STUDY FOR UP TO A TWO-YEAR PERIOD. EACH SITE WILL COORDINATE WITH THE PRIME SITE, ENROLL PARTICIPANTS, COLLECT DATA IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE STUDY PROTOCOL, AND AID IN PARTICIPATE IN STUDY DISSEMINATION. TASK 1- PROVIDE FEEDBACK REGARDING THE FEASIBILITY OF THE STUDY PROTOCOL THE PRIME SITE WILL PROVIDE NIOSH WITH A DRAFT COPY OF THE PROTOCOL FOR REVIEW. NIOSH WILL REVIEW THE PROTOCOL AND PROVIDE COMMENTS. THE SITES WILL PROVIDE FEEDBACK REGARDING THE FEASIBILITY OF THE STUDY PROTOCOL AT EACH SITE. TASK 2- VERIFY IRB APPROVAL OF PROTOCOL WITH LOCAL IRB THE PRIME SITE WILL PRODUCE AND SUBMIT ALL REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION FOR APPROVAL OF THE STUDY INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB). EACH SITE WILL WORK WITH PRIME SITE, SINGLE IRB, AND LOCAL IRB TO OBTAIN NECESSARY APPROVALS. IRB APPROVALS AT ALL SIX LOCATIONS WILL BE COMPLETED PRIOR TO SAMPLE COLLECTION. TASK 3- COORDINATE WITH PRIME SITE TO STANDARDIZE STUDY PROCEDURES, PURCHASE SUPPLIES, AND ENSURE ADEQUATE PARTICIPANT ENROLLMENT AND RECRUITMENT THE PRIME SITE WILL BE COORDINATE TRAINING OF THE NIOSH-APPROVED PROTOCOL METHODOLOGY FOR ALL STUDY PERSONNEL AND STUDY PARTICIPANTS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL PURCHASE FIT TESTING AND OTHER NECESSARY SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT

description: OPTION 10A NASOPHARYNGEAL ASPIRATES WILL BE COLLECTED FROM CHILDREN ENROLLED IN THE UMOYA COHORT AT TYBERBERG HOSPITAL (STELLENBOSCH UNIVERSITY) IN CAPE TOWN, SOUTH AFRICA. THOSE SAMPLES TESTING POSITIVE FOR INFLUENZA VIRUS OR SARS-COV-2 WILL BE IDENTIFIED VIA MULTIPLEX RT-PCR. SARS-COV-2 POSITIVE SAMPLES WILL BE SENT FOR VIRUS ISOLATION AT THE DIVISION OF MEDICAL VIROLOGY, STELLENBOSCH UNIVERSITY (WHERE THE BSL3 LAB IS LOCATED, AND WHERE STAFF FROM THE SHAW LAB ARE ALSO WORKING). RNA WILL ALSO BE EXTRACTED FOR SEQUENCING. INFLUENZA POSITIVE SAMPLES WILL BE SENT TO THE SHAW LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF THE WESTERN CAPE FOR VIRUS ISOLATION, AND RNA EXTRACTION/CDNA AMPLIFICATION. TITERED STOCKS WILL BE ESTABLISHED FOR EACH VIRUS ISOLATE WHICH WILL BE SEQUENCE VERIFIED AND CHARACTERIZED FOR GROWTH PROPERTIES. ANTIVIRAL SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING WILL BE PERFORMED FOR INFLUENZA VIRUS ISOLATES. REPRESENTATIVE VIRUSES WILL BE SHIPPED TO ISMMS FOR DEPOSITION WITH BEI. RNA FROM THE INFLUENZA OR SARS-COV-2 POSITIVE SAMPLES WILL BE ISOLATED AND FOLLOWING CDNA AMPLIFICATION, FULL LENGTH VIRAL GENOME SEQUENCES WILL BE DETERMINED BY NEXT GENERATION SEQUENCING METHODS. FULL LENGTH SEQUENCES WILL BE DEPOSITED IN PUBLIC DATABASES E.G. GISAID. PHYLOGENETIC ANALYSES WILL BE PERFORMED TO COMPARE THE GENETIC RELATIONSHIP OF THESE VIRUSES TO OTHER INFLUENZA VIRUSES OR SARS-COV-2 ISOLATES IN THE GLOBAL DATABASE. FINALLY, FOR INFLUENZA VIRUSES, WE WILL DETERMINE THE GENETIC HETEROGENEITY OF THE QUASISPECIES IN A PATIENT BY CALCULATING THE INTRINSIC SEQUENCE DIVERSITY OF THE INFLUENZA VIRUS POPULATION IN EACH CLINICAL SAMPLE.

description: OPTION 18A: 0258-A705-4609 AS PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED, WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A ROBUST CD8+ T CELL DEPLETION STRATEGY TO PROBE FOR THE ROLE OF T CELLS IN SARSÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½COVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½2 CONTROL. IN THIS ANALYSIS, 24 ANIMALS WILL BE VACCINATED WITH THE ORIGINAL WA J&J VACCINE INSERT. IN 12 ANIMALS, CD8+ T CELLS WILL BE DEPLETED PRIOR TO B.1.351 CHALLENGE. A SIMILAR ANALYSIS WILL BE PERFORMED WITH THE P.1 VARIANT TO CONFIRM PROTECTIVE CORRELATES ARE CONSERVED ACROSS VOCS. VIRAL LOADS FOLLOWING CHALLENGE WILL DEFINE EXPLICITLY WHETHER VACCINEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ELICITED CD8 T CELLS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROTECTION AGAINST HETEROLOGOUS CHALLENGE WITH SARSÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½COVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½2 VARIANTS OF CONCERN. OPTION 18D: 0258-A716-4609 WE HAVE DEVELOPED NONHUMAN PRIMATE MODELS FOR ALL THE MAJOR SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS TO DATE, INCLUDING WA1/2020, ALPHA, BETA, GAMMA, DELTA, AND MOST RECENTLY OMICRON. WE HAVE ALREADY TITRATED THE SARS-COV-2 OMICRON STOCK (FROM THE NIH SAVE CONSORTIUM) IN MACAQUES, AND THUS THE PROPOSED VACCINE STUDY CAN BE PERFORMED RAPIDLY. WE PROPOSE TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF THE CLINICAL PFIZER BNT162B2 VACCINE AND J&J AD26.COV2.S VACCINE AGAINST A HETEROLOGOUS OMICRON CHALLENGE. WE EXPECT THAT THESE VACCINES WILL LIKELY BE LESS EFFECTIVE AT PROTECTING AGAINST OMICRON INFECTION COMPARED WITH WA1/2020 INFECTION, DUE TO THE ABILITY OF OMICRON TO EVADE VACCINE-ELICITED NABS. HOWEVER, OMICRON-SPECIFIC NABS WILL LIKELY BE INDUCED FOLLOWING A BOOST IMMUNIZATION. MOREOVER, VACCINE-ELICITED T CELL RESPONSES ARE HIGHLY CROSS-REACTIVE TO OMICRON, AND THUS WE MAY OBSERVE SUBSTANTIAL CONTROL OF VIRUS REPLICATION IN THE UPPER AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACTS FOLLOWING INFECTION. WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER NABS AND/OR CD8 T CELL RESPONSES ARE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION AGAINST OMICRON INFECTION AND VIROLOGIC CONTROL. WE WILL ALSO ASSESS WHETHER OMICRON INFECTION RESULTS IN MORE OF AN UPPER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTION AND LESS OF A LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTION COMPARED WITH PRIOR VARIANTS. WE WILL CHALLENGE 30 RHESUS OR CYNOMOLGUS MACAQUES WITH SARS-COV-2 OMICRON.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY OF LEIDOS AS PART OF THE IEDB & AR PROGRAM IS TO MAINTAIN AND IMPROVE THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE AND CURATION SYSTEMS. IN ADDITION, LEIDOS SHALL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC MEETINGS, PROVIDE PROGRESS REPORTS ON THE WORK AND RESPOND TO IEDB HELP DESK TICKETS IF REQUIRED. AN OVERVIEW OF TASKS TO BE ACCOMPLISHED BY LEIDOS ARE LISTED BELOW: A. IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE SYSTEM AND MAKING IT AVAILABLE TO END USERS. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, STORAGE, ANALYSIS, ARCHIVE AND EXCHANGE OF IMMUNE EPITOPE DATA AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. 2. ASSIST LJI IN MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF THE IEDB WEB PORTAL INCLUDING: A. FURTHER OPTIMIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF UNIFORM, INTELLIGENT WEB-BASED INTERFACES FOR MAKING DATA ACCESSIBLE TO END USERS. THE INTERFACE SHALL MINIMALLY INCLUDE COMPLEX QUERY; SEMANTIC QUERY; DOWNLOAD; EPITOPE SUBMISSION; LINKS TO RELATED RESOURCES; AND REPORTS, MANUSCRIPTS, NEWSLETTERS, AND COMPENDIA. B. UPDATE EXISTING FEATURES AND IMPLEMENT NEW FEATURES IN THE IEDB WEB PORTAL AS NEEDED. C. ASSIST IN ESTABLISHING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE METRICS TO DETERMINE UTILIZATION AND UTILITY OF THE WEB PORTAL WITHIN THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. RELEVANT METRICS SHALL FREQUENCY OF DATA DOWNLOADS, CHARACTERIZATION OF USERS AND USER QUERY STATISTICS. AT A MINIMUM, THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE CONDUCTED BIANNUALLY (EVERY 2 YEARS). 3. UPON REQUEST, ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE AND UPDATING OF SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION INCLUDING: A. DOCUMENT ALL SYSTEM COMPONENTS, SOFTWARE AND DATABASES IN ACCORDANCE WITH INDUSTRY BEST PRACTICES AND IN A MANNER THAT WILL ALLOW ANOTHER CONTRACTOR OR USER TO UNDERSTAND AND UTILIZE THE SYSTEM. B. PROVIDE A HIGH LEVEL OVERVIEW OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES OF THE SYSTEM, INCLUDING SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DESIGN, DATABASE DESIGN AND DATA MODELS. THIS COMPENDIUM OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES SHALL BE UPDATED SEMI-ANNUALLY OR AS REQUESTED BY THE COTR OR CONTRACTING OFFICER. C. WORK WITH LJI TO ESTABLISH AND DOCUMENT A SCHEDULE OF SYSTEM UPDATES AND RELEASES. 4. COMPLY WITH SECTION 508 OF THE REHABILITATION ACT (29 U.S.C. 794D), (SEE HTTP://WWW.SECTION508.GOV/) IN TERMS OF DATABASE/WEBSITE USE AND DIRECT EPITOPE/DATA SUBMISSION BY THE BROADER RESEARCH COMMUNITY. B. CURATION SYSTEM TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB CURATION SYSTEM. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, TRACKING, AND ASSIGNMENT OF PUBLISHED MANUSCRIPTS AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. C. MEETINGS AND REPORTS PARTICIPATE IN WEEKLY MEETINGS TO COORDINATE SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS. ADDITIONALLY, PROVIDE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS SUMMARIZING WORK PERFORMED. D. COMMUNITY OUTREACH 1. IF REQUESTED, ASSIST WITH ADDRESSING ANY HELP DESK TICKETS RELATED TO ANY IEDB SYSTEMS INFRASTRUCTURE. 2. ASSIST LJI WITH PREPARING A COMPENDIUM OF THE DATA IN THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS-2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORT AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDY. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, BIOREPOSITORY AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID-19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN.

description: DR. WARD WILL SERVE AS PI OF THIS SUBCONTRACT AND WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR COORDINATING ACTIVITIES TO IDENTIFY, SELECT AND CHARACTERIZE SARS-COV-2 POSITIVE SAMPLES FOR GENOMIC SEQUENCING AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSIS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE PIS AND CO-INVESTIGATORS OF THIS PROPOSAL. DR. WARD WILL SUPERVISE UMASS MEDICAL SCHOOL RESEARCH PERSONNEL AND ACTIVITIES. AT THE TIME OF SUBMISSION, UMASS MEDICAL SCHOOL HAS ESTABLISHED A BIOREPOSITORY OF OVER 5000 SARS-COV-2 POSITIVE SAMPLES FROM PATIENTS AND HEALTHCARE WORKERS REPRESENTING AN AFFECTED POPULATION FROM WORCESTER COUNTY AND CENTRAL MASSACHUSETTS. DR. WARD WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ELLISON TO IDENTIFY PRIORITY SAMPLES FROM HEALTH CARE WORKERS AND PATIENTS FOR GENOMIC SEQUENCING OF SARS-COV-2. DRS. WARD AND ELLISON WILL MANAGE DATA EXTRACTION, FROM ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS, TO SUPPORT EPIDEMIOLOGICAL EFFORTS. DRS. WARD AND ELLISON WILL PURSUE FOLLOW-UP ANALYSIS OF PATIENT AND HEALTH CARE WORKERS WITHIN UMASS HOSPITALS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL TRANSMISSION ROUTES WITHIN THE HOSPITAL. IN ADDITION, DRS. WARD AND ELLISON WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE MASSACHUSETTS DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEATH TO IDENTIFY CROSS TRANSMISSION ROUTES WITHIN THE COMMUNITY. DRS. WARD AND ELLISON WILL PROMOTE COLLABORATIVE INTERACTIONS BY FACILITATING DATA SHARING AND BY PARTICIPATING AND/OR HOSTING RESEARCH WORKING GROUPS AND SEMINARS WITH OTHER PIS AND WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE OVERALL SCIENTIFIC DESIGN, INTERPRETATION ON SCIENTIFIC RESULTS. DR. WARD WILL BE PRIMARILY RESPONSIBLE FOR SUPPORTING GENERATION OF GENOMIC DATA AND ANALYSIS, AND DATA EXTRACTION. DR. ELLISON WILL BE PRIMARILY RESPONSIBLE FOR CLINICAL INTERPRETATION AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL INVESTIGATIONS OF HEALTH CARE WORKERS. SCOPE OF WORK: THE SCOPE OF WORK WILL BE MANAGED TO MATCH THE CAPACITIES OF THE BROAD INSTITUTE AS DETERMINED BY THE AWARD. AT PRESENT, SARS-COV-2 POSITIVE SAMPLE COLLECTIONS MAY EXCEED THE PARAMETERS OF ANTICIPATED FUNDING. UMASS MEDICAL SCHOOL WILL PROVIDE SARS-COV-2 POSITIVE SAMPLES AND EXTRACTED CLINICAL METADATA TO SUPPORT FUNDED GENOMIC EFFORTS AT THE BROAD INSTITUTE. REGULAR MEETINGS AND COLLABORATIVE ANALYSIS WILL BE HELD TO COORDINATE ACTIVITIES ACROSS ALL PARTICIPATING INSTITUTIONS. description: STATEMENT OF WORK SARS-COV-2 B CELL EPITOPE MAPPING SUPPLEMENT (WILSON) SUBCONTRACT TO THE SUPPLEMENT FOR: NIAID CONTRACT 75N93019C00062 (FREEMONT, PI, PD) B CELL MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF PROTECTION FROM SARS-COV-2 PATRICK C. WILSON, SUBCONTRACT PI DEPARTMENT OF MEDICINE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO CHICAGO IL 60637 E-MAIL: WILSONP@UCHICAGO.EDU Ã¢Â‚¬Æ’ STATEMENT OF WORK CORONAVIRUSES ARE ENVELOPED NON-SEGMENTED POSITIVE-SENSE RNA VIRUSES BELONGING TO THE FAMILY CORONAVIRIDAE AND CIRCULATE BROADLY AMONGST AND BETWEEN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS. OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, TWO BETACORONAVIRUSES, SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (SARS-COV) AND MIDDLE EAST RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (MERS-COV), WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVER 10,000 CASES OF INFECTION. THE MORTALITY RATE OF SARS-COV WAS 10% WITH 29 COUNTRIES AFFECTED, AND THE MORTALITY RATE OF MERS WAS 35% WITH 27 COUNTRIES AFFECTED GLOBALLY. IN DECEMBER OF 2019, A NOVEL CORONAVIRUS (2019-NCOV) WAS DISCOVERED THROUGH DEEP SEQUENCING ANALYSIS AFTER A SERIES OF PNEUMONIA CASES WERE REPORTED IN WUHAN, HUBEI, CHINA WITH UNKNOWN VIRAL ORIGIN. SEVERAL INDEPENDENT STUDIES HAVE SINCE CONFIRMED THAT THE NOVEL VIRUS ORIGINATED FROM EXPOSURES IN A WUHAN SEAFOOD MARKET. BY ONLY MARCH 16, 2020, 2019-NCOV CAUSED A PANDEMIC SPANNING MOST COUNTRIES ON EARTH WITH A REPORTED 167,000 PEOPLE INFECTED WORLDWIDE, AND ALMOST 7000 CONFIRMED DEATHS. CASE AND MORTALITY RATES ARE CONTINUING TO RISE AND THE LACK OF ADEQUATE TESTING IN MAJOR POPULATION CENTERS PLUS CLEAR EVIDENCE OF COMMUNITY TRANSMISSIONS SUGGESTS THAT THE NUMBER OF INFECTED IS LIKELY SIGNIFICANTLY GREATER. MOREOVER, AS THE VIRUS CONTINUES TO SPREAD, ITS HIGH MUTATION RATE INTRODUCES THE THREAT OF INFECTIONS WITH NEW VARIANTS WHICH COULD HAVE ALTERED SEVERITY AND TRANSMISSIBILITY. THESE OCCURRENCES NECESSITATE THE URGENCY OF NOVEL PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC MEASURES TO HELP PREVENT THE SPREAD OF NCOV-2019, WHICH POSES ONE OF THE GREATEST GLOBAL HEALTH THREATS IN MODERN HISTORY. MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MAB) ARE MONOVALENT PROTEINS EXPRESSED BY B CELLS THAT CAN SPECIFICALLY TARGET 3-DIMENSIONAL VIRAL EPITOPES, LEADING TO POTENT VIRAL NEUTRALIZATION. MABS HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED MODERN MEDICINE BY PROVIDING PRECISION MEDICINE AGAINST MANY DISEASES, WITH OVER 70 MAB-BASED DRUGS APPROVED BY THE FDA. THE ISOLATION OF HUMAN MABS SPECIFIC FOR HIGHLY IMMUNOGENIC NCOV-2019 PROTEINS CAN BE RAPIDLY USED AS THERAPEUTIC AGENTS, FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS, AND FOR TEMPLATING THE GENERATION OF VACCINES THAT CAN PROTECT AGAINST NCOV-2019. OUR LABORATORY IS HIGHLY SPECIALIZED IN THE RAPID GENERATION OF NEUTRALIZING MABS FROM HUMAN B CELLS. WE AIM TO APPLY THIS EXPERTISE TO GENERATE HUMAN NCOV-2019-SPECIFIC MABS, WHICH HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RAPIDLY ALLEVIATE THE GLOBAL HEALTH BURDEN IMPOSED BY NCOV-2019 THROUGH THREE CRITICAL MEASURES: PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC. BY INVESTIGATING THE HUMAN ANTIBODY RESPONSE TO NCOV-2019, WE WILL GAIN IMPORTANT INSIGHT INTO THE IMMUNOGENICITY AND IMMUNODOMINANCE OF NCOV-2019 VIRAL PROTEINS, WHICH WILL IN TURN INFORM WHICH VIRAL TARGETS WILL BE MOST IMPORTANT TO PURSUE WITH THERAPEUTICS AND VACCINES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROPOSED SUPPLEMENT ARE AS FOLLOWS: A) GENERATE PANELS OF HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS. COVID-19 PATIENT BLOOD WILL BE OBTAINED FROM SEVERAL SOURCES INCLUDING VERIFIED INFECTED SAMPLES FROM TOKYO THROUGH COLLABORATOR YOSHI KAWAOKA, THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO OR OTHER HOSPITALS FROM COVID-19 ADMITTED PATIENTS, OR THROUGH OTHER COLLABORATING LABS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 SPIKE PROTEIN, SPIKE RBD AND ORF7 FROM DAVED FREEMONTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, VERSIONS OF THE SPIKE PROTEIN AND RBD FROM FLORIAN KRAMMERS LABORATORY, PLUS NSP3, NSP5, NSP9, NSP10, NSP15, NSP16, AND N PROTEIN FROM ANDRJEZ JOACHIMIACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, OR TO UNBIASED OTHER EPITOPES TARGETED BY ACTIVATED B CELLS AND PLASMABLASTS WILL BE DEVELOPED BY PATRICK WILSONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE RICKETTS BIOCONTAINMENT LABORATORY ON THE ARGONNE NATIONAL LABS CAMPUS AND AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO. B) EVALUATE THE B CELL RESPONSE OF COVID-19 PATIENTS: THE WILSON LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO WILL CHARACTERIZE PERIPHERAL BLOOD B CELLS REACTIVE TO SARS-COV-2 ENCODED PROTEINS OR ACTIVATED DURING INFECTION PLUS TFH CELLS USING SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOME AND CITE-SEQ ANALYSIS ON THE 10XGENOMICS PLATFORM. FROM THIS WE WILL LEARN ABOUT THE UNDERLYING IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THIS NOVEL CORONAVIRUS AND CORRELATE IMMUNE ACTIVITIES TO SERUM AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY PROTECTION, INFORMING FUTURE VACCINE-DESIGN AND EVALUATION EFFORTS. C) EVALUATE SERUM REACTIVITY TO A PANEL OF SARS-COV-2 PROTEINS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL BE VALUABLE AS POSSIBLE THERAPEUTIC AGENTS OR FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL ALSO GUIDE AND TEMPLATE THE GENERATION OF VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST COVID-19. THIS CONTRACT SUPPLEMENT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. WE WILL DEVELOP A DATABASE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO AND AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY THAT CATALOGS THE DATA GENERATED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY VARIOUS MAPPING STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. FREMONT AND COLLEAGUES AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY WILL MIRROR THIS DATA AS WELL AS PROGRESS OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY EXPERIMENTS OF THE ANTIBODY-ANTIGEN COMPLEXES. THE TEAMS OF INVESTIGATORS AND COLLABORATING LABORATORIES WILL DEPOSIT ALL VALIDATED EPITOPE DATA WITH THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE (IEDB) WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF IDENTIFICATION. THEY ALSO WILL SUBMIT ALL STRUCTURAL DATA FOR DEPOSITION IN THE RCSB PROTEIN DATABASE (PDB). ADDITIONAL RESOURCE SHARING, INCLUDING PUBLICATION UPLOADING FOR PMC FREE-ACCESS, WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY ALL INVESTIGATORS. ALL MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE GREATER RESEARCH COMMUNITY IN PUBLIC DEPOSITORIES SUCH AS BEI OR UPON REQUEST.

YOSHIHIRO KAWAOKA WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR RESEARCH TO ASSESS THE TRANSMISSION POTENTIAL OF WILD-TYPE AVIAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES IN MAMMALS; RESEARCH TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE ANTIGENIC EVOLUTION OF HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES; RESEARCH TO STUDY THE ROLE OF HOST FACTORS IN THE OUTCOME OF INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTIONS; AND AVIAN INFLUENZA SURVEILLANCE IN POULTRY IN VIETNAM AND INDONESIA. OPTION 12A: 0258-A702-4609 ISOLATE AND CHARACTERIZE NEW SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS. FROM NASOPHARYNGEAL SWAB AND SALIVA SAMPLES OBTAINED IN WISCONSIN AND SIERRA LEONE ALONG WITH POTENTIALLY OTHER PARTS OF THE WORLD, WE WILL ISOLATE AND CHARACTERIZE SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS. SANGER SEQUENCING WILL BE PERFORMED FOR RAPID IDENTIFICATION OF VARIANTS, BUT NGS WILL ALSO BE PERFORMED TO ANALYZE THE ENTIRE VIRAL GENOME. SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS WILL BE CHARACTERIZED BY USING A LIVE VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY AGAINST PANELS OF SERA COLLECTED FROM HUMANS AND ANIMALS IMMUNIZED WITH DIFFERENT VACCINES AND PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. OPTION 18A: 0258-A705-4609 TRANSMISSION OF SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS BETWEEN PAIRS OF HAMSTERS (NON-VACCINATED AND VACCINATED). FOR SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS, WE WILL CARRY OUT TRANSMISSION STUDIES BETWEEN PAIRS INFECTED, NON-VACCINATED AND VACCINATED CONTACT HAMSTERS. BASED ON AVAILABILITY, THE PFIZER, MODERNA, OR JOHNSON & JOHNSON VACCINE WILL BE USED TO VACCINATE THE HAMSTERS AND THE TRANSMISSION STUDIES WILL BE INITIATED AT LEAST 2 MONTHS AFTER THE LAST IMMUNIZATION. VIRUS TITERS WILL BE DETERMINED BY EXAMINING NASAL WASHES FROM THE NON-VACCINATED, INFECTED HAMSTERS AND FROM THE NASAL TURBINATE AND LUNG TISSUES OF THE VACCINATED, EXPOSED ANIMALS; LUNG TISSUE PATHOLOGY WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED. IN CASES OF HIGH VIRUS REPLICATION IN THE LUNGS, WE WILL PERFORM SEQUENCING TO DETERMINE WHETHER ANY ADDITION AMINO ACID SUBSTITUTIONS HAVE OCCURRED IN THE VIRAL GENOME, PARTICULARLY THE SPIKE GENE. OPTION 18D: 0258-A716-4609 WE WILL EXAMINE THE POTENTIAL OF NEW EMERGING SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS TO INFECT OR RE-INFECT HAMSTERS THAT WERE VACCINATED, PREVIOUSLY INFECTED, OR VACCINATED AND PREVIOUSLY INFECTED. TO PERFORM THESE STUDIES, WE WILL ESTABLISH GROUPS OF PFIZER OR MODERNA VACCINATED HAMSTERS. IN ADDITION, WE WILL ESTABLISH GROUPS OF HAMSTERS FIRST INFECTED WITH A PREVIOUS VARIANT SUCH AS DELTA OR OMICRON (BA.1 OR BA.5). ADDITIONAL GROUPS OF HAMSTERS WILL BE FIRST VACCINATED AND THEN INFECTED WITH BA.1 TO MIMIC HUMAN BREAKTHROUGH INFECTIONS. AGE-MATCHED, NAÃƑÂ¯VE HAMSTERS WILL BE ALSO ESTABLISHED AS CONTROLS. ALL HAMSTERS WILL BE HELD FOR AT LEAST THREE MONTHS PRIOR TO EVALUATION OF INFECTION WITH A NEW EMERGING VARIANT. SERUM SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED AT LEAST THREE MONTHS AFTER VACCINATION AND/OR INFECTION TO DETERMINE NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODY TITERS AGAINST DIFFERENT VARIANTS. AFTER (RE-) CHALLENGE WITH A NEW VARIANT, TISSUES WILL BE COLLECTED FROM ANIMALS AT TWO TIME POINTS AFTER CHALLENGE TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL STATISTICAL DIFFERENCES IN VIRAL TITERS IN THE VACCINATED AND/OR PREVIOUSLY INFECTED GROUPS RELATIVE TO THE NAÃƑÂ¯VE, CONTROL HAMSTERS. OPTION 9B: 0258-A730-4609 ANTIGENIC CARTOGRAPHY IS A POWERFUL TOOL TO DETERMINE THE ANTIGENIC DISTANCES BETWEEN DIFFERENT SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS. THIS APPROACH IS HELPFUL WHEN SELECTING NEW VARIANTS FOR VACCINE UPDATES. OPTION 18D EQUITABLE ADJUSTMENT: 0258-A746-4609 WE WILL ISOLATE NEW SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS FROM SWAB SAMPLES AND PERFORM SEQUENCING ON THE VIRAL GENOMES. description: OPTION 18C CEIRR CONCEPT PROPOSAL: LYMPHOID TISSUE RESERVOIRS OF HEMAGGLUTININ-SPECIFIC MEMORY B CELLS AND ROLE IN THE RESPONSE TO INACTIVATED INFLUENZA VACCINATION IT IS WELL ESTABLISHED THAT EARLY ANTIBODY (AB) PRODUCTION AFTER INACTIVATED INFLUENZA VACCINATION (IIV) IN HUMANS RESULTS FROM PRE-EXISTING MEMORY B CELL (MBC) ACTIVATION, LEADING TO A TRANSIENT WAVE OF CIRCULATING AB-SECRETING PLASMABLASTS (PBS). RECENTLY, DR. ALI ELLEBEDYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GROUP AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY, ST. LOUIS, EXTENDED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROCESS BY ANALYZING EVENTS IN AXILLARY LYMPH NODES, WHICH DRAIN THE SITE OF IIV ADMINISTRATION. FINDINGS INDICATED THAT PRE-EXISTING MBCS SPECIFIC FOR CONSERVED HEMAGGLUTININ (HA) EPITOPES WERE ACTIVATED BY THE VACCINE, GENERATING EARLY CIRCULATING PBS AND SEEDING GERMINAL CENTER (GC) REACTIONS. IN ADDITION, THE RESPONSE INCLUDED ACTIVATION AND GC ENTRY OF NAÃƑÂ¯VE B CELLS THAT RECOGNIZED NOVEL HA EPITOPES. HOWEVER, QUESTIONS REMAIN REGARDING PATHWAYS OF MBC ACTIVATION AND THE REPLENISHMENT AND EVOLUTION OF MBC POPULATIONS. THE MBC RESPONSE TO IIV IS ASSUMED TO BE LARGELY DRIVEN BY RESIDENT MBCS IN THE AXILLARY LYMPH NODES. AFTER FORMATION, ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC MBCS DISPERSE TO LYMPHOID TISSUES THROUGHOUT THE BODY AND MAINTAIN A LOW FREQUENCY (OFTEN BELOW THE LEVEL OF DETECTION) IN THE CIRCULATION. HOWEVER, DISPERSION PATTERNS ARE NON-UNIFORM AND MOBILIZATION OF LYMPHOID TISSUE-RESIDENT MBCS AND DIRECTED TRAFFICKING TO RESPONDING TISSUES CAN OCCUR. THE PROCESSES THAT DETERMINE THE MBCS THAT CAN BE RECRUITED INTO THE RESPONSE TO IIV ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. IN THE PROPOSED STUDIES, WE WILL COLLABORATE WITH DR. ELLEBEDY TO INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF PRE-EXISTING MBCS IN THE RESPONSE TO THE H3 COMPONENT OF THE 2018/19 AND 2019/20 IIVS, WHICH CONTAIN DIFFERENT H3 STRAINS. THE ANALYSIS WILL MONITOR RESPONSES AT THE LEVEL OF H3-REACTIVE MBC ACTIVATION AND FORMATION. SAMPLES FROM SUBJECTS RESPONDING TO IIV WILL BE PROVIDED BY DR. ELLEBEDY AND WILL INCLUDE SERA AND PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS, AS WELL AS >700 VACCINE-REACTIVE ABS CLONED FROM GC B CELLS. A SECOND COMPONENT OF THE WORK WILL INVESTIGATE THE COMPLEXITY OF LYMPHOID TISSUE RESERVOIRS OF INFLUENZA HA-REACTIVE MBC POPULATIONS, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THESE POPULATIONS AS INDICATORS OF AN INDIVIDUALÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S INFLUENZA EXPOSURE HISTORY AND SOURCES OF MBCS THAT TRAFFIC TO RESPONDING LYMPHOID TISSUES ELSEWHERE IN THE BODY. A LARGE AND DIVERSE COLLECTION OF HUMAN LYMPHOID TISSUES ARE AVAILABLE TO US FOR THIS ANALYSIS. IN ADDITION, MOUSE MODELS WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY FACTORS INFLUENCING MBC DISPERSION, MOBILIZATION, AND TRAFFICKING TO RESPONDING AND NON-RESPONDING LYMPHOID TISSUES.

description: THE SCOPE OF THE WORK IS TO MEASURE NEUTRALIZATION ACTIVITY OF SERUM OBTAINED FROM NURSING HOME RESIDENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED COVID-19 VACCINES. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL UTILIZE AN EXTENSIVELY VALIDATED HIGH-THROUGHPUT MICRO-NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY TO OBTAINED PRECISE INHIBITORY CONCENTRATION MEASUREMENTS FOR EACH SAMPLE PROVIDED BY THE CONSORTIUM. THESE WILL BE PERFORMED IN DUPLICATE OR QUADRUPLICATE AS REQUIRED BY THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL CLONE, PRODUCE AND CHARACTERIZE PSEUDOVIRUS BEARING THE SPIKE PROTEIN ENCODED BY CURRENTLY ADMINISTERED SARS-COV-2 VACCINES. THEY WILL ALSO PRODUCE PSEUDOVIRUS HARBORING SARS-COV-2 VARIANT SPIKE PROTEINS, REPRESENTING STRAINS THAT ARE CURRENTLY CIRCULATING GLOBALLY. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ALSO CREATE NOVEL SARS-COV-2 PSEUDOVIRUSES ENCODING SPIKE PROTEINS BASED ON THE GENETIC SEQUENCE OBSERVED FOR THE S GENE IN BREAKTHROUGH INFECTIONS DETECTED IN VACCINATED NURSING HOME RESIDENTS AND USE THESE NOVEL REAGENTS TO DETERMINE THE INHIBITORY CONCENTRATION OF A SUBSET OF THE TOTAL SERUM SAMPLES AGAINST THESE NOVEL VARIANTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ANALYZE DATA OBTAINED DURING EXECUTION OF THIS WORK, AND PROVIDE THESE TO THE CONSORTIUM AS REQUESTED AND PARTICIPATE IN THE WRITING OF MANUSCRIPTS DESCRIBING THESE RESULTS.

description: UNDER CDC FUNDING OPPORTUNITY AND RESEARCH PROPOSAL, Ã¢Â‚¬Å“APPLIED RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THE CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) CONTINUED PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ DEVELOPING STRATEGIES FOR PROTECTION, PREVENTION & CONTROL IN COMMUNITIESÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½, A WHITE PAPER WAS SUBMITTED BY UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN - MADISON ALONG WITH OTHER PARTNERS INCLUDING CITY OF MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY (MHDL). AS PER PROPOSED RESEARCH, MHDL WILL PARTNER WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN - MILWAUKEE (UWM) TO CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS THE STUDY TO UNDERSTAND SPREAD OF SARS-COV-2 AMONG COLLEGE STUDENTS DURING ON CAMPUS CLASSES AND BETWEEN THEIR COMMUNITIES. IN COLLEGE SETTING, THERE ARE HIGHER RISKS OF THE SPREAD OF VIRUS AND WOULD LIKELY IMPACT POPULATION AT-LARGE. WHILE THIS STUDY ALLOW COLLABORATIONS WITH UW-MADISON AND UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, PARTNERING WITH UWM WILL BE CRITICAL IN UNDERSTANDING TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS OF SARS-COV-2 IN THE METRO-WITH ADVANCED GENOMIC SURVEILLANCE APPROACH. SAMPLES FROM UW-MILWAUKEE STUDENTS SEEN AT CAMPUS CLINIC, NORRIS HEALTH CENTER FOR EXPECTED TO THOSE SHOWING COVID-19 SYMPTOMS, KNOWN OR POTENTIALLY EXPOSED, ARE ROUTINELY SENT TO MHDL FOR DETECTION OF SARS-COV-2. DURING THE BAA STUDY PERIOD I AND II, UP TO 300 SAMPLES POSITIVE FOR SARS-COV-2 (CT VALUE ? 30) WILL COLLECTED TO COLLECTED TO BE SEQUENCED USING MINION (OXFORD NANOPORE TECHNOLOGIES) DEVICE FOR REAL-TIME SEQUENCING. THE CITY OF MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY HAS AN ESTABLISHED COLLABORATION TO SEQUENCE SARS-COV-2 GENOMES WITH DRS. OÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢CONNOR AND FRIEDRICH AT UW-MADISON. SPECIMENS FROM UW-MILWAUKEE STUDENTS AND GREATER MILWAUKEE AREA FOR SEQUENCING. EVENTUALLY ABOUT 900 SAMPLES WILL BE SEQUENCED AT THE MHDL. THE SAMPLING STRATEGY WILL ALLOW COLLECTING SAMPLES FROM HIGH RISK, OUTBREAKS, LTCF, HOT SPOTS AS WELL AS GENERAL POPULATION TESTING SITES TO ALLOW EVEN DISTRIBUTION OF SAMPLING FROM THE MILWAUKEE COUNTY.

description: OVER THE LAST TWO DECADES, THE MINING INDUSTRY HAS EXPERIENCED A SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION IN FATAL ACCIDENTS IN THE UNITED STATES (FIG. 1). WHILE ENCOURAGING, THESE STATISTICS ARE SOMEWHAT MISLEADING SINCE THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MINE WORKERS AND EMPLOYEE HOURS WORKED HAVE ALSO DECLINED OVER THIS PERIOD, ESPECIALLY IN THE COAL SECTOR (MSHA, 2019A). CONSEQUENTLY, THE OVERALL INCIDENCE RATE OF FATAL ACCIDENTS HAS REMAINED ESSENTIALLY UNCHANGED SINCE 2015 (FIG. 1). DESPITE THIS TREND, INDUSTRY AND GOVERNMENT HAVE SHOWN A SINCERE COMMITMENT TO ACTIVELY PROMOTE EFFORTS TO REDUCE THE INCIDENT RATES FOR FATALITIES AND NONFATAL LOST-TIME INJURIES BY IMPLEMENTING NEW INITIATIVES, PROCESSES, AND TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING ADVANCES IN SAFETY AND HEALTH MANAGEMENT AND DATA-DRIVEN DECISION MAKING. THE U.S. MINE SAFETY AND HEALTH ADMINISTRATION (MSHA) HAS INITIATED SEVERAL DIFFERENT STRATEGIES TO FACILITATE CONSTANT IMPROVEMENT IN OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH. MSHA SHARED AN EXTENSIVE DATABASE ON OPERATING MINES THROUGH THE OPEN-SOURCE GOVERNMENT INITIATIVE PORTAL, INCLUDING SECTOR AND MINE TYPE, FATALITIES/NON-FATAL-LOST-TIME INJURIES, MINE EMPLOYMENT/PRODUCTION, AND INSPECTION AND VIOLATION DATA. MSHA HAS ALSO PROPOSED SEVERAL TOOLS, BASED ON CITATION HISTORY, INCLUDING THE PATTERN OF VIOLATION (POV) MONITORING TOOL, AND SIGNIFICANT AND SUBSTANTIAL (S&S) CALCULATOR, TO ENCOURAGE MINING COMPANIES TO MONITOR THEIR SAFETY PERFORMANCE PROACTIVELY. THE LIMITATION OF THE POV TOOL HIGHLIGHTED IN PREVIOUS RESEARCH (KINILAKODI AND GRAYSON, 2011) IS THAT THE POV PROCESS DEPENDS ON THE DISPOSITION OF THE FINAL CITATION, WHICH IS COMPLEX TO CALCULATE WITH TEN COMPONENTS AND CHALLENGING TO IMPLEMENT. MOREOVER, THE POV PROVIDES A BINARY ANSWER (YES/NO), WHERE NO QUANTITATIVE VALUE IS PROVIDED. THEREFORE, IT IS DIFFICULT FOR MINE OPERATORS AND CONTRACTORS TO USE POV FOR RISK MANAGEMENT AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT RELATIVE TO REGULATORY COMPLIANCE. CONVERSELY, THE S&S CALCULATOR IS A STRAIGHTFORWARD METHOD, PROVIDES A QUANTITATIVE VALUE, AND IS SIMPLE TO CALCULATE. HOWEVER, IT ONLY USES TWO PARAMETERS (I.E., THE NUMBER OF S&S CITATIONS AND INSPECTION HOURS), IGNORING OTHER CITATIONS AND ORDERS. BOTH THE POV AND S&S APPROACHES PRIMARILY UTILIZE MSHA VIOLATION DATA AND ONLY PROVIDE A RELATIVE RISK BUT CANNOT IDENTIFY THE RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH ANY VIOLATION OR ACCIDENT. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL DEVELOP ROBUST MODELS TO IDENTIFY RISK FACTORS USING LEADING INDICATORS FROM LARGE MINING HEALTH AND SAFETY (H&S) DATA. ENABLING TECHNOLOGY MSHA OPEN DATA (HTTPS://ARLWEB.MSHA.GOV/OPENGOVERNMENTDATA/OGIMSHA.ASP) HAS A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF INFORMATION RELATED TO PRODUCTION (I.E., FOR COAL), EMPLOYMENT, AND INJURY AND FATALITY STATISTICS FOR EACH AND EVERY PERMITTED, ACTIVE MINE IN THE UNITED STATES. THE OPEN DATA ALSO HAS INFORMATION REGARDING ALL INSPECTIONS, CITATIONS, AND VIOLATIONS. MSHA AND THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH (NIOSH) ARE ENCOURAGING MINING COMPANIES TO USE THIS LARGE VOLUME OF DATA TO EVALUATE THEIR SAFETY TRENDS AND SPECIFIC RISK FACTORS TO MINIMIZE THE INCIDENCE OF INJURIES AND ACCIDENTS AT THEIR OPERATIONS. TRADITIONALLY, THE LOST TIME INJURY FREQUENCY RATES AND TOTAL RECORDABLE INJURY FREQUENCY RATES ARE WIDELY USED SAFETY INDICATORS; HOWEVER, THEY HAVE SEVERAL LIMITATIONS. THEY ARE RETROSPECTIVE INDICATORS (LAGGING INDICATORS) CAPTURING INCIDENTS THAT HAVE ALREADY GONE WRONG. THEY MEASURE THE ABSENCE RATHER THAN THE PRESENCE OF SAFETY (AREZES AND MIGUEL, 2003). THEREFORE, THEY CANNOT BE REGARDED AS A DIRECT MEASURE OF THE LEVEL OF SAFETY IN A WORK SYSTEM (LOFQUIST, 2010). MSHA OFFERS TWO LEADING INDICATOR TOOLS: POV MONITORING TOOL AND S&S CALCULATOR FOR MINING COMPANIES TO EVALUATE THEIR SAFETY TRENDS. description: THE WEST VIRGINIA TRAINING AND CONFERENCE CENTER (WVTCC) WILL HOST AND ASSIST IN THE FULL-SCALE TESTING OF THE SHUTTLE CAR NAVIGATION CONTROL ALGORITHM. THIS FACILITY, FORMERLY THE RUNNING RIGHT LEADERSHIP ACADEMY (RRLA), IS NOW PART OF THE WEST VIRGINIA OFFICE OF MINERSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ HEALTH, SAFETY, AND TRAINING (WVOMHST). THE WVTCC IS A STATE-OF-THE-ART FACILITY AND COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING GROUNDS FOR SAFETY AND OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE, LOCATED IN JULIAN, WV. CLASSROOM SPACE IS AVAILABLE FOR UP TO 580 PEOPLE AND THE FACILITY INCLUDES A SIMULATED MINE LAB WITH A 96,000 SQUARE-FOOT AREA TO PROVIDE REAL UNDERGROUND MINE SITUATIONS AND CONDITIONS. THE SIMULATED MINE LAB HAS AN OPERATIONAL CONTINUOUS MINER AND SHUTTLE CAR WITHIN IT THAT WILL BE USED IN THE TESTING. SPECIFICALLY, THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES SUPPORT OF TASKS 5 AND 6 AS OUTLINED IN THE TECHNICAL PROPOSAL. TASK 5: ACQUIRE AND INSTALL SENSORS ON A FULL-SCALE SHUTTLE CAR. THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY (UKY) WILL PURCHASE SENSORS FOR THIS TASK, BASED ON THE RESULTS OF THE PREVIOUS TASKS. PERSONNEL AT THE WVTCC WILL ASSIST IN DETERMINING THE OPTIMUM LOCATION FOR MOUNTING THE SENSORS AND ASSIST IN MOUNTING THE SENSORS ON OUR FULL-SCALE, FULLY OPERATIONAL SHUTTLE CAR. THE SENSORS WILL BE WIRED TO A PORTABLE COMPUTER (PROVIDED BY UKY) AND THE COMPUTER WILL BE TEMPORARILY MOUNTED ON THE SHUTTLE CAR. A DISPLAY WILL ALSO BE MOUNTED TEMPORARILY ON THE SHUTTLE CAR AT A LOCATION CONVENIENT FOR OUR SHUTTLE CAR OPERATOR TO SEE WHILE OPERATING THE SHUTTLE CAR. AFTER THE SENSORS ARE MOUNTED, WE WILL ASSIST UKY RESEARCHERS IN ACQUIRING IMAGES OF THE CONTINUOUS-MINER COAL-DISCHARGE CONVEYOR FROM VARIOUS VIEWPOINTS OF THE SHUTTLE CAR, E.G., FROM THE STRAIGHT, TURNING A CROSSCUT, ETC. OUR PERSONNEL WILL REPOSITION THE SHUTTLE CAR AND UKY PERSONNEL WILL CAPTURE IMAGES WITH THEIR EQUIPMENT TEMPORARILY MOUNTED ON THE SHUTTLE CAR. TASK 6: MODIFY POSITIONING ALGORITHM FOR FULL-SCALE SHUTTLE CAR AND TEST PERFORMANCE SPECIFIC POSITIONAL SITUATIONS WILL BE DEFINED, WITH WVTCC PERSONNEL ASSISTANCE, AND THE NAVIGATION SYSTEM PERFORMANCE WILL BE EVALUATED. THESE SITUATIONS WILL INCLUDE HAVING THE CONTINUOUS MINER (CM) POSITIONED AT A SUITABLE LOCATION IN AN ENTRY OR CROSSCUT WITHIN THE WVTCC SIMULATED MINE AND DETERMINING SUITABLE STARTING POINTS AND POSITIONS OF THE SHUTTLE CAR LOCATED NEAR THE CHANGE POINT. TESTING WILL CONSIST OF HAVING ONE OF THE WVTCC PERSONNEL OPERATING THE SHUTTLE CAR, FOLLOWING THE TRAJECTORY COMMANDS DISPLAYED ON THE MONITOR FOR TRAMMING THE SHUTTLE CAR TO THE DISCHARGE CONVEYOR OF THE CONTINUOUS MINER. WVTCC WILL PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON THE SUITABILITY AND ACCURACY OF THE TRAJECTORY COMMANDS. WVTCC PERSONNEL WILL ALSO PROVIDE ADVICE ON IMPROVING THE ALGORITHM PERFORMANCE.

description: TASK/PROJECT SCOPE: THE SCOPE OF THIS TASK IS TO MODEL IMMUNE RESPONSES TO INFLUENZA VACCINE IN A PREVIOUSLY UNVACCINATED INDIGENOUS POPULATION IN COLOMBIA AND DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE OF INFECTION BETWEEN VACCINATED AND NON-VACCINATED PEOPLE. DURING THE PREVIOUS CONTRACT PERIOD, WE ESTABLISHED A STRONG COLLABORATION WITH THE ARHUACO COMMUNITY AT NABUSIMAKE AND STAFFED A COMMUNITY FEVER CLINIC. THIS IS THE SOLE SOURCE OF MEDICAL CARE FOR THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY OF > 4,500 PEOPLE WITH 70 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ 100 PEOPLE PER MONTH SEEKING MEDICAL CARE DUE TO RESPIRATORY/FEBRILE ILLNESS. WE DEMONSTRATED THAT HUMAN (AND ANIMAL) INFLUENZA VIRUSES WERE CIRCULATING IN THE COMMUNITY AND IDENTIFIED AN INFLUENZA B OUTBREAK IN 2017 THAT RESULTED IN SIGNIFICANT MORTALITY, ESPECIALLY IN CHILDREN, FOLLOWED BY A MEASLES OUTBREAK. DUE TO THESE EVENTS, THE COMMUNITY REQUESTED THAT WE BEGIN OFFERING VACCINES PROVIDING AN OPPORTUNITY TO EVALUATE THE IMMUNE RESPONSES IN A PREVIOUSLY UNVACCINATED POPULATION OF CHILDREN AND ADULTS. IN RESPONSE, WE WILL ENROLL 100 PEOPLE EACH YEAR WHO WILL BE VACCINATED WITH SEASONAL TIV/QIV. BLOOD (VOLUME DEPENDENT ON AGE) WILL BE COLLECTED FROM EACH SUBJECT AT THE TIME OF VACCINATION (D0) AND COLLECTED AGAIN 21Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ28 DAYS (D28), AROUND DAY 90-120 (D90) AND 1-YEAR POST-VACCINATION. ENROLLEES WILL BE ASKED TO COME TO THE CLINIC IF THEY EXPERIENCE ILI. IF THEY MEET THE WHO DEFINITION OF ILI, NASAL AND THROAT SWABS WILL BE COLLECTED AND TESTED FOR INFLUENZA BY RAPID TEST OR QRT-PCR. THE PREVALENCE OF INFLUENZA VIRUS BETWEEN VACCINATED AND NON-VACCINATED PEOPLE CAN BE COMPARED. ALL SAMPLES HAVE BEEN AND WILL BE CONSENTED FOR BANKING, FUTURE USE AND DISTRIBUTION, TESTING FOR OTHER PATHOGENS AND GENETIC TESTING. A RISK FACTOR QUESTIONNAIRE WITH INFORMATION ON NUTRITIONAL STATUS, CONTACT WITH ANIMALS, UNDERLYING CO-MORBIDITIES, AND CONTACT WITH NON-INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS WILL ALSO BE COMPLETED. WE WILL HARMONIZE OUR STUDIES WITH HUMAN COHORT 4 (INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS IN AUSTRALIA) TO ALLOW THE RESULTS TO BE ANALYZED TOGETHER

description: TASK/PROJECT SCOPE: THE SCOPE OF THIS TASK IS TO UNDERSTAND MECHANISMS UNDERLYING DISEASE SEVERITY AND POOR VACCINE EFFICACY IN THE SOUTHERN HEMISPHERE TO INFORM RATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY BIOMARKERS FOR INFLUENZA DISEASE SEVERITY AND IMPROVED THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION FOR PATIENTS AT RISK OF DYING. TO ACHIEVE THIS, WE WILL RECRUIT PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED WITH INFLUENZA DISEASE IN OUR WELL-ESTABLISHED RESPIRATORY DISI COHORT (AIM 1) AND RECRUIT TOP END INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIANS INTO OUR WELL-ESTABLISHED LIFT/LIFT-V COHORTS AT A ROYAL DARWIN HOSPITAL AND A REMOTE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY IN THE NORTHERN TERRITORY (AIM 3). IN OUR DISI COHORT, WE WILL COLLECT LONGITUDINAL BLOOD SAMPLES AND NASAL SWABS IN PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED INFLUENZA-LIKE ILLNESS (ILI). INFLUENZA-POSITIVE PATIENTS ARE PCR-CONFIRMED, WHILE ILI INFLUENZA-NEGATIVE PATIENTS POSITIVE FOR OTHER RESPIRATORY DISEASES ARE TREATED AS CONTROLS. BLOODS ARE COLLECTED WITHIN 24-72 HOURS OF HOSPITAL ADMISSION (VISIT 1, V1), EVERY 2-5 DAYS UNTIL DISCHARGE (V2, V3, V4 ETC.), THEN FOLLOWED UP A30 DAYS LATER. OUR WELL-ESTABLISHED LIFT COHORT REPRESENTS ADULT INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIANS, EITHER HEALTHY DONORS OR PATIENTS WITH ILIS (LIFT), OR INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING SEASONAL INFLUENZA VACCINE (LIFT-V). WE HAVE LONGSTANDING RESEARCH RELATIONSHIPS WITH A REMOTE ABORIGINAL COMMUNITY, WHERE WE HAVE INVESTED IN CAPACITY BUILDING LOCAL COMMUNITY-BASED ABORIGINAL RESEARCH ASSISTANTS, INCLUDING 4 WHO HAVE COMPLETED A FORMAL CERTIFICATE 2 IN COMMUNITY-BASED RESEARCH THROUGH CHARLES DARWIN UNIVERSITY. THIS COMMUNITY WITH A POPULATION OF 2500-3000 IS A TWO-HOUR FLIGHT FROM DARWIN AND HAS A CLINIC, WHICH PROVIDES PRIMARY HEALTH CARE; UNWELL PATIENTS ARE EVACUATED TO ROYAL DARWIN HOSPITAL (RDH). WE WILL RECRUIT INTO 2 ARMS (1) HEALTHY INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIANS RECRUITED IN A REMOTE ABORIGINAL COMMUNITY; (2) HEALTHY INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIANS RECEIVING SEASONAL INFLUENZA VACCINATION RECRUITED IN A REMOTE ABORIGINAL COMMUNITY, AS ABOVE.. WE WILL HARMONIZE OUR STUDIES WITH HUMAN COHORT 5 (INDIGENOUS POPULATIONS IN COLUMBIA) SO THE RESULTS CAN BE ANALYZED TOGETHER.

description: INSIGHT GLOBAL (IG) IS A PREMIER PROVIDER OF EMPLOYMENT SOLUTIONS TO FORTUNE 1000 CUSTOMERS AND GOVERNMENT AGENCIES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR, IG CURRENTLY PROVIDES SUBCONTRACTING SERVICES, BOTH AS A PRE-AWARD TEAMMATE AND A POST-AWARD SUBCONTRACTOR, ON APPROXIMATELY 400 PROGRAMS WITHIN DEFENSE, INTELLIGENCE, CIVILIAN, AND PUBLIC HEALTH. INSIGHT GLOBAL HAS OVER 65 OFFICES AND 2,000 RECRUITERS NATIONWIDE, GIVING IG THE ABILITY TO LEVERAGE INTERNAL RESOURCES TO MEET LARGE SURGE DEMANDS WITH QUALIFIED CANDIDATES IN A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME. IG SUPPORTS A WIDE RANGE OF SKILLSETS THAT INCLUDE IT, ENGINEERING, FINANCE, HEALTH, AND LIFE SCIENCES, AND HAS A PROVEN TRACK RECORD OF DELIVERING ON EVEN THE MOST CHALLENGING POSITIONS. OUR FLEXIBLE SUBCONTRACTING OFFERINGS INCLUDE OUTSOURCED MANAGED SERVICES, SHORT TERM AND LONG-TERM CONTRACTING FOR BOTH CONUS AND OCONUS WORK. IN 2021 ALONE, INSIGHT GLOBAL MADE OVER 66,000 UNIQUE PLACEMENTS ACROSS DOZENS OF MARKETS. IG'S PROPOSAL SUPPORT INCLUDES SUPPLYING PAST PERFORMANCE DETAILS, ASSISTANCE WITH PRICING MODELS, AND DRAFTING STAFFING, RETENTION, AND TRANSITION RISK PLANS.

description: THE OVERALL SCOPE OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO TEST WHETHER COMBINATION TREATMENT WITH KRAS OR EGFR MULTIPEPTIDE VACCINES AND AEROSOLIZED CA-170 WILL IMPROVE IMMUNOPREVENTIVE EFFICACY OF THESE VACCINES AGAINST LUNG TUMOR PROGRESSION IN TRANSGENIC ANIMAL MODELS DRIVEN BY KRAS OR EGFR MUTATIONS, AND ASSESS IMMUNOLOGIC RESPONSES THAT CORRELATE WITH VACCINE EFFICACY. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE TO: 1. DETERMINE THE TOLERABILITY AND OPTIMUM DOSING REGIMEN OF AEROSOLIZED CA-170 IN WILD-TYPE MICE. BREED/EXPAND THE NECESSARY TRANSGENIC MOUSE COLONIES FOR OBJECTIVE 2. 2. DETERMINE IN VIVO EFFICACY OF KRAS OR EGFR VACCINE COMBINED WITH ORAL AND AEROSOLIZED CA-170 USING GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MOUSE MODELS (GEM) OF LUNG TUMORIGENESIS DRIVEN BY KRAS OR EGFR MUTATIONS. 3. EVALUATE THE IMMUNE RESPONSES TO EGFR OR KRAS VACCINE ADMINISTERED WITH OR WITHOUT CA-170 AND ESTABLISH IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION AGAINST LUNG TUMOR PROGRESSION.
