description: OPTION 16B THE GOAL OF THIS CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE FOR INFLUENZA RESEARCH AND RESPONSE (CEIRR) PROPOSAL IS TO GENERATE RECOMBINANT (R)SARS-COV-2 EXPRESSING DIFFERENT VIRAL SPIKE (S) GLYCOPROTEINS AND FLUORESCENT PROTEINS, USING OUR RECENTLY DESCRIBED BACTERIAL ARTIFICIAL CHROMOSOME (BAC)-BASED REVERSE GENETICS APPROACHES, TO DEVELOP A NOVEL MULTI-FLUORESCENT MICRONEUTRALIZATION ASSAY (MFMA) FOR THE RAPID, SENSITIVE, AND SIMULTANEOUS IDENTIFICATION OF NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODY (NAB) RESPONSES AGAINST SARS-COV-2, INCLUDING THOSE WITH BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ACTIVITY AGAINST RECENTLY IDENTIFIED VARIANTS OF CONCERN (VOC) WITHIN THE SAME WELL. THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THIS MFMA WILL REDUCE THE NUMBER OF SAMPLES AND TIME REQUIRED TO ASSESS NAB RESPONSES, INCLUDING THOSE IN SERA SAMPLES FROM SARS-COV-2 NATURALLY INFECTED OR VACCINATED INDIVIDUALS, AND HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (HMABS) AND, THEREFORE, FACILITATE THE IDENTIFICATION OF EFFECTIVE VACCINE APPROACHES AGAINST SARS-COV-2, INCLUDING CURRENT OR NEWLY IDENTIFIED VOC. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST TIME THAT A MFMA WILL BE USED TO SIMULTANEOUSLY ASSESS NABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2. TO THAT END, WE PROPOSE TO COMPLETE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1: WE WILL GENERATE BOTH WILD-TYPE (WT) AND FLUORESCENT RSARS-COV-2, INCLUDING SARS-COV-2 USA-WA1/2020 (WA-1), AND B.1.351 (SOUTH AFRICA), P.1. OR 20J/501Y.V3 (JAPAN), B.1427 (CALIFORNIA), AND B.1.617 (INDIA) VOC. EACH RSARS-COV-2 WILL BE DESIGNED TO EXPRESS A DIFFERENT VOC SPIKE (S) AND FLUORESCENT PROTEIN (AIM 1A). WE WILL NEXT CHARACTERIZE AND COMPARE WT AND FLUORESCENT RSARS-COV-2 EXPRESSING DIFFERENT VOC S PROTEINS BY GROWTH PROPERTIES IN VERO E6 (ATCC CRL-1586) AND CALU-3 (ATCC HTB-55) CELLS TO ASSESS WHETHER FLUORESCENT RSARS-COV-2 RETAIN VIRAL FITNESS IN CULTURED CELLS COMPATIBLE TO THOSE OF WT RSARS-COV-2, AND NATURAL VIRAL ISOLATES (AIM 1B). AIM 2: WE WILL DEMONSTRATE THAT OUR APPROACH PROVIDES A ROBUST AND REPRODUCIBLE SIGNAL OF SUFFICIENT INTENSITY THAT CAN BE EASILY MEASURED ABOVE BACKGROUND LEVELS DURING INDIVIDUAL INFECTION WITH DIFFERENT FLUORESCENT RSARS-COV-2 TO IDENTIFY NABS USING A COLLECTION OF WELL-CHARACTERIZED HMABS AVAILABLE IN OUR LABORATORY. INITIAL EXPERIMENTS WILL DETERMINE THE BEST ASSAY CONDITIONS BY OPTIMIZING MULTIPLICITY OF INFECTION (MOI), CELL DENSITY, AND DURATION OF THE ASSAY (AIM 2A). ONCE OPTIMIZED, WE WILL VALIDATE THE FEASIBILITY OF OUR MFMA FOR THE SIMULTANEOUS IDENTIFICATION OF STRAIN-SPECIFIC OR BROADLY NABS USING THE SAME COLLECTION OF HMABS (AIM 2B). TO FURTHER DEMONSTRATE THE FEASIBILITY OF USING OUR MFMA TO EVALUATE IMMUNE RESPONSES IN A COMPLEX COMBINATION OF NABS, WE WILL NEXT CHARACTERIZE A SELECTED PANEL OF CURRENTLY AVAILABLE HUMAN SERA SAMPLES FROM SARS-COV-2 NATURALLY INFECTED AND VACCINATED INDIVIDUALS AND COMPARE OUR RESULTS WITH THOSE OBTAINED USING OUR PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED MICRONEUTRALIZATION ASSAY (MNA) WITH INDIVIDUAL WT RSARS-COV-2 AND NATURAL VIRAL ISOLATES, INCLUDING WA-1 AND B.1.351, P.1., B.1427, AND B.1.617 VOC (AIM 2C). IN Y1, WE WILL GENERATE AND CHARACTERIZE THE FLUORESCENT RSARS-COV-2 WITH THE S PROTEIN OF CURRENT VOC (AIM 1). IN Y2, WE WILL DEVELOP THE RAPID AND FLEXIBLE MFMA FOR THE DETECTION OF NABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 VOC (AIM 2).

WE HAVE RECENTLY ESTABLISHED THAT IMMUNIZATION OF HUMANS WITH AN MRNA-BASED SARS-COV-2 VACCINE INDUCES A REMARKABLY ROBUST AND PERSISTENT GERMINAL CENTER (GC) B CELL RESPONSE. WE WILL INDEX SPIKE-SPECIFIC HUMAN B CELL RESPONSES BASED ON THEIR Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒNEUTRALIZATION BREADTHÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ AND COMPARE THE ORIGIN AND PERSISTENCE OF B CELL CLONES THAT ARE DIRECTED AGAINST CONSERVED VERSUS STRAIN-SPECIFIC EPITOPES. 2) COMPARE THE BREADTH AND DURABILITY OF RESPONSES TO HOMOLOGOUS VERSUS HETEROLOGOUS SARSCOV-2 BOOSTER IMMUNIZATIONS.

description: LUNA IS DEVELOPING A NANOSPRI (NANOENHANCED SURFACE PLASMON RESONANCE IMAGING)-BASED IMMUNOSENSING PLATFORM (TERMED AS MULTINANOSPRI) THAT CAN BE USED FOR MULTIPLEX DETECTION OF INFECTIOUS INDICATORS (I.E., REACTIVE ANTIBODY ISOTYPES IGG AND IGM, DNA/RNA NUCLEIC ACIDS AND BIOMARKERS) OF DENGUE, CHIKUNGUNYA AND ZIKA VIRUSES IN SERA FROM HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS AND INFECTED PATIENTS ON A SINGLE SENSING CHIP. SPECIFICALLY, THE PHASE II SUBCONTRACTING WORK INCLUDES (1) ANALYSES OF COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE SERUM SAMPLES USING EXISTING PCR- AND ELISA-BASED ASSAYS AND (2) SUBMISSION OF REPORT CONTAINING THE OBTAINED DATA TO LUNA. ALL SERUM SAMPLES NEEDED FOR THE ANALYSES WILL BE PROVIDED BY LUNA AND WILL BE SENT TO DR. JULANDER. THE ANALYSES WILL COVER 3 VIRUSES (CHIKV, ZIKV, DENV), 3 ASSAYS (RNA, IGG, AND IGM DETECTIONS) PER VIRUS, AND 25 SERUM SAMPLES PER ASSAY.

description: THE SCOPE OF THIS TASK IS TO COLLECT SAMPLES ON 140 CHILDREN (AGE <21 YEARS) WITH SEVERE INFLUENZA INFECTION (ADMITTED TO HOSPITAL) WHO ARE PREDOMINANTLY CRITICALLY ILL (ADMITTED TO IN THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT [ICU] OR STEPDOWN UNIT [SDU]) AND CONTROL PATIENTS WHO ARE CRITICALLY ILL BUT NOT INFECTED (N=30) AND PEDIATRIC CONTROLS IN THEIR USUAL STATE OF HEALTH ACROSS THE AGE RANGE (N=50; 10 EACH OF <1 YEAR, 1-4 YEARS, 5-12, 13-17, 18-21 YEARS). WE WILL ENROLL UP ~40 INFLUENZA INFECTED HOSPITALIZED CHILDREN PER YEAR TO MEET OUR TARGET ENROLLMENT, AND COLLECT BLOOD AND RESPIRATORY SAMPLES AT ENROLLMENT, ON HOSPITAL DAY 7Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ9 DAY (D7), AND AT 28-30 DAYS (D28/30) TO ASSESS THE SEROLOGICAL AND CELLULAR RESPONSES TO ACUTE ILLNESS; CYTOKINE LEVELS REFLECTING INFLAMMATION AND IMMUNITY; TRANSCRIPTOMICS, AND RESPIRATORY IMMUNE AND REPAIR RESPONSE. ALTHOUGH THESE CHILDREN WILL BE SEVERELY ILL, THE COHORT WILL HAVE A RANGE OF DISEASE SEVERITY. THIS PROJECT IS BEING CONDUCTED BY THE PICFLU NETWORK, A NETWORK OF INVESTIGATORS AT OVER 40 PEDIATRIC SITES WHO HAVE WORKED TOGETHER FOR OVER A DECADE TO ENROLL PATIENTS IN STUDIES TO UNDERSTAND THE EPIDEMIOLOGY AND IMMUNE RESPONSE OF INFLUENZA CRITICAL ILLNESS IN CHILDREN. ALL SAMPLES WILL BE SENT FROM THE SITES TO THE PICFLU NETWORK CORE LABORATORY AT BOSTON CHILDRENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S HOSPITAL, WHICH CURRENTLY HAS SAMPLES ON OVER 500 CHILDREN WITH INFLUENZA CRITICAL ILLNESS FROM SITES REPRESENTING EVERY U.S. REGION FROM PRIOR STUDIES FUNDED BY THE NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH (NIH) AND THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC). SAMPLES FROM THE EXISTING PICFLU BIOBANK WILL BE USED TO MEET THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS STUDY AND WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO CIDER CEIRR PARTICIPATING SITES TO MEET THE GOALS OF THE PROJECTS AS SPECIFIED.

description: "DR. SHEAHAN WILL SERVE AS SITE PI AT THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH CAROLINA, CHAPEL HILL AND WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PERFORMING THE EXPERIMENTS INVOLVING IN VITRO AND IN VIVO ASSESSMENTS OF THE ANTIVIRAL ACTIVITY OF PI-4-KINASE INHIBITORS PROVIDED BY THE GLENN LAB AGAINST SARS-COV-2, INCLUDING THE VARIOUS ISOLATES ROUTINELY RUN IN THE SHEAHAN LAB. THE IN VIVO ASSESSMENTS WILL USE THE MOUSE MODELS WITH WHICH DR. SHEAHAN HAS EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE, INCLUDING THOSE EMPLOYING MOUSE-ADAPTED AND HIGH PATHOGENICITY ISOLATES. VARIOUS BLOOD AND TISSUE SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE COLLECTED AND PROCESSED TO THE POINT WHERE THEY CAN BE SAFELY SHIPPED TO STANFORD UNIVERSITY SO THAT THE GLENN LAB CAN PERFORM MASS SPECTROMETRY ANALYSIS OF THE LEVELS OF COMPOUNDS AND METABOLITES. DR. SHEAHAN WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN REGULARLY SCHEDULED VIDEOCONFERENCES WITH THE GLENN LAB. TECHNICAL JUSTIFICATION DRS. SHEAHAN AND GLENN HAVE PRODUCTIVELY COLLABORATED ON SARS-COV-2, INCLUDING THE RECENT TESTING OF INTERFERON LAMBDA IN THE MOUSE-ADAPTED MODEL. THE SUBCONTRACT WILL ENABLE THIS TESTING AGAINST SARS-COV-2 AS PART OF TASK 1. DR. SHEAHAN IS UNIQUELY QUALIFIED IN ELUCIDATING VIRUS-HOST BIOLOGY THAT FORMS THE BASIS OF NEW TARGETS FOR ANTIVIRALS DEVELOPMENT. HE HAS EXTENSIVE KNOWLEDGE OF CORONAVIRUS (COV) MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, PATHOGENESIS, VACCINOLOGY, AND ANIMAL MODEL DEVELOPMENT WITHIN WHICH TO EVALUATE THERAPEUTICS THROUGH HIS GRADUATE RESEARCH AT UNC CHAPEL HILL WITH DR. RALPH S. BARIC, THE WORLD AUTHORITY ON CORONAVIRUS BIOLOGY. UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF DR. CHARLES M. RICE AT THE ROCKEFELLER UNIVERSITY, HIS POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCH FOCUSED ON THE CREATION OF SINGLE CELL SYSTEMS TO BETTER, UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS GUIDING HEPATITIS C VIRUS (HCV) CHRONIC INFECTION. SINCE BECOMING A FACULTY MEMBER AT UNC CHAPEL HILL IN THE DEPARTMENT OF EPIDEMIOLOGY, HIS RESEARCH HAS FOCUSED ON COV BIOLOGY WITH THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF DEVELOPING EFFECTIVE VACCINES AND THERAPEUTICS THAT CAN COMBAT CURRENT AND FUTURE PANDEMICS. THROUGH A PARTNERSHIP R01 (PI SHEAHAN/BARIC) AWARDED IN 2016, HE HAS BEEN WORKING WITH GILEAD SCIENCES AND VANDERBILT SCHOOL OF MEDICINE TO ACCELERATE THE PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT OF THE BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIVIRAL, REMDESIVIR, TO TREAT MERS-COV AND RELATED COVS, NOW THE 1ST APPROVED SARS-COV-2 DIRECTED THERAPEUTIC. DURING HIS TIME AT THE ANTIVIRAL DISCOVERY PERFORMANCE UNIT AT GLAXOSMITHKLINE (GSK) BASED IN RESEARCH TRIANGLE PARK, HE WAS PART OF AN INVESTIGATIVE TEAM FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING HOST TARGETING SMALL MOLECULES ANTIVIRALS. THIS COLLABORATIVE EFFORT WITH DR. JEFFREY GLENN AT STANFORD IS AN IDEAL TYPE OF COLLABORATION, WITH INITIAL EXCITING DATA SHOWING ITS THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL AGAINST SARS-COV-2. HIS LAB IS WELL SUITED TO PERFORM ALL THE PRECLINICAL STUDIES INCLUDING ANIMAL STUDY FOR SARS-COV-2 AND COVID-19 DISEASE."

description: WE ARE PROVIDING RNA VACCINES NECESSARY TO SUPPORT MT. SINAIÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S STUDIES OF THE CHIMERIC HEMAGGLUTININ (CHA) VACCINATION STRATEGY TO ACHIEVE BROAD PROTECTION AGAINST INFLUENZA INFECTION. TIBAÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CONTRIBUTION WILL BE THE DESIGN, PRODUCTION, INITIAL TESTING, AND FINAL DELIVERY OF SUFFICIENT QUANTITIES OF THE NECESSARY RNA FORMULATIONS FOR ADMINISTRATION TO MICE FOR IN-DEPTH STUDY AT MT. SINAI. THE MH10/3, MH14/3, CH4/3, AND CH15/3 HA AMINO ACID SEQUENCES PROVIDED BY MOUNT SINAI WILL BE CODON-OPTIMIZED AND CLONED INTO THE SUBGENOMIC ORF REGIONS OF TIBAÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S VEEV-BASED REPLICON VECTORS. RNA WILL BE MANUFACTURED BY IN VITRO TRANSCRIPTION AND ENZYMATIC CAPPING TO GENERATE 5Ã¢Â‚¬Â„¢ M7GPPPNM-CAPPED TRANSCRIPTS. BHK AND 293T CELLS WILL BE TRANSFECTED WITH THE RNAS PRODUCED FROM THESE VECTORS TO TEST FOR TRANSLATION OF EACH ANTIGEN AND CONFIRM EQUIVALENT EXPRESSION EFFICIENCY ACROSS CONSTRUCTS. EXPRESSION OF EACH ANTIGEN WILL BE MEASURED BY SURFACE STAINING AND WESTERN BLOT. EACH VALIDATED RNA WILL BE FORMULATED BY MICROFLUIDIC IN-LINE MIXTURE WITH TIBAÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PROPRIETARY IONIZABLE ALKYL-MODIFIED DENDRIMER DELIVERY MATERIAL, TESTING VARIOUS CONDITIONS AT SMALL SCALE (VARYING N:P RATIO, FLOW RATE) IN ORDER TO OPTIMIZE FOR THE GENERATION OF MONODISPERSE, SPHERICAL LAMELLAR NANOPARTICLES ~100-150 NM IN DIAMETER. PARTICLE QUALITY WILL BE ASSESSED BY DYNAMIC LIGHT SCATTERING, AND RNA ENCAPSULATION EFFICIENCY WILL BE EVALUATED BY RIBOGREENÃ‚Â® DYE EXCLUSION ASSAY. VACCINE LOTS WILL BE PROVIDED TO DR. FLORIAN KRAMMERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY TO COMPLETE NECESSARY STUDIES, GROUPS OF MICE (N=10 PER GROUP) WILL RECEIVE A SERIES OF 2 IMMUNIZATIONS, 3 WEEKS APART (DELIVERY ROUTE TO BE FINALIZED) WITH 2 Ã‚ÂΜG OF RNA. THIS DOSE WAS PREVIOUSLY SHOWN IN BENCHMARKING EXPERIMENTS USING THE A/CALIFORNIA/04/09 STRAIN TO INDUCE BOTH ROBUST HEMAGGLUTINATION INHIBITION (HI) TITERS AND T CELL RESPONSES IN BALB/C MICE. IMMUNOLOGICAL ASSAYS WILL CONFIRM ANTIBODY RESPONSES AGAINST THE FOUR CONSTRUCTS ABOVE DELIVERED BY TIBA BIOTECH. THE STUDY DESIGN OUTLINED BELOW WILL REQUIRE 20 Ã‚ÂΜG OF EACH VACCINE, WHICH REPRESENTS A SMALL-SCALE PRODUCTION RUN. 80 Ã‚ÂΜG MINIMUM OF TOTAL VACCINE WILL BE SHIPPED FOR THIS FIRST STUDY. THE SECOND AIM OF THE PROPOSED STUDY PERIOD IS TO EXAMINE THE ABILITY OF THE IMMUNITY INDUCED BY THE VARIOUS VACCINES TO CONFER PROTECTION AGAINST LETHAL CHALLENGE WITH INFLUENZA VIRUSES IN VIVO. THE VALIDATED CONSTRUCTS PRODUCED AND TESTED AT TIBA BIOTECH AS DESCRIBED ABOVE WILL BE MANUFACTURED AT DOUBLE THE ABOVE SCALE, TO PROVIDE 40 Ã‚ÂΜG OF EACH VACCINE MINIMUM. THIS IS TO ACCOUNT FOR EACH STUDY GROUP ABOVE BEING PERFORMED IN QUADRUPLICATE, AT N = 5. description: THIS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT (R&D) CONTRACT WAS AWARDED AS PART OF THE MULTIPLE-AWARD INDEFINITE DELIVERY, INDEFINITE QUANTITY (IDIQ) CONTRACTS FOR THE CONTRACEPTIVE CLINICAL TRIALS NETWORK (CCTN) FEMALE SITES. THE PURPOSE OF THESE CONTRACTS IS TO ESTABLISH A NETWORK OF CLINICAL RESEARCH SITES COLLABORATING TO EVALUATE NEW FEMALE CONTRACEPTIVE DRUGS AND DEVICES FOR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN PHASE I, II, III AND IV CLINICAL TRIALS. THIS CONTRACT SHALL PROVIDE THE REQUISITE PERSONNEL, FACILITIES AND SERVICES TO CONDUCT AND SUPPORT THESE CLINICAL TRIALS. THE DATA COLLECTED FROM THE CCTN THROUGH CLINICAL TRIALS ON NEW ENTITIES ARE THE BASIS FOR ADVANCING CANDIDATE DRUGS AND DEVICES THROUGH DEVELOPMENT WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF SUBMISSION TO THE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) IN SUPPORT OF REGULATORY APPROVAL. PRODUCTS EVALUATED IN THE CCTN ARE SELECTED TO ADDRESS GAPS IN AVAILABLE CONTRACEPTIVE TECHNOLOGY, INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SAFER, MORE ACCEPTABLE, AND MORE ACCESSIBLE CONTRACEPTIVE METHODS FOR WOMEN, INCLUDING WOMEN WHO ARE OBESE OR HAVE OTHER RISK FACTORS THAT LIMIT THEIR USE OF EXISTING METHODS.

description: DRS. POLLACK AND HUGHES HAVE EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN RESEARCH WITH MSM, PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV, AND HIV PREVENTION. THEY HAVE BEEN INVOLVED IN PREVIOUS EFFORTS TO DESIGN STUDIES OF THE ACCEPTABILITY OF DIFFERENT QUESTION-BASED STRATEGIES FOR BLOOD DONOR SELECTION FROM SELF-REPORTED BEHAVIOR, AND OTHER SURVEYS OF DONOR COMPLIANCE WITH DEFERRAL CRITERIA. IN GENERAL, THEY WILL SERVE AS CONSULTANTS TO THE ADVANCE STUDY TEAM AROUND ISSUES OF DATA COLLECTION, ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION. DR. POLLACK WILL DEVELOP A STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN (SAP) FOR THE SURVEY RESPONSES FROM THE ELIGIBILITY SURVEY, ADVANCE STUDY QUESTIONNAIRE, AND FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONNAIRE BASED ON BIOMARKER TEST RESULTS FOR HIV AND PREP. THE SAP WILL BE PROVIDED TO THE FDA AND DR. POLLACK WILL HELP IN ADDRESSING COMMENTS ON THE SAP FROM THE FDA AND OTHER MEMBERS OF THE ADVANCE STUDY TEAM. IN ADDITION, DR. POLLACK WILL CONSULT WITH THE VRI TEAM ON THE DESIGN OF DATA COLLECTION MONITORING REPORTS. AS DATA COLLECTION OCCURS, HE WILL WORK WITH PERSONNEL AT VRI TO REVIEW SUMMARY REPORTS FOCUSED ON QUALITY CONTROL OF THE DATA AND EXECUTE ANALYTICS. HE WILL ATTEND STANDING OPERATIONAL STUDY MEETINGS AS POSSIBLE, PROVIDE PERIODIC BRIEFINGS ON ANALYTICAL PROGRESS (AS NEEDED), AND CONSULT ON ACTIVITIES RELATED TO DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH FINDINGS. DR. HUGHES WILL PROVIDE INTERPRETATION OF FINDINGS BASED ON HER EXPERTISE IN BEHAVIORAL RESEARCH, WITH A PARTICULAR FOCUS ON RESPONSES FROM THE ADVANCE STUDY QUESTIONS AND FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONNAIRE FOR STUDY PARTICIPANTS WHOSE BLOOD SAMPLES TEST POSITIVE FOR HIV OR PREP.

description: OPTION 2 OBJECTIVE: EVALUATE IMMUNOGENICITY AND SAFETY OF LEAD CANDIDATE FORMULATION IN NHPS. SAFETY EVALUATION FOR A COMBINATION TLR LIGAND AND INTRANASAL ROUTE OF DELIVERY IS OF PRIME IMPORTANCE. GIVEN THAT TLR EXPRESSION AS WELL AS NASAL ANATOMY WIDELY VARIES BETWEEN ANIMAL MODELS, IT IS IMPORTANT TO EVALUATE IMMUNOGENICITY AND SAFETY IN THE RHESUS MACAQUE MODEL WHICH HAS THE CLOSEST KNOWN TLR EXPRESSION TO HUMANS AS WELL AS RELEVANT NASAL ANATOMY (1, 2). NOTABLY, THE TLR7/8 LIGAND R848 WAS FOUND TO BE THE MOST EFFECTIVE INTRANASAL ADJUVANT MOLECULE AMONG A VARIETY OF TLR LIGANDS SCREENED FOR ENHANCING ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC IGA AND IGG RESPONSES IN RHESUS MACAQUES (3). THUS, EVALUATION IN RHESUS MACAQUES WILL SEEK TO DETERMINE NECESSITY OF INCLUDING BOTH TLR LIGANDS, REFINE ANTIGEN AND ADJUVANT DOSES, AND EVALUATE SAFETY USING THE LMA MAD NASAL SPRAY TIP. TASK 2.1. PILOT STUDY FOR ANTIGEN DOSE OPTIMIZATION IN NHPS TASK 2.2. EVALUATION OF IMMUNOGENICITY, SAFETY, AND ADJUVANT DOSE IN NHPS IMMUNIZED WITH LEAD FORMULATION VIA NASAL SPRAY.

description: TASK 1 THE EMORY SUBCONTRACT PI AND OR HIS SURROGATES WILL JOIN MEETINGS AND PROVIDE PERSPECTIVE / CONSULTATION ON TASK 1 IMPACTS AND APPLICATIONS TO TASK 3 AND VICE VERSA TO ENSURE CONTINUITY BETWEEN ALL TASKSÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ TASK 2 THE EMORY SUBCONTRACT PI AND OR HIS SURROGATES WILL JOIN MEETINGS AND PROVIDE PERSPECTIVE / CONSULTATION ON TASK 1 IMPACTS AND APPLICATIONS TO TASK 3 AND VICE VERSA TO ENSURE CONTINUITY BETWEEN ALL TASKSÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ TASK 3: EVALUATE PERFORMANCE OF CELL THERAPY PRODUCTS USING IN VIVO MODEL OF OA. EVALUATING THE IN VIVO PERFORMANCE OF ALL CELL THERAPY PRODUCTS INCLUDED IN THIS PROPOSAL ARE LIMITED TO UCT-MSCS AND BMAC-DERIVED MSCS. UNLIKE BMAC THAT ARE COMPRISED OF SEVERAL CELL TYPES THAT EXPRESS HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGENS (HLAS) THAT MAY BE DETRIMENTAL BY CAUSING GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE AND/OR CONFOUND RESULTS, BMAC-DERIVED MSCS ARE KNOWN TO BE IMMUNE EVASIVE, THUS NOT GENERATING IMMUNE RECOGNITION RESPONSES, DUE TO THEIR LACK OR LOW EXPRESSION OF HLAS ON THEIR SURFACE. BY USING A RAT MODEL OF OA, CALLED THE MEDIAL MENISCAL TRANSECTION (MMT) MODEL, DAMAGE TO THE KNEE, ENSUING PATHOLOGIES, AND MEASURABLE OUTCOMES OF PAIN, FUNCTION, AND HISTOLOGY CAN OPTIMALLY REPRESENT OA IN HUMANS. THE RESULTS COLLECTED FOR THIS TASK WILL CORRELATE AS OUTPUTS/PERFORMANCE THAT WILL BE USED FOR COMPUTATIONAL PREDICTIVE MODELING IN TASK 1.2. GENERAL METHODS: MEDIAL MENISCAL TRANSECTION SURGERY: SURGERY WILL BE PERFORMED ACCORDING TO PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED METHODS BRIEFLY, 12-WEEK OLD MALE LEWIS RATS WILL BE ANESTHETIZED WITH ISOFLURANE. BILATERAL PROCEDURES WILL BE PERFORMED ON THE HINDLIMBS. AN INCISION WILL BE MADE IN THE SKIN OF THE LEFT KNEE AND THE MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT WILL BE EXPOSED AND TRANSECTED. FOR MMT, THE MENISCUS WILL BE CUT THROUGH THE FULL THICKNESS AT ITS NARROWEST POINT. THE JOINT WILL BE IRRIGATED WITH NORMAL SALINE, THE CAPSULE SUTURED WITH 4-0 VICRYL, AND THE SKIN CLOSED WITH WOUND CLIPS. SHAM ANIMAL UNDERGOES IDENTICAL SURGICAL MANIPULATION AS AN MMT ANIMAL EXCEPT THE MENISCUS IS NOT TRANSECTED. CELL INJECTIONS: INTRA-ARTICULAR INJECTIONS OF CELLS WILL BE PERFORMED AT 3 WEEKS POST-SURGERY, A STANDARD TIME POINT IN THE MMT MODEL CORRESPONDING TO THE PRESENTATION OF OA-ASSOCIATED PHENOTYPICAL CARTILAGE DEGENERATION. ALL INTRA-ARTICULAR INJECTIONS WILL BE PERFORMED USING A 25-GAUGE NEEDLE. CELL GROUPS AS DESCRIBED ABOVE WILL BE SUSPENDED IN HANKS BALANCED SALT SOLUTION AND 106 CELLS IN A 50Ã‚ÂΜL VOLUME WILL BE INJECTED INTRA-ARTICULARLY. INJECTIONS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO THE ANIMALS AND EACH ANIMAL WILL RECEIVE ONE TREATMENT PER KNEE. TACTILE ALLODYNIA MEASUREMENTS USING VON FREY FILAMENTS: TACTILE ALLODYNIA MEASUREMENTS WILL BE MADE USING VON FREY FILAMENTS ACCORDING TO PUBLISHED PROTOCOLS AND OTHER GROUPS WITH ESTABLISHED PROCEDURES IN THE MMT MODEL. BRIEFLY VON FREY FILAMENTS (STOELTING, WOOD DALE, IL, USA) WILL BE APPLIED THROUGH A WIRE CAGE TO THE PLANTAR SURFACE OF THE RATS' HINDPAWS. THE SMALLEST FILAMENT TO INDUCE WITHDRAWAL WILL BE RECORDED FOR THE PAW WITHDRAWAL THRESHOLD MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS SUGGESTIVE OF PAIN SENSITIVITY. EPIC-Ã‚ÂΜCT ANALYSIS: TO ASSESS THE STAGE AND SEVERITY OF OA, WE WILL CONDUCT EPIC-Ã‚ÂΜCT STUDIES ON THE SAME ANIMALS USED FOR NIR STUDIES (FOR BOTH). EPIC-Ã‚ÂΜCT IS A NON-DESTRUCTIVE TECHNIQUE AND THE SAME SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE USED FOR HISTOLOGY. AT DESIGNATED TIMEPOINTS, THE HINDLIMBS WILL BE HARVESTED AND FIXED IN 10% NEUTRAL BUFFERED FORMALIN. TIBIAE WILL BE DISSECTED FREE AND PREPARED FOR EPIC-Ã‚ÂΜCT ANALYSIS. BRIEFLY, TIBIAE WILL BE IMMERSED IN 2ML OF 30% HEXABRIXÃ¢Â€ŽÂ¢ 320 CONTRAST AGENT (COVIDIEN, HAZELWOOD, MO) AND 70% PBS AT 37Ã‚Â°C FOR 30 MINUTES. SAMPLES WILL THEN BE SCANNED USING A Ã‚ÂΜCT 40 (SCANCO MEDICAL, BRÃƑÂ¼TTISELLEN, SWITZERLAND) AT 45K VP, 177 Ã‚ÂΜA, 200 MS INTEGRATION TIME, AND A VOXEL SIZE OF 16 Ã‚ÂΜM. CORONAL SECTIONS OF THE CARTILAGE WILL BE CONTOURED AND THRESHOLDED WITH GLOBAL SEGMENTATION PARAMETERS. OUTCOME MEASURES WILL INCLUDE AVERAGE ARTICULAR CARTILAGE THICKNESS, VOLUME AND ATTENUATION.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK SARS-COV-2 B CELL EPITOPE MAPPING SUPPLEMENT (WILSON) SUBCONTRACT TO THE SUPPLEMENT FOR: NIAID CONTRACT 75N93019C00062 (FREEMONT, PI, PD) B CELL MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF PROTECTION FROM SARS-COV-2 PATRICK C. WILSON, SUBCONTRACT PI DEPARTMENT OF MEDICINE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO CHICAGO IL 60637 E-MAIL: WILSONP@UCHICAGO.EDU Ã¢Â‚¬Æ’ STATEMENT OF WORK CORONAVIRUSES ARE ENVELOPED NON-SEGMENTED POSITIVE-SENSE RNA VIRUSES BELONGING TO THE FAMILY CORONAVIRIDAE AND CIRCULATE BROADLY AMONGST AND BETWEEN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS. OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, TWO BETACORONAVIRUSES, SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (SARS-COV) AND MIDDLE EAST RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (MERS-COV), WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVER 10,000 CASES OF INFECTION. THE MORTALITY RATE OF SARS-COV WAS 10% WITH 29 COUNTRIES AFFECTED, AND THE MORTALITY RATE OF MERS WAS 35% WITH 27 COUNTRIES AFFECTED GLOBALLY. IN DECEMBER OF 2019, A NOVEL CORONAVIRUS (2019-NCOV) WAS DISCOVERED THROUGH DEEP SEQUENCING ANALYSIS AFTER A SERIES OF PNEUMONIA CASES WERE REPORTED IN WUHAN, HUBEI, CHINA WITH UNKNOWN VIRAL ORIGIN. SEVERAL INDEPENDENT STUDIES HAVE SINCE CONFIRMED THAT THE NOVEL VIRUS ORIGINATED FROM EXPOSURES IN A WUHAN SEAFOOD MARKET. BY ONLY MARCH 16, 2020, 2019-NCOV CAUSED A PANDEMIC SPANNING MOST COUNTRIES ON EARTH WITH A REPORTED 167,000 PEOPLE INFECTED WORLDWIDE, AND ALMOST 7000 CONFIRMED DEATHS. CASE AND MORTALITY RATES ARE CONTINUING TO RISE AND THE LACK OF ADEQUATE TESTING IN MAJOR POPULATION CENTERS PLUS CLEAR EVIDENCE OF COMMUNITY TRANSMISSIONS SUGGESTS THAT THE NUMBER OF INFECTED IS LIKELY SIGNIFICANTLY GREATER. MOREOVER, AS THE VIRUS CONTINUES TO SPREAD, ITS HIGH MUTATION RATE INTRODUCES THE THREAT OF INFECTIONS WITH NEW VARIANTS WHICH COULD HAVE ALTERED SEVERITY AND TRANSMISSIBILITY. THESE OCCURRENCES NECESSITATE THE URGENCY OF NOVEL PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC MEASURES TO HELP PREVENT THE SPREAD OF NCOV-2019, WHICH POSES ONE OF THE GREATEST GLOBAL HEALTH THREATS IN MODERN HISTORY. MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MAB) ARE MONOVALENT PROTEINS EXPRESSED BY B CELLS THAT CAN SPECIFICALLY TARGET 3-DIMENSIONAL VIRAL EPITOPES, LEADING TO POTENT VIRAL NEUTRALIZATION. MABS HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED MODERN MEDICINE BY PROVIDING PRECISION MEDICINE AGAINST MANY DISEASES, WITH OVER 70 MAB-BASED DRUGS APPROVED BY THE FDA. THE ISOLATION OF HUMAN MABS SPECIFIC FOR HIGHLY IMMUNOGENIC NCOV-2019 PROTEINS CAN BE RAPIDLY USED AS THERAPEUTIC AGENTS, FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS, AND FOR TEMPLATING THE GENERATION OF VACCINES THAT CAN PROTECT AGAINST NCOV-2019. OUR LABORATORY IS HIGHLY SPECIALIZED IN THE RAPID GENERATION OF NEUTRALIZING MABS FROM HUMAN B CELLS. WE AIM TO APPLY THIS EXPERTISE TO GENERATE HUMAN NCOV-2019-SPECIFIC MABS, WHICH HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RAPIDLY ALLEVIATE THE GLOBAL HEALTH BURDEN IMPOSED BY NCOV-2019 THROUGH THREE CRITICAL MEASURES: PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC. BY INVESTIGATING THE HUMAN ANTIBODY RESPONSE TO NCOV-2019, WE WILL GAIN IMPORTANT INSIGHT INTO THE IMMUNOGENICITY AND IMMUNODOMINANCE OF NCOV-2019 VIRAL PROTEINS, WHICH WILL IN TURN INFORM WHICH VIRAL TARGETS WILL BE MOST IMPORTANT TO PURSUE WITH THERAPEUTICS AND VACCINES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROPOSED SUPPLEMENT ARE AS FOLLOWS: A) GENERATE PANELS OF HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS. COVID-19 PATIENT BLOOD WILL BE OBTAINED FROM SEVERAL SOURCES INCLUDING VERIFIED INFECTED SAMPLES FROM TOKYO THROUGH COLLABORATOR YOSHI KAWAOKA, THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO OR OTHER HOSPITALS FROM COVID-19 ADMITTED PATIENTS, OR THROUGH OTHER COLLABORATING LABS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 SPIKE PROTEIN, SPIKE RBD AND ORF7 FROM DAVED FREEMONTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, VERSIONS OF THE SPIKE PROTEIN AND RBD FROM FLORIAN KRAMMERS LABORATORY, PLUS NSP3, NSP5, NSP9, NSP10, NSP15, NSP16, AND N PROTEIN FROM ANDRJEZ JOACHIMIACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, OR TO UNBIASED OTHER EPITOPES TARGETED BY ACTIVATED B CELLS AND PLASMABLASTS WILL BE DEVELOPED BY PATRICK WILSONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE RICKETTS BIOCONTAINMENT LABORATORY ON THE ARGONNE NATIONAL LABS CAMPUS AND AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO. B) EVALUATE THE B CELL RESPONSE OF COVID-19 PATIENTS: THE WILSON LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO WILL CHARACTERIZE PERIPHERAL BLOOD B CELLS REACTIVE TO SARS-COV-2 ENCODED PROTEINS OR ACTIVATED DURING INFECTION PLUS TFH CELLS USING SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOME AND CITE-SEQ ANALYSIS ON THE 10XGENOMICS PLATFORM. FROM THIS WE WILL LEARN ABOUT THE UNDERLYING IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THIS NOVEL CORONAVIRUS AND CORRELATE IMMUNE ACTIVITIES TO SERUM AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY PROTECTION, INFORMING FUTURE VACCINE-DESIGN AND EVALUATION EFFORTS. C) EVALUATE SERUM REACTIVITY TO A PANEL OF SARS-COV-2 PROTEINS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL BE VALUABLE AS POSSIBLE THERAPEUTIC AGENTS OR FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL ALSO GUIDE AND TEMPLATE THE GENERATION OF VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST COVID-19. THIS CONTRACT SUPPLEMENT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. WE WILL DEVELOP A DATABASE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO AND AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY THAT CATALOGS THE DATA GENERATED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY VARIOUS MAPPING STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. FREMONT AND COLLEAGUES AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY WILL MIRROR THIS DATA AS WELL AS PROGRESS OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY EXPERIMENTS OF THE ANTIBODY-ANTIGEN COMPLEXES. description: TITLE: EVALUATING HOSPITAL-ONSET BACTEREMIA (HOB) AND FUNGEMIA AS PREVENTABLE HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS 1. BACKGROUND AND NEED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (BSIS) ARE A SERIOUS AND LIFE THREATENING INFECTION. FOR THE PURPOSES OF TRACKING HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS (HAIS), MOST ATTENTION HAS BEEN PAID TO CENTRAL-LINE ASSOCIATED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (CLABSIS). PREVENTION OF CLABSIS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE FEASIBLE VIA WELL-STUDIED BUNDLES OF CARE RELATED TO CATHETER INSERTION AND MAINTENANCE. HOWEVER, TRACKING CLABSIS IS DIFFICULT, TIME CONSUMING AND HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE SUBJECTIVE WITH SUBSTANTIAL INTERRATER VARIABILITY. RESEARCHERS IN THE UNITED STATES HAVE BEGUN TO EVALUATE THE UTILITY OF TRACKING HOSPITAL-ONSET BACTEREMIA AND FUNGEMIA (HOB) AS A RELEVANT HAI OUTCOME IN LIEU OF CLABSI. HOB COMPRISES ALL POSITIVE BLOOD CULTURES TAKEN AT LEAST 48 HOURS POST ADMISSION TO THE HOSPITAL. THUS, IT INCLUDES CLABSIS AND NON-CENTRAL LINE ASSOCIATED BSIS THAT PRESUMABLY OCCURRED WITHIN THE HOSPITAL INITIAL HOB STUDIES IN THE UNITED STATES HAVE SHOWN THAT CLABSIS COMPRISE LESS THAN 20% OF TOTAL HOBS LEADING TO QUESTIONS OF WHETHER THESE NON-CLABSI HOBS REPRESENT PREVENTABLE INFECTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT HOB MAY ALSO BE A REASONABLE PROXY FOR CLABSI RATES. SEVERAL STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT HOB RATES TRACKED WELL WITH CLABSI RATES WHEN BOTH WERE MEASURED SIMULTANEOUSLY AND IN ONE STUDY HOB RATES TRENDED DOWNWARDS PROPORTIONALLY WITH CLABSI RATE DECREASES AFTER A CLABSI INTERVENTION WAS IMPLEMENTED. THESE DATA SUGGEST THAT A HEALTHCARE FACILITY MAY BE ABLE TO EXPEND LESS RESOURCES FOLLOWING HOB AND STILL DETECT CLABSI DECREASES WHEN IMPLEMENTING TARGETED PREVENTION BUNDLES. ONGOING WORK TO DETERMINE THE ETIOLOGY AND PREVENTABILITY OF HOB IS UNDERWAY AS WELL; PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGESTS THAT POTENTIALLY HALF OF HOB EVENTS MIGHT BE AVOIDABLE WITH KNOWN INTERVENTIONS. IN LOW AND MIDDLE-INCOME (LMIC) COUNTRIES WHERE BOTH HUMAN AND MONETARY RESOURCES ARE LIMITED AND EPIDEMIOLOGY OF HAI INFECTIONS HAVE BEEN STUDIED LESS ROBUSTLY, USING HOB AS A HAI METRIC HAS SEVERAL POTENTIAL ADVANTAGES. IT CAN OFTEN BE COLLECTED FROM MICROBIOLOGY DATA ALONE, RATHER THAN REQUIRING A LARGE REVIEW OF A PATIENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CHART OR MEDICAL RECORDS. ADDITIONALLY, IT IS OBJECTIVE AND LIKELY REQUIRES LESS INTENSIVE TRAINING FOR STAFF THAN CLABSI SURVEILLANCE. FINALLY, IN LMICS WHERE PROMPT TREATMENT AND PREVENTION OF SEPSIS IS OFTEN INADEQUATE, THERE ARE LIKELY A POOL OF NON-CLABSI HOB THAT ARE PREVENTABLE WITH SIMPLE, KNOWN INTERVENTIONS. CURRENTLY, ALL STUDIES ON HOB HAVE BEEN IN HIGH-INCOME COUNTRIES. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO DETERMINE WHETHER HOB IS A FEASIBLE, USEFUL, AND ACCEPTABLE METRIC FOR HAI SURVEILLANCE IN HOSPITALS IN LMIC. 2. SCOPE OF WORK THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO EVALUATE HOB IN HOSPITALS IN LMICS AS A FEASIBLE, USEFUL AND ACCEPTABLE METRIC FOR HAI SURVEILLANCE. THE SPECIFIC GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO: X SET UP HOB SURVEILLANCE IN ONE OR MORE SITES WITHIN A LOW OR MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRY (ACCORDING TO WORLD BANK CLASSIFICATIONS) AND DESCRIBE THE FOLLOWING: O THE ETIOLOGIES AND SYNDROMES ASSOCIATED WITH HOB O THE EPIDEMIOLOGY OF HOB IN TERMS OF PERSON, PLACE AND TIME X DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK FOR DETERMINING WHICH HOB EVENTS ARE LIKELY TO BE PREVENTABLE WITH INFECTION CONTROL MEASURES AND QUALITY HOSPITAL CARE AND COLLECT CLINICAL DATA TO DETERMINE THE PROPORTION OF HOB EVENTS OBSERVED THAT MEET THE CRITERIA OUTLINED IN THE FRAMEWORK. THIS SHOULD BE DONE VIA PROSPECTIVE DATA COLLECTION THAT CAPTURES RELEVANT CLINICAL DATA AND SHALL NOT RELY SOLELY ON DATA FROM MEDICAL CHARTS WHICH LIKELY WILL NOT HAVE SUFFICIENT DETAIL TO MAKE DETERMINATIONS. X EVALUATE THE COST, FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF IMPLEMENTING AN HOB SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM IN 200-2016-91804 75D30119F00003 PAGE 5 OF 28 LMIC. THIS WILL INCLUDE COLLECTION OF QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE DATA ON ACCEPTABILITY OF THE SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM FROM STAFF AND HOSPITAL ADMINISTRATION AS WELL AS COLLECTION OF DIRECT AND INDIRECT COSTS OF IMPLEMENTING THE SURVEILLANCE OUTSIDE A RESEARCH STUDY. X DETERMINE WHAT DATA MIGHT BE NEEDED TO BE INCLUDED IN AN HOB SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM TO ADEQUATELY TARGET PREVENTION EFFORTS. 3. TASKS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ALL LABOR, EXPERTISE, MATERIALS, AND SUPPLIES AND PERFORM ALL SERVICES REQUIRED TO CARRY OUT THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT. TASK 1: START UP MEETING X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ARRANGE AND CONDUCT AN INITIAL MEETING (BY TELECONFERENCE) WITH THE COR AND OTHER RELEVANT STAFF WITHIN 2 WEEKS OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE TASK ORDER. THE PURPOSE OF THE MEETING WILL BE TO REVIEW AND CLARIFY THE SCOPE OF WORK AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE FOR TASKS, TO DELINEATE ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES, AND TO ESTABLISH COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS. EACH TASK AND DELIVERABLE WILL BE REVIEWED. X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT AN AGENDA FOR THE ABOVE MEETING WITHIN 1 WEEK OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE TASK ORDER. TASK 2: MAINTAIN COMMUNICATION WITH THE SCIENCE OFFICER X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH THE COR FOR ALL PROJECT RELATED COMMUNICATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL MAINTAIN REGULAR COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE SCIENCE OFFICER AND COR INVOLVED WITH THE PROJECT. THE CHIEF MEANS OF COMMUNICATION WILL BE VIA CONFERENCE CALLS THAT WILL BE SCHEDULED EVERY MONTH THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT PERIOD AND ONE IN-PERSON MEETING. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE AN AGENDA AND MEETING MINUTES FOR EACH CALL. ALL CONFERENCE CALLS SHALL BE SCHEDULED AND ADMINISTERED BY THE CONTRACTOR. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL RESPOND TO ALL EMAILS AND TELEPHONE COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE SCIENCE OFFICER WITHIN 2-3 WORKING DAYS. X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH THE COR FOR AN IN-PERSON MEETING ASSOCIATED WITH TASK 5 & 6 (FRAMEWORK AND PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT MEETING) WHERE THEY WILL MEET WITH THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER AND OTHER RELEVANT CDC STAFF. THE IN-PERSON MEETING MAY BE AT THE CONTRACTORÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SITE OR AT CDCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ATLANTA, GA LOCATION. TASK 3: QUARTERLY PROGRESS REPORTS X ON THE 10TH DAY FOLLOWING THE 3 MONTHS BEING REPORTED, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE AND SUBMIT A QUARTERLY PROGRESS REPORT CONTAINING THE CURRENT STATUS OF WORK AND PROJECT SPENDING. THE REPORT SHALL CONTAIN, AT A MINIMUM, THE CURRENT PROGRESS ON EACH OF THE REQUIREMENTS SET FORTH BELOW, THE FINANCIAL STATUS OF THE PROJECT, PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED DURING THE MONTH, SOLUTIONS IMPLEMENTED, PLANNED ACTIVITY FOR THE UPCOMING MONTH AND ANY OTHER INFORMATION MUTUALLY AGREED UPON BETWEEN THE CONTRACTOR AND THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER. TASK 4: FINALIZE WORK PLAN AND TIMELINE X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL FINALIZE THE DETAILED PLAN AND TIMELINE, SUBMITTED IN THEIR PROPOSAL, FOR DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A STUDY EVALUATING THE USE OF HOB AS AN HAI METRIC THAT ADDRESSES THE SPECIFIC AIMS OUTLINED ABOVE IN THE STATEMENT OF WORK. THE WORK PLAN SHALL SPECIFY THE APPROACH TO DEVELOPING A STUDY PROTOCOL AND IMPLEMENTING ACTIVITIES OUTLINED IN THE PROTOCOL. A FINALIZED TIMELINE FOR THE COMPLETION OF THESE TASKS INCLUDING THE IDENTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL FACTORS THAT MAY HASTEN OR IMPEDE THE ACCOMPLISHMENT OF STATED OBJECTIVES WILL BE PRESENTED TO THE COR AND SCIENCE OFFICER FOR APPROVAL. TASK 5: DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK AND GUIDE FOR DETERMINING HOB PREVENTABILITY X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK AND SET OF CRITERIA TO DETERMINE THE PREVENTABILITY OF HOB EVENTS IN THIS STUDY AS WELL AS THE DATA THAT NEEDS TO BE COLLECTED TO PROVIDE A PREVENTABLE/NOT PREVENTABLE DETERMINATION FOR EACH HOB EVENT. THE FINAL FRAMEWORK AND CRITERIA SHOULD BE APPROVED BY THE CDC PROJECT OFFICER PRIOR TO USE. 200-2016-91804 75D30119F00003 PAGE 6 OF 28 X THIS FRAMEWORK SHALL BE DEVELOPED USING INPUT FROM AN EXPERT PANEL OF PHYSICIANS WITH BACKGROUNDS IN CRITICAL CARE, INFECTIOUS DISEASE, AND HOSPITAL EPIDEMIOLOGY. USING DELPHI METHODOLOGY, THE EXPERT PANEL SHALL BE CONVENED TO DEVELOP AND DEFINE THE FRAMEWORK AND GUIDE. THE GUIDING QUESTION FOR PREVENTABILITY SHALL BE Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒWAS THIS BACTEREMIA OR FUNGEMIA PREVENTABLE IN AN IDEAL HOSPITAL SETTING, PRACTICING PERFECT CLINICAL CARE AND INFECTION PREVENTION (EVEN IF THAT DOESNÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢TEXIST)Ã¢Â‚¬Â„¢. X THE GOAL OF THE FRAMEWORK IS TO THEN DEVELOP A GUIDE TO OPERATIONALIZE THE FRAMEWORK WITHIN THE SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM AND DETERMINE THE DATA THAT NEEDS TO BE COLLECTED FOR HOB EVENTS TO MAKE THE DETERMINATION. X THE GUIDE AND FRAMEWORK SHALL ALSO INCLUDE CONTINGENCY PLANS FOR HOW TO DEAL WITH DIFFICULT CASES OR CASES WHERE THE DETERMINATION CANNOT BE MADE WITH THE EXISTING FRAMEWORK (E.G., REFERRAL TO A TWOPERSON EVALUATION TEAM TO MAKE A DETERMINATION). X AN IN-PERSON MEETING OF THE CONTRACTOR, SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS AND CDC REPRESENTATIVES TO DEVELOP AND APPROVE THE DRAFT FRAMEWORK SHALL BE PLANNED AS OUTLINED IN TASK 2. DUE TO PRA LIMITATIONS, THE EXPERT PANEL SHOULD INCLUDE NOT MORE THAN 9 EXTERNAL EXPERTS. TASK 6: DEVELOP A PROTOCOL X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE PROJECT OFFICER ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOCOL THAT SPECIFICALLY LAYS OUT THE STUDY QUESTION, METHODOLOGY, DATA SOURCES, LABORATORY METHODS, STUDY POPULATION, ANALYTIC STRATEGY AND RELATED TASKS. X IN ORDER TO IMPROVE GENERALIZABILITY IT WOULD BE FAVORED FOR THE PROTOCOL TO INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION AT SEVERAL SITES, THOUGH THE AREAS OF DATA COLLECTION COULD BE SUBSETS OF THE LARGER HOSPITAL POPULATION (E.G., WITHIN THE ICUS OF SEVERAL HOSPITALS). X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP A PROTOCOL THAT OUTLINES THE FOLLOWING: O HOW HOB RATE DATA WILL BE COLLECTED AND COMPARED AT THE GIVEN FACILITY/FACILITIES OR WARD/WARDS. O HOW THE DATA REQUIRED TO DETERMINE THE PREVENTABILITY OF HOB INFECTIONS (AS DEFINED IN TASK 5) WILL BE COLLECTED, HOW DIFFICULT DETERMINATIONS WILL BE ADJUDICATED, AND WHEN DETERMINATIONS WILL BE MADE. THIS DATA WILL NEED TO BE COLLECTED PROSPECTIVELY AND SHALL MAKE USE OF ALL AVAILABLE DATA INCLUDING MEDICAL CHART DATA (THOUGH SHALL NOT SOLELY RELY ON THIS), INTERVIEWS WITH CLINICAL STAFF, REVIEW OF LABORATORY DATA AND OTHER RELEVANT MEDICAL INFORMATION. O HOW FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF HOB SURVEILLANCE WILL BE ASSESSED, INCLUDING POTENTIALLY QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE DATA AS APPROPRIATE. O HOW COSTS OF HOB SURVEILLANCE WILL BE CAPTURED X IN ADDITION THE PROTOCOL SHALL INCLUDE: O DEFINITIONS TO BE USED FOR HOB NUMERATORS O DENOMINATOR TO BE USED TO CALCULATE RATES O SAMPLE SIZE, POWER CALCULATIONS AS APPROPRIATE AND NEEDED TASK 7: OBTAIN INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB) AND OTHER SCIENCE OR ADMINISTRATIVE APPROVALS X THE CONTRACTOR WILL PREPARE AND SUBMIT THE RESEARCH PROTOCOL TO ALL RELEVANT AND NEEDED IRB BODIES AS WELL AS ANY ADDITIONAL SCIENTIFIC OR ADMINISTRATIVE APPROVALS THAT MAY EXIST IN COUNTRY. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF PACKAGE DEVELOPMENT AND SUBMISSION AS REQUIRED PRIOR TO COLLECTION OF ANY DATA. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE THE PACKAGES INCLUDING ALL FORMS AND ATTACHMENTS FOR CDC SCIENCE OFFICER APPROVAL AS NEEDED. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT THE IRB PACKAGE TO THE RELEVANT IRB(S) AND SHALL ENSURE THAT CLINICAL SITES INVOLVED IN THE STUDY APPLY FOR AND RECEIVE IRB APPROVAL. COPIES OF IRB APPROVALS FROM THE CONTRACTOR AND ALL CLINICAL SITES SHALL BE PROVIDED TO THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER. TASK 8: COLLECT DATA X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HAVE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR COLLECTING AND MANAGING RELEVANT MICROBIOLOGY, CLINICAL AND OTHER DATA TO FULFILL THE OBJECTIVES OF THE STUDY. THE DATA COLLECTED SHALL INCLUDE, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO, THE FOLLOWING: O NUMBER OF HOB EVENTS AND MICROBIOLOGIC DESCRIPTION INCLUDING RESISTANCE DATA IF AVAILABLE O CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGIC DATA AS WELL AS ANY OTHER DATA Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ DETERMINED VIA TASKS 5 AND 6 - TO DETERMINE PREVENTABILITY OF INFECTIONS 200-2016-91804 75D30119F00003 PAGE 7 OF 28 O APPROPRIATE DENOMINATOR DATA (E.G. ANY DATA COLLECTION ISSUES SHALL BE REPORTED IN A TIMELY MANNER, BY PHONE OR EMAIL, NO LATER THAN 2 WEEKS AFTER ONSET. TASK 9: DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYSIS X THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COLLECT, MANAGE, ANALYZE AND SECURELY STORE ALL RELEVANT DATA AND SHALL DESIGN AND MAINTAIN A DATA MANAGEMENT STRUCTURE AND PROCEDURES THAT WILL ENSURE CONSISTENT DATA COLLECTION FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT. THIS DATA ANALYTIC PLAN SHALL BE SUBMITTED TO AND APPROVED BY THE CDC SCIENCE OFFICER BEFORE DATA ANALYSES CAN PROCEED. THE PLAN SHALL OUTLINE HOW THE FOLLOWING OUTCOMES WILL BE OUTPUT FROM THE PROPOSED ANALYSIS: O DESCRIPTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGY OF HOB EVENTS O PROPORTION OF PREVENTABLE EVENTS O MEASURES OF FEASIBILITY AND COST X ONCE DATA ANALYSIS HAS BEGUN, UPDATES ON DATA ANALYTICS SHALL BE INCLUDED IN QUARTERLY REPORTS GIVEN TO COR AND CDC SCIENCE OFFICER. description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES OF DTU AS PART OF IEDB & AR PROGRAM ARE TO MAINTAIN, ENHANCE AND UPDATE THE EXISTING SET OF EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS, AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS FOR THE ANALYSIS RESOURCE. DTU WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC TELECONFERENCES AND MEETINGS, AND PROVIDE TASK STATUS FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. SPECIFICALLY , DTU WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS: ANALYSIS RESOURCE TASKS MAINTAIN AND UPDATE THE EXISTING MHC CLASS I AND II BINDING PREDICTION TOOLS.THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. DEVELOP NEW MHC CLASS I AND II EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF TCR BASED EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING THE TCR SEQUENCE AND STRUCTURE INFORMATION. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE MHC PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. UPDATE EVALUATIONS OF THE MHC BINDING AND T CELL PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. MAINTAIN EXISTING B CELL TOOLS DEVELOPED BY DTU. DEVELOP NEW B CELL EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODY SPECIFIC EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING BCR SEQUENCE INFORMATION. ESTABLISH AUTOMATED BENCHMARKING SYSTEMS FOR PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS AS WELL AS PREDICTION TOOLS NOT HOSTED IN THE IEDB. PROVIDE UPDATED BENCHMARK DATASETS WITH RESPECT TO THESE TASKS, DTU WILL DEVELOP CODE IN THEIR LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND ENSURE THAT IT CAN BE EXECUTED APPROPRIATELY IN THE IEDB PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT AND WORK WITH THE LJI TEAM TO UPDATE WEB SERVERS EXECUTING THE CODE AS NECESSARY. THIS INCLUDES RETRAINING, BUG FIXES, AND FEATURE ENHANCEMENTS AS THEY OCCUR. FOR ANY NEW TOOL OR SUBSTANTIAL TOOL UPDATE DEVELOPED WITH FUNDING FROM THE IEDB BY DTU, THE PRIMARY PUBLICATION WILL INCLUDE A LINK TO THE WORKING TOOL ON THE IEDB WEBSITE. MEETINGS AND REPORTS MEETINGS/TELECONFERENCESNIDEOCONFERENCES DTU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH LJI AT A MINIMUM OF TWICE PER MONTH, EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA TELECONFERENCE/VIDEOCONFERENCE. THE PURPOSE OF THESE MEETINGS WILL BE TO COORDINATE EFFORTS AND REPORT PROGRESS. DTU WILL ALSO BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN 1-2 US BASED PROGRAM MEETINGS PER CONTRACT YEAR FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING FEEDBACK TO NIH AND FURTHER PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. description: NORTHWESTERN UNIVERSITY WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF GRAPHENE INKS AND THE PRINTING OF GRAPHENE INTERDIGITATED ELECTRODES (IDES) USING AEROSOL JET PRINTING AND SCREEN PRINTING. IN PARTICULAR, NORTHWESTERN UNIVERSITY WILL LEAD THE SUBTASKS LISTED BELOW: TASK 1: RAPID PROTOTYPING OF AEROSOL JET PRINTED GRAPHENE ELECTROCHEMICAL SENSORS: THIS TASK WILL IDENTIFY OPTIMAL PRINTABLE GRAPHENE INKS AND IDE GEOMETRIES FOR HIGHLY SENSITIVE ELECTROCHEMICAL DETECTION OF SARS-COV-2 USING AEROSOL JET PRINTING. THE FIRST SUBTASK WILL DEVELOP A PRINTABLE GRAPHENE INK THAT IS SHELF-STABLE AND FORMS HIGHLY CONDUCTIVE PATTERNS FOLLOWING DEPOSITION AND CURING. THE SECOND SUBTASK WILL EXPLORE RAPID PROTOTYPING OF GRAPHENE IDE GEOMETRIES SUCH AS ELECTRODE FINGER WIDTH AND SPACING TO ACHIEVE LARGE ELECTROCHEMICAL SENSING AREAS. THE RESULTING GRAPHENE IDES WILL BE SENT TO IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY, WHERE THE THIRD SUBTASK WILL PURSUE FUNCTIONALIZATION OF THE BIOSENSORS WITH S1 MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES AND VALIDATION OF THE SENSORS IN AN ARTIFICIAL SALIVA TESTING ENVIRONMENT. TASK 2: HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREEN PRINTED GRAPHENE ELECTROCHEMICAL SENSORS: THIS TASK WILL EXPLORE HIGH-THROUGHPUT MANUFACTURING OF THE OPTIMIZED GRAPHENE ELECTROCHEMICAL SENSORS USING SCREEN PRINTING. THE FIRST SUBTASK WILL DEVELOP A SCALABLE GRAPHENE INK FORMULATION FOR LARGE-SCALE SCREEN PRINTING USING CELLULOSIC POLYMER ADDITIVES. THE SECOND SUBTASK WILL DEMONSTRATE HIGH-THROUGHPUT AND HIGH-RESOLUTION SCREEN PRINTING TO SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASE THE NUMBER OF GRAPHENE IDES AVAILABLE FOR TESTING. THE RESULTING GRAPHENE IDES WILL BE SENT TO IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY, WHERE THE THIRD SUBTASK WILL PERFORM SENSOR VALIDATION STUDIES IN HUMAN SALIVA USING A PORTABLE ELECTROCHEMICAL POTENTIOSTAT TO DEMONSTRATE THE POTENTIAL OF THIS TECHNOLOGY FOR POINT-OF-SERVICE APPLICATION.

description: THE QUALITY PAYMENT PROGRAM RESOURCE CENTER FOR THE MIDWEST (QPP RESOURCE CENTER) REMAINS DEDICATED PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO SMALL CLINICIAN PRACTICES WITH 15 OR FEWER CLINICIANS UNDER ONE TIN WHO ARE ALSO ELIGIBLE FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE MERIT-BASED INCENTIVE PAYMENT SYSTEM (MIPS). THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER, THROUGH THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL, WILL SUPPORT CLINICIANS IN THEIR TRANSITION FROM A FEE-FOR-SERVICE MODEL TO AN ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT MODEL (APM) OR THE MERIT BASED INCENTIVE PAYMENT SYSTEM (MIPS). WORKING UNDER THE DIRECTION OF ALTARUMÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S QPP RESOURCE CENTER PROJECT MANAGER, NIU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOWING TASKS AND ACTIVITIES: TASK 1: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) ASSIGN QPP ADVISOR STAFF AND ENSURE THEIR AVAILABILITY FOR ONBOARDING/TRAINING SESSIONS ON PROGRAM OBJECTIVES, VIRTUAL SUPPORT SERVICES, QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM WEB PORTAL WORKFLOWS AND TOOLS, AND CMS TOOLS, AND (2) DESIGNATE STAFF MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE IN APPROPRIATE WORKGROUPS TASK 2: RESOURCE CENTER CONTENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IDENTIFY AND PROVIDE EXISTING QPP RELATED RESOURCES AND TOOLS WITHIN YOUR ORGANIZATION IN A FORMAT APPROPRIATE FOR UPLOAD TO THE WEBSITE AND USE BY CLINICIANS, AND (2) ASSIST WITH RESEARCH FOR PUBLICLY AVAILABLE TOOLS AND RESOURCES TO BE LINKED TO OR UPLOADED ONTO THE QPP RESOURCE CENTERTM TASK 3: MARKETING ACTIVITIES - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IDENTIFY A STAFF PERSON TO PARTICIPATE IN THE MARKETING & OUTREACH WORKGROUP, (2) IDENTIFY NEW, AND USE EXISTING, COMMUNICATION AVENUES TO PROMOTE THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER, QPP TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND CMS/CMS QPP-SURS CENTRAL SUPPORT CONTRACTOR SPONSORED EVENTS, (3) REACH OUT TO LOCAL AND STATE CLINICIAN ORGANIZATIONS, PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATIONS, AND OTHER RELEVANT GROUPS TO HAVE THE QPP RESOURCE CENTER ADVERTISED ON THEIR WEBSITES, IN NEWSLETTERS, E-NEWSLETTERS, AND OTHER CLINICIAN COMMUNICATIONS TASK 4: CLINICIAN ENGAGEMENT - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) PROVIDE INFORMATION IN THE CMS CRM AS REQUIRED TO DOCUMENT THE BI-LATERAL ENGAGEMENT OF ILLINOIS CLINICIANS, AS WELL AS UNREACHABLE CLINICIANS, (2) PROVIDE UPDATES ON CLINICIAN ELIGIBILITY OR ELIGIBLE CLINICIAN FILE ERRORS TO CMS BY SUBMITTING CASES VIA THE CMS CRM, (3) ASSIGN QPP ADVISORS TO ASSIST ALL ENROLLED PRACTICES IN THE STATE OF ILLINOIS THAT ARE ASSIGNED TO NIU FOR VIRTUAL TA SERVICE, (4) CONTINUE BI-LATERAL ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES UNTIL 90% OF SURS ELIGIBLE CLINICIANS IN ILLINOIS HAVE BEEN BI-LATERALLY ENGAGED FOR THE PROGRAM YEAR AND THIS BILATERAL ENGAGEMENT HAS BEEN DOCUMENTED AT THE TIN AND/OR INDIVIDUAL NPI LEVEL. TASK 5: DELIVER VIRTUAL SUPPORT AND TA TASK 6: CUSTOMER SATISFACTION ASSESSMENT TASK 7: DATA CAPTURE AND REPORTING - THIS INCLUDES ACTIVITIES SUCH AS, (1) IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE A SELF-SELECTED PROGRAM/METHOD TO TRACK ALL OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT EVENTS (INCLUDING DATE, ENGAGEMENT TYPE, AND AFFILIATED NPIS/TINS). MAINTAIN DATA IN SUPPORT OF UNREACHABLE CLINICIAN DOCUMENTATION, (2) SUPPORT COMPLETE DOCUMENTATION OF AND RECORD PRACTICE AND CLINICIAN DEMOGRAPHIC INFORMATION, (3) DOCUMENT PROGRAM MILESTONES.

description: COMMUNITY HEALTH REPRESENTATIVES, COMMUNITY HEALTH AIDES, HEALTH EDUCATORS AND PUBLIC HEALTH NURSES HAVE BEEN ON THE FRONTLINES OF THE PUBLIC HEALTH MOBILIZATION TO ADDRESS COVID-19 IN AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE U.S. THE IHS COMMUNITY HEALTH ECHO FOCUSES ON SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE APPLICABLE TO COMMUNITY LEVEL RESPONSE, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON SOCIAL DETERMINANTS AND THE PUBLIC HEALTH SCOPE OF PRACTICE. THE INSTITUTE WILL CONSULT WITH THE JOHNS HOPKINS CENTER FOR AMERICAN INDIAN HEALTH (JHCAIH), A WIDELY RESPECTED ORGANIZATION IN THE AL/AN PUBLIC HEALTH TRAINING FIELD AND COMMUNITY COVID-19 RESPONSE, TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE IHS COMMUNITY HEALTH TELEECHO. THE POINT OF CONTACT WILL BE KRISTEN SPEAKMAN. SCOPE OF SERVICES AS A CONSULTANT FOR THE IHS COMMUNITY HEALTH ECHO PROGRAM, JHCAIH WILL: 1) SUPPORT AND ADVISE ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROGRAM CURRICULUM; 2) CREATE AND DELIVER DIDACTIC PRESENTATIONS; AND 3) PARTICIPATE IN PLANNING AND DEBRIEF MEETINGS. JHCAIH WILL CONSULT WITH THE ECHO INSTITUTE FROM FEBRUARY 1, 2021 THROUGH AUGUST 18, 2021. JHCAIH WILL INVOICE EACH PRESENTATION WITH COSTS AND ANY SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION, IN LINE WITH ATTACHMENT 5 AND ATTACHMENT (WHATEVER THE INVOICE ATTACHMENT IS), UP TO A TOTAL OF $1000/PRESENTATION. JHCAIH WILL DELIVER A TOTAL OF 5 PRESENTATIONS. TOTAL INVOICES ARE NOT TO EXCEED $5,000 FOR THIS PROJECT.

description: THE INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH INSTITUTE (IDRI) IS IN THE PROCESS OF DEVELOPING AN ADJUVANTED TUBERCULOSIS VACCINE. THE PROTEIN VACCINE IS FORMULATED AS AN OIL-IN-WATER EMULSION, STABILIZED BY A PHOSPHOLIPID AND A DISACCHARIDE. THE CURRENT LEAD FORMULATIONS ARE STABLE UNDER REFRIGERATED CONDITIONS AND CAN BE SPRAY DRIED TO INCREASE ROBUSTNESS TO HEAT EXPOSURE. IDRI WOULD LIKE TO ASSESS THE SCALABILITY OF THE SPRAY DRYING PROCESS TO PRODUCE LARGER BATCH SIZES, TEST THE PERFORMANCE OF CANDIDATE FORMULATIONS ON NASAL DELIVERY DEVICES AND ASSESS THE COMPATIBILITY OF THE FORMULATION PLATFORM IN PROPELLANT-BASED DELIVERY DEVICES. THE FOLLOWING SERVICES WILL BE SUPPLIED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF ALBERTA: 1. OPTIMIZATION OF PROCESS PARAMETERS FOR INCREASED THROUGHPUT OF EXISTING FORMULATIONS (THEORETICALLY AND EMPIRICALLY). 2. MODIFICATION AND EXTENSION OF OUR EXISTING PROCESS EQUIPMENT FOR LARGER BATCH SIZES (DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, TEST AND PROCEDURE DEVELOPMENT) ALLOWING PRODUCTION OF 100 G BATCHES. 3. PRODUCTION AND TESTING OF SEVERAL SMALL SCALE LOTS AT VARIOUS HUMIDITY LEVELS AND DRYING GAS TEMPERATURES TO ASSESS THE EFFECT OF MORE AGGRESSIVE PROCESSING CONDITIONS ON PROCESS LOSS (REQUIRES COLLABORATION FOR ASSAYS WITH IDRI). - DELIVERABLE 1: STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ CAPTURES ACTIVITIES 1 -3. 4. PRODUCTION OF A PROOF OF CONCEPT LARGER SCALE PRODUCTION LOT AND INITIATION OF A SHORT ACCELERATED STABILITY. - DELIVERABLE 2: COA FOR BATCH RELEASE AND STABILITY SUMMARY FROM SHORT-TERM ACCELERATED STABILITY STUDY Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ CAPTURES ACTIVITIES 3-4 5. SOURCING OF A SUITABLE NASAL DELIVERY DEVICE AND ASSOCIATED FILL-FINISH EQUIPMENT, DEVELOPMENT OF MANUAL FILL FINISH PROCEDURES (APTAR DEVICE). - DELIVERABLE 3: FILL-FINISH SOP Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ CAPTURES ACTIVITY 5. 6. MANUFACTURING OF A BATCH OF FINISHED NASAL DELIVERY DEVICES FOR PERFORMANCE TESTING. 7. DEVELOPING TEST PROCEDURE AND TESTING PERFORMANCE OF THE NASAL DELIVERY DEVICES IN AN IDEALIZED NOSE MODEL. 8. ASSESSING THE COMPATIBILITY OF THE FORMULATION PLATFORM IN PROPELLANT-BASED DELIVERY DEVICES (NASAL OR PULMONARY), INCLUDING ALTERNATIVE PROPELLANTS. - DELIVERABLE 4: TESTING PROCEDURE SOP, TESTING PERFORMANCE COMPARISON SUMMARY REPORT Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ CAPTURES ACTIVITIES 6 - 8. 9. PULLING AND TESTING THE REMAINING TIME-POINT ON THE ONGOING STABILITY STUDY. - DELIVERABLE 5: FINAL REPORT OF ALL ACTIVITIES ABOVE INCLUDING DATA FROM 36-MONTH STABILITY TIME POINT 10. PREPARATION OF MATERIALS SUITABLE FOR DISSEMINATION (CONFERENCE, PUBLICATION, ETC.) AS APPROPRIATE BASED ON THE PROJECTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S FINDINGS.

description: HOSPITAL ACQUIRED INFECTIONS (HAIS) ARE SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO PATIENTSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ SAFETY WORLDWIDE. LOW AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRIES (LMICS) HAVE HIGHER PREVALENCE OF HAIS AND SURGICAL SITE INFECTIONS (SSIS) WHEN COMPARED TO THE UNITED STATES (US) AND EUROPE. THE OVERALL OCCURRENCE OF HAIS IN ADULTS IN INTENSIVE CARE UNITS (ICUS) IS AT LEAST 3 TIMES HIGHER IN LMICS VERSUS THE UNITED STATES. ALTHOUGH COUNTRY-WIDE HAI RATES ARE NOT AVAILABLE FOR INDIA, A RECENT STUDY OF ICUS IN 40 INDIAN HOSPITALS REPORTED HAI RATES TO BE SUBSTANTIALLY HIGHER THAN THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION'S NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY NETWORK (CDC-NHSN) MEDIAN RATES, DESPITE INDIAN ICUS HAVING LOWER UTILIZATION OF DEVICES. CENTRAL LINE ASSOCIATED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (CLABSI) RATES IN INDIAN ICUS WERE AT LEAST 5 TIMES HIGHER THAN RATES IN US ICUS. HOWEVER, RECENT US STUDIES FOUND THAT CLABSIS COMPRISE LESS THAN 20% OF TOTAL HOSPITAL ONSET BACTEREMIA AND FUNGEMIA (HOB). IMPORTANTLY, TWO-THIRDS OF THE HOB EVENTS WERE JUDGED TO BE PREVENTABLE. SUB-OPTIMAL INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES IN INDIA, AS EVIDENCED BY HIGH CLABSI AND OTHER HAI RATES, INDICATE THAT NON-CLABSI HOB EVENTS MAY ACCOUNT FOR SIGNIFICANT PROPORTION OF POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE INFECTIONS IN INDIAN HOSPITALS. THESE DATA SUGGEST THAT EVALUATING THE LARGER GROUP OF HOB EVENTS MAY ALLOW US TO EXPAND THE TARGETS FOR HAI DETECTION, AND MORE APPROPRIATELY DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO REDUCE ADDITIONAL SIGNIFICANT HAI EVENTS NOT BEING CURRENTLY ADDRESSED IN A SYSTEMATIC MANNER IN RESOURCE LIMITED SETTINGS. IN THIS STUDY WE WILL IDENTIFY AND VALIDATE NEW STRATEGIES FOR HAI PREVENTION IN RESOURCE LIMITED SETTINGS SUCH AS INDIAN HOSPITALS WITH AN AIM TO ADVANCE SURVEILLANCE OF HAI AND GUIDE INFECTION PREVENTION ACTIVITIES TO IMPROVE HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND PATIENT SAFETY. SCOPE OF WORK HOSPITAL-ONSET BACTEREMIA AND FUNGEMIA (HOB) IS BEING EVALUATED IN THE UNITED STATES AS AN OBJECTIVE METRIC FOR SURVEILLANCE OF HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS (HAI). GIVEN THE HIGH BURDEN OF HAI AND ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN LOW AND MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRIES, IT IS APPROPRIATE TO EXPAND THE STUDY OF HOB TO THOSE COUNTRIES. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, THE FRAMEWORK FOR THE STUDY OF HOB DEVELOPED FOR US HOSPITALS WILL BE ADAPTED AND EVALUATED IN INDIA TO UNDERSTAND THE EPIDEMIOLOGY, SOURCES, PREVENTABILITY, AND FEASIBILITY OF HOB SURVEILLANCE IN THE INDIAN HOSPITAL SETTING. AIM 1: ASSESS THE INCIDENCE OF HOB THROUGH BLOOD CULTURE DATA COLLECTION PROSPECTIVELY FOR 6 MONTHS IN TWO STUDY HOSPITALS IN INDIA WE WILL CONDUCT A PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY TO EXAMINE HOB INCIDENCE AMONG PATIENTS ADMITTED TO THE TWO HOSPITALS FROM MARCH 1, 2020 TO AUGUST 31, 2020. EVERY BLOOD CULTURE PROCESSED BETWEEN MARCH 1, 2020 AND AUGUST 31, 2020 IN MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORIES OF TWO HOSPITALS WILL BE INCLUDED IN THE STUDY. FOR EACH BLOOD CULTURE, INFORMATION WILL BE COLLECTED BY INFECTION CONTROL NURSES. AIM 2: ASSESS THE SOURCES AND PREVENTABILITY OF HOB THROUGH A DETAILED REVIEW OF SPECIFIED NUMBER OF HOB EVENTS IN TWO STUDY HOSPITALS IN INDIA TO ASSESS THE SOURCE AND PREVENTABILITY OF HOB CASES, 300 CONSECUTIVE HOB CASES FROM AMRITA HOSPITAL AND 150 HOB CASES FROM FORTIS HOSPITAL WILL BE EXAMINED IN SELECTED UNITS (MICU, SICU, BMTU, NCU, PICU, NEURO ICU, INPATIENT MEDICAL AND SURGICAL WARDS INCLUDING LABOR AND DELIVERY WARDS) PROSPECTIVELY FROM APRIL 1, 2020 TO AUGUST 31, 2020. AT THE TWO HOSPITALS, A STANDARDIZED DATA COLLECTION FORM WILL BE USED TO CAPTURE KEY CLINICAL, MICROBIOLOGIC, AND DEMOGRAPHIC DATA, TO DETERMINE THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE OR SOURCE OF HOB, AND DETERMINE DEGREE OF PREVENTABILITY USING THE EXPERT-CONSENSUS BASED LIKERT SCALE PREVENTABILITY ASSESSMENT TOOL DEVELOPED FOR US HOSPITALS IN AN ONGOING STUDY. AIM 3: ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY AND COST FOR CONDUCTING HOB SURVEILLANCE IN THE TWO STUDY HOSPITALS IN INDIA TO ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY, INFORMATION ON FACTORS AFFECTING HOB SURVEILLANCE IMPLEMENTATION WILL BE COLLECTED AT THE TWO HOSPITALS BY CONDUCTING QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH STUDY INFECTION CONTROL NURSES, 3-5 CLINICIANS, THE HEAD OF INFECTION CONTROL PROGRAM AND THE STUDY STAFF. THESE INTERVIEWS WILL BE CONDUCTED BY PIS EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA SKYPE. CO-I: SURBHI LEEKHA (8% EFFORT) DR. LEEKHA WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. GANDRA IN PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC INPUT INTO THE DESIGN AND CONDUCT OF ALL ASPECTS OF THIS PROPOSAL. SPECIFICALLY, SHE WILL USE HER EXPERTISE IN DEVELOPING THE PREVENTABILITY FRAMEWORK INCLUDING THE DELPHI CONSENSUS METHODOLOGY USED FOR THE ONGOING US STUDY OF HOB, AS WELL AS EVALUATION OF SOURCES OF HOB. SHE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE START-UP MEETING, REGULAR COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE STUDY TEAM AND CDC, DEVELOPMENT OF THE PREVENTABILITY FRAMEWORK, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, DATA COLLECTION, AND DATA ANALYSIS.

THE END OF EBOLA OUTBREAK #11 IN THE DRC WAS DECLARED ON 11/18/2020 AND THEREFORE ALL SUPPORT OF THE OUTBREAK IS IN THE PROCESS OF BEING WITHDRAWN OVER THE COMING MONTH. SUPPORT OF THE INRB BIOREPOSITORY STAFFING WILL CONTINUE UNDER THIS SUBCONTRACT THROUGH 8/30/2021 AT WHICH TIME THESE HUMAN RESOURCES WILL BE SUPPORTED BY WAY OF PARTNER INSTITUTIONS. BIOSPECIMENS COLLECTED DURING THE EBOLA OUTBREAK WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE INRB BIOREPOSITORY AND MAY BE USED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH STUDIES.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING FIFTEEN CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR (SEPT 1, 2022 THROUGH AUG 31, 2023). UW-CRYOEM MAY ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) AND WILL SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. B. PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS: UW-CRYOEM WILL LEAD A STUDY WITH THE GOAL OF IDENTIFYING EPITOPES TARGETED BY CROSS-REACTIVE AND BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES AGAINST BETACORONAVIRUSES TO OBTAIN AN ANTIGENIC MAP OF TARGETS PRESENT AT THE SURFACE OF THE SPIKE TRIMER. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-CRYOEM WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FOMR UW-CRYOEM WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-NMR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 1 NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS ONE YEAR SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, 9/1/2022 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ 8/31/2023). UW-NMR WILL ALSO LEAD ONE SVTD AND SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULE BY NMR: UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED FROM COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND INTERNAL BATCHES; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITIES ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. STRUCTURE-GUIDED VACCINE DESIGN AND THERAPEUTICS DISCOVERY: UW-NMR WILL LEAD A SVTD STUDY FOCUSED ON IDENTIFYING HOW SMALL DRUG-LIKE MOLECULES BIND TO RNA REGULATORY ELEMENTS IN DENGUE. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. description: THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NTM INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, PROTEOMICS, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB TASK 3.5 TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS OF NHP SAMPLES. FHCC WILL EXECUTE GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING WITH RNASEQ/NANOSTRING ASSAYS ON NHP SAMPLES GENERATED IN OPTION 3 AT UKHSA. TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS WILL BE FOCUSED ON IDENTIFYING A PERIPHERAL BLOOD SURROGATE ENDPOINT FOR THE M.TB ERDMAN ULDA CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. THE INITIAL UNBIASED RNA SEQUENCING APPROACH WILL USE WHOLE-BLOOD SAMPLES FROM PRE AND POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL LOOK FOR TRANSCRIPTS THAT ARE CORRELATED WITH M.TB CFU AND M.TB QPCR ASSAYS FROM BAL, THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCE AT POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS, WE WILL ALSO LOOK FOR CHANGES IN TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE RELATIVE TO THE DAY OF CHALLENGE AS A POTENTIAL CORRELATE OF CHALLENGE OUTCOME. AS WE BUILD A MODEL TO PREDICT CHALLENGE OUTCOME FROM THESE GENE EXPRESSION MEASURES WE WILL SPECIFICALLY CONSIDER TRANSCRIPTS THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN IDENTIFIED AS PREDICTORS OF PROGRESSION TO TB DISEASE, SUCH AS TYPE I IFN-RELATED GENES WHOSE EXPRESSION INCREASES DURING DISEASE PROGRESSION. THE HUMAN EXPRESSION SIGNATURES WILL BE EVALUATED IN NHPS AND VICE VERSA; ADDITIONALLY, A JOINT MODEL WILL BE DEVELOPED, ALLOWING FOR DIFFERENCES IN NHP AND HUMAN ASSOCIATIONS, WHILE IDENTIFYING A COMMON GENE SIGNATURE. ONCE TRANSCRIPTS OR GENES HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED, A TARGETED CROSS-SPECIES NANOSTRING PANEL WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EVALUATION IN THE SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AS WELL AS IN FUTURE NHP AND CLINICAL TRIALS. WE PLAN TO DEVELOP A NANOSTRING NCOUNTER GENE PANEL WHICH CAN ACCOMMODATE UP TO 800 GENES AND WOULD BE SIGNIFICANTLY MORE COST EFFECTIVE THAN RNA SEQUENCING. ALTERNATIVELY, DEPENDING ON THE COMPLEXITY OF THE GENE PANEL, IT COULD BE DEVELOPED AS A 96 TRANSCRIPT/GENE (INCLUDING HOUSEKEEPING GENES) QPCR BIOMARK FLUIDIGM ASSAY. TASK 3.7 COMPARE IMMUNE PROFILES IN NHP, SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AND HUMANS TO IDENTIFY CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. CYTOF EXPERIMENTS WE HAVE EVALUATED THE ASSAY/SAMPLE PRIORITY LIST AS WELL AS THE BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED ON THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, TO ENUMERATE THE NUMBER OF STORED SAMPLES AVAILABLE FOR THE OBJECTIVES RELATED TO THE PROPOSED CYTOF END ASSAY. THUS FAR (AS OF NOV 9, 2021), OF ALL THE MAIN STUDY PARTICIPANT SAMPLES FROM WHICH BAL AND PBMC HAVE BEEN COLLECTED (N=66), A TOTAL OF 22 PARTICIPANTS DID NOT YIELD SUFFICIENT BAL CELLS FOR CYTOF ANALYSIS. THERE ARE ONGOING DISCUSSIONS WITH THE CLINICAL TEAM REGARDING THE POSSIBLE REPLACEMENT OF THESE PARTICIPANTS WITH LOW CELL YIELDS, WITH NEW PARTICIPANTS FROM THE CORRESPONDING CLINICAL GROUPS. ALL PARTICIPANT SAMPLES YIELDED SUFFICIENT NUMBERS OF PBMCS FOR THE CYTOF ASSAY. C. OTHER LABORATORY WORK CONTINUOUS ASSESSMENT OF BAL CELL YIELDS HAS REVEALED THAT BAL SAMPLES WITH EXTREME PARTICULATE MATTER LOADING, DISPLAY EXCELLENT VIABILITIES PRIOR TO CRYOPRESERVATION, BUT UPON THAWING, SHOW A HETEROGENOUS VIABILITY PATTERN. EXTENSIVE INVESTIGATIONS REVEALED THAT THE LARGE, GIANT MACROPHAGES, WITH HEAVY PARTICULATE MATTER LOADING, ARE MORE LIKELY TO SHOW POOR VIABILITY. THESE GIANT MACROPHAGES APPEARED TO EXCEED A SIZE OF 40 ÃŽÂ¼M, WHICH LED TO THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A 40 ÃŽÂ¼M CELL STRAINING STEP, TO IMPROVE VIABILITY OF BAL CELLS UPON THAWING. THIS PREVENTATIVE MEASURE WILL BE ROUTINELY MONITORED AS RESIDUAL CELLS BECOME AVAILABLE TO THAW FOR VIABILITY TESTING. WE WILL CONTINUE OUR LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS TO INFORM THE DECISION OF REPLACING BAL CELL PHENOTYPING USING CYTOF INSTRUMENT, WITH THE SPECTRAL CYTOMETER (AURORA) PLATFORM. WE HAVE ALREADY USED ONE BAL SAMPLE WITH EXTREME PARTICULATE MATTER LOADING, AND THEREFORE MAXIMAL AUTOFLUORESCENT SIGNAL, AND IN PARALLEL COMPARED ITS PERFORMANCE ON THE SPECTRAL CYTOMETER TO THAT OF THE CYTOF INSTRUMENT, USING THE CORE PANEL OF CYTOF ANTIBODIES ACROSS THESE TWO INSTRUMENTS.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK SARS-COV-2 B CELL EPITOPE MAPPING SUPPLEMENT (WILSON) SUBCONTRACT TO THE SUPPLEMENT FOR: NIAID CONTRACT 75N93019C00062 (FREEMONT, PI, PD) B CELL MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF PROTECTION FROM SARS-COV-2 PATRICK C. WILSON, SUBCONTRACT PI WEILL COLLEGE OF MEDICINE OF CORNELL UNIVERSITY E-MAIL: PCW4001@MED.CORNELL.EDU Ã¢Â‚¬Æ’ STATEMENT OF WORK CORONAVIRUSES ARE ENVELOPED NON-SEGMENTED POSITIVE-SENSE RNA VIRUSES BELONGING TO THE FAMILY CORONAVIRIDAE AND CIRCULATE BROADLY AMONGST AND BETWEEN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS. OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, TWO BETACORONAVIRUSES, SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (SARS-COV) AND MIDDLE EAST RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS (MERS-COV), WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR OVER 10,000 CASES OF INFECTION. THE MORTALITY RATE OF SARS-COV WAS 10% WITH 29 COUNTRIES AFFECTED, AND THE MORTALITY RATE OF MERS WAS 35% WITH 27 COUNTRIES AFFECTED GLOBALLY. IN DECEMBER OF 2019, A NOVEL CORONAVIRUS (2019-NCOV) WAS DISCOVERED THROUGH DEEP SEQUENCING ANALYSIS AFTER A SERIES OF PNEUMONIA CASES WERE REPORTED IN WUHAN, HUBEI, CHINA WITH UNKNOWN VIRAL ORIGIN. SEVERAL INDEPENDENT STUDIES HAVE SINCE CONFIRMED THAT THE NOVEL VIRUS ORIGINATED FROM EXPOSURES IN A WUHAN SEAFOOD MARKET. BY ONLY MARCH 16, 2020, 2019-NCOV CAUSED A PANDEMIC SPANNING MOST COUNTRIES ON EARTH WITH A REPORTED 167,000 PEOPLE INFECTED WORLDWIDE, AND ALMOST 7000 CONFIRMED DEATHS. CASE AND MORTALITY RATES ARE CONTINUING TO RISE AND THE LACK OF ADEQUATE TESTING IN MAJOR POPULATION CENTERS PLUS CLEAR EVIDENCE OF COMMUNITY TRANSMISSIONS SUGGESTS THAT THE NUMBER OF INFECTED IS LIKELY SIGNIFICANTLY GREATER. MOREOVER, AS THE VIRUS CONTINUES TO SPREAD, ITS HIGH MUTATION RATE INTRODUCES THE THREAT OF INFECTIONS WITH NEW VARIANTS WHICH COULD HAVE ALTERED SEVERITY AND TRANSMISSIBILITY. THESE OCCURRENCES NECESSITATE THE URGENCY OF NOVEL PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC MEASURES TO HELP PREVENT THE SPREAD OF NCOV-2019, WHICH POSES ONE OF THE GREATEST GLOBAL HEALTH THREATS IN MODERN HISTORY. MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MAB) ARE MONOVALENT PROTEINS EXPRESSED BY B CELLS THAT CAN SPECIFICALLY TARGET 3-DIMENSIONAL VIRAL EPITOPES, LEADING TO POTENT VIRAL NEUTRALIZATION. MABS HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED MODERN MEDICINE BY PROVIDING PRECISION MEDICINE AGAINST MANY DISEASES, WITH OVER 70 MAB-BASED DRUGS APPROVED BY THE FDA. THE ISOLATION OF HUMAN MABS SPECIFIC FOR HIGHLY IMMUNOGENIC NCOV-2019 PROTEINS CAN BE RAPIDLY USED AS THERAPEUTIC AGENTS, FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS, AND FOR TEMPLATING THE GENERATION OF VACCINES THAT CAN PROTECT AGAINST NCOV-2019. OUR LABORATORY IS HIGHLY SPECIALIZED IN THE RAPID GENERATION OF NEUTRALIZING MABS FROM HUMAN B CELLS. WE AIM TO APPLY THIS EXPERTISE TO GENERATE HUMAN NCOV-2019-SPECIFIC MABS, WHICH HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RAPIDLY ALLEVIATE THE GLOBAL HEALTH BURDEN IMPOSED BY NCOV-2019 THROUGH THREE CRITICAL MEASURES: PROPHYLACTIC, THERAPEUTIC, AND DIAGNOSTIC. BY INVESTIGATING THE HUMAN ANTIBODY RESPONSE TO NCOV-2019, WE WILL GAIN IMPORTANT INSIGHT INTO THE IMMUNOGENICITY AND IMMUNODOMINANCE OF NCOV-2019 VIRAL PROTEINS, WHICH WILL IN TURN INFORM WHICH VIRAL TARGETS WILL BE MOST IMPORTANT TO PURSUE WITH THERAPEUTICS AND VACCINES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROPOSED SUPPLEMENT ARE AS FOLLOWS: A) GENERATE PANELS OF HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS. COVID-19 PATIENT BLOOD WILL BE OBTAINED FROM SEVERAL SOURCES INCLUDING VERIFIED INFECTED SAMPLES FROM TOKYO THROUGH COLLABORATOR YOSHI KAWAOKA, THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO OR OTHER HOSPITALS FROM COVID-19 ADMITTED PATIENTS, OR THROUGH OTHER COLLABORATING LABS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST SARS-COV-2 SPIKE PROTEIN, SPIKE RBD AND ORF7 FROM DAVED FREEMONTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, VERSIONS OF THE SPIKE PROTEIN AND RBD FROM FLORIAN KRAMMERS LABORATORY, PLUS NSP3, NSP5, NSP9, NSP10, NSP15, NSP16, AND N PROTEIN FROM ANDRJEZ JOACHIMIACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LABORATORY, OR TO UNBIASED OTHER EPITOPES TARGETED BY ACTIVATED B CELLS AND PLASMABLASTS WILL BE DEVELOPED BY PATRICK WILSONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE RICKETTS BIOCONTAINMENT LABORATORY ON THE ARGONNE NATIONAL LABS CAMPUS AND AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO. B) EVALUATE THE B CELL RESPONSE OF COVID-19 PATIENTS: THE WILSON LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO WILL CHARACTERIZE PERIPHERAL BLOOD B CELLS REACTIVE TO SARS-COV-2 ENCODED PROTEINS OR ACTIVATED DURING INFECTION PLUS TFH CELLS USING SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOME AND CITE-SEQ ANALYSIS ON THE 10XGENOMICS PLATFORM. FROM THIS WE WILL LEARN ABOUT THE UNDERLYING IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THIS NOVEL CORONAVIRUS AND CORRELATE IMMUNE ACTIVITIES TO SERUM AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY PROTECTION, INFORMING FUTURE VACCINE-DESIGN AND EVALUATION EFFORTS. C) EVALUATE SERUM REACTIVITY TO A PANEL OF SARS-COV-2 PROTEINS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. SERUM FROM THE PATIENT BLOOD SAMPLES WILL ALSO BE ANALYZED FOR BINDING TO THE VARIOUS COVID-19 PROTEINS WE HAVE ACCESS TO BY ELISA ASSAYS AT THE RBL UNDER BSL3/SELECT AGENT CONDITIONS TO LEARN WHICH COVID-19 PROTEINS ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC, FURTHER GUIDING VACCINE DESIGN EFFORTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL BE VALUABLE AS POSSIBLE THERAPEUTIC AGENTS OR FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH SENSITIVITY AND HIGH SPECIFICITY DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL ALSO GUIDE AND TEMPLATE THE GENERATION OF VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST COVID-19. THIS CONTRACT SUPPLEMENT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. WE WILL DEVELOP A DATABASE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO AND AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY THAT CATALOGS THE DATA GENERATED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY VARIOUS MAPPING STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. FREMONT AND COLLEAGUES AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY WILL MIRROR THIS DATA AS WELL AS PROGRESS OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY EXPERIMENTS OF THE ANTIBODY-ANTIGEN COMPLEXES. THE TEAMS OF INVESTIGATORS AND COLLABORATING LABORATORIES WILL DEPOSIT ALL VALIDATED EPITOPE DATA WITH THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE (IEDB) WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF IDENTIFICATION. THEY ALSO WILL SUBMIT ALL STRUCTURAL DATA FOR DEPOSITION IN THE RCSB PROTEIN DATABASE (PDB). ADDITIONAL RESOURCE SHARING, INCLUDING PUBLICATION UPLOADING FOR PMC FREE-ACCESS, WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY ALL INVESTIGATORS. ALL MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE GREATER RESEARCH COMMUNITY IN PUBLIC DEPOSITORIES SUCH AS BEI OR UPON REQUEST.

description: OPTION 9A: 0258-A709-4612 THE AIM OF THE FIRST STUDY IS TO ISOLATE SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS DETECTED IN AUSTRIA. NEW ISOLATES WILL BE SEQUENCED USING WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING AND REPRESENTATIVE ISOLATES CHARACTERIZED IN VITRO BY GROWTH KINETICS AND NEUTRALIZATION PROFILES USING A SELECTION OF SERA FROM CONVALESCENT AND/OR VACCINATED INDIVIDUALS. FOR THE SECOND STUDY, SERA FROM VACCINATED AND/OR CONVALESCENT INDIVIDUALS WILL BE COLLECTED. NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS WILL BE PERFORMED AGAINST A PANEL OF SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS TO CHARACTERIZE THE NEUTRALIZATION PROFILE OF THE SERA. OPTION 9B: 0258-A730-4612 ISOLATION AND ANTIGENIC CHARACTERIZATION OF NEW VIRUS VARIANTS IN AUSTRIA THE OVERALL AIM OF THE PROJECT IS THE ANTIGENIC CHARACTERIZATION OF NEW SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS. POSITIVE SWAB AND GARGLE SAMPLES WILL BE SEQUENCED VIA OXFORD NANOPORE SEQUENCING. FOR INTERESTING VARIANTS, VIRUS WILL BE ISOLATED AND ANTIGENICALLY CHARACTERIZED USING A PANEL OF HUMAN FIRST INFECTION SERA. ANTIGENIC CHARTOGRAPHIE BASED ON HUMAN SERA IS LIMITED FOR NEWER VARIANTS AS HUMAN FIRST EXPOSURE SERA BEYOND THE EARLY OMICRON VARIANTS ARE RARE OR NOT AVAILABLE. THEREFORE, WE WILL COMPARE ANTIGENIC MAPS DERIVED FROM HUMAN OR ANIMAL SERA. ADDITIONALLY, NEUTRALIZATION PROFILES OF NEW VIRUS VARIANTS WILL BE ANALYZED IN SERA FROM INDIVIDUALS AFTER MORE COMPLEX EXPOSURE HISTORIES, E.G. BIVALENT BOOSTER IMMUNIZATION, HYBRID IMMUNITY, MULTIPLE INFECTIONS.

AIM 2: DEVELOP CONSENSUS HEADLESS MINI-HA TO TARGET INFLUENZA A AND B USING SEVERAL STRATEGIES TO CLUSTER INFLUENZA SEQUENCE ALIGNMENTS WE WILL GENERATE AS POSITION-SPECIFIC SCORING MATRIX (PSSM) TO GENERATE A CONSENSUS-BASED REDESIGN OF THE TEMPLATE STRUCTURE WHICH WILL BE TAKEN FROM VARIANTS OF AIM 1. TO AVOID BIAS CAUSED BY THE STARTING CRYSTAL STRUCTURE, WE WILL UTILIZE MULTIPLE TEMPLATES. CONSTRUCTS WILL BE EXPRESSED AND BIOCHEMICALLY EVALUATED. STATEMENT OF WORK (DR. TOMPKINS) AIM 3: EVALUATION OF EFFICACY OF GENERATED CONSTRUCTS IN VIVO TOP DESIGNS THAT SHOW BINDING TO STEM-SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN MICE. VACCINATED MICE WILL BE BLED FOR ASSESSMENT OF SERUM ANTIBODY RESPONSES AND THEN CHALLENGED WITH H1, H3, OR IBV TO ASSESS EFFICACY. SERUM WILL BE EVALUATED FOR ITS NEUTRALIZATION POTENTIAL AND IN ABSENCE OF NEUTRALIZATION, WE WILL EXAMINE FC-MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF CLEARANCE. OPTION 11I (0258-A482-4609) MUCOSAL IMMUNITY, WHICH HAS BEEN SHOWN TO OFFER INCREASED BREADTH OF PROTECTION, IS UNDERSTUDIED IN FERRETS DUE TO A LACK OF FERRET IMMUNOGLOBULIN REAGENTS. THIS IS A CRITICAL GAP AS FERRETS ARE ALSO THE BEST MODEL TO STUDY INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTION AND TRANSMISSION. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP IN AIM 1, WE WILL ENGINEER AND EXPRESS FERRET IGA, DIMERIC IGA (DIGA), AND SECRETORY IGA (SIGA) SPECIFIC FOR THE CONSERVED CENTRAL STALK DOMAIN OF INFLUENZA A VIRUS HA, USING CR9114 VARIABLE REGION SEQUENCES (FE-IGA-CR9114), AND THE VARIABLE REGIONS OF CR3022 (ANTI-SARS-COV-2 SPIKE) TO PRODUCE FE-IGA-CR3022, FOR USE AS A CONTROL. WE WILL ALSO PRODUCE RECOMBINANT FERRET IGG AS A COMPLEMENTARY REAGENT. THE FERRET MABS WILL BE CHARACTERIZED BY SDS-PAGE AND WESTERN BLOT. ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAYS (ELISAS) WILL BE PERFORMED TO CONFIRM HA AND SPIKE SPECIFICITY AND ANTI-FERRET ANTIBODY REACTIVITY AND CONFIRMED THROUGH ASSESSING AVIDITY AND AFFINITY THROUGH BIOLAYER INTERFEROMETRY (BLI). FULLY FORMED FE-SIGA, FE-DIGA, AND FE-MIGA, AS WELL AS FE-IGA-CR9114 AND -CR3022 COMPLEXED WITH HA OR SPIKE, RESPECTIVELY, WILL BE PURIFIED BY SEC AND USED FOR STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS USING NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (NS-EM). THE FULLY CHARACTERIZED FE-IGA PROTEINS WILL BE USED TO ASSESS COMMERCIAL ANTI-FERRET IGA REAGENTS TO DETERMINE WHICH COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS AND LOTS ARE RELIABLE. THIS REAGENT QUALITY CONTROL INFORMATION WILL BE SHARED WITH THE NETWORK. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS RECOMBINANT FERRET IGA PROTEINS FOR BREADTH OF REACTIVITY AND IN FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS, IN VITRO AND IN VIVO. FERRET SIGA-CR9114 WILL BE TESTED FOR ELISA AND HAI REACTIVITY TO A PANEL OF ANTIGENICALLY DIVERSE VIRUSES SPANNING BOTH FLUAV HA GROUPS AND FLUBV LINEAGES. MULTIVALENT IGA TARGETING THE HA STALK HAS BEEN SHOWN TO INHIBIT NA ACTIVITY VIA STERIC HINDERANCE, SO WE WILL MEASURE NA INHIBITION ACTIVITY BY ELLA. WE WILL ASSESS NAB POTENCY IN MICRONEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS, COMPARING IGG TO IGA, DIGA, AND SIGA.
