description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS-2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORT AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDY. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL, AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, BIOREPOSITORY, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID-19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 WAS REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 03 TO ADDRESS AN INCREASE IN THE TARGET ENROLLMENT TO 1,100 PARTICIPANTS UNDER INVITE PROTOCOL V2.0 ASSUMPTIONS. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 03 ADDRESSED COSTS FOR THE PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR A RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED TRIAL OF THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF TECOVIRIMAT FOR THE TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX VIRUS DISEASE, SUCH AS PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT AND RESEARCH SITE ASSESSMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 IS BEING REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 04 NOW REFERRED TO AS THE INVITE COVID-19 OBSERVATIONAL VACCINE STUDY TO INCLUDE THE PALM 007 MONKEYPOX TREATMENT RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT (TPOXX) IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 05 ADDRESSED INCLUDING TO INCLUDE COST TO SUPPORT PALM 007 MONKEYPOX RCT BUDGET TO INCLUDE (1) ONE MONTH OF STAFFING AND INITIAL MEETING COSTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION AT THE CLINICAL SITE IN TUNDA FROM AUGUST 1, 2022 THROUGH AUGUST 30, 2022; AND (2) INCLUDE THE KOLE SITE PREPARATION/RENOVATION COSTS.

description: THIS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT (R&D) CONTRACT WAS AWARDED AS PART OF THE MULTIPLE-AWARD INDEFINITE DELIVERY, INDEFINITE QUANTITY (IDIQ) CONTRACTS FOR THE CONTRACEPTIVE CLINICAL TRIALS NETWORK (CCTN) FEMALE SITES. THE PURPOSE OF THESE CONTRACTS IS TO ESTABLISH A NETWORK OF CLINICAL RESEARCH SITES COLLABORATING TO EVALUATE NEW FEMALE CONTRACEPTIVE DRUGS AND DEVICES FOR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN PHASE I, II, III AND IV CLINICAL TRIALS. THIS CONTRACT SHALL PROVIDE THE REQUISITE PERSONNEL, FACILITIES AND SERVICES TO CONDUCT AND SUPPORT THESE CLINICAL TRIALS. THE DATA COLLECTED FROM THE CCTN THROUGH CLINICAL TRIALS ON NEW ENTITIES ARE THE BASIS FOR ADVANCING CANDIDATE DRUGS AND DEVICES THROUGH DEVELOPMENT WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF SUBMISSION TO THE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) IN SUPPORT OF REGULATORY APPROVAL. PRODUCTS EVALUATED IN THE CCTN ARE SELECTED TO ADDRESS GAPS IN AVAILABLE CONTRACEPTIVE TECHNOLOGY, INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SAFER, MORE ACCEPTABLE, AND MORE ACCESSIBLE CONTRACEPTIVE METHODS FOR WOMEN, INCLUDING WOMEN WHO ARE OBESE OR HAVE OTHER RISK FACTORS THAT LIMIT THEIR USE OF EXISTING METHODS.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 3. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1 AND 2 IS ONGOING. 1. DR. HAWN WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS LARGELY COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 3. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL. 2. DR. HAWN WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. HAWN WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. HAWN WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

description: THE BAROUCH LABORATORY AT BIDMC WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE URDAHL LABORATORY AT SCRI IN THE EVALUATION OF TB VACCINE CANDIDATES AND THE DETERMINATION OF IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION IN MICE. VACCINES INCLUDE BCG AND LPRG. VACCINES WILL BE EVALUATED IN MULTIPLE STRAINS OF MICE (E.G. C57BL/6, C3H/FEJ, AND C129F1) AND WILL BE ADMINISTERED BY BOTH SC AND IV ROUTES. MTB STRAINS WILL BE PROVIDED BY SCRI FOR CHALLENGE STUDIES. IN YEAR 3 WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF THE LPRG VACCINE AND ITS PROTECTIVE EFFICACY AGAINST CHALLENGE USING SPECIFIC CONDITIONS AND COMBINATIONS OF MOUSE AND MTB CHALLENGE STRAINS BASED ON THE RESULTS OF THE SCREENING COMPLETED IN YEARS 1 & 2. WE WILL ALSO TEST ADDITIONAL VARIABLES IN THE MOST PROMISING CONDITIONS/COMBINATIONS. UNDER THESE SETTINGS WE WILL INVESTIGATE IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION IN MICE.

description: DR. MICHAEL GERNERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB, UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON SCHOOL OF MEDICINE Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY, WILL HAVE A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB PROPOSED MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS, THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, DR. GERNERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GROUP WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. THE GERNER LAB WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF VARIOUS CHEMOTACTIC OR ADHESION MOLECULES IN GUIDING IMMUNE CELLS TO VARIOUS SITES WITHIN THE INFECTED LUNG TISSUES AND LYMPHOID ORGANS, AS WELL AS IN MEDIATING PROTECTION FROM MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. IN YEAR 3 DR GERNERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S TEAM WILL: I. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. II. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EXPERIMENTS AIMED TO ELUCIDATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES WITHIN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION, WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. III. PERFORM AND ASSIST WITH COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES OF SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING DATA OBTAINED BY OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. THIS WILL INVOLVE IMPLEMENTATION OF ADVANCED STATISTICAL ALGORITHMS TO STUDY A) CELLULAR HETEROGENEITY AND IMMUNE RESPONSES WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, B) ANALYZE EXPRESSION OF CHEMOTACTIC AND ADHESION MOLECULES THAT MAY REGULATE CELLULAR POSITIONING, AS WELL AS C) RECEPTOR-LIGAND ANALYSIS ON SINGLE CELL DATA TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL MOLECULES OF INTEREST THAT MAY BE INVOLVED IN CELLULAR ORGANIZATION AND FORMATION OF TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS WHICH CORRELATE WITH PROTECTION. IV. IDENTIFIED MOLECULES OF INTEREST FROM PART III) WILL ALSO BE USED TO POWER FOLLOW-UP MICROSCOPY AND SPATIAL ANALYSIS STUDIES TO REVEAL HOW THESE CORRELATE WITH CELLULAR ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTION WITHIN INFECTED LUNG AND LYMPH NODE TISSUES. V. PERFORM CROSS-SPECIES CORRELATIVE ANALYSES USING GENERATED SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING DATA TO IDENTIFY CONSERVED FEATURES OF IMMUNE CELL RESPONSES TO INFECTION AND AFTER IMMUNIZATION. VI. DATA FROM I-V) WILL HELP IDENTIFY SPECIFIC MOLECULES OF INTEREST FOR FOLLOW-UP FUNCTIONAL STUDIES. AS EXAMPLE, IDENTIFIED CHEMOTACTIC MOLECULES WILL BE TARGETED USING EITHER AVAILABLE KO MICE OR USING IN VIVO BLOCKADE WITH ANTIBODIES OR SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITORS. ALTERNATIVELY, IMMUNE CELLS CAN BE ENGINEERED EX VIVO (E.G. CRISPR) TO ENHANCE TRAFFICKING OF EFFECTOR CELLS TO SPECIFIC TISSUE SITES DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. BASED ON THE LENGTH OF TIME THAT I-V) STEPS ABOVE WILL TAKE TO IMPLEMENT, THESE FUNCTIONAL MAY BE PERFORMED IN LATER YEARS OF THE CONTRACT. VII. BEGIN TESTING / DEVELOPMENT OF HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE.

description: PROJECT OBJECTIVE: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF A LARGE (N=6,012), WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF AFRICAN AMERICAN WOMEN WITH LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENTS OF CERVICAL LENGTH BEGINNING IN THE MID- TRIMESTER AND THE COLLECTION OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL TO PERMIT GENOTYPING OF MOTHERS FOR THIS PROPOSAL. FOR FUTURE STUDIES, BIOBANKED SAMPLES OF OFFSPRING DNA, CERVICO-VAGINAL FLUID FOR THE MICROBIOME, AND OTHER BIOMARKERS INCLUDING CYTOKINES ARE AVAILABLE. THE COHORT ALSO INCLUDES 83 WOMEN TREATED WITH VAGINAL PROGESTERONE DUE TO A PREGNANCY COMPLICATED BY A SHORT CERVIX. THE KEY COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE A GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (GWAS) OF MATERNAL DNA FOR LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF ULTRASOUND-MEASURED CERVICAL LENGTH AS A QUANTITATIVE TRAIT. THE FINDINGS OF THE DISCOVERY GWAS WILL BE VALIDATED BY TARGETED GENOTYPING OF AN INDEPENDENT AFRICAN-AMERICAN COHORT. THE VALIDATED LOCI WILL THEN BE USED TO ASSESS HOW SELECT GENOTYPES CAN MODIFY PROGESTERONE RESPONSIVENESS. WORK BEING PERFORMED: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CONTINUED DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION, AND INTERPRETATION OF THE LONGITUDINAL MODELING FRAMEWORK AND ANALYTIC PLAN. SPECIFICALLY, THE WORK WILL INCLUDE (1) FINALIZING THE PRETERM BIRTH (PTB) RISK MODEL, (2) EXTERNALLY VALIDATING PROSPECTIVE ASSOCIATIONS IDENTIFIED BETWEEN THE GROWTH PARAMETERS FOR CERVICAL LENGTH (CL) AND PTB OUTCOMES, (3) DEVELOPING AND PILOT TESTING A MODEL TO FORMALLY ASSESS MEDIATION OF GENOMIC INFLUENCES (E.G., POLYGENIC RISK SCORES; PGX) ON PTB VIA PREGNANCY-SPECIFIC CHANGES IN CL, AND (4) EXTENDING THE AFOREMENTIONED MEDIATION MODEL TO TEST FOR MODERATION OF PGX ASSOCIATIONS (I.E., WITH CL GROWTH PARAMETERS AND PTB) BY SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS (SNPS). DELIVERABLES: QUARTER 1 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ AUGUST 15TH, 2022: DEVELOPMENT OF A TESTABLE MODEL OF MEDIATION OF GENOMIC INFLUENCES ON PRETERM BIRTH OUTCOMES VIA PREGNANCY-SPECIFIC CHANGES IN CERVICAL LENGTH QUARTER 2 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ NOVEMBER 15TH, 2022: PUBLICATION OF PROSPECTIVE LINKS BETWEEN PRE-PREGNANCY MATERNAL COVARIATES AND PRETERM BIRTH OUTCOMES, AND MEDIATION THROUGH PREGNANCY-SPECIFIC CHANGES IN CERVICAL LENGTH; PILOT TESTING OF MODERATED-MEDIATION MODELS.

description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS-2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES.SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORT AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDY.THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL, AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, BIOREPOSITORY, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES.THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID-19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 WAS REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 03 TO ADDRESS AN INCREASE IN THE TARGET ENROLLMENT TO 1,100 PARTICIPANTS UNDER INVITE PROTOCOL V2.0 ASSUMPTIONS. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 03 ADDRESSED COSTS FOR THE PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR A RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED TRIAL OF THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF TECOVIRIMAT FOR THE TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX VIRUS DISEASE, SUCH AS PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT AND RESEARCH SITE ASSESSMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 IS BEING REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 04 NOW REFERRED TO AS THE INVITE COVID-19 OBSERVATIONAL VACCINE STUDY TO INCLUDE THE PALM 007 MONKEYPOX TREATMENT RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT (TPOXX) IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 04 ADDRESSED INCLUDING COSTS TO SUPPORT THE RENOVATION AND PREPARATION REQUIREMENTS AT THE TUNDA SITE.

description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW VACCINATION ALTERS THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING TO THE EFFECTS OF VACCINATION USING SEVERAL DIFFERENT VACCINATION MODALITIES AND A MOUSE MODEL OF AEROSOL CHALLENGE. ALL INFECTION STUDIES WILL TAKE PLACE IN THE ABSL-3 FACILITY IN LSL (N163) AT UMASS AMHERST. DR. ROTHCHILD WILL BE FULLY INVOLVED IN THE PROJECT THROUGHOUT THE YEAR, INCLUDING DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION AND ANALYSES TO ENSURE THAT THE SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES ARE MET, IN ADDITION TO ALL TRAINING AND SUPERVISION IN ABSL-3 BIOCONTAINMENT PRACTICES. LINH PHAM WILL HELP TO SET-UP AND PERFORM THE IN VIVO MURINE MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION STUDIES AND IN VITRO STUDIES UNDER DR. ALISSA ROTHCHILDÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUPERVISION. SHE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO DATA ANALYSIS AND MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION. MARITZA CERVANTES WILL ASSIST IN THE IN VIVO MURINE MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION STUDIES, VACCINATIONS, AND PERFORM ADDITIONAL RELEVANT IMMUNOLOGICAL AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY EXPERIMENTS. SHE WILL ALSO MANAGE THE MOUSE COLONY FOR THE RESEARCH GROUP.

description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE IMPAC-TB PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING AND POTENTIALLY EVEN ERADICATING MTB. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. 1. DR. GALE WILL LEAD THE DATA AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TEAM THIS TEAM, COMPRISED OF MEMBERS FROM ALL LABORATORIES IN IMPAC-TB, WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A DATA AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR 1) STORAGE, RETRIEVAL, AND ANALYSIS OF CENTER-GENERATED DATA 2) CATALOGING AND REPORTING OF ALL CENTER-GENERATED REAGENTS AND RESOURCES, AND 3) DISSEMINATION OF DATA AND CENTER RESULTS INTERNALLY, TO OTHER NIAID-SUPPORTED PROGRAMS, AND TO THE BROADER SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL TAKE PLACE OVER THE SEVEN YEARS OF THE CONTRACT. IN YEAR 3, THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT THE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM WITH ASSISTANCE FROM OTHER TEAM MEMBERS. 2. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. IN YEAR 3, WE WILL PERFORM RNA-SEQ ASSAYS ON SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM NHP STUDIES PERFORMED IN BOTH YEAR 1 AND YEAR 2. TASKS INCLUDE 1) RECEIVING SAMPLES FROM THE PICKER LAB, 2) ISOLATING RNA FROM THESE SAMPLES AND PERFORMING RNA QC, 3) CONSTRUCTING RNA-SEQ LIBRARIES AND LIBRARY QC USING THE ISOLATED RNA, AND 4) GENERATING SEQUENCING DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES. 3. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON THE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. IN YEAR 3, WE WILL ANALYSIS DATA SETS GENERATED FROM THE RNA-SEQ ASSAY THAT WE PERFORM USING SAMPLES FROM THE NHP STUDIES. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRIXES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND WHEN APPROPRIATE RULE-BASED MODELING.

description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF OUR PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING OR ERADICATING MTB. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON- HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROGRAM ARE AS FOLLOWS: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ OBJECTIVE #1: CHARACTERIZE IMMUNE LANDSCAPES IN THE LUNG AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES ASSOCIATED WITH THE CAPACITY TO ERADICATE OR CONTROL A SUBSEQUENT MTB CHALLENGE. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ OBJECTIVE #2: DEFINE EARLY IMMUNE EVENTS IN THE LUNG AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES THAT LEAD TO MTB ERADICATION OR CONTAINMENT PRIOR TO OVERT DISEASE. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ OBJECTIVE #3: ELUCIDATE THE SPATIAL ORGANIZATION OF SUCCESSFUL MTB CONTAINMENT DURING CHRONIC INFECTION. OHSU PROGRAM #1: ANALYSIS OF PROTECTIVE ANTI-TB IMMUNITY IN NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP) RM ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO MTB CHALLENGE, EVEN WITH VERY LOW DOSE, AND SHOW VERY SIMILAR IMMUNOLOGY AND PATHOLOGY TO HUMAN, MAKING THIS MODEL THE CLOSEST-TO-HUMAN FULLY MANIPULATABLE ANIMAL MODEL AVAILABLE FOR TB RESEARCH. THE OHSU NHP TEAM, LED BY DR. LOUIS PICKER, HAS EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN NHP IMMUNOLOGY AND THE NHP MTB MODEL, USING THE BSL-3 FACILITIES AVAILABLE AT THE OREGON NATIONAL PRIMATE RESEARCH CENTER. IN ADDITION, DR. PICKERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GROUP HAS INDEPENDENTLY DEVELOPED THE RHCMV/TB VACCINE, WHICH HAS BEEN SHOWN TO PROVIDE 60-70% PROTECTION AGAINST DISEASE PROGRESSION WITH HIGHLY PATHOGENIC ERDMAN MTB IN RHESUS MACAQUES. UNDERSTANDING THE IMMUNOLOGIC BASIS OF THIS EFFICACY, AS WELL AS THE EFFICACY OF OTHER VACCINE MODALITIES, OFFERS A UNIQUE PATH TO IDENTIFY IMMUNOLOGIC MECHANISMS ABLE TO EFFECTIVELY COMBAT MTB INFECTION. SINCE A MAJOR HYPOTHESIS UNDERLYING THE EFFICACY OF RHCMV/TB VACCINE VECTORS IS THE POTENTIAL OF THE EFFECTOR DIFFERENTIATED MTB-SPECIFIC CD4+ AND/OR CD8+ T CELL ELICITED BY THESE VECTORS TO INTERCEPT NASCENT TB INFECTION EARLIER THAN OTHER TYPES OF RESPONSES WE ARE ESPECIALLY INTERESTED IN USING THE NHP MODEL TO DEFINE EARLY IMMUNOLOGIC PROCESSES IN MTB, PROCESSES THAT OCCUR BEFORE THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MATURATION OF GRANULOMAS (WHICH IN OUR NHP MODEL CORRESPONDS TO EVENTS PRIOR TO 4 WEEKS POST CHALLENGE, THE TIMEPOINT WHICH IN MOST INFECTIONS, MATURE GRANULOMAS BECOME APPARENT). THUS, OUR PRIMARY CURRENT OBJECTIVE IN THIS PROGRAM IS COMPARE AND CONTRAST IMMUNE RESPONSES TO MTB CHALLENGE AT, AND PRIOR TO 4 WEEKS POST CHALLENGE IN MONKEYS THAT HAVE BEEN EITHER LEFT UNVACCINATED OR WERE PREVIOUSLY VACCINATED WITH CONVENTIONAL BCG, IV BCG AND RHCMV/TB VACCINES. description: TASK 1: TRANSITION HITECH TA WEBSITE AIR WILL LEAD THIS TASK. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL OVERSEE AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR THE PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT TASKS AND WILL IMPLEMENT CHANGES AND REVISIONS. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ADVISE AND OVERSEE WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS TASK. KEY COMPONENTS OF THIS TASK INCLUDE ROUTINE MAINTENANCE OF THE REPOSITORY CONTENT INCLUDING CONTENT UPLOADS AND UPDATES TO EXISTING RESOURCES INCLUDING THE AUDIT TOOLKIT AND FAQS. THIS TASK ALSO INCLUDES SECTION 508 REVIEWS OF BOTH ARTIFACTS AND CONTENT DEVELOPED BY OTHER MEMBERS OF THE UI MET. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ALSO SERVE AS THE QA REVIEWER FOR THESE ACTIVITIES. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL MANAGE THE PERMISSIONS AND REQUESTS FOR ACCESS OF HUNDREDS OF SITE USERS TO ACCESS THE VARIOUS TABS, PAGES AND MODULES. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PERFORM AN UPGRADE TO THE WEBSITE PLATFORM TO ENSURE OPTIMAL SITE PERFORMANCE AND SECURITY. DURING THE BASE YEAR, SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP A SYSTEM OF SUBFOLDERS FOR ORGANIZING AND ARCHIVING WEBSITE CONTENT, MAINTAINING AN INVENTORY, AND TRANSFERRING THE CONTENT TO A CMS ENVIRONMENT. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ALSO ARCHIVE THE FULL WEBSITE AND TRANSFER IT TO CMS. BECAUSE THE WEBSITE IS BEING RETIRED IN DECEMBER 2022, THERE WILL BE NO HOURS BUDGETED FOR TASK 1 IN THE OPTION YEAR. TASKS 2, 3, 4: PROJECT MANAGEMENT TASKS SUBCONTRACTOR WILL CONTRIBUTE TO TASK 2 (CONTRACTOR PROJECT MANAGEMENT REQUIREMENTS), TASK 3 (CONTRACTOR DEVELOP A PROJECT MANAGEMENT PLAN [PMP]), AND TASK 4 (CONTRACTOR QUARTERLY STATUS REPORT REQUIREMENTS). SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PREPARE FOR AND PARTICIPATE IN THE KICK-OFF MEETING AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE PMP AND QUARTERLY UPDATES. TASK 7: STATES QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTING ON MEANINGFUL USE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL SET UP AND MAINTAIN THE DATA COLLECTION AND TASK 7 WITHIN THE WEBSITE. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL MAKE MODIFICATIONS AND PREPARATIONS TO THE USER INTERFACE AND DATABASE TO PREPARE FOR THE DATA COLLECTION. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE A TESTING ENVIRONMENT AND THEN A PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT FOR THE PREPARATION AND LAUNCH PHASES. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND TROUBLESHOOTING AS NEEDED, INCLUDING ASSISTANCE WITH USER ACCOUNTS PERTAINING TO THE DATA COLLECTION PROCESS. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ALSO PRODUCE THE OUTPUT DATA FILES FOR THE MET. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE FUNCTIONING IN AN ADVISORY ROLE AND QA REVIEWER ON THE TASK. TASK 9: DEVELOP SUPPORT ACT REPORT AND PUBLISH ON WEBSITE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP A REPORT ABOUT SUCCESSFUL PDMP PRACTICES, THEIR IMPACT ON OPIOID PRESCRIBING OUTCOMES AND ADDITIONAL GUIDANCE TO STATES ON HOW TO INCREASE PROVIDER USE OF PDMPS. THE DESIGN WILL UTILIZE CONTRIBUTION ANALYSIS TO GUIDE THE DATA AND WRITING. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL LEAD THE DESIGN OF THE CONTRIBUTION ANALYSIS, CONDUCTING THE ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN, DEVELOPING A THEORY OF CHANGE AND DESIGNING THE INITIAL LOGIC MODEL WHICH WILL CAPTURE BOTH PDMP-RELATED AS WELL AS EXTERNAL FACTORS WHICH IMPACT OPIOID PRESCRIPTION OUTCOMES. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ALSO DESIGN DATA COLLECTION PROTOCOLS IN ORDER TO USE QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE DATA FROM SELECT STATES AS EVIDENCE TO INFORM AND UPDATE THE MODEL AND CONTRIBUTION NARRATIVE. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ALSO LEAD THE REPORT WRITING OF THIS TASK, ENSURE THAT IT IS 508 COMPLIANT AND POSTED ON THE CMS WEBSITE BEFORE OCTOBER 1, 2023. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL LEAD THE QUALITATIVE DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS FOR THIS TASKÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CONTRIBUTION ANALYSIS PROCESS. THIS INCLUDES IDENTIFYING AND CONTACTING 3 OR 4 REPRESENTATIVES OF THE SELECTED EXEMPLARY STATE(S) (E.G., PDMP DIRECTOR, KEY STAFF IN A STATEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PDMP AGENCY), DESIGNING SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEW GUIDES, CARRYING OUT INTERVIEWS AND ANALYZING INTERVIEW DATA IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS RELATED TO THE IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVENESS OF STRATEGIES THAT SEEK TO PROMOTE PROVIDER USE OF THE PDMP. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL LEAD THE QUANTITATIVE DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS FOR THIS TASKSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ CONTRIBUTION ANALYSIS PROCESS. THIS INCLUDES COLLECTING, COMPARING AND ANALYZING T-MSIS DATA FROM SELECT STATES. THIS DATA WILL BE TRIANGULATED WITH THE INTERVIEW DATA AND USED TO INFORM AND UPDATE THE CONTRIBUTION NARRATIVE ON AN ONGOING BASIS. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE GENERAL SUPPORT FOR THIS TASK, SUCH AS COORDINATING MEETINGS WITH STATE PDMP REPRESENTATIVES, SCHEDULING INTERVIEWS WITH PARTICIPANTS, DISTRIBUTING HOURS AND RESOURCES AMONG TEAM STAFF, AS WELL AS CLEANING, CATEGORIZING AND ANALYZING DATA.

description: BASE ACTIVITIES: DEVELOP IMMUNE RESPONSE ASSAYS AND HARMONIZE PROTOCOLS AND ASSAYS TASK B.2: IMMUNOLOGICAL ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, HARMONIZATION OF PROTOCOLS AND IN VIVO STUDIES TASK B.4: HUMAN CLINICAL PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE THAT BIOLOGICAL RESULTS GENERATED IN THE VARIOUS CONSORTIUM LABS ARE COMPARABLE, WE WILL STANDARDIZE THE PRIMARY ASSAYS USED IN IMMUNOGENICITY ASSESSMENTS FOR EACH SPECIES (TABLE 1). IN LINE WITH THE PROJECT GOALS TO DEVELOP A CROSS-SPECIES INTERROGATION PLATFORM, WE WILL HARMONIZE KEY ASSAYS ACROSS MULTIPLE SPECIES AND ENSURE STATISTICAL PLANS FOR CROSS SPECIES ANALYSIS ARE IN PLACE. SCRI WILL APPOINT AN OVERALL TASK LEADER TO COORDINATE AND OVERSEE THE WORK. ALL ASSAY STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) WILL BE SHARED WITH A PRECLINICAL OR CLINICAL LABORATORY LEAD, DESIGNATED FOR EACH ASSAY, WHO WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HARMONIZING. FINAL SOPS WILL BE SHARED AND LEAD ASSAY LABS WILL CONDUCT SIDE-BY-SIDE TRAINING SESSIONS, AS WELL AS, MAINTAIN AND DISTRIBUTE COMMON REFERENCE STANDARDS AND REAGENTS, SUCH AS IDENTICAL STIMULATION ANTIGENS (BCG, PPD, SEB, 15-MER PEPTIDES, NTM AND M.TB LYSATE AND CULTURE FILTRATE AND UNSTIMULATED) AND BCG VACCINATION STRAIN (BCG AJ/BCG SSI). THIS BASE-PERIOD HARMONIZATION WILL INCLUDE OPTIMIZED MULTICOLOR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE PANEL (OMIP) DEVELOPMENT. FURTHERMORE, IN THE BASE PERIOD WE WILL AGREE TO A SPECIFIC MONTH IN WHICH EACH TEAM WILL ANNUALLY THAW INFECTION STOCKS AND PLATE FOR BACTERIAL ENUMERATION TO ENSURE VIABILITY AND STOCK CONCENTRATION IS MAINTAINED OVER THE ENTIRE COURSE OF THE CONTRACT. THESE STOCK COUNTS AND VIABILITY MAINTENANCE TESTS WILL BE REPORTED BACK TO SCRI. FHCRC INDIVIDUALS WILL ENSURE THAT THE ASSAY HARMONIZATION EFFORTS WILL LEAD TO APPROACHES FOR THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS THAT ARE STATISTICALLY SOUND AND ADEQUATELY POWERED, INCLUDING EXPERIMENTS INVOLVING PRIMARY AND EXPLORATORY ENDPOINTS IN PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL STUDIES. DATA FROM HARMONIZATION EXPERIMENTS WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE STATISTICAL CENTER AND A FORMAL INTER-SITE AND INTER-SPECIES VARIABILITY ASSESSMENT WILL BE PERFORMED. VARIABILITY WILL BE DETERMINED USING COEFFICIENTS OF VARIATION (CV), MEAN AND STANDARD DEVIATION OF RESPONSES. DESIRED CUT-OFFS FOR ACCEPTABLE CVS WILL BE PRE-SPECIFIED FOR EACH ASSAY. IF CVÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S DO NOT MEET THESE CUT-OFFS, FOR EXAMPLE >30%, FURTHER EFFORTS WILL BE MADE TO STANDARDIZE THE ASSAYS AND HARMONIZATION ASSESSMENTS WILL BE REPEATED. A SUMMARY REPORT OF ALL ACTIVITIES AND STANDARDIZED PROTOCOLS FROM THE BASE PERIOD WILL BE DRAFTED AND SUBMITTED TO NIAID FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. FHCRC AND CSU WILL PROVIDE ALL THE NECESSARY DATA AND INPUT REQUIRED FOR THE COMPLETION AND ACCEPTANCE OF THE FINAL REPORT FOR BASE PERIOD ACTIVITIES. FHCRC WILL ALSO SERVE AS THE LEAD SITE (CLINICAL AND PRECLINICAL) FOR GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING WITH RNASEQ/NANOSTRING ASSAYS. TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS WILL BE FOCUSED ON IDENTIFYING A PERIPHERAL BLOOD SURROGATE ENDPOINT FOR THE BCG/MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB) ERDMAN/MTB HN878 CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN THE STATISTICAL LITERATURE THIS IS REFERRED TO A CORRELATE OF RISK (COR) OR CORRELATE OF PROTECTION (COP) ANALYSIS, WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF DEVELOPING A SURROGATE ENDPOINT (A KIND OF COP) FOR FUTURE VACCINE STUDIES. THE STRATEGY WILL BE TO START WITH AN UNBIASED RNA SEQUENCING APPROACH USING WHOLE-BLOOD HUMAN SAMPLES FROM PRE AND POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL LOOK FOR TRANSCRIPTS THAT ARE CORRELATED WITH BCG CFU AND BCG QPCR ASSAYS FROM BAL, THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCE AT POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS, WE WILL ALSO LOOK FOR CHANGES IN TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE RELATIVE TO THE DAY OF CHALLENGE AS A POTENTIAL CORRELATE OF CHALLENGE OUTCOME.

description: THE HARTFORD HOSPITAL TEAM WILL BE LED BY DR. MANDEEP KUMAR. WE EXPECT TO ENROLL 300 PATIENTS IN THIS STUDY WHO WILL HAVE A WIDE RANGE OF CLINICAL ISSUES THAT REQUIRE THE USE OF OPIATES FOR PAIN CONTROL. HH IS AN 830 BED HOSPITAL THAT SERVES PATIENTS LIVING IN GREATER HARTFORD, CT AND WHICH DISCHARGES OVER 13,000 PATIENTS TO HOME IN A GIVEN YEAR. WE SERVE A VERY DIVERSE GROUP OF PATIENTS AND THUS CAN EXPECT TO ENROLL A MIX OF AGES, GENDERS AND RACES/ETHNICITIES AND FINANCIAL SITUATIONS AS REFLECTED IN THEIR INSURANCE COVERAGE. AS SEEN HERE, OVER HALF OUR PATIENTS RECEIVE MEDICARE; TABLE X. PATIENTS: WE WILL ENROLL PATIENTS WHO ARE IDENTIFIED BY THE RESEARCH STAFF AS BEING DISCHARGED FROM THE MEDICINE SERVICE WITH AN OPIATE PRESCRIPTION. ACROSS OUR MEDICINE SERVICES, OVER 3000 PATIENTS ARE DISCHARGED WITH UNDER 10 DAYS OF AN OPIATE PRESCRIPTION. EXAMPLES OF THE CLINICAL SITUATIONS WHERE PATIENTS ARE DISCHARGED WITH A SHORT TERM OPIATE PRESCRIPTION INCLUDE: ACUTE PAIN DUE TO INJURIES SUCH AS SPRAINS, SHINGLES, ENDOMETRIOSIS, CARPAL TUNNEL SYNDROME, DIABETIC NEUROPATHY, FIBROMYALGIA, GOUT, KIDNEY STONES AND PAIN FOLLOWING INVASIVE PROCEDURES SUCH AS BIOPSIES. THESE PATIENTS ARE ONLY GIVEN A SHORT COURSE OF OPIATES AS THEY ARE EXPECTED TO FOLLOW UP WITH THEIR PRIMARY CARE PROVIDER FOR SUBSEQUENT PAIN MANAGEMENT. PATIENTS WITH CONDITIONS THAT REQUIRE MORE AGGRESSIVE PAIN MANAGEMENT WOULD NOT BE ELIGIBLE; THESE INCLUDE CONDITIONS SUCH AS SICKLE CELL DISEASE, CANCER, COMPLEX REGIONAL PAIN SYNDROME (CRPS). RECRUITMENT: ELIGIBLE PATIENTS WILL BE IDENTIFIED BY THE RESEARCH ASSISTANT WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF THE HOSPITALIST TEAM. THE PATIENTS WILL BE INVITED TO PARTICIPATE, AND THE STUDY DESCRIBED TO THEM AND CONSENT OBTAINED FOR THOSE WHO ELECT TO PARTICIPATE. WE WILL ATTEMPT TO RECRUIT CONSECUTIVE ELIGIBLE PATIENTS TO ENSURE THAT WE HAVE A REPRESENTATIVE MIX OF PATIENTS, USING AGE, GENDER AND RACE/ETHNICITY AS THE MAIN VARIABLES. IF OUR DATA ARE SIGNIFICANTLY SKEWED, WE WILL TARGET PATIENTS IN THE UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS FOR INCLUSION. ANY NEEDED DATA WILL BE COLLECTED AT THE TIME THAT CONSENT WAS OBTAINED AND STORED IN A SECURE DATABASE. STUDY ACTIVITIES. WHEN PATIENTS HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED AS STUDY PARTICIPANTS, THE MEDICATION WILL BE DELIVERED BY THE PHARMACY DEPARTMENT AS PART OF OUR MED-TO-BEDS PROGRAM. THE CLINICAL COORDINATOR AND/OR THE CLINICAL STAFF WILL REVIEW HOW TO USE NEW PACKAGING AND EXPECTATIONS AROUND FUTURE CONTACTS. THE PATIENTS WILL THEN BE CONTACTED BY THE UCONN TEAM TO COLLECT THE STUDY DATA.

description: UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND SCHOOL OF MEDICINE THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH ARE AS FOLLOWS. 1) TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED RISK FACTORS FOR ASYMPTOMATIC INTESTINAL CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND INCIDENCE OF INTESTINAL AND NON-INTESTINAL CRE ACQUISITION DURING ICU STAY AMONG PATIENTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICUS. DELIVERABLES: WE WILL DETERMINE BASELINE ADMISSION CRE PREVALENCE AND CRE ACQUISITION RATES IN THE ICUS IN THE STUDY HOSPITAL USING SCS. IN ADDITION, RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND CRE ACQUISITION DURING ICU STAY WILL BE DETERMINED. CRE PREVALENCE DETECTED BY ROUTINE CLINICAL CARE VERSUS SURVEILLANCE CULTURES WILL ALSO BE DETERMINED. 2) TO DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY UTILIZING BASELINE PHASE DATA FROM AIM 1. DELIVERABLES: WE WILL DETERMINE HOW ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE CRE RATE RATIOS IN THE ICUS COMPARE WITH SCS VERSUS LCS BASED ON VARIOUS DAYS OF THE WEEK IN THE TWO ICUS, AND WHETHER CLINICAL RISK FACTOR AND CLINICAL CULTURE INFORMATION COULD AUGMENT THE LCS STRATEGY. 3) TO DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION(S) ON INTESTINAL CRE COLONIZATION PREVALENCE AT DISCHARGE USING LCS STRATEGY. DELIVERABLES: WE WILL COMPARE THE CRE INCIDENCE RATE RATIOS BEFORE AND AFTER THE INTERVENTION TO DETERMINE THE FEASIBILITY OF LCS STRATEGY TO GUIDE INFECTION PREVENTION MEASURES. DR. SURBHI LEEKHA WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. GANDRA IN PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC INPUT INTO THE DESIGN AND CONDUCT OF ALL ASPECTS OF THIS PROPOSAL. SHE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE START-UP MEETING, REGULAR COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE STUDY TEAM AND CDC, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, DATA COLLECTION, AND DATA ANALYSIS. SHE WILL ALSO TRAVEL TO THE STUDY HOSPITAL IN INDIA TWICE DURING THE STUDY ALONG WITH WASHU TEAM. THE TRAVEL TO INDIA WILL DEPEND ON THE PANDEMIC SITUATION AND UNIVERSITY AND CDC GUIDELINES FOR TRAVEL.

description: SUMMARY OF WORK FOR AMERICAN RED CROSS (ARC); EXPANDED COHORT 2022 CONTINUED FOLLOW-UP SAMPLE ACQUISITION FROM 77,089 SURVEYED ARC REPEAT DONORS AND CHARACTERIZATION OF THEM AS PREVIOUSLY INFECTED, PREVIOUSLY VACCINATED, PREVIOUSLY INFECTED/VACCINATED, AND UNINFECTED/NON-VACCINATED DONORS. THE BUDGET COVERS SAMPLE ACQUISITION, PROCESSING AND REPOSITORY WORK, EPIDEMIOLOGY, LAB SERVICES, AND DONOR SURVEY WORK, INCLUDING QUARTERLY SURVEYS OF DONORS WHO RESPONDED TO BASELINE SURVEYS TO CAPTURE UPDATED VACCINATION AND SYMPTOM DATA ON AN ONGOING BASIS. A TOTAL OF 77,089 SURVEYED DONORS (58,139 CASES THROUGH JUNE 2021, THE END OF UNIVERSAL TESTING, AND 18,950 CONTROLS THROUGH DEC 2021) IDENTIFIED OVER THE YEAR OF UNIVERSAL COVID-19 ANTIBODY SCREENING, BASED ON ACTUAL ACCRUAL NUMBERS TOTALS 308,000 TUBES, WHICH ARE ESTIMATED TO BE SHIPPED FROM SCIENTIFIC AFFAIRS TO VITALANT FOR FURTHER TESTING. THE BUDGET COVERS THE COST OF THE TUBES AND SHIPPING FROM CREATIVE TESTING SOLUTIONS, SCIENTIFIC AFFAIRS LAB (SCIENTIFIC SUPPORT OFFICE, SSO) COST TO PROCESS THE TUBES AND SHIPPING OF THE TUBES TO VITALANT FOR TESTING OF ARCHIVED AND PROSPECTIVE SAMPLES USING THE ORTHO S IGG AND NC TOTAL IG ASSAYS WITH SUBSETS OF CASES WITH EVIDENCE OF VACCINE BREAKTHROUGH INFECTIONS, REINFECTIONS, VACCINE BOOSTING FOLLOWING INFECTION AND CONTROLS TESTED BY MSD AND RVPNT USING VARIANT-SPECIFIC ASSAYS, AND OTHER AGREED UPON ASSAYS AS APPROPRIATE, AND SHIPPING OF TUBES BACK FROM VITALANT TO THE SSO FOR STORAGE IN A REPOSITORY. DEMOGRAPHIC AND SURVEY DATA WILL BE PROVIDED USING A STANDARDIZED FORMAT DETERMINED IN COLLABORATION BETWEEN VITALANT AND THE ARC TO WESTAT FOR ANALYSIS.

description: DR. FERNANDO GENTA AND HIS TEAM WILL BE TESTING THE EFFICACY OF THE DIFFERENT PREPARATIONS OF ENCAPSULATED MANDARIN ORANGE OIL AND/OR ORANGE OIL (HENCEFORTH REFERRED TO AS "LARVICIDE") IN SEMI-FIELD TRIALS. TO THIS END, THE FOLLOWING EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED FOR THESE ENCAPSULATED OILS: 1. DETERMINING THE STABILITY AND THE EFFICACY OF THE LARVICIDE IN SMALL CONTAINERS (SEMI-FIELD TRIALS) UNDER VARYING WEATHER CONDITIONS (WINTER, SPRING, SUMMER) IN ENDEMIC URBAN AREAS AROUND RIO DE JANEIRO AND RECIFE, BRAZIL 2. TESTING THE EFFICACY OF THE LARVICIDE IN BRAZILIAN STRAINS OF MOSQUITOS THAT ARE RESISTANT TO STANDARD INSECTICIDES 3. DETERMINING THE EFFECT OF THE LARVICIDE ON OVIPOSITION OF FEMALE MOSQUITOS 4. DETERMINING THE FEEDING PREFERENCES OF MOSQUITO LARVAE WHEN LARVICIDE IS PRESENT

description: "LABORATORY TESTING WILL BE PERFORMED BY REAL TIME RT-PCR ON 2,000 SPECIMENS SENT TO THE LABORATORY. BRIEFLY, VIRAL RNA WILL BE EXTRACTED USING THE MAXMAX VIRAL/PATHOGEN II NUCLEIC ACID ISOLATION KIT (UP TO 2,000 PREPARATIONS, WHEN 200 Ã‚ÂΜL OF SAMPLE IS USED) (THERMOFISHER SCIENTIFIC CAT# A48383) ON THE KINGFISHER EXTRACTION PLATFORM USING THE TAQPATH COVID-19 COMBO KIT (INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE PUBLICATION NUMBER MAN0019181 REVISION G.0) ON THE QUANTSTUDIO 7 PRO REAL TIME PCR INSTRUMENT. THE ASSAY HAS BEEN VALIDATED TO MEET CLIA STANDARDS OF PERFORMANCE IN THE PERFORMING LABORATORY. PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE ASSAY INCLUDING ACCURACY, PRECISION AND SENSITIVITY (LIMIT OF DETECTION) WERE ASSESSED AND MET THE PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS PUBLISHED IN THE EUA INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE BY THE MANUFACTURER. IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT A MULTIPLEX FLU/COVID ASSAY WILL BE AVAILABLE BY THIS MANUFACTURER FOR THE UPCOMING INFLUENZA SEASON. INFLUENZA B LINEAGE AND A SUBTYPING ASSAYS WILL BE VALIDATED USING AVAILABLE PROBES AND PRIMERS PROVIDED BY THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION PRIOR TO THE INITIATION OF THE INFLUENZA SEASON ON THE AFOREMENTIONED EXTRACTION AND PCR SYSTEMS. RESULTS FOR TESTS WILL BE SENT TO THE ENROLLING SITES USING EXISTING REDCAP DATABASE INFRASTRUCTURE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH INVESTIGATOR. SAMPLES WILL BE STORED AND SHIPPED/RETURNED UPON REQUEST FOLLOWING TESTING."

description: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF A LARGE (N=6,012), WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF AFRICAN AMERICAN WOMEN WITH LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENTS OF CERVICAL LENGTH BEGINNING IN THE MIDTRIMESTER AND THE COLLECTION OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL TO PERMIT GENOTYPING OF MOTHERS FOR THIS PROPOSAL. FOR FUTURE STUDIES, BIOBANKED SAMPLES OF OFFSPRING DNA, CERVICO-VAGINAL FLUID FOR THE MICROBIOME,AND OTHER BIOMARKERS INCLUDING CYTOKINES ARE AVAILABLE. THE COHORT ALSO INCLUDES 83 WOMEN TREATED WITH VAGINAL PROGESTERONE DUE TO A PREGNANCY COMPLICATED BY A SHORT CERVIX. THE KEY COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE A GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (GWAS) OF MATERNAL DNA FOR LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF ULTRASOUND-MEASURED CERVICAL LENGTH AS A QUANTITATIVE TRAIT. THE FINDINGS OF THE DISCOVERY GWAS WILL BE VALIDATED BY TARGETED GENOTYPING OF AN INDEPENDENT AFRICAN-AMERICAN COHORT. THE VALIDATED LOCI WILL THEN BE USED TO ASSESS HOW SELECT GENOTYPES CAN MODIFY PROGESTERONE RESPONSIVENESS.

description: AMRITA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES, KOCHI, KERALA STATE, INDIA DR. SANJEEV SINGH WILL BE THE LEAD INVESTIGATOR AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND HE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. GANDRA AND ENSURE COMPLETION OF WORK AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL PROVIDE HIS INPUT IN PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT. HE WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR IRB SUBMISSION AND GETTING NECESSARY APPROVALS AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND HIRING STAFF AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ALSO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SUBMITTING THE PROTOCOL TO INDIAN HEALTH MINISTRY SCREENING COMMITTEE (HMSC) AND GETTING THEIR APPROVAL BEFORE STARTING THE PATIENT ENROLLMENT. HE WILL OVERSEE ACTIVITIES FOR TRAINING AND PILOT DATA COLLECTION AT AMRITA HOSPITAL WITH WASHU TEAM. HE WILL OVERSEE PATIENT ENROLLMENT PROCESS AND ENSURE THE TARGETS FOR PATIENT ENROLLMENT INCLUDED IN THIS STUDY PROTOCOL WILL REACH. HE WILL ENSURE ACCESS TO DOCUMENTS RELATED TO INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND PROVIDE INPUT ON THE INFECTION CONTROL INTERVENTIONS THAT CAN BE IMPLEMENTED AS PROPOSED IN THE STUDY PROTOCOL. HE WILL ENSURE THE INTERVENTIONS WILL BE IMPLEMENTED IN THE STUDY ICUS. HE WILL WORK WITH THE STUDY TEAM AT AMRITA HOSPITAL TO RESOLVE ANY ISSUES WITH DATA COLLECTION AND OVERSEE DATA COLLECTION PROCESS. HE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE TWICE MONTHLY MEETINGS WITH THE WASHU TEAM ON ZOOM. HE WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN DATA ANALYSIS AND FINAL REPORT. DR. ANU GEROGE WILL BE THE PROJECT COORDINATOR AT AMRITA HOSPITAL, AND SHE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. SINGH TO ENSURE COMPLETION OF WORK AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. SHE WILL ASSIST DR. SINGH FOR IRB SUBMISSION, GETTING NECESSARY APPROVALS AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND GETTING APPROVAL FROM INDIAN HMSC. SHE WILL ASSIST DR. SINGH TO COORDINATE ACTIVITIES FOR TRAINING AND PILOT DATA COLLECTION AT AMRITA HOSPITAL WITH DR. GANDRA AND DR. WARREN. SHE WILL OVERSEE DAY TO DAY PATIENT ENROLLMENT, DATA COLLECTION, SPECIMEN COLLECTION BY STUDY STAFF AND INFECTION CONTROL NURSES AND REPORT TO DR. SINGH WITH ANY ISSUES THAT ARISE. SHE WILL MAKE SURE INTERVENTIONS ARE IMPLEMENTED AS PART OF THE STUDY. SHE WILL COORDINATE THE TWICE MONTHLY MEETINGS WITH WASHU TEAM ON ZOOM. DR. ANIL KUMAR IS THE CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGIST AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ENSURE APPROPRIATE LABORATORY PROCEDURES ARE FOLLOWED IN PROCESSING THE PERI-RECTAL SWABS AND STORING THE ISOLATES DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. HE WILL MAINTAIN PAPER RECORDS FOR PERI-RECTAL SWAB CULTURE RESULTS. HE WILL DOCUMENT AND REPORT THE QUALITY CONTROL PROCESSES INVOLVED IN IDENTIFICATION OF THE ORGANISMS AND PERFORMING ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING BY VITEK AND REPORT THE RESULTS TO DR. GANDRA MONTHLY. HE WILL HELP IN GIVING ACCESS TO ALL POSITIVE CRE CULTURES TO STUDY STAFF FOR STUDY PERIOD. HE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE TWICE MONTHLY MEETINGS WITH WASHU TEAM. DR. ZUBAIR MOHAMED IS THE MEDICAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT SPECIALIST AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ASSIST THE STUDY STAFF WITH ENROLLMENT OF PATIENTS INTO THE STUDY, MAKE SURE NURSES OBTAIN SPECIMENS FORM ENROLLED PATIENTS, GIVE ACCESS TO NECESSARY MEDICAL RECORDS FOR DATA COLLECTION AND MAKE INFECTION CONTROL PRACTICES ARE FOLLOWED AS PER STUDY PROTOCOL. HE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ANU GEORGE AND DR. SANJEEV SINGH. DR. DIPU SATYAPALAN IS THE SURGICAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT SPECIALIST AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ASSIST THE STUDY STAFF WITH ENROLLMENT OF PATIENTS INTO THE STUDY, MAKE SURE NURSES OBTAIN SPECIMENS FORM ENROLLED PATIENTS, GIVE ACCESS TO NECESSARY MEDICAL RECORDS FOR DATA COLLECTION AND MAKE INFECTION CONTROL PRACTICES ARE FOLLOWED AS PER STUDY PROTOCOL. HE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ANU GEORGE AND DR. SANJEEV SINGH. TWO STUDY COORDINATORS WILL BE INVOLVED FOR ENROLLMENT OF PATIENT INTO THE STUDY, OBTAINING CONSENT FROM PATIENT OR FAMILY, OBTAIN SPECIMEN FROM ENROLLED PATIENTS, TRACK SPECIMEN COLLECTION, COLLECT CLINICAL DATA FROM TWO ICUS AND THE CRE POSITIVE CULTURES FROM THE MICROBIOLOGY LAB OBTAINED FROM 2 ICUS DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. THEY WILL COLLECT DATA ON VARIABLES INDICATED IN THE STUDY PROTOCOL AND ENTER ALL DATA INTO REDCAP. THEY WILL COORDINATE WITH DR. ANIL KUMAR REGARDING PERI-RECTAL CULTURE DATA AND CRE CLINICAL CULTURE DATA FROM STUDY ICUS. THEY WILL PERFORM DIRECT OBSERVATIONS TO RECORD THE COMPLIANCE WITH INFECTION CONTROL PRACTICES DURING PRE-INTERVENTION AND INTERVENTION PHASES AND ENTER THAT INFORMATION INTO REDCAP. THEY WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ANU GEORGE AND REPORTS ANY ISSUES TO DR. ANU GEORGE IMMEDIATELY. THEY MAY PARTICIPATE IN ZOOM MEETINGS ONCE A MONTH WITH WASHU TEAM. A MICROBIOLOGY LAB TECHNICIAN WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROCESSING THE SPECIMENS (PERI-RECTAL SWABS), PLATING THEM ON CHROMOGENIC AGAR, IDENTIFYING POTENTIAL CRE COLONIES, PERFORM IDENTIFICATION AND SUSCEPTIBILITY. HE WILL PERFORM NECESSARY QUALITY CONTROL EXPERIMENTS. HE/SHE WILL MAINTAIN A RECORD OF ALL STUDY SAMPLES WITH RESULTS. HE/SHE WILL WORK UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. ANIL KUMAR. AIM 1: TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED RISK FACTORS FOR ASYMPTOMATIC INTESTINAL CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND INCIDENCE OF INTESTINAL AND NON-INTESTINAL CRE ACQUISITION USING SCS STRATEGY AND CLINICAL CULTURE DATA DURING ICU STAY AMONG PATIENTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICUS WE WILL PROSPECTIVELY ENROLL CONSENTED PATIENTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICU AT AMRITHA HOSPITAL, KOCHI, INDIA. THE ENROLLMENT WILL HAPPEN FOR THREE MONTHS OR FOR A MAXIMUM OF 300 PATIENTS, WHICHEVER COMES EARLIER. PERIRECTAL SWABS WILL BE OBTAINED ON CONSENTED PATIENTS WITHIN 24-48 HOURS OF ICU ADMISSION, EVERY WEEK, AND AT THE TIME OF ICU DISCHARGE OR DEATH FOR A MAXIMUM OF FOUR WEEKS OR UNTIL THE PATIENT IS IDENTIFIED AS COLONIZED WITH CRE. FOR PATIENTS COLONIZED WITH CRE ON PERI-RECTAL SWABS ON ICU ADMISSION, WE WILL NOT OBTAIN FURTHER PERI-RECTAL SWABS. WE WILL ALSO COLLECT ALL CRE POSITIVE CLINICAL CULTURE DATA FROM PATIENTS IN THE TWO ICUS FOR A MAXIMUM OF THREE MONTHS CORRESPONDING TO THE ENROLLMENT PERIOD. THIS INFORMATION WILL BE OBTAINED FROM MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY, BY REVIEWING THE CHARTS IF NEEDED AND HOSPITAL INFORMATION SYSTEM. WE WILL REQUEST WAIVER OF CONSENT FOR THIS INFORMATION AS IT IS MINIMAL RISK TO THE PATIENTS. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL COLLECT BASIC INFORMATION ON EXISTING INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES AT BASELINE AND ANY CHANGES THAT OCCUR INDEPENDENT OF THE STUDY PROTOCOL DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. DETAILED INFORMATION ON INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES FOCUSING ON ENVIRONMENTAL CLEANING OF IMMEDIATE PATIENT ENVIRONMENT, HAND HYGIENE PRACTICES AND CONTACT ISOLATION PRECAUTION PRACTICES OF CRE POSITIVE PATIENTS IN TWO ICUS WILL BE COLLECTED. THIS WILL BE OBTAINED FROM INFECTION PREVENTION DEPARTMENT AND DIRECT OBSERVATION FROM STUDY TEAM (IF ABLE TO TRAVEL TO INDIA). A DATA COLLECTION FORM WILL BE CREATED BY ADAPTING THE WHO INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK (IPCAF)(9) AND CDC TOOL KITS(10). EXPECTED OUTCOMES FROM SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ESTIMATES OF ADMISSION CRE PREVALENCE AND CRE ACQUISITION RATES IN THE STUDY ICUS USING SCS Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND CRE ACQUISITION DURING ICU STAY. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ESTIMATES OF CRE PREVALENCE DETECTED BY ROUTINE CLINICAL CULTURES ADJUSTED FOR OVERALL CULTURES PERFORMED VERSUS SURVEILLANCE CULTURES. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ BASELINE INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES DETAILS IN STUDY ICUS AIM 2: TO DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS) STRATEGY UTILIZING BASELINE PHASE DATA FROM AIM 1 THE GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY AN LCS STRATEGY WHICH HAS CRE RATE RATIOS COMPARABLE TO SCS STRATEGY BUT LESS BURDENSOME TO IMPLEMENT COMPARED TO SCS STRATEGY ( SEE TABLE 1 FOR STUDY ACTIVITIES). TABLE 1: STUDY PHASES, CRE SURVEILLANCE STRATEGIES IN EACH PHASE AND DURATION PHASE CRE SURVEILLANCE STRATEGY DURATION BASELINE PERIOD STANDARD ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (SCS): OBTAIN PERIRECTAL SWAB FOR ENROLLED NEW ADMISSIONS TO TWO ICUS ON ADMISSION, WEEKLY AND AT DISCHARGE 3 MONTHS OR 300 PATIENTS WHICHEVER COMES FIRST DATA ANALYSIS IDENTIFY OPTIMAL LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS) STRATEGY: THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY WILL BE IDENTIFIED USING DATA OBTAINED FROM THE BASELINE PERIOD SCS STRATEGY. 3 MONTHS PRE-INTERVENTION LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS): THIS MAY INVOLVE SELECTING ONE DAY OR MULTIPLE DAYS OF THE WEEK AND OBTAIN PERIRECTAL SWABS ON PATIENTS ADMITTED WITHIN 24 HOURS TO THE ICU AND ON THEIR DISCHARGE, AS WELL AS ON ALL PATIENTS TO BE DISCHARGED FROM ICU ON THAT DAY. NO CHANGE IN INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES 3 MONTHS INTERVENTION LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS): SAME AS PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE AND PERFORM AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION 3 MONTHS THE LCS STRATEGY MAY INVOLVE SELECTING ONE DAY OR MULTIPLE DAYS OF THE WEEK AND PERFORMING INTESTINAL CRE SCREENING BY OBTAINING PERIRECTAL SWABS ON PATIENTS ADMITTED WITHIN 24-48 HOURS TO THE ICU AND ON THEIR DISCHARGE AS WELL AS ON ALL PATIENTS TO BE DISCHARGED WITHIN 24 HOURS. THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY WILL BE IDENTIFIED AFTER ANALYZING THE SCS DATA COLLECTED FOR 3 MONTHS IN AIM1 TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE ACCURACY OF THE CRE RATE RATIOS COMPARED TO SCS STRATEGY, THE EFFORT OF HCWS, LABORATORY STAFF, RESOURCES NEEDED AND AFTER DISCUSSIONS WITH CDC SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS (SMES). USING THE DATA COLLECTED FROM BASELINE PHASE, CRE RATE RATIOS WITH SELECTION OF DIFFERENT DAYS OR MULTIPLE DAYS WILL BE PERFORMED TO IDENTIFY AN LCS STRATEGY THAT IS COMPARABLE AND LESS BURDENSOME TO SCS STRATEGY FOR ESTIMATING CRE RATE RATIOS . THIS WILL ALLOW US TO DETERMINE THE BEST DAY/S OF THE WEEK TO PERFORM LCS IN MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICUS, AS THEY MAY HAVE DIFFERENT PATTERNS OF PATIENT TURNOVER RATES. IN ADDITION, WE WILL EXAMINE THE UTILITY OF ADDING RISK FACTORS AND CLINICAL CULTURE DATA TO AUGMENT THE SELECTED LCS STRATEGY, ESPECIALLY TO DECREASE THE BURDEN ON HCWS AND THE LABORATORY STAFF FOR CONDUCTING CRE SURVEILLANCE. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL DO A QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW WITH THE RESEARCH NURSE ON THE ACCESSIBILITY OF CLINICAL RISK FACTOR DATA. THE INTERVIEW WILL BE CONDUCTED BY PIS EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA SKYPE. AIM 3: TO DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION(S) ON CRE INCIDENCE RATE RATIOS USING LCS STRATEGY IN THIS AIM, WE WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION(S) ON CRE INCIDENCE RATE RATIOS USING LCS STRATEGY. TO DO THIS, WE WILL HAVE A PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE AND INTERVENTION PHASE EACH OF 3 MONTHS DURATION AND PROSPECTIVELY ENROLL CONSENTED PATIENTS. THE PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE WILL BE INITIATED AFTER ANALYSIS OF BASELINE PHASE DATA TO DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY AFTER DISCUSSION WITH CDC SMES. THE GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY A LCS STRATEGY WHICH INVOLVES SELECTING ONE OR TWO DAYS OF THE WEEK AND PERFORMING INTESTINAL CRE SCREENING BY OBTAINING PERIRECTAL SWABS ON CONSENTED PATIENTS ADMITTED WITHIN 24-48 HOURS TO THE ICU AND ON THEIR DISCHARGE AS WELL AS ON ALL CONSENTED PATIENTS TO BE DISCHARGED WITHIN 24 HOURS FROM ICU. THE INTERVENTION PHASE WILL BE INITIATED ONE MONTH AFTER THE PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE IS COMPLETED. AFTER DISCUSSIONS WITH THE CDC SMES, THE INTERVENTION WILL BE FINALIZED, AND IT WILL BE PILOTED IN THE MONTH BETWEEN PRE-INTERVENTION AND INTERVENTION PHASE. DURING THE INTERVENTION PHASE, THE LCS WILL BE RESUMED AND CONTINUED FOR THREE MONTHS. WE WILL ALSO COLLECT ALL CRE POSITIVE CLINICAL CULTURE DATA FROM PATIENTS IN THE TWO ICUS DURING THE TWO PHASES. THIS INFORMATION WILL BE OBTAINED FROM MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY, BY REVIEWING THE CHARTS IF NEEDED AND HOSPITAL INFORMATION SYSTEM. WE WILL REQUEST WAIVER OF CONSENT FOR THIS INFORMATION AS IT IS MINIMAL RISK TO THE PATIENTS. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL COLLECT DATA ON COMPLIANCE WITH INFECTION PREVENTION DURING PRE-INTERVENTION AND INTERVENTION PHASE USING A STANDARDIZED METHOD BY PERFORMING DIRECT OBSERVATIONS. THE DETAILS WILL BE DECIDED ONCE THE INTERVENTION IS DECIDED. SOME POTENTIAL INTERVENTIONS COULD BE ENHANCED TERMINAL CLEANING WITH EDUCATION AND FEEDBACK OR WITH MINIMAL EQUIPMENT CHANGES, COHORTING OF CRE POSITIVE PATIENTS AND ENHANCING HAND HYGIENE MEASURES WITH EDUCATION AND FEEDBACK. SPECIMEN COLLECTION AND MICROBIOLOGY PROCEDURES: PERI-RECTAL SWAB WILL BE OBTAINED FROM THE CONSENTED PATIENTS BY INSERTING TIP OF THE SWAB INTO RECTUM AND GENTLY ROTATING IT 360 DEGREES. VISIBLE BROWN PIGMENT SHOULD BE OBSERVED ON THE SWAB. IF NO PIGMENT IS PRESENT, THE SWAB WILL BE REINSERTED INTO THE RECTUM. ONCE PERIRECTAL SPECIMENS ARE OBTAINED USING HICULTUREÃ¢Â€ŽÂ¢ TRANSPORT SWABS W/ AMIES MEDIUM (HIMEDIA LABORATORIES, INDIA) SPECIMEN COLLECTION AND TRANSPORT SYSTEM, THEY WILL BE TRANSPORTED TO MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY IMMEDIATELY AT ROOM TEMPERATURE AND WILL BE PROCESSED WITHIN 24 HOURS. THE SWABS WILL BE DIRECTLY PLATED ONTO MSUPERCARBA (CHROMAGAR)(11, 12). QUALITY CONTROL OF THE MSUPERCARBA MEDIA WILL BE PERFORMED AS PER MANUFACTURERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RECOMMENDATIONS USING FOLLOWING ATCC STRAINS: E. COLI IMP NCTC 1347 & K. PNEUMONIAE ATCCÃ‚Â® BAA 1705 AS POSITIVE CONTROLS AND E. FAECALIS ATCCÃ‚Â® 29212 AND K. PNEUMONIAE ESBL ATCCÃ‚Â® 700603 AS NEGATIVE CONTROLS. THE PLATES WILL BE INCUBATED AT 35 Ã‚Â°C IN AN INCUBATOR FOR 24 HOURS IN AIR ATMOSPHERE. COLONIES WHICH ARE DARK PINK TO REDDISH (E. COLI) AND METALLIC BLUE (KLEBSIELLA, ENTEROBACTER, CITROBACTER) ARE CONSIDERED AS POSSIBLE CRE. THESE COLONIES WILL BE PICKED TO PERFORM MCIM AND ECIM TESTS TO RULE OUT NONÃ¢Â‚¬Â€ŒCARBAPENEMASE-PRODUCING ENTEROBACTERALES AND TO DIFFERENTIATE METALLO-ÃŽÂ²-LACTAMASES FROM SERINE CARBAPENEMASES (13). ONCE CONFIRMED BY MCIM TEST, ONLY ONE ISOLATE (PREFERABLY E.COLI OR KLEBSIELLA SPP.) PER PATIENT WILL BE TESTED USING VITEK2 (BIOMERIEUX) FOR IDENTIFICATION AND ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY. THE GRAM NEGATIVE VITEK2 ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY PANEL INCLUDES FOLLOWING ANTIBIOTICS- AMIKACIN, AZTREONAM, CEFEPIME, CEFTAZIDIME, CIPROFLOXACIN, COLISTIN, DORIPENEM, GENTAMICIN, IMIPENEM, LEVOFLOXACIN, MEROPENEM, MINOCYCLINE, PIPERACILLIN/TAZOBACTAM, TIGECYCLINE, AND TRIMETHOPRIM/SULFAMETHOXAZOLE. THE CONTRACT WILL ALSO CONDUCT RSV SURVEILLANCE AMONG INPATIENTS WITH ARI AND BUILD ON PRIOR EFFORTS TO UNDERSTAND SEVERE ARI, SEVERITY SCORES, SUSCEPTIBILITY TO INFECTION, MECHANISMS OF DISEASE ATTENUATION, AND VACCINE FAILURES. description: PI: HONG QI, QOOLABS INC, 1915 ASTON AVE, CARLSBAD, CA 92008 I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION GUINEA PIGS HAVE BEEN USED AS EXPERIMENTAL ANIMALS FOR CENTURIES. DUE TO THEIR BIOLOGICAL SIMILARITIES TO HUMANS, GUINEA PIGS WERE USED IN MANY FIELDS OF BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH, SUCH AS NUTRITIONAL RESEARCH, VACCINE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT, HORMONAL STUDIES, AUDITORY SYSTEM STUDIES, AND INFECTIOUS DISEASE STUDIES. GUINEA PIGS ARE ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT IN TUBERCULOSIS RESEARCH. THE USEFULNESS OF GUINEA PIG AS A SMALL ANIMAL MODEL FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH HAS BEEN CONSTRAINED BY THE LACK OF IMMUNOLOGICAL REAGENTS, PARTICULARLY FOR IMMUNOLOGICAL ANALYSIS. AFFINITY REAGENTS FOR IMMUNE SYSTEM OF GUINEA PIGS ARE OF GREAT NEED TO FACILITATE THE IMMUNOLOGICAL ANALYSIS USING THIS ANIMAL MODEL. QOOLABS HAS DEVELOPED A ROBUST METHOD OF GENERATING RECOMBINANT RABBIT MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD (QMABÃ¢Â€ŽÂ¢ FOR QUICK MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY FROM BLOOD). USING QMAB TECHNOLOGY, QOOLABS WAS AWARDED AN SBIR CONTRACT PREVIOUSLY TO GENERATE RABBIT MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES FOR SELECTED GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES. OVER 100 CLONES OF ANTIBODIES WERE GENERATED FOR DIFFERENT GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES. IN COLLABORATION WITH SEATTLE CHILDRENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RESEARCH INSTITUTE AND COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY (CSU), MULTIPLE CLONES OF ANTIBODIES WERE VERIFIED FOR THEIR FUNCTION IN DETECTING ENDOGENOUS GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES. A LARGE NUMBER OF CLONES HAVE BEEN GENERATED AGAINST RECOMBINANT GUINEA PIG CYTOKINE IMMUNOGENS. THESE CLONES MUST BE DOWN SELECTED AND PAIRED TOGETHER TO GENERATE ASSAYS WITH CAPACITY TO QUANTIFY GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES. IN WORKING WITH CSU, QOOLABS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO IDENTIFYING THE MOST REACTIVE CLONES AND ESTABLISH FUNCTIONAL ANTIBODY PAIRS THAT CAN BE DEPLOYED IN ASSAYS. THIS WILL REQUIRE SHARING OF GUINEA PIG CELL-DERIVED SUPERNATANTS AND HARMONIZATION OF ASSAY CONDITIONS ACROSS CSU AND QOOLABS. CSU WILL THEN DEPLOY DEVELOPED ASSAYS IN THE GUINEA PIG MODEL OF TUBERCULOSIS. IN ORDER TO ACCOMPLISH THE GOALS OF FURTHER CHARACTERIZING THESE ANTIBODIES AND USING THEM IN TB RESEARCH, THE REQUIREMENTS ARE TWO-FOLD: 1) LARGE QUANTITIES OF THESE ANTIBODIES ARE NEEDED; AND 2) ANTIBODY CLONES MUST BE SELECTED FOR BEST AFFINITY AGAINST SAMPLES CONTAINING THE BIOLOGICAL PROTEIN. IN THIS COLLABORATIVE EFFORT BETWEEN QOO LABS AND CSU, ENTITIES WILL CROSS-HARMONIZE STRATEGIES FOR PRODUCTION OF CYTOKINES FROM PRIMARY GUINEA PIG DERIVED CELLS, IDENTIFY THE APPROACH TO PAIR ANTIBODIES FOR DEVELOPMENT OF ELISA AND ELISPOT ASSAYS, THEN PRODUCE LARGE QUANTITIES OF THE BEST PERFORMING ANTIBODY CLONES FOR APPLICATION IN THE GUINEA PIG MODEL OF TUBERCULOSIS. OWING TO THE LACK OF IMMUNOLOGICAL REAGENTS SPECIFIC TO GUINEA PIG TARGETS, THIS COLLABORATIVE CONTRACT HARNESSES EXPERTISE IN ANTIBODY DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION (QOOLABS) AND EXPERTISE IN GUINEA PIG IMMUNOLOGY AND THE GUINEA PIG MODEL OF TUBERCULOSIS (CSU). II. SCOPE THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON THE SELECTION AND PRODUCTION OF SELECTED RABBIT MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITIES TO SUPPORT THE RESEARCH NEEDS PROPOSED TO ESTABLISH THE KINETIC GUINEA PIG CYTOKINE RESPONSE TO INFECTION WITH M. TUBERCULOSIS. III. OBJECTIVES THIRTY-TWO (32) CLONES OF RABBIT MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES SELECTED FOR PRIMARY TESTING. 5MG OF EACH ANTIBODY WILL BE PRODUCED AND PURIFIED. EACH ANTIBODY WILL BE BIOTINYLATED AT 1MG SCALE. TESTING WILL BE PERFORMED IN COLLABORATION BETWEEN CSU AND QOOLABS, USING CELL STIMULATION CONDITIONS AND CELL-DERIVED MATERIALS AS DEVELOPED UNDER THIS CONTRACT AT CSU. description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES CAN BE ALTERED BY VACCINATION AND OTHER HOST FACTORS, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE IMPACT OF INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING BY VACCINATION TO THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE AND BACTERIAL CONTROL USING SEVERAL DIFFERENT VACCINATION MODALITIES, ACROSS DIFFERENT MOUSE AND MTB STRAIN COMBINATIONS. THE SUBAWARD WILL ALSO PERFORM A CROSS-SPECIES ANALYSIS OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC STATES ACROSS MOUSE AND HUMAN SAMPLES. 1) OPTIMIZE ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING FROM FRESH AND FROZEN MURINE MYELOID CELLS. 2) PREPARE FROZEN HUMAN SAMPLES FOR ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING INCLUDING: CELL PREPARATION, TRANSPOSITION REACTION AND PURIFICATION, PCR AMPLIFICATION, LIBRARY PURIFICATION, AND LIBRARY QC. 3) ANALYZE MOUSE AND HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES AND CONNECT THEM BACK TO THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES. 4) GENERATE BULK RNA-SEQUENCING SAMPLES FOR MTB-INFECTED B6 AND C3H ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES FOLLOWING SA161 HIGH DOSE AEROSOL INFECTION. 5) GENERATE SP140-/- AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MURINE EX VIVO ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE (MEXAM) PRIMARY CELL LINES. 6) MEASURE INNATE RESPONSES OF B6, SP140-/-, AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MEXAMS TO MTB-RELATED PAMPS AND IN RESPONSE TO EXOGENOUS TYPE I INTERFERON.

description: RATIONALE: OPTION 4 WAS ORIGINALLY DEVISED AS A PLACEHOLDER EXPERIMENT TO PROVIDE FOR EARLY AND/OR LATE Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒOMICS-FOCUSED NECROPSY ANALYSIS OF A TO-BE-NAMED-LATER Ã¢Â‚¬Å“EFFECTIVEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ NON-RHCMV VACCINE. SINCE PREVIOUS CHANGES TO OUR STUDY PLAN PROVIDED FOR EARLIER ANALYSIS OF IV BCG (CURRENTLY ONGOING AS EXPT. #4, SEE UPDATED STUDY PLAN BELOW), THE ONLY KNOWN NON-RHCMV-BASED MTB VACCINE WITH DEMONSTRATED EFFICACY IN NHP, WE INITIALLY CONSIDERED IDENTIFYING ANOTHER EFFECTIVE OR OTHERWISE INTERESTING VACCINE FOR ANALYSIS, INCLUDING THE H107/BCG, ID93/GAL-SE, AND ÃŽÂ€?LPRG VACCINES. HOWEVER, THESE CANDIDATE VACCINES EITHER WERE NOT AVAILABLE FOR OUR TESTING OR IN OUR VIEW LACKED SUFFICIENT JUSTIFICATION TO PURSUE FOR IN DEPTH ANALYSIS. AT THE SAME TIME, OUR INCREASINGLY DETAILED ANALYSIS OF THE PILOT STUDIES INDICATED THAT RELATIVE TO TB-NAÃƑÂ¯VE RM, ANTI-MTB IMMUNITY ESTABLISHED BY ID BCG HAD POTENTIALLY PROFOUND EFFECTS ON THE NATURE AND DYNAMICS OF THE EARLY IMMUNE RESPONSE TO MTB CHALLENGE, INCLUDING GRANULOMA STRUCTURE AND THE IMMUNE PROCESSES INVOLVED IN THE RESPONSE. THESE CHANGES WERE MORE APPARENT IN BCG GIVEN IN ADOLESCENCE RELATIVE TO BCG GIVEN AT BIRTH, SUGGESTING THAT BCG VACCINATION IN ADOLESCENCE WAS AN EXCELLENT MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE HOW PRE-EXISTING IMMUNITY CHANGES THE HOST RESPONSE TO MTB, A FUNDAMENTAL QUESTION THAT IS ALSO BE BEING ADDRESSED BY OUR CASCADE IMPAC-TB COLLEAGUES IN MICE. HOWEVER, DURING THIS INCREASINGLY IN-DEPTH PILOT STUDY ANALYSIS, WE ALSO DETERMINED THAT EACH POST NECROPSY TIMEPOINT (WEEK 2, 3, ETC.) MUST BE ANALYZED INDEPENDENTLY (AS TIME POST INFECTION IS A CRITICAL VARIABLE) AND THAT N = 4 RMS PER TIMEPOINT/PER GROUP IS INSUFFICIENT TO DEFINITIVELY CHARACTERIZE THE DIFFERENCES WITH AND WITHOUT PRE-EXISTING IMMUNITY. IN ADDITION, OUR PILOT STUDIES DID NOT INCLUDE A WEEK 1 POST-CHALLENGE ANALYSIS FOR ANY BCG VACCINATED RM, AND WE ALSO DETERMINED THAT WEEK 4 POST- CHALLENGE WAS STILL TOO EARLY TO PRECISELY DEFINE THE TRAJECTORY FOR SUBSEQUENT DISEASE, SUGGESTING THAT WEEK 1 ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION OF ONE OR MORE LATER (AFTER WEEK 4) TIMEPOINTS WOULD BE CRUCIAL TO COMPLETELY DEFINE RESPONSE DYNAMICS. IN THIS REGARD, EXPT. #3 (SEE STUDY PLAN BELOW) PROVIDES WEEK 10-12 ANALYSIS OF ID BCG-AT-BIRTH BUT NOT FOR THE APPARENTLY MORE POTENT ID BCG IN ADOLESCENCE. MOREOVER, NO STUDIES HAVE BEEN PERFORMED BETWEEN WEEK 5 AND WEEK 9, THE TIME PERIOD DURING WHICH THE EVENTUAL EXTENT OF DISEASE BECOMES MANIFEST. GIVEN THE HISTORIC SCOPE OF THIS STUDY [WHICH WE CONSIDER GENERATIONAL SINCE A SUCCESSIVE (DYNAMIC) Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒOMICS-FOCUSED NECROPSY ANALYSIS OF TB VACCINES IN RMS OF THIS STUDYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SCOPE IS UNLIKELY TO BE REPEATED BY ANY GROUP IN THE NEAR FUTURE], WE FEEL ITÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S IMPORTANT TO HAVE A MORE COMPLETE ANALYSIS OF ID BCG, WHICH IS THE ONLY VACCINE BEING STUDIED THAT IS CURRENTLY AVAILABLE FOR CLINICAL USE. UNDERSTANDING THE DETAILED EFFECT OF ESTABLISHING PRE-EXISTING ANTI-MTB IMMUNITY WITH THIS APPROVED VACCINE WILL BE IMPORTANT TO BOTH IMPROVE ITS USE (PERHAPS PROVIDING ADDITIONAL RATIONALE FOR BCG RE-VACCINATION) OR TO SERVE AS A COMPARATOR TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE EFFECTS OF OTHER POSSIBLY MORE EFFICACIOUS VACCINE APPROACHES. TO THIS END, WE ARE PROPOSING TO EXPAND THE ANALYSIS OF ID BCG IN ADOLESCENCE TO INCLUDE N = 7 RM NECROPSIES AT WEEKS 1, 2, 3 AND 4 (VS. N = 6 FOR UNVACCINATED CONTROL RM, N = 8 FOR RHCMV/TB VACCINATED RM, AND N = 5 FOR IV BCG VACCINATED RM), AND TO EXPAND THE WEEKS STUDIED TO WEEK 7 POST CHALLENGE (N = 7 ID BCG RM VS. description: THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS, THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF VARIOUS CHEMOTACTIC OR ADHESION MOLECULES IN GUIDING IMMUNE CELLS TO VARIOUS SITES WITHIN THE INFECTED LUNG TISSUES AND LYMPHOID ORGANS, AS WELL AS IN MEDIATING PROTECTION FROM MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. IN YEAR 5, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL: I. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. II. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EXPERIMENTS AIMED TO ELUCIDATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES WITHIN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION, WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. III. VALIDATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. IV. PERFORM SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS ANALYSIS OF LUNG GRANULOMAS OVER THE EARLY COURSE OF INFECTION WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. THIS WILL INVOLVE SAMPLE PROCESSING, DATA ACQUISITION, AND FOLLOW-UP ANALYSIS. V. ASSIST WITH MULTIOMICS ANALYSIS AND DATA INTERPRETATION FOR FLOW CYTOMETRY, SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA OBTAINED BY THE GERNER LAB AND OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. THIS WILL INVOLVE ANALYSIS OF CHEMOTACTIC AND ADHESION MOLECULES THAT MAY REGULATE CELLULAR POSITIONING, AS WELL AS HELPING IDENTIFY POTENTIAL MOLECULES OF INTEREST THAT MAY BE INVOLVED IN IMMUNE RESPONSES WHICH CORRELATE WITH PROTECTION. VI. IDENTIFIED MOLECULES OF INTEREST FROM PART III) WILL ALSO BE USED TO POWER FOLLOW-UP MICROSCOPY AND SPATIAL ANALYSIS STUDIES TO REVEAL HOW THESE CORRELATE WITH CELLULAR ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTION WITHIN INFECTED LUNG AND LYMPH NODE TISSUES. VII. CONTINUE COLLABORATIVE INTERACTIONS WITH OHSU ON PERFORMING CROSS-SPECIES CORRELATIVE ANALYSES USING GENERATED SEQUENCING AND IMAGING DATA TO IDENTIFY CONSERVED FEATURES OF IMMUNE CELL RESPONSES TO INFECTION AND AFTER IMMUNIZATION. VIII. DATA FROM I-VII) WILL HELP IDENTIFY SPECIFIC MOLECULES OF INTEREST FOR FOLLOW-UP FUNCTIONAL STUDIES. AS EXAMPLE, IDENTIFIED CHEMOTACTIC MOLECULES WILL BE TARGETED USING EITHER AVAILABLE KO MICE OR USING IN VIVO BLOCKADE WITH ANTIBODIES OR SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITORS. ALTERNATIVELY, IMMUNE CELLS CAN BE ENGINEERED EX VIVO (E.G. CRISPR) TO ENHANCE TRAFFICKING OF EFFECTOR CELLS TO SPECIFIC TISSUE SITES DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. BASED ON THE LENGTH OF TIME THAT I-V) STEPS ABOVE WILL TAKE TO IMPLEMENT, THESE FUNCTIONAL MAY BE PERFORMED IN LATER YEARS OF THE CONTRACT.

description: COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER SUBCONTRACT SCOPE OF WORK THE OVERALL PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING 4 TASKS: DESIGN A MULTI-SITE STUDY OF INFLUENZA TRANSMISSION WITHIN HOUSEHOLDS, ENROLL ELIGIBLE HOUSEHOLDS AND CONDUCT PROSPECTIVE STUDY ACTIVITIES, CONDUCT LABORATORY STUDIES TO CHARACTERIZE SUSCEPTIBILITY AND INFECTION, AND, PROVIDE DATA MANAGEMENT FOR SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND ANALYSES. COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER WILL SERVE AS A SITE FOR THE RESPIRATORY VIRUS TRANSMISSION NETWORK (RVTN) TO STUDY HOUSEHOLD TRANSMISSION OF INFLUENZA. COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER WILL RECRUIT APPROXIMATELY 150 PARTICIPANTS WITH ACUTE INFLUENZA INFECTION AND THEIR HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS TO THE STUDY. USING STUDY MATERIALS PROVIDED BY WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY, COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER INVESTIGATORS WILL PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH SELF-COLLECTION MATERIALS, COLLECT QUESTIONNAIRE DATA, MONITOR PARTICIPANT ACTIVITIES, AND RECEIVE COMPLETED SAMPLES. COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER WILL STORE SAMPLES IN THE COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER LABORATORY AS DIRECTED BY THE PROTOCOL AND SHIP SAMPLES TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY OR OTHER DESIGNATED LABORATORY. THE SITE WILL ENTER DATA IN A TIMELY FASHION INTO THE REDCAP DATABASE. THE ONLY SAMPLES TO BE COLLECTED FOR THIS PROJECT ARE NASAL SWABS. SEVEN NASAL SWABS PER PARTICIPANT WILL BE COLLECTED DURING THE STUDY ENROLLMENT PERIOD. THIS IS CONSISTENT ACROSS ALL PARTICIPATING SITES. DATA COLLECTION WILL PRIMARILY FOCUS ON SURVEYS THAT ARE COMPLETED BY STUDY PARTICIPANTS. PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE SEVERAL SURVEYS INCLUDING: A HOUSEHOLD ENROLLMENT SURVEY - THIS WILL BE COMPLETED BY ONE HOUSEHOLD MEMBER AT THE TIME OF STUDY ENROLLMENT AND WILL COLLECT DATA ABOUT THE INDIVIDUALS LIVING IN THE HOUSEHOLD AND THE HOME, ITSELF. A PARTICIPANT ENROLLMENT SURVEY - THIS WILL BE COMPLETED BY EACH PARTICIPANT TO PROVIDE DATA ABOUT DEMOGRAPHICS, HIGH-RISK HEALTH CONDITIONS, INFLUENZA VACCINATION STATUS, AND INTERACTIONS WITH PEOPLE IN THE HOUSEHOLD AND OUTSIDE OF THE HOUSEHOLD. RETROSPECTIVE DAILY DIARIES - THESE WILL COLLECT DATA ABOUT SYMPTOMS, MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR SYMPTOMS, AND INTERACTIONS WITH OTHER HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS THAT OCCURRED BETWEEN ILLNESS ONSET AND STUDY ENROLLMENT. THERE WILL BE ONE DIARY/SURVEY FOR EACH DAY WITHIN THIS PERIOD. PROSPECTIVE DAILY DIARIES- THESE WILL COLLECT DATA ABOUT SYMPTOMS, MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR SYMPTOMS, AND INTERACTIONS WITH OTHER HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS DURING THE INITIAL 7-DAY STUDY SPECIMEN COLLECTION PERIOD. THERE WILL BE A TOTAL OF 7 SURVEYS PER PARTICIPANT (ONE FOR EACH DAY THAT THEY COLLECT A NASAL SWAB SPECIMEN). A 30-DAY FOLLOW UP STUDY - THIS WILL COLLECT DATA ABOUT RESPIRATORY VIRUS TESTING AND MEDICAL CARE NEEDED AFTER THE INTIAL ENROLLMENT PERIOD, AS WELL AS DATA ABOUT THE IMPACT OF THE INFLUENZA ILLNESS ON DAILY LIFE ACTIVITIES. IN ADDITION TO THE SURVEY DATA LISTED ABOVE, DATA ON INFLUENZA AND OTHER RESPIRATORY VIRUS TESTING WILL BE ABSTRACTED FROM THE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORD BY PARTICIPATING SITES AS PART OF THE RECRUITMENT AND SCREENING PROCESS FOR PARTICIPANTS; THIS DATA WILL BE USED IN THE STUDY ANALYSIS. SITES WILL ALSO ABSTRACT DATA FROM MEDICAL RECORDS AND LOCAL/STATE VACCINE REGISTRIES TO COLLECT INFLUENZA VACCINATION DATA ABOUT STUDY PARTICIPANTS. DR. MELISSA STOCKWELL, PROFESSOR OF PEDIATRICS AND POPULATION AND FAMILY HEALTH, WILL BE THE SITE PI ON THE SUBAWARD. SHE WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ASSURING THAT ALL STUDY ACTIVITIES ARE CARRIED OUT AS OUTLINED IN THE PROTOCOL. SHE WILL OBTAIN AN IRB RELIANCE AGREEMENT WITH WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY AND MAINTAIN APPROVAL. SHE WILL HIRE AND OVERSEE STUDY STAFF TO CARRY OUT THE STUDY ACTIVITIES DESCRIBED ABOVE. SHE WILL ALSO SERVE ON THE STEERING COMMITTEE AS COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S REPRESENTATIVE AND MAINTAIN FREQUENT CONTACT WITH THE STUDY PI DR. KWON.

description: THE CONCURRENT RISE OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE AND INCIDENCE OF SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS IS A WORRYING COMBINATION. IN THE PAST DECADE, CASES OF GONORRHEA HAVE MORE THAN DOUBLED IN MANY COUNTRIES – IN THE US THERE ARE AN ESTIMATED 1.6 MILLION NEW INFECTIONS EACH YEAR, HALF OF WHICH ARE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANT. OVER THE PAST 80 YEARS, NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE, THE CAUSATIVE AGENT OF GONORRHEA, HAS STEADILY DEVELOPED RESISTANCE TO ALL ANTIMICROBIAL TREATMENTS. ALREADY TODAY, ONLY ONE RECOMMENDED TREATMENT OPTION REMAINS, AND FAILURES HAVE BEEN OBSERVED IN MULTIPLE COUNTRIES. GONORRHEA WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP RESISTANCE TO ANY NEW ANTIMICROBIALS, AND IN JUST A FEW YEARS UNTREATABLE DISEASE COULD BE WIDESPREAD. AN ALTERNATIVE SOLUTION IS URGENTLY NEEDED – A VACCINE. THERE ARE NO KNOWN EXAMPLES OF A PATHOGEN DEVELOPING RESISTANCE TO A VACCINE, AND ONLY LIMITED EXAMPLES OF EVASION BY SEROTYPE REPLACEMENT. BY PREVENTING INFECTIONS AND ILLNESS, ANTIBIOTIC PRESCRIPTIONS ARE REDUCED, AND SO IS DEVELOPMENT OF RESISTANCE. WIDESPREAD USE OF PNEUMOCOCCAL VACCINES HAS EVEN BEEN SHOWN TO SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE CIRCULATING LEVELS OF RESISTANT BACTERIA. LIMMATECH BIOLOGICS AG IS DEVELOPING A VACCINE IS BASED ON A COMBINATION OF NOVEL ANTIGENS DELIVERED IN A NOVEL PRODUCTION PLATFORM. IMMUNE EVASION BY N. GONORRHOEAE MEANS THAT NATURAL INFECTION WITH THE PATHOGEN DOES NOT RESULT IN PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY, AND MANY GONOCOCCAL SURFACE ANTIGENS ARE HIGHLY VARIABLE IN STRUCTURE OR EXPRESSION, MAKING THEM POOR TARGETS FOR VACCINATION. OUR VACCINE IS DESIGNED TO OVERCOME THESE MECHANISMS BY AVOIDING PHASE VARIABLE STRUCTURES AND IMMUNOGENIC SURFACE DECOY ANTIGENS. ALL OUR ANTIGENS ARE HIGHLY CONSERVED BETWEEN STRAINS, INCLUDING RECENT AND RESISTANT CLINICAL ISOLATES, AND THIS, TOGETHER WITH THE MULTIVALENT DESIGN OF THE VACCINE MEANS COVERAGE IS EXPECTED TO BE 100%. ALL OUR ANTIGENS ARE HIGHLY IMMUNOGENIC IN PRECLINICAL STUDIES. THEY HAVE BEEN EXTENSIVELY VALIDATED USING A SET OF COMPLEMENTARY IN VITRO ASSAYS THAT DEMONSTRATE ANTIBODY FUNCTIONALITY AND PROTECTIVE MECHANISMS OF ACTION. THESE ASSAYS HAVE ALSO BEEN USED TO CONFIRM ANTIBODY FUNCTIONALITY AGAINST MULTIPLE STRAINS INCLUDING AMR CLINICAL ISOLATES. WE HAVE COMPLETED GMP PRODUCTION OF OUR VACCINE CANDIDATE, LTB-NG6, AND THE MATERIAL IS READY TO BE TESTED IN A FIRST-IN-HUMAN STUDY. WE HAVE SUBMITTED THE REGULATORY APPLICATION AND ARE AIMING TO START THIS PHASE I SAFETY AND IMMUNOGENICITY IN Q3 2026, AT A LOCATION IN GERMANY.

description: BACKGROUND KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE (K. PNEUMONIAE, KP) IS A NOTORIOUS PATHOGEN FREQUENTLY RESPONSIBLE FOR NOSOCOMIAL RESPIRATORY TRACT AND INTENSIVE CARE INFECTIONS. IT IS THE SECOND MOST COMMON CAUSE OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTEREMIA AND URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS. DRUG RESISTANT ISOLATES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH MORTALITY (GREATER THAN 50% ACCORDING TO SOME STUDIES), ADD SIGNIFICANTLY TO HOSPITAL STAYS, AND ARE ESPECIALLY PROBLEMATIC IN SUCH MEDICAL AREAS AS ICUS. K. PNEUMONIAE PROPHYLACTIC VACCINATION AGAINST DRUG RESISTANT STRAINS WOULD BE AN EFFECTIVE STRATEGY TO REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF INFECTIONS AND ANTI-MICROBIAL RESISTANCE. THERE ARE NO APPROVED K. PNEUMONIAE VACCINES AND NO CLEAR EVIDENCE OF ANY ADVANCING IN DEVELOPMENT. IDORSIA BERLIN IS WORKING ON A MULTIVALENT VACCINE TARGETING MULTIPLE STRAINS OF CARBAPENEM RESISTANT K. PNEUMONIAE (CRKP). IDORSIA BERLINÃ‚Â´S PRODUCT IS A MULTI-VALENT O ANTIGEN PROPHYLACTIC VACCINE CURRENTLY IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT. TARGET COVERAGE IS MORE THAN 90% OF CARBAPENEM RESISTANT STRAINS. UNMET MEDICAL NEED ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE HAS BECOME AN INCREASINGLY SERIOUS PROBLEM IN K. PNEUMONIAE INFECTIONS. CRKP STRAINS ARE THE MOST PROMINENTLY FOUND AMONG THE RESISTANT PATHOGENS, OFTEN CARRYING ADDITIONAL GENES THAT CONFER RESISTANCE TO SEVERAL OTHER CLASSES OF ANTIMICROBIALS. THIS RESULTS IN MORE THAN 40% OF K. PNEUMONIAE ISOLATES SHOWING MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE-PHENOTYPES IN CERTAIN O-ANTIGEN EXPRESSING STRAINS. GIVEN THE LIMITED TREATMENT OPTIONS OF CRKP INFECTIONS, MORTALITY RATES ARE HIGH, VARYING BETWEEN 10% AND 70%, DEPENDING ON THE SITE OF INFECTION. IT IS RECOGNIZED THAT THE PREVENTION OF THE TRANSMISSION FROM CRKP-COLONIZED OR INFECTED INDIVIDUALS REPRESENTS A VERY EFFECTIVE STRATEGY TO REDUCE THE IMPACT OF THE INFECTION IN ACUTE CARE HOSPITALS AND LONG-TERM CARE FACILITIES. WHILE, CURRENT PREVENTIVE RECOMMENDATIONS FOCUS ON BASIC INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES, THERE IS AN URGENT UNMET NEED FOR EFFECTIVE INTERVENTION STRATEGIES TO PREVENT TRANSMISSION OF CRKP INFECTIONS. IDORSIA BERLINÃ‚Â´S TECHNOLOGY APPROACH CHALLENGES IN DEVELOPMENT TIMELINES, MANUFACTURING AND QUALITY CONTROL COMPLEXITY STILL BROADLY PERSIST AS EVIDENCED BY THE DISCONTINUATION OF MANY CONJUGATE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS AND LENGTHY DEVELOPMENT PATHWAYS OF CURRENTLY APPROVED ONES. IDORSIA BERLIN COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY THE PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT OF A C. DIFFICILE SPECIFIC VACCINE WHICH WILL NOW ENTER CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT IN 2024. TECHNOLOGY APPLIED TO K. PNEUMONIAE K. PNEUMONIAE CONSISTS OF CAPSULAR POLYSACCHARIDES (CPS) AND LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDES (LPS) ON ITS OUTER SHELL. THESE CPS AND LPS STRUCTURES ARE IMMUNOGENIC AND ARE RECOGNIZED BY THE IMMUNE SYSTEM UPON INFECTIONS, EITHER CAUSING IMMUNITY NATURALLY, OR BY VACCINES SPECIFICALLY TARGETING CPS- OR LPS-ANTIGENS. FOR K. PNEUMONIAE, THE LIMITED VARIATION IN LPS-ANTIGENS WHEN COMPARED TO CPS ANTIGENS, MAKES THEM MORE SUITABLE TARGETS FOR VACCINE DEVELOPMENT. HOWEVER, PRODUCTION OF LPS-BASED VACCINES IS EXTREMELY CHALLENGING DUE TO TOXIC COMPONENTS THAT ATTACH THE LPS TO THE OUTER MEMBRANE OF BACTERIA. LPS DETOXIFIED MOLECULES ARE VIRTUALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO ISOLATE AND PURIFY, SO FAR PREVENTING DEVELOPMENT OF SUCH VACCINES. IDORSIA BERLIN EMPLOYS AN ALTERNATIVE APPROACH: THE SYNTHESIS OF LPS O-ANTIGENS WHICH AMONG OTHER ADVANTAGES OF SYNTHETIC GLYCAN CHEMISTRY ELIMINATES THE POTENTIAL CONTAMINATION RISKS OF THE LPS. IDORSIA BERLIN HAS IDENTIFIED THE LEAD ANTIGENS AND WILL COMPLETE PRECLINICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THE MULTIVALENT VACCINE IN Q1/2024.

description: NEONATAL SEPSIS (NNS) IS OF GROWING CONCERN GLOBALLY, PARTICULARLY IN LOW AND MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRIES (LMICS), AS ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE INCREASES. NNS IS A SYSTEMIC IMMUNE DYSREGULATION RESULTING FROM BLOODSTREAM INFECTION IN BABIES LESS THAN 28 DAYS OLD. NNS IS OFTEN CAUSED BY BACTERIA AND IS STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH COLONIZATION OF THE MATERNAL URINARY TRACT BY BACTERIA. PREGNANT WOMEN ARE AT INCREASED RISK FOR BACTERIAL COLONIZATION OF THE URINARY TRACT DUE TO CHANGES IN IMMUNOLOGY, URINE COMPOSITION AND THE URINARY TRACT THAT CREATE MORE HOSPITABLE CONDITIONS FOR UROPATHOGENIC BACTERIA. BACTERIAL COLONIZATION CAN LEAD TO URINARY TRACT INFECTION (UTI); TOGETHER, THESE ARE ESTIMATED TO OCCUR IN 50-75% OF PREGNANT WOMEN IN LMICS, RESULTING IN AS MUCH AS A FIVE-FOLD INCREASE IN THE RISK OF NNS. COLONIZATION ALSO INCREASES THE RISK OF PRETERM LABOR AND PREMATURE DELIVERY. BACTERIAL COLONIZATION IN THE URINE DURING PREGNANCY IS RARELY DIAGNOSED IN LMICS, AND EVEN WHEN IT IS, MANY ANTIMICROBIALS ARE UNSAFE FOR USE IN PREGNANT WOMEN. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO VACCINATE A NEONATE SUFFICIENTLY EARLY TO PROTECT AGAINST NNS, AND PROGRESSION TO SYSTEMIC IMMUNE DYSREGULATION IS OFTEN TOO RAPID TO ENABLE ANTIMICROBIAL THERAPY. A MATERNAL VACCINE WOULD PROTECT BOTH MOTHERS AND INFANTS DURING THIS CRITICAL PERIOD, BUT THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO LICENSED VACCINES INDICATED TO PREVENT MATERNAL COLONIZATION/NNS. A MATERNAL VACCINE TARGETING THE COMMON UROPATHOGENS ASSOCIATED WITH NNS IS URGENTLY NEEDED. SYNTIRONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ALLOY VACCINE TARGETS UROPATHOGENS AND COULD SUBSTANTIALLY IMPROVE MATERNAL AND INFANT HEALTH BY REDUCING MATERNAL BACTERIAL COLONIZATION, THEREBY REDUCING TRANSMISSION OF UROPATHOGENS TO THE NEONATE WHILE ALSO PROTECTING THE INFANT THROUGH THE TRANSFER OF MATERNAL IMMUNITY. SYNTIRONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ALLOY MATERNAL VACCINE TARGETS ALL STRAINS OF E. COLI AND KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE, UROPATHOGENS THAT COMMONLY COLONIZE THE URINARY TRACT AND CAUSE UTI AND NNS IN LMICS. THE VACCINE WILL BE EVALUATED IN THREE PHASES: 1) DURING LEAD OPTIMIZATION, THE VACCINE FORMULATION WILL BE EVALUATED AND OPTIMIZED TO ELICIT AN APPROPRIATE IMMUNE RESPONSE IN PREGNANT ANIMALS AND THEIR OFFSPRING; 2) DURING PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT, THE PROTEIN ANTIGEN WILL BE MANUFACTURED IN ACCORDANCE WITH CGMP AND TESTED FOR SAFETY AND TOXICITY; 3) DURING CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT, THE IMMUNE RESPONSE OF 90 HEALTHY MALE AND FEMALE VOLUNTEERS AGED 18-45 YEARS WILL BE EVALUATED IN THE FIRST-IN-HUMAN VACCINE SAFETY TRIAL; MEANWHILE, PREGNANT ANIMALS WILL BE IMMUNIZED TO ASSESS SAFETY AND TOXICITY OF THE VACCINE IN PREPARATION FOR A PHASE 2 EFFICACY EVALUATION AS MATERNAL VACCINE. A MATERNAL VACCINE THAT CAN PROTECT AGAINST A BROAD RANGE OF UROPATHOGENS IS URGENTLY NEEDED. SYNTIRONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ALLOY MATERNAL VACCINE COULD PROTECT MATERNAL HEALTH DURING PREGNANCY, REDUCE ANTIMICROBIAL USE, REDUCE PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS AND REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF NNS.

SCOPE CURRENT VACCINES AGAINST SEASONAL INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTION REDUCE INFLUENZA ILLNESS BY 40- 60% AMONG THE TOTAL POPULATION. HOWEVER, THE VACCINE PROTECTION IS INSUFFICIENT WHEN THE CIRCULATING INFLUENZA STRAINS DO NOT MATCH THE ONES IN THE SEASONAL VACCINES, AND THE PATIENTS ARE IN IMMUNOCOMPROMISED POPULATIONS LEADING ONLY TO LIMITED PROTECTION AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS STRAINS. SUCH GAPS BETWEEN VACCINATED STRAINS AND CIRCULATING STRAINS LOWER THE VACCINE EFFECTIVENESS RESULTING IN SEASONAL EPIDEMICS. ADDITIONALLY, NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODY LEVELS INDUCED BY THE VACCINES DO NOT RELIABLY PERSIST YEAR-ROUND. description: "THE GOAL OF THE CARDIA STUDY IS TO ASSESS THE EVOLUTION OF CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE RISK FACTORS IN HEALTHY 18-30 YEAR OLDS AT BASELINE IN 1985-6. COLLABORATING ENTITIES INCLUDE FOUR FIELD CENTERS (FCS), A COORDINATING CENTER (CC), FOUR LABORATORIES (CENTRAL BLOOD AND URINE REPOSITORY, LIPIDS LABORATORY, BLOOD AND URINE CHEMISTRIES LABORATORY, AND DNA LABORATORY), AND ANY SPECIFIC ANCILLARY STUDY SITE. THE STEERING COMMITTEE (SC) INCLUDES THE CHAIR, AND THE PUBLICATIONS & PRESENTATIONS (P&P) SUBCOMMITTEE CHAIR. PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS (PIS) FROM EACH FC, COORDINATING CENTER, LABORATORY, READING CENTER, AND ANCILLARY STUDY, THE NHLBI CONTRACTING OFFICER AND PROJECT OFFICER, AND OTHER CARDIA SCIENTISTS. THE SC WILL OVERSEE ALL SCIENTIFIC ISSUES AND MEET TWICE PER MONTH VIA VIDEO CONFERENCE, WITH TWO IN-PERSON MEETINGS PER YEAR. THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE (EC) INCLUDES THE SC CHAIR, FC PIS, CC PI AND DEPUTY DIRECTOR, AND THE NHLBI PROJECT OFFICER. IT OVERSEES DAY-TO-DAY OPERATIONS, REVIEWS AND APPROVES ANCILLARY STUDIES, AND DISCUSSES IMPORTANT ISSUES FOR SC APPROVAL. IT MEETS MONTHLY VIA VIDEO CONFERENCE AND IN-PERSON IN CONJUNCTION WITH IN-PERSON SC MEETINGS, AND ALSO CONDUCTS BUSINESS ELECTRONICALLY WHEN NEEDED (E.G., APPROVAL OF ANCILLARY STUDIES AS CIRCUMSTANCES DICTATE)."

PATIENTS WILL BE DISCHARGED. 4.
