description: THE TTIMS LRCC PROJECT PURPOSE IS TO SERVE AS THE BIOSTATISTICAL AND ANALYTICAL CENTER FOR SPECIFIC ANALYSES RELEVANT TO THE EVALUATION AND MONITORING OF HIV (INCIDENT AND PREVALENT INFECTIONS), HCV (INCIDENT) AND HBV (INCIDENT), AND SYPHILIS POSITIVE BLOOD DONORS. SPECIFICALLY, THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THIS CONTRACT ARE TO: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE AND MONITOR RISK FACTOR CHARACTERISTICS OF DONATIONS CONFIRMED POSITIVE FOR TTIS AND COMPARISON UNINFECTED (CONTROL) DONORS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ COMPARE/ANALYZE RISK FACTOR DATA TO THAT OBTAINED IN THE EARLIER TTIMS STUDY PERIOD AND THE REDS-II TTVI MARKER PREVALENCE AND RISK FACTOR STUDY. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ INTEGRATE RISK FACTOR DATA AND DISEASE MARKER SURVEILLANCE INFORMATION ACROSS DIFFERENT BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ MONITOR ARV AND PREP/PEP USE IN US ALLOGENEIC BLOOD DONOR POPULATION BASED ON TESTING OF BOTH HIV-POSITIVE AND INFECTION NEGATIVE DONATIONS FOR THE PRESENCE OF ARV DRUGS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EXPLORE THE CHARACTERISTICS OF BLOOD DONORS WHO USE ARV/PREP/PEP TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THEIR RISKS, KNOWLEDGE, AND MOTIVATIONS FOR DONATING WHILE USING THESE THERAPIES. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE WELL-CHARACTERIZED US BLOOD DONOR SAMPLES FROM TTIMS AND OTHER SOURCES FOR THE REFINEMENT OF EXISTING ANALYTICAL METHODS SUCH AS THE SEDIA LAG AVIDITY ASSAY TO DERIVE ESTIMATES OF RECENT INFECTION WITH HIV WITH A GOAL OF RAPIDLY OBTAINING MORE ACCURATE AND TIMELY RESULTS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ PROVIDE LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT AND FOR THE COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE MEETINGS, CONFERENCES, AND DONATION(S) TRANSFER/SHIPMENT. IN SUPPORT OF THESE OBJECTIVES, ONEBLOOD WILL RECRUIT, ENROLL AND INTERVIEW ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDE DATA AS REQUIRED IN THE TTIMS LRCC STATEMENT OF WORK, PROVIDE BIOSPECIMENS FOR RESEARCH TESTING AT VRI, AND WILL ACTIVELY COLLABORATE IN THE ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, AND REPORTING OF FINDINGS IN TTIMS. DR. RITA A. REIK, MD, WILL SERVE AS THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI) AT ONEBLOOD. SHE WILL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF ONEBLOODÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PARTICIPATION IN THE LRCC PORTION OF TTIMS INCLUDING ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA AND BIOSPECIMENS AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT. IN ADDITION, DR. TISHA FOSTER, MD, WILL SERVE AS THE CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR AT ONEBLOOD. DR. FOSTER WILL ASSIST IN THE OVERSIGHT OF THE ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA, AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT WHEN NECESSARY. ONEBLOOD WILL RECRUIT DONORS WITH QUALIFYING TEST RESULTS; ADMINISTER THE WEB-BASED QUESTIONNAIRE AND ENTER RISK FACTOR DATA INTO AN ELECTRONIC DATABASE; PERFORM QUALITY CONTROL (QC) ON ALL DATA ENTERED INTO THE DATABASE; RESPOND TO REQUESTS FROM THE LRCC REGARDING DATA QUALITY ASSURANCE AND QC; DEVELOP AND SUBMIT TO THE LOCAL IRB DOCUMENTS AND AMENDMENTS FOR APPROVAL. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ONEBLOOD WILL ALSO MAINTAIN AND UPDATE THE STUDY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (SMS) THAT SUPPORTS THESE ACTIVITIES AT ALL PARTICIPATING SITES, WORKING THE LRCC TO DEFINE TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS AND RESOURCES NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THIS ACTIVITY. ONEBLOOD STAFF WILL FORWARD PLASMA BAGS AND/OR PILOT TUBES TO CREATIVE TESTING SOLUTIONS (CTS) SO THAT CTS CAN CREATE UP TO 5 X 2 ML PLASMA CYROVIALS AND A SINGLE 15 ML PLASMA CRYOVIAL FOR EACH PARTICIPANT AND PREPARE ALIQUOTS FOR SHIPMENT TO THE REPOSITORY AND ADDITIONAL TESTING AT VRI FOR ALL INFECTIONS OF INTEREST AS DEFINED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE. IN COLLABORATION WITH THE LRCC, ONEBLOOD WILL COORDINATE SAMPLE SHIPMENT WITH DESIGNATED CTS STAFF. IN ADDITION, ONEBLOOD WILL WORK WITH THE LRCC AND CTS TO SOURCE SPECIMENS FOR ARV/PEP/PREP TESTING. ONEBLOOD WILL ALSO WORK THE LRCC TO FACILITATE SURVEYS AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS OF ARV/PEP/PREP REACTIVE BLOOD DONORS. ONEBLOOD WILL NOT BE EXPECTED TO LEAD THE COLLECTION OF THESE SURVEY AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW DATA BUT WILL ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING AND RECRUITING PARTICIPANTS FOR THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDENDUMS TO THIS SOW WILL BE DEVELOPED AFTER THE RESEARCH PROTOCOLS TO SUPPORT EXPANDED ART/PEP/PREP STUDIES ARE FULLY DEFINED AND APPROVED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE.

description: VISBY MEDICAL IS THE MAKER OF AN INNOVATIVE INSTRUMENT-FREE, SINGLE USE PCR PLATFORM FOR THE DETECTION OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES. THEIR SEXUAL HEALTH TEST DETECTS CHLAMYDIA, GONORRHEA, AND TRICHOMONAS WITH ~97% ACCURACY IN LESS THAN 30 MINUTES. THIS TEST IS FDA AUTHORIZED FOR OVER THE COUNTER (OTC) USE WITHOUT THE NEED FOR A PRESCRIPTION. CARB-X FUNDING WILL ALLOW VISBY TO ADD THE DETECTION OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE TO THE SEXUAL HEALTH TEST, BY DEVELOPING OUR ASSAY FOR THE DETECTION OF A MUTATION IN THE GYRA GENE OF N. GONORRHOEAE THAT CONFERS RESISTANCE TO CIPROFLOXACIN. THE CDC LISTS ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE IN N. GONORRHOEAE AS ONE OF THE TOP 5 URGENT THREATS. DUE TO LACK OF A DIAGNOSTIC TEST RESULT FOR CIPROFLOXACIN RESISTANCE, CURRENT TREATMENT GUIDELINES RECOMMEND USING ONE OF THE LAST REMAINING ANTIBIOTICS (CEFTRIAXONE) AVAILABLE AGAINST GONORRHEA INFECTIONS. THE NEW VISBY TEST WILL HELP CLINICIANS KNOW WHEN CIPROFLOXACIN CAN BE USED WHICH CAN BE ADMINISTERED ORALLY AND WILL HELP TO CONSERVE OUR LAST LINES OF ANTIBIOTIC DEFENSE ONLY FOR THE CASES THAT REQUIRE IT. BY MAKING A SIMPLE, RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TEST FOR ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE, VISBY MEDICAL WILL PROVIDE A MUCH-NEEDED TOOL IN THE FIGHT AGAINST ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE.

description: ONORRHEA IS A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTABLE DISEASE THAT IS CAUSED BY INFECTION WITH NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE BACTERIA (ALSO KNOWN AS GONOCOCCI). IT AFFECTS CLOSE TO 100 MILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE ON A YEARLY BASIS AND ALTHOUGH MORTALITY IS LOW, THE DISEASE CAN HAVE SEVERE HEALTH CONSEQUENCES LIKE INFERTILITY, NEONATAL BLINDNESS, AND INCREASED RISK OF HIV INFECTION. ANTIBIOTIC-BASED TREATMENT IS UNDER INCREASED PRESSURE BECAUSE OF THE RISE OF MULTI DRUG RESISTANCE STRAINS AND IN SOME CASES, CLINICIANS HAVE TO RESORT TO SO-CALLED Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒLAST LINEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ ANTIBIOTICS. VACCINE DEVELOPMENT AGAINST GONOCOCCI HAS FOR DECADES BEEN HAMPERED BY THE MULTITUDE OF WAYS THAT THESE BACTERIA USE TO EVADE THE HUMAN IMMUNE SYSTEM AS WELL AS THEIR STRONG GENETIC VARIATION. CURRENTLY NO VACCINE AGAINST GONORRHEA IS AVAILABLE. IT HAS RECENTLY BEEN FOUND THAT PEOPLE THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN VACCINATED AGAINST MENINGITIS USING OUTER MEMBRANE VESICLES (OMVS) HARVESTED FROM NEISSERIA MENINGITIDIS, A CLOSE RELATIVE OF THE GONOCOCCUS, HAVE A REDUCED RISK OF CONTRACTING GONORRHEA. INTRAVACC IS DEVELOPING A VACCINE FOR GONORRHEA BASED ON ITS NEISSERIA MENINGITIDIS OMV PLATFORM TECHNOLOGY. THE NEISSERIA MENINGITIDIS BACTERIA ARE DESIGNED TO EXPRESS NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE ANTIGENS ON THEIR SURFACE THAT ARE CONSERVED AMONG STRAINS AND/OR IMPORTANT FOR GROWTH, AND CAPABLE OF INDUCING BACTERICIDAL ANTIBODIES, THEREBY ENSURING BROAD PROTECTION AND STRAIN COVERAGE. IN ADDITION, THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF THE NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE PROTEINS IS OPTIMIZED BY THE HETEROLOGOUS EXPRESSION OF THESE ANTIGENS IN NEISSERIA MENINGITIDIS. THIS ENSURES BETTER NATURAL FOLDING OF THE PROTEINS AS COMPARED TO RECOMBINANT PROTEINS. THIS HETEROLOGOUS MENINGOCOCCAL OMV VACCINE FOR PREVENTION OF NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A CONSIDERABLY INCREASED EFFECTIVENESS AGAINST GONORRHEA. IN THIS CARB-X FUNDED PROJECT INTRAVACC AIMS TO DEVELOP THIS NOVEL VACCINE CONCEPT NAMED AVACC 12 UP TO A FIRST IN HUMAN STUDY.

description: OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE: THIS SOW COVERS THE IN SILICO COMPUTATIONAL RESEARCH PROJECT MINING THE GENERATED CELLULAR/HUMORAL DATASETS IN IMPACÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ TB ACROSS DIFFERENT TIME POINTS IN ESTABLISHED HUMAN COHORTS AND NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½HUMAN PRIMATE MODELS WITH IVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BCG INTERVENTION. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP NOVEL COMPUTATIONAL PIPELINES TO ANALYZE TIME COURSE DATASETS TO DEFINE THE IMMUNE SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH TB PROGRESSION. BACKGROUND: TUBERCULOSIS (TB) IS THE DEADLIEST PATHOGEN IN HISTORY AND REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH, ESPECIALLY IN RESOURCEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ POOR COUNTRIES. UP TO 25% OF THE WORLDÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S POPULATION HAS ASYMPTOMATIC MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB) INFECTIONS, WHICH CAN REACTIVATE AND CAUSE TRANSMISSIBLE PULMONARY TB DISEASE. THERE IS A HUGE WIDE SPECTRUM OF TB DISEASE STATUS, WHICH MAKES IT CHALLENGING TO UNDERSTAND THE IMMUNE MECHANISMS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF VACCINE DESIGN AND DRUG TREATMENT STRATEGIES. THEREFORE, UNDERSTANDING THE SYSTEMATIC IMMUNE RESPONSES ALONG THE TB DISEASE PROGRESSION USING COMPUTATIONAL PIPELINES WILL BOOST THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROPHYLACTIC AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. THERE ARE TWO PROJECTS UNDER THIS SUBCONTRACT. THE FIRST ONE FOCUSES ON IDENTIFYING THE HUMORAL IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO PREDICT TB PROGRESSION WHILE THE OTHER ONE IS THE TEMPORAL IMMUNE DYNAMICS OF IVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BCG ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROTECTION STATUS OF THE FOLLOWING BACTERIA CHALLENGE. THE PROPOSED COMPUTATIONAL METHODOLOGIES ARE DESCRIBED IN DETAIL LATER. TRANSFER OF MATERIALS: ALL THE EXPERIMENTAL SLIDES WILL BE MAINTAINED IN IMPACTÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½TB, IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH DR. LEELA DAVIES UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. SARAH FORTUNE AND DR. DOUGLAS LAUFFENBURGER. THE GENERATED DATASETS WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE WANG LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO, ANSCHUTZ MEDICAL CAMPUS. ALL THE DATASETS AND ANALYSES WILL BE PERFORMED ON THE APPROPRIATE CLOUDÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BASED SERVER UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. WANG. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: WE AIM TO DEVELOP ADVANCED TEMPORAL MODELING PIPELINES TO DIGEST THE DATASETS FROM FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SYSTEMS SEROLOGY PLATFORMS, DETAILED IN TWO FOLLOWING PROJECTS: 1) HUMORAL IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO PREDICT THE TB PROGRESSOR/NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROGRESSOR. WE AIM TO IDENTIFY THE IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO DISTINGUISH THE PROGRESSOR FROM THE NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROGRESSOR PATIENTS IN THE ACS COHORT, WHICH COULD BE FURTHER VALIDATED IN THE GC6 COHORT. IN THE ACS COHORT, WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THE NONLINEAR XGBOOST METHOD TO CLASSIFY THE PROGRESSOR FROM THE NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROGRESSOR IN DIFFERENT TIME INTERVALS (0Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½9M, 9Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½18M, 18Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½27M) BEFORE POSITIVE DIAGNOSTIC AND EVALUATE THE FEATURE IMPORTANCE USING INFORMATION GAIN AND THE ADVANCED INTERPRETED PREDICTION METHOD: SHAP (SHAPLEY ADDITIVE EXPLANATIONS). THEN USING THE IMPORTANCE OF FEATURES, WE COULD DEFINE THE CONCORDANCE SCORE AS THE IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO PREDICT THE PROGRESSOR/NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ PROGRESSOR ACROSS DIFFERENT COHORTS. 2) TEMPORAL IMMUNE DYNAMICS OF IVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BCG INVESTIGATION ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROTECTION STATUS OF THE FOLLOWING BACTERIA CHALLENGE. WE AIM TO PROPOSE A DATAÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½STREAM CLUSTERING STRATEGY TO IDENTIFY THE CLUSTERS INDEPENDENT FROM THE TIME POINTS COLLECTED ACROSS THE ANIMALS AND THEN BUILD THE SEPARATE TRANSITION NETWORKS ALONG THE TIME USING THE TIMEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ HOMOGENEOUS MARKOV CHAIN IN DIFFERENT STATUSES OF CHALLENGE (PROTECTION VS NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROTECTION). ALSO, WE IDENTIFY THE IMMUNE SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH DIFFERENT IMMUNE CLUSTERS USING DIFFERENTIAL ANALYSIS. AFTER THAT, WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THE LASSOÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½GRANGER CAUSALITY STRATEGY TO INVESTIGATE THE TEMPORAL ORDERS OF DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS. DELIVERABLES: THIS SUBCONTRACT AIMS TO DEVELOP SEVERAL COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS TO ANALYZE THE TEMPORAL DATASET IN IMPACTÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½TB. ALL THE PUBLICATIONS AND DISCLOSURE OF RESULTS WILL BE APPROVED BY THE COMMITTEE OF IMPACTÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½TB.

description: 1 SCOPE OF WORK C.1 BACKGROUND AND NEED THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER (VUMC) (NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE, USA). VUMC IS A NON-PROFIT 501(C) (3) HOSPITAL INCORPORATED IN THE STATE OF TENNESSEE. THE US ADVISORY COMMITTEE ON IMMUNIZATION PRACTICES (ACIP) RECOMMENDS ANNUAL INFLUENZA VACCINATION FOR THOSE 6 MONTHS OLD OR OLDER. WHILE PRIOR INFLUENZA VACCINE EFFECTIVENESS (VE) STUDIES HAVE EVALUATED PREVENTION OF DISEASE IN DIFFERENT HEALTHCARE SETTINGS, THE IMPACT OF THESE VACCINES IN PREVENTING TRANSMISSION OF INFECTION REMAINS UNDERSTUDIED. MOREOVER, THE ONGOING STUDIES CONDUCTED DURING THE SARS-COV-2 PANDEMIC HAVE DOCUMENTED THAT THE RISK OF SECONDARY INFECTIONS IN HOUSEHOLDS HAVE BEEN CONSISTENTLY HIGHER THAN THOSE MEASURED WITH SIMILAR METHODOLOGIES PRIOR TO THE START OF THE PANDEMIC. THE IMPACT OF THOSE CHANGES IN TRANSMISSION RISK ON THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INFLUENZA VACCINES FOR PREVENTING TRANSMISSION REMAINS UNCLEAR. THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO ASCERTAIN SECONDARY INFECTION RISKS AND CONDUCT A ROBUST MULTI-CENTER EVALUATION OF INFLUENZA VE IN PREVENTING LABORATORY-CONFIRMED INFECTION TRANSMISSION IN HOUSEHOLDS. WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN COMPLETING ALL AIMS OUTLINED FOR THIS APPLICATION. WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE DESIGN AND ASSEMBLY OF A NETWORK OF 3 US RESEARCH SITES AND SERVE AS AN ENROLLING SITE AND AS THE DATA AND LABORATORY COORDINATING CENTER FOR THE NETWORK. WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE DESIGN AND EXECUTION OF A CASE-ASCERTAINED STUDY WITH DAILY COLLECTION OF DATA AND SPECIMENS TO ASSESS THE TRANSMISSION OF INFLUENZA INFECTIONS AND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF VACCINATION IN PREVENTING SUSCEPTIBILITY AND INFECTIVITY. WE WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN EXAMINING THE ROLE OF THERAPEUTICS, ISOLATION AND QUARANTINE ON THE FREQUENCY OF SECONDARY INFECTIONS IN HOUSEHOLDS. WE WILL HELP CHARACTERIZE IN DETAIL THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGICAL COURSE OF SYMPTOMATIC, ASYMPTOMATIC AND PAUCI-SYMPTOMATIC INFECTIONS. OUR STUDY WILL BE LED BY INVESTIGATORS WHO HAVE VAST EXPERIENCE CONDUCTING MULTI-CENTER CASE-ASCERTAINED STUDIES AND COLLABORATING WITH CDC SCIENTISTS IN DESIGNING, EXECUTING AND GENERATING CRUCIAL EVIDENCE FROM THOSE STUDIES. WE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY (MAIN CONTRACTOR) LEADERSHIP, OTHER ENROLMENT SITES AND CDC TO DESIGN AND STANDARDIZE DATA AND SPECIMEN COLLECTION INSTRUMENTS AND PROCEDURES, PLANS FOR TESTING OF SPECIMENS, PREPARATION OF ANALYTICAL DATASETS AND COMPLETION OF ANALYSES AND REPORTS. C.2 PROJECT OBJECTIVE THE OVERALL PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING 4 TASKS: DESIGN A MULTI-SITE STUDY OF INFLUENZA TRANSMISSION WITHIN HOUSEHOLDS, ENROLL ELIGIBLE HOUSEHOLDS AND CONDUCT PROSPECTIVE STUDY ACTIVITIES, CONDUCT LABORATORY STUDIES TO CHARACTERIZE SUSCEPTIBILITY AND INFECTION, AND, PROVIDE DATA MANAGEMENT FOR SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND ANALYSES. C.3 SCOPE OF WORK THE MAIN PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE WILL BE 12-MONTHS FROM SEPTEMBER 1, 2023, THROUGH AUGUST 31, 2024, ENCOMPASSING APPROXIMATELY 8 MONTHS DEDICATED TO FIELD OPERATIONS, INCLUDING ENROLLMENT AND FOLLOW-UP AND TIME TO PREPARE FOR FIELD OPERATIONS AS WELL AS TIME FOR DATA ANALYSES AND PREPARATION OF REPORTS. TO ACCOMPLISH THE PROJECTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S OBJECTIVES, OUR VUMC SITE WILL ENROLL AND FOLLOW APPROXIMATELY 150 HOUSEHOLDS. VUMC WILL SERVE AS A SUBCONTRACTOR TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY AND WILL SERVE AS THE DATA COORDINATING CENTER (DCC) AND CENTRAL VIRAL LABORATORY FOR THE NETWORK. TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT IDENTIFICATION OF INDEX CASES, REGARDLESS OF PRESENCE OF SYMPTOMS AND RAPID ENROLMENT AND COMPLETE FOLLOW-UP OF INDEX CASES AND HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS, WE WILL IMPLEMENT A MODIFIED CASE-ASCERTAINED STUDY DESIGN. WE WILL USE ESTABLISHED HIGH-THROUGHPUT STATE-OF-THE-ART TESTING PLATFORMS TO ACCURATELY IDENTIFY INFLUENZA INFECTIONS AND APPLY A DETAILED ALGORITHM TO DETERMINE AND VERIFY VACCINATION HISTORY. IN ADDITION, WE WILL IMPLEMENT AN INTEGRATED DATA SYSTEM FOR COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF ALL STUDY ELEMENTS, THAT ENSURES REAL-TIME DATA SHARING. 2 C.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE 4 TASKS, WITH EACH TASK HAVING MULTIPLE SUBTASKS. EACH TASK/SUBTASK IS LINKED TO A DISCRETE DELIVERABLE THAT WILL BE DELIVERED FROM THE CONTRACTOR TO CDC. A DESCRIPTION OF VUMC ROLE IN EACH TASK IS OUTLINED BELOW. TASK 1: DESIGN A MULTI-SITE STUDY OF INFLUENZA TRANSMISSION WITHIN HOUSEHOLDS. OUR SITE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE PREPARATION OF A DETAILED WORK PLAN, A FULLY EXECUTED RESEARCH AGREEMENT AND/OR SUBCONTRACT WITH THE MAIN CONTRACTOR. WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE PREPARATION OF A SUMMARY OF PLANNED TASKS/OBJECTIVES, FINAL PROTOCOL AND DATA COLLECTION INSTRUMENTS, PACKET OF TRAINING SOPS AND TIMELINES FOR TRAINING. WE WILL PROVIDE DOCUMENTATION OF IRB APPROVAL AND ALL MATERIALS REVIEWED BY THE IRB AND CONTRIBUTE TO DRAFT A REPORTING DASHBOARD TO MONITOR STUDY PROGRESSION. TASK 2: ENROLL ELIGIBLE HOUSEHOLDS AND CONDUCT PROSPECTIVE STUDY ACTIVITIES (TASK 2). IN COORDINATION WITH THE MAIN CONTRACTOR, OUR SITE WILL PROVIDE WEEKLY DASHBOARD UPDATES TO THE NETWORK AND CDC Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ ON THE RECRUITMENT, ENROLLMENT, STUDY ACTIVITIES, AND DATA COLLECTION ACTIVITIES AND PROVIDE EFFICIENT ELECTRONIC REPORTING PLAN THROUGHOUT THE FULL PERIOD OF ENROLLMENT, UTILIZING REDCAP, A VUMC APPLICATION THAT IS BOTH CONFIDENTIAL AND EASILY ACCESSIBLE TO CDC AND NETWORK SITES TASK 3: CONDUCT LABORATORY STUDIES TO CHARACTERIZE SUSCEPTIBILITY AND INFECTION (TASK 3). IN COORDINATION WITH THE MAIN CONTRACTOR, WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE PREPARATION OF A SUMMARY OF PLANNED ASSAYS, LABORATORY SOPS, PLAN FOR DETERMINING PROFICIENCY (AND ONGOING COMPETENCY) OF THE PROPOSED LABORATORIES. WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE A SUMMARY OF PLAN AND PROCEDURES INVOLVED IN SPECIMEN STORAGE FOR FUTURE TESTING, INCLUDING TRANSPORT OF SPECIMENS TO CDC FOR LONG-TERM STORAGE OR FUTURE TESTING. TASK 4: PROVIDE DATA MANAGEMENT FOR SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND ANALYSES (TASK 4). IN COORDINATION WITH THE MAIN CONTRACTOR, WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE PREPARATION OF A DRAFT DATA MANAGEMENT PLAN, DEVELOPMENT OF DATABASE FORMS FOR THE CENTRAL DATABASE(S), DATA DICTIONARY OF DATABASES MAPPED TO THE DATA COLLECTION INSTRUMENTS, DRAFT DATA CLEANING PLAN, API KEY OR OTHER ACCESS METHOD (DETERMINED WITH CDC), AND SUBMISSION OF ALL FILES (RAW AND EDITED), INCLUDING DATABASE(S) TO CDC. C.5 SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS NONE C.6 PERIOD AND PLACE OF PERFORMANCE THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE WILL BE FROM SEPTEMBER 1, 2023, THROUGH AUGUST 31, 2024. DURING THE PERFORMANCE OF THE PROJECT, ENROLMENT, DATA COORDINATION AND SPECIMENS TESTING ACTIVITIES WILL BE CONDUCTED AT VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER LOCATED IN NASHVILLE, TN. C.7 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY WE DO NOT REQUEST ANY GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY FOR THIS PROJECT. C.8 TRAVEL INTERNAL LOCAL TRAVEL TO DELIVER OR RETRIEVE DATA OR SPECIMENS TO OR FROM PARTICIPATING HOUSEHOLD IS CONSIDERED IN THE PROJECT AND DETAILS ARE PROVIDED IN THE BUDGET SECTION. C.9 DELIVERABLES AND PAYMENTS THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT WE WILL MAINTAIN FREQUENT COMMUNICATION WITH THE MAIN CONTRACTOR SITE AND WITH CDC AND PARTICIPATING SITES AS APPROPRIATE. WE WILL PARTICIPATE IN CONFERENCE CALLS AS SCHEDULED BY THE MAIN CONTRACTOR AND CDC. DURING THE MEETINGS, AND IN COORDINATION WITH THE MAIN CONTRACTOR, WE WILL PRESENT AND DISCUSS PROJECT UPDATES, PROGRESS REPORTS, DASHBOARDS AS WELL AS PLANS FOR NEXT STEPS AND PLANS FOR DATA MANAGEMENT, ANALYSES AND REPORTS. DURING THOSE MEETINGS WE WILL ALSO ADDRESS POTENTIAL 3 CHALLENGES AND SOLUTIONS FOR THE PROJECT ACTIVITIES. AS A SUBCONTRACT SITE, WE WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE DELIVERY OF THE REQUIRED TASKS OUTLINED BELOW. description: OPTION 11A (0258-A468-4609) GENERATION OF GMP REAGENT DELTAFLU H5/1 THE PURPOSE OF THIS OPTION IS TO GENERATE A NEEDED REAGENT TO CONDUCT A UNIVERSAL INFLUENZA VIRUS VACCINE CLINICAL TRIAL SPONSORED BY THE CIVIC PROGRAM. THE SPECIFIC REAGENT CONSISTS OF A GMP MANUFACTURED FINAL DRUG PRODUCT (FDP) AND THE ASSOCIATED QC INFORMATION OF THE LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS VACCINE DELTAFLUH5/1. THIS LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS VACCINE CONSISTS OF AN INFLUENZA A VIRUS DELETED FOR THE NS1 GENE AND CONTAINING A CHIMERIC HEMAGGLUTININ (HA) WITH THE HEAD OF AN H5 VIRUS AND THE STALK OF AN H1 VIRUS. THIS REAGENT WILL BE USED IN A CIVIC SPONSORED CLINICAL TRIAL TOGETHER WITH A GMP MANUFACTURED FDP OF THE LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS VACCINE DELTAFLUH12/1 VIRUS, THAT WILL BE GENERATED UNDER AN ADDITIONAL OPTION 11. THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS ARE PROPOSED: AIM 1: PERFORM GMP PRODUCTION AND FILLING OF THE DELTAFLUH5/1 FDP FROM A BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE (BDS) STARTING MATERIAL GENERATED UNDER GRANT R01AI141226. THIS LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS VACCINE CONSISTS OF AN INFLUENZA A VIRUS DELETED FOR THE NS1 GENE AND CONTAINING A CHIMERIC HEMAGGLUTININ (HA) WITH THE HEAD OF AN H12 VIRUS AND THE STALK OF AN H1 VIRUS. THIS REAGENT WILL BE USED IN A CIVIC SPONSORED CLINICAL TRIAL TOGETHER WITH A GMP MANUFACTURED FDP OF THE LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS VACCINE DELTAFLUH5/1 VIRUS, THAT WILL BE GENERATED UNDER AN ADDITIONAL OPTION 11. description: BACKGROUND/CONTEXT: THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT, SCHOOL OF SOCIAL WORK INNOVATIONS INSTITUTE WILL SERVE AS A PARTNER AND PROVIDE STRATEGIC GUIDANCE AND ADVISING FOR THE CCBHC S-TAC AND WILL CONTRIBUTE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE IN DELIVERING TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE SERVICES TO SUPPORT TA DELIVERY AND THE IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE PILOT. USING STATE-OF-THE-ART RESEARCH, TRAINING, AND TECHNOLOGY, THE INNOVATIONS INSTITUTE HAS TRAINED OVER 80,000 PRACTITIONERS. THE INNOVATIONS INSTITUTE WILL USE THEIR EXPERIENCE OF WORKING WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL AND SAMHSA, AND THEIR UNIQUE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE TO SUPPORT DIRECT CONSULTATION TA AND THE S-TAC IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE PILOT. TASK 2 - TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND TRAINING TO THE FIELD AND SAMHSA Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ TASK 2.4.1 - DIRECT CONSULTATION INDIVIDUAL TA: COLLABORATE WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL TO PROVIDE DIRECT CONSULTATION INDIVIDUAL TA. description: IN COLLABORATION WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN-MADISON AND ESTABLISHED KEY COMMUNITY PARTNERS IN MILWAUKEE COUNTY, THE CITY OF MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY (MHDL) WILL CONDUCT WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING FOR SARS-COV-2 TO EVALUATE THE IMPACTS OF VACCINATION STATUS, GEOGRAPHIC SETTING, AND SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC FEATURES ON VIRAL TRANSMISSION AND EVOLUTION. MHDLÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON THE FOLLOWING KEY POPULATIONS IN MILWAUKEE COUNTY: URBAN AND UP-TO-DATE ON VACCINATION AT THE TIME OF SAMPLING AND URBAN NOT-UP-TO-DATE. AS STATED IN THE FULL PROJECT STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW), A PRIMARY DELIVERABLE FOR THIS PROJECT WILL BE ATTEMPTING TO COLLECTIVELY GENERATE 32,000 SARS-COV-2 GENOME SEQUENCES FROM METADATA-TARGETED SPECIMENS FROM THE STATES OF MINNESOTA, MICHIGAN, AND WISCONSIN. FOR MILWAUKEE URBAN AREAS, THIS WILL NOT ONLY ADDRESS SIGNIFICANT REGIONAL AND LOCAL DIFFERENCES IN SARS-COV-2 VACCINATION RATES BUT ALSO WILL ALLOW CONSISTENT SAMPLING FROM UNDERSERVED OR LIMITED ACCESS COMMUNITIES TO UNDERSTAND HOW TRENDS IN VACCINE RATES AND VIRAL DYNAMICS INTERACT OVER TIME. MHDL WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SEQUENCING APPROXIMATELY 2,000 SPECIMENS PER YEAR IN MILWAUKEE COUNTY, INCLUDING BOTH THE AFFLUENT MILWAUKEE COUNTY NEIGHBORHOODS THAT HAVE HIGHER VACCINATION RATES, AND THOSE THAT HAVE LOWER VACCINATION RATES, INCLUDING RESIDENTS LIVING IN POVERTY. MHDL WILL ALSO OBTAIN CLINICAL SPECIMENS FROM 3 MHD CLINIC LOCATIONS, AS WELL AS PROCESS REFERRAL SPECIMENS FROM 3 LOCAL REFERENCE COVID TESTING LABORATORIES IN THE METRO-MILWAUKEE AREA. ADDITIONALLY, SPECIMENS WILL BE RECEIVED FROM TWO OF THE LOCAL UNIVERSITYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S STUDENT HEALTH CENTERS (UW-MILWAUKEE AND MARQUETTE UNIVERSITY) AND COVID SHELTERS IN MILWAUKEE. PRIMARY SAMPLING GUIDELINES WILL BE THROUGH THE WISCONSIN DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SERVICES Ã¢Â‚¬Å“COVID-19 HEALTH ALERT # 25: SURVEILLANCE FOR NEW GENETIC VARIANTS OF SARS-COV-2: INFORMATION FOR CLINICIANS,Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ WHICH AUTHORIZES SARS-COV-2 TESTING PROVIDERS TO SHARE RESIDUAL SAMPLES FROM INDIVIDUALS WITH IMMUNE FAILURE, AS WELL AS FROM ITS HIGH-RISK COVID-19 SURVEILLANCE SITES, INCLUDING MILWAUKEE COUNTY JAILS, DETENTION CENTERS, CORRECTIONAL FACILITIES, HOMELESS SHELTERS, GROUP HOMES, AND OTHER COMMUNITY SETTINGS. ALL OF THOSE SITES ARE CURRENTLY MILWAUKEE HEALTH DEPARTMENT LABORATORY COVID-19 SURVEILLANCE SITES.

description: THE WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY IN ST. LOUIS, UNDER THE DIRECTION OF CRAIG SMITH, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (9/1/2023-8/31/2024). A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY: WUSTL WILL TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS HOW TO ANALYZE PROTEIN STRUCTURES. THE STUDENTS WILL WRITE MANUSCRIPTS DESCRIBING THE STRUCTURE AND (PREDICTED) FUNCTION OF SELECTED PROTEINS. IF POSSIBLE, ONE OR TWO STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN A SUMMER RESEARCH PROJECT FOCUSED ON CHARACTERIZING THE FUNCTION OF TARGET(S) USING A VARIETY OF LABORATORY METHODS. WUSTL WILL SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: WUSTL WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. WUSTL WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY STAFF MEMBERS FROM WUSTL WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. WUSTL STAFF WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR (SEPT 1, 2023 THROUGH AUG 31, 2024). UW-CRYOEM MAY ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) AND WILL SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. B. PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS: UW-CRYOEM WILL LEAD A STUDY ON THE STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THE LANGYA VIRUS ATTACHMENT AND FUSION GLYCOPROTEINS. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-CRYOEM WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FOMR UW-CRYOEM WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. description: KIP LUDWIG HAS TWO KEY ROLES IN THE NIH SPARC REVA PROJECT: AS A MEMBER OF THE END-USER EXPERT ADVISORY BOARD AND AS AN EXPERT IN VAGAL ANATOMY AND IMAGING. LUDWIG IS AN ESSENTIAL MEMBER OF THE PANEL OF NEUROMODULATION EXPERTS WHO CONSTITUTE A WORLD-CLASS PANEL OF "END USERS" OF THE REVA MAPPING DATASETS. "CLOSING THE LOOP" IS A CRITICAL STEP IN THE DATA COLLECTION PROCESS TO ENSURE THAT THIS PROJECT PRODUCES A LARGE REPOSITORY OF DATA THAT ARE USEFUL TO THE NEUROMODULATION COMMUNITY. DATA WITHOUT INSIGHT IS UNLIKELY TO LEAD TO CHANGES IN NEUROMODULATION DEVICES, PARAMETERS, OR OUTCOMES. WE ASSEMBLED A TEAM OF END USERS TO INTERPRET AND APPLY THE MAPPING DATA TO MAXIMIZE THE IMPACT OF THE REVA EFFORT ON THE NEUROMODULATION FIELD. NEUROMODULATION EXPERTS WILL REGULARLY REVIEW THE DATA TO PROVIDE EARLY, RAPID, AND ITERATIVE FEEDBACK TO THE IMAGING AND DATA TEAMS TO REFINE OUR CAPTURE AND ANNOTATION METHODOLOGIES TO MAXIMIZE THE USABILITY OF OUR DATA FOR ANALYSIS AND DESIGN OF VAGUS NERVE STIMULATION THERAPIES. THE END USER TEAM IS OF VITAL IMPORTANCE TO ENSURE THAT THE DATA FROM THE ANATOMY, IMAGING, AND DATA ANALYSIS TEAMS PROVIDE DATA RELEVANT TO NEUROMODULATION. LUDWIG HAS EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN DISSECTION, SAMPLE PREPARATION, AND IMAGING OF THE VAGUS NERVE, WHICH WILL HELP INFORM THE PROTOCOLS USED FOR THE REV ATA ARE CONTEXTUALIZED IN PRIOR ANATOMICAL AND NEURAL ENGINEERING LITERATURE.

description: SUPPORT FOR AMERICAÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CHILDREN 2023 THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL WORK WITH THE PROJECT TEAM TO PRODUCE THE ANNUAL PUBLICATION FOR THE FORUM FOR CHILD AND FAMILY STATISTICS, NAMELY AMERICAÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CHILDREN: KEY NATIONAL INDICATORS OF WELL-BEING. THE PUBLICATION TYPE IS BASED ON THE RELEASE YEAR; FULL INDICATOR REPORTS ARE RELEASED IN ODD YEARS, AND SPECIAL OR BRIEF REPORTS ARE RELEASED IN EVEN YEARS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE DESKTOP PUBLISHING SUPPORT FOR THE PDF VERSION OF THE PUBLICATION AND PROVIDE SECTION 508 REMEDIATION ON THE FINAL VERSION OF THE PDF. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL USE PROFESSIONAL LAYOUT AND GRAPHICS SOFTWARE FROM THE ADOBE CLOUD CREATIVE SUITE (INDESIGN, ILLUSTRATOR, AND PHOTOSHOP) TO PREPARE THE REPORT MATERIALS AND WILL SUBMIT THE FINAL PACKAGE TO THE PROJECT TEAM AS PART OF FINAL DELIVERABLES AT THE END OF THE PRODUCTION CYCLE. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE DESKTOP PUBLISHING SUPPORT THROUGHOUT THE PRODUCTION CYCLE, PROVIDING MULTIPLE DRAFTS FOR TEAM AND CLIENT REVIEW AND WILL IMPLEMENT REVISIONS ONLY AS REQUESTED WHILE MAINTAINING VERSION CONTROL THROUGHOUT THE PRODUCTION PROCESS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE NON-SECTION 508 COMPLIANT PDF VERSIONS FOR ITERATIVE REVIEWS THROUGHOUT THE PRODUCTION CYCLE, AND THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL THEN PROVIDE A SECTION 508 COMPLIANT PDF FOR THE FINAL VERSION BASED ON THE ACCESSIBILITY GUIDELINES PROVIDED BY THE PROJECT TEAM. AS REQUESTED, THE SUBCONTRACTOR MAY ALSO PROVIDE OTHER POST-PRODUCTION SERVICES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO A PRINT PACKAGE FOR SUBMISSION TO A GPO-APPROVED PRINTER AND SPECIFIED FILE FORMATS OF REPORT FIGURES, PHOTOS, AND CONTENT TO SHARE WITH THE WEB TEAM.

description: WE WILL WORK WITH UW-MADISON AND OTHER PARTNERS TO COMPARE SARS-COV-2 SEQUENCE DIVERSITY AND VIRAL PHYLODYNAMICS WITHIN AND BETWEEN REGIONS WITH DIFFERENCES IN VACCINE UPTAKE. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL WORK IN COLLABORATION WITH THE MINNESOTA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (MDH) TO GENERATE 1000 SEQUENCES PER YEAR FROM VACCINE Ã¢Â‚¬Å“UP-TO-DATEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ INDIVIDUALS AND 1000 SEQUENCES PER YEAR FROM UNVACCINATED OR NOT UP-TO-DATE PEOPLE IN RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES IN MN. IN ADDITION, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF VACCINATION STATUS AND GEOGRAPHIC SETTING ON SARS-COV-2 TRANSMISSION AND EVOLUTION IN MN. WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACTS OF VACCINATION STATUS, GEOGRAPHIC SETTING, AND SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC FEATURES ON VIRAL TRANSMISSION AND EVOLUTION. WE WILL MODEL TRANSMISSION AMONG 4 GROUPS: URBAN AND UP-TO-DATE ON VACCINATION AT THE TIME OF SAMPLING, URBAN NOT-UP-TO-DATE, RURAL UP-TO-DATE, AND RURAL NOT-UP-TO-DATE. WE WILL INFER HOW TRANSMISSION RATES AMONG THESE GROUPS VARY OVER TIME AND WITH THE EMERGENCE OF NEW VARIANTS. FINALLY, WE WILL WORK WITH MDH (AND OTHER PARTNERS) TO DEVELOP A DATA INFRASTRUCTURE CAPABLE OF MANAGING ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN PUBLICLY AVAILABLE SEQUENCE DATA AND PROTECTED HEALTH INFORMATION.

description: THE NIH SPARC REVA AWARDEES WILL CONDUCT MULTIMODAL, MULTISCALE IMAGING OF 100 HUMAN VAGUS NERVES TO SEED AND ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL NEUROMODULATION THERAPIES FOR AUTONOMIC REGULATION. AT DUKE, WE WILL USE THE MULTIMODAL, MULTISCALE IMAGING DATA FOR ANALYSIS AND DESIGN OF VAGUS NERVE STIMULATION (VNS) WITH COMPUTATIONAL MODELING. THIS WORK WILL SEED AND ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL NEUROMODULATION THERAPIES FOR AUTONOMIC REGULATION. THE INFORMATION GAINED FROM OUR MULTI-MODAL MAPPING WILL PROVIDE UNRIVALED ACCURACY TO COMPUTATIONAL MODELS TO PREDICT NEUROMODULATION STIMULATION EFFICACY AND SIDE EFFECTS. EARLY IN THE PROJECT, WE WILL IMPLEMENT COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF VNS USING PILOT MICROCT, MUSE, AND HISTOLOGY IMAGING DATASETS TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK TO THE IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS, AND DATA CURATION TEAMS. WE WILL EXPAND OUR EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE FOR MODELING VNS TO HANDLE NEW IMAGING DATA TYPES THAT DEFINE FIBER PATHWAYS, RASTRUCTURE, WE WILL DEFINE 3D FIBER PATHWAYS USING TRACTOGRAPHY DATA FROM MICROSCOPY WITH ULTRAVIOLET SURFACE EXCITATION (MUSE), COMPLEMENTING OUR EXISTING PHYSICS-BASED APPROACH. WE WILL ALSO ADVANCE OUR MODELING INFRASTRUCTURE TO ENABLE USER-SPECIFIED PAIRS OF VALUES FOR FIBER DIAMETER AND LOCATION (AS DEFINED BY MUSE AND HISTOLOGICAL DATA). USING THIS COMPUTATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE, WE WILL MODEL CERVICAL VNS FOR NERVES FROM MULTIPLE INDIVIDUALS, IMAGED USING MULTIPLE MODALITIES. CERVICAL VNS HAS BEEN USED TO TREAT EPILEPSY, RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS, AND HEART FAILURE, AMONG MANY OTHER CONDITIONS. WE WILL DEFINE THE NERVE MORPHOLOGY USING MICROCT, MUSE, AND HISTOLOGY; WE WILL DEFINE FIBER PATHWAYS, DIAMETERS, AND LOCATIONS USING MUSE AND HISTOLOGY, AS DESCRIBED ABOVE. WE WILL ALSO INTEGRATE DATA FROM IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY TO LOCALIZE AFFERENT VERSUS EFFERENT FIBERS. WE WILL ANALYZE THE RESULTING ACTIVATION THRESHOLDS TO QUANTIFY FIBER RECRUITMENT INPUT-OUTPUT RESPONSES ACROSS STIMULATION AMPLITUDES. WE WILL ALSO IMPLEMENT MODELS OF VNS AT DIFFERENT LOCATIONS ALONG THE NERVE. VNS IS TYPICALLY IMPLANTED AT THE MID-CERVICAL LEVEL, BUT THE FASCICULAR ORGANIZATION CHANGES DRAMATICALLY OVER THE LENGTH OF THE CERVICAL NERVE IN HUMANS, AND OTHER STIMULATION LOCATIONS MAY PROVIDE MORE SELECTIVE ACTIVATION, WITH FEWER SIDE EFFECTS. THEREFORE, WE WILL SIMULATE ACTIVATION THRESHOLDS AT THE MID-CERVICAL LEVEL (I.E., STANDARD IMPLANT LOCATION), CAUDAL- MOST CERVICAL LEVEL (I.E., SURGICALLY ACCESSIBLE IN THE NECK), CAUDAL TO THE RECURRENT LARYNGEAL BRANCH (I.E., TO AVOID LARYNGEAL SIDE EFFECTS), ABDOMINAL TRUNK, HEPATIC BRANCH, AND GASTRIC BRANCH. THE APPLICATION OF THE REVA IMAGING DATA IN COMPUTATIONAL MODELS WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL END-USE VALIDATION AND DEMONSTRATED APPLICATIONS OF ANALYSIS AND THROUGH ANATOMICALLY-REALISTIC, BIOPHYSICAL, VALIDATED COMPUTATIONAL MODELS.

description: THE WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY GROUP (WSU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GARRY BUCHKO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENTS. WSU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST ONE NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS YEAR OF THE CONTRACT (SEPT 1, 2023 THROUGH AUG 31, 2024), WHICH MAY SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR). WSU MAY ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY NMR: WSU (DR. BUCHKO) WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST ONE PROTEIN USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE, AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE SEATTLE CHILDRENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY WSU. description: THE OBJECTIVE IS TO ADDRESS UNMET NEEDS IN SARS COV 2 SEROLOGICAL TESTING: 1) STANDARDIZATION; 2) ASSAY DEVELOPMENT; AND 3) AVAILABILITY OF LARGE SCALE TESTING TO IDENTIFY THOSE WHO MAY HAVE BEEN INFECTED OR EXPOSED TO THE VIRUS. SCALING UP OF VALIDATED SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGICAL ASSAYS WITH EMERGENCY USE AUTHORIZATION (EUA) WITH EVIDENCE OF HIGH SPECIFICITY, SENSITIVITY AND REPRODUCIBILITY, WILL INCREASE NOT ONLY THE NATIONAL TESTING CAPACITY, BUT ALSO ENABLE COMPARISONS OF DATA ACROSS DIFFERENT SITES AND STUDIES. THEREFORE, IT WILL FACILITATE AN UNDERSTANDING OF NATURAL HISTORY OF THE SARS COV 2 INFECTION; VACCINE DEVELOPMENT; AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW VACCINE CANDIDATES. THIS WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SERONET (ACADEMIC AND COMMERCIAL SEROLOGY LABORATORIES); INCLUDING THE FNLCR SEROLOGY LABORATORY; SSNCC AND THE SSC TO DEVELOP AND MAKE AVAILABLE REAGENTS AND STANDARDS TO THE SEROLOGY COMMUNITY ONCE GENERATED AND QUALIFIED.

description: THIS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT (R&D) CONTRACT WAS AWARDED AS PART OF THE MULTIPLE-AWARD INDEFINITE DELIVERY, INDEFINITE QUANTITY (IDIQ) CONTRACTS FOR THE CONTRACEPTIVE CLINICAL TRIALS NETWORK (CCTN) FEMALE SITES. THE PURPOSE OF THESE CONTRACTS IS TO ESTABLISH A NETWORK OF CLINICAL RESEARCH SITES COLLABORATING TO EVALUATE NEW FEMALE CONTRACEPTIVE DRUGS AND DEVICES FOR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN PHASE I, II, III AND IV CLINICAL TRIALS. THIS CONTRACT SHALL PROVIDE THE REQUISITE PERSONNEL, FACILITIES AND SERVICES TO CONDUCT AND SUPPORT THESE CLINICAL TRIALS. THE DATA COLLECTED FROM THE CCTN THROUGH CLINICAL TRIALS ON NEW ENTITIES ARE THE BASIS FOR ADVANCING CANDIDATE DRUGS AND DEVICES THROUGH DEVELOPMENT WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF SUBMISSION TO THE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) IN SUPPORT OF REGULATORY APPROVAL. PRODUCTS EVALUATED IN THE CCTN ARE SELECTED TO ADDRESS GAPS IN AVAILABLE CONTRACEPTIVE TECHNOLOGY, INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SAFER, MORE ACCEPTABLE, AND MORE ACCESSIBLE CONTRACEPTIVE METHODS FOR WOMEN, INCLUDING WOMEN WHO ARE OBESE OR HAVE OTHER RISK FACTORS THAT LIMIT THEIR USE OF EXISTING METHODS.

description: THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO DEVELOP THE APPLICATION OF THE ZINC IONOPHORE PBT2 TO DISRUPT THE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE MECHANISMS OF STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE, HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE, AND MORAXELLA CATARRHALIS, THE PRIMARY ETIOLOGICAL AGENTS OF COMMUNITY ACQUIRED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA (CABP). PBT2 IS A SAFE-FOR-HUMAN-USE HYDROXYQUINOLINE IONOPHORE THAT WAS ORIGINALLY DEVELOPED TO TREAT HUMAN NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES AND PROGRESSED TO PHASE II CLINICAL TRIALS. WE HAVE REPURPOSED PBT2 TO FACILITATE THE INTRACELLULAR ACCUMULATION OF ZINC IONS WITHIN BACTERIAL PATHOGENS AND SHOWN THAT THIS DISRUPTS THEIR ABILITY TO RESIST TREATMENT BY BETA-LACTAM AND TETRACYCLINE CLASS ANTIBIOTICS. IN THE CARB-X SUPPORT PROJECT WE WILL DEMONSTRATE THE BREADTH OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE BREAKAGE BY PBT2 AGAINST A PANEL OF GLOBAL STRAINS, GENERATE FURTHER EFFICACY DATA FOR PBT2+ANTIBIOTIC TREATMENT IN MOUSE MODELS OF LUNG INFECTION, UNDERTAKE A PRELIMINARY PHARMACOKINETIC STUDY, AND PERFORM A GAP ANALYSIS OF THE PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL DATA FOR PBT2.

description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO DRC, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORTS AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE SEVERAL CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDIES. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE FOLLOWING PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS 2 SARS COV 2 INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID 19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID 19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE PALM 007 PROTOCOL. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THE PALM 007 TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT TPOXX IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE PALM 008 PROTOCOL. PALM 008 IS A COHORT EVENTS MONITORING STUDY FOR THE ASSESSMENT OF SAFETY PROFILE OF MVA BN JYNNEOS VACCINE IN ADULT PERSONNEL AND STAFF IN THE PALM 007 STUDY IN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO. MODIFICATION 12 SUPPORTS RESEARCH ACTIVITIES FOR THE PROTOCOLS DESCRIBED ABOVE THROUGH THE CY24 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE.

description: OPTION 19A: 0258-A466-4609 THIS PROJECT WILL ASSESS THE IMMUNE RESPONSES INDUCED BY SERIAL VACCINATION WITH GROUP 2 CHIMERIC HEMAGGLUTININ CONSTRUCTS (CHA) IN MICE. THE CHA VACCINATION STRATEGY, WHICH REFOCUSES THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TOWARD THE STALK DOMAIN AND THE CONSERVED NEURAMINIDASE, HAS BEEN TESTED IN CLINICAL TRIALS WITH SUCCESSFUL RESULTS IN TERMS OF SUSTAINED AND BROADLY CROSS-REACTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES. RECENT ADVANCES ON THE MRNA PLATFORM HAVE OPENED THE OPPORTUNITY TO USE THIS TECHNOLOGY AS A DELIVERY PLATFORM FOR CHA CONSTRUCTS. WE WILL COMPARE SIDE BY SIDE CHA VACCINES DELIVERED USING THE MRNA PLATFORM AND THE INACTIVATED SPLIT VACCINE PLATFORM WITH THE GOAL OF INDUCING BROAD AND LONG-LASTING IMMUNE RESPONSES. DR. PARDI WILL COLLABORATE WITH DRS. KRAMMER AND PUENTE-MASSAGUER IN DESIGN, EXECUTION, ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, PRESENTATION, AND PUBLICATION OF EXPERIMENTS. DR. PARDI WILL SPECIFICALLY BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DESIGN AND PRODUCTION OF ALL MRNA CONSTRUCTS USED IN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH. ADDITIONALLY, HIS LABORATORY WILL PERFORM SELECT IMMUNIZATION EXPERIMENTS AND EVALUATION OF INDUCED IMMUNE RESPONSES. OPTION 19B: IF300302079-940002 DR. PARDI WILL COLLABORATE WITH DRS. SIMON AND KRAMMER IN DESIGN, EXECUTION, ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, PRESENTATION, AND PUBLICATION OF EXPERIMENTS. DR. PARDI WILL SPECIFICALLY BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DESIGN AND PRODUCTION OF ALL MRNA-LNP CONSTRUCTS USED IN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH. HE WILL ALSO PROVIDE ADVICE AND OVERSIGHT FOR THE EXPERIMENTS USING MRNA-LNPS.

description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID 19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS 2 (SARS COV 2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID 19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYS NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORT AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDY. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL, AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, BIOREPOSITORY, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID 19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGS SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 WAS REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 03 TO ADDRESS AN INCREASE IN THE TARGET ENROLLMENT TO 1,100 PARTICIPANTS UNDER INVITE PROTOCOL V2.0 ASSUMPTIONS. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 03 ADDRESSED COSTS FOR THE PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR A RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED TRIAL OF THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF TECOVIRIMAT FOR THE TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX VIRUS DISEASE, SUCH AS PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT AND RESEARCH SITE ASSESSMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGS SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 WAS REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 04 NOW REFERRED TO AS THE INVITE COVID-19 OBSERVATIONAL VACCINE STUDY TO INCLUDE THE PALM 007 MONKEYPOX TREATMENT RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT (TPOXX) IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. MODIFICATION 05 ADDRESSED INCLUDING TO INCLUDE COST TO SUPPORT PALM 007 MONKEYPOX RCT BUDGET TO INCLUDE (1) ONE MONTH OF STAFFING AND INITIAL MEETING COSTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION AT THE CLINICAL SITE IN TUNDA FROM AUGUST 1, 2022 THROUGH AUGUST 30, 2022; AND (2) INCLUDE THE KOLE SITE PREPARATION/RENOVATION COSTS. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 06 INCLUDED RE-COSTING PALM 007 MONKEYPOX RCT BUDGET TO (1) INCLUDE PROTOCOL IMPLEMENTATION AT ONE SITE, TUNDA GENERAL HOSPITAL, WITH A TARGET ENROLLMENT OF 200 PARTICIPANTS, INCLUDING SUPPORT REQUIRED FOR THE JYNNEOS SAFETY STUDY; (2) EXTEND POP FOR THE CY23 8/31/2022-8/30/2023 BY EXERCISING OPTION PERIOD ONE FOR THE INVITE AND BIOREPOSITORY BUDGET.

description: UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND SCHOOL OF MEDICINE THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH ARE AS FOLLOWS. 1) TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED RISK FACTORS FOR ASYMPTOMATIC INTESTINAL CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND INCIDENCE OF INTESTINAL AND NON-INTESTINAL CRE ACQUISITION DURING ICU STAY AMONG PATIENTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICUS. DELIVERABLES: WE WILL DETERMINE BASELINE ADMISSION CRE PREVALENCE AND CRE ACQUISITION RATES IN THE ICUS IN THE STUDY HOSPITAL USING SCS. IN ADDITION, RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND CRE ACQUISITION DURING ICU STAY WILL BE DETERMINED. CRE PREVALENCE DETECTED BY ROUTINE CLINICAL CARE VERSUS SURVEILLANCE CULTURES WILL ALSO BE DETERMINED. 2) TO DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY UTILIZING BASELINE PHASE DATA FROM AIM 1. DELIVERABLES: WE WILL DETERMINE HOW ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE CRE RATE RATIOS IN THE ICUS COMPARE WITH SCS VERSUS LCS BASED ON VARIOUS DAYS OF THE WEEK IN THE TWO ICUS, AND WHETHER CLINICAL RISK FACTOR AND CLINICAL CULTURE INFORMATION COULD AUGMENT THE LCS STRATEGY. 3) TO DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION(S) ON INTESTINAL CRE COLONIZATION PREVALENCE AT DISCHARGE USING LCS STRATEGY. DELIVERABLES: WE WILL COMPARE THE CRE INCIDENCE RATE RATIOS BEFORE AND AFTER THE INTERVENTION TO DETERMINE THE FEASIBILITY OF LCS STRATEGY TO GUIDE INFECTION PREVENTION MEASURES. DR. SURBHI LEEKHA WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. GANDRA IN PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC INPUT INTO THE DESIGN AND CONDUCT OF ALL ASPECTS OF THIS PROPOSAL. SHE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE START-UP MEETING, REGULAR COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE STUDY TEAM AND CDC, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, DATA COLLECTION, AND DATA ANALYSIS. SHE WILL ALSO TRAVEL TO THE STUDY HOSPITAL IN INDIA TWICE DURING THE STUDY ALONG WITH WASHU TEAM. THE TRAVEL TO INDIA WILL DEPEND ON THE PANDEMIC SITUATION AND UNIVERSITY AND CDC GUIDELINES FOR TRAVEL.

description: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE STUDY AND THE MEASLES STUDY AS FURTHER OUTLINED IN THE SOW. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID 19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY AND DURABILITY, AND SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS 2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE THROUGH THEIR COUNTRYS NATIONAL VACCINATION PROGRAMS. THE STUDY TEAM WILL NOT BE ADMINISTERING THE VACCINE; RECEIPT OF VACCINE WILL BE PROVIDED THROUGH EACH COUNTRYS VACCINE PROGRAM. BLOOD SPECIMENS WILL BE COLLECTED TO MEASURE THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THE VACCINE. THE MEASLES PROTOCOL IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL, LONGITUDINAL PEDIATRIC STUDY TO BE CONDUCTED IN 4 AFRICAN COUNTRIES (GUINEA, MALI, LIBERIA, AND DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO) TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECTS OF MEASLES VIRUS (MEV) INFECTION ON PRE-EXISTING IMMUNITY, VACCINE RESPONSE, AND SUSCEPTIBILITY TO SUBSEQUENT ILLNESS. ELIGIBLE CHILDREN WILL BE ENROLLED INTO EITHER THE CASE ARM (ACUTE MEV INFECTION) OR CONTROL ARM (NO ACUTE MEV INFECTION) AS DETERMINED BY UPPER RESPIRATORY AND BLOOD SAMPLES. ALL PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE A STANDARD 3-DOSE SERIES OF RABIES VACCINATION, RANDOMIZED TO EITHER 2 MONTHS OR 11 MONTHS AFTER ENROLLMENT. BLOOD SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED AT SCREENING/ENROLLMENT (DAY 0) AND FOLLOW-UP VISITS ON DAY 14, MONTH 3, AND MONTH 12 TO ASSESS ANY DIFFERENCES IN RABIES VACCINE RESPONSES BETWEEN CHILDREN WITH AND WITHOUT MEV INFECTION, AND ANY DIFFERENCES BASED ON THE TIME OF THE VACCINE RECEIPT. THE SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN GUINEA, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THESE CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORTS AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH (MOH) TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THESE CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDIES. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES AS FURTHER OUTLINED IN THE STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW).

IMMUNIZATION MATERIAL WILL INCLUDE 3RD PARTY OWNED MATERIALS. ANIMALS WILL BE CHALLENGED WITH H7N9 OR H5N1 AND ASSESSED FOR SEVERAL EXPERIMENTAL ENDPOINTS.

description: IN ORDER TO GENERATE AND COLLECT THE DATA TO BE USED TO EVALUATE THE MEASUREMENT PROPERTIES OF THE 88 TMD PROM ITEMS, AIR IS WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH L&E RESEARCH TO CONTACT AND RECRUIT UP TO 800 ADULT PATIENTS WITH TMDS TO PARTICIPATE IN AN ONLINE REDCAP SURVEY. ONCE ENROLLED, L&E RESEARCH WILL ASK PARTICIPANTS TO RESPOND TO AN ONLINE SURVEY ESTIMATED TO TAKE APPROXIMATELY 30 MINUTES. L&E WILL PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH THE SURVEY LINK WHICH WILL BE PROVIDED TO L&E BY AIR. FOLLOWING PARTICIPANTSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ COMPLETION OF THE SURVEY, L&E RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH A LINK TO THE TREMENDOUS WEBSITE TO DISPERSE A $50 GIFT CARD INCENTIVE. ADDITIONALLY, AIR WILL NEED TO RESURVEY A SUBSET OF THE SAMPLE IN ORDER TO SUPPORT ESTIMATES OF TEST-RETEST RELIABILITY. L&E WOULD ASSIST AIR TO RE-ADMINISTER THE TMD PROM SURVEY TWO WEEKS FOLLOWING THE INITIAL DATA COLLECTION TO A SUBSAMPLE OF UP TO 300 PARTICIPANTS WHO HAVE STABLE SYMPTOMS AND FUNCTIONING. THESE PARTICIPANTS WOULD RECEIVE A SECOND $50 INCENTIVE PAYMENT FROM L&E. THE SUBSAMPLE OF PARTICIPANTS WILL BE IDENTIFIED DURING THE INITIAL PARTICIPANT SCREENING PROTOCOL BY ASKING POTENTIAL RECRUITS TO CHARACTERIZE THE STABILITY OF THEIR TMD SYMPTOMS OVER ANY TWO-WEEK PERIOD. PLEASE SEE THE RECRUITMENT MATERIALS THAT AIR HAS CREATED FOR L&E PRESENTED IN APPENDIX A AND SECTIONS 2 AND 3 BELOW FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS REGARDING THE RECRUITMENT AND SCREENING PROCESS.

description: THE ACCELERATOR WILL PROVIDE A BROAD RANGE OF SUPPORT TO PRODUCT DEVELOPERS FUNDED BY CARB-X. THIS WILL INCLUDE PROJECT SPECIFIC SUPPORT, SUPPORT ACROSS PROJECTS, AND SUPPORT CULTIVATING THE BROADER COMMUNITY OF PEOPLE DEDICATED TO FIGHTING DRUG RESISTANT BACTERIA. PROJECT SPECIFIC SUPPORT WILL INCLUDE GUIDANCE AND MONITORING ACROSS A RANGE OF ALL TECHNICAL NEEDS: CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGY, STUDY DESIGN, DATA ANALYSIS, REGULATORY, AND MANUFACTURING PROCESSES. FROM A BUSINESS STAND POINT, THE ACCELERATORS COULD POTENTIALLY BE ABLE TO FACILITATE INTRODUCTIONS TO POTENTIAL INVESTORS, COLLABORATORS, EXPERIENCED BIOTECH EXECUTIVES AND OTHER STRATEGIC PARTNERS. CROSS PROJECT SUPPORT WILL INVOLVE ADDRESSING NEEDS OR OPPORTUNITIES ACROSS MULTIPLE PRODUCT DEVELOPERS. THESE OPPORTUNITIES WILL BE PRIORITIZED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CARB-X. THEY MAY BE ADDRESSED VIA EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL, SEMINARS, ON-LINE SESSIONS, OR OTHER APPROACHES. ACCELERATORS WILL ALSO SUPPORT COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BY CREATING OPPORTUNITIES FOR ALL CONTRIBUTORS IN THE ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR) COMMUNITIES TO MEET, EXCHANGE IDEAS, AND MAKE NEW CONNECTIONS. THESE OPPORTUNITIES CAN ALSO BE IN PERSON OR VIA ON-LINE APPROACHES.

description: THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NTM INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, PROTEOMICS, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB TASK 3.6 PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS OF NHP SAMPLES VALIDATING TRANSCRIPTOMIC RESULTS. PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS ON A SUBSET OF SAMPLES GENERATED IN NONHUMAN PRIMATES IN OPTION 3. VALIDATION OF TRANSCRIPTOMICS RESULTS WILL BE PERFORMED BY TARGETED PROTEOMICS ON NONHUMAN PRIMATE (NHP) SAMPLES GENERATED BY UKHSA AND SENT TO CSU. MULTIPLE REACTION MONITORING Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ MASS SPECTROMETRY (MRM-MS) WILL BE USED TO DETECT AND QUANTIFY THE RELATIVE ABUNDANCE OF BIOMARKERS IDENTIFIED VIA RNASEQ AND NANOSTRING. THE TOP 20 TARGETS WILL BE SELECTED FOR VALIDATION. FIRST, A HOMOLOGY SEARCH ACROSS THE FOUR SPECIES WILL BE MADE WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF SELECTING PEPTIDES WITH IDENTICAL SEQUENCE AMONG THE SPECIES. THREE PEPTIDES PER TARGET WILL BE INCLUDED TO DEVELOP AND OPTIMIZE MRM-MS FOR EACH OF THE TARGETS. A HEAVY LABELED PEPTIDE WILL BE CUSTOM MADE AND USED AS AN INTERNAL STANDARD TO FACILITATE DETECTION, QUANTIFICATION, AND REPRODUCIBILITY AMONG SAMPLES. THIS FINAL ASSAY WILL BE EVALUATED FOR LIMIT OF DETECTION (LOD), LIMIT OF QUANTIFICATION (LOQ) AND REPRODUCIBILITY. METHODS OPTIMIZED IN THE BASE PERIOD WILL BE USED TO PROCESS SAMPLES (REMOVING ALBUMIN AND IGG, WHICH INTERFERE WITH ANALYSIS). IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THE TOP 20 TARGETS MAY NOT PRESENT HIGH HOMOLOGY AMONG SPECIES. THIS WILL MAKE DIFFICULT TO CHOOSE A REPRESENTATIVE PEPTIDE FOR ALL SPECIES. IF WE FIND THIS TO BE THE CASE, WE WILL INCLUDE ONE UNIQUE PEPTIDE PER SPECIES PER TARGET. BECAUSE OF THE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS STRATEGY WE WILL REDUCE THE NUMBER OF TARGETS FOR VALIDATION TO A MAXIMUM OF 15. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOME OF THE TOP 20 TARGETS SELECTED VIA TRANSCRIPTOMICS MAY NOT TRANSLATE TO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES AMONG GROUPS WHEN EVALUATED VIA PROTEOMICS. THIS MAY BE DUE TO A MULTITUDE OF FACTORS SUCH AS POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS, LOCALIZATION OF PROTEINS, DEGRADATION BY INTERNAL PROTEASES, LOW STABILITY OF BOTH MRNA AND PROTEINS. IN ORDER TO COMPLEMENT THE TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA, WE WILL USE THE SPIKEMIXTM CYTOKINES PANELS DEVELOPED DURING THE BASE PERIOD TO COMPARE THE DIFFERENT COHORTS WITH THE GOAL OF IDENTIFYING ADDITIONAL PROTEIN BIOMARKERS. THE SPIKEMIXTM CYTOKINES MAY ALLOW FOR THE DETECTION OF MORE THAN 80 NHP PRIMATE CYTOKINES. TASK 3.7 COMPARE IMMUNE PROFILES IN NHP, SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AND HUMANS TO IDENTIFY CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. CONFIGURE A BROADER DEDICATED NETWORK DATABASE/COMPUTATIONAL SERVER, EXPANDING ON RESOURCES GENERATED IN THE BASE PERIOD. 2. ESTABLISH PROTOCOLS AND STANDARDIZED DOCUMENTATION FOR DATA COLLECTION AND PRE-PROCESSING FOR ALL THE EXPERIMENTS USING MICE AND GUINEA PIG MODELS 3. CONSTRUCT A RELATIONAL DATABASE (RDB) FOR THE PRIMARY DATA FROM MOUSE EXPERIMENTS. 4. DEVELOP A SINGLE-TYPE DATA DRIVEN ANALYSIS TOOLS FOR EACH EXPERIMENTAL DATA TYPE. 5. DEVELOP A BROADER DYNAMICAL SYSTEM MODEL FOR CELL MEDIATED IMMUNITY BASED ON THE AVAILABLE MOUSE VACCINATION AND TB INFECTION MODELS. 6. description: BWC0977 IS A SMALL MOLECULE NOVEL BACTERIAL TOPOISOMERASE INHIBITOR (NBTI), UNDER DEVELOPMENT AS A BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBIOTIC FOR THE POTENTIAL TREATMENT OF COMPLICATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CUTI), COMPLICATED INTRA-ABDOMINAL INFECTIONS (CIAI), SKIN AND SOFT TISSUE INFECTIONS (SSTI) AND HOSPITAL ACQUIRED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA (HABP)/VENTILATOR ASSOCIATED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA (VABP). BWC0977 SELECTIVELY INHIBITS BACTERIAL DNA REPLICATION BY INTERACTING IN A UNIQUE WAY WITH THE GYRA SUBUNIT OF BACTERIAL DNA GYRASE AND THE PARC SUBUNIT OF BACTERIAL TOPOISOMERASE IV. BWC0977 EXHIBITS MIC90 0.5-2 ΜG/ML AGAINST PATHOGENS WITHIN ENTEROBACTERIACEAE, K. PNEUMONIAE, A. BAUMANNII AND P. AERUGINOSA, AND < 0.1 ΜG/ML AGAINST MRSA AND VRE. BWC0977 HAS SHOWN NO TARGET-MEDIATED CROSS-RESISTANCE WITH AGENTS IN CURRENT USE, INCLUDING FLUOROQUINOLONES, AND DEMONSTRATES EFFICACY IN LUNG, THIGH AND URINARY TRACT BACTERIAL INFECTION MODELS OF E. COLI, K. PNEUMONIAE, P. AERUGINOSA, AND A. BAUMANNII. THE DOSE LIMITING TOXICITY FOR BWC0977 IN PRECLINICAL STUDIES WAS AN ACUTE TOLERABILITY SYNDROME, WHICH WAS DOSE DEPENDENT. BASED ON RAT AND DOG TOXICOLOGY STUDIES, THE PREDICTED THERAPEUTIC INDEX BASED ON CMAX AND AUC TO ACHIEVE EFFICACY VERSUS KEY GRAM-NEGATIVE PATHOGENS IS ESTIMATED TO BE > 5 & 1, RESPECTIVELY. TO ESTABLISH THE SAFETY PROFILE FOR BWC0977, A FIRST-IN-HUMAN (FIH) STUDY WAS CONDUCTED AS A RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLINDED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED, SINGLE ASCENDING-DOSE (SAD) AND MULTIPLE ASCENDING-DOSE (MAD) STUDY IN HEALTHY SUBJECTS. BWC0977 WAS ADMINISTERED INTRAVENOUSLY (IV), DOSED IN AN ASCENDING FASHION WITH STAGGERED DOSING WITHIN EACH COHORT TO ENSURE ADEQUATE CLINICAL SAFETY BEFORE PROCEEDING WITH THE REMAINDER OF THE SUBJECTS IN THE COHORT. IN HUMAN SAD STUDIES, PLASMA CMAX AND AUC INCREASED PROPORTIONALLY WITH DOSE. THE DRUG WAS WELL-TOLERATED; DYSGEUSIA WAS THE MOST COMMON TREATMENT ASSOCIATED ADVERSE EVENT (TEAE). HOWEVER, IN THE FIRST COHORT IN MAD PHASE, ALL SUBJECTS EXPERIENCED INFUSION SITE REACTIONS (ISRS). THE TRIAL WAS PAUSED TO ALLOW DEVELOPMENT OF AN OPTIMIZED FORMULATION. A NEW RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLIND, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED, PHASE 1 STUDY OF THE SAFETY, TOLERABILITY, AND PHARMACOKINETICS OF SINGLE AND MULTIPLE ASCENDING DOSES OF BWC0977 BY INTRAVENOUS (IV) INFUSION WITH A NEW FORMULATION IN HEALTHY ADULT VOLUNTEERS IS PLANNED. THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS THE SAFETY AND TOLERABILITY OF BWC0977. THE SECONDARY OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS THE PHARMACOKINETIC (PK) CHARACTERISTICS IN PLASMA AND URINE OF BWC0977. THE EXPLORATORY OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS THE QT/CORRECTED QT (QTC) PROLONGATION POTENTIAL OF BWC0977.

description: INDIRECT-ACTING SMALL-MOLECULE INHIBITORS OF ELASTASE (LASB) FOR THE TREATMENT OF P. AERUGINOSA LUNG INFECTIONS THIS PROGRAM AIMS AT DISCOVERING A PRECLINICAL CANDIDATE FOR THE TREATMENT OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS (CF) IN ADOLESCENT AND PEDIATRIC PATIENTS. OUR LEAD COMPOUNDS TARGET THE EXTRACELLULAR ZINC-METALLOPROTEASE LASB, WHICH PLAYS A PIVOTAL ROLE IN THE PATHOGENESIS AND INFECTIVITY OF PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (P.A.). THIS GRAM-NEGATIVE PATHOGEN IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY RESISTANT AND WITH THAT HIGHLY DIFFICULT TO TREAT. DURING HIT-TO-LEAD DEVELOPMENT OF TWO COMPOUND CLASSES IN THE FRAME OF CARB-X FUNDING, COMPOUNDS WILL BE OPTIMIZED IN A MULTIPARAMETER APPROACH. THE LEAD PROFILE COMPRISES POTENT IN VITRO ACTIVITY, SELECTIVITY OVER HUMAN MATRIX-METALLOPROTEASES (MMPS), IN VITRO/EX VIVO TARGET ENGAGEMENT AND, IMPORTANTLY, IN VIVO EFFICACY IN A MURINE LASB INSTILLATION MODEL. THIS WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY EARLY IN VITRO ADME/T STUDIES TO ALLOW SELECTION FOR FAVORABLE ADME/T PROPERTIES. THE SUBSEQUENT LEAD OPTIMIZATION PROCESS WILL AIM AT THE FURTHER PROFILING OF THE MOST PROMISING INHIBITORS. KEY GOALS OF THE LEAD OPTIMIZATION PHASE INCLUDE: IN VITRO TARGET-ENGAGEMENT STUDIES, IN VITRO STUDIES AIMING TO DEMONSTRATE SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS WITH STANDARD-OF-CARE (SOC) ANTIBIOTICS ON BIOFILM ERADICATION; IN VIVO PHARMACOKINETIC STUDIES, AIMING AT FAVORABLE EXPOSURE IN THE TARGET COMPARTMENT AFTER INHALATIVE APPLICATION; IN VIVO PD STUDIES USING P.A. INFECTION MODELS; FORMULATION DEVELOPMENT TO FACILITATE DRUG DELIVERY TO THE TARGET COMPARTMENT; AND SAFETY ASSESSMENT TO ENABLE DOSING IN HUMANS (I.E., CEREP, MINI-AMES). THIS WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY CONTINUOUS SYNTHETIC OPTIMIZATION TOWARD BENEFICIAL PHARMACOKINETIC AND PHARMACODYNAMIC PROPERTIES. COMPOUND SYNTHESIS WILL BE SUPPORTED BY STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, CAPITALIZING ON OUR WELL ESTABLISHED CO-CRYSTALLIZATION PROTOCOLS FOR LASB INHIBITORS. ON TOP OF THE VALUABLE ADVICE PROVIDED BY CARB-X WE ARE FURTHER PLANNING TO CONSULT REGULATORY AGENCIES SUCH AS FDA.

description: A MAJOR RESEARCH FOCUS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF APPLIED TUMOR BIOLOGY AT THE GERMAN CANCER RESEARCH CENTER (DKFZ) IS THE MOLECULAR PATHOGENESIS OF HEREDITARY COLORECTAL CANCER AND NOVEL DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES DERIVED THEREOF. IN FRAME OF THE PROPOSED COLLABORATIVE PROJECT (APPLICATION TITLE: COMBINED CHEMO- AND IMMUNOPREVENTION FOR GASTROINTESTINAL CANCER IN A MOUSE MODEL OF LYNCH SYNDROME), THE CONTRIBUTION OF OUR DEPARTMENT WILL BE (1) THE IDENTIFICATION OF DEFINED MUTATIONS IN MOUSE LYNCH SYNDROME TUMORS, (2) THE PREDICTION AND IN VITRO EVALUATION OF TUMOR ANTIGENS GENERATED AS A CONSEQUENCE OF THESE MUTATIONS, AND (3) THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN EXPERIMENTAL VACCINE FOR TUMOR PREVENTION IN LYNCH SYNDROME MICE. THE PLANNED CONTRIBUTION WILL BE BASED ON IN SILICO PREDICTION TOOLS TO IDENTIFY CODING MICROSATELLITES IN THE MOUSE GENOME, MUTATION TESTING OF PREDICTED CODING MICROSATELLITE TARGETS IN DNA ISOLATED FROM MOUSE TUMORS, THE VALIDATION OF THESE TARGETS IN INDEPENDENT TUMOR DNA SPECIMENS, THE GENERATION OF CODING MICROSATELLITE MUTATION-DERIVED PEPTIDES, THE IN VITRO EVALUATION OF THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF THE PEPTIDES, THE GENERATION OF PEPTIDES FOR A VACCINE, AND THE IMMUNOLOGICAL EVALUATION OF MOUSE T CELLS AND ANTIBODIES BEFORE AND AFTER VACCINATION.

description: THE ADJUVANT DISCOVERY CONTRACT PROPOSED HEREIN WILL IDENTIFY, CHARACTERIZE, AND ADVANCE NOVEL SYNTHETIC IL-1R-BASED ADJUVANTS FOR USE IN COMBINATION WITH AN INFLUENZA VACCINE TO INDUCE RAPID AND SUSTAINED BROADLY PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY TO SEASONAL AND/OR PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS. THIS PROPOSAL BRINGS TOGETHER HIGHLY EXPERIENCED RESEARCH TEAMS FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA, DUKE UNIVERSITY, THE ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI AND INIMMUNE CORPORATION, EACH WITH UNIQUE EXPERTISE AND PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN NIAID ADJUVANT DISCOVERY AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS. DR. EVANS, DIRECTOR OF THE CTM, AND COLLEAGUES AT UM WILL LEAD THE DISCOVERY EFFORTS AND COORDINATE ACTIVITIES OF ALL SUBCONTRACTORS. THE RESEARCH TEAM AT UM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HIGH THROUGHPUT IN SILICO SCREENING, PEPTIDE LIBRARY PRODUCTION, COMPOUNDS SYNTHESIS AND SAR, MECHANISTIC STUDIES, FORMULATION, SAFETY ASSESSMENTS AND EFFICACY STUDIES. DR. STAATS, PROFESSOR OF PATHOLOGY, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF IMMUNOLOGY AND MEDICINE, DUKE, AND COLLEAGUES WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE TEAM FROM UM TO COMPLETE THE HTS SCREENING OF SYNTHETIC PEPTIDE LIBRARIES, APTAMER LIBRARY PRODUCTION AND SCREENING, CONFIRMATION SCREEN OF SELECTED HITS USING IL-1R REPORTER CELLS, EVALUATION OF BINDING AND INTERNALIZATION, CRITICALLY EVALUATE THE INTRACELLULAR SIGNALING PATHWAYS OF LEAD IL- 1R AGONISTS AND ASSESS THE ROUTE OF ADMINISTRATION AND SCHEDULE TO OPTIMIZE BOTH PARENTERAL (IM) AND MUCOSAL (IN, SL) VACCINATION THROUGH ADJUVANT SELECTION AND FORMULATION. DR. KRAMMER, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF MICROBIOLOGY, AND COLLEAGUES AT THE ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI BRING EXPERTISE AND CONSIDERABLE KNOWLEDGE IN INFLUENZA VIRUS ANIMAL MODELS AND THE PRODUCTION OF RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA ANTIGENS. DR. KRAMMER WILL PROVIDE RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA ANTIGENS AND LEAD EFFORTS TOWARDS THE IN VIVO INFLUENZA CHALLENGE MODELS (MOUSE AND FERRET) FOR EVALUATION OF IL-1 ADJUVANTED INFLUENZA VACCINES. THE TEAM AT MOUNT SINAI ALSO BRINGS SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE IN THE SEROLOGICAL MECHANISM OF PROTECTION AND A WIDE ARRAY OF ANTIGENS AND VIRUSES TO ASSESS HETEROSUBTYPIC PROTECTION AGAINST SELECTED SEASONAL AND HIGHLY PATHOGENIC INFLUENZA VIRUS STRAINS. DR. BAZIN-LEE, VICE PRESIDENT OF DISCOVERY RESEARCH, ALONG WITH HER COLLEAGUES AT INIMMUNE CORPORATION, WILL OVERSEE ANALYTICAL ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, PHYSIOCHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION, STABILITY AND SCALE-UP SYNTHESIS OF LEAD IL-1R ADJUVANTS IDENTIFIED IN RESEARCH AREAS 1-3.

description: AMRITA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES, KOCHI, KERALA STATE, INDIA DR. SANJEEV SINGH WILL BE THE LEAD INVESTIGATOR AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND HE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. GANDRA AND ENSURE COMPLETION OF WORK AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL PROVIDE HIS INPUT IN PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT.
