HE WILL OVERSEE PATIENT ENROLLMENT PROCESS AND ENSURE THE TARGETS FOR PATIENT ENROLLMENT INCLUDED IN THIS STUDY PROTOCOL WILL REACH. HE WILL ENSURE ACCESS TO DOCUMENTS RELATED TO INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND PROVIDE INPUT ON THE INFECTION CONTROL INTERVENTIONS THAT CAN BE IMPLEMENTED AS PROPOSED IN THE STUDY PROTOCOL. HE WILL ENSURE THE INTERVENTIONS WILL BE IMPLEMENTED IN THE STUDY ICUS. HE WILL WORK WITH THE STUDY TEAM AT AMRITA HOSPITAL TO RESOLVE ANY ISSUES WITH DATA COLLECTION AND OVERSEE DATA COLLECTION PROCESS. HE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE TWICE MONTHLY MEETINGS WITH THE WASHU TEAM ON ZOOM. HE WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN DATA ANALYSIS AND FINAL REPORT. DR. ANU GEROGE WILL BE THE PROJECT COORDINATOR AT AMRITA HOSPITAL, AND SHE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. SINGH TO ENSURE COMPLETION OF WORK AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. SHE WILL ASSIST DR. SINGH FOR IRB SUBMISSION, GETTING NECESSARY APPROVALS AT AMRITA HOSPITAL AND GETTING APPROVAL FROM INDIAN HMSC. SHE WILL ASSIST DR. SINGH TO COORDINATE ACTIVITIES FOR TRAINING AND PILOT DATA COLLECTION AT AMRITA HOSPITAL WITH DR. GANDRA AND DR. WARREN. SHE WILL OVERSEE DAY TO DAY PATIENT ENROLLMENT, DATA COLLECTION, SPECIMEN COLLECTION BY STUDY STAFF AND INFECTION CONTROL NURSES AND REPORT TO DR. SINGH WITH ANY ISSUES THAT ARISE. SHE WILL MAKE SURE INTERVENTIONS ARE IMPLEMENTED AS PART OF THE STUDY. SHE WILL COORDINATE THE TWICE MONTHLY MEETINGS WITH WASHU TEAM ON ZOOM. DR. ANIL KUMAR IS THE CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGIST AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ENSURE APPROPRIATE LABORATORY PROCEDURES ARE FOLLOWED IN PROCESSING THE PERI-RECTAL SWABS AND STORING THE ISOLATES DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. HE WILL MAINTAIN PAPER RECORDS FOR PERI-RECTAL SWAB CULTURE RESULTS. HE WILL DOCUMENT AND REPORT THE QUALITY CONTROL PROCESSES INVOLVED IN IDENTIFICATION OF THE ORGANISMS AND PERFORMING ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING BY VITEK AND REPORT THE RESULTS TO DR. GANDRA MONTHLY. HE WILL HELP IN GIVING ACCESS TO ALL POSITIVE CRE CULTURES TO STUDY STAFF FOR STUDY PERIOD. HE WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE TWICE MONTHLY MEETINGS WITH WASHU TEAM. DR. ZUBAIR MOHAMED IS THE MEDICAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT SPECIALIST AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ASSIST THE STUDY STAFF WITH ENROLLMENT OF PATIENTS INTO THE STUDY, MAKE SURE NURSES OBTAIN SPECIMENS FORM ENROLLED PATIENTS, GIVE ACCESS TO NECESSARY MEDICAL RECORDS FOR DATA COLLECTION AND MAKE INFECTION CONTROL PRACTICES ARE FOLLOWED AS PER STUDY PROTOCOL. HE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ANU GEORGE AND DR. SANJEEV SINGH. DR. DIPU SATYAPALAN IS THE SURGICAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT SPECIALIST AT AMRITA HOSPITAL. HE WILL ASSIST THE STUDY STAFF WITH ENROLLMENT OF PATIENTS INTO THE STUDY, MAKE SURE NURSES OBTAIN SPECIMENS FORM ENROLLED PATIENTS, GIVE ACCESS TO NECESSARY MEDICAL RECORDS FOR DATA COLLECTION AND MAKE INFECTION CONTROL PRACTICES ARE FOLLOWED AS PER STUDY PROTOCOL. HE WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ANU GEORGE AND DR. SANJEEV SINGH. TWO STUDY COORDINATORS WILL BE INVOLVED FOR ENROLLMENT OF PATIENT INTO THE STUDY, OBTAINING CONSENT FROM PATIENT OR FAMILY, OBTAIN SPECIMEN FROM ENROLLED PATIENTS, TRACK SPECIMEN COLLECTION, COLLECT CLINICAL DATA FROM TWO ICUS AND THE CRE POSITIVE CULTURES FROM THE MICROBIOLOGY LAB OBTAINED FROM 2 ICUS DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. THEY WILL COLLECT DATA ON VARIABLES INDICATED IN THE STUDY PROTOCOL AND ENTER ALL DATA INTO REDCAP. THEY WILL COORDINATE WITH DR. ANIL KUMAR REGARDING PERI-RECTAL CULTURE DATA AND CRE CLINICAL CULTURE DATA FROM STUDY ICUS. THEY WILL PERFORM DIRECT OBSERVATIONS TO RECORD THE COMPLIANCE WITH INFECTION CONTROL PRACTICES DURING PRE-INTERVENTION AND INTERVENTION PHASES AND ENTER THAT INFORMATION INTO REDCAP. THEY WORK CLOSELY WITH DR. ANU GEORGE AND REPORTS ANY ISSUES TO DR. ANU GEORGE IMMEDIATELY. THEY MAY PARTICIPATE IN ZOOM MEETINGS ONCE A MONTH WITH WASHU TEAM. A MICROBIOLOGY LAB TECHNICIAN WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROCESSING THE SPECIMENS (PERI-RECTAL SWABS), PLATING THEM ON CHROMOGENIC AGAR, IDENTIFYING POTENTIAL CRE COLONIES, PERFORM IDENTIFICATION AND SUSCEPTIBILITY. HE WILL PERFORM NECESSARY QUALITY CONTROL EXPERIMENTS. HE/SHE WILL MAINTAIN A RECORD OF ALL STUDY SAMPLES WITH RESULTS. HE/SHE WILL WORK UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. ANIL KUMAR. AIM 1: TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED RISK FACTORS FOR ASYMPTOMATIC INTESTINAL CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND INCIDENCE OF INTESTINAL AND NON-INTESTINAL CRE ACQUISITION USING SCS STRATEGY AND CLINICAL CULTURE DATA DURING ICU STAY AMONG PATIENTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICUS WE WILL PROSPECTIVELY ENROLL CONSENTED PATIENTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICU AT AMRITHA HOSPITAL, KOCHI, INDIA. THE ENROLLMENT WILL HAPPEN FOR THREE MONTHS OR FOR A MAXIMUM OF 300 PATIENTS, WHICHEVER COMES EARLIER. PERIRECTAL SWABS WILL BE OBTAINED ON CONSENTED PATIENTS WITHIN 24-48 HOURS OF ICU ADMISSION, EVERY WEEK, AND AT THE TIME OF ICU DISCHARGE OR DEATH FOR A MAXIMUM OF FOUR WEEKS OR UNTIL THE PATIENT IS IDENTIFIED AS COLONIZED WITH CRE. FOR PATIENTS COLONIZED WITH CRE ON PERI-RECTAL SWABS ON ICU ADMISSION, WE WILL NOT OBTAIN FURTHER PERI-RECTAL SWABS. WE WILL ALSO COLLECT ALL CRE POSITIVE CLINICAL CULTURE DATA FROM PATIENTS IN THE TWO ICUS FOR A MAXIMUM OF THREE MONTHS CORRESPONDING TO THE ENROLLMENT PERIOD. THIS INFORMATION WILL BE OBTAINED FROM MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY, BY REVIEWING THE CHARTS IF NEEDED AND HOSPITAL INFORMATION SYSTEM. WE WILL REQUEST WAIVER OF CONSENT FOR THIS INFORMATION AS IT IS MINIMAL RISK TO THE PATIENTS. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL COLLECT BASIC INFORMATION ON EXISTING INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES AT BASELINE AND ANY CHANGES THAT OCCUR INDEPENDENT OF THE STUDY PROTOCOL DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. DETAILED INFORMATION ON INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES FOCUSING ON ENVIRONMENTAL CLEANING OF IMMEDIATE PATIENT ENVIRONMENT, HAND HYGIENE PRACTICES AND CONTACT ISOLATION PRECAUTION PRACTICES OF CRE POSITIVE PATIENTS IN TWO ICUS WILL BE COLLECTED. THIS WILL BE OBTAINED FROM INFECTION PREVENTION DEPARTMENT AND DIRECT OBSERVATION FROM STUDY TEAM (IF ABLE TO TRAVEL TO INDIA). A DATA COLLECTION FORM WILL BE CREATED BY ADAPTING THE WHO INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK (IPCAF)(9) AND CDC TOOL KITS(10). EXPECTED OUTCOMES FROM SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ESTIMATES OF ADMISSION CRE PREVALENCE AND CRE ACQUISITION RATES IN THE STUDY ICUS USING SCS Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH CRE COLONIZATION ON ADMISSION AND CRE ACQUISITION DURING ICU STAY. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ESTIMATES OF CRE PREVALENCE DETECTED BY ROUTINE CLINICAL CULTURES ADJUSTED FOR OVERALL CULTURES PERFORMED VERSUS SURVEILLANCE CULTURES. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ BASELINE INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES DETAILS IN STUDY ICUS AIM 2: TO DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS) STRATEGY UTILIZING BASELINE PHASE DATA FROM AIM 1 THE GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY AN LCS STRATEGY WHICH HAS CRE RATE RATIOS COMPARABLE TO SCS STRATEGY BUT LESS BURDENSOME TO IMPLEMENT COMPARED TO SCS STRATEGY ( SEE TABLE 1 FOR STUDY ACTIVITIES). TABLE 1: STUDY PHASES, CRE SURVEILLANCE STRATEGIES IN EACH PHASE AND DURATION PHASE CRE SURVEILLANCE STRATEGY DURATION BASELINE PERIOD STANDARD ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (SCS): OBTAIN PERIRECTAL SWAB FOR ENROLLED NEW ADMISSIONS TO TWO ICUS ON ADMISSION, WEEKLY AND AT DISCHARGE 3 MONTHS OR 300 PATIENTS WHICHEVER COMES FIRST DATA ANALYSIS IDENTIFY OPTIMAL LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS) STRATEGY: THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY WILL BE IDENTIFIED USING DATA OBTAINED FROM THE BASELINE PERIOD SCS STRATEGY. 3 MONTHS PRE-INTERVENTION LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS): THIS MAY INVOLVE SELECTING ONE DAY OR MULTIPLE DAYS OF THE WEEK AND OBTAIN PERIRECTAL SWABS ON PATIENTS ADMITTED WITHIN 24 HOURS TO THE ICU AND ON THEIR DISCHARGE, AS WELL AS ON ALL PATIENTS TO BE DISCHARGED FROM ICU ON THAT DAY. NO CHANGE IN INFECTION PREVENTION PRACTICES 3 MONTHS INTERVENTION LOW INTENSITY ACTIVE CRE SURVEILLANCE (LCS): SAME AS PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE AND PERFORM AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION 3 MONTHS THE LCS STRATEGY MAY INVOLVE SELECTING ONE DAY OR MULTIPLE DAYS OF THE WEEK AND PERFORMING INTESTINAL CRE SCREENING BY OBTAINING PERIRECTAL SWABS ON PATIENTS ADMITTED WITHIN 24-48 HOURS TO THE ICU AND ON THEIR DISCHARGE AS WELL AS ON ALL PATIENTS TO BE DISCHARGED WITHIN 24 HOURS. THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY WILL BE IDENTIFIED AFTER ANALYZING THE SCS DATA COLLECTED FOR 3 MONTHS IN AIM1 TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE ACCURACY OF THE CRE RATE RATIOS COMPARED TO SCS STRATEGY, THE EFFORT OF HCWS, LABORATORY STAFF, RESOURCES NEEDED AND AFTER DISCUSSIONS WITH CDC SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS (SMES). USING THE DATA COLLECTED FROM BASELINE PHASE, CRE RATE RATIOS WITH SELECTION OF DIFFERENT DAYS OR MULTIPLE DAYS WILL BE PERFORMED TO IDENTIFY AN LCS STRATEGY THAT IS COMPARABLE AND LESS BURDENSOME TO SCS STRATEGY FOR ESTIMATING CRE RATE RATIOS . THIS WILL ALLOW US TO DETERMINE THE BEST DAY/S OF THE WEEK TO PERFORM LCS IN MEDICAL AND SURGICAL ICUS, AS THEY MAY HAVE DIFFERENT PATTERNS OF PATIENT TURNOVER RATES. IN ADDITION, WE WILL EXAMINE THE UTILITY OF ADDING RISK FACTORS AND CLINICAL CULTURE DATA TO AUGMENT THE SELECTED LCS STRATEGY, ESPECIALLY TO DECREASE THE BURDEN ON HCWS AND THE LABORATORY STAFF FOR CONDUCTING CRE SURVEILLANCE. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL DO A QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW WITH THE RESEARCH NURSE ON THE ACCESSIBILITY OF CLINICAL RISK FACTOR DATA. THE INTERVIEW WILL BE CONDUCTED BY PIS EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA SKYPE. AIM 3: TO DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION(S) ON CRE INCIDENCE RATE RATIOS USING LCS STRATEGY IN THIS AIM, WE WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT AN INFECTION PREVENTION INTERVENTION(S) ON CRE INCIDENCE RATE RATIOS USING LCS STRATEGY. TO DO THIS, WE WILL HAVE A PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE AND INTERVENTION PHASE EACH OF 3 MONTHS DURATION AND PROSPECTIVELY ENROLL CONSENTED PATIENTS. THE PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE WILL BE INITIATED AFTER ANALYSIS OF BASELINE PHASE DATA TO DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL LCS STRATEGY AFTER DISCUSSION WITH CDC SMES. THE GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY A LCS STRATEGY WHICH INVOLVES SELECTING ONE OR TWO DAYS OF THE WEEK AND PERFORMING INTESTINAL CRE SCREENING BY OBTAINING PERIRECTAL SWABS ON CONSENTED PATIENTS ADMITTED WITHIN 24-48 HOURS TO THE ICU AND ON THEIR DISCHARGE AS WELL AS ON ALL CONSENTED PATIENTS TO BE DISCHARGED WITHIN 24 HOURS FROM ICU. THE INTERVENTION PHASE WILL BE INITIATED ONE MONTH AFTER THE PRE-INTERVENTION PHASE IS COMPLETED. AFTER DISCUSSIONS WITH THE CDC SMES, THE INTERVENTION WILL BE FINALIZED, AND IT WILL BE PILOTED IN THE MONTH BETWEEN PRE-INTERVENTION AND INTERVENTION PHASE. DURING THE INTERVENTION PHASE, THE LCS WILL BE RESUMED AND CONTINUED FOR THREE MONTHS. WE WILL ALSO COLLECT ALL CRE POSITIVE CLINICAL CULTURE DATA FROM PATIENTS IN THE TWO ICUS DURING THE TWO PHASES. THIS INFORMATION WILL BE OBTAINED FROM MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY, BY REVIEWING THE CHARTS IF NEEDED AND HOSPITAL INFORMATION SYSTEM. WE WILL REQUEST WAIVER OF CONSENT FOR THIS INFORMATION AS IT IS MINIMAL RISK TO THE PATIENTS. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL COLLECT DATA ON COMPLIANCE WITH INFECTION PREVENTION DURING PRE-INTERVENTION AND INTERVENTION PHASE USING A STANDARDIZED METHOD BY PERFORMING DIRECT OBSERVATIONS. THE DETAILS WILL BE DECIDED ONCE THE INTERVENTION IS DECIDED. SOME POTENTIAL INTERVENTIONS COULD BE ENHANCED TERMINAL CLEANING WITH EDUCATION AND FEEDBACK OR WITH MINIMAL EQUIPMENT CHANGES, COHORTING OF CRE POSITIVE PATIENTS AND ENHANCING HAND HYGIENE MEASURES WITH EDUCATION AND FEEDBACK. SPECIMEN COLLECTION AND MICROBIOLOGY PROCEDURES: PERI-RECTAL SWAB WILL BE OBTAINED FROM THE CONSENTED PATIENTS BY INSERTING TIP OF THE SWAB INTO RECTUM AND GENTLY ROTATING IT 360 DEGREES. VISIBLE BROWN PIGMENT SHOULD BE OBSERVED ON THE SWAB. IF NO PIGMENT IS PRESENT, THE SWAB WILL BE REINSERTED INTO THE RECTUM. ONCE PERIRECTAL SPECIMENS ARE OBTAINED USING HICULTUREÃ¢Â€ŽÂ¢ TRANSPORT SWABS W/ AMIES MEDIUM (HIMEDIA LABORATORIES, INDIA) SPECIMEN COLLECTION AND TRANSPORT SYSTEM, THEY WILL BE TRANSPORTED TO MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY IMMEDIATELY AT ROOM TEMPERATURE AND WILL BE PROCESSED WITHIN 24 HOURS. THE SWABS WILL BE DIRECTLY PLATED ONTO MSUPERCARBA (CHROMAGAR)(11, 12). QUALITY CONTROL OF THE MSUPERCARBA MEDIA WILL BE PERFORMED AS PER MANUFACTURERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RECOMMENDATIONS USING FOLLOWING ATCC STRAINS: E. COLI IMP NCTC 1347 & K. PNEUMONIAE ATCCÃ‚Â® BAA 1705 AS POSITIVE CONTROLS AND E. FAECALIS ATCCÃ‚Â® 29212 AND K. PNEUMONIAE ESBL ATCCÃ‚Â® 700603 AS NEGATIVE CONTROLS. THE PLATES WILL BE INCUBATED AT 35 Ã‚Â°C IN AN INCUBATOR FOR 24 HOURS IN AIR ATMOSPHERE. COLONIES WHICH ARE DARK PINK TO REDDISH (E. COLI) AND METALLIC BLUE (KLEBSIELLA, ENTEROBACTER, CITROBACTER) ARE CONSIDERED AS POSSIBLE CRE. THESE COLONIES WILL BE PICKED TO PERFORM MCIM AND ECIM TESTS TO RULE OUT NONÃ¢Â‚¬Â€ŒCARBAPENEMASE-PRODUCING ENTEROBACTERALES AND TO DIFFERENTIATE METALLO-ÃŽÂ²-LACTAMASES FROM SERINE CARBAPENEMASES (13). ONCE CONFIRMED BY MCIM TEST, ONLY ONE ISOLATE (PREFERABLY E.COLI OR KLEBSIELLA SPP.) PER PATIENT WILL BE TESTED USING VITEK2 (BIOMERIEUX) FOR IDENTIFICATION AND ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY. THE GRAM NEGATIVE VITEK2 ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY PANEL INCLUDES FOLLOWING ANTIBIOTICS- AMIKACIN, AZTREONAM, CEFEPIME, CEFTAZIDIME, CIPROFLOXACIN, COLISTIN, DORIPENEM, GENTAMICIN, IMIPENEM, LEVOFLOXACIN, MEROPENEM, MINOCYCLINE, PIPERACILLIN/TAZOBACTAM, TIGECYCLINE, AND TRIMETHOPRIM/SULFAMETHOXAZOLE. ALL CRE ISOLATES WILL BE STORED FROZEN IN TSB-GLYCEROL AT -800C.

description: THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS, THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF VARIOUS CHEMOTACTIC OR ADHESION MOLECULES IN GUIDING IMMUNE CELLS TO VARIOUS SITES WITHIN THE INFECTED LUNG TISSUES AND LYMPHOID ORGANS, AS WELL AS IN MEDIATING PROTECTION FROM MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. IN YEAR 4, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL: I. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. II. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EXPERIMENTS AIMED TO ELUCIDATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES WITHIN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION, WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. III. PERFORM AND ASSIST WITH COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES OF SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING DATA OBTAINED BY OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. THIS WILL INVOLVE IMPLEMENTATION OF ADVANCED STATISTICAL ALGORITHMS TO STUDY A) CELLULAR HETEROGENEITY AND IMMUNE RESPONSES WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, B) ANALYZE EXPRESSION OF CHEMOTACTIC AND ADHESION MOLECULES THAT MAY REGULATE CELLULAR POSITIONING, AS WELL AS C) HELP IDENTIFY POTENTIAL MOLECULES OF INTEREST THAT MAY BE INVOLVED IN IMMUNE RESPONSES WHICH CORRELATE WITH PROTECTION. IV. IDENTIFIED MOLECULES OF INTEREST FROM PART III) WILL ALSO BE USED TO POWER FOLLOW-UP MICROSCOPY AND SPATIAL ANALYSIS STUDIES TO REVEAL HOW THESE CORRELATE WITH CELLULAR ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTION WITHIN INFECTED LUNG AND LYMPH NODE TISSUES. V. PERFORM CROSS-SPECIES CORRELATIVE ANALYSES USING GENERATED SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING DATA TO IDENTIFY CONSERVED FEATURES OF IMMUNE CELL RESPONSES TO INFECTION AND AFTER IMMUNIZATION. VI. DATA FROM I-V) WILL HELP IDENTIFY SPECIFIC MOLECULES OF INTEREST FOR FOLLOW-UP FUNCTIONAL STUDIES. AS EXAMPLE, IDENTIFIED CHEMOTACTIC MOLECULES WILL BE TARGETED USING EITHER AVAILABLE KO MICE OR USING IN VIVO BLOCKADE WITH ANTIBODIES OR SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITORS. ALTERNATIVELY, IMMUNE CELLS CAN BE ENGINEERED EX VIVO (E.G. CRISPR) TO ENHANCE TRAFFICKING OF EFFECTOR CELLS TO SPECIFIC TISSUE SITES DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. BASED ON THE LENGTH OF TIME THAT I-V) STEPS ABOVE WILL TAKE TO IMPLEMENT, THESE FUNCTIONAL MAY BE PERFORMED IN LATER YEARS OF THE CONTRACT. VII. TEST / DEVELOP HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE.

description: CURRENTLY PLANNED STUDIES USING 13-PLEX MICROSCOPY CAN PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO CELL TYPE COMPOSITION BUT NOT THE MOLECULAR REGULATION OF HOW DIFFERENT GRANULOMA STRUCTURES DEVELOP. IN CONTRAST, BULK AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING APPROACHES FAIL TO PROVIDE DETAIL ON THE SPATIAL MICROANATOMY OF DISEASE, ESPECIALLY WHEN ANALYZING SMALL LESIONS AT EARLY STAGES OF INFECTION. USING THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMIC SUPPLEMENT, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL USE NANOSTRING GEOMX DSP SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS (ST) PLATFORM AVAILABLE THROUGH SEATTLE GENETICS TO DEFINE THE HETEROGENEITY OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB) LUNG LESIONS IN THE C3HEB/FEJ SA161 MOUSE MODEL OF DISEASE AND IN HUMAN INFECTED LUNG SAMPLES. 1. THE UW WILL PERFORM ST PROFILING AND INFORMATIC ANALYSIS OF ~40 MOUSE LUNG GRANULOMA LESIONS OBTAINED FROM SA161-INFECTED C3HEB/FEJ MICE AT VARIOUS STAGES OF DISEASE, RANGING FROM DAY 7 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ DAY 35. 2. THE UW WILL EXAMINE THE HETEROGENEITY OF ~40 HUMAN LUNG MTB LESIONS FROM PATIENTS WITH EITHER ASYMPTOMATIC MTB INFECTION OR ACTIVE PULMONARY TB. SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH THE ONGOING POST-MORTEM IMPACTB STUDIES IN UGANDA.

description: THE HAWN LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 4. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1-3 IS ONGOING. 1. UW WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS LARGELY COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 4. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL. 2. UW WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. ANALYSES ARE UNDERWAY TO EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN CANDIDATE GENES WITH MTB-INDUCED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES IN A COHORT OF 100 HEALTHY DONORS. . 3. UW WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. STUDIES WILL INCLUDE INFECTION OF MACROPHAGES WITH MTB AND ANALYSIS OF IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND CONTROL OF MTB REPLICATION. CELL SUPERNATANTS WILL BE HARVESTED FOR CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE ELISA AND RNA EXTRACTED FROM CELLS, QUANTIFIED, AND ANALYZED. 4. UW WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE IMPAC-TB PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING AND POTENTIALLY EVEN ERADICATING MTB. THE GALE LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. 1. DR. GALE AT UW WILL LEAD THE DATA AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TEAM THIS TEAM, COMPRISED OF MEMBERS FROM ALL LABORATORIES IN IMPAC-TB, WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A DATA AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR 1) STORAGE, RETRIEVAL, AND ANALYSIS OF CENTER-GENERATED DATA 2) CATALOGING AND REPORTING OF ALL CENTER-GENERATED REAGENTS AND RESOURCES, AND 3) DISSEMINATION OF DATA AND CENTER RESULTS INTERNALLY, TO OTHER NIAID-SUPPORTED PROGRAMS, AND TO THE BROADER SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL TAKE PLACE OVER THE SEVEN YEARS OF THE CONTRACT. IN YEAR 4, THE GALE LABORATORY AT UW WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT THE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM WITH ASSISTANCE FROM OTHER TEAM MEMBERS. 2. UW WILL CONDUCT RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. IN YEAR 4, UW WILL PERFORM RNA-SEQ ASSAYS ON SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM NHP STUDIES PERFORMED IN YEARS 1-3. TASKS INCLUDE 1) RECEIVING SAMPLES FROM THE PICKER LAB, 2) ISOLATING RNA FROM THESE SAMPLES AND PERFORMING RNA QC, 3) CONSTRUCTING RNA-SEQ LIBRARIES AND LIBRARY QC USING THE ISOLATED RNA, AND 4) GENERATING SEQUENCING DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES. 3. UW WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON THE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. IN YEAR 4, UW WILL ANALYZE DATA SETS GENERATED FROM THE RNA-SEQ ASSAY THAT UW PERFORMS USING SAMPLES FROM THE NHP STUDIES. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRIXES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND, WHEN APPROPRIATE, RULE-BASED MODELING.

IN ADDITION, CTS STAFF, LED BY DR. MARION LANTERI, WILL CONTRIBUTE TO STUDY EXECUTION INCLUDING DATA ANALYSIS AND MANUSCRIPT DEVELOPMENT PER BELOW AND PER THEIR ATTACHED BUDGET. MARION LANTERI WILL DEDICATE 3 MONTHS OR 25% EFFORT TO THIS PROJECT. DR. LANTERI WILL ATTEND WEEKLY PHONE CALLS AND REGULAR VIRTUAL AND IN PERSON MEETINGS TO PLAN AND COORDINATE ACTIVITIES REQUIRING CTS ENGAGEMENT. SHE OVERSEES CTS R&D DEPARTMENT AND WILL PRIORITIZE TESTING ACTIVITIES WITHIN CTS R&D DEPARTMENT TO MEET THE EXPECTED TIMELINES OF STUDY DELIVERABLES RELATED TO SAMPLE TESTING AND RESULTS TURNAROUND. DR. LANTERI WILL ACTIVELY CONTRIBUTE TO DATA ANALYSES, PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS, AND PUBLICATIONS (ABSTRACT SUBMISSION TO KEY CONFERENCES AND MANUSCRIPT DEVELOPMENT). VALERI GREEN WILL DEDICATE 3.2 MONTHS ON THIS PROJECT, INCLUDING 40% EFFORT OVER THE FIRST 4 MONTHS AND 20% FOR THE FOLLOWING 8 MONTHS. THIS INCLUDES 40% OF HER ACTIVITY DURING THE FIRST 4 MONTHS OF THIS NO COST EXTENSION PERIOD AS SHE MANAGES THE R&D STAFF INVOLVED IN SAMPLE TESTING ACTIVITIES FOR THIS PROJECT; SHE WILL ORGANIZE THE WORKFLOW OF SAMPLES AND TESTING AT CTS, ENSURE SAMPLES ARE TESTED IN A TIMELY MANNER, REVIEW RESULTS FOR ACCURACY, ORGANIZE FOR RESULTS TO BE PROVIDED TO VRI. SHE WILL MAKE SURE REAGENTS ARE ORDERED IN TIME, INSTRUMENTS ARE PROPERLY MAINTAINED, AND WORKLOAD IS EFFECTIVELY MANAGED. AFTER THE FIRST 4 MONTHS OF MORE INTENSE TESTING ACTIVITIES, MRS. GREENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S EFFORT WILL DROP DOWN TO 20% TO ORGANIZE FOR COMPLEMENTARY TESTING AS NEEDED WHILE CONTRIBUTING TO DATA ANALYSES AND PUBLICATION EFFORTS UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. LANTERI. CYRUS WILL ALSO MANAGE ORDERS, INVOICES AND PROPER ACCOUNTING FOR THIS PROJECT. SHE WILL SERVE AS BACK-UP FOR MRS. GREEN DURING VACATION AND SICK TIME AND WILL TAKE OVER CTS R&D STAFF MANAGEMENT AS NEEDED THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT. ONE MEMBER OF THE CTS IT AND BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE TEAM WILL DEDICATE 0.5 MONTH OR 4% EFFORT ON THIS PROJECT TO HELP MAINTAIN, MODIFY AS NEEDED, AND MANAGE THE COHORT WEB APP ALLOWING FOR CONTINUOUS GENERATION OF LIST OF SAMPLES NEEDING TESTING, AND RESULTS TO BE RETURNED IN THE FORMAT REQUIRED FOR ONGOING DATABASE POPULATION.

description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS-2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORT AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THIS CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDY. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL, AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, BIOREPOSITORY, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID-19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 WAS REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 03 TO ADDRESS AN INCREASE IN THE TARGET ENROLLMENT TO 1,100 PARTICIPANTS UNDER INVITE PROTOCOL V2.0 ASSUMPTIONS. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 03 ADDRESSED COSTS FOR THE PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR A RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED TRIAL OF THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF TECOVIRIMAT FOR THE TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX VIRUS DISEASE, SUCH AS PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT AND RESEARCH SITE ASSESSMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACT SCOPE FOR TMGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S SUBCONTRACT 20X127F4 WAS REVISED THROUGH MODIFICATION 04 NOW REFERRED TO AS THE INVITE COVID-19 OBSERVATIONAL VACCINE STUDY TO INCLUDE THE PALM 007 MONKEYPOX TREATMENT RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT (TPOXX) IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. MODIFICATION 05 ADDRESSED INCLUDING TO INCLUDE COST TO SUPPORT PALM 007 MONKEYPOX RCT BUDGET TO INCLUDE (1) ONE MONTH OF STAFFING AND INITIAL MEETING COSTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION AT THE CLINICAL SITE IN TUNDA FROM AUGUST 1, 2022 THROUGH AUGUST 30, 2022; AND (2) INCLUDE THE KOLE SITE PREPARATION/RENOVATION COSTS. IN ADDITION, MODIFICATION 06 INCLUDED RE-COSTING PALM 007 MONKEYPOX RCT BUDGET TO (1) INCLUDE PROTOCOL IMPLEMENTATION AT ONE SITE, TUNDA GENERAL HOSPITAL, WITH A TARGET ENROLLMENT OF 200 PARTICIPANTS, INCLUDING SUPPORT REQUIRED FOR THE JYNNEOS SAFETY STUDY; (2) EXTEND POP FOR THE CY23 8/31/2022-8/30/2023 BY EXERCISING OPTION PERIOD ONE FOR THE INVITE AND BIOREPOSITORY BUDGET.

description: THIS SOW COVERS THE IN SILICO COMPUTATIONAL RESEARCH PROJECT MINING THE GENERATED CELLULAR/HUMORAL DATASETS IN IMPACÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ TB ACROSS DIFFERENT TIME POINTS IN ESTABLISHED HUMAN COHORTS AND NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½HUMAN PRIMATE MODELS WITH IVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BCG INTERVENTION. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP NOVEL COMPUTATIONAL PIPELINES TO ANALYZE TIME COURSE DATASETS TO DEFINE THE IMMUNE SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH TB PROGRESSION. BACKGROUND: TUBERCULOSIS (TB) IS THE DEADLIEST PATHOGEN IN HISTORY AND REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH, ESPECIALLY IN RESOURCEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ POOR COUNTRIES. UP TO 25% OF THE WORLDÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S POPULATION HAS ASYMPTOMATIC MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB) INFECTIONS, WHICH CAN REACTIVATE AND CAUSE TRANSMISSIBLE PULMONARY TB DISEASE. THERE IS A HUGE WIDE SPECTRUM OF TB DISEASE STATUS, WHICH MAKES IT CHALLENGING TO UNDERSTAND THE IMMUNE MECHANISMS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF VACCINE DESIGN AND DRUG TREATMENT STRATEGIES. THEREFORE, UNDERSTANDING THE SYSTEMATIC IMMUNE RESPONSES ALONG THE TB DISEASE PROGRESSION USING COMPUTATIONAL PIPELINES WILL BOOST THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROPHYLACTIC AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. THERE ARE TWO PROJECTS UNDER THIS SUBCONTRACT. THE FIRST ONE FOCUSES ON IDENTIFYING THE HUMORAL IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO PREDICT TB PROGRESSION WHILE THE OTHER ONE IS THE TEMPORAL IMMUNE DYNAMICS OF IVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BCG ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROTECTION STATUS OF THE FOLLOWING BACTERIA CHALLENGE. THE PROPOSED COMPUTATIONAL METHODOLOGIES ARE DESCRIBED IN DETAIL LATER. TRANSFER OF MATERIALS: ALL THE EXPERIMENTAL SLIDES WILL BE MAINTAINED IN IMPACTÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½TB, IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH DR. LEELA DAVIES UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. SARAH FORTUNE AND DR. DOUGLAS LAUFFENBURGER. THE GENERATED DATASETS WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE WANG LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO, ANSCHUTZ MEDICAL CAMPUS. ALL THE DATASETS AND ANALYSES WILL BE PERFORMED ON THE APPROPRIATE CLOUDÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BASED SERVER UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DR. WANG. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: WE AIM TO DEVELOP ADVANCED TEMPORAL MODELING PIPELINES TO DIGEST THE DATASETS FROM FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SYSTEMS SEROLOGY PLATFORMS, DETAILED IN TWO FOLLOWING PROJECTS: 1) HUMORAL IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO PREDICT THE TB PROGRESSOR/NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROGRESSOR. WE AIM TO IDENTIFY THE IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO DISTINGUISH THE PROGRESSOR FROM THE NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROGRESSOR PATIENTS IN THE ACS COHORT, WHICH COULD BE FURTHER VALIDATED IN THE GC6 COHORT. IN THE ACS COHORT, WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THE NONLINEAR XGBOOST METHOD TO CLASSIFY THE PROGRESSOR FROM THE NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROGRESSOR IN DIFFERENT TIME INTERVALS (0Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½9M, 9Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½18M, 18Ã¢Â‚¬Ï¿½27M) BEFORE POSITIVE DIAGNOSTIC AND EVALUATE THE FEATURE IMPORTANCE USING INFORMATION GAIN AND THE ADVANCED INTERPRETED PREDICTION METHOD: SHAP (SHAPLEY ADDITIVE EXPLANATIONS). THEN USING THE IMPORTANCE OF FEATURES, WE COULD DEFINE THE CONCORDANCE SCORE AS THE IMMUNE SIGNATURE TO PREDICT THE PROGRESSOR/NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ PROGRESSOR ACROSS DIFFERENT COHORTS. 2) TEMPORAL IMMUNE DYNAMICS OF IVÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½BCG INVESTIGATION ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROTECTION STATUS OF THE FOLLOWING BACTERIA CHALLENGE. WE AIM TO PROPOSE A DATAÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½STREAM CLUSTERING STRATEGY TO IDENTIFY THE CLUSTERS INDEPENDENT FROM THE TIME POINTS COLLECTED ACROSS THE ANIMALS AND THEN BUILD THE SEPARATE TRANSITION NETWORKS ALONG THE TIME USING THE TIMEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ HOMOGENEOUS MARKOV CHAIN IN DIFFERENT STATUSES OF CHALLENGE (PROTECTION VS NONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½PROTECTION). ALSO, WE IDENTIFY THE IMMUNE SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH DIFFERENT IMMUNE CLUSTERS USING DIFFERENTIAL ANALYSIS. AFTER THAT, WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THE LASSOÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½GRANGER CAUSALITY STRATEGY TO INVESTIGATE THE TEMPORAL ORDERS OF DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS. DELIVERABLES: THIS SUBCONTRACT AIMS TO DEVELOP SEVERAL COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS TO ANALYZE THE TEMPORAL DATASET IN IMPACTÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½TB. ALL THE PUBLICATIONS AND DISCLOSURE OF RESULTS WILL BE APPROVED BY THE COMMITTEE OF IMPACTÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½TB.

description: PROPOSE TO STUDY THE PREVALENCE, IMPACT, AND MITIGATION OF RACIALLY- AND ETHNICALLY-MOTIVATED COMMUNITY VIOLENCE-PROVOKING HEALTH MISINFORMATION ONLINE. SUCH MISINFORMATION TENDS TO HARM MINORITY AND MARGINALIZED COMMUNITIES, WHO ARE ALREADY VICTIMS OF DISCRIMINATION AND SYSTEMATIC STRUCTURAL INEQUITIES. HATE SPEECH, BULLYING, AND CALLS FOR RACIALLY-MOTIVATED VIOLENCE ARE PREVALENT ON WEB AND SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS. MISINFORMATION DIRECTED AGAINST MINORITY COMMUNITIES MAY TAKE SEVERAL FORMS, RANGING FROM EXPLICIT CALLS FOR VIOLENCE AGAINST THE COMMUNITY TO OFFENSIVE, HATEFUL, AND ANXIETY- AND FEAR-INDUCING STATEMENTS AGAINST THE TARGETED COMMUNITY. REGARDLESS, THESE FORMS OF MISINFORMATION INCREASE FRAGMENTATION AND POLARIZATION IN SOCIETY. HEALTH MISINFORMATION IS DESIGNED TO PROVOKE NEGATIVE AFFECTIVE EMOTIONS (E.G., ANGER, ANXIETY), DEGRADING OF ATTITUDES (E.G., TRUST, LIKING, EMPATHY) TOWARDS TARGET COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND MAY INCREASE THEIR INTENTION TO ENGAGE IN ONLINE AND PHYSICAL HARM TOWARDS SELF OR OTHERS [5,6]. THIS ADVERSELY IMPACTS THE MEMBERS OF THE TARGET COMMUNITY BOTH IN THE ONLINE AND THE PHYSICAL WORLD. TARGET COMMUNITY MEMBERS EXPERIENCE HARASSMENT, AGGRESSION, TROLLING, DOXING, AND RACISM ONLINE [93], ALONG WITH PHYSICAL ASSAULTS, ABUSE, RIOTS, AND MOB LYNCHINGS IN THE REAL WORLD [108]. FOR INSTANCE, MORE THAN 11,000 INCIDENTS OF PHYSICAL VIOLENCE AND ONLINE AGGRESSION AGAINST ASIANS WERE REPORTED IN THE WAKE OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC [8, 9, 14]. COVID-19 FALSE CLAIMS HAVE ALSO LED TO DESTRUCTION OF PROPERTY [11] AND OVER 800 DEATHS [12]. THE MENTAL HEALTH COSTS ARE MASSIVE TOO. TARGETED HARASSMENT DETERIORATES THE VICTIMÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S MENTAL HEALTH [10]. THUS, IT IS CRUCIAL TO UNDERSTAND THE PREVALENCE AND IMPACT OF RACIALLY- AND ETHNICALLY-MOTIVATED COMMUNITY VIOLENCE CAUSED BY HEALTH MISINFORMATION ONLINE [4]. WE SHALL FOCUS ON STUDYING HEALTH MISINFORMATION IN SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS BECAUSE OF ITS ABILITY TO REACH MILLIONS AT AN EXCEPTIONAL SPEED AND SCALE [13]. SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS SUCH AS TWITTER AND FACEBOOK ARE OFTEN THE Ã¢Â‚¬Å“GROUND-ZEROÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ FOR THE SEEDING OF HEALTH MISINFORMATION, WHICH TENDS TO TRAVEL FASTER, FARTHER, AND DEEPER THAN TRUTH ON SOCIAL MEDIA [14]. IT IS THUS ESSENTIAL TO UNDERSTAND THE DAMAGING IMPACT THAT ONLINE HEALTH MISINFORMATION CAN HAVE. OUR WORK HAS FOUR GOALS: (1) IDENTIFYING HEALTH MISINFORMATION THAT PROMOTES COMMUNITY VIOLENCE, (2) MAPPING AND MEASURING THE PREVALENCE OF COMMUNITY VIOLENCE-PROVOKING HEALTH MISINFORMATION ACROSS SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS, (3) ESTABLISHING THE CAUSAL IMPACT OF SUCH MISINFORMATION ON THE READERSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ REACTIONS AND INTENTION TO ENGAGE IN HARM, AND (4) DESIGNING MITIGATION AND INTERVENTION STRATEGIES TO REDUCE THE PREVALENCE OF SUCH MISINFORMATION.

description: THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL OF SIZE-DEPENDENT METRIC ANALYSIS OF RESPIRABLE COAL MINE DUST (RCMD) WAS SPLIT TWO PHASES, BASE-PHASE AND OPTION PHASES, ACCORDING TO FUNDING AGENT. IN BASE PHASE THE RESEARCH WORK IS TO PROVIDE PROOF OF CONCEPT FOR DIRECT-ON-FILTER CHARACTERIZATION OF DUSTY PARTICLES INCLUDING PARTICLE SIZE DISTRIBUTION AND COMPOSITION. THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH AS A SUBCONTRACT WILL CARRY OUT FOLLOWING RESEARCH TASKS ACCORDING TO THE PROPOSAL. PROPOSED BUDGET FOR BASE PHASE IS $25000. 1. BASE PHASE: PROOF OF CONCEPT TASK A. LITERATURE REVIEW PARTICIPATE LITERATURE REVIEW ON PREVIOUS WORK ON SURFACE ANALYSIS OF CONTINUOUS PERSONAL DUST MONITOR (CPDM) TAPERED ELEMENT OSCILLATING MICROBALANCE (TEOM) FILTERS. PROVIDE A REPORT AND THE PLANNED PROTOCOL FOR DIRECT ON-FILTER ANALYSIS AND INDIRECT DISPERSED-PARTICLE ANALYSIS. THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL FOCUS ON REVIEW OF MICRO-XRF ANALYSIS RESEARCH WORK. TASK B. DIRECT-ON-FILTER CHARACTERIZATION OF DUSTY PARTICLES FOR DIRECT-ON-FILTER ANALYSIS, SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPE (SEM) AND MICRO X-RAY FLUORESCENCE (MICRO-XRF) AND OTHER APPROPRIATE METHODS WILL BE UTILIZED TO DETERMINE THE ABILITY TO CHARACTERIZE THE PARTICLES ON THE CPDM TEOM FILTERS. THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL FOCUS ON THE RESEARCH WORK OF DIRECT-ON-FILTER CHARACTERIZATION BY USING MICRO-XRF. THE RESEARCH WORK INCLUDE THE SAMPLE PREPARATION, PROCEDURE DEVELOPMENT, MICRO-XRF ANALYSIS. TASK C. INDIRECT DISPERSED-PARTICLE ANALYSIS THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL PARTICIPATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROCEDURE FOR NONDESTRUCTIVE DISPERSION OF PARTICLES FROM CPDM TEOM FILTERS. TASK D. RESULTS ANALYSIS AND FINAL REPORT A FINAL REPORT OF TAKES WHICH ARE CONDUCTED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL REPORTED TO THE TEAM FOR COMPLETE FINAL REPORT ON PROOF OF CONCEPT.2. OPTION PHASE: WILL CONTINUE THE ORIGINAL PROPOSED RESEARCH TASK E. DUST SAMPLING OF UNDERGROUND COAL MINE SITE ONE TO FOUR UNDERGROUND COAL MINES WILL BE VISITED BY THE TEAM. CPDM TEOM FILTERS WILL BE COLLECTED AND CAPPED WITH THE 3D-PRINTED CAPS FROM THE PROOF OF CONCEPT CONTRACT. STUDENTS FROM THREE UNIVERSITIES WILL TRAVEL TO UNDERGROUND COAL MINE SITES, WORK ALONG WITH EMPLOYEES ON SITE, AND COLLECT DUST SAMPLES. CPDM/TEOM DUST SAMPLES WILL BE OUR TARGET SAMPLE. DUST-LOADED TEOM FILTER SAMPLES AFTER EACH SHIFT WILL BE CAREFULLY REMOVED FROM CPDM DEVICES. FILTER SAMPLES WILL BE PACKED, SEALED, AND TRANSPORTED TO PISÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ LABORATORIES. ALTERNATIVELY, DUST-LOADED TEOM FILTERS WILL BE STORED IN SEALED GLASS/PLASTIC TUBES FOR SAMPLE TRANSPORTATION. THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL PARTICIPATE AND ORGANIZED THE SAMPLING IN ONE OF COAL MINE IN UTAH.

description: SEPSIS REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT MEDICAL CHALLENGE WITH NO EFFECTIVE TREATMENT AVAILABLE. THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL HUMAN MACROPHAGE-DERIVED NANOSPONGE-BASED DRUG PRODUCT CANDIDATE, CTI-111, FOR THE TREATMENT OF SEPSIS CAUSED BY GRAM-POSITIVE AND GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. CTI-111 IS DESIGNED TO SEQUESTER AND INACTIVATE BACTERIAL CYTOLYTIC TOXINS, ENDOTOXINS, AND HOST PROINFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES. CTI-111 IS DERIVED FROM A MACROPHAGE CELL LINE AND WILL BE FURTHER TESTED FOR BROAD-SPECTRUM EFFICACY IN MURINE SEPSIS MODELS TO COLLECT ADDITIONAL PHARMACOLOGY DATA TO SUPPORT MECHANISM OF ACTION, LACK OF INTERFERENCE WITH ANTIBIOTICS, AND MINIMAL EFFECTIVE DOSE DETERMINATIONS. CELLICS WILL CONCURRENTLY DEVELOP A SCALABLE MANUFACTURING PROCESS TO CREATE CLINICAL TRIAL MATERIAL FOLLOWING COMPLETION OF A GOOD LABORATORY PRACTICE (GLP)-COMPLIANT NONCLINICAL TOXICOLOGY STUDY AND OTHER NONCLINICAL STUDIES TO SUPPORT INVESTIGATIONAL NEW DRUG APPLICATION (IND) FILING WITH THE U.S. FDA.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES OF DTU AS PART OF IEDB & AR PROGRAM ARE TO MAINTAIN, ENHANCE AND UPDATE THE EXISTING SET OF EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS, AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS FOR THE ANALYSIS RESOURCE. DTU WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC TELECONFERENCES AND MEETINGS, AND PROVIDE TASK STATUS FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. SPECIFICALLY, DTU WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS: A. ANALYSIS RESOURCE TASKS 1. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE THE EXISTING MHC CLASS I AND II BINDING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 2. DEVELOP NEW MHC CLASS I AND II EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF TCR BASED EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING THE TCR SEQUENCE AND STRUCTURE INFORMATION. 3. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE MHC PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 4. UPDATE EVALUATIONS OF THE MHC BINDING AND T CELL PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. 5. MAINTAIN EXISTING B CELL TOOLS DEVELOPED BY DTU. 6. DEVELOP NEW B CELL EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODY SPECIFIC EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING BCR SEQUENCE INFORMATION. 7. ESTABLISH AUTOMATED BENCHMARKING SYSTEMS FOR PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS AS WELL AS PREDICTION TOOLS NOT HOSTED IN THE IEDB. 8. PROVIDE UPDATED BENCHMARK DATASETS WITH RESPECT TO THESE TASKS, DTU WILL DEVELOP CODE IN THEIR LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND ENSURE THAT IT CAN BE EXECUTED APPROPRIATELY IN THE IEDB PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT AND WORK WITH THE LJI TEAM TO UPDATE WEB SERVERS EXECUTING THE CODE AS NECESSARY. THIS INCLUDES RETRAINING, BUG FIXES, AND FEATURE ENHANCEMENTS AS THEY OCCUR. FOR ANY NEW TOOL OR SUBSTANTIAL TOOL UPDATE DEVELOPED WITH FUNDING FROM THE IEDB BY DTU, THE PRIMARY PUBLICATION WILL INCLUDE A LINK TO THE WORKING TOOL ON THE IEDB WEBSITE. B. MEETINGS AND REPORTS 1. MEETINGS/TELECONFERENCES/VIDEOCONFERENCES DTU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH LJI AT A MINIMUM OF TWICE PER MONTH, EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA TELECONFERENCE/VIDEOCONFERENCE. THE PURPOSE OF THESE MEETINGS WILL BE TO COORDINATE EFFORTS AND REPORT PROGRESS. DTU WILL ALSO BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN 1-2 US BASED PROGRAM MEETINGS PER CONTRACT YEAR FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING FEEDBACK TO NIH AND FURTHER PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. 2. QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS DTU WILL PROVIDE INPUT FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS ON A TIMELY BASIS SO THEIR CONTENT CAN BE INCORPORATED IN ADVANCE OF THE SPECIFIED DELIVERY DATE TO NIAID.

description: TASK 1: VIRUSES OF STUDY AND GENERATION OF RECOMBINANT VIRUSES (CEIRR-CRIPT). THE RECENT IDENTIFICATION AND COLLECTION OF 2009 PANDEMIC PRECURSOR VIRUSES BY THE LAB OF PROF. DR. ADOLFO GARCIA SASTRE AT CEIRR-CRIPT ALLOWS NEW EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH INTO PANDEMIC EMERGENCE AT THE HUMAN-SWINE INTERFACE . THE VIRUSES OF THIS COLLECTION WILL BE COMPARED TO A SET OF H1N1 AND H3N2 HUMAN VIRUSES AVAILABLE AT UU. GUIDED BY PHYLOGENETIC ANALYSES AND RESULTS FROM TASK 2-4 (UU), CEIRR-CRIPT WILL GENERATE RECOMBINANT VIRUSES TO MAKE CAUSAL LINKS BETWEEN PHENOTYPIC TRAITS TO GENETIC FEATURES (UU). TASK 2: BIOLAYER INTERFEROMETRIC KINETIC ANALYSIS OF VIRUS-RECEPTOR INTERACTIONS (UU). THE HA-NA-RECEPTOR BALANCE OF (PRE)PANDEMIC VIRUSES WILL BE STUDIED USING BLI. WE WILL USE TAILOR-MADE RECOMBINANT GLYCOPROTEINS DEVELOPED AT UU THAT BETTER MIMIC THE RECEPTORS IAVS ENCOUNTER IN VIVO THAN THE TYPICALLY USED SYNTHETIC GLYCANS. THE GLYCOSYLATION AND SIALYLATION OF THESE RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE GLYCOPROTEINS (E.G. LAMP1 AND GLYCOPHORIN A) CAN BE MODIFIED BY CO-EXPRESSION OF ENZYMES SUCH AS ST6GAL1 (INCREASED ÃŽÂ±2,6-LINKED SIAS) AND CMAH (SYNTHESIS OF NEU5GC, ONLY PRESENT IN SWINE) AND BY THEIR EXPRESSION IN HEK293T CELL DERIVATIVES LACKING ONE OR MORE GLYCOSYLTRANSFERASES. VIRUSES WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ABILITY TO BIND SYNTHETIC GLYCANS AND RECOMBINANT BIOTINYLATED GLYCOPROTEINS. BINDING VIA HA WILL BE STUDIED IN THE PRESENCE OF NA INHIBITORS (NAI). VIRUS PARTICLE NUMBERS WILL BE DETERMINED AS THESE CO-DETERMINE THE INITIAL BINDING RATE, WHICH IS THE PRIME PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT PARAMETER OF VIRUS-RECEPTOR BINDING. NA-DEPENDENT SELF-ELUTION OF VIRUS PARTICLES WILL BE EXAMINED BECAUSE IT REFLECTS THE HA-NA-RECEPTOR BALANCE. TASK 3: INTERACTION OF IAV WITH MUCUS (UU). THE HA-NA BALANCE IS CRUCIAL FOR MOTILITY IN MUCUS LAYERS AND REACHING OF EPITHELIAL CELLS FOR UPTAKE. MUCUS WILL BE HARVESTED FROM PRIMARY EPITHELIAL CELL CULTURES ESTABLISHED AT UU AND CHARACTERIZED USING LECTIN BINDING ASSAYS AND PROTEOMICS AND GLYCOMICS ANALYSIS VIA MASS SPEC (UU). FOR BLI ASSAYS, MUCUS WILL BE ATTACHED TO SENSORS USING DIFFERENT LECTINS AND THE INTERACTION KINETICS OF VIRUSES WILL BE ESTABLISHED. IN ADDITION, WE WILL ANALYZE THE ABILITY OF MUCUS TO INTERFERE WITH RECEPTOR BINDING TO OR DRIVE ELUTION FROM RECEPTOR-COATED SURFACES USING BLI. UU PREVIOUSLY CONFIRMED THAT THE ABILITY OF MUCUS TO INTERFERE WITH VIRUS-RECEPTOR BINDING DEPENDS ON THE PRESENCE OF SIAS IN MUCUS. THE INHIBITORY EFFECT OF MUCUS ON THE CLEAVAGE ACTIVITY OF THE NA PROTEIN WILL BE PROBED USING IN SOLUTION MUNANA CLEAVAGE ASSAYS AND/OR ENZYME-LINKED LECTIN ASSAYS. THIS WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO: I) THE ABILITY OF HUMAN AND SWINE MUCUS TO INTERFERE WITH RECEPTOR INTERACTIONS OF SWINE AND HUMAN IAVS AND II) TO WHAT EXTENT THIS IS CORRELATED WITH CHARACTERISTICS OF HA, NA, AND THEIR BALANCE. TASK 4: IMPORTANCE OF HA-NA BALANCE FOR HUMAN AND SWINE VIRUS REPLICATION IN (PRIMARY) EPITHELIAL CELLS (UU). LASTLY WE WILL ADDRESS THE INHIBITORY EFFECT OF SWINE AND HUMAN MUCUS, THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE TARGET CELL RECEPTOR-REPERTOIRE, AND THE HA-NA-RECEPTOR BALANCE ON VIRUS PROPAGATION. REPLICATION ASSAYS WILL BE CONDUCTED ON IMMORTALIZED CELLS IN THE PRESENCE/ABSENCE OF SWINE AND HUMAN MUCUS TO ESTABLISH THE SPECIES- AND MUCUS-SPECIFIC INTERFERENCE OF VIRUS REPLICATION. IN ADDITION, WE WILL STUDY REPLICATION ON SWINE AND HUMAN PRIMARY EPITHELIAL CELL CULTURES WITH VIRUSES THAT DIFFER IN THEIR HA-NA-RECEPTOR BALANCE. WE WILL PERFORM COMPETITION ASSAYS TO ELUCIDATE SUBTLER DIFFERENCES IN REPLICATIVE ABILITIES. COLLECTIVELY, THESE ASSAYS WILL ALLOW US TO DETERMINE THE CORRELATION BETWEEN I) VIRUS TROPISM AND ZOONOTIC POTENTIAL, II) IAV REPLICATION IN PRIMARY CULTURES, III) HA-NA-RECEPTOR BALANCE AND IV) THE INTERFERENCE OF MUCUS.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK TITLE: DIAGNOSTIC PERFORMANCE OF SEROLOGICAL ASSAYS FOR DETECTION OF OPISTHORCHIS VIVERRINI INFECTION BACKGROUND: OPISTHORCHIASIS IS A FOODBORNE TREMATODE INFECTION CAUSED BY THE OPISTHORCHIS VIVERRINI (OV). THE IMPORTANCE OF OV INFECTION IS THAT CHRONIC OPISTHORCHIASIS CAN CAUSE AN ADVANCED PERIDUCTAL FIBROSIS IN HEPATOBILIARY SYSTEM. THIS ADVANCED HEPATOBILIARY PATHOLOGY CAN LEAD TO AN INTRAHEPATIC CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA (CCA). THEREFORE, PREVENTION AND ERADICATION OF OV BY SCREENING, DIAGNOSIS, AND TREATMENT OF OV INFECTION ARE AN IMPORTANT STRATEGY TO DECREASE THE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY FROM CCA IN THE POPULATION. THE CURRENT GOLD STANDARD TEST FOR DIAGNOSIS OV INFECTION IS FECAL EXAMINATION USING THE FORMALIN ETHYL ACETATE CONCENTRATION TECHNIQUE (FECT). HOWEVER, FECAL EXAMINATION BY FECT HAS SEVERAL LIMITATIONS. FOR INSTANCE, LOW-INTENSITY OF OV INFECTION CANNOT BE DETECTED BY THIS METHOD. THUS EXTENSIVE FECAL SAMPLING OVER DAYS IS REQUIRED TO INCREASE THE SENSITIVITY OF THE TEST. MOREOVER, OV EGGS ARE FREQUENTLY MISTAKEN WITH EGGS FROM AN INFECTION WITH MINUTE INTESTINAL FLUKES THAT NEEDS AN EXPERT MICROSCOPIST TO DIFFERENTIATE OV EGGS FROM OTHER MINUTE INTESTINAL FLUKES. THUS, THE NEW DIAGNOSTIC TEST IS NECESSARY TO INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD OF DIAGNOSIS OV INFECTION, ESPECIALLY IN THE PERSONS HAVING LIGHT INFECTION. CURRENTLY, A SEROLOGICAL TEST DETECTING OV IGG ANTIBODIES USING ELISA AND POINT-OF-CARE LATERAL FLOW ASSAY HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED TO IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS WHO CURRENTLY OR PREVIOUSLY HAVE OV INFECTION. HOWEVER, THE PERFORMANCE OF THE ELISA AND POINT-OF-CARE LATERAL FLOW ASSAY HAS NOT BEEN INVESTIGATED IN THE GENERAL POPULATION THAT IS THE TARGETED POPULATION FOR SCREENING OV INFECTION. PURPOSE/GOALS: 1. TO ASSESS THE PERFORMANCE OF THE ELISA TEST FOR DIAGNOSIS OF OV INFECTION AMONG PEOPLE LIVING IN NAMPHONG DISTRICT, KHON KAEN PROVINCE, THAILAND 2. TO ASSESS THE PERFORMANCE OF THE LATERAL FLOW ASSAY FOR DIAGNOSIS OF OV INFECTION AMONG PEOPLE LIVING IN NAMPHONG DISTRICT, KHON KAEN PROVINCE, THAILAND SCOPE: LABORATORY AGREES TO: 1. DEVELOP THE RESEARCH PROTOCOL 2. SUBMIT THE PROTOCOL TO WRAIR AND LOCAL IRB 3. CONDUCT THE COMMUNITY SURVEY IN KHON KAEN PROVINCE, THAILAND 4. COLLECT THE SERUM AND STOOL SPECIMENS FROM STUDYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PARTICIPANTS 5. TRANSFER THE SERUM SPECIMENS TO THE COMPANY IN U.S. 6. PERFORM THE STOOL EXAMINATION TO DIAGNOSIS OV INFECTION 7. PROVIDE MONTHLY UPDATES VIA EMAIL ON THE STATUS OF THE PROJECT COOPERATOR AGREES TO: 1. PERFORM THE ELISA TESTS AND LATERAL FLOW ASSAY 2. PROVIDE CONSULTATION TO AFRIMS ABOUT STOOL EXAMINATION FOR DIAGNOSIS OF OV INFECTION THE PARTIES AGREE TO: 1. JOINTLY ANALYZE DATA 2. PREPARE RESEARCH REPORT 3. COOPERATE ON ANY PUBLICATIONS REGARDING THE RESEARCH PROJECT IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTIONS 9.5 AND 9.6.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF QUEENSLAND (UQ) IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CARB-X, WILL DEVELOP NEW ANTIBIOTICS TO TREAT GRAM-NEGATIVE PATHOGENS THAT ARE DESIGNATED AS SERIOUS PUBLIC HEALTH THREATS BY THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC) AND THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION (WHO). UQÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S APPROACH IS TO ADVANCE A NOVEL ANTIBIOTIC CLASS CALLED OCTAPEPTIN-X (OPX), WHICH IS A LIPOPEPTIDE WITH NATURAL PRODUCT ORIGINS. OPX EXHIBITS BROAD SPECTUM ACTIVITY AGAINST A RANGE OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA, INCLUDING THOSE THAT ARE RESISTANT TO POLYMYXIN. THE NOVELTY AND UTILITY OF OPX IS EXEMPLIFIED BY: (I) INTRINSIC ACTIVITY AGAINST POLYMYXIN-RESISTANT PATHOGENS; (II) A LOW PROPENSITY TO INDUCE RESISTANCE, OCCURING BY UNIQUE MECHANISMS NOT SHARED BY POLYMYXIN; (III) REDUCED NEPHROTOXIC POTENTIAL. POLYMYXIN BASED ANTIBIOTICS ARE TOXIC, SUFFERING FROM A NARROW THERAPEUTIC WINDOW AND HIGH INCIDENCES OF KIDNEY TOXICITY. NEXT-GENERATION POLYMYXIN CANDIDATES CURRENTLY IN DEVELOPMENT OFFER PROMISE OF REDUCED TOXICITY, BUT REMAIN INEFFECTIVE AGAINST POLYMYXIN RESISTANT ISOLATES. THE LACK OF CROSS-RESISTANCE BETWEEN OPX AND POLYMYXIN THEREFORE MAKES OPX A POTENTIAL CHOICE TO TREAT PATIENTS SUFFERING FROM INFECTIONS CAUSED BY GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA RESISTANT TO POLYMYXIN, AND/OR OTHER ANTIBIOTIC CLASSES COMPROMISED BY CONTEMPORARY MULTI-DRUG RESISTANCE. THUS, UQÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S COMMITMENT IS TO DEVELOP OPX AS A SAFE AND NOVEL TREATMENT PARADIGM FOR DRUG-RESISTANT INFECTIONS DEEMED UNTREATABLE BY CONVENTIONAL THERAPIES. TARGET INDICATIONS MAY INCLUDE MAY INCLUDE URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CUTIS), ACUTE PYELONEPHRITIS, COMPLICATED INTRA-ABDOMINAL INFECTIONS (CIAIS), OR COMMUNITY/HOSPITAL/VENTILATOR-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP/HAP/VAP). WITH CARB-X SUPPORT, UQ WILL TAKE THE APPROACH OF MITIGATING TOXICITY RISKS VERY EARLY IN THE PROGRAM BY PRIMING ITS DISCOVERY PATHWAY WITH DETAILED ANIMAL MODELS DESIGNED TO IDENTIFY EVIDENCE OF KIDNEY TOXICITY WITHIN ITS LEAD COMPOUND PORTFOLIO. THE FIRST STAGE OF THE PROGRAM WILL CULMINATE IN THE NOMINATION OF A MOLECULE SUITABLE FOR PROGRESSION INTO DETAILED MICROBIOLOGICAL, SAFETY AND EFFICACY TESTING TOWARD CANDIDATE SELECTION (2021). SUBSEQUENT STAGES OF THE PROGRAM WILL ADDRESS ASPECTS OF CHEMISTRY MANUFACTURING AND CONTROLS (CMC; 2022) FOLLOWED BY GLP TOXICOLOGY STUDIES TOWARD INVESTIGATIONAL NEW DRUG (IND) SUBMISSION (2023), AND LASTLY FIRST IN HUMAN PHASE 1 CLINICAL TRIALS (2024). INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY FOR OPX IS SOLELY OWNED BY UQ.

description: OPTION SAMPLE AND DATA 6 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ GALE THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE IMPAC-TB PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING AND POTENTIALLY EVEN ERADICATING MTB. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. THE TASKS COVERED IN OUR OPTION 6 BUDGET ARE DESIGNED TO AUGMENT THE TASKS THAT WE ARE PERFORMING THROUGH OUR YEAR 6 BASE BUDGET. SPECIFICALLY: 1. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. OUR YEAR 6 BASE BUDGET COVERS PERFORMING RNA-SEQ ASSAYS ON THE MAJORITY OF THE SAMPLES FROM NHP EXPERIMENTS BUT NOT ALL OF THEM. UNDER OUR OPTION 6 BUDGET, WE WILL PROCESS THE REMAINING SAMPLES FROM THESE STUDIES. TASKS INCLUDE 1) RECEIVING THESE ADDITIONAL SAMPLES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA FROM THE PICKER LAB (OHSU), 2) ISOLATING RNA FROM THESE SAMPLES AND PERFORMING RNA QC, 3) CONSTRUCTING RNA-SEQ LIBRARIES AND PERFORMING LIBRARY QC USING THE ISOLATED RNA, AND 4) GENERATING RNA SEQUENCE DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES. 2. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. OUR YEAR 6 BASE BUDGET COVERS DATA ANALYSIS ON THE MAJORITY OF THE SAMPLES FROM NHP EXPERIMENTS BUT NOT ALL OF THEM. UNDER OUR OPTION 6 BUDGET, WE WILL PERFORM DATA ANALYSIS ON DATA GENERATED FROM THE REMAINING SAMPLES. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRIXES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND WHEN APPROPRIATE RULE-BASED MODELING.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW GERNER) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. YEAR 6 (BASE) Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ HAWN THE HAWN LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 6. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1-5 IS ONGOING. 1. UW WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 6. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL. 2. UW WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. ANALYSES ARE UNDERWAY TO EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN CANDIDATE GENES WITH MTB-INDUCED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES IN A COHORT OF 100 HEALTHY DONORS. . 3. UW WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. STUDIES WILL INCLUDE INFECTION OF MACROPHAGES WITH MTB AND ANALYSIS OF IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND CONTROL OF MTB REPLICATION. CELL SUPERNATANTS WILL BE HARVESTED FOR CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE ELISA AND RNA EXTRACTED FROM CELLS, QUANTIFIED, AND ANALYZED. 4. UW WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

EXPANSION OF MICROSCOPY CAPABILITIES IN IMPACTB CASCADE WORK WITH IBEX IMAGING OF HUMAN SAMPLES AN EXTENSION OF WORK UNDER THE 75N93019C00070 CASCADE IMPAC-TB CONTRACT. ONGOING IMPACTB CASCADE STUDIES USING 10-13-PLEX IMAGING HAVE PROVIDED MANY KEY INSIGHTS INTO CELL TYPE COMPOSITION AND LESION ORGANIZATION DURING MTB INFECTION ACROSS ANIMAL MODELS, AND MOST RECENTLY IN HUMAN LESIONS OF PATIENTS WITH END-STAGE DISEASE. THE SUPPLEMENT WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: AIM 1: THE ULTRA-HIGH PLEX (IBEX) IMAGING APPROACH DEVELOPED BY DR. RONALD GERMAINÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE NIH WILL BE USED TO BETTER CHARACTERIZE HUMAN LUNG LESIONS DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THIS WILL LEAD TO IMPROVED DEFINITION OF CELLULAR COMPOSITION AND HETEROGENEITY. ADOPTION OF THIS TECHNOLOGY WILL INITIALLY BE IMPLEMENTED ON AND APPLIED TO ALREADY AVAILABLE SAMPLES PROVIDED THROUGH THE ONGOING POST-MORTEM IMPACTB STUDIES IN UGANDA WITH STEVE COSE. AIM 2: OBTAIN AND INCLUDE IN OUR WORKFLOW ADDITIONAL SAMPLES FROM A BROADER SPECTRUM OF LESION TYPES AND DISEASE STAGES. TO THIS END WE WILL ESTABLISH A COLLABORATION WITH DR. ADRIE STEYNÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GROUP AT THE AFRICA HEALTH RESEARCH INSTITUTE (AHRI), LEVERAGING THEIR EXTENSIVE HUMAN LUNG TISSUE REPOSITORY AT THE ALBERT LUTHULI CENTRAL HOSPITAL AS PART OF THE HUMAN LUNG PROJECT. THROUGH THIS COLLABORATION, WE WILL OBTAIN HUMAN LUNG GRANULOMA SAMPLES AND LINKED DRAINING AND NON-DRAINING LNS FROM INDIVIDUALS WITH VARIOUS STAGES OF TB DISEASE. THESE SAMPLES WILL THEN BE ANALYZED USING THE IBEX IMAGING PIPELINE IN THE GERNER LAB. USING IBEX ULTRA-HIGH PLEX IMAGING ON THESE UNIQUE AND PRECIOUS SAMPLES, WE WILL NOT ONLY BETTER DEFINE THE HETEROGENEITY OF HUMAN DISEASE AT A HIGH LEVEL OF CELLULAR AND SPATIAL RESOLUTION, BUT ALSO LINK HOW LUNG DISEASE AFFECTS PROCESSES TAKING PLACE IN ASSOCIATED LUNG DRAINING LYMPH NODES.

description: THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO COMPLETE PHASE 1 CLINICAL TRIALS WITH A NEW VACCINE FORMULATION THAT PREVENTS INVASIVE DISEASE CAUSED BY ESCHERICHIA COLI. DIFFERENT PATHOGENIC BACTERIA, INCLUDING E. COLI, POSSESS AN EXTRACELLULAR FORM OF GLYCERALDEHYDE-3-PHOSPHATE DEHYDROGENASE (GAPDH) THAT HAS A POTENT IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE ACTIVITY IN THE MAMMALIAN HOSTS. HOST IMMUNOSUPPRESSION IS MEDIATED BY THE ABILITY OF GAPDH TO BIND TO TLR2 AND TO TRIGGER A FAST PRODUCTION OF INTERLEUKIN-10. EXCRETION OF BACTERIAL GAPDH THROUGHOUT THE BLOOD STREAM OF THE HOST OCCURS IMMEDIATELY AFTER INFECTION AND INHIBITS EARLY EVENTS OF THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE, ALLOWING THE BACTERIA TO SPREAD SYSTEMICALLY WITHIN FEW HOURS. NEUTRALIZATION OF BACTERIAL GAPDH IS ESSENTIAL TO PROMOTE A PROTECTIVE RESPONSE AGAINST E. COLI INFECTIONS. ACKNOWLEDGING THE IMPORTANCE OF EXTRACELLULAR GAPDH IN THE PATHOGENICITY OF E.COLI CAN EXPLAIN WHY OTHER ATTEMPTS TO DEVELOP VACCINES THAT TARGET ONLY STRUCTURAL EPITOPES HAVE FAILED. AS IT IS WIDELY KNOWN, GAPDH IS AN UBIQUITOUS ENZYME THAT, IN ITS INTRACELLULAR FORM IS ESSENTIAL FOR GLYCOLYSIS. HOWEVER, E. COLI POSSESS TWO DIFFERENT GENES THAT CODE FOR TWO DIFFERENT GAPDH: I) THE INTRACELLULAR GLYCOLYTIC ENZYME CODED BY GAPA GENE AND II) THE EXTRACELLULAR VIRULENCE FACTOR CODED BY GAPC GENE. THE ABROGATION OF GAPC GENE DOES NOT INFLUENCE THE METABOLIC RATE OF THE BACTERIA BUT REDUCES DRAMATICALLY THE ABILITY OF BACTERIA TO CAUSE DISEASE. HUMANS DO NOT POSSESS GAPC-ENCODED GAPDH, BUT THERE IS STILL A SIGNIFICANT DEGREE OF IDENTITY BETWEEN GAPC- AND GAPA-ENCODED GAPDH (APPROX. 50%). TO OVERCOME ANY REACTIVITY TO HUMAN GAPDH, WE IDENTIFIED REGIONS (PEPTIDES) EXPOSED TO SOLVENT ON BACTERIAL GAPDH THAT ARE COMPLETELY ABSENT FROM HUMAN GAPDH. WITHIN THIS PROJECT WE INTEND TO DEVELOP AN IMMUNOGENIC FORMULATION THAT TARGETS THE IDENTIFIED REGIONS. DIFFERENT FORMULATIONS WILL BE TESTED FOR THEIR IMMUNOGENICITY AND ABILITY TO PREVENT INVASIVE DISEASE CAUSED BY E. COLI IN IN VIVO CHALLENGING ASSAYS IN THE MOUSE MODEL. THE BEST COMBINATION OF POLYPEPTIDE + CARRIER PROTEIN WILL PROCEED TO PRECLINICAL STUDIES AND PHASE 1 STUDIES.

description: PEARL DIAGNOSTICS INC. (PEARLDX) DEVELOPS NOVEL IN VITRO DIAGNOSTIC (IVD) TESTS THAT AID NON-INVASIVE DIAGNOSIS OF LIFE-THREATENING LUNG INFECTIONS. PEARLDXÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S TECHNOLOGY LEVERAGES THE DISCOVERY THAT MICROBIAL EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS) RELEASED FROM ORGANISMS GROWING IN THE LUNGS ARE EXCRETED IN URINE. IDENTIFICATION OF SPECIFIC LUNG PATHOGENS SUCH AS PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (PSA) AS A CAUSE OF PNEUMONIA IS CRITICAL IN MITIGATING THE IMPACT OF ANTIMICROBIAL DRUG RESISTANCE. WHILE A LESS COMMON CAUSE OF COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP), THIS GRAM-NEGATIVE ROD (GNR) IS INTRINSICALLY RESISTANT TO SEVERAL ANTIBIOTIC CLASSES, INCLUDING B-LACTAMS, AND EXHIBITS FREQUENT MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE (MDR). THE PREVALENCE OF PSA IN CAP IS REPORTED AS VARIABLE, RANGING FROM 0 TO 23%, WITH A POOLED PREVALENCE OF 8.6% IN PEOPLE WITH IDENTIFIED RISKS FOR MDR INFECTIONS. IDENTIFICATION OF PSA IN CULTURES ENABLES SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING AND TAILORING OF EMPIRIC THERAPY FOR BOTH CAP AND HOSPITAL- AND VENTILATOR-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (HAP, VAP) IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS. HOWEVER, THIS FREQUENTLY REQUIRES BAL SAMPLING AND CULTURE YIELD IS VARIABLE. IDENTIFICATION OF THE ORGANISM IS NOT AN ASSURANCE OF ACUTE DISEASE ETIOLOGY, AS COLONIZATION IS COMMON IN PEOPLE WITH POOR AIRWAY CLEARANCE, SUCH AS IN THOSE WITH BRONCHIECTASIS AND CYSTIC FIBROSIS (CF). VARIABLE PERFORMANCE, NON-SPECIFICITY OF CLINICAL FINDINGS, RELIANCE ON INVASIVE SAMPLING, AND TIME TO CULTURE DRIVE A HIGH AMOUNT OF ANTIBIOTIC EMPIRICISM, ULTIMATELY GENERATING AND PROPAGATING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR). PEARLDXÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PRODUCTS PROVIDE ADVANTAGES WITH REGARD TO ACCESS (REFERENCE LABS VS. LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS), COSTS (> $2000/TEST VS. < $20), AND TIME TO RESULT (3-5 DAYS VS. < 2 HR.). OTHER TECHNOLOGIES TYPICALLY RELY ON LARGE INSTRUMENTS AND/OR REFERENCE TESTING. THEREFORE, THERE REMAIN CRITICAL UNMET NEEDS AND OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES WITH EASIER-TO-DEPLOY, LESS EXPENSIVE IVDS USING URINE AS AN ADJUNCT DIAGNOSTIC AID FOR PNEUMONIA. THE AVAILABILITY OF ADJUNCTIVE NON-CULTURE-BASED TESTS (NCBT) TO AID IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF PNEUMONIA IS A LONG-APPRECIATED PRIORITY. PEARLDX, WITH SUPPORT FROM CARB-X, INTENDS TO DEVELOP A LOW-COST, LOW TURNAROUND TIME (TAT) URINE ASSAY FOR THE DETECTION OF PSEUDOMONAS PNEUMONIA (PMA). THE INITIAL AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A PROTOTYPE ASSAY. ALL ASSAYS DEVELOPED BY PEARLDX, INCLUDING THE PROPOSED CARB-X-SUPPORTED PSA ASSAY, ARE ADVANCED USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PATIENTS, WITH ITERATIVE IMPROVEMENTS OF THE ASSAY INFORMED BY THE CHARACTERIZATION OF URINARY ANTIGENS AND BY REDUCING MATRIX INTERFERENCE.

description: MELIO IS COMMITTED TO REVOLUTIONIZING THE HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY BY OFFERING RAPID INFECTIOUS DISEASE DIAGNOSTIC SOLUTIONS. BY REDEFINING STANDARDS OF CARE, MELIO AIMS TO DRIVE A SHIFT TOWARD PRECISION HEALTHCARE, EMPOWERING CLINICIANS TO MAKE INFORMED, TIMELY DECISIONS FOR TREATMENT FOR INFECTIONS, REDUCING HEALTHCARE COSTS, AND THE OVERPRESCRIPTION OF ANTIBIOTICS. MELIO’S FIRST PRODUCT FOCUSES ON PROVIDING A BREAKTHROUGH IN BOTH SPEED AND PATHOGEN COVERAGE FOR DIAGNOSING BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS DIRECTLY FROM A PATIENT’S BLOOD SAMPLE FOR NEONATES. UNLIKE THE STANDARD CULTURE METHOD, WHICH SERVES AS A BOTTLENECK BY TAKING DAYS TO DELIVER RESULTS, MELIO’S TECHNOLOGY OFFERS AN EXPEDITED ALTERNATIVE THAT COULD TRANSFORM PATIENT CARE.

description: PNEUMONIA IS A COMMON CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS THAT OFTEN LACKS A MICROBIOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS BECAUSE NO PATHOGEN IS IDENTIFIED. WITHOUT A MICROBIOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS, ANTIBIOTICS TARGETING A BROAD RANGE OF PATHOGENS ARE USED, INCREASING THE RISKS FOR RESISTANCE ALONG WITH POOR OUTCOMES IF INAPPROPRIATE ANTIBIOTICS ARE CHOSEN. THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM PROPOSES TO DIAGNOSE LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN FOUR HOURS, MUCH FASTER THAN CURRENT CULTURE TECHNIQUES. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM IS TO DEVELOP RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TESTS THAT WILL BE INDICATED IN ALL PATIENTS WITH A CLINICAL SUSPICION FOR PNEUMONIA. THE SHORT-TERM OBJECTIVE WILL FOCUS ON PNEUMONIAS CAUSED BY STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS, PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA, AND HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE, WITH THE GOAL OF HAVING RESULTS AVAILABLE IN 4 HOURS. THE STRATEGY USED IN THIS DIAGNOSTIC TEST DISTINGUISHES IT FROM COMPETITORS AND ALTERNATIVES. THIS DIAGNOSTIC IS BASED ON DETECTING RNA SEQUENCE(S) SPECIFIC FOR THE PATHOGEN CAUSING PNEUMONIA IN A HUMAN PATIENT. TESTING WILL BE DONE ON BLOOD DRAWN DIRECTLY FROM THE PATIENT, MAKING IT LESS INVASIVE THAN OTHER METHODS THAT OBTAIN SAMPLES FROM THE AIRWAYS, SUCH AS BRONCHOSCOPY OR DEEP SUCTIONING. THIS TEST WILL NOT REQUIRE THE SPECIMEN TO BE CULTURED, ALLOWING FOR FASTER RESULTS THAN TRADITIONAL MICROBIOLOGICAL METHODS. THE RNA TARGETED BY THE TEST IS IDENTIFIED VIA RNA SEQUENCING OF BLOOD FROM PATIENTS WITH THE INFECTION. RNA SEQUENCING DATA SHOWS RNA SPECIFIC TO THE PATHOGEN OF INTEREST (S. AUREUS., P. AERUGINOSA, AND H. INFLUENZAE) THAT IS ALSO SPECIFIC FOR AN ACTIVE INFECTION. TARGETING RNA ALSO ENSURES THAT THE INFECTION IS CURRENT SINCE RNA IS LESS STABLE THAN DNA, LASTING MINUTES TO HOURS WHEN FROM A BACTERIUM. THE METHOD, HOWEVER, IMMEDIATELY STABILIZES THE RNA FOR TESTING. RNA ALSO IDENTIFIES BACTERIA THAT ARE ACTIVELY MAKING RESISTANCE PROTEINS, RATHER THAN BACTERIA WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR RESISTANCE BASED ONLY ON GENOMIC DNA. AT THE END OF THIS PROJECT, PCR BASED TESTS WILL BE CREATED THAT ARE INFORMED BY RNA SEQUENCING DATA. THESE WILL DIAGNOSE PNEUMONIA DUE TO S. AUREUS., P. AERUGINOSA, AND H. INFLUENZAE, ALONG WITH RELEVANT ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE, USING BLOOD FROM THE PATIENT. THIS PCR TESTING PLATFORM USES FDA-APPROVED INSTRUMENTATION TO FACILITATE TRANSITIONING FROM A RESEARCH LABORATORY TO A CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY.

description: OUR PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A NEW DRUG EFFECTIVE AGAINST MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT (MDR) GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. OUR EARLY LEAD COMPOUNDS ARE DERIVED FROM A NATURAL PRODUCT AND REPRESENT A NOVEL CLASS OF COMPOUNDS FEATURING A NOVEL MODE OF ACTION. THE AGENTS ARREST THE FUNCTION OF BAMA, AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT FOR BACTERIAL SURVIVAL, WHICH NO CURRENT DRUGS TARGET. BAMA, IS AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT OF THE ÃƑÅ¸-BARREL ASSEMBLY MACHINERY (BAM), LOCATED IN THE OUTER MEMBRANE (OM) OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA; THE TARGET IS NOT PRESENT IN HUMANS (SPECIFIC). BAMA FOLDS AND INTEGRATES OM-PROTEINS INTO THE OM; INHIBITION LEADS TO OM BLEBBING AND ULTIMATELY CELL LYSIS (ESSENTIAL). SINCE BAMA HAS NOT BEEN TARGETED BY ANY EXISTING DRUGS, BACTERIA HAVE NOT DEVELOPED TARGET-BASED RESISTANCE. HENCE, OUR PROGRAM CAN BE REGARDED AS THE FOUNDATION FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FIRST IN CLASS BAMA INHIBITOR. WE WILL FOCUS ON TREATING HOSPITAL-ACQUIRED INFECTIONS SUCH AS PNEUMONIA CAUSED BY MDR BACTERIA. description: URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (UTIS) ARE AN INCREASING CLINICAL PROBLEM, HAVING INCREASED BY 60% BETWEEN 1990 AND 2019 AND ACCOUNTING FOR 40% OF ALL NOSOCOMIAL INFECTIONS. APPROXIMATELY 65% OF COMPLICATED OR RECURRENT UTIS (RUTIS) ARE DUE TO UROPATHOGENIC E. COLI (UPEC), ALTHOUGH SEVERAL OTHER GRAM-NEGATIVE AND GRAM-POSITIVE PATHOGENS ARE ALSO IMPLICATED. CLARAMETYX BIOSCIENCES, INC. (CLARAMETYX) IS DEVELOPING A VACCINE CANDIDATE, CMTX-301, TO PREVENT RUTIS. CMTX-301 IS A PATHOGEN-AGNOSTIC VACCINE CANDIDATE FOR THE PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL BIOFILMS, A KEY COMPONENT OF MANY RECALCITRANT AND/OR RECURRENT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, SUCH AS RUTIS. IMMUNIZATION WITH CMTX-301 FOCUSES THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE ON SPECIFIC PROTECTIVE EPITOPES WITHIN COMPONENTS OF THE BACTERIAL BIOFILM RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS STRUCTURAL STABILITY, THEREBY PREVENTING BIOFILM FORMATION. GIVEN THAT BIOFILMS ARE A SIGNIFICANT DEFENSE MECHANISM AGAINST DISEASE RESOLUTION, PREVENTING DEVELOPMENT OF THESE PROTECTIVE STRUCTURES SHOULD REDUCE DISEASE OCCURRENCE AND THUS PROVIDE SIGNIFICANT BENEFITS. . UNLIKE OTHER BACTERIAL VACCINES THAT TARGET SPECIFIC BACTERIAL SPECIES, CMTX-301 IMMUNIZATION TO PREVENT BACTERIAL BIOFILM FORMATION WILL ALLOW THE HOST’S NATURAL IMMUNE RESPONSE TO CLEAR INFECTION IN A PATHOGEN-AGNOSTIC MANNER. THE PROGRAM PROPOSED HEREIN WILL ESTABLISH PROOF-OF-CONCEPT PRECLINICAL STUDIES AGAINST RUTI DUE TO E. COLI , DEVELOP A LAB-SCALE MANUFACTURING PROCESS THAT CAN SCALE FOR NEED, AND SEEK FDA GUIDANCE ON THE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM TO ADVANCE CMTX-301 TO CLINICAL EVALUATION.

description: THE I LEAD PROGRAM IS A LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVE DESIGNED TO ENHANCE PARTICIPANTS' SKILLS IN NAVIGATING CHANGE AND COMPETING PRIORITIES. IT FOCUSES ON A VARIETY OF KEY LEADERSHIP TOPICS (E.G., INTEREST-BASED NEGOTIATION, RESULTS-BASED ACCOUNTABILITY, SITUATIONAL LEADERSHIP, EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE, AND OTHERS). THE PROGRAM SPANS UP TO 12 MONTHS AND INCLUDES FIVE GROUP TRAINING SESSIONS, EACH 6 HOURS IN LENGTH. THROUGHOUT THE PROGRAM, PARTICIPANTS SHALL REFINE AND APPLY THEIR LEADERSHIP SKILLS THROUGH NINE ONE-ON-ONE COACHING SESSIONS AND NINE FOUR COLLABORATIVE SKILLS TEAM MEETINGS, WHICH SHALL BE CONDUCTED IN SMALL GROUPS. THE PROGRAM INCLUDES UP TO 25 FEDERAL EMPLOYEES AT GS 14 AND 15 LEVELS, AND T42 (OR EQUIVALENT). DPCPSI OVERSEES THE APPLICATION AND SELECTION PROCESS FOR THE 25 PARTICIPANTS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TWO COACHES FOR THE I LEAD PROGRAM. YOSI WILL COACH FOUR COACHEES, AND PATTY WILL COACH FIVE COACHEES. SPECIFICALLY, THE CONTRACTOR COACHES SHALL: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ATTEND THE TWO-HOUR PROGRAM ORIENTATION SESSION FROM 8-10 ET ON 01/14/25 Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ CONDUCT NINE ONE-HOUR INDIVIDUAL COACHING SESSIONS BEGINNING IN JANUARY 2025 FOR EACH COACHEE (36 TO 45 TOTAL SESSIONS) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ DEBRIEF 360 SURVEY RESULTS WITH EACH COACHEE DURING ONE OF THE COACHING SESSIONS (FMP WILL ADMINISTER THE 360 AND PROVIDE THE COACH THE REPORT) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ LEAD FOUR GROUP "SKILLS TEAM" MEETINGS WHERE THE COACH MEETS WITH THEIR FOUR COACHEES TO HELP THEM APPLY CONCEPTS FROM THE TRAINING PROGRAM (4 TOTAL HOURS).

description: THE ADJUVANT DISCOVERY CONTRACT PROPOSED HEREIN WILL IDENTIFY, CHARACTERIZE, AND ADVANCE NOVEL SYNTHETIC IL-1R-BASED ADJUVANTS FOR USE IN COMBINATION WITH AN INFLUENZA VACCINE TO INDUCE RAPID AND SUSTAINED BROADLY PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY TO SEASONAL AND/OR PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS. THIS PROPOSAL BRINGS TOGETHER HIGHLY EXPERIENCED RESEARCH TEAMS FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA, DUKE UNIVERSITY, THE ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI AND INIMMUNE CORPORATION, EACH WITH UNIQUE EXPERTISE AND PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN NIAID ADJUVANT DISCOVERY AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS. DR. EVANS, DIRECTOR OF THE CTM, AND COLLEAGUES AT UM WILL LEAD THE DISCOVERY EFFORTS AND COORDINATE ACTIVITIES OF ALL SUBCONTRACTORS. THE RESEARCH TEAM AT UM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HIGH THROUGHPUT IN SILICO SCREENING, PEPTIDE LIBRARY PRODUCTION, COMPOUNDS SYNTHESIS AND SAR, MECHANISTIC STUDIES, FORMULATION, SAFETY ASSESSMENTS AND EFFICACY STUDIES. DR. STAATS, PROFESSOR OF PATHOLOGY, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF IMMUNOLOGY AND MEDICINE, DUKE, AND COLLEAGUES WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE TEAM FROM UM TO COMPLETE THE HTS SCREENING OF SYNTHETIC PEPTIDE LIBRARIES, APTAMER LIBRARY PRODUCTION AND SCREENING, CONFIRMATION SCREEN OF SELECTED HITS USING IL-1R REPORTER CELLS, EVALUATION OF BINDING AND INTERNALIZATION, CRITICALLY EVALUATE THE INTRACELLULAR SIGNALING PATHWAYS OF LEAD IL- 1R AGONISTS AND ASSESS THE ROUTE OF ADMINISTRATION AND SCHEDULE TO OPTIMIZE BOTH PARENTERAL (IM) AND MUCOSAL (IN, SL) VACCINATION THROUGH ADJUVANT SELECTION AND FORMULATION. DR. KRAMMER, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF MICROBIOLOGY, AND COLLEAGUES AT THE ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI BRING EXPERTISE AND CONSIDERABLE KNOWLEDGE IN INFLUENZA VIRUS ANIMAL MODELS AND THE PRODUCTION OF RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA ANTIGENS. DR. KRAMMER WILL PROVIDE RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA ANTIGENS AND LEAD EFFORTS TOWARDS THE IN VIVO INFLUENZA CHALLENGE MODELS (MOUSE AND FERRET) FOR EVALUATION OF IL-1 ADJUVANTED INFLUENZA VACCINES. THE TEAM AT MOUNT SINAI ALSO BRINGS SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE IN THE SEROLOGICAL MECHANISM OF PROTECTION AND A WIDE ARRAY OF ANTIGENS AND VIRUSES TO ASSESS HETEROSUBTYPIC PROTECTION AGAINST SELECTED SEASONAL AND HIGHLY PATHOGENIC INFLUENZA VIRUS STRAINS. DR. BAZIN-LEE, VICE PRESIDENT OF DISCOVERY RESEARCH, ALONG WITH HER COLLEAGUES AT INIMMUNE CORPORATION, WILL OVERSEE ANALYTICAL ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, PHYSIOCHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION, STABILITY AND SCALE-UP SYNTHESIS OF LEAD IL-1R ADJUVANTS IDENTIFIED IN RESEARCH AREAS 1-3.

description: [THE MATIC-2 TRIAL IS A BAYESIAN, RANDOMIZED, MULTICENTER, ADAPTIVE PLATFORM PHASE III TRIAL. THE TRIAL WILL INCLUDE INJURED CHILDREN WITH HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK ANTICIPATED TO REQUIRE MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION, WHO WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE EITHER LTOWB OR CT AND TRANEXAMIC ACID OR PLACEBO. IT'S HYPOTHESIZED THAT THE USE OF LTOWB IS NON-INFERIOR AND/OR SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY AND THAT LTOWB DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES, SUCH AS THROMBOTIC EVENTS, COMPARED TO CT. IT'S ALSO HYPOTHESIZED THAT THE USE OF TXA IS SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY AND DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES, SUCH AS THROMBOTIC EVENTS, COMPARED TO PLACEBO. THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1. DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF LTOWB TO REDUCE ALL-CAUSE 24-HOUR MORTALITY COMPARED TO CT IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. 2. DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TXA TO REDUCE ALL-CAUSE 24-HOUR MORTALITY COMPARED TO PLACEBO IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. SECONDARY OBJECTIVES ARE TO DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF LTOWB AND TXA TO IMPROVE SECONDARY AND EXPLORATORY OUTCOMES (OR ENDPOINTS) IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. SAFETY OBJECTIVES ARE TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF LTOWB AND TXA ON SAFETY RELATED OUTCOMES/ENDPOINTS. MECHANISTIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1. DEFINE TRAUMA INDUCED COAGULOPATHY (TIC) ACCORDING TO MEASURES OF SHOCK, HEMOSTASIS, AND ENDOTHELIAL AND IMMUNE FUNCTION. 2. TO DETERMINE IF MEASURES OF SHOCK, ENDOTHELIAL, IMMUNE, AND HEMOSTASIS FUNCTION UPON ADMISSION (TIC ENDOTYPE) PREDICTS WHICH HEMOSTATIC RESUSCITATION THERAPIES OR COMBINATIONS OF THERAPIES (LTOWB, CT, LTOWB + TXA, CT+TXA) FOR EACH STUDY GROUP IMPROVES OUTCOMES WITHOUT INCREASING THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS. 3. TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS OF HOW HEMOSTATIC RESUSCITATION THERAPIES OR COMBINATIONS OF THERAPIES (LTOWB, CT, LTOWB + TXA, CT+TXA) IMPROVE TIC ENDOTYPES AND OUTCOMES. PHARMACOKINETIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO EVALUATE THE PK AND PD PROPERTIES OF TXA IN A POPULATION OF CHILDREN WITH LIFETHREATENING TRAUMATIC BLEEDING. ]

description: THE MISSION OF THE NIH OFFICE OF DATA SCIENCE STRATEGY IS TO ENHANCE BIOMEDICAL DATA SCIENCE BY LEADING AND COORDINATING EFFORTS ACROSS NIH TO MODERNIZE DATA RESOURCES, DEVELOP A SKILLED DATA SCIENCE WORKFORCE, AND BUILD STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS FOR ADVANCING TECHNOLOGIES AND METHODS. NIH EMPHASIZES THE MANAGEMENT AND SHARING OF RESEARCH DATA ACCORDING TO THE FAIR PRINCIPLES, ENSURING DATA IS FINDABLE, ACCESSIBLE, INTEROPERABLE, AND REUSABLE. ACHIEVING THESE PRINCIPLES RELIES ON WELL-DOCUMENTED SEMANTIC RESOURCES LIKE STANDARDS AND ONTOLOGIES. WHILE TOP-DOWN APPROACHES TO CREATING THESE RESOURCES MAY FAIL, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN, CO-DEVELOPED RESOURCES ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE WIDELY ADOPTED. THIS APPROACH BENEFITS KEY NIH STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING NIH-FUNDED BIOMEDICAL RESEARCHERS, DATA AND COMPUTER SCIENTISTS, AND EARLY CAREER RESEARCHERS AND STUDENTS, PARTICULARLY THOSE FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS AND MINORITY-SERVING INSTITUTIONS.

description: OVERALL RESPONSIBILITIES: • PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACTIVITIES FOR 5 HRSA RURAL HEALTH GRANTEES IN THE DIRECT SERVICES PROGRAM, 2 QUALITY GRANTEES AND 3 OUTREACH GRANTEES. ALL WORK WILL BE PROVIDED BY CATHERINE LIEMOHN, PRINCIPAL. RURAL HEALTH NETWORK DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM TASK 3: EXECUTE TA PROVIDE TA TO 5 DIRECT SERVICES GRANTEES. TARGETED TA INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING: O SCHEDULE REGULAR MEETINGS WITH GRANTEES: SET UP THE MEETING, INVITE GRANTEE AND FORHP PROJECT OFFICER TO PARTICIPATE. CONDUCT HOUR-LONG, MONTHLY CALLS WITH RHND GRANTEES. BEFORE BEGINNING CALLS WITH EACH GRANTEE, TA PROVIDERS WILL REVIEW ALL DOCUMENTATION RELATED TO EACH GRANTEE. TA PROVIDERS WILL SUBMIT CALL AGENDAS FIVE DAYS IN ADVANCE OF EACH CALL TO BOTH THE GRANTEE AND PO AND WILL INCLUDE WORK PLAN PROGRESS, CURRENT ISSUES AND CHALLENGES, TA SUPPORT NEEDS, REVIEW OF DELIVERABLES, AND ANY RELEVANT FORHP OR TA ANNOUNCEMENTS. O TAKE NOTES OF THE CALL ON TEMPLATE PROVIDED AND SUBMIT THEM ELECTRONICALLY TO THE PO AND GRANTEE WITHIN FIVE DAYS. O UPLOAD FINAL MEETING SUMMARIES TO ONE DRIVE, NO LATER THAN FIVE (5) BUSINESS DAYS AFTER EACH CALL. GHPC WILL COMPILE ALL SUMMARIES FOR SUBMISSION TO THE COR. O LOG MONTHLY MEETINGS CONDUCTED INTO HTTPS://GHPC-CHSD.ORG/LOGIN/. TASK 3: TAAPS: COMPLETE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACTION PLANS FOR THREE OUTREACH GRANTEES IN THE 2025 COHORT AFTER USING THE FIRST MONTHLY CALL AS AN INTAKE CALL. O INFORMED BY INTRODUCTORY CALLS WITH GRANTEES, THE TA TEAM WILL DOCUMENT GRANTEE NEEDS AND SUPPORTS USING A TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACTION PLAN (TAAP). BUILDING ON AN ESTABLISHED TEMPLATE AND PROCEDURES DEVELOPED FOR OTHER FORHP GRANTEES, THE TAAP WILL INCLUDE BACKGROUND INFORMATION ON THE GRANTEE PROGRAM AND NETWORK, PERCEIVED STRENGTHS AND POTENTIAL BARRIERS, GRANTEE NEEDS, TA STRATEGIES, EXPECTED OUTCOMES, AND TIMELINE. IN ADDITION, ESTABLISH THE ROUTINE MONTHLY CALL TIME AND DOCUMENT IT IN THE TAAP. O TA PROVIDERS WILL ELECTRONICALLY SUBMIT DRAFT TAAPS AND CALL SUMMARIES PREVIOUSLY DRAFTED TO GHPC, GRANTEES AND POS WITHIN THREE WEEKS OF EACH CALL. THE ASSOCIATED PO AND GRANTEE WILL REVIEW THE TAAP AND SUBMIT REVISIONS TO THE TA PROVIDER. WITHIN FIVE DAYS OF RECEIVING REVISIONS, THE TA PROVIDER WILL ELECTRONICALLY SUBMIT THE REVISED TA PLAN TO THE PO AND GRANTEE AS A FINAL TAAP. O UPLOAD CALL SUMMARIES AND FINAL TAAPS TO ONE DRIVE. GHPC WILL COMPILE ALL SUMMARIES FOR SUBMISSION TO THE COR. O LOG FINAL TAAPS INTO CHSDTEAM.COM. TASK 7 SITE VISITS: THIS INCLUDES INDIVIDUAL SITE VISITS FOR 2 QUALITY GRANTEES, 3 OUTREACH GRANTEES AND 2 REVERSE SITE VISITS. TRAVEL WILL BE REIMBURSED SEPARATELY WITH PROPER DOCUMENTATION AND A TRAVEL BUDGET IS PROVIDED. SUBCONTRACT UNDER A FEDERAL CONTRACT ATTACHMENT 4 STATEMENT OF WORK SUBCONTRACT NO. description: PEPTILOGICS IS A BIOTECHNOLOGY COMPANY THAT UTILIZES AN INNOVATIVE PLATFORM TO DEVELOP NOVEL PEPTIDE THERAPEUTICS TO ADDRESS UNMET MEDICAL NEEDS. OUR PIPELINE INCLUDES A NOVEL CLASS OF ENGINEERED CATIONIC ANTIBIOTIC PEPTIDES. OUR LEAD CANDIDATE, PLG0206, BASED ON NATURALLY OCCURRING ANTIMICROBIAL PEPTIDES, EXHIBITS BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY AGAINST CLINICALLY IMPORTANT MDR GRAM-POSITIVE (S. AUREUS, INCLUDING MRSA, AND E. FAECIUM, INCLUDING VRE) AND GRAM-NEGATIVE (P. AERUGINOSA, E. COLI, AND A. BAUMANNII) PATHOGENS. PLG0206 EXHIBITS THE ABILITY TO RAPIDLY INACTIVATE BOTH PLANKTONIC AND BIOFILM PATHOGENS. THIS WITH ITS BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY MAKE IT AN IDEAL DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE FOR PREVENTING INVASIVE INFECTIONS. PLG0206 TARGETS AND DISRUPTS THE BACTERIAL MEMBRANE, CAUSING RAPID BACTERIAL DEATH VIA CELLULAR CHEMICAL IMBALANCE. SINCE BACTERIAL MEMBRANES ARE A CONSERVED EVOLUTIONARY TARGET, THIS MOA APPEARS TO LIMIT THE RISK FOR RESISTANCE COMPARED TO OTHER ANTIBIOTICS. WITH RAPID BACTERICIDAL AND ANTI-BIOFILM ACTIVITY ON CONTACT, PLG0206 IS BEING DEVELOPED FOR THE PREVENTION OF TRAUMATIC FRACTURE-RELATED INFECTIONS (FRI) VIA LOCAL ADMINISTRATION IN CONJUNCTION STANDARD SURGICAL CARE. FRI IS A SERIOUS, LIFE-THREATENING INFECTION WITH SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC BURDEN. FRI TREATMENT REQUIRES HOSPITALIZATION AND ONE OR MORE REPEAT SURGICAL PROCEDURES. MICROORGANISMS THAT CAUSE FRI INCLUDE S. AUREUS, COAGULATE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCUS SPP., ENTEROCOCCUS SPP., AND AEROBIC GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI. THE POTENTIAL INFECTING PATHOGEN IS UNKNOWN AT THE TIME OF TRAUMATIC INSULT AND INITIAL SURGERY. CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES RECOMMEND 2-5 DAYS OF SYSTEMIC ANTIBIOTICS FOLLOWING TRAUMATIC INJURY TO PREVENT FRI. DESPITE THIS, TRAUMATIC FRACTURES HAVE A HIGH INFECTION RATE (UP TO 40%). FRI OFTEN REQUIRES MULTIPLE SURGICAL PROCEDURES, LEADING TO SUBSTANTIAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY WITH AN UP TO 25% 5-YEAR MORTALITY RISK. CURRENT STRATEGIES DO NOT ADEQUATELY PREVENT THE INFECTIONS THAT LEAD TO FRI'S HIGH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY BURDEN, AND FRI REMAINS AN UNMET MEDICAL NEED AND REQUIRES A DIFFERENT APPROACH TO THAT CURRENTLY EMPLOYED. PLG0206, ADMINISTERED AT THE TIME OF INJURY, THROUGH ITS RAPIDLY ACTING BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY AGAINST THE PATHOGENS COMMONLY CAUSING FRI HAS THE POTENTIAL TO ADDRESS THIS UNMET NEED. PLG0206 WILL BE ADMINISTERED FOLLOWING TRAUMATIC INJURY IN THE OPERATING THEATER AFTER SURGICAL DEBRIDEMENT AND BONE FIXATION AS A LONG-ACTING CONTROLLED RELEASE FORMULATION. IT IS EXPECTED TO BE MORE EFFECTIVE THAN THE CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE BY PROVIDING LONG-LASTING PATHOGEN-INACTIVATING DRUG LEVELS TO PREVENT INFECTION NIDI (DEVITALIZED AND CONTAMINATED BONE AND SOFT TISSUE AND METAL FIXATION DEVICES) THAT LEAD TO INVASIVE INFECTION. THE EXPECTED LIMITED SYSTEMIC EXPOSURE WITH LOCAL DRUG DEPOT SHOULD ENSURE A GOOD SAFETY PROFILE. THE DEVELOPMENT PLAN WILL ASSESS THE IN VITRO AND IN VIVO RELEASE CHARACTERISTICS OF VARIOUS PLG0206 CONTROLLED-RELEASE FORMULATIONS ALONG WITH PK, TOLERABILITY, AND EFFICACY IN ANIMAL MODELS OF FRI. ADDITIONAL STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY THE MOST EFFECTIVE, WELL-TOLERATED CONCENTRATION TO BE USED IN HUMAN TRIALS TO ESTABLISH SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF LOCAL ADMINISTRATION IN THE PREVENTION OF FRI IN CONJUNCTION WITH CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE.
