description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-NMR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 1 NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS ONE YEAR SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, 9/1/2024 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ 8/31/2025) AND FOR LEADING ONE PROJECT ON PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULE BY NMR: UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED FROM COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND INTERNAL BATCHES; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITIES ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. LEAD ONE PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS PROJECT. THE UN-NMR GROUP WILL LEAD A PROJECT ON STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION OF AN ESSENTIAL RNA PACKAGING ELEMENT FROM THE INFLUENZA A VIRUS. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. UW-NMR IS EXPECTED TO SOLVE AT LEAST 1 NMR STRUCTURE FROM THESE STUDIES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY (CSU) WILL BE PERFORMING THROUGHOUT THE PROPOSED WORK PERIOD. THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF ACTIVITIES IN THE M72-SPECIFIC PACKAGE OF THE PRIME CONTRACT. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE PREVENTION OF DISEASE OUTCOMES AND ARCHIVE SAMPLES FOR ANALYZING BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, TO BE COMPLETED IF FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE. THIS WORK WILL INCLUDE STUDIES THAT ADDRESS BCG PRIME AND BOOSTS WITH M72 COMBINED WITH 3 DIFFERENT ADJUVANT SYSTEMS IN THE GUINEA PIG MODEL. PBMC WILL BE COLLECTED AND ARCHIVED FOR IMMUNOGENICITY AND POST-INFECTION ANALYSIS WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB) ERDMAN, IF FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE, IN AN EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC) AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. OPTION 2.M72 ACTIVITIES TASK 2.M72. EVALUATE IMMUNOGENICITY AND POD EFFICACY OF M72 COMBINED WITH DIFFERENT ADJUVANT FORMULATIONS AGAINST M.TB IN GUINEA PIGS SOME OF THE HARVESTED SAMPLES IN THIS M72 TASK OUTLINED BELOW WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO COLLABORATOR SITES. CSU WILL PROVIDE THESE SAMPLES TO COLLABORATORS AS NEEDED AND PREDETERMINED BY THE NEEDS OF SOPS. THIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: SERUM OR BLOOD FOR ENDPOINT ANTIBODY ELISAS (SCRI), SYSTEMS SEROLOGY (HSPH) AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC (FHCC) ASSAYS ACROSS SPECIES. FURTHERMORE, DATA GENERATED IN THIS OPTION WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO CSU AND FHCC SYSTEMS BIOLOGISTS IN THE CORRECT FORMAT, AS DEFINED IN THE BASE PERIOD, FOR INTEGRATED ANALYSIS. ITERATIVE ANALYSIS WILL INVOLVE PRECLINICAL BIOLOGISTS AND SYSTEMS BIOLOGISTS FOR OPTIMAL DATA INTEGRITY AND IMPACT. GUINEA PIG STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED IN PARALLEL IMMUNOPATHOLOGIC STUDIES, USING THE LABORATORY ISOLATE, M.TB ERDMAN. GUINEA PIGS WILL BE BCG OR MOCK VACCINATED AND AFTER 120 DAYS, GUINEA PIGS WILL BE MOCK BOOSTED, OR BOOSTED WITH TWO INTERVALS OF THE M72 CANDIDATE VACCINE + 3 CANDIDATE ADJUVANTS, INCLUDING GLA-SE, GLA-LSQ, OR UM-1098. GUINEA PIGS WILL BE INFECTED WITH 20-50 BACILLI OF M.TB ERDMAN AND SAMPLES WILL BE HARVESTED AT VARIOUS INTERVALS. WE WILL DETERMINE THE COURSE OF THE INFECTIONS BY MEASURING CFU LEVELS IN THE LUNGS AND BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE CELLS, AND DETERMINE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF VACCINE STRATEGIES USING QUANTITATIVE HISTOPATHOLOGY. SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED AND ARCHIVED FOR DOWNSTREAM USE, BUT NOT FULLY ANALYZED, INCLUDING: PBMC TO MEASURE VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY STUDIES PRE-INFECTION AND PERIPHERAL RESPONSE POST-INFECTION, SERUM FOR SYSTEMS SEROLOGY AND CYTOKINE ELISA, LUNG AND SPLEEN CELL SUSPENSIONS FOR ANTIGEN STIMULATION AND CYTOKINE ANALYSIS, LUNG TISSUE FOR CYTOKINE ELISA, AND BAL FLUID FOR CYTOKINE ELISA. PARAFORMALDEHYDE-FIXED LUNG TISSUE WILL BE ARCHIVED IN PARAFFIN BLOCKS. IN SITU ANALYSIS OF BACTERIAL RESPONSE WILL BE ANALYZED BY RNASCOPE ISH ON FORMALIN-FIXED PARAFFIN-EMBEDDED LUNG TISSUE AND ON CELLS ISOLATED BY BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE TO DETECT BACTERIA-SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTS, WHICH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO REVEAL THEIR PRECISE LOCATION AND REPLICATIVE STATE IN LESIONS. LUNG AND SPLEEN TISSUE WILL BE COLLECTED FOR HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION AT POST-MORTEM. THE SAMPLES FOR HISTOLOGY WILL BE COLLECTED INTO 4% PARAFORMALDEHYDE IN LABELLED POTS PROVIDED BY THE STUDY DIRECTOR FROM THE HISTOLOGY DEPARTMENT. THE TISSUES COLLECTED AT NECROPSY WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE HISTOLOGY DEPARTMENT WHERE THEY WILL BE PROCESSED TO PARAFFIN FOR ROUTINE SECTIONING AND THEN HEMATOXYLIN AND EOSIN (H&E) STAINING WILL BE PERFORMED. SLIDES WILL BE EXAMINED MICROSCOPICALLY BY IN-HOUSE VETERINARY PATHOLOGISTS AND A DESCRIPTIVE REPORT OF THE NATURE OF THE DISEASE IN THE TARGET ORGANS IN EACH GROUP, TOGETHER WITH RELEVANT DATA TABLES, WILL BE PROVIDED F

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT THE SITES Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ DENVER RESEARCH INSTITUTE (AKA DRI, ADMINISTRATIVE/SUBCONTRACT SITE) AND ROCKY MOUNTAIN REGIONAL VA MEDICAL CENTER (AKA RMR-VAMC, EXPERIMENTAL WORK SITE) Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ WILL BE PERFORMING FOR THIS PROJECT. description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT FRED HUTCHINSON CANCER CENTER (FHCC) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA VACCINE DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB) THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB TASK 3.5 TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS OF NHP SAMPLES. FHCC WILL EXECUTE GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING WITH RNASEQ/NANOSTRING ASSAYS ON NHP SAMPLES GENERATED IN OPTION 3 AT UKHSA. TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS WILL BE FOCUSED ON IDENTIFYING A PERIPHERAL BLOOD SURROGATE ENDPOINT FOR THE M.TB ERDMAN ULDA CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. THE INITIAL UNBIASED RNA SEQUENCING APPROACH WILL USE WHOLE-BLOOD SAMPLES FROM PRE- AND POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL LOOK FOR TRANSCRIPTS THAT ARE CORRELATED WITH M.TB COLONY FORMING UNITS (CFU) AND M.TB QPCR ASSAYS FROM BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL), THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCE AT POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS, WE WILL ALSO LOOK FOR CHANGES IN TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE RELATIVE TO THE DAY OF CHALLENGE AS A POTENTIAL CORRELATE OF CHALLENGE OUTCOME. AS WE BUILD A MODEL TO PREDICT CHALLENGE OUTCOME FROM THESE GENE EXPRESSION MEASURES WE WILL SPECIFICALLY CONSIDER TRANSCRIPTS THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN IDENTIFIED AS PREDICTORS OF PROGRESSION TO TB DISEASE, SUCH AS TYPE I IFN-RELATED GENES WHOSE EXPRESSION INCREASES DURING DISEASE PROGRESSION. THE HUMAN EXPRESSION SIGNATURES WILL BE EVALUATED IN NHPS AND VICE VERSA; ADDITIONALLY, A JOINT MODEL WILL BE DEVELOPED, ALLOWING FOR DIFFERENCES IN NHP AND HUMAN ASSOCIATIONS, WHILE IDENTIFYING A COMMON GENE SIGNATURE. ONCE TRANSCRIPTS OR GENES HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED, A TARGETED CROSS-SPECIES NANOSTRING PANEL WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EVALUATION IN THE SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AS WELL AS IN FUTURE NHP AND CLINICAL TRIALS. WE PLAN TO DEVELOP A NANOSTRING NCOUNTER GENE PANEL WHICH CAN ACCOMMODATE UP TO 800 GENES AND WOULD BE SIGNIFICANTLY MORE COST EFFECTIVE THAN RNA SEQUENCING. ALTERNATIVELY, DEPENDING ON THE COMPLEXITY OF THE GENE PANEL, IT COULD BE DEVELOPED AS A 96 TRANSCRIPT/GENE (INCLUDING HOUSEKEEPING GENES) QPCR BIOMARK FLUIDIGM ASSAY. TASK 3.7 COMPARE IMMUNE PROFILES IN NHP, SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AND HUMANS TO IDENTIFY CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. SUBTASK 3.7.4 INTEGRATED ANALYSIS AND DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS MODELING OF EXPERIMENTAL IMMUNOLOGY DATA ACROSS ALL SPECIES EXPERIMENTAL DATA WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE STATISTICAL CENTER AND A FORMAL INTER-SITE AND INTER-SPECIES VARIABILITY ASSESSMENT WILL BE PERFORMED. VARIABILITY WILL BE DETERMINED USING COEFFICIENTS OF VARIATION (CV), MEAN AND STANDARD DEVIATION OF RESPONSES. DESIRED CUT-OFFS FOR ACCEPTABLE CVS WILL BE PRE-SPECIFIED FOR EACH ASSAY. EFFORT IN THE BASE PERIOD WILL HAVE BEEN MADE TO STANDARDIZE THE ASSAYS AND HARMONIZATION ASSESSMENTS WILL HAVE BEEN REPEATED IF CVS DID NOT MEET THE CUT OFF. description: NASMHPD WILL SERVE AS A COLLABORATOR AND PROVIDE STRATEGIC GUIDANCE AND SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE FOR THE SMI TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE CENTER. NASMHPD WILL CONTRIBUTE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE IN SMI TO SUPPORT THE SMI TTAC TA DELIVERY AND THOUGHT LEADERSHIP ACROSS MULTIPLE TASKS. SMI TTAC IS FUNDED BY THE SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA), WHO HAS APPROVED NASMHPD AS A SUBCONTRACTOR IN BOTH THE PROPOSAL AND CONTRACT. BECAUSE NASMHPD’S MEMBERSHIP INCLUDES EXECUTIVES REPRESENTING PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY SYSTEM, THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO SMI TTAC WILL BE CRITICAL TO ENSURING TA EFFORTS AND OFFERINGS ALIGN WITH THE NEEDS OF PROVIDERS AND ADMINISTRATORS ACROSS THE FIELD. NASMHPD WILL ALSO USE THEIR EXPERIENCE AND KNOWLEDGE OF WORKING WITH SAMHSA, NATIONAL COUNCIL, AND SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS TO PROVIDE THOUGHT LEADERSHIP AND SUPPORT CONSULTATIVE MONITORING BOARD ESTABLISHMENT, SELECT PERSONALIZED INTENSIVE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (PITA) DELIVERY, SELECT TA PLANNING AND EXECUTION, LEARNING COLLABORATIVES, AND VIRTUAL WEBINARS. NASMHPD, FOUNDED IN 1959, REPRESENTS THE PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY SYSTEM IN ALL 50 STATES, 6 TERRITORIES, AND THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA. NASMHPD SERVES AS THE NATIONAL REPRESENTATIVE AND ADVOCATE FOR STATE MENTAL HEALTH AGENCIES AND THEIR DIRECTORS AND SUPPORTS EFFECTIVE STEWARDSHIP OF STATE MENTAL HEALTH SYSTEMS. NASMHPD WORKS WITH STATES, FEDERAL PARTNERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS TO PROMOTE WELLNESS, RECOVERY, AND RESILIENCY FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS OR CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE RELATED DISORDERS ACROSS ALL AGES AND CULTURAL GROUPS, INCLUDING: YOUTH, OLDER PERSONS, VETERANS AND THEIR FAMILIES, AND PEOPLE UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE COURT. description: THE KEY GOALS OF THIS PROGRAM ARE TO DEMONSTRATE DETECTION OF GONORRHEA FROM CRUDE VAGINAL SWAB AND URINE SAMPLES AND DEMONSTRATE PROOF-OF-FEASIBILITY FOR THE STI SCOUT, A PRODUCT INTENDED FOR AT HOME AND POINT-OF-NEED TESTING FOR GONORRHEA AND CHLAMYDIA. THE TARGET PATHOGENS ARE NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE AND CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS. THE KEY CLINICAL INDICATIONS ARE SYMPTOMATIC AND ASYMPTOMATIC INFECTIONS OR SUSPECTED INFECTIONS OF THE UROGENITAL TRACT BY CHLAMYDIA OR GONORRHEA, THE TWO MOST COMMON, TREATABLE SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS IN THE UNITED STATES. SCOUT IS TARGETING DIFFERENTIATION AGAINST OTHER APPROACHES BY OFFERING PCR-LEVEL ACCURACY WITH THE CONVENIENCE AND COST OF RAPID ANTIGEN TESTING. UNLIKE COLLECT-AT-HOME AND SEND-IN TESTING OPTIONS, STI SCOUT DELIVERS RESULTS IMMEDIATELY TO THE USER (WITHIN 30 MINUTES). THE SCOUT HUB IS A REUSABLE DEVICE THAT ENABLES TESTING FOR MULTIPLE INDICATIONS, NOT JUST STIS, ADDING A VALUABLE TOOL TO INDIVIDUALSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ OR CLINICSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ TOOLKIT FOR DIAGNOSING COMMON, TREATABLE ILLNESSES OR INFORMING ON OVERALL WELLNESS. A MOBILE APPLICATION, SCOUT CONNECT, PERMITS RESULT TRACKING, SHARING, AND FOLLOW-ON CARE VIA TELEHEALTH AND E-PRESCRIPTIONS FROM QUALIFIED HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS. A PLANNED REFLEX TEST FOR NG AMR WILL ENABLE BETTER STEWARDSHIP OF ANTIBIOTICS.

description: THIS PROJECT IS FOCUSSED ON DEVELOPING AND CHARACTERISING ASSAYS FOR CHLAMYDIA (CT) AND GONORRHOEA (NG) THAT ARE SUITABLE FOR INTEGRATION INTO FUSE'S APEX CT/NG, A NEXT-GENERATION, INSTRUMENT-FREE MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC TEST. EXISTING TESTS ARE UNSUITABLE FOR THE WIDESPREAD, FLEXIBLE DEPLOYMENT NECESSARY TO COMBAT THE NG EPIDEMIC, DUE TO THE LOGISTICAL COMPLEXITY OF CENTRALIZED APPROACHES AND THE OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINTS INHERENT IN INSTRUMENTED PLATFORMS. LAB PCR TESTS EXHIBIT GOLD-STANDARD PERFORMANCE BUT REQUIRE SPECIALIST EQUIPMENT AND COMPLEX LOGISTICS WHICH HAMPERS ADOPTION AND MEANS THAT RESULTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE IN TIME TO INFORM EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OR MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. RAPID LATERAL FLOW TESTS ARE CONVENIENT, LOW-COST SOLUTIONS WELL SUITED TO WIDESPREAD DEPLOYMENT, BUT THEIR SENSITIVITY IS INSUFFICIENT FOR CT/NG. COMPETITORS HAVE MADE SUBSTANTIAL INVESTMENTS TO ATTEMPT TO BRING MOLECULAR TESTS FOR CT/NG OUTSIDE OF THE CENTRAL LAB BY DEVELOPING 'NEAR-PATIENT' PLATFORM INSTRUMENTS. WHILST SUCH PRODUCTS ARE EASIER TO USE, THEIR REQUIREMENT FOR A TEST MACHINE MEANS THEY DO NOT YET MEET THE CRITERIA FOR A DECENTRALIZED TEST. INSTRUMENT-FREE MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTICS PROMISE TO ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGE BY COMBINING THE BENEFITS OF LAB PCR WITH THE FLEXIBILITY OF A DISPOSABLE DEVICE FOR DECENTRALISED USE. SUCH TESTS CAN BE READILY ADOPTED IN A WIDE RANGE OF LOCATIONS, INCLUDING SMALL CLINICS AND PHARMACIES, AND PERFORMED BY A WIDE RANGE OF END USERS WITHOUT TRAINING. APEX CT/NG IS A NEXT-GENERATION INSTRUMENT-FREE MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC TEST THAT COMBINES INNOVATIVE DEVICE DESIGNS AND MOLECULAR TECHNOLOGIES TO FUNDAMENTALLY REDUCE THE COST-OF-GOODS AND SIZE OF THE TEST. IT WILL DELIVER LAB PCR ACCURACY IN AN ULTRA-RAPID (<10 MIN) DEVICE, IDEALLY SUITED TO WIDESPREAD DEPLOYMENT.

description: IN THIS CARB-X PROJECT, WE AIM AT DEVELOPING OUR NOVEL CLASS OF COMPOUNDS TARGETING THE BACTERIAL SLIDING CLAMP (DNAN) AS ANTIBIOTIC LEAD CANDIDATES FOR THE TREATMENT OF GRAM-POSITIVE BACTERIAL INFECTIONS. IT WILL BE GUIDED BY A PRIMARY TPP OF A STANDALONE THERAPY FOR THE TREATMENT OF COMMUNITY ACQUIRED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA (CABP) CAUSED BY SUSCEPTIBLE AS WELL AS MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT (MDR) STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE. WITHIN THE FRAME OF CARB-X FUNDING FOR THIS HIT-TO-LEAD BASE STAGE, WE WILL FOCUS IN THE FIRST PLACE ON THREE GOALS, NAMELY OPTIMIZATION OF TARGET AFFINITY AND ANTIBACTERIAL ACTIVITY AGAINST MAINLY TWO KEY GRAM-POSITIVE TPP PATHOGENS (STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE AND STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS), DEMONSTRATION OF TARGET ENGAGEMENT IN A GRAM-POSITIVE BACTERIAL STRAIN, AND PROOF-OF-CONCEPT IN A MURINE INFECTION MODEL. IF THESE AIMS ARE ACHIEVED, WE WILL THEN CONCENTRATE ON OPTIMIZATION OF BOTH THE PHARMACOKINETIC (PK) PROPERTIES AND THE ANTIBIOTIC SPECTRUM OF OUR COMPOUND CLASS IN ORDER TO COVER OTHER GRAM-POSITIVE TPP-RELEVANT GERMS, INCLUDING MDR CLINICAL ISOLATES, AS WELL AS OPPORTUNISTIC GRAM-NEGATIVE PATHOGENS INVOLVED IN CABP INFECTIONS. MOREOVER, WE WILL IMPLEMENT IN VITRO SAFETY PHARMACOLOGY AGAINST HUMAN OFF-TARGETS AND IN VIVO SAFETY AND EFFICACY PROFILING TO IDENTIFY THE MOST PROMISING 2Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ3 LEAD CANDIDATES. THE ENVISAGED LEAD COMPOUNDS WILL DEMONSTRATE POTENT ANTIBIOTIC ACTIVITY AGAINST MULTIPLE GRAM-POSITIVE STRAINS, IN VITRO AND IN CELLUO TARGET ENGAGEMENT, PROMISING IN VITRO ADME-TOX PROFILE, AS WELL AS FAVORABLE IN VIVO PK AND PHARMACODYNAMICS (PD) PROPERTIES.

description: IN SUPPORT OF THE MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL EFFORT TO CHARACTERIZE T CELL EPITOPES OF FUNGI, IOGENETICS WILL APPLY ITS EIGENBIO IMMUNOINFORMATICS PLATFORM TO PROVIDE DETAILED EPITOPE MAPS AND RANKINGS. THIS WILL BE DONE IN TWO WAYS. FIRST A GROUP OF "FAST TRACK" PROTEINS HAS BEEN SELECTED BY THE MYCOLOGISTS IN EACH PARTICIPATING UNIVERSITY . FOR THESE PROTEINS IOGENETICS WILL PROCEED DIRECTLY TO GENERATE DETAILED IMMUNOME MAPS AND TO IDENTIFY PROBABLE T CELL EPITOPES THAT WILL BE RESTRICTED BY MHC II OF THE DR1*0401 ALLELE AS WELL AS FOR A SERIES OF OTHER HUMAN MHC 1 1 ALLELES. SECONDLY A RATIONAL DOWN SELECTION APPROACH WILL BE USED TO PROVIDE AN UNBIASED APPROACH TO IDENTIFYING OTHER T CELL EPITOPES . THE TOTAL PROTEOME OF EACH OF FOUR FUNGAL SPECIES, BLASTOMYCES DERMATITIDIS, HISTOP/ASMA CAPSULATUM, COCCIDIOIDES POSADASII AND CRYPTOCOCCUS NEOFORMANS WILL BE FILTERED BASED ON EXPRESSION IN ITS PARASITIC PHASE, UPREGULATION AND PRESENCE OF OTHER FEATURES SUCH AS SURFACE EXPOSURE TO IDENTIFY PROTEINS MOST LIKELY TO CARRY RELEVANT T CELL EPITOPES. THE PROTEOMES WILL BE SCREENED TO IDENTIFY IMMUNOSTIMULATORY VS IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE PROTEINS. BASE DON THIS A SET OF 100-200 PROTEINS WILL BE SELECTED FOR EACH FUNGUS AND SUBJECT TO THE DETAILED MAPPING DESCRIBED FOR THE FAST TRACK GROUP. IN BOTH CASES THE GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY EXTENDED EPITOPE RICH PEPTIDES WHICH CAN BE EVALUATED AND VALIDATED IN MICE, HUMAN PATIENTS AND IN VITRO. IOGENETICS EFFORTS WILL BE MOST INTENSE IN THE FIRST TWO YEARS OF THE PROJECT FOLLOWED BY ONGOING ANALYSIS OF RESULTS AND TROUBLE SHOOTING DURING THE OUT YEARS OF THE PROJECT.

description: FOR EACH VIRAL FAMILY, JCVI WILL DEFINE SETS OF HIGHLY- AND MODERATELY-CONSERVED REGIONS FOR EACH PROTEIN AND TAXONOMIC GROUP, PARSED INTO CONSERVED 9-MER, 10-MER, AND 15-MER PEPTIDES. ACCORDINGLY, TO BIOINFORMATICALLY CHARACTERIZE THE SEQUENCE CONSERVATION OF IDENTIFIED EPITOPES ACROSS DIFFERENT VIRAL VARIANTS AND DIFFERENT VIRAL SPECIES DERIVED FROM EACH OF THE VIRAL FAMILIES OF CONCERN, WE WILL: 1. USE THE CD-HIT ALGORITHM TO CONTROL FOR THE IMPACT OF SAMPLING BIAS ON ESTIMATES, ENABLING US TO BOTH PROVIDE EFFECTIVE COVERAGE AND OPTIMAL T CELL INDUCTION, WHILE AT THE SAME TIME ALLOWING US TO ANTICIPATE THE NEXT OUTBREAK THAT COULD EMERGE FROM OTHER SOURCE SPECIES. 2. DOWNLOAD SEQUENCES FOR EACH OF THE PROTEINS FROM DIFFERENT VIRAL ISOLATES FROM THE BV-BRC DATABASE. SEQUENCES WILL BE PROCESSED USING CD-HIT AT DIFFERENT SIMILARITY THRESHOLDS. 3. EVALUATE THE RESULTING SEQUENCE SETS BY PHYLOGENETIC ANALYSIS TO SELECT THE OPTIMAL SEQUENCE SIMILARITY THRESHOLD THAT PROVIDES FOR EQUAL REPRESENTATION OF SEQUENCES WITH LONG AND SHORT BRANCH LENGTHS. 4. PRODUCE A COLLECTION OF SEQUENCES FOR EACH OF THE PROTEINS AND TAXONOMIC GROUPS THAT EQUALLY REPRESENTS THE SEQUENCE DIVERSITY OF THE GROUP. 5. UTILIZE MUSCLE TO ALIGN PROTEIN SEQUENCES FROM EACH COLLECTION. 6. CALCULATE THE EXTENT OF SEQUENCE CONSERVATION/VARIATION AT EACH ALIGNED POSITION USING THREE METRICS: PERCENT IDENTITY TO THE CONSENSUS RESIDUE, AVERAGE BLOSUM SCORE IN COMPARISON WITH THE CONSENSUS RESIDUE, AND ENTROPY SCORE. 7. IDENTIFY PROTEIN REGIONS OF CONSERVATION USING THE MEDIAN VALUE OF EACH OF THESE METRICS IN A SLIDING WINDOW OF 10 RESIDUES. 8. EVALUATE THE DISTRIBUTIONS OF EACH METRIC TO ESTABLISH CUTOFFS FOR DEFINING REGIONS WITH HIGH AND MODERATE SEQUENCE CONSERVATION FOR EACH OF THE PROTEIN AND TAXONOMIC GROUPS, AND THE RESULTS COMBINED TO DERIVE A CONSENSUS CONSERVATION SCORE. IF THE APPROACH FOR SELECTING CONSERVATION SCORE CUTOFFS PRODUCES TOO MANY OR TOO FEW CANDIDATE REGIONS, WE WILL MANUALLY ADJUST THE CONSERVATION SCORE CUTOFFS TO PRODUCE A REASONABLE NUMBER OF CANDIDATE EPITOPES/REGIONS. 9. DERIVE CONSENSUS REGION/SEQUENCE FOR EACH GROUP, AND THEN PARSE EACH INTO 9-MER, 10-MER, AND 15-MER PEPTIDES. 10. PREPARE REPORTS REGARDING THE SEQUENCE CONSERVATION ANALYSIS FOR SUBMISSION TO NIH. 11. CONTRIBUTE TO MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION DESCRIBING THE ANALYSIS FOR SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATION IN PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS. 12. PARTICIPATE IN ANNUAL SCIENTIFIC REVIEW MEETINGS AS NEEDED.

description: THE COLOGNE TEAM WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE FOLLOWINGS PROJECT GOALS. NUMBERINGS REFER TO THE PROPOSAL. AIM 1.1 SELECTION OF VACCINE STRAINS (Ã…Ï¿½UKSZA, LÃƑÂ¤SSIG, LEWIS). WE SELECT REPRESENTATIVE STRAIN PAIRS FOR MOUSE VACCINATION EXPERIMENTS IN THE TIME INTERVAL 2014-2022 BY THE FOLLOWING CRITERIA: (A) THE CORRESPONDING CLADES OF THE STRAINS ARE CLEARLY SEPARATED ON THE STRAIN PHYLOGENETIC TREE (RELEVANT HA AMINO ACID DISTANCES ARE IN THE RANGE 1 - 3%) AND HAVE COMPLEMENTARY CROSS-PROTECTION PROFILES. (B) THE STRAINS OF EACH PAIR CIRCULATE SIMULTANEOUSLY AT SUBSTANTIAL POPULATION FREQUENCY. (C) THE PAIRS COVER A RANGE OF ANTIGENIC DISTANCES, AS COMPUTED FROM AVAILABLE FERRET ANTIGENIC DATA. IN SOME CASES, THE ANTIGENIC DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE STRAINS ARISES FROM A SINGLE EPITOPE MUTATION; THIS TYPE OF ANTIGENIC DIFFERENCES HAS PREVIOUSLY BEEN STUDIED. THE COMPREHENSIVE FERRET ANTIGENIC DATA THAT WILL INFORM OUR STRAIN SELECTION IS GENERATED AT THE WORLDWIDE INFLUENZA CENTRE, LONDON (A WHO COLLABORATING CENTRE), AND WILL BE PROVIDED BY NICOLA LEWIS. AIM 2.2 IMMUNE REPERTOIRE ANALYSIS (KLEIN). AT THE LAB OF FLORIAN KLEIN, WE WILL PERFORM SINGLE B CELL RECEPTOR ANALYSES, TO IDENTIFY BCRS REPERTOIRES SPECIFIC TO EACH OF THE ANTIGENS AND THEN TRACK THEIR DISTRIBUTION TO TRACK THEIR DYNAMICS IN THE DUAL VACCINATION SCENARIO. WE WILL BUILD ON OUR EXPERIENCE IN ISOLATING ANTIGEN SPECIFIC B CELLS AGAINST NUMEROUS DIFFERENT PATHOGENS FROM HUMAN AS WELL AS HUMANIZED MICE AND ADAPT OUR HIGH-THROUGHPUT B CELL RECEPTOR CLONING PROTOCOLS TO INFLUENZA-SPECIFIC MURINE REPERTOIRES. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL PURIFY B CELLS FROM POOLED SPLENOCYTES OF THE 10 MICE IN EACH VACCINATION GROUP AND SEPARATE SINGLE B CELLS REACTIVE TO ONE OR BOTH IMMUNIZING ANTIGENS BY MULTICOLOR FLUORESCENCE-ACTIVATED CELL SORTING (FACS) INTO MULTI-WELL PLATES. AGE AND SEX MATCHED ANTIGEN-NAÃƑÂ¯VE MICE WILL BE USED AS NEGATIVE CONTROLS. ABOUT 500 TO 600 INFLUENZA-REACTIVE B CELL RECEPTORS PER GROUP WILL BE AMPLIFIED WITH MOUSE SPECIFIC V GENE PRIMERS AND ANALYZED BY SANGER OR ILLUMINA-BASED NEXT GENERATION SEQUENCING TO BUILD GROUP-SPECIFIC BCR REPERTOIRES. AIM 2.3 DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELLING (Ã…Ï¿½UKSZA, LÃƑÂ¤SSIG). WE WILL USE BIOPHYSICAL MODELS AND MACHINE LEARNING TO PREDICT GENERIC COMBINATION TITERS GIVEN STANDARD (MONOVALENT) TITER DATA. THESE MODELS WILL BE INFORMED BY THE NEUTRALIZATION AND IMMUNE REPERTOIRE DATA GAINED IN AIMS 2.1 AND 2.2. HERE WE ASSUME THAT THE POTENCY DROPS CAN BE COMPUTED IN UNIVERSAL FORM FROM A SUITABLY DEFINED ANTIGENIC DISTANCE, WHICH, IN TURN, IS GIVEN IN TERMS OF TITER DATA. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL USE THE DATA TO DEVELOP MODELS OF IMMUNE ACTIVATION AND AFFINITY MATURATION UNDER SIMULTANEOUS PRESSURE FROM TWO ANTIGENS, USING EVOLUTIONARY RESOURCE-CONSTRAINT MODELS. TOGETHER WITH THE EXPERIMENTAL AND SEQUENCING ANALYSIS, THIS WILL IDENTIFY ORIGIN AND EXPECTED CONDITIONS OF INTERFERENCE EFFECTS FOR SIMULTANEOUS AND SEQUENTIAL IMMUNIZATION. AIM 3.1. MODEL-BASED ANALYSIS (Ã…Ï¿½UKSZA, LÃƑÂ¤SSIG). WE WILL EVALUATE COMPUTATIONAL CROSS-PROTECTION LANDSCAPES FOR ALL COMBINATIONS OF RELEVANT CANDIDATE VACCINE STRAINS. WE WILL COMBINE THESE LANDSCAPES WITH PREDICTIVE ANALYSIS OF VIRAL EVOLUTION BASED ON ESTABLISHED ANTIGENIC FITNESS MODELS. THIS ANALYSIS WILL RANK COMBINATION VACCINE CANDIDATES BY EXPECTED MEAN PROTECTION AGAINST THE NEXT-YEAR VIRAL POPULATION. AIM 3.2 VALIDATION (GARCÃƑÂ­A-SASTRE, LEWIS, Ã…Ï¿½UKSZA, LÃƑÂ¤SSIG). TO TEST MODEL PREDICTIONS FOR PRO-ACTIVE VACCINE SELECTION, WE WILL CHOOSE A NEW SET OF VACCINE STRAIN PAIRS WITH CROSS-IMMUNITY AGAINST CURRENTLY CIRCULATING STRAINS, FOR WHICH THE EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOL DESCRIBED UNDER AIM 1.1 IS REPEATED. MODEL PREDICTIONS FOR THE PROTECTION OF COMBINATION VACCINES WILL BE COMPARED TO THE OBSERVED PROTECTION, AS MEASURED WITH THE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY TITERS AGAINST THE PANEL OF TEST VIRUSES.

description: THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY T-CELL EPITOPES OF PATHOGENIC FUNGI INCLUDING SPECIES IN THE GENERA OF BLASTOMYCES, COCCIDIOIDES, CRYPTOCOCCUS, AND HISTOPLAMA. THE SUBCONTRACT SITE AT UTSA WILL CONDUCT THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS FOR THE IDENTIFICATION AND CONFIRMATION OF COCCIDIOIDES T CELL EPITOPES. THE NEWLY IDENTIFIED T-CELL EPITOPES CAN BE USED IN AN ARRAY OF BASIC IMMUNOLOGICAL RESEARCH TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE FUNGUS-HOST INTERACTION AS WELL AS TRANSLATIONAL APPLICATIONS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF VACCINES AND DIAGNOSTIC REAGENTS FOR COCCIDIOIDES INFECTION. DR. HUNG WILL DIRECT ALL EXPERIMENTS AT UTSA AND COLLABORATE WITH DR. STU LEVITZ AND OTHER COLLABORATORS ON THIS PROJECT TO COMPLETE THE FOLLOWING TASKS: 1. COMPILE A SET OF FAST TRACK PROTEINS THAT HAVE BEEN PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED AND EVALUATED AS COCCIDIOIDES ANTIGENS FOR VACCINE AND SEROLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS. 2. ASSIST IN THE DOWN SELECTION OF COCCIDIOIDES ANTIGENS AND POTENTIAL T-CELL EPITOPES THAT ARE PREDICTED BY BIOINFORMATICS ANALYSIS. 3. CONDUCT T-CELL ACTIVATION ASSAYS TO EVALUATE IMMUNOREACTIVITY OF THE PREDICTED T-CELL EPITOPES FROM THE NEWLY PREDICTED EPITOPES USING HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGEN (HLA-DR4) TRANSGENIC MICE THAT ARE VACCINATED WITH THE FAST TRACK OR NEWLY IDENTIFIED COCCIDIOIDES ANTIGENS. 4. HUNG'S LABORATORY WILL PREPARE SAMPLES FOR EVALUATION CD4+ T CELLS RESPONSE OF THE VACCINATED AND CONTROL MICE. SAMPLES WILL BE SHIPPED TO UMMS FOR CYTOKINE ASSAYS INCLUDING TH1 AND TH17 RESPONSES WILL BE USED TO DELINEATE THE PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY ELICITED BY THE VACCINE. 5. HUNG'S LABORATORY WILL PREPARE HUMAN PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTIC CELLS (PBMCS) FROM BLOOD SAMPLES DONATED BY PATIENTS WHO HAVE RECOVERED FROM PULMONARY COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS. DR. NEIL AMPEL WILL COLLECT THOSE BLOOD SAMPLES AND SHIP THEM TO HUNG'S LABORATORY. EACH PREDICTED EPITOPES WILL BE INCUBATED WITH HUMAN PBMCS SEPARATELY TO STIMULATE T-CELL RESPONSE. THE CULTURE SUPERNATANTS WILL BE COLLECTED FOR CYTOKINE ASSAYS. 6. HUNG WILL COMMUNICATE WITH DR. STUART LEVITZ AND OTHER COLLABORATORS IN THIS PROJECT. HUNG'S LABORATORY WILL ALSO ASSIST IN ANALYZING DATA AND WRITING SCIENTIFIC REPORTS. 7. THE NEWLY IDENTIFIED AND CONFIRMED HUMAN T-CELL EPITOPES OF COCCIDIOIDES WILL BE DEPOSITED INTO IEDB EPITOPE DATABASED FOR SHARING WITH THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY.

description: DR. TIROUVANZIAM AND HIS LABORATORY AT EMORY UNIVERSITY COMMITS TO PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR THE FDA GRANT DIRECTED BY DR. SHUICHI TAKAYAMA (THE GEORGIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY AND EMORY UNIVERISTY, ATLANTA, GEORGIA, USA), ENTITLED: Ã¢Â‚¬Å“IN VITRO ASSESSMENT OF CHEMICAL MIXTURE- INDUCED AIRWAY INFLAMMAAON IN HEALTHY AND DISEASED LUNGSÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½. THIS PROJECT WILL USE A HIGH-THROUGHPUT IN VITRO AIR-BLOOD BARRIER ARRAY BASED BARRIER BREAKDOWN AND NEUTROPHIL TRANSMIGRATION/ACTIVATION ASSAY TO PREDICT HUMAN ADVERSE REACTIONS TO INHALED SUBSTANCES. DOSE RESPONSE CURVES AND BENCHMARK DOSES (BMD) WILL BE DETERMINED FOR A RANGE OF WELL-KNOWN AND UNKNOWN SUBSTANCES INCLUDING ELECTRONIC NICOTINE DELIVERY SYSTEMS (ENDS) CONSTITUENTS AND MIXTURES. INITIAL YEARS WILL FOCUS ON HIGH-THROUGHPUT E-CIGARETTE VAPOR EXTRACTS (EVE) ANALYSIS, LATER YEARS WILL ALSO ANALYZE E-CIGARETTE AEROSOL DIRECTLY IN A LOWER-THROUGHPUT FORMAT. THE ORGAN-LEVEL FUNCTIONAL READOUTS (TEER & TRANSMIGRATION) RELATE CLOSELY TO CLINICAL/PRE-CLINICAL BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) MEASURES, ARE CONVENIENT IN CONSISTING OF JUST A FEW KEY NUMBERS, YET ARE INTEGRATIVE OF MULTIPLE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR PATHWAYS AND THUS HIGHLY PHYSIOLOGICALLY-RELEVANT. THIS PROJECT WILL ANALYZE THE EFFECT OF BIOLOGICALLY VARIABILITY WITH REGARDS TO THE SEX OF THE PRIMARY HUMAN NEUTROPHILS AND EPITHELIAL CELLS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ANALYZE THE IMPACT VAPING PLUS OTHER LUNG INSULTS CAN HAVE WHEN COMBINED TOGETHER BY TESTING EVES IN COMBINATION WITH DEFINED INFLAMMATORY COCKTAILS REFERRED TO AS SYNTHETIC AIRWAY FLUID SUPERNATANT (SASN) (EARLY YEARS) OR COPD ASN (LATER YEARS). SUPPORT PROVIDED BY THE TIROUVANZIAM LAB AT ERMORY WILL BE IN THE FORM OF: (I) SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PRIMARY MODEL; (II) PERFORMANCE OF PHENOTYPIC AND FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS; (III) SUPPORT FOR DATA ANALYSIS AND INTEGRATION; AND (IV) REPORTING OF RESULTS AND CONTRIBUTION TO SCIENTIFIC ABSTRACTS AND MANUSCRIPTS. THE TIROUVANZIAM LAB IS PARTICULARLY WELL EQUIPPED FOR SUCH STUDIES AND HAS UNIQUE EXPERTISE IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF IN VITRO ASSAYS RELATED TO AIRWAY NEUTROPHLIC INFLAMMATION, AS EVIDENCED BY PRIOR PUBLICATIONS RELEVANT TO THIS TOPIC. TO ENSURE PROPER IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EXTENSIVE WORK INCLUDED IN THIS STATEMENT, DR. TIROUVANZIAM WILL COMMIT 10% OF HIS EFFORT, 10% OF EFFORT FOR A POSTDOCTORAL BIOINFORMATICIAN AND 20% FOR A RESEARCH SPECIALIST SUPERVISOR IN EACH OF YRS 1-3 OF THIS PROJECT.

description: THE WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY GROUP (WSU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GARRY BUCHKO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENTS. WSU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST ONE NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS YEAR OF THE CONTRACT (SEPT 1, 2024 THROUGH AUG 31, 2025), WHICH MAY SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR). WSU MAY ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR) FOR PROJECTS OF SPECIAL INTEREST TO THE CENTER OR THROUGH COMMUNITY REQUESTS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY NMR: WSU (DR. BUCHKO) WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST ONE PROTEIN USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE, AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE SEATTLE CHILDRENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY WSU. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND SIDE CHAIN 1H, 13C, AND 15N RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C, AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION, AND REPORTING: WSU WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. WSU WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS, AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUESTED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. THE MAJOR AIM OF THE PROJECT WORK WILL BE IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR (SEPT 1, 2024 THROUGH AUG 31, 2025). UW-CRYOEM MAY ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) AND WILL SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. B. PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS: UW-CRYOEM WILL LEAD A STUDY ON THE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF STABILIZED NIPAH VIRUS ATTACHMENT AND FUSION GLYCOPROTEINS. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-CRYOEM WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FOMR UW-CRYOEM WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. PROTEIN FOLDING, AGGREGATION, AND/OR STABILITY) OF THE PURIFIED SAMPLES TO ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORTS. KEY UW-PPG STAFF WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. UW-PPG WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. description: SCOPE OF WORK - VUMC THE OVERALL PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING 4 TASKS: DESIGN A MULTI-SITE STUDY OF INFLUENZA TRANSMISSION WITHIN HOUSEHOLDS, ENROLL ELIGIBLE HOUSEHOLDS AND CONDUCT PROSPECTIVE STUDY ACTIVITIES, CONDUCT LABORATORY STUDIES TO CHARACTERIZE SUSCEPTIBILITY AND INFECTION, AND, PROVIDE DATA MANAGEMENT FOR SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND ANALYSES. TO ACCOMPLISH THE PROJECTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S OBJECTIVES, OUR VUMC SITE WILL ENROLL AND FOLLOW APPROXIMATELY 150 HOUSEHOLDS. VUMC WILL SERVE AS A SUBCONTRACTOR TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY AND WILL SERVE AS THE DATA COORDINATING CENTER (DCC) AND CENTRAL VIRAL LABORATORY FOR THE NETWORK. TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT IDENTIFICATION OF INDEX CASES, REGARDLESS OF PRESENCE OF SYMPTOMS AND RAPID ENROLMENT AND COMPLETE FOLLOW-UP OF INDEX CASES AND HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS, WE WILL IMPLEMENT A MODIFIED CASE-ASCERTAINED STUDY DESIGN. WE WILL USE ESTABLISHED HIGH-THROUGHPUT STATE-OF-THE-ART TESTING PLATFORMS TO ACCURATELY IDENTIFY INFLUENZA INFECTIONS AND APPLY A DETAILED ALGORITHM TO DETERMINE AND VERIFY VACCINATION HISTORY. IN ADDITION, WE WILL IMPLEMENT AN INTEGRATED DATA SYSTEM FOR COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF ALL STUDY ELEMENTS, THAT ENSURES REAL-TIME DATA SHARING.

description: THE UM TEAM WILL PROVIDE RESEARCH AND EVALUATION EXPERTISE TO THE STUDY INVESTIGATORS AND OTHER PROJECT STAFF MEMBERS. THE UM STAFF WILL ATTEND ALL WEEKLY STAFF MEETINGS AND REQUIRED MEETINGS/TRAININGS WITH THE CDC. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL REVIEW AND ASSIST WITH ALL DATA COLLECTION ACTIVITIES AND ALL RELATED RESEARCH TASKS, INCLUDING ASSISTING IN THE ANALYSIS OF THE DATA SETS RELATING TO CARDIAC AND CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH AND PREPARING MANUSCRIPTS RELATED TO THESE MEASURES. THEY WILL ENSURE THAT ALL STAFF MEMBERS AND PERTINENT PARTNERS WHO ADMINISTER INSTRUMENTS FOLLOW ALL CITI HUMAN SUBJECTS PROTOCOLS, WHICH INCLUDE ELEMENTS OF SUBJECT PROTECTION, INCLUDING THE HISTORY, ETHICS, AND RULES REGARDING PROTECTING SUBJECTS. ALSO, ENSURE THAT PERSONNEL FOLLOW ALL CONFIDENTIALITY PRACTICES. THEY WILL ASSIST WITH ALL LEVELS OF RECRUITMENT AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, STRATEGIC PLANNING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND PARTNER ENGAGEMENT. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH ALL STAFF TO MONITOR ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDING RECRUITMENT EFFORTS, DATA COLLECTION, PATIENT FOLLOW-UP, AND THAT INCENTIVES ARE PROVIDED IN THE FORM OF GIFT CARDS AND MEDICAL REPORTS. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL ASSIST WITH FOLLOWING ALL PROJECT TIMELINES AND ENSURING THAT PARTICIPANTS ARE CONTACTED FOR ALL FOLLOW-UP ASSESSMENTS AND APPOINTMENTS. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH ALL PROJECT STAFF TO DISCUSS REPORTING FORMS AND DASHBOARDS, RECRUITMENT, SURVEY ADMINISTRATION, DATA COLLECTION, MEDICAL APPTS FOR PARTICIPANTS IN THE PHENOTYPING STUDY, AND OTHER IMPORTANT PROJECT ELEMENTS. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL ASSIST IN THE MANAGEMENT OF DATA COLLECTED BY PROJECT STAFF TO REPORT ON THE REQUIRED PERFORMANCE MEASURES, INCLUDING OBJECTIVES. PROVIDE ONGOING FEEDBACK AND REPORTS TO THE PROJECT STAFF AND STAKEHOLDERS ON PRELIMINARY OUTCOMES. CONTINUALLY REVIEW PROGRAM GOALS ON NUMBERS SERVED, COMPLETION RATES, AND BARRIERS TO PROGRAMMING BY ANALYZING REPORTS AND CONDUCTING MEETINGS WITH STAFF. CONTACT PROJECT STAFF WEEKLY REGARDING ALL ASPECTS OF THE PROGRAM TO COLLECT AND REVIEW NEW PROCESS DATA, DISCUSS THE REVIEW OF THE PROCESS AND OUTCOME DATA FROM PREVIOUS WEEKS, AND REVIEW THE PROGRAM STATED GOALS AND OBJECTIVES TO SEE IF THEY ARE BEING MET OR IF PROGRAM ADJUSTMENTS ARE NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE THOSE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. CONDUCT SITE VISITS AND MEETINGS WITH ALL PARTNERS AS PART OF THE MANAGEMENT OF THE PROJECT. ENSURE PROJECT STAFF REVIEW AND PROVIDE ALL MEDICAL REPORTS TO THE PARTICIPANTS AS PART OF THEIR INCENTIVE PACKAGE. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL ASSIST IN MAKING SURE REPORTS ARE SENT IN A TIMELY FASHION. ENTER OUTCOME AND PROCESS DATA INTO ALL PROJECT DASHBOARDS. REVIEW DASHBOARDS REGULARLY TO MONITOR ALL PROJECT-RELATED ACTIVITIES. PERFORM REGULAR DATA CHECKS AND TRANSFER THE DATA TO SPSS TO PERFORM DATA ANALYSIS. REPORT SEMIANNUAL AND ANNUAL FINDINGS ON PROGRAM GOALS, OBJECTIVES, AND OUTCOMES. USE PERFORMANCE MEASURE DATA TO MAKE CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS. AS MENTIONED, EVALUATE THE IMPLEMENTATION AND OUTCOMES OF PROGRAM ACTIVITIES. PROVIDE INPUT TO THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS SUBMITTED TO THE CDC AND PERFORM A QUARTERLY REVIEW OF DATA TO ASSESS FOR QUALITY AND INTERIM ANALYSES. CONTINUALLY LOOK FOR MEANS OF COMMUNICATING PROJECT ACTIVITIES, PERFORMANCE, ACHIEVEMENTS, AND LIMITATIONS TO THE MEDICAL, HUMAN SERVICE, AND RESEARCH FIELDS THROUGH PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS, LOCAL AND NATIONAL PRESENTATIONS AND PUBLICATIONS, PUBLIC FORUMS, SOCIAL MEDIA, ETC. DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A SUSTAINABILITY PLAN TO ENSURE THE CONTINUATION OF PROGRAM EFFORTS BEYOND THE GRANT.

description: DR. ROBERT SMITH AND COLLEAGUES AT MAINEHEALTH AND MAINEHEALTH INSTITUTE FOR RESEARCH WILL IDENTIFY PATIENTS WITH LYME DISEASE IN THE MAINEHEALTH SYSTEM THROUGH REGULARLY SCHEDULED ELECTRONIC MEDICAL HEALTH RECORD (EPIC) SCANS AND EXTRACT CLINICAL INFORMATION TO PROVIDE DEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½IDENTIFIED DETAILS OF DISEASE TO A COMBINED DATA BASE IN CONCERT WITH A COORDINATED APPROACH AT MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL HOSPITAL (MGH) AND TUFTSMEDICINE. AGGREGATED DATA WILL BE SHARED WITH RESEARCHERS AT THE FEDERAL CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE HEALTH BURDEN AND OUTCOMES IN OF LYME DISEASE IN OUR HIGHLY ENDEMIC REGION. MAINEHEALTH INSTITUTE FOR RESEARCH INVESTIGATORS UNDER DR. SMITHÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S DIRECTION WILL WORK WITH MGH AND TUFTS TEAMS TO CREATE A UNIFIED AND EFFECTIVE CASE DEFINITION FOR IDENTIFYING PATIENTS WITH LYME DISEASE. DR. SMITH, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF INFECTIOUS DISEASE COLLEAGUE DR. STEPHEN RAWLINGS, WILL ASSIST A TRAINED CLINICAL STUDY COORDINATOR IN CASE IDENTIFICATION AND DATA EXTRACTION. DR. SUSAN ELIAS WILL OVERSEE DATA MANAGEMENT AT THE MHIR SITE AND COÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ORDINATE WITH THE TEAMS AT MGH AND TUFTSMEDICINE TO ASSURE STANDARDIZATION. THE FIRST YEAR OF WORK WILL INVOLVE COORDINATED (MGH, TUFTS, MAINEHEALTH) MODEL DEVELOPMENT, VALIDATION, AND DEPLOYMENT AS DESCRIBED IN THE FULL PROPOSAL. WE WILL FIRST CREATE A BASELINE MODEL OF SUBJECTS WHO ARE DIAGNOSED AS HAVING LYME DISEASE BY ICD9/10 CODES. WE WILL THEN WORK TO DERIVE IMPROVED MODELS BY IDENTIFYING INFORMATIVE DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FROM CLINICAL, EPIDEMIOLOGICAL, MICROBIOLOGICAL AND FREE TEXT DATA IN CASE AND CONTROL VISITS. WE WILL COMPARE THE PERFORMANCE OF ONE OR MORE IMPROVED MODELS AND SELECT THE BEST PERFORMING ONE. WE WILL IMPLEMENT THE SELECTED MODEL FOR RECORD REVIEW AT MAINEHEALTH, SUMMARIZE THE RESULTS, AND AGGREGATE SUMMARY STATISTICS ACROSS SITES. BASED UPON A UNIFIED, EFFECTIVE CASE DEFINITION AND A ROBUST MODEL TO IDENTIFY CASES OF LYME DISEASE FROM EPIC DATA, WE WILL CONDUCT TARGETED INVESTIGATIONS TO ANSWER SPECIFIC QUESTIONS. WE WILL IDENTIFY POTENTIAL RECRUITMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR RESEARCH SUBJECTS BASED UPON SPECIFIC CRITERIA (E.G. NEUROBORRELIOSIS, PREGNANCY, IMPACT OF COÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½INFECTIONS, VACCINATION) DEFINED IN CONSULTATION WITH THE FULL INVESTIGATOR TEAM AND RELEVANT TECHNICAL TEAM AT CDC. WE WILL ENROLL A SUBSET OF THESE INDIVIDUALS IN CLINICAL STUDIES TO ADDRESS CURRENT GAPS OR NEW QUESTIONS, INCLUDING THE PERFORMANCE OF NOVEL DIAGNOSTIC ASSAYS, THE OUTCOMES OF PREGNANCY, AND VACCINE EFFICACY.

description: COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER SUBCONTRACT SCOPE OF WORK COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER WILL SERVE AS A SITE FOR THE RESPIRATORY VIRUS TRANSMISSION NETWORK (RVTN) TO STUDY HOUSEHOLD TRANSMISSION OF INFLUENZA. COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER WILL RECRUIT APPROXIMATELY 150 PARTICIPANTS WITH ACUTE INFLUENZA INFECTION AND THEIR HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS TO THE STUDY. USING STUDY MATERIALS PROVIDED BY WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY, COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER INVESTIGATORS WILL PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH SELF-COLLECTION MATERIALS, COLLECT QUESTIONNAIRE DATA, MONITOR PARTICIPANT ACTIVITES, AND RECEIVE COMPLETED SAMPLES. COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER WILL STORE SAMPLES IN THE COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER LABORATORY AS DIRECTED BY THE PROTOCOL AND SHIP SAMPLES TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY OR OTHER DESIGNATED LABORATORY. THE SITE WILL ENTER DATA IN A TIMELY FASHION INTO THE REDCAP DATABASE. DR. MELISSA STOCKWELL, PROFESSOR OF PEDIATRICS AND POPULATION AND FAMILY HEALTH, WILL BE THE SITE PI ON THE SUBAWARD. SHE WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ASSURING THAT ALL STUDY ACTIVITIES ARE CARRIED OUT AS OUTLINED IN THE PROTOCOL. SHE WILL OBTAIN AN IRB RELIANCE AGREEMENT WITH WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY AND MAINTAIN APPROVAL. SHE WILL HIRE AND OVERSEE STUDY STAFF TO CARRY OUT THE STUDY ACTIVITIES DESCRIBED ABOVE. SHE WILL ALSO SERVE ON THE STEERING COMMITTEE AS COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTERÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S REPRESENTATIVE AND MAINTAIN FREQUENT CONTACT WITH THE STUDY PI DR. KWON.

description: THE VACCINE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT TEAMS AT UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA (PI-EVANS), INIMMUNE (PI-BURKHART & MILLER), AND MOUNT SINAI (PI-KRAMMER) HAVE AN ESTABLISHED COLLABORATION FOR DEVELOPING LATE-STAGE ADJUVANTS AND FORMULATIONS WITH SUBUNIT ANTIGENS FROM INFLUENZA VIRUS (HA AND NA). THESE STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED REMARKABLE PROTECTION AGAINST CHALLENGE WITH BOTH HOMOLOGOUS AND HETEROSUBTYPIC VIRUSES FOLLOWING IM OR IN VACCINATION WITH LEAD CANDIDATE VACCINES ADVANCING TO IND WITH CIVICS. WE PROPOSE TO EXPAND THIS WORK PERFORMED UNDER CIVICS AND ADJUVANT DEVELOPMENT CONTRACTS TO DEVELOP AND ADVANCE A DURABLE CROSS-PROTECTIVE ADJUVANTED H5N1 AND H5N2 SUBUNIT VACCINES. H5 AND N1 ANTIGENS FROM RECENT RELEVANT STRAINS AND CHALLENGE MODELS ARE ALREADY DEVELOPED AND AVAILABLE AT MOUNT SINAI. ADVANCED (CGMP PRODUCED) THERMOSTABLE ADJUVANTS AND FORMULATIONS ARE AVAILABLE FROM UM AND INIMMUNE. WE PROPOSE TO EVALUATE TRAC-478 (IM), SAS (IM), AND MUCOADHESIVE, TRAC-478, SAS, INI-2004 AND INI-4001 LIPOSOMES (INTRANASAL) FOR IMMUNOGENICITY WITH H5, N1/2 AND A COMBINATION H5+N1/2 ANTIGENS. COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATION OF VACCINE SAFETY AND IMMUNOGENICITY WILL BE CONDUCTED IN MICE, INCLUDING THE EVALUATION OF HUMORAL AND CELL MEDIATED IMMUNITY AS WELL AS VACCINE DURABILITY, DOSE SPARING, AND HETEROSUBTYPIC IMMUNITY ACROSS A RANGE OF H5N1 VARIANTS. LEAD CANDIDATE VACCINES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR PROTECTION USING AN ESTABLISHED H5N1 CHALLENGE MODEL IN MICE. THE PROJECT WILL SELECT A SINGLE LEAD VACCINE CANDIDATE FOR TRANSITION TO HUMAN CLINICAL EVALUATION. PROCESS DEVELOPMENT, SCALE-UP, CGMP MANUFACTURING AND GLP TOXICOLOGY TESTING OF THE LEAD VACCINE CANDIDATE IS INCLUDED IN OPTIONAL BUDGET PERIODS (YEARS 2 AND 3). THE FUNDING WOULD PROVIDE A PHASE I READY VACCINE WITH STRONG IND ENABLING PRECLINICAL POC AND SAFETY DATA. A NOVEL VACCINE INDUCING DURABLE HETEROSUBTYPIC IMMUNITY ACROSS A BROAD RANGE OF H5N1 VARIANTS IS CRITICAL FOR PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AS STOCKPILE OF THIS VACCINE WILL REMAIN EFFECTIVE ACROSS MANY YEARS OF ANTIGENIC DRIFT.

description: THE SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED BY THE SUBCONTRACTOR ARE AS FOLLOWS: TASK 1: CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT THE PROTOCOLS AND PLANS FOR THE SUID AND SDY CASE R E G I S T R Y BIOREPOSITORY FOR DATA MANAGEMENT, COLLECTION, PROCESSING, SHIPPING, TRACKING, STORAGE, AND REDISTRIBUTION OF SPECIMENS CREATED IN THE PREVIOUS FUNDING CYCLE. THIS PLAN WILL ENSURE THAT: A. THE BIOSPECIMENS WILL BE LINKED, IN A BLINDED FASHION, TO THE SDY CASES. B. THE REPOSITORY WILL RECEIVE SAMPLES, EXTRACT DNA FROM SPECIMENS, STORE EXTRACTED DNA, AND DISTRIBUTE TO RESEARCHERS, AS REQUESTED. C. BIOSPECIMENS WILL BE SHARED WITH RESEARCHERS FUNDED THROUGH FUTURE NIH GRANT MECHANISMS. THESE BIOLOGICAL SAMPLES, WHICH WILL REMAIN LINKED TO DETAILED CLINICAL DATA, WILL CONTINUE TO SERVE AS A RESOURCE FOR LONG-TERM INVESTIGATIONS INTO THE GENETIC BASIS OF SUDDEN DEATH IN THE YOUNG. D. STORAGE OF SAMPLES AT THE REPOSITORY WILL CONTINUE UNTIL AT LEAST MAY OF 2029, WHEN THE CURRENT FUNDING CYCLE FOR THE SUDDEN DEATH IN THE YOUNG INITIATIVE ENDS. SPECIMENS WILL BE OBTAINED FROM UP TO 5,000 SUBJECTS (AND PERHAPS MORE) DURING THIS PERIOD. E. THE BIOLOGIC SPECIMEN REPOSITORY WILL BE IN COMPLIANCE WITH ALL FEDERAL AND STATE REQUIREMENTS AND CURRENT BEST PRACTICES FOR THE COLLECTION, STORAGE, RETRIEVAL AND DISTRIBUTION OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIAL FOR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH. MPHI AND UM WILL FOLLOW CURRENT BEST PRACTICES AND THE NHLBI BIOLOGIC SPECIMEN AND DATA REPOSITORY OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR ACQUIRING AND DISTRIBUTING BIOSPECIMENS.

description: THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL, MULTIVALENT MRNA VACCINE AND TO TEST IN VIVO, IN SYNGENEIC AND SPONTANEOUS TNBC MOUSE MODELS, THE VACCINEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S EFFICACY IN PREVENTING TNBC DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION. THE THREE CANDIDATE ANTIGENS ARE TOP2A, CYCLIN E2 (CCNE2) AND KIF15. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE CURRENT TASK ORDER ARE AS FOLLOWS: (1) DESIGN, SYNTHESIS, CHARACTERIZATION, AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE MONOVALENT TOP2A, CCNE2 AND KIF15 MRNA VACCINES. (2) EVALUATION OF IMMUNOGENICITY, EFFICACY, AND PRELIMINARY TOLERABILITY OF THE MONOVALENT MRNA VACCINES (INDIVIDUALLY OR GIVEN THREE TOGETHER), IN COMPARISON WITH THE RESPECTIVE PEPTIDE VACCINES IN SYNGENEIC MICE. DIFFERENT IMMUNIZATION ROUTES, DOSES AND SCHEDULES SHALL BE EVALUATED. (3) OPTIONAL TASK: UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF OBJECTIVES (1) AND (2), AND AT THE REQUEST OF THE NCI, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DESIGN, SYNTHESIZE, CHARACTERIZE, AND OPTIMIZE THE TRIVALENT MRNA VACCINE FOR TUMOR PREVENTION EFFICACY IN A SPONTANEOUS MOUSE MODEL OF TNBC.

description: THE FDA'S RISK EVALUATION AND MANAGEMENT (REMS) PROGRAM ENSURES THE SAFE USE OF HIGH-RISK MEDICATIONS BUT CURRENTLY RELIES ON MANUAL DATA ENTRY, WHICH BURDENS PATIENTS, PRESCRIBERS, AND PHARMACISTS, LEADING TO DELAYS IN ACCESSING CRITICAL MEDICATIONS. THE CODEX INITIATIVE, PART OF HL7 FHIR ACCELERATOR, AIMS TO CREATE AN INTEROPERABLE REMS ECOSYSTEM THAT STREAMLINES THESE PROCESSES. MITRE INTENDS TO PARTNER WITH INVARYANT TO IMPLEMENT A FHIR-BASED USE CASE UNDER CODEX, FOCUSING ON REDUCING REMS-RELATED ADMINISTRATIVE BURDENS. INVARYANT'S ROLE WILL INCLUDE COORDINATING THE INTEGRATION USE CASE, TESTING STANDARDS IN REAL-WORLD SETTINGS, AND SUPPORTING POST-STUDY ACTIVITIES, WITH THE GOAL OF UPDATING THE HL7 IMPLEMENTATION GUIDE BY MAY 2025.

NOTE, BASED UPON APPROVAL BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER (CO), THE CONTRACTOR WILL IDENTIFY CERTAIN DELIVERABLES APPROPRIATE FOR EXTERNAL- RELEASE AND PURSUE THE RELEVANT PROCEDURES, TO MAKE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE HIGH-IMPACT PRODUCTS FOR KEY STAKEHOLDERS. ANY AND ALL CONTRACTUAL CHANGES SHALL BE PRESENTED TO BRYCETECH FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL PRIOR TO THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ANY CONTRACTUAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS. 5.1 ENVIRONMENTAL LANDSCAPE ANALYSIS OF CURRENT INDUSTRY CAPACITIES AND SPEND RESERVED 5.2 STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT - THE CONTRACTOR IS THE LEAD FOR THIS TASK THE STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT TASK FOCUSES ON TWO MAJOR TYPES OF STAKEHOLDERS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ GOVERNMENT AND INDUSTRY Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ AND HAS TWO MAJOR SUBTASKS THAT ARE DESCRIBED BELOW. 5.2.1 GOVERNMENT STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BUILD AND MAINTAIN RELATIONSHIPS WITH DIFFERENT GROUPS (E.G., COMMERCE - INTERNATIONAL TRADE ADMINISTRATION AND BUREAU OF SECURITY AND INDUSTRY, INTERNATIONAL TRADE COMMISSION, WHITE HOUSE - US TRADE REPRESENTATIVE, INNOVATIVE STARTUPS, ETC.) TO UNDERSTAND AND RESPOND TO PHIB SUPPLY CHAIN AND DISTRIBUTION CHALLENGES. THE CONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP A THOROUGH UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLES, RESPONSIBILITIES, AND VARIOUS TOOLS THAT THE STAKEHOLDERS HAVE AND COULD UTILIZE TO HELP ADDRESS THE PHIB CHALLENGES. ACTIVITIES MAY INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: 5.2.1.1 ESTABLISHING A REGULAR COMMUNICATION MECHANISM FOR IBMSC TO COMMUNICATE WITH INTERAGENCY PARTNERS THAT SUPPORT PHIB CAPACITY. 5.2.1.2 IDENTIFYING, CHARACTERIZING, AND PRIORITIZING POTENTIAL GOVERNMENT AND NON-GOVERNMENT PROGRAMS AND FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES (E.G., SBIR) TO SUPPORT PHIB CAPACITY SUSTAINMENT AND DEVELOPMENT. 5.2.1.3 EXPLORING THE POSSIBILITY OF CREATING A PUBLIC/PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP (PPP) TO SUPPORT PHIB CAPACITY SUSTAINMENT, NEW TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION, AND THREAT REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT. 5.2.1.4 CREATING AN ONLINE WEB PRESENCE THAT FACILITATES STAKEHOLDER COMMUNICATIONS AND DISSEMINATION OF KEY PROGRAM INFORMATION. 5.2.2 INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BUILD AND MAINTAIN RELATIONSHIPS WITH MANUFACTURERS AND UPSTREAM SUPPLIERS; ROUTINELY COLLECT PROPRIETARY DATA FROM MANUFACTURERS TO UNDERSTAND THE PHIB LANDSCAPE AND TO INFORM IBMSC STRATEGIC PLAN. description: STATEMENT OF WORK OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO QUANTIFY THE RISK OF PATHOGEN TRANSFER TO ENVIRONMENTS AND PATIENTS ASSOCIATED WITH DIFFERENT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT USES FOR HEALTHCARE WORKERS. WE WILL DEVELOP A MATHEMATICAL MODEL TO EXTRAPOLATE THE RISK OF PATHOGEN TRANSFER DURING MULTIPLE CONTAMINATION EVENTS. WE WILL PARAMETERIZE THE MODEL WITH THE DATA COLLECTED ON DURING THE OBSERVATIONAL PERIODS (4H) IN THE EXTENT PPE STUDY. SIMULATION SCENARIOS SUMMARIZING THE RISK OF PATHOGEN TRANSFER AND PATIENT/HEALTHCARE WORKER EXPOSURE FOR ONE OR MULTIPLE SHIFTS, AND WARD-LEVEL CONTAMINATION WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AND ANALYZED. ASSOCIATED TASKS: 1. DEVELOP A MATHEMATICAL MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE THE ACCUMULATIVE RISK OF CONTAMINATION ASSOCIATED TO A SET OF EVENTS (E.G. DONNING, HAND WASHING CONTACT WITH ROOM SURFACES, CONTACT WITH OUTSIDE ROOM SURFACES, DOFFING). WE WILL COMPARE TWO COMMONLY APPROACHES TO ADDRESS FOMITE-MEDIATED TRANSMISSION: DISCRETE EVENT-BASED SIMULATION AND DISCRETE MARKOV CHAIN MODELS. 2. PARAMETERIZE THE MATHEMATICAL MODEL WITH THE COLLECTED DATA ON SEQUENCE OF EVENTS AND PROBABILITIES OF CONTAMINATION OBSERVED DURING OBSERVATIONAL PERIODS. 3. VERIFY AND VALIDATE THE MODEL WITH A SUBSET OF THE AVAILABLE DATA 4. PERFORM SIMULATIONS TO REPRESENT SCENARIOS OF INTEREST (E.G. RISK OF CONTAMINATION FOLLOWING A COMPLETE SHIFT). 5. SUMMARIZE RESULTS FOR PUBLICATION AND FINAL REPORT TIMELINE: YEAR 2 (09/23 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ 8/24): MODEL DEVELOPMENT AND PARTIAL PARAMETERIZATION AND ANALYSIS (TASKS 1- 2) YEAR (9/24-8/25): COMPLETE PARAMETERIZATION, VALIDATION AND SCENARIO SIMULATION (TASKS 2-5) EXCERPT FROM IRB STUDY PROTOCOL: "IN ORDER TO EXPAND THE SCOPE OF THE STUDY FINDINGS, WE WILL UTILIZE MATHEMATICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING STRATEGIES TO PROJECT THE FINDINGS OF THE STUDY, WHICH SIMULATE SELFCONTAMINATION AND DOWNSTREAM ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINATION ATTRIBUTABLE TO A SINGLE CONTAMINATION, TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF MULTIPLE SEQUENTIAL CONTAMINATION EVENTS THAT MIGHT OCCUR DURING A HEALTHCARE SHIFT. THE MODELING ANALYSIS WILL BE LED BY DR. CRISTINA LANZAS, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF POPULATION HEALTH AND PATHOBIOLOGY AT NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY. DE-IDENTIFIED DATA FROM THE STUDY WILL BE SHARED WITH DR. LANZAS IN ORDER TO INFORM THE MODELING ANALYSIS. THIS DATA WILL INCLUDE DATE/TIME STAMPS FROM THE STUDY OBSERVATIONS; HOWEVER, PARTICIPANTS WILL BE IDENTIFIED ONLY BY THEIR STUDY ID NUMBER. DR. LANZAS AND HER TEAM WILL NOT HAVE ACCESS TO PARTICIPANT NAMES OR OTHER IDENTIFYING INFORMATION.

THE SPECIFIC LIST OF SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED ON AN ONGOING BASIS, BASED ON INDIVIDUAL REQUESTS FOR SERVICES ARE DETAILED BELOW: I. IV. IFA OR IHC STAINING OF PREPARED OR SUBMITTED SLIDES. METHODS TO BE FOLLOWED WILL BE DETAILED IN THE INDIVIDUAL REQUESTS AND MAY INVOLVE EITHER AUTOMATED STAINING USING THE BOND RX OR BENCHTOP METHODS.

description: THE NATIONAL COUNCIL FOR MENTAL WELLBEING IS DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING SMI TTAC STARTING ON SEPTEMBER 10, 2024. SMI TTAC WILL EXIST TO SERVE THOSE INVOLVED IN THE OVERSIGHT AND DELIVERY OF MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI). IN ADDITION, THE TTAC WILL OFFER PERSONALIZED INTENSIVE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (PITA) TO AID IN THE TREATMENT AND RECOVERY OF INDIVIDUALS WITH SMI, AS WELL AS YOUTHS AGED 10 AND OLDER WHO ARE EXPERIENCING A FIRST EPISODE PSYCHOSIS (FEP). WITHIN SMI TTAC, APA WILL SUPPORT SEVERAL ACTIVITIES ACROSS THE PROJECT'S CORE TASK ORDERS, ESPECIALLY THOSE RELATED TO THE PROVISION OF PITA, THE FORMATION AND OPERATION OF THE TECHNICAL EXPERT PANEL, DEVELOPMENT OF PRODUCTS AND PROVISION OF TRAINING. PER GUIDANCE FROM SAMHSA ON DECEMBER 9, 2024, THIS SUBCONTRACTOR’S SCOPE OF WORK SMI TTAC FOR THE PURPOSES OF PITA MANAGED UNDER THIS SUBCONTRACTOR, SMI IS LIMITED TO TASKS ADDRESSING SMI CONSISTING OF DIAGNOSES OF SCHIZOPHRENIA, MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, BIPOLAR DISORDER AND FIRST EPISODE PSYCHOSIS (FEP). AS USED THROUGHOUT THIS SUBCONTRACTOR’S SCOPE OF WORK, WHEN REFERRED TO IN THE CONTEXT OF PITA, SMI SHALL MEAN DIAGNOSES OF SCHIZOPHRENIA, MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, BIPOLAR DISORDER AND/OR FEP. IN THIS SUBCONTRACT, ALL REFERENCES TO SMI BEYOND THOSE IN THE CONTEXT OF PITA WILL ENCOMPASS THE SAMHSA DEFINITION, INCLUDED BELOW. • SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS IS DEFINED BY SOMEONE OVER 18 HAVING (WITHIN THE PAST YEAR) A DIAGNOSABLE MENTAL, BEHAVIOR, OR EMOTIONAL DISORDER THAT CAUSES SERIOUS FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT THAT SUBSTANTIALLY INTERFERES WITH OR LIMITS ONE OR MORE MAJOR LIFE ACTIVITIES. BETWEEN SEPTEMBER 10, 2024 – SEPTEMBER 9, 2025, APA WILL WORK WITH THE PROJECT TEAM TO PROVIDE SUPPORT TO THE PROJECT. NOTWITHSTANDING ANYTHING TO THE CONTRARY IN THIS DOCUMENT, ALL EFFORT BY APA UNDER THIS SCOPE OF WORK SHALL BE BILLED AGAINST THE BUDGETED SCOPE ALLOTTED TO APA UNDER THE SMI TTAC CONTRACT AWARDED TO NATIONAL COUNCIL; THERE IS NO GUARANTEE THAT ALL TASKS SET FORTH IN THIS DOCUMENT WILL BE COMPLETED WITHIN THE SCOPE BUDGET. UPON EXHAUSTION OF THE BUDGET, NO ADDITIONAL EFFORT WILL BE PERFORMED BY APA UNLESS A CHANGE ORDER IS EXECUTED BY THE PARTIES TO INCREASE THE BUDGET TO ACCOUNT FOR THE REQUIRED EFFORT. TASKS MAY INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO THE BELOW, UP TO THE BUDGETED SCOPE ALLOTTED TO APA UNDER THE SMI TTAC CONTRACT AWARDED TO NATIONAL COUNCIL. ...

REPORTING WILL INVOLVE MONTHLY PERFORMANCE REPORTS AND AN ANNUAL REPORT, WHICH WILL DETAIL ACHIEVEMENTS, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE PLANS ASSOCIATED WITH THE DELIVERY OF SERVICES. ALL ACTIVITIES WILL INVOLVE COLLABORATION WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL SMI TTAC TEAM, INCLUDING TIMELY SUBMISSION OF DRAFT MATERIALS AND APPROVAL BY THE NATIONAL COUNCIL TEAM AS WELL AS SAMHSA WHERE REQUIRED.

description: AS PART OF A PROGRAM SPONSORED BY CARB-X TO HELP DEFINE AN EVIDENCE-BASED CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK FOR THE EVALUATION OF DECOLONIZATION AGENTS USED FOR THE PREVENTION OF SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, DR. JULIA OH, DR. WEI ZHOU, AND MR. RYAN CALDWELL OF THE OH LAB AT THE JACKSON LABORATORY WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A METAGENOMIC PIPELINE FOR PATHOGEN DETECTION AND MICROBIAL LOAD ESTIMATION OF COLONIZATION OF MULTIPLE BODY SITES. THIS PIPELINE SIMULTANEOUSLY GENERATES DEEP METAGENOMIC DATA THAT MAY CONTAIN RELEVANT INFORMATION ABOUT INFECTION RISK AS WELL AS ACCURATELY DETECT, AT THE STRAIN LEVEL, MOST LIKELY STRAIN LEVELS OF PATHOGENS OF INTEREST. THIS PIPELINE WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY QPCR TO CALCULATE MICROBIAL LOAD, DATA WHICH WILL THEN BE USED TO EXTRAPOLATE BIOBURDEN AS A FUNCTION OF CFUS PER GRAM OF STOOL OR SKIN SWAB. THE OH LAB WILL RETURN 1) A DETAILED WORKFLOW FOR SAMPLE ACQUISITION, PREPARATION, AND ANALYSIS, 2) ALGORITHMS AND DATABASES FOR PATHOGEN DETECTION IN METAGENOMIC DATA, AND 3) BENCHMARK TESTING FOR THIS PIPELINE.

description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO (DRC), SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORTS AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE SEVERAL CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDIES. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL AND HUMAN P.O. BOX B, FREDERICK, MD 21702-1201 Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ 301-846-1000 A SUBSIDIARY OF RCF-505 PAGE 4 OF 4 REV. AUGUST 2023 RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE FOLLOWING PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS-2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID-19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE PALM 007 PROTOCOL, INCLUDING SUPPORT OF BIOREPOSITORY ACTIVITIES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THE PALM 007 TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT (TPOXX) IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE PALM 008 PROTOCOL. PALM 008 IS A COHORT EVENTS MONITORING STUDY FOR THE ASSESSMENT OF SAFETY PROFILE OF MVA-BN (JYNNEOS) VACCINE IN ADULT PERSONNEL AND STAFF IN THE PALM 007 STUDY AS WELL AS THE PALM 011 RCT WHICH IS A RANDOMIZED, CONTROLLED TRIAL FOR THE TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH MPOX VIRUS DISEASE IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO.

description: DR. VANCE FOWLER AND DR. WILL WOODHOUSE OF DUKE UNIVERSITY WILL BE SUPPORTING A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW PROJECT SPONSORED BY CARB-X TO HELP DEFINE AN EVIDENCE-BASED CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK FOR THE EVALUATION OF DECOLONIZATION AGENTS USED FOR THE PREVENTION OF SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTIONS. MICROBIAL COLONIZATION OF MUCOSAL SURFACES AND SKIN BY ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANT MICROBES IS AN IMPORTANT DRIVER OF INTRACTABLE INFECTIONS IN COLONIZED INDIVIDUALS. DECOLONIZATION OF SKIN AND MUCOSA HAS BEEN SHOWN TO REDUCE RATES OF PATIENT INFECTION IN SEVERAL HEALTHCARE SETTINGS. IMPORTANTLY, AN ADDITIONAL PUBLIC HEALTH BENEFIT IS THAT DECOLONIZATION MAY DECREASE PERSON-TO-PERSON OR ENVIRONMENTAL TRANSMISSION IN HEALTH CARE FACILITIES. THEREFORE, DECOLONIZATION AGENTS MAY PRODUCE TWO DIFFERENT, BUT RELATED, BENEFICIAL CLINICAL OUTCOMES. INNOVATORS AND PRODUCT DEVELOPERS ARE EXPLORING Ã¢Â‚¬Å“NON-TRADITIONALÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ NOVEL ANTI-INFECTIVES THAT ARE MICROBIOME-SPARING BY SELECTIVELY TARGETING PATHOGENS SUCH AS LIVE BIOTHERAPEUTIC PRODUCTS (LBPS), WHICH SEEK TO DISPLACE POTENTIALLY HARMFUL BACTERIA IN CERTAIN TARGET BODY SITES, AND ENGINEERED BACTERIOPHAGE PRODUCTS, WHICH SEEK TO EXCISE HARMFUL BACTERIA FROM CERTAIN TARGET BODY SITES. THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL, NON-TRADITIONAL DECOLONIZATION AGENTS TO PREVENT BREAKTHROUGH INFECTIONS IN PATIENTS COLONIZED WITH ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT BACTERIA, OR TO DECREASE PERSON-TO-PERSON TRANSMISSION IN HEALTHCARE SETTINGS, IS HINDERED BY THE LACK OF DEFINED REGULATORY AND CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT PATHWAYS FOR APPROVAL. THIS SYSTEMATIC REVIEW IS INTENDED TO UNDERSCORE WHAT IS CURRENTLY KNOWN ABOUT THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN COLONIZATION AND INFECTION RISK AND/OR TRANSMISSION OF ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT PATHOGENS. THE REVIEW WILL BE FOLLOWED BY A GAP ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY AREAS WHERE NEW OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES ARE REQUIRED TO PROVIDE THE EVIDENCE-BASE TO SUPPORT THE DESIGN OF STUDIES TO SUPPORT THE APPROVAL OF NOVEL DECOLONIZATION AGENTS.

description: OVERVIEW: UCSF HOLDS AN FDA CONTRACT ENTITLED, Ã¢Â‚¬Å“COMMUNITY USES OF PSYCHEDELICS AND SAFETY STUDYÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ (CUPS) WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF USING A MULTIMODAL SET OF RESEARCH METHODS TO ASSESS FOR EMERGING TRENDS OF HARM, AND ESTABLISHED METHODS FOR ASSURING SAFETY, AMONG PSYCHEDELIC USERS IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE TRAJECTORY OF PSYCHEDELICS USE AND ASSOCIATED PUBLIC HEALTH CONSEQUENCES. THE SUBPROJECT CUPS3 WILL INVESTIGATE THE ASSOCIATION OF IMPLEMENTATION OF DRUG REGULATORY CHANGES IN OREGON WITH PSILOCYBIN-RELATED ADVERSE OUTCOMES BY COLLECTING DETAILED DE-IDENTIFIED* INDIVIDUAL PATIENT-LEVEL DATA ON RELEVANT ENCOUNTERS FROM INSTITUTIONAL ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHRS). THE SUBCONTRACTING SITE WILL PROVIDE DATA FOR THIS EFFORT. THE SUBCONTRACTING INVESTIGATOR WILL CONTRIBUTE THEIR EFFORT AND THE EFFORT OF THEIR STAFF TO SECURING EHR DATA FROM THEIR HEALTHCARE INSTITUTION SITES LOCATED IN THE STATE OF OREGON. description: "THE GOAL OF THE CARDIA STUDY IS TO ASSESS THE EVOLUTION OF CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE RISK FACTORS IN HEALTHY 18-30 YEAR OLDS AT BASELINE IN 1985-6. COLLABORATING ENTITIES INCLUDE FOUR FIELD CENTERS (FCS), A COORDINATING CENTER (CC), FOUR LABORATORIES (CENTRAL BLOOD AND URINE REPOSITORY, LIPIDS LABORATORY, BLOOD AND URINE CHEMISTRIES LABORATORY, AND DNA LABORATORY), AND ANY SPECIFIC ANCILLARY STUDY SITE. THE STEERING COMMITTEE (SC) INCLUDES THE CHAIR, AND THE PUBLICATIONS & PRESENTATIONS (P&P) SUBCOMMITTEE CHAIR. PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS (PIS) FROM EACH FC, COORDINATING CENTER, LABORATORY, READING CENTER, AND ANCILLARY STUDY, THE NHLBI CONTRACTING OFFICER AND PROJECT OFFICER, AND OTHER CARDIA SCIENTISTS. THE SC WILL OVERSEE ALL SCIENTIFIC ISSUES AND MEET TWICE PER MONTH VIA VIDEO CONFERENCE, WITH TWO IN-PERSON MEETINGS PER YEAR. THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE (EC) INCLUDES THE SC CHAIR, FC PIS, CC PI AND DEPUTY DIRECTOR, AND THE NHLBI PROJECT OFFICER. IT OVERSEES DAY-TO-DAY OPERATIONS, REVIEWS AND APPROVES ANCILLARY STUDIES, AND DISCUSSES IMPORTANT ISSUES FOR SC APPROVAL. IT MEETS MONTHLY VIA VIDEO CONFERENCE AND IN-PERSON IN CONJUNCTION WITH IN-PERSON SC MEETINGS, AND ALSO CONDUCTS BUSINESS ELECTRONICALLY WHEN NEEDED (E.G., APPROVAL OF ANCILLARY STUDIES AS CIRCUMSTANCES DICTATE)."

description: TRAUMA IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF DEATH FOR CHILDREN1. BLEEDING IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF PREVENTABLE DEATH IN INJURED CHILDREN2-4. MORTALITY RATES AT 28-DAYS IN INJURED CHILDREN WITH LIFE THREATENING HEMORRHAGE (LTH) RANGE FROM 36-50%,5-7 APPROXIMATELY TWICE THAT OF INJURED ADULTS (21-24%)6,7 . DESPITE THE FACT THAT CHILDRENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S COAGULATION AND PHYSIOLOGIC RESPONSE TO BLEEDING DIFFERS FROM ADULTS8-11, PEDIATRIC TRAUMA RESUSCITATION PRACTICE GUIDELINES ARE DERIVED FROM ADULT DATA DUE TO A LACK OF HIGH QUALITY RESEARCH IN CHILDREN12,13. HEMORRHAGE IS INITIALLY ADDRESSED BY HEMOSTATIC RESUSCITATION14-19, A STRATEGY THAT RESTORES ADEQUATE PERFUSION AND MITIGATES THE EFFECTS OF TRAUMA-INDUCED COAGULOPATHY (TIC). THE CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE IS TO TRANSFUSE COMPONENT THERAPY (CT) (I.E., RBC, FFP, PLATELETS) IN BALANCED RATIOS. 20,21 HOWEVER, THE MIXTURE OF CT IS MORE DILUTE WITH INCREASED ANTICOAGULANTS AND ADDITIVE SOLUTIONS 22 COMPARED TO WHOLE BLOOD. THE NEED TO OPTIMIZE BALANCED RESUSCITATION HAS LED TO THE CLINICAL USE OF COLD-STORED LOW TITER GROUP O WHOLE BLOOD (LTOWB) 23, WHICH HAS MULTIPLE POTENTIAL ADVANTAGES OVER CT (IMPROVED OXYGEN DELIVERY, HEMOSTATIC FUNCTION22,24-30, EASE OF ADMINISTRATION,31 32 AND REDUCED RISK OF FATAL HEMOLYTIC REACTIONS AND DONOR EXPOSURES33). IN CHILDREN WITH LTH FROM TRAUMA, LTOWB COMPARED TO CT MAY DECREASE TOTAL BLOOD PRODUCTS TRANSFUSED, IMPROVE OXYGEN DELIVERY, COAGULATION, AND 72-HOUR AND 28-DAY SURVIVAL WITHOUT INCREASING THE RISK OF HEMOLYSIS AND ORGAN FAILURE34-36. THOUGH PROMISING, THE DATA ARE LIMITED BY SINGLE-CENTER STUDIES AND SMALL COHORT SIZE; NO MULTICENTER TRIALS COMPARE LTOWB TO CT IN PEDIATRIC TRAUMA PATIENTS. TRANEXAMIC ACID (TXA) IS AN ANTIFIBRINOLYTIC THAT HAS BEEN PROVEN TO IMPROVE SURVIVAL IN SEVERELY INJURED ADULT TRAUMA PATIENTS AND THERE IS OBSERVATIONAL DATA IT IS INDEPENDENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH IMPROVED SURVIVAL IN CHILDREN37. THE TIC TOC TRIAL WILL EXAMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF TXA IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC BLEEDING38. HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK PRECIPITATES THE BODYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S COMPLEX ENDOGENOUS RESPONSE TO HYPOPERFUSION AND INJURY. WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT TIC IS COMMON IN INJURED CHILDREN AND HIGHLY ASSOCIATED WITH DEATH, DISABILITY, ORGAN FAILURE AND NEED FOR GREATER VOLUMES OF BLOOD PRODUCTS. 39-43 DESPITE THE CRITICAL IMPORTANCE OF PEDIATRIC TIC, DATA REGARDING UNDERLYING MECHANISMS ARE SPARSE. TO OPTIMIZE TRANSFUSION STRATEGIES INCHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK, IT IS ESSENTIAL TO INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS OF TIC COMPREHENSIVELY.WE PROPOSE THE MASSIVE TRANSFUSION IN CHILDREN-2 (MATIC-2) TRIAL, A PRAGMATIC, BAYESIAN, GROUP SEQUENTIAL, COMBINED NON-INFERIORITY/SUPERIORITY, RANDOMIZED, CONTROLLED, MULTICENTER, PHASE III, PLATFORM TRIAL TO EXAMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF LTOWB RELATIVE TO STANDARD CT IN 1000 DOCUSIGN ENVELOPE ID: CD235578-BBE9-4B23-927D-107F20895C9F DOCUSIGN ENVELOPE ID: A0A11664-A9BF-4977-8D06-2C403DCC96CE SUBCONTRACT NO. AWD00008169-9 SUBCONTRACTOR: ARKANSAS CHILDRENÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S RESEARCH INSTITUTE PAGE 23 OF 26 CHILDREN AT 18 US ACADEMIC PEDIATRIC TRAUMA CENTERS. MECHANISMS OF TIC AND RESUSCITATION EFFECTS WILL ALSO BE INVESTIGATED. AIM 1:Ã¢Â‚¬Â¯ASSESSÃ¢Â‚¬Â¯THE EFFECT OF LTOWB VERSUS CT ON CLINICAL OUTCOMES.Ã¢Â‚¬Â¯ H1: WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT COMPARED TO CT, LTOWB IS A) NON-INFERIOR AND/OR B) SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY. AIM 2: ASSESS THE SAFETY OF LTOWB VERSUS CT. H2: WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LTOWB TRANSFUSION DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES COMPARED TO CT. AIM 3: DEFINE THE MECHANISMS OF TIC AND ASSESS THE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF TRANSFUSION STRATEGIES ON MEASURES OF OXYGEN DELIVERY, HEMOSTASIS, IMMUNE AND ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION. H3: WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LTOWB IS SUPERIOR TO CT IN CORRECTING THE HYPOPERFUSION, ENDOTHELIAL INJURY, IMMUNE DYSFUNCTION, AND DYSREGULATION OF COAGULATION AND FIBRINOLYSIS PATHWAYS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THE ETIOLOGY OF TIC IN CHILDREN. description: OPTION 11C: 0258-A474-4612 DEVELOPMENT OF A TAG-LESS RNA DOWNSTREAM PURIFICATION PROCESS AND ASSISTANCE IN OPTIMIZING AN AFFINITY-BASED RNA DOWNSTREAM PURIFICATION PROCESS THE UNIVERSITY OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND LIFE SCIENCES, VIENNA WILL AID IN THE BIOPROCESS DEVELOPMENT OF A NOVEL RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA VIRUS NEURAMINIDASE. THIS PROTEIN IS INTENDED TO BE USED AS A SUBUNIT VACCINE. RECOMBINANT NEURAMINIDASE (RNA) WILL BE PRODUCED IN INSECT CELLS, USING THE BACULOVIRUS SYSTEM, AT MOUNT SINAI AND/OR EXPRESSION SYSTEMS. DR. LINGGÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S TEAM WILL DEVELOP A DOWNSTREAM PROCESS (DSP) FOR HIGHLY PURE RNA USING TWO STRATEGIES. FIRSTLY, AN ALREADY EXISTING POLY-HISTIDINE-TAG BASED DSP WILL BE OPTIMIZED TO ENSURE A ROBUST PROCESS WITH A YIELD SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL PRODUCTION AT EXPRESSION SYSTEMS. SECONDLY, A NOVEL DSP THAT DOES NOT RELY ON THE POLY-HISTIDINE-TAG, WILL BE DEVELOPED. TASK 1: OPTIMIZE AFFINITY-BASED PROCESS THE CURRENT AFFINITY-BASED PROCESS UTILIZES POLY-HISTIDINE TAGGED RNA WHICH CAN BE PURIFIED USING IMMOBILIZED METAL AFFINITY CHROMATOGRAPHY. WHILE THE PROCESS PRODUCES RNA OF SUFFICIENT PURITY, IT SUFFERS FROM LOW SCALABILITY DUE TO LACKING ROBUSTNESS OF THE PROCESS. PROTEIN LOSSES DURING COLUMN WASH STEPS WERE OBSERVED. THE AFFINITY CHROMATOGRAPHY STEP WILL BE OPTIMIZED USING VARIOUS STRATEGIES AND AN ARRAY OF ANALYTICAL TOOLS TO MONITOR THE CONCENTRATION OF PRODUCT AND CRITICAL IMPURITIES. OPTION 11D: 0258-A475-4612 DEVELOPMENT OF A TAG-LESS RNA DOWNSTREAM PURIFICATION PROCESS AND ASSISTANCE IN OPTIMIZING AN AFFINITY-BASED RNA DOWNSTREAM PURIFICATION PROCESS THE UNIVERSITY OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND LIFE SCIENCES, VIENNA WILL AID IN THE BIOPROCESS DEVELOPMENT OF A NOVEL RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA VIRUS NEURAMINIDASE. THE WORK ON THIS OPTION WILL BE AS FOLLOWS: TASK 2: DEVELOP TAG-LESS PROCESS A CONVENTIONAL DSP FOR THE PRODUCTION OF RNA WITHOUT AFFINITY TAG WILL BE DEVELOPED USING STATE-OF-THE-ART BIOCHEMICAL ENGINEERING METHODS. THE PROPOSED PROCESS WILL CONSIST OF SEVERAL UNIT OPERATIONS, NAMELY CLARIFICATION USING DEPTH FILTRATION, VIRAL INACTIVATION, CONCENTRATION USING ULTRAFILTRATION, CAPTURE USING ANION-EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY, POLISHING USING AN ORTHOGONAL CHROMATOGRAPHY METHOD, FORMULATION USING ULTRAFILTRATION/DIAFILTRATION AND VIRUS FILTRATION. PROCESS DEVELOPMENT WILL BE SUPPORTED BY MECHANISTIC MODELS AND AN ARRAY OF ANALYTICAL TOOLS FOR MASS BALANCES OF PRODUCT AND IMPURITIES ACROSS UNIT OPERATIONS. SCALABILITY PARAMETERS OF ALL UNIT OPERATIONS WILL BE DETERMINED TO ENSURE SEAMLESS PROCESS TRANSFER FOR SUPPORT OF PHASE II CLINICAL TRIALS AND BEYOND.

description: TASK 1: DEVELOP OVERALL STRATEGY FOR ADVANCING PROGRAM PRIORITIES THROUGH THE NEWS MEDIA AND OTHER COMMUNICATION CHANNELS. CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP OVERALL NEWS MEDIA STRATEGIES FOR ADVANCING NCHHSTP PRIORITY OBJECTIVES, AS WELL AS PROVIDING ONGOING STRATEGIC COUNSEL ON EMERGING NEWS MEDIA OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES, WHICH MAY REQUIRE MODIFICATION TO PROACTIVE OR REACTIVE STRATEGIES. THIS WILL REQUIRE PERIODIC FACE-TO-FACE MEETINGS AND WEEKLY COORDINATION AND COMMUNICATION WITH THE NCHHSTP NEWS MEDIA TEAM. TASK 2: IMPLEMENTATION OF SELECTED NEWS MEDIA STRATEGIES FOR EACH PROJECT IDENTIFIED, INCLUDING THE ELECTRONIC DISTRIBUTION OF MATERIALS AS NEEDED. THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING SELECTED STRATEGIES AND TACTICS FROM THE FOLLOWING LIST, NOT TO EXCEED 10 ACROSS PROJECTS IN ANY ONE-MONTH PERIOD, WHICH MAY INCLUDE: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ DEVELOPING TACTICAL PLANS Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ DRAFTING MESSAGES AND OTHER NEWS MEDIA MATERIALS (I.E., PRESS RELEASES, FACT SHEETS, GRAPHICS, ELECTRONIC PRESS KITS ) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ FORMATTING (INCLUDING 508 COMPLIANCE) OF MEDIA MATERIALS Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ MEDIA TRAINING OF CDC SPOKESPERSONS (1-2 TRAININGS PER CONTRACT PERIOD) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ DENTIFICATION OF KEY THIRD-PARTY SPOKESPERSONS WHO SHOULD BE ENGAGED, AND ASSESSMENT OF KEY ISSUES AND OBJECTIVES FOR THIRD-PARTY ENGAGEMENT (CONTRACTOR WILL NOT BE REQUIRED TO IMPLEMENT THIRD-PARTY ENGAGEMENT, BUT RATHER ONLY TO ASSESS KEY ISSUES AND STAKEHOLDERS) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR PRESS CONFERENCES AND TELEBRIEFINGS Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ COMPILING QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE COVERAGE REPORTS AND MESSAGE ANALYSIS Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ RECOMMENDATIONS FOR HOW OUTCOMES AND LESSONS LEARNED IMPACT LONG-TERM STRATEGIC OBJECTIVES AND ONGOING MEDIA STRATEGY AND/OR THIRD-PARTY ENGAGEMENT TASK 3: DAILY MONITORING OF THE NEWS MEDIA AND ADVOCACY DISCUSSIONS SURROUNDING KEY ISSUES IMPACTING NCHHSTP. USING DAILY MONITORING SYSTEMS THAT ARE COMPREHENSIVE IN PICKING UP ALL RELEVANT DISCUSSIONS, BUT COST-EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT IN ELIMINATING IRRELEVANT COVERAGE. TASK 4: ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS AND ISSUES MANAGEMENT: A) TO IDENTIFY BOTH OPPORTUNITIES AND THREATS TO NCHHSTP PREVENTION POLICY AND PROGRAM OBJECTIVES, CDC REQUIRES IN-DEPTH ANALYSIS OF THE MEDIA AND ADVOCACY ENVIRONMENT SURROUNDING ITS PROGRAMS. UPON REQUEST, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE ANALYSES OF THE MEDIA COVERAGE, AND QUALITATIVE ASSESSMENT OF ADVOCACY DIALOGUE, SURROUNDING NCHHSTP PROGRAMS OVERALL, AS WELL AS ISSUE-SPECIFIC ANALYSES. COMPREHENSIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SCANS SHALL BE DEVELOPED ON THREE NCHHSTP DIVISIONS EACH YEAR, AND MAY BE REQUESTED ON ADDITIONAL SPECIFIC PROGRAMS OR ISSUES PERIODICALLY (UP TO 3 PER YEAR). ANALYSES SHOULD BE BASED UPON SOURCES MONITORED IN TASK 3. B) ADDITIONALLY, AS ISSUES ARISE, CONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A RESPONSE STRATEGY, WHICH MAY INCLUDE ISSUE ANALYSIS, RECOMMENDED TACTICS, MESSAGE DEVELOPMENT, MATERIAL DEVELOPMENT, AND MEDIA OUTREACH.
