description: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO PROVIDE RAPID DEPLOYMENT OF TECHNICAL, OPERATIONAL, AND CLINICAL RESEARCH RESOURCES AND EXPERTISE FOR THIS TIME SENSITIVE INITIATIVE. THE PROTOCOL IS TITLED, ASSESSMENT OF IMMUNE RESPONSE TO EBOLA VIRUS DISEASE AS MODULATED BY VACCINES AND MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES, AND IS ALSO KNOWN AS PALM 005. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: STRATEGIC AND OPERATIONAL PLANNING AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, INFRASTRUCTURE OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE; LOGISTICS AND PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT; SITE DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE ALL CLINICAL SITES REMAIN IN A STATE OF PREPAREDNESS AND COMPLIANCE WITH PROTOCOL REQUIREMENTS, INITIATING AND COMPLETING ENROLLMENT AND FOLLOW-UP FOR THE CLINICAL RESEARCH PROTOCOL; OVERALL MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF THE CONDUCT OF THE MOBILIZATION, PSYCHOSOCIAL SUPPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS EFFORTS, AND OTHER ACTIVITIES SUCH AS LABORATORY SERVICES AND PHARMACY SUPPORT. THE SPECIFIC SUPPORT TO EBOLA OUTBREAK #14 IN THE EQUATOR PROVINCE IS TO COVER GAPS IN THE SAFE ADMINISTRATION OF INVESTIGATIONAL PRODUCT UNTIL SUPPORT OF OTHER EBOLA RESPONSE PARTNERS HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED IN THIS REGION. THE CURRENT PORTFOLIO OF PALM RESEARCH STUDIES TO SUPPORT IN THIS SOW INCLUDES: PALM 010 MPOX VACCINE RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL INITIATION PHASE PALM 007 EXTENSION: A SINGLE ARM, OPEN LABEL EXTENSION TO THE PALM007 RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL FOR FURTHER CLINICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THE NATURAL HISTORY OF MPOX.

description: THIS WORK IS A CONTINUATION OF THE PROJECT THAT THE ACI GROUP BEGAN UNDER THE PREVIOUS TASK ORDER. BELOW IS THE RATIONALE FOR INITIALLY SELECTING PAUL JEFFREY OF THE ACI GROUP. THE CONTRACTOR'S EXPERTISE IN PRESCRIPTION DRUG MANUFACTURER NEGOTIATIONS, PARTICULARLY IN OUTCOME-BASED AGREEMENTS, WILL BE INVALUABLE IN ASSISTING CMMI TO ESTABLISH A FRAMEWORK FOR THE NEW CGT FOCUSING ON SICKLE CELL DISEASE (SCD). THEIR GUIDANCE WILL NOT ONLY HELP DETERMINE TREATMENT COSTS BUT ALSO SUGGEST POTENTIAL SOLUTIONS TO THE AFFORDABILITY AND ACCESS ISSUES OF THE NEW THERAPY. ADDITIONALLY, THEIR ANALYSIS OF DATA ON SCD PREVALENCE AND TREATMENT COSTS WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS TO GUIDE NEGOTIATIONS WITH PRESCRIPTION DRUG MANUFACTURERS.

description: THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO COMPREHENSIVELY ANALYZE THE SPILLOVER EFFECTS OF THE GOVERNMENT CLIENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S MODEL TESTS ON THE HEALTHCARE MARKET. THE CONTRACTOR WILL CONDUCT A QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY, DESCRIBE, AND CATALOGUE THESE EFFECTS, CONSIDERING FACTORS SUCH AS THE REASONS, TIMING, METHODS OF SPILLOVER, AND THE AFFECTED HEALTHCARE STAKEHOLDERS. RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WILL ENCOMPASS LITERATURE REVIEWS, MARKET SCANS, INTERVIEWS WITH VARIOUS STAKEHOLDERS, AND DATA ANALYSIS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL DOCUMENT AND SHARE KEY TAKEAWAYS FROM THE INTERVIEWS. THE FINDINGS WILL BE COMPILED INTO A REPORT AND PRESENTATION DETAILING THE TYPES AND MAGNITUDE OF SPILLOVER EFFECTS, THEIR CATEGORIZATION, DESCRIPTIONS OF THE GOVERNMENT CLIENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S MODEL SPILLOVER EFFECTS, AND THE CORRELATION OF SPECIFIC EFFECTS TO ROOT CAUSES. THE REPORT WILL FEATURE REAL MARKET EXAMPLES AND CASE STUDIES OF STAKEHOLDERS' SPILLOVER EFFECTS. FINALLY, THE FINDINGS WILL BE VALIDATED THROUGH PRESSURE TESTING WITH INDUSTRY EXPERTS AND STAKEHOLDER REPRESENTATIVES. 2/2

description: TITLE: ASPR PROFESSIONAL TECHNICAL & MEDICAL STAFFING SUPPORT IDIQ TO SUPPORT THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES (HHS) RESPONSE TO THE COVID- 19 PANDEMIC. REQUIRING ORGANIZATION: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES (HHS), ADMINISTRATION FOR STRATEGIC PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE (ASPR), CENTER FOR INDUSTRIAL BASE EXPANSION AND SUPPLY CHAIN (IBMSC). TASK ORDER LABOR CATEGORIES REQUIREMENTS LABOR CATEGORIES (LCATÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S) Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ LEVEL OF EFFORT FTE PROGRAM MANAGER 1 INTRODUCTION: ASPR STOOD UP THE CENTER FOR INDUSTRIAL BASE EXPANSION AND SUPPLY CHAIN (IBMSC) FOCUSED ON MAKING OUR NATIONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S INDUSTRIAL BASE MORE RESILIENT, DIVERSE, AND SECURE. ASPR IS WORKING WITH PARTNERS ACROSS GOVERNMENT AND INDUSTRY TO STRENGTHEN PUBLIC HEALTH AND MEDICAL SUPPLY CHAINS AND TO ADDRESS CONCERNS REGARDING DOMESTIC MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY CHAIN SURGE CAPABILITIES. WITHIN IBMSC THERE ARE FIVE DOMAINS, INCLUDING THOSE THAT OVERSEE PORTFOLIOS FOR OFFICE OF CRITICAL MEDICAL EQUIPMENT (OCME), OFFICE OF TESTING AND DIAGNOSTICS (OTD), THE OFFICE OF DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE (DPA-ERA), OFFICE OF ENABLING INNOVATIONS AND TECHNOLOGIES (OEIT), AND OFFICE OF SUPPLY CHAIN OPTIMIZATION (OSCO). THE POSITIONS LISTED IN THE SOW BELOW WILL SUPPORT ALL THESE DOMAINS. PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND: ASPR IS A PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE ORGANIZATION IN THE OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY AT THE HHS. ASPR WAS CREATED UNDER THE PANDEMIC AND ALL HAZARDS PREPAREDNESS ACT IN THE WAKE OF HURRICANE KATRINA TO LEAD THE NATION IN PREVENTING, PREPARING FOR, AND RESPONDING TO THE ADVERSE HEALTH EFFECTS OF PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES AND DISASTERS, SUCH AS THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. TO MEET ASPRÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ONGOING AND NEW MISSION OBJECTIVES, THERE IS A HIGH DEMAND FOR CONTRACTOR RESOURCES IN MULTIPLE LABOR CATEGORIES TO SUPPORT THIS EFFORT THAT CANNOT EASILY BE MET THROUGH THE CONVENTIONAL (OR DIRECT) HIRING PROCESS. THEREFORE, COMMERCIAL RESOURCES ARE SOUGHT TO ONBOARD CRITICALLY NEEDED PROFESSIONAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES FOR ACTIVE AND PLANNED COVID-19 IBMSC EFFORTS. SCOPE: ASPR REQUIRES PROFESSIONAL SUPPORT ACROSS THE FOLLOWING DISCIPLINES: PROJECT MANAGEMENT; PROGRAM & OPERATIONS SUPPORT; COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT; COST/PRICING & BUDGET SUPPORT; AND ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT FOR ACTIVE AND PLANNED COVID-19 IBMSC EFFORTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFIED HEREIN ALL SUBCONTRACTOR PERSONNEL, MATERIALS, SERVICES, FACILITIES, EQUIPMENT, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, AND MANUFACTURING CERTIFICATIONS REQUIRED TO CONDUCT PERFORMANCE FOR ALL REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SOW. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE (POP): THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE IS FROM JUNE 24, 2024 THROUGH JUNE 4, 2025. FAR 52.217-8: OPTION TO EXTEND UP TO SIX MONTHS. WORK SCHEDULE AND LOCATION: WORK LOCATION THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM WORK ASSOCIATED WITH THIS TASK ORDER IN THE DESIGNATED GREATER WASHINGTON, D.C. METROPOLITAN AREA AND VIRTUALLY AS IDENTIFIED PER POSITION AND BY THE PROGRAM OFFICE. OTHER LOCATIONS MAY BE DESIGNATED BY THE PROGRAM OFFICE DEPENDING ON STAFFING NEEDS. UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED BY THE PROGRAM OFFICE, CONTRACTORS SHALL REPORT TO THE CONSTITUTION CENTER BUILDING BUT MAY BE DIVERTED TO AN ALTERNATIVE/CONTINUITY OF OPERATIONS PLAN (COOP) SITE IN A RESPONSE ACTIVATION. FEDERAL HOLIDAYS THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL NOT PERFORM SERVICES ON DAYS DESIGNATED AS A FEDERAL HOLIDAY BY FEDERAL STATUS, EXECUTIVE ORDER OR PRESIDENTIAL PROCLAMATION. FEDERAL HOLIDAYS ARE AN EXCEPTION TO THE REGULAR DUTY HOURS. ANY OF THE HOLIDAYS LISTED BELOW FALLING ON A SATURDAY WILL BE OBSERVED ON THE PRECEDING FRIDAY; HOLIDAYS FALLING ON A SUNDAY WILL BE OBSERVED ON THE FOLLOWING MONDAY. description: THE MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY FOCUS ON PI4K IS TO IDENTIFY A NOVEL SERIES OF BACK-UP COMPOUNDS THAT ARE DIVERSE WITH OFF-TARGET TOXICITY AS WELL AS PHARMACOKINETIC PROPERTIES. ACME IS BEST SITED TO PERFORM THIS WORK GIVEN THEIR PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN SYNTHESIZING A LARGE A RANGE OF PI4K MOLECULES IN A TIMELY FASHION. THE COMPANY WILL SYNTHESIZE CHEMICALS THAT ARE DESIGNED BY THE STANFORD MEDICINAL CHEMISTS. THE SCOPE OF CHEMISTRY ACTIVITIES: TYPICAL ACTIVITIES INCLUDE SYNTHESIS OF FOCUSED COMPOUND LIBRARIES (TYPICALLY 20-200 COMPOUNDS PER LIBRARY) ON A SCALE OF 10-50 MG AND PURITY OF >95%. PROVIDE RELEVANT ANALYTICAL DATA INCLUDING 1H, 13C NMR AND LCMS. SYNTHESIS (TYPICALLY >50 MG) OF ANALOGS OF EACH STRUCTURE TO SUPPORT LEAD OPTIMIZATION AND LEAD SERIES IDENTIFICATION ACTIVITIES. SYNTHESIS OF KEY REFERENCE COMPOUNDS IN THE 0.5-5 G RANGE AND A PURITY OF ~95-98% (>98% WHEN RELEVANT). SYNTHESIS OF KEY INTERMEDIATES ON 5-50 G SCALE AND A PURITY OF ~95%. SCALE-UP OF SELECTED COMPOUNDS FOR ADVANCED IN-VIVO STUDIES ON A SCALE OF 5-50 G AND PURITY OF 95% (>98% WHEN RELEVANT). DEVISING CHEMICAL SYNTHETIC ROUTES WHEN NECESSARY. TECHNICAL JUSTIFICATION WHEN FACTORING IN THE ANTICIPATED EXTRA FEES AND LACK OF CLOSE PROXIMITY, COMBINED WITH A LONG- STANDING TRACK RECORD OF PRODUCTIVE AND COST-EFFECTIVE WORK DONE BY ACME ON OUR BEHALF, THEY WERE FELT TO BE THE OVERALL BEST VALUE.

description: THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NTM INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). OPTION 1 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN MOUSE TB MODELS SIX-WEEK OLD MALE AND FEMALE C57BL/6 AND CBA (CBA EXCLUSIVELY USED IN TASK 1.4 & 1.5) MICE WILL BE MAINTAINED IN THE BIOSAFETY LEVEL-III BIOENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS BUILDING AT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY, AND WILL BE GIVEN STERILE WATER, MOUSE CHOW, BEDDING, AND ENRICHMENT FOR THE DURATION OF THE EXPERIMENTS. ALL EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOLS WILL BE APPROVED BY THE ANIMAL CARE AND USAGE COMMITTEE OF COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY AS PER THE DEFINED DELIVERABLE IN THE BASE PERIOD. SOME OF THE HARVESTED SAMPLES IN OPTION 1 TASKS OUTLINED BELOW WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO COLLABORATOR SITES. CSU WILL PROVIDE THESE SAMPLES TO COLLABORATORS AS NEEDED AND PREDETERMINED BY THE NEEDS OF SOPS. THIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: SERUM OR BLOOD FOR ENDPOINT ANTIBODY ELISAS (SCRI), SYSTEMS SEROLOGY (RAGON) AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC (FHCC) ASSAYS ACROSS SPECIES. FURTHERMORE, DATA GENERATED IN THIS OPTION WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO CSU AND FHCC SYSTEMS BIOLOGISTS IN THE CORRECT FORMAT, AS DEFINED IN THE BASE PERIOD, FOR INTEGRATED ANALYSIS. ITERATIVE ANALYSIS WILL INVOLVE PRECLINICAL BIOLOGISTS AND SYSTEMS BIOLOGISTS FOR OPTIMAL DATA INTEGRITY AND IMPACT. MICE WILL BE PROPHYLACTICALLY VACCINATED ONCE WITH BCG [SUBCUTANEOUS OR INTRADERMAL] OR TWICE WITH ID93+GLA-SE [0.5 Ã‚ÂΜG FUSION PROTEIN DELIVERED IN 5Ã‚ÂΜG GLA STABLE EMULSION ADJUVANT INTRAMUSCULARLY]. CONTROL MICE WILL INJECTED WITH SALINE OR GLA-SE ALONE ON THE SAME REGIMEN AS ID93+GLA-SE. IN CHALLENGE STUDIES WE WILL INFECT GROUPS OF MICE (4 MALE AND 4 FEMALE, 8 TOTAL PER GROUP) BY LOW-DOSE AEROSOL (LDA, 50-100 BACTERIA INTO THE LUNGS) WITH ONE EXPERIMENT SUITE RECEIVING LABORATORY ISOLATE M.TB ERDMAN AND A SEPARATE SUITE RECEIVING CLINICAL ISOLATE M.TB HN878. FOR AEROSOL CHALLENGE, MICE ARE PLACED IN A GLAS-COL CIRCULAR [5-CHAMBER] STAINLESS STEEL CAGING SYSTEM WHICH IS THEN PLACED IN A CENTRAL CHAMBER AND SEALED BY A GASKET. AEROSOLIZED BACTERIA ARE GENERATED IN A NEBULIZER AND BLOWN THROUGH THE CENTRAL CHAMBER FOR 30-MINUTES, FOLLOWED BY CLEAN AIR AND BRIEF EXPOSURE TO ULTRA-VIOLET LIGHT. description: PROMPT DIAGNOSTICS LLC (PROMPT) IS DEVELOPING A PCR PLATFORM THAT WILL STREAMLINE SAMPLE-TO-ANSWER STI IDENTIFICATION AND AMR RESULTS WITHIN 20 MINUTES IN A LOW-COST, PORTABLE PACKAGE. THIS PLATFORM IS BUILT ON MAGNETOFLUIDIC CARTRIDGE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPED BY THE CO-FOUNDERS OF PROMPT, DR. JEFF WANG AND DR. ALEXANDER TRICK. WITH MAGNETOFLUIDIC CARTRIDGES, AUTOMATION OF NUCLEIC ACID EXTRACTION FROM PATIENT SAMPLES AND TRANSFER TO PCR IS AUTOMATED WITH MAGNETIC ATTRACTION OF MICRON-SCALE BEADS THROUGH PRELOADED REAGENTS. THIS TECHNIQUE OBVIATES THE NEED FOR COMPLEX FLUIDIC CONTROLS, ENABLES SAMPLE PROCESSING OF BIOLOGICAL MATRICES INCLUDING BLOOD PLASMA, SALIVA, AND URINE, AND IS SIMPLE ENOUGH TO PACKAGE IN A PORTABLE BATTERY-POWERED DEVICE. THE PROPOSED HIGHLY MULTIPLEXED STI/AMR ASSAY WILL WILL PROVIDE A POWERFUL DIAGNOSTIC TO CONFIRM THE PRESENCE OF NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE (NG), CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS (CT), AND TRICHOMONAS VAGINALIS (TV) INFECTIONS WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY GUIDING TREATMENT OF NG WITH GENOTYPIC CHARACTERIZATION OF RESISTANCE TO CIPROFLOXACIN, AZITHROMYCIN, AND CEFTRIAXONE.

description: GENERAL DESCRIPTION: WE PROPOSE TO COLLECT SPUTUM AND BLOOD SPECIMENS FROM 20 RESEARCH PARTICIPANTS (10 ENROLLED IN THE FIRST YEAR AND 10 IN THE SECOND YEAR) WITH ESTABLISHED DIAGNOSIS OF CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE OR COPD (CHRONIC BRONCHITIS OR MIXED PHENOTYPES, I.E., THOSE WHO REPORT COUGH AND SPUTUM PRODUCTION FOR AT LEAST 3 MONTHS ANNUALLY IN THE PAST 2 YEARS, WITH AND WITHOUT EVIDENCE OF EMPHYSEMA ON IMAGING STUDIES). MALE AND FEMALE SUBJECTS BETWEEN 40 AND 80 YEARS OF AGE WILL BE ENROLLED; WOMEN OF REPRODUCTIVE AGE WILL UNDERGO PREGNANCY TESTING BEFORE THE STUDY PROCEDURES ARE EMPLOYED. IN ORDER TO ELIMINATE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF HETEROGENEITY RELATED TO SMOKING STATUS, WE WILL ENROLL ONLY EX-SMOKERS (I.E., THOSE WHO QUIT SMOKING EITHER REGULAR OR ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES, AT LEAST 6 MONTHS PRIOR TO THE ENROLLMENT DATE), AND AT LEAST 2 WEEKS AFTER A KNOWN COPD EXACERBATION TREATED WITH ANTIBIOTICS AND/OR CORTICOSTEROIDS. SMOKING CESSATION WILL BE DOCUMENTED BY MEASURING COTININE LEVELS IN THE COLLECTED BLOOD SAMPLES. PROCEDURES: DEMOGRAPHIC, ANTHROPOMETRIC, FUNCTIONAL AND IMAGING DATA RELEVANT TO THE UNDERLYING DIAGNOSIS, AS WELL AS COPD EXACERBATION HISTORY, USE OF MEDICATIONS AND SUPPLEMENTAL OXYGEN WILL BE COLLECTED. NO INTERVENTION IS PLANNED ON THE ENROLLED PARTICIPANTS. IN ORDER TO BETTER CHARACTERIZE FUNCTIONALLY THEIR DISEASE SEVERITY, WE WILL PERFORM FIRST PULMONARY FUNCTION TESTS (PFTS) IN OUR LABORATORY, CONSISTING OF SPIROMETRY (BEFORE AND AFTER INHALED BRONCHODILATOR ADMINISTRATION), LUNG VOLUME AND DLCO MEASUREMENTS. AFTER INFORMED CONSENT IS OBTAINED, PFTS ARE PERFORMED BETWEEN 8 AND 10 AM LOCAL TIME. AFTER THE PFTS ARE PERFORMED, SPUTUM AND BLOOD SPECIMENS ARE OBTAINED IN THE ATLANTA VA CLINICAL RESEARCH CENTER; THE CLINICAL RESEARCH TEAM MEMBERS WILL WEAR APPROPRIATE PPE (PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT) FOR ALL INDUCTION AND COLLECTION OF RESPIRATORY AND WHOLE BLOOD SPECIMENS. ONCE COLLECTED, THE SPECIMENS WILL BE KEPT ON ICE AND HAND-DELIVERED IMMEDIATELY TO THE PROCESSING LAB AT EMORY UNIVERSITY. THE LOCAL CLINICAL PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR OR DESIGNEE WILL ENSURE THAT SAMPLES ARE LABELLED AND SHIPPED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LABORATORY MANUAL AND THE BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE REGULATIONS. description: OPTION 12B: DESCRIPTION OF WORK: IN SUPPORT OF THE MUCOSAL SAMPLING CONSORTIUM TO INFORM PROJECT NEXTGEN, THE CENTER FOR VACCINE DEVELOPMENT AND GLOBAL HEALTH (CVDGH) AT UMB WILL COLLECT MUCOSAL AND BLOOD SAMPLES THROUGH AN EXISTING DONOR PROTOCOL (CVD 4000). SAMPLES WILL EITHER BE SHIPPED DIRECTLY TO A CENTRAL REPOSITORY OR WILL BE PROCESSED AT UMB AND THEN SHIPPED TO THE REPOSITORY. NASAL AND SALIVA SAMPLES FROM ALL FOUR CONSORTIUM SITES WILL BE SHIPPED FROM THE CENTRAL REPOSITORY TO DR. MARCELA PASETTIÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S APPLIED IMMUNOLOGY LABORATORY (AIL) FOR MUCOSAL ANTIBODY ANALYSES. A. CVDGH CLINIC: THE CLINIC WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR CONSENTING AND ENROLLING ELIGIBLE DONORS IN THE BLOOD DONOR CVD 4000 PROTOCOL. AFTER ENROLLMENT AND SCREENING, MUCOSAL AND BLOOD SAMPLES (TABLE 1) WILL BE COLLECTED FROM 10-15 PARTICIPANTS ON DAY 1, DAY 3, AND DAY 15 USING HARMONIZED SAMPLING PROTOCOLS. THE CLINIC WILL COLLECT AND SECURELY MAINTAIN DEMOGRAPHIC AND BASELINE MEDICAL DATA. I. UP TO 270 SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED. TWO NASAL AND TWO SALIVA SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED AT EACH VISIT FROM EACH PARTICIPANT (LEFT AND RIGHT SIDES). ONE MID-TURBINATE SWAB WILL BE COLLECTED FROM EACH PARTICIPANT AT ALL TIMEPOINTS. AT ONE TIMEPOINT, VENOUS BLOOD WILL BE COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS FOR PBMCS, SERUM, AND/OR PLASMA. B. APPLIED IMMUNOLOGY LABORATORY: THE AIL (PASETTI LAB) SPECIMEN PROCESSING GROUP WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROCESSING (PBMCS, SERUM, PLASMA), LABELING, STORING, AND SHIPPING ALL SAMPLES COLLECTED BY THE CLINIC. ADDITIONALLY, THE AIL WILL CONDUCT ANALYSES ON NASAL AND SALIVARY SAMPLES TO QUANTIFY BINDING ANTIBODIES SPECIFIC TO SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS AND TOTAL ANTIBODIES. I. SPECIMEN PROCESSING AND MANAGEMENT: THE AIL SPECIMEN PROCESSING GROUP WILL RECEIVE THE OUTLINED SAMPLES (TABLE 1) FROM THE CVDGH CLINIC. NASAL SECRETIONS (NASOSORPTION), SALIVA (ORACOL+), AND NASAL CELL (MID-TURBINATE SWAB) SAMPLES WILL BE LABELED, DOCUMENTED, RECORDED IN GLOBALTRACE, AND STORED PER THE PROTOCOL. BLOOD SAMPLES WILL BE PROCESSED BY THE SPECIMEN PROCESSING GROUP TO COLLECT SERUM, PBMCS, AND/OR PLASMA ACCORDING TO THE STUDY PROTOCOL. SAMPLES WILL BE ALIQUOTED, LABELED, AND STORED AS INSTRUCTED. ALL SAMPLES WILL BE STORED AND MONITORED UNTIL THEY ARE SHIPPED TO THE CENTRAL REPOSITORY ONCE DIRECTED. II. SAMPLE TESTING: THE AIL WILL ALSO MEASURE MUCOSAL ANTIBODIES SPECIFIC TO SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS OF INTEREST IN NASAL SECRETIONS (NASOSORPTION) AND SALIVA (ORACOL+) USING A CUSTOMIZED MULTIPLEXED BINDING ANTIBODY ASSAY FROM MESO SCALE DISCOVERY (MSD). TOTAL IGG AND IGA CONTENT WILL ALSO BE QUANTIFIED WITH THE MSD HU/NHP ISOTYPING PANEL 1 MULTIPLEXED ASSAY. NASOSORPTION AND ORACOL+ SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM ALL PARTICIPANTS AT ALL SITES WILL BE SHIPPED TO THE AIL FROM THE CENTRAL REPOSITORY FOR TESTING. UP TO 360 MUCOSAL SAMPLES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR SARS-COV-2-SPECIFIC AND TOTAL IGG AND IGA (TABLE 2). I. THE MSD V-PLEX SARS-COV-2 CUSTOM 10-SPOT PLATE INCLUDES EIGHT SARS-COV-2 ANTIGENS. SEVERAL ANTIGENS MAY BE PRIORITIZED AND ANTIBODY DATA AGAINST THE OTHER ANTIGENS WILL BE ANALYZED AND REPORTED LATER. PRIORITY ANTIGENS ARE TBD. II. INDIVIDUAL NASAL FLUID SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM THE LEFT OR RIGHT NOSTRILS MAY BE EVALUATED AND/OR POOLED SAMPLES MAY BE TESTED. THE CONSTRUCT OF THE SAMPLE SET IS TO BE DETERMINED BUT SHOULD NOT EXCEED 360 SAMPLES. III. SARS-COV-2-SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES MAY BE MEASURED IN SERUM. TESTING OF SERUM IS TO BE DETERMINED.

AHRI,PARTNERS TOWARDS BI-DIRECTIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF ALL STUDIES AND INTERVENTION IMPLEMENTATIONS – FROM CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORKS TO ANALYSIS AND PUBLICATION. WORK PACKAGE 1 (WP1): OBJECTIVE: BASELINE BIONOMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF ETHIOPIAN POPULATIONS OF AN. STEPHENSI, IN RELATIONSHIP TO APPROPRIATE INTERVENTION STRATEGIES AND THEIR EVALUATION. SUB-OBJECTIVES OUTLINED ARE BASED ON THE QUESTION BEING ASKED AND OVERLAP IN TERMS OF STUDY IMPLEMENTATION. SUB-OBJECTIVE 1.1: TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING THE SAMPLING DEVICE THAT APPROPRIATELY CAPTURES AN. STEPHENSI (BASED ON THE QUESTION) A LATIN SQUARE STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED USING MULTIPLE SAMPLING METHODS. COMPARING THESE METHODS WILL ALLOW US TO UNDERSTAND THE RELATIONSHIPS (CATCH RATES) BETWEEN SAMPLING METHODS (ESPECIALLY WITH HLCS) TOWARDS THE UTILITY OF EACH METHOD IN LONGITUDINAL ADULT SAMPLING (HUMAN BITING RATE, INVASION DETECTION, INTERVENTION EFFECTIVENESS, CHANGES IN BIONOMICS, ETC.). THIS STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED IN BOTH AN URBAN AND RURAL AREA WITH AN. STEPHENSI POPULATIONS PRESENT. A GAPS IN PROTECTION ANALYSIS WILL ENABLE US TO UNDERSTAND WHERE AND WHEN HUMANS ARE EXPOSED TO VECTOR BITES, ITN PROTECTIONS, AND THE POTENTIAL OF SUPPLEMENTARY INTERVENTION PARADIGMS SUCH AS SPATIAL REPELLENTS AND ENDECTOCIDES. SUB-OBJECTIVE 1.3: TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING THE POTENTIAL (AND LIMITATIONS) OF INDOOR RESIDUAL SPRAYING (IRS) AS AN INTERVENTION, PYRETHROID SPRAY CATCHES (PSCS) (OR INDOOR ASPIRATIONS (IAS)) WILL BE CONDUCTED INSIDE SLEEPING STRUCTURES AND ANIMAL SHELTERS. ENDECTOCIDES). SUB-OBJECTIVE 1.5: COMPREHENSIVE LARVAL SAMPLING IN BOTH URBAN AND RURAL AREAS WITH AN. STEPHENSI, WILL ELUCIDATE THE POTENTIAL AND REQUIREMENTS FOR LARVICIDING (AND LARVAL SOURCE MANAGEMENT), INVASION DETECTION, AS WELL AS GENERATING SAMPLES FOR INSECTICIDE RESISTANCE ASSAYS. description: THE PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO COMPREHENSIVELY ANALYZE THE SPILLOVER EFFECTS OF THE GOVERNMENT CLIENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S MODEL TESTS ON THE HEALTHCARE MARKET. THE CONTRACTOR WILL CONDUCT A QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY, DESCRIBE, AND CATALOGUE THESE EFFECTS, CONSIDERING FACTORS SUCH AS THE REASONS, TIMING, METHODS OF SPILLOVER, AND THE AFFECTED HEALTHCARE STAKEHOLDERS. RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WILL ENCOMPASS LITERATURE REVIEWS, MARKET SCANS, INTERVIEWS WITH VARIOUS STAKEHOLDERS, AND DATA ANALYSIS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL DOCUMENT AND SHARE KEY TAKEAWAYS FROM THE INTERVIEWS. THE FINDINGS WILL BE COMPILED INTO A REPORT AND PRESENTATION DETAILING THE TYPES AND MAGNITUDE OF SPILLOVER EFFECTS, THEIR CATEGORIZATION, DESCRIPTIONS OF THE GOVERNMENT CLIENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S MODEL SPILLOVER EFFECTS, AND THE CORRELATION OF SPECIFIC EFFECTS TO ROOT CAUSES. THE REPORT WILL FEATURE REAL MARKET EXAMPLES AND CASE STUDIES OF STAKEHOLDERS' SPILLOVER EFFECTS. FINALLY, THE FINDINGS WILL BE VALIDATED THROUGH PRESSURE TESTING WITH INDUSTRY EXPERTS AND STAKEHOLDER REPRESENTATIVES.

description: THE SCOPE OF WORK AT THE GEORGETOWN UNIVERSITY LABORATORY WILL INCLUDE THE CONTINUED USE OF ITS LIBRARY OF CELL LINES THAT STABLY EXPRESS DIFFERENT SUBTYPES OF NEURONAL NICOTINIC ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTORS (NACHRS) TO SCREEN COMPOUNDS SENT TO THE PDSP FROM LABORATORIES THROUGHOUT THE U.S. FOR ACTIVITY AT NACHR SUBTYPES. THE COMPOUNDS THAT DISPLAY HIGH AFFINITY FOR ANY OF THE NACHRS ARE FURTHER EXAMINED IN FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS. THOSE COMPOUNDS WHICH HAVE VERY FAST CHANNEL KINETICS THAT MAKE IT VIRTUALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO ACCURATELY MEASURE ITS FUNCTION WITH BIOCHEMICAL METHODS, THE LAB WILL CONTINUE TO MEASURE ITS ION CHANNEL FUNCTION ELECTRO-PHYSIOLOGICALLY VIA FAST PATCH CLAMP METHODS.

description: THIS STUDY WILL UTILIZE SYSTEMS IMMUNOLOGY APPROACHES TO INVESTIGATE THE IMMUNE SIGNATURES GENERATED BY OUR SARNA YFV VACCINE AND COMPARE THESE TO THE GOLD STANDARD YFV-17D LIVE-ATTENUATED VACCINE (YF-VAX). IMMUNE SIGNATURES WILL BE OBTAINED BY TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS FOLLOWING PRIME AND BOOST IMMUNIZATIONS AND WILL CAPTURE BOTH EARLY INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE SIGNATURES. IN ADDITION, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE GENERATED BY OUR VACCINE PLATFORM. WE WILL CORRELATE THESE SIGNATURES TO RESPONSE MEASURES OF CELLULAR AND HUMORAL IMMUNITY. CELLULAR IMMUNITY WILL FOCUS ON MARKERS OF MEMORY DEPOSITION FOR B CELLS (E.G., CD27) AND T CELLS AS A PRELIMINARY INDICATOR OF RESPONSE DURABILITY AND LONGEVITY.

description: KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE IS A MAJOR CAUSE OF HOSPITAL-ACQUIRED INFECTIONS AND HAS RECENTLY BEEN RECOGNIZED AS A LEADING CAUSE OF NEONATAL SEPSIS. PREVIOUSLY SUCCESSFUL ANTIBIOTIC REGIMENS FOR K. PNEUMONIAE ARE RAPIDLY BECOMING INEFFECTIVE DUE TO THE GROWING INCIDENCE OF MULTI-DRUG RESISTANT (MDR) STRAINS. THERE ARE NO LICENSED VACCINES TO PREVENT K. PNEUMONIAE INFECTIONS AND CURRENTLY ONLY ONE VACCINE IS IN CLINICAL TESTING. ANTIBODIES TARGETING K. PNEUMONIAE O POLYSACCHARIDES (OPS) ARE PROTECTIVE AGAINST K. PNEUMONIAE INFECTIONS AND ARE UNAFFECTED BY MDR PHENOTYPES. BACTERIAL POLYSACCHARIDES ARE GENERALLY POOR IMMUNOGENS, HOWEVER, THAT DO NOT ELICIT ROBUST OR DURABLE ANTIBODY LEVELS, AFFINITY MATURATION, CLASS SWITCHING, OR IMMUNOLOGIC MEMORY. THESE LIMITATIONS HAVE BEEN OVERCOME BY CHEMICAL LINKAGE (I.E., CONJUGATION) TO PROTEINS. SINCE 4 K. PNEUMONIAE OPS SEROTYPES (O1, O2, O3, O5) ARE ASSOCIATED WITH > 80% OF K. PNEUMONIAE BACTEREMIC INFECTIONS, IN PRINCIPLE, A QUADRIVALENT K. PNEUMONIAE OPS-BASED CONJUGATE VACCINE WOULD BE FEASIBLE, IMMUNOGENIC AND BROADLY PROTECTIVE. THE LIMITED NUMBER OF ANTIGENIC COMPONENTS WOULD ALSO REDUCE THE COST AND COMPLEXITY OF MANUFACTURING AND FORMULATION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A CONJUGATE VACCINE THAT CAN BE ADMINISTERED TO PREGNANT WOMEN TO PROTECT THEIR INFANTS FROM SEPSIS DUE TO K. PNEUMONIAE.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO QUANTIFY THE RISK OF PATHOGEN TRANSFER TO ENVIRONMENTS AND PATIENTS ASSOCIATED WITH DIFFERENT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT USES FOR HEALTHCARE WORKERS. WE WILL DEVELOP A MATHEMATICAL MODEL TO EXTRAPOLATE THE RISK OF PATHOGEN TRANSFER DURING MULTIPLE CONTAMINATION EVENTS. WE WILL PARAMETERIZE THE MODEL WITH THE DATA COLLECTED ON DURING THE OBSERVATIONAL PERIODS (4H) IN THE EXTENT PPE STUDY. SIMULATION SCENARIOS SUMMARIZING THE RISK OF PATHOGEN TRANSFER AND PATIENT/HEALTHCARE WORKER EXPOSURE FOR ONE OR MULTIPLE SHIFTS, AND WARD-LEVEL CONTAMINATION WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AND ANALYZED. ASSOCIATED TASKS: 1. DEVELOP A MATHEMATICAL MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE THE ACCUMULATIVE RISK OF CONTAMINATION ASSOCIATED TO A SET OF EVENTS (E.G. DONNING, HAND WASHING CONTACT WITH ROOM SURFACES, CONTACT WITH OUTSIDE ROOM SURFACES, DOFFING). WE WILL COMPARE TWO COMMONLY APPROACHES TO ADDRESS FOMITE-MEDIATED TRANSMISSION: DISCRETE EVENT-BASED SIMULATION AND DISCRETE MARKOV CHAIN MODELS. 2. PARAMETERIZE THE MATHEMATICAL MODEL WITH THE COLLECTED DATA ON SEQUENCE OF EVENTS AND PROBABILITIES OF CONTAMINATION OBSERVED DURING OBSERVATIONAL PERIODS. 3. VERIFY AND VALIDATE THE MODEL WITH A SUBSET OF THE AVAILABLE DATA 4. PERFORM SIMULATIONS TO REPRESENT SCENARIOS OF INTEREST (E.G. RISK OF CONTAMINATION FOLLOWING A COMPLETE SHIFT). 5. SUMMARIZE RESULTS FOR PUBLICATION AND FINAL REPORT TIMELINE: YEAR 2 (09/23 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ 8/24): MODEL DEVELOPMENT AND PARTIAL PARAMETERIZATION AND ANALYSIS (TASKS 1- 2) YEAR (9/24-8/25): COMPLETE PARAMETERIZATION, VALIDATION AND SCENARIO SIMULATION (TASKS 2-5) EXCERPT FROM IRB STUDY PROTOCOL: "IN ORDER TO EXPAND THE SCOPE OF THE STUDY FINDINGS, WE WILL UTILIZE MATHEMATICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING STRATEGIES TO PROJECT THE FINDINGS OF THE STUDY, WHICH SIMULATE SELFCONTAMINATION AND DOWNSTREAM ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINATION ATTRIBUTABLE TO A SINGLE CONTAMINATION, TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF MULTIPLE SEQUENTIAL CONTAMINATION EVENTS THAT MIGHT OCCUR DURING A HEALTHCARE SHIFT. THE MODELING ANALYSIS WILL BE LED BY DR. CRISTINA LANZAS, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF POPULATION HEALTH AND PATHOBIOLOGY AT NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY. DE-IDENTIFIED DATA FROM THE STUDY WILL BE SHARED WITH DR. LANZAS IN ORDER TO INFORM THE MODELING ANALYSIS. THIS DATA WILL INCLUDE DATE/TIME STAMPS FROM THE STUDY OBSERVATIONS; HOWEVER, PARTICIPANTS WILL BE IDENTIFIED ONLY BY THEIR STUDY ID NUMBER. DR. LANZAS AND HER TEAM WILL NOT HAVE ACCESS TO PARTICIPANT NAMES OR OTHER IDENTIFYING INFORMATION."

description: BACKGROUND/CONTEXT: S-TAC IS FUNDED BY THE SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA) TO SUPPORT STATES IMPLEMENTING THE CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC (CCBHC) MODEL THROUGH THEIR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND MEDICAID SYSTEMS. IT ALSO AIMS TO PROMOTE AN INTEGRATED AND COORDINATED TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (TA) APPROACH THAT IS RESPONSIVE TO THE INCREASED NEEDS OF STATES WORKING TOWARD CCBHC UPTAKE AND IMPLEMENTATION ACROSS THE COUNTRY. THIS RESOURCE IS ONE REQUESTED BY SAMHSA AND IS REQUIRED TO BE COMPLETED BEFORE THE END OF THE PROJECT YEAR ON SEPT 15, 2024. THEREFORE, ITÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CRITICAL FOR THE S-TAC TEAM TO PARTNER WITH A LONGSTANDING EXPERT ON THIS TOPIC WHO CAN EXECUTE THIS IMPORTANT RESOURCE BY THE SAMHSA REQUESTED DEADLINE. MR. BOWLING (AND HIS TEAM AT BOWLING BUSINESS STRATEGIES) BRINGS EXPERTISE IN WORKING WITH SAMHSA AND SAMHSA-CONTRACTED PARTNERS ON TA DELIVERY AND THOUGHT LEADERSHIP ACTIVITIES RELATED TO STRATEGIC PLANNING, SERVICE DESIGN/IMPLEMENTATION, AND PAYMENT AND DELIVERY REFORMS. AS A SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT WITHIN THE NATIONAL COUNCILÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CCBHC SUCCESS CENTER, MR. BOWLING HAS CONTRIBUTED TO SHAPING AND ELEVATING THE MODEL BY AUTHORING SEVERAL CCBHC TOOLKITS AND RESOURCES FOR THE CENTER. HE HAS ALSO PROVIDED ESSENTIAL CCBHC-FOCUSED CONSULTING SERVICES INCLUDING RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC EXPANSION (CCBHC-E) TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE CENTER AND THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR INTEGRATED HEALTH SOLUTIONS (COE-IHS) FOR MANY YEARS. MR. BOWLING AND HIS TEAM OF CONSULTANTS WILL USE THEIR 20+ YEARS OF EXPERIENCE DESIGNING, OVERSEEING, AND EXECUTING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STRATEGY, POLICY, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND PROGRAMMING TO DEVELOP A SAMHSA-APPROVED CCBHC DATA PLATFORM AND HEALTH LEARNING NETWORK STRATEGY REPORT IN COLLABORATION WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL PROJECT TEAM. SCOPE: TASK ORDER 2 Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ TASK 2.7: RESOURCES AND MATERIAL DEVELOPMENT Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ LEAD THE PROJECT MANAGEMENT (INCLUDING PLANNING, DRAFTING, AND COMPLETION) OF A 12Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ30-PAGE RESOURCE. THE TOPIC AND PROPOSED CONTENT OF THIS RESOURCE HAVE BEEN APPROVED BY SAMHSA. KEY DELIVERABLES FOR THIS RESOURCE WILL INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: CONTRACT NO. _2850.0013_ PAGE 1 OF 11 O LEAD A PROJECT KICK-OFF AND ONGOING DISCOVERY CALLS. O PROVIDE ONGOING PROJECT MANAGEMENT TO AID IN THE COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED RESOURCES. O CONDUCT A REVIEW OF ACADEMIC LITERATURE AND ONLINE RESOURCES. O CONDUCT BACKGROUND INTERVIEWS WITH SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS. O DEVELOP AN INFORMATION GATHERING PLAN AND ASSOCIATED INFORMATION GATHERING TOOLS (I.E., INTERVIEW QUESTIONS AND FACILITATION GUIDES) O FACILITATE INFORMATION GATHERING, VISIONING ACTIVITIES, AND SOLICIT IDEAS FROM STAKEHOLDERS. O DEVELOP AND PRESENT A DRAFT ANNOTATED OUTLINE AND INCORPORATE EDITS INTO A FINALIZED OUTLINE. O DRAFT AN APPROXIMATELY 20-PAGE RESOURCE. O RECEIVE AND INCORPORATE FEEDBACK AND EDITS INTO A FINALIZED RESOURCE.

description: DEVERICK J. ANDERSON, IS A PROFESSOR OF MEDICINE IN THE DUKE CENTER FOR ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP AND INFECTION PREVENTION AND IN THE DIVISION OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES IN THE DEPARTMENT OF MEDICINE AT DUKE UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF MEDICINE. ANDERSON IS ALSO THE EXECUTIVE MEDICAL DIRECTOR OF THE DUKE INFECTION CONTROL OUTREACH NETWORK (DICON), THE CODIRECTOR OF THE DUKE ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP OUTREACH NETWORK (DASON) AND HAS EXTENSIVE KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE IN INFECTION PREVENTION AND ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP. THE NETWORK ALSO PROVIDES FOCUSED AND PRACTICAL STRATEGIES TO PREVENT HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS FOR 80 ADDITIONAL HOSPITALS LOCATED THROUGHOUT THE UNITED STATES THAT HAVE SIGNED CONTRACTS TO USE ONLINE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS AND PREVENTION INITIATIVES DEVELOPED BY DICON. IN HIS ROLE AS PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR, DR. ANDERSON WILL OVERSEE ALL ADMINISTRATIVE ASPECTS OF THE PROJECT. DR. ANDERSON WILL HELP PROVIDE DATA AND CLINICAL EXPERTISE TO THE MODELING TEAM AT WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY THROUGH THE EXTRACTION OF DATASETS AND ANALYSES. DR. ANDERSON HAS 10.20 CALENDAR MONTHS AVAILABLE FOR ACTIVITIES AT DUKE UNIVERSITY, AND THE INSTITUTIONAL BASE SALARY AND EFFORT REQUESTED IS BASED ON DUKE UNIVERSITY ACTIVITIES ONLY AND THE SALARY CAP HAS BEEN PRORATED TO REFLECT THE % DUKE APPOINTMENT.

description: TUFTS UNIVERSITY WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR IDENTIFYING PATIENTS WITH LYME DISEASE IN THE TUFTSMEDICINE HOSPITAL AND PRIMARY CARE NETWORK THROUGH REGULARLY SCHEDULED ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHR) SCANS AND EXTRACTING CLINICAL INFORMATION TO PROVIDE DEIDENTIFIED DETAILS OF THE DISEASE TO A COMBINED DATABASE AT MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL HOSPITAL (MGH) FOR SUBSEQUENT TRANSMISSION TO THE CDC. TUFTS UNIVERSITY INVESTIGATORS WILL WORK WITH MGH INVESTIGATORS TO CREATE A UNIFIED AND EFFECTIVE CASE DEFINITION FOR IDENTIFYING PATIENTS WITH LYME DISEASE.TUFTS UNIVERSITY INVESTIGATORS WILL ASSIST IN THE MODEL DEVELOPMENT, VALIDATION, AND DEPLOYMENT PROCESS AS DESCRIBED IN THE FULL PROPOSAL. WE WILL FIRST DEVELOP A BASELINE MODEL OF SUBJECTS PRESENTING TO TUFTSMEDICINE WHO ARE DIAGNOSED AS HAVING LYME DISEASE BY ICD9/10 CODES. WE WILL THEN WORK WITH MASS GENERAL BRIGHAM AND MAINEHEALTH TO DERIVE ONE OR MORE IMPROVED MODELS BY IDENTIFYING INFORMATIVE DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FROM CLINICAL, MICROBIOLOGICAL, EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND FREE TEXT DATA IN CASE AND CONTROL VISITS. WE WILL COMPARE THE PERFORMANCE OF ONE OR MORE IMPROVED MODELS AND SELECT THE BEST-PERFORMING ONE. WE WILL IMPLEMENT THE BEST-PERFORMING MODEL FOR RECORDS AT TUFTS UNIVERSITY, SUMMARIZE THE RESULTS, AND AGGREGATE SUMMARY STATISTICS ACROSS SITES. BASED ON A UNIFIED, EFFECTIVE CASE DEFINITION AND A ROBUST MODEL TO IDENTIFY CASES OF LYME DISEASE FROM EHR DATA, WE WILL CONDUCT TARGETED COLLECTIONS. WE WILL IDENTIFY POTENTIAL RECRUITMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR RESEARCH SUBJECTS BASED ON SPECIFIC CRITERIA (E.G. NEUROBORRELIOSIS, PREGNANCY, SUSPECTED CO-INFECTIONS, VACCINATION RECIPIENT) DEFINED IN CONSULTATION WITH THE FULL INVESTIGATOR TEAM AND THE RELEVANT TECHNICAL TEAM AT CDC. WE WILL ENROLL A SUBSET OF THESE INDIVIDUALS IN CLINICAL STUDIES TO ASSESS ASPECTS OF LYME DISEASE POTENTIALLY INCLUDING THE PERFORMANCE OF DIAGNOSTIC ASSAYS, THE OUTCOMES OF PREGNANCY-ASSOCIATED LYME DISEASE, AND VACCINE EFFICACY.

description: SOW FOR SUBCONTRACTOR CUPS3 COLLABORATION ON EHR DATA GATHERING AND ANALYSIS OVERVIEW: UCSF HOLDS AN FDA CONTRACT ENTITLED, Ã¢Â‚¬Å“COMMUNITY USES OF PSYCHEDELICS AND SAFETY STUDYÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ (CUPS) WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF USING A MULTIMODAL SET OF RESEARCH METHODS TO ASSESS FOR EMERGING TRENDS OF HARM, AND ESTABLISHED METHODS FOR ASSURING SAFETY, AMONG PSYCHEDELIC USERS IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE TRAJECTORY OF PSYCHEDELICS USE AND ASSOCIATED PUBLIC HEALTH CONSEQUENCES. THE SUBPROJECT CUPS3 WILL INVESTIGATE THE ASSOCIATION OF IMPLEMENTATION OF DRUG REGULATORY CHANGES IN OREGON WITH PSILOCYBIN-RELATED ADVERSE OUTCOMES BY COLLECTING DETAILED DE-IDENTIFIED* INDIVIDUAL PATIENT-LEVEL DATA ON RELEVANT ENCOUNTERS FROM INSTITUTIONAL ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHRS). THE SUBCONTRACTING SITE WILL PROVIDE DATA FOR THIS EFFORT. THE SUBCONTRACTING INVESTIGATOR WILL CONTRIBUTE THEIR EFFORT AND THE EFFORT OF THEIR STAFF TO SECURING EHR DATA FROM THEIR HEALTHCARE INSTITUTION SITES LOCATED IN THE STATE OF OREGON. IN ADDITION TO SHARING DATA, THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL COLLABORATE ON DATA ANALYSIS AND MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION AND CO-AUTHORSHIP. DATA OWNERSHIP IS TO BE DETERMINED BY THE APPROPRIATE DATA USE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE SUBCONTRACTOR AND THE PRIME CONTRACTOR (UCSF). SALARIES WILL BE LIMITED TO FEDERAL EXECUTIVE LEVEL II. SUMMARY OF APPROACH: INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL PATIENT DATA FROM ENCOUNTERS THAT ARE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (ED) VISITS AND PSYCHIATRIC OR MEDICAL HOSPITALIZATIONS AS DOCUMENTED IN AN ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) WITH DIAGNOSTIC CODES THAT INDICATE HALLUCINOGEN OR PSYCHEDELIC USE. DATA REQUESTED INCLUDE PATIENT DATA (E.G., DEMOGRAPHICS, COMORBIDITIES) AND ENCOUNTER DATA (E.G., MEDICATIONS ADMINISTERED, DIAGNOSES, DISPOSITION). RETROSPECTIVE DATA WILL BE SHARED TO ESTABLISH A BASELINE FROM WHICH TO COMPARE CURRENT AND FUTURE TRENDS; DATA WILL ALSO BE COLLECTED AND SHARED AT QUARTERLY INTERVALS. description: THE MATIC-2 TRIAL IS A BAYESIAN, RANDOMIZED, MULTICENTER, ADAPTIVE PLATFORM PHASE III TRIAL. THE TRIAL WILL INCLUDE INJURED CHILDREN WITH HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK ANTICIPATED TO REQUIRE MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION, WHO WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE EITHER LTOWB OR CT AND TRANEXAMIC ACID OR PLACEBO. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE USE OF LTOWB IS NON-INFERIOR AND/OR SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY AND THAT LTOWB DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES, SUCH AS THROMBOTIC EVENTS, COMPARED TO CT. WE ALSO HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE USE OF TXA IS SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY AND DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES, SUCH AS THROMBOTIC EVENTS, COMPARED TO PLACEBO. THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1. DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF LTOWB TO REDUCE ALL-CAUSE 24-HOUR MORTALITY COMPARED TO CT IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. 2. DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TXA TO REDUCE ALL-CAUSE 24-HOUR MORTALITY COMPARED TO PLACEBO IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE.

description: INFECTIONS CAUSED BY MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT BACTERIA HAVE BECOME ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT THREATS TO GLOBAL HEALTH, RESULTING IN AN ESTIMATED 1.27 MILLION GLOBAL DEATHS IN 2019. GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA ARE OF PARTICULAR CONCERN, BECAUSE OF THEIR INTRINSIC RESISTANCE, RAPID ACQUISITION AND SPREAD OF NEW RESISTANCE, AND THE PAUCITY OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTIC DEVELOPMENT TARGETING THESE BACTERIA IN THE LAST DECADES. THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION AND THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION IDENTIFIED CARBAPENEM-RESISTANT ENTEROBACTERIACEAE AS HIGH PRIORITY PATHOGENS FOR WHICH NEW AND EFFECTIVE ANTIBIOTIC TREATMENTS ARE URGENTLY NEEDED. BAL2420 (ALSO NAMED BAL0302420) IS A NOVEL ANTIBACTERIAL CANDIDATE FOR DEVELOPMENT AS INTRAVENOUS (IV) TREATMENT FOR SEVERE INFECTIONS CAUSED BY GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. THE COMPOUND IS A 16-MER CYCLIC PEPTIDE WITH A DISULFIDE BRIDGE AND AN INHIBITOR OF THE LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE TRANSPORT PROTEIN A (LPTA), WHICH IS A NOVEL TARGET/MODE OF ACTION CURRENTLY NOT EXPLOITED BY ANY ANTIBIOTIC CURRENTLY AVAILABLE FOR CLINICAL USE. BAL2420 IS TO BE DEVELOPED AS A SAFE AND EFFECTIVE NOVEL TREATMENT OPTION FOR SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, INCLUDING BLOODSTREAM INFECTIONS ASSOCIATED WITH PNEUMONIA (HOSPITAL-ACQUIRED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA [HABP] / VENTILATOR-ASSOCIATED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA [VABP]), COMPLICATED INTRA-ABDOMINAL INFECTIONS (CIAIS), AND COMPLICATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CUTIS), AND FOR CIAIS, CUTIS, AND HABP/VABP. IF SUCCESSFULLY DEVELOPED THE PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE A NOVEL CLASS OF ANTIBIOTICS TO TREAT LIFE-THREATENING INFECTIONS CAUSED BY DIFFICULT-TO-TREAT GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA SUCH AS CARBAPENEM-RESISTANT ENTEROBACTERIACEAE (CRE) ADDRESSING A HIGH UNMET MEDICAL NEED. BAL2420 SHOWS POTENT, BACTERICIDAL ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITY AGAINST ENTEROBACTERIACEAE. ENTEROBACTERIACEAE ARE A FAMILY OF IMPORTANT PATHOGENS CAUSING INFECTIONS IN HUMANS AND INCLUDE BACTERIA SUCH AS ESCHERICHIA COLI OR KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE. BAL2420 IS ALSO ACTIVE AGAINST ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT BACTERIA INCLUDING CARBAPENEM-RESISTANT ENTEROBACTERIACEAE, STRAINS RESISTANT TO COLISTIN, AN ANTIBIOTIC REGARDED AS LAST-RESORT THERAPY, AND AGAINST STRAINS WITH MBLS AND PBP3 MUTATIONS. BAL2420 HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE EFFICACIOUS IN A WIDE VARIETY OF ANIMAL MODELS OF BACTERIAL INFECTION, INCLUDING LUNG AND URINARY TRACT MODELS. MOREOVER, THE CANDIDATE MOLECULE SHOWS FAVORABLE IN VITRO DMPK PROPERTIES, WITH GOOD PLASMA, LIVER MICROSOMAL, AND HEPATOCYTE STABILITIES, MODERATE PLASMA PROTEIN BINDING AND LOW POTENTIAL FOR DRUG-DRUG-INTERACTIONS. BAL2420 IS NOT GENOTOXIC OR PHOTOTOXIC AND HAS FAVORABLE SAFETY PROPERTIES WITH THE KIDNEY BEING THE PRIMARY TARGET ORGAN IN SYSTEMIC TOXICITY STUDIES. THE PROGRAM HAS NOW REACHED CLINICAL STAGE WITH THE CLINICAL TRIALS INFORMATION SYSTEM (CTIS) SUBMISSION ACHIEVED IN DECEMBER 2025. THE FIRST-IN-HUMAN STUDY (BAL2420-CP-101) INCLUDES SINGLE ASCENDING DOSE (SAD) AND MULTIPLE ASCENDING DOSE (MAD) PARTS AND BASILEA PLAN TO INITIATE THE FIRST IN-HUMAN CLINICAL STUDY IN THE FIRST HALF OF 2026.

description: OPTION 9B: 0258-A730-4609 RECOVERY AND IMMUNOLOGIC COMPARISONS ACROSS THE GROUP B MERBECOVIRUSES USING ANTIGENIC CARTOGRAPHY INTRODUCTION: MERBECOVIRUSES INCLUDE A DIVERSE ARRAY OF POSITIVE STRANDED RNA VIRUSES WITHIN THE BETACORONAVIRUS GENUS AND INCLUDE THE HIGHLY PATHOGENIC MERS-COV STRAIN THAT CAUSED 2604 LABORATORY-CONFIRMED CASES OF MIDDLE EAST RESPIRATORY SYNDROME (MERS) INCLUDING 936 ASSOCIATED DEATHS AT A CASE-FATALITY RATIO (CFR) OF 36% SINCE 2012. IMPORTANTLY, NUMEROUS ZOONOTIC BAT MERS-LIKE VIRUSES CIRCULATE IN NATURE INCLUDING SEVERAL STRAINS THAT CAN USE THE HUMAN DIPEPTIDYL PEPTIDASE RECEPTOR (HDPP4) FOR DOCKING AND ENTRY. SOME REPLICATE EFFICIENTLY OR ARE ANTICIPATED TO REPLICATE EFFICIENTLY IN PRIMARY HUMAN AIRWAY EPITHELIAL CELLS (E.G., MERS-422, MJHKU4R -COV-1, NEO, ), WHILE MOST HAVE NOT BEEN STUDIED. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO APPROVED VACCINES OR THERAPEUTICS FOR USE AGAINST MERS-COV INFECTION OR ANY OTHER MERBECOVIRUS. GIVEN THE EXTREME PATHOGENIC POTENTIAL OF MERS-COV, COUPLED WITH THE PRESENCE OF MERBECOVIRUSES THAT CAN USE DPP4 OR ANGIOTENSIN 1 CONVERTING ENZYME 2 (ACE2) AS RECEPTORS FOR DOCKING AND ENTRY, THE DEVELOPMENT OF PANMERBECOVIRUS VACCINES IS STILL CONSIDERED HIGH PRIORITY TARGETS FOR COUNTERMEASURE INVESTMENTS BY HEALTH AGENCIES ACROSS THE WORLD (HTTPS://WWW.WHO.INT/TEAMS/BLUEPRINT). THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DETERMINE THE ANTIGENIC DISTANCE BETWEEN HIGHLY HETEROGENEOUS MERBECOVIRUSES, CREATE AN ANTIGENIC CARTOGRAPHY MAP, AND PRODUCE DEFINED SERA AND RECOMBINANT VIRUS REAGENTS THAT WILL ENHANCE GLOBAL PREPAREDNESS AGAINST FUTURE MERBECOVIRUS EPIDEMICS AND PANDEMICS. THE PROPOSAL HAS THREE AIMS: AIM I) PRODUCTION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF MERBECOVIRUS SPIKE ANTIGENS AND PRODUCTION OF MURINE ANTISERUM. FROM PUBLISHED SEQUENCES, MERBECOVRIRUS SPIKE GENES WILL BE SYNTHESIZED AND EXPRESSED AT UNCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PROTEOMIC CORE. RECOMBINANT PROTEINS PLUS ADJUVANT WILL BE INJECTED INTO RODENTS FOR THE PRODUCTION OF SERUM NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES. AIM II) RECOVERY OF RECOMBINANT MERBECOVIRUSES AND DERIVATIVE VIRUSES ENCODING NANOLUCIFERASE. (FOR LIVE VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY DEVELOPMENT). A SELECT PANEL OF RECOMBINANT MERBECOVIRUSES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PUBLISHED SEQUENCES, INCLUDING DERIVATIVES THAT ENCODE THE NANOLUCIFERASE GENE IN REPLACE OF A KNOWN ACCESSORY ORF. LIVE VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS WILL BE DEVELOPED USING A 96 WELL FORMAT AS PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED BY OUR GROUP. AIM III) PERFORM LIVE VIRUS CROSS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS AND ANTIGENIC CARTOGRAPHY. USING CELLS EXPRESSING HDPP4, WE WILL PERFORM LIVE VIRUS NLUC NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS ACROSS EACH MEMBER OF THE PANEL, USING MURINE ANTISERUM (N=3/EACH SPIKE). THE RESULTS WILL BE SHARED WITH DR. DEREK SMITH, WHO WILL PERFORM ANTIGENIC CARTOGRAPHY STUDIES ON THE DATA. DELIVERABLES: RECOMBINANT MERBECOVIRUS SPIKES, RECOMBINANT WILDTYPE AND DERIVATIVE VIRUSES ENCODING NLUC, REFERENCE SERA, ANTIGENIC CARTOGRAPHY MAPS, IDENTIFICATION OF BNAB FROM EXISTING PANELS OBTAINED FROM COLLABORATORS ACROSS THE US AND ELSEWHERE. description: THE SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO (DRC), SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORTS AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE SEVERAL CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDIES. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, AND COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT FOR BIOSPECIMENS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT AND IT SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE FOLLOWING PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE INVITE PROTOCOL. THE INVITE PROTOCOL IS A MULTICENTER STUDY OF COVID-19 VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY, DURABILITY, AND BREAKTHROUGH SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME CORONAVIRUS-2 (SARS-COV-2) INFECTIONS IN PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE A COVID-19 VACCINE ACCORDING TO THEIR RESPECTIVE COUNTRYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S NATIONAL VACCINATION GUIDELINES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AVAILABLE COVID-19 VACCINES IN THE OVERALL STUDY POPULATION AND IN DEFINED SUBGROUPS AT 2 MONTHS POST COMPLETION OF VACCINE REGIMEN. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE PALM 007 PROTOCOL. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THE PALM 007 TRIAL ARE TO EVALUATE THE CLINICAL AND VIROLOGIC EFFICACY, AND SAFETY OF TECOVIRIMAT (TPOXX) IN PATIENTS WITH MONKEYPOX INFECTION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO SUPPORT ALL ASPECTS OF THE PALM 008 PROTOCOL. description: THE GOAL OF GLYPROVACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S WORK SUPPORTED BY CARB-X IS TO DEVELOP THEIR VACCINE ANTIGEN GPV02 AS A MATERNAL VACCINE CANDIDATE AGAINST NEO-NATAL SEPSIS. THE VACCINE, WHEN DEVELOPED TO APPROVAL AND MARKET, WILL BENEFIT MOTHERS AND NEWBORN IN LOW MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRIES, WHERE SERIOUS INFECTIONS WITH E. COLI IN BABIES POSE A SIGNIFICANT RISK AND WHERE TREATMENT FACILITIES AND HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS MAY BE DIFFICULT TO REACH. THE PROJECT WILL TAKE THE GPV02 BASED VACCINE TOWARDS AND THROUGH A FIRST-IN-HUMAN PHASE 1 CLINICAL SAFETY TRIAL. GPV02 IS GLYPROVACÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LEAD CANDIDATE AND REPRESENTS A NEW TYPE OF VACCINE. IT IS A SPECIFIC PROTEIN FOUND IN THE FAMILY OF BACTERIA CALLED E. COLI BUT WITH A UNIQUE FEATURE NOT PREVIOUSLY EXPLOITED IN BACTERIAL VACCINE DEVELOPMENT: GPV02 IS COVERED IN A TYPE OF SUGAR MODIFICATION CALLED Ã¢Â‚¬Å“GLYCOSYLATIONÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½. THE SUGAR MODIFIED SITES CAN BE MAPPED USING THE GLYPROVAC TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM BEMAP AND NOT ONLY CHANGE THE CHEMISTRY OF GPV02 BUT ARE ALSO FOUND TO BE RECOGNIZED TO A VERY HIGH EXTENT BY THE HUMAN IMMUNE SYSTEM. GPV02 IS PRESENT IN OVER 85% OF THE E. COLI STRAINS THAT CAUSE INFECTIONS IN HUMANS SUCH AS NEONATAL SEPSIS AS WELL AS HEALTHCARE ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (HAUTI) AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO PROVIDE PROTECTION AGAINST BOTH THESE TYPES OF INFECTION. COMPARISON OF THE PRODUCT PROFILES FOR BOTH THE MATERNAL VACCINE AND HAUTI REVEALED SYNERGIES IN THE CO-DEVELOPMENT OF GPV02 FOR THESE INDICATIONS. SPECIFICALLY, PRODUCTION PROCESSES ARE IDENTICAL, RESULTING IN SIGNIFICANT COST SAVINGS DURING THE GMP PHASE. ADDITIONALLY, THERE ARE SYNERGIES IN AREAS SUCH AS IMMUNOGENICITY STUDIES, POTENCY ASSAYS, AND SAFETY STUDIES. THEREFORE, GLYPROVAC WILL PURSUE, IN THIS PROJECT, NOT ONLY GPV02 FOR MATERNAL VACCINATION AGAINST NEONATAL SEPSIS, BUT ALSO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE DEVELOPMENT SYNERGIES TO MATURE A GPV02 BASED HAUTI VACCINE. THE LARGE UNMET NEED AND COMMERCIAL POTENTIAL FOR A HAUTI VACCINE WILL HELP DRIVE AND FUND THE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT FOR BOTH INDICATIONS TO THE BENEFIT OF PATIENTS IN BOTH INDICATIONS AND TO THE FIGHT AGAINST GLOBAL DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE!

description: STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (SA), CAUSES SERIOUS DISEASES INCLUDING BLOOD STREAM INFECTION, SEPSIS, ENDOCARDITIS, SURGICAL SITE INFECTIONS (SSI), AND PNEUMONIA. METHICILLIN RESISTANT SA (MRSA) IS CURRENTLY A LEADING CAUSE OF THESE LIFE THREATENING INFECTIONS WITH LIMITED OPTIONS FOR TREATMENT. FOUR VACCINE AND IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC APPROACHES TARGETING SA SURFACE ANTIGENS HAVE BEEN TESTED IN EFFICACY TRIALS IN HUMANS AND ALL HAVE FAILED. ONE OF THESE VACCINES (V710) CAUSED MULTI-ORGAN FAILURE IN VACCINATED INDIVIDUALS WHO WERE INFECTED WITH SA LEADING TO TRIAL TERMINATION BY FDA. STUDIES IN ANIMALS HAVE ALSO SHOWN THAT VACCINES TARGETING SURFACE ANTIGENS INCREASE THE RISK OF DEATH FROM SA INFECTION. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL, ENTIRELY TOXOID BASED VACCINE (LTB-SA7) FOR PREVENTION OF MRSA INFECTIONS. LTB-SA7 CONSISTS OF FIVE COMPONENTS REPRESENTING TOXOIDS FOR SIX SA TOXINS. DUE TO CROSS REACTIVITY, THESE TOXOIDS ELICIT PROTECTIVE RESPONSES TO 12-15 SA TOXINS. EFFICACY OF THE LTB-SA7 COMPONENTS HAS BEEN SHOWN IN VARIOUS MOUSE AND RABBIT MODELS OF INFECTION. THIS IS THE FIRST ENTIRELY NON-SURFACE ANTIGEN BASED VACCINE FOR SA DISEASE. THE STUDIES COMPLETED UNDER CARB-X SUPPORT PRECLINICAL ACTIVITIES, GMP MANUFACTURING AND IND ACTIVATION, AND ENTER INTO A PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL. FOLLOWING THIS FUNDING PERIOD, LIMMATECH BIOLOGICS AG INTENDS TO TEST THE VACCINE IN PHASE II AND PHASE III CLINICAL TRIALS FOR PREVENTION OF SSTI IN RECURRENT SA SKIN INFECTIONS AND LATER IN SSI IN ELECTIVE SURGERIES. A TEAM OF EXPERIENCED SCIENTISTS AND PROGRAM MANAGERS AT LIMMATECH BIOLOGICS AG WILL LEAD THE PROGRAM. WORLD EXPERTS AND COLLABORATORS IN THE FIELD OF SA WILL COLLABORATE WITH LIMMATECH BIOLOGICS AG ON THIS PROJECT.

description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES CAN BE ALTERED BY VACCINATION AND DISEASE STATE, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING BY VACCINATION AND BACTERIAL EXPOSURE AS WELL AS THE IMPACT ON THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE AND BACTERIAL CONTROL. THE SUBAWARD WILL PERFORM EPIGENETIC ANALYSIS OF HUMAN AND MOUSE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER LABORATORIES IN THE CONSORTIUM TO LINK MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC STATES TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES. 1) PERFORM ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING AND ANALYSIS ON ADDITIONAL FROZEN HUMAN ADHERENT BAL SAMPLES FROM ACTIVE TB, RESISTER, HEALTHY CONTROLS, AND ASYMPTOMATIC TB INDIVIDUALS. PROFILING INCLUDES: CELL PREPARATION, TRANSPOSITION REACTION AND PURIFICATION, PCR AMPLIFICATION, LIBRARY PURIFICATION, AND LIBRARY QC. ANALYSIS INCLUDES: SEQUENCING FILTERING AND ALIGNMENT, DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, PATHWAY ANALYSIS, AND MOTIF ENRICHMENT ANALYSIS. 2) ANALYZE LINKAGE BETWEEN HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES (IN COLLABORATION WITH WALZL/DU PLESSIS LABS). 3) COMPARE HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES TO EPIGENETIC PROFILES OF MURINE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES TRAINED BY TYPE I OR TYPE II INTERFERONS. 4) TRANSCRIPTIONAL ANALYSIS OF SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQUENCING DATA FROM HUMAN MACROPHAGES PROFILED FROM NONADHERENT BAL SAMPLES (IN COLLABORATION WITH WALZL/DU PLESSIS/LEWINSOHN LABS). 5) COMPLETE STUDIES COMPARING INNATE RESPONSES AND PRODUCTION OF IFN-BETA FOR WT, SP140-/-, IFNAR-/-, AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MEXAMS AND BMDMS FOLLOWING STIMULATION WITH LPS OR INFECTION WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS TO CHARACTERIZE MACROPHAGE SUBSET-SPECIFIC REGULATION OF TYPE I IFN AND CYTOKINE RESPONSES.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – HAWN THE HAWN LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 7. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1-6 IS ONGOING. 1) UW WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 6. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL. 2) UW WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. ANALYSES ARE UNDERWAY TO EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN CANDIDATE GENES WITH MTB-INDUCED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES IN A COHORT OF 100 HEALTHY DONORS. 3) CELLULAR GWAS: UW WILL PERFORM CELLULAR GWAS EXPERIMENTS TO DISCOVER GENETIC REGULATORS OF MTB-INDUCED MYELOID CELL PHENOTYPES. LEAD FINDINGS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR ASSOCIATION WITH CLINICAL PHENOTYPES WITH AN OVERALL GOAL TO DISCOVER MAJOR GENETIC DETERMINANTS OF TB CLINICAL PHENOTYPES. 4) UW WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. STUDIES WILL INCLUDE INFECTION OF MACROPHAGES WITH MTB AND ANALYSIS OF IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND CONTROL OF MTB REPLICATION. CELL SUPERNATANTS WILL BE HARVESTED FOR CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE ELISA AND RNA EXTRACTED FROM CELLS, QUANTIFIED, AND ANALYZED. 5) UW WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) THE DU PLESSIS/WALZL LABORATORY AT STELLENBOSCH UNIVERSITY (SU) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CLINICAL AND IMMUNOLOGICAL WORK (INCLUDING ON-SITE DATA MANAGEMENT) OF THE PROJECT. SU WILL COORDINATE THE STUDY DESIGN, PARTICIPANT SCREENING AND ENROLLMENT FOR THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, PERFORM BRONCHOSCOPIES AND MANAGE SAMPLE SHARING TO PARTICIPATING SITES. SU WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN THE DESIGN, EXECUTION AND DATA ANALYSIS OF IMMUNOLOGICAL STUDIES AND PARTICIPATE IN THE LEADERSHIP TEAM OF “CASCADE IMPAC-TB” CENTER. SU WILL INTERACT AND COORDINATE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WITH THE PI OF THE PROJECT. DR. DU PLESSIS AND DR. WALZL, THE SU CO-PI’S WILL REVIEW ALL RAW DATA GENERATED BY THE SU TEAM, AND SUPERVISE THE LABORATORY WORK, AND THE RESEARCH TECHNICIANS. SPECIFIC DELIVERABLES FOR YEAR 7 OF THE CONTRACT AT SU INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: A. RECRUITMENT: SU WILL CONDUCT PET/CT, BRONCHOSCOPY AND PHLEBOTOMY IN ALL COHORTS TO COVER THE FULL SPECTRUM OF INFECTION AND OBTAIN BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES FROM EACH. RECRUITMENT HAS BEEN COMPLETED, AND NO NEW PARTICIPANTS ARE BEING ENROLLED. HOWEVER, WE ARE FOLLOWING UP SELECTED PARTICIPANTS TO SCREEN FOR TB PROGRESSION WITH LONGITUDINAL SAMPLING, REQUIRING ETHICS APPROVAL AND LIMITED CONTINUED CLINICAL INVOLVEMENT. B. END-ASSAYS: IMMUNOPHENOTYPING EXPERIMENTS – ONE OF THE DELIVERABLES AT SU IS TO CONDUCT DEEP PHENOTYPING OF PAIRED BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) AND PBMC FROM THE VARIOUS CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY CLINICAL GROUPS. SU HAS EVALUATED THE ASSAY PRIORITY LIST, AS WELL AS THE BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED IN THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, TO ENUMERATE THE NUMBER OF STORED SAMPLES AVAILABLE FOR THE OBJECTIVES RELATED TO THE PROPOSED PLANS FOR THIS END-ASSAY. OF ALL MAIN STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM WHICH PAIRED BAL AND PBMC HAVE BEEN COLLECTED, SUFFICIENT CELL NUMBERS WERE OBTAINED FROM 88% OF PARTICIPANTS, WHICH INCLUDES MAKING USE OF RESIDUALLY STORED BAL CELLS. WE WILL PERFORM MULTIPARAMETER FLOW CYTOMETRY ANALYSES ON UNFRACTIONATED BAL CELLS AND PBMC SAMPLES FROM A SUBSET OF INDIVIDUALS FROM THE CASCADE CLINICAL GROUPS ALL COHORTS TO DEFINE THE PHENOTYPE OF LUNG RESIDENT AND CIRCULATING LYMPHOCYTE POPULATIONS. IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF THESE SU HHC PBMC SAMPLES FOR THE LYMPHOID FLOW CYTOMETRY PANEL WILL BE COMPLETED BY MARCH 2026. GRANULOMA MODEL/KILLING ASSAYS – SU WILL MAKE USE OF THE IN VITRO GRANULOMA MODEL ALONG WITH PARALLEL ASSESSMENTS IN MONOLAYER CULTURE AND UNFRACTIONATED PBMC AND BAL, TO ASSESS MTB KILLING AMONGST THE VARIOUS CLINICAL GROUPS. INTERESTING FINDINGS RELATED TO MTB CONTROL WILL BE TESTED IN FUTURE IN GRANULOMA MODEL EXPERIMENTS. BY USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PARTICIPANTS NOT ELIGIBLE ACCORDING TO THE CASCADE HHC STUDY CRITERIA, SU HAS OPTIMIZED THE MODEL AND ALSO IMPLEMENTED CHANGES TO STREAMLINE BACTERIAL LOAD ASSESSMENT THROUGH MGIT CULTURE. description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – GERNER THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB), THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MTB SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE DIVERSIFICATION OF MTB STATES AND EXPRESSION OF DIFFERENT ANTIGENS IN DIFFERENT TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS AND CELL TYPES, AND STUDY HOW THIS CORRESPONDS TO LOCAL IMMUNE ACTIVITY BY MTB-SPECIFIC T CELLS. IN YEAR 7, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL: I. CONTINUE IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MTB INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. SUBSTANTIAL EFFORT WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING STUDIES DESCRIBING MTB DISSEMINATION TO LUNG-DRAINING LYMPH NODES AND MECHANISMS OF HOW VACCINATION PREVENTS LOCAL GENERATION OF MYELOID NICHES FOR MTB PERSISTENCE. SPECIFIC EFFORTS WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING THE MANUSCRIPT FOR PUBLICATION AND PERFORMING REVIEWER REQUESTED STUDIES. II. CONTINUE EVALUATING THE DISTRIBUTION OF MTB ANTIGENS WITH RESPECT TO DISTINCT BACILLARY STATES WITHIN TISSUES. WE HAVE IDENTIFIED THAT MAJOR IMMUNODOMINANT ANTIGENS DO NOT APPEAR PHYSICALLY COUPLED WITH MTB BACILLI AND ARE OFTEN EXPORTED TO NEIGHBORING CELLS. THIS INDICATES THAT VACCINE EFFORTS AIMED AT ELICITING ADAPTIVE RESPONSES TO THOSE ANTIGENS WILL LARGELY FAIL TO AFFECT CELLS WHICH ARE ACTUALLY INFECTED WITH MTB – RATHER THE BYSTANDER CELLS CONTAINING ANTIGENS. UNDERSTANDING THESE PROCESSES WILL HELP IDENTIFY MECHANISMS OF VACCINE SUCCESS VS. FAILURE ALLOWING FOR CURBING MTB INFECTION AND ITS EVENTUAL PERSISTENCE. III. IMPLEMENT ESTABLISHED HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. PREVIOUS EFFORTS IDENTIFIED DIVERSE GRANULOMA STRUCTURES IN LUNGS FROM DECEASED INDIVIDUALS WITH ADVANCED DISEASE. WE HAVE ALSO DEVELOPED EXTENSIVE ANTIBODY PANELS AGAINST MAJOR IMMUNE POPULATIONS OF INTEREST AS WELL AS IMPLEMENTED AN HIGHLY-MULTIPLEX ITERATIVE IMAGING TECHNIQUE, IBEX. UPCOMING WORK WILL USE THESE ADVANCED METHODS TO ELUCIDATE MAJOR STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF THESE LESIONS. WE WILL ALSO CONTINUE TO DISSECT HOW MTB INFECTION OCCURS WITHIN HUMAN LUNG-DRAINING LNS, DIRECTLY RELATING TO THE MURINE STUDY DESCRIBED ABOVE. IV. CONTINUE WITH ANALYSIS OF THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA FOR LUNG GRANULOMAS OVER THE EARLY COURSE OF INFECTION WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. WE HAVE COLLECTED LARGE NUMBERS OF SAMPLES OF EARLY LUNG LESIONS FOR THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS STUDY AND HAVE BEGUN ANALYSIS. MAJOR SLOWDOWNS IN WORK RESULTED DUE TO MICHAEL GALE’S LAB RELOCATING, BUT WE HAVE NOW BEGUN ANALYSIS WORK WITH JOHN AITCHINSON AND FERGUL DUFFY AT SCRI. IN THE COMING YEAR, THE GERNER LAB WILL FINALIZE ANALYSIS OF THE COLLECTED DATASET. V. ASSIST WITH MULTIOMICS ANALYSIS AND DATA INTERPRETATION FOR FLOW CYTOMETRY, SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA OBTAINED BY THE GERNER LAB AND OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. THIS WILL INVOLVE ANALYSIS OF CHEMOTACTIC AND ADHESION MOLECULES THAT MAY REGULATE CELLULAR POSITIONING, AS WELL AS HELPING IDENTIFY POTENTIA

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT STATENS SERUM INSTITUT (SSI) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, , SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB TASK 3.1: NHP SAFETY AND EFFICACY AGAINST ULTRA-LOW DOSE AEROSOL (ULDA) M.TB ERDMAN TO ENSURE THAT BIOLOGICAL RESULTS GENERATED IN THE VARIOUS CONSORTIUM LABS ARE COMPARABLE, WE WILL STANDARDIZE THE PRIMARY ASSAYS USED IN IMMUNOGENICITY ASSESSMENTS FOR EACH SPECIES. IN LINE WITH THE PROJECT GOALS TO DEVELOP A CROSS-SPECIES INTERROGATION PLATFORM, WE WILL HARMONIZE KEY ASSAYS ACROSS MULTIPLE SPECIES. SCRI WILL APPOINT AN OVERALL TASK LEADER TO COORDINATE AND OVERSEE THE WORK. ALL ASSAY STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) WILL BE SHARED WITH A PRECLINICAL LABORATORY LEAD, DESIGNATED FOR EACH ASSAY, WHO WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HARMONIZING. FINAL SOPS WILL BE SHARED AND LEAD ASSAY LABS WILL CONDUCT SIDE-BY-SIDE TRAINING SESSIONS, AS WELL AS, MAINTAIN AND DISTRIBUTE COMMON REFERENCE STANDARDS AND REAGENTS, SUCH AS IDENTICAL STIMULATION ANTIGENS (BCG, PPD, SEB, PEPTIDE POOLS AS DESCRIBED BELOW (NTM MEGAPOOL, MTB300, MTB300-ID93, AND MTB300-M72), 15-MER PEPTIDES FOR ID93, COMPONENTS OF ID93, AND M72,AND UNSTIMULATED) AND BCG VACCINATION STRAIN (BCG AJ/BCG SSI). THESE REGENTS WILL BE INCLUDED IN AN OPTIMIZED MULTICOLOR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE PANEL (OMIP). FURTHERMORE, SSI WILL ASSIST IN THE ANALYSIS OF REACTIVITY OF PEPTIDES IN HUMAN AND ANIMAL MODELS IN ANTIGENICITY ASSAYS PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION IN OPTIONS 1-4. A POOL OF 15-MER T CELL EPITOPES WHICH ARE FOUND IN DIVERSE NTMS BUT ABSENT FROM M.TB (PMID: 25548174) WILL BE SUPPLIED BY SSI IN THE OPTION 3 PERIOD TO COLLABORATOR LABS THAT REQUIRE THEM FOR IMMUNE PHENOTYPING ASSAYS. TAKING ADVANTAGE OF THE RECENTLY DEVELOPED APPROACH OF COMBINING A LARGE NUMBER OF EPITOPES IN ONE SINGLE POOL AS A "MEGAPOOL" (PMID: 27409590) WE COMBINE ALL EPITOPES IDENTIFIED IN THE PNAS STUDY TOGETHER WITH PEPTIDES IDENTIFIED BY OTHER MEMBERS OF OUR GROUP (PMID: 22046285). IN SUMMARY, LJI AND/OR SSI WILL PROVIDE: A. MEGAPOOL OF 15-MER T CELL EPITOPES WHICH ARE FOUND IN DIVERSE NTMS BUT ABSENT FROM M.TB B. MEGAPOOL OF M.TB -DERIVED EPITOPES (MTB300). C. MEGAPOOL OF M.TB -DERIVED EPITOPES FROM WHICH ID93-DERIVED EPITOPES WERE OMITTED (MTB300-ID93). D. MEGAPOOL OF M.TB-DERIVED EPITOPES FROM WHICH M72-DERIVED EPITOPES WERE OMITTED (MTB300-M72) A SUMMARY REPORT OF ALL ACTIVITIES AND STANDARDIZED PROTOCOLS FROM THE OPTION 3 PERIOD WILL BE DRAFTED AND SUBMITTED TO NIAID FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. SSI WILL PROVIDE ALL THE NECESSARY DATA AND INPUT REQUIRED FOR THE COMPLETION AND ACCEPTANCE OF THE ANIMAL STUDY REPORT. SHIPMENT PLANNING AND DOCUMENTATION WILL BE PROVIDED FOR THE PEPTIDE POOLS TO BE USED IN PRECLINICAL (OPTION 3) NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. description: THE KEY GOAL OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO DEVELOP A DESIGN-LOCKED VERSION OF STI SCOUT, AN IN VITRO DIAGNOSTIC (IVD) FOR THE DETECTION OF GONORRHEA AND CHLAMYDIA FROM MALE URINE AND FEMALE VAGINAL SWAB SAMPLES. THE TARGET PATHOGENS ARE NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE AND CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS. STI SCOUT WILL ENABLE PCR-LEVEL ACCURACY WITH THE CONVENIENCE AND COST OF RAPID ANTIGEN TESTING. COSTS OF GOODS SOLD ARE PROJECTED TO BE FAR LOWER THAN COMPETITIVE PRODUCTS, MAKING IT FINANCIALLY VIABLE TO ENTER GLOBAL LOW RESOURCE MARKETS. THE SCOUT PLATFORM INCLUDES A SCOUT HUB—A LOW-COST REUSABLE DEVICE—AND THE SCOUT CONNECT MOBILE APPLICATION FOR IOS AND ANDROID OS. TOGETHER, THESE ENABLE TESTING FOR A DEVELOPING MENU OF INDICATIONS, NOT JUST STIS, AND PERMIT RESULT TRACKING, SECURE SHARING, AND FOLLOW-ON CARE VIA TELEHEALTH. SCOUT WAS PREVIOUSLY AWARDED A CARB-X SEED AWARD CONTRACT TO DEMONSTRATE LOOP-DE-LOOP (LDL) CHEMISTRY WITH CRUDE PATIENT SAMPLES (URINE, VAGINAL SWABS). SCOUT SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED ALL MILESTONES WITHIN THE SEED CONTRACT AND DEMONSTRATED ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE IN POSITIVE AND PATIENT SPIKED SAMPLES THAT EXCEEDED THE TARGETS SET WITHIN THE CONTRACT. IN THIS DEVELOPMENT STAGE WORK, SCOUT WILL GENERATE ROBUST DATA AND DOCUMENTATION TO REACH DESIGN LOCK FOR STI SCOUT IN ADVANCE OF DOWNSTREAM FORMAL VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION ACTIVITIES THAT WILL EVENTUALLY SUPPORT A WHO PREQUALIFICATION AND US FDA 510(K) CLEARANCE. SCOUT WILL COMPLETE ASSAY DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES TO ENHANCE BOTH PERFORMANCE AND REGULATORY ALIGNMENT WITH WHO DRAFT TECHNICAL GUIDANCE. STI SCOUT PERFORMANCE AGAINST DESIGN INPUT REQUIREMENTS WILL BE ASSESSED ON THE INTEGRATED SCOUT SYSTEM (SCOUT HUB, SCOUT CONNECT APP) USING CONTROLLED TEST PROTOCOLS TO PROVIDE A SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND AND STATISTICALLY RIGOROUS EVALUATIONS. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PHASE WILL BE A CLEAR, DE-RISKED PATH TO INTERNATIONAL AND US COMMERCIALIZATION OF STI SCOUT, WITH SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND EARLY PERFORMANCE AND USABILITY DATA TO INFORM FUTURE PIVOTAL STUDIES. IN ALIGNMENT WITH CARB-X’S MISSION TO COMBAT THE GROWING THREAT OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE, SCOUT WILL ALSO ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY OF EXPANDING THE STI SCOUT PLATFORM TO DETECT NUCLEIC ACID MARKERS OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR) ALONGSIDE PATHOGEN IDENTIFICATION.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR (SEPT 1, 2025 THROUGH AUG 31, 2026). UW-CRYOEM WILL ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) A PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS PROJECT AND WILL SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. B. PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS: UW-CRYOEM WILL LEAD A STUDY ENTITLED “MARBURG VIRUS GLYCOPROTEIN CHARACTERIZATION FOR ANTIGEN DESIGN.” C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-CRYOEM WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-CRYOEM WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FROM UW-CRYOEM WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VEESLER AND/OR STAFF FOMR UW-CRYOEM WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. TAKEN TOGETHER IN PARTS A AND B ABOVE

description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE IMPAC-TB PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING AND POTENTIALLY EVEN ERADICATING MTB. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. 1. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. IN YEAR 6, THE GALE LABORATORY WILL PERFORM RNA-SEQ ASSAYS ON NHP SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM EXP #1, EXP #2, AND EXP #4. TASKS INCLUDE 1) RECEIVING TISSUE HOMOGENATE SAMPLES RECEIVED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA FROM LOUIS PICKER (OHSU), 2) ISOLATING RNA FROM THESE SAMPLES AND PERFORMING RNA QC, 3) CONSTRUCTING RNA-SEQ LIBRARIES AND LIBRARY QC USING THE ISOLATED RNA, AND 4) GENERATING RNA SEQUENCE DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES. 2. description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW GERNER) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. GERNER LAB (YEAR 6 BASE) THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB), THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MTB SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF VARIOUS CHEMOTACTIC OR ADHESION MOLECULES IN GUIDING IMMUNE CELLS TO VARIOUS SITES WITHIN THE INFECTED LUNG TISSUES AND LYMPHOID ORGANS, AS WELL AS IN MEDIATING PROTECTION FROM MTB INFECTION. IN YEAR 6, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL: I. CONTINUE IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MTB INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. SUBSTANTIAL EFFORT WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING STUDIES DESCRIBING THE ROLE OF NEUTROPHILS IN SHAPING LUNG GRANULOMA STRUCTURE AND IN IMMUNOREGULATION WITHIN THE GRANULOMA. II. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT EXPERIMENTS AIMED TO ELUCIDATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES WITHIN DRAINING LYMPH NODES DURING MTB INFECTION, WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. SPECIFIC EFFORTS WILL BE PLACED ON ELUCIDATION OF CHANGES OCCURRING WITHIN THE MYELOID COMPARTMENT IN LYMPH NODES WHICH PROMOTE VERSUS INHIBIT FUNCTIONAL T CELL ACTIVATION AT DIFFERENT TIMEPOINTS DURING INFECTION. ADDITIONAL WORK WILL INVESTIGATE HOW BCG VACCINATION INHIBITS THE GENERATION OF MYELOID MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LNS WHICH SERVE AS A NICHE FOR CHRONIC MTB PERSISTENCE. III. CONTINUE DEVELOPMENT OF HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. PREVIOUS EFFORTS IDENTIFIED DIVERSE GRANULOMA STRUCTURES IN LUNGS FROM DECEASED INDIVIDUALS WITH ADVANCED DISEASE. UPCOMING WORK WILL ELUCIDATE ADDITIONAL IMMUNOLOGICAL FEATURES OF THESE STRUCTURES AND HOW THESE RELATE TO PROCESSES WITHIN THE DRAINING LNS. SPECIFIC GOAL WILL BE TO INVESTIGATE THE MICROANATOMY OF MTB INFECTION IN LUNG-DRAINING LNS, INCLUDING THE CELL TYPES, SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION, AND FUNCTIONAL STATES OF THE INFECTED CELLS. COMPARATIVE ANALYSES WITH MOUSE MODELS OF INFECTION (POINT II ABOVE) WILL BE PERFORMED. IV. PERFORM ANALYSIS OF THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA FOR LUNG GRANULOMAS OVER THE EARLY COURSE OF INFECTION WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. IN THE PAST YEAR, WE HAVE COLLECTED LARGE NUMBERS OF SAMPLES OF EARLY LUNG LESIONS FOR THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS STUDY. description: IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A NEW TYPE OF ADJUVANTED VACCINE THAT BOTH ACTIVATES AND LIMITS THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE. IN PRELIMINARY WORK, WE SHOWED THAT ADDING MOLECULES THAT ALTER THE SIGNALING OF THE NF-􀈛􀀥 AND IRF PATHWAY IN COMBINATION WITH A WELL-CHARACTERIZED TLR AGONIST RESULTED IN NEAR-ZERO SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION WHILE MAINTAINING MINIMAL LOCAL INFLAMMATION. AT THE SAME TIME, ADDITION OF THIS COMPOUND, PME-564, INCREASED AND MODIFIED ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR SEVERAL COMMERCIAL VACCINES – MOST NOTABLY FLUZONE. IN THIS WORK, WE PROPOSE TO FURTHER DEVELOP THIS COMPOUND, PME-564, ALONGSIDE MRNA VACCINES TO FIND A SINGLE ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT CAN BE USED IN AN IMPROVED H5N1 VACCINE. WE HAVE TWO GOALS: (1) IDENTIFY A FORMULATION CANDIDATE THAT CAN BE RAPIDLY ADMIXED WITH EITHER CURRENT QUADRIVALENT FLU VACCINES OR MRNA VACCINES. PAIRING THESE FORMULATIONS WITH THE HIGHEST PERFORMING VACCINE PLATFORM TO DEVELOP VACCINE CANDIDATES. IMPROVING REACTOGENICITY, REDUCING DOSAGE, AND INCREASING DURABILITY OF EACH VACCINE. (2) RAPIDLY TESTING THESE CANDIDATES FOR COMPATIBILITY WITH COMMERCIAL VACCINE SYSTEMS AND PRE-CLINICAL PANDEMIC FLU VACCINES, DETERMINING AN APPROPRIATE TOXICITY AND SAFETY PROFILE FOR BOTH THE INDEPENDENT AND MIXED FORMULATION. THIS NEW APPROACH ADDRESSES A LIMITATION IN CURRENT ADJUVANT TECHNOLOGY. ADJUVANTS TRANSITIONING OUT OF BASIC DISCOVERY HAVE LIMITED METHODS TO CONTROL EXCESS INFLAMMATION IN THE FORM OF INCREASED CYTOKINES – REPRESENTED BY EXCESS TNF-􀄮􀀃􀁄􀁑􀁇􀀃􀀬􀀯-6 PRODUCTION. THE FOCUS OF THIS SUPPLEMENTAL PROGRAM WILL BE THE COFORMULATION OF THESE MOLECULES WITH MRNA VACCINES, SPECIFICALLY IN THE CONTEXT OF PANDEMIC FLU. FORMULATIONS DO HELP ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM TO SOME EXTENT, BUT THEY DO NOT ADDRESS THE FUNDAMENTAL ACTIVITY OF THE COMPOUND, WHICH GENERATES A LARGE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AT THE CELLULAR LEVEL. OUR APPROACH DIRECTLY TARGETS THE PATHWAY THAT CAUSES THIS EXCESSIVE AND OFTEN SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND REDUCES IT. THE ADDED BENEFIT IS THAT BECAUSE THE MODULATION OCCURS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE AGONIST, IT CAN PROVIDE AN ADDED BENEFIT NOT JUST TO A SPECIFIC AGONIST BUT TO ANY H5N1, QUADRIVALENT, OR MRNA FLU VACCINE. THE RESULT IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE BUT EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, A BROAD INCREASE IN ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR THESE VACCINES. AS WELL, EXPERIMENTS IN FORMULATION, DOSAGE, AND CONCENTRATION WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL INFORMATION FOR DEFINING HOW IMMUNE-MODULATORS SUCH AS PME-564 ARE CONSIDERED IN USE IN VACCINE FORMULATIONS. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE USE OF OUR IMMUNOMODULATOR IN THE CONTEXT OF DOSE SPARING FOR PANDEMIC FLU VACCINES. IF NEEDED, SEPARATE VIALS OF IMMUNOMODULATOR CAN BE CO-MIXED ON SITE OF VACCINATION WHICH WILL ENABLE DOSE SPARING FOR AVAILABLE VACCINES. WE WILL EXPLORE MAXIMAL AND MINIMAL DOSES OF MRNA IN COMBINATION WITH OUR IMMUNOMODULATORS TO SELECT THE BEST BALANCE BETWEEN DURABILITY, IMMUNOGENICITY, AND REACTOGENICITY. OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP AN ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT INCREASES THE NEUTRALIZING IGG LEVELS AND DURABILITY OF THOSE LEVELS FOR A PLATFORM OF MRNA VACCINES WITH A FOCUS ON H5N1 FLU SYSTEMS WHILE MINIMIZING THE INFLAMMATORY EFFECTS UPON INJECTION. OUR SECONDARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF IMMUNOMODULATORY COMPOUND PME-564 􀀋􀀥􀁄􀁉􀁈􀁗􀁌􀁑􀁌􀁅􀀌􀀃􀁄􀁖􀀃􀁄􀀃􀁅􀁕􀁒􀁄􀁇-SPECTRUM VACCINE ENHANCING OR DOSE SPARING EXCIPIENT THAT CAN BE USED AS PART OF MULTIPLE FORMULATIONS. TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOME OF THE FORMULATION AND TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF PME-􀀘􀀙􀀗􀀃􀀋􀀥􀁄􀁉􀁈􀁗􀁌􀁑􀁌􀁅􀀌􀀏􀀃􀁚􀁈􀀃 WILL EXPLORE THE MECHANISM OF A SERIES OF CHEMICALLY SYNTHESIZED DERIVATIVES, OPTIMIZE THEIR STRUCTURE AND FORMULATION, AND TEST THEM AS ADJUVANTS WITH MULTIPLE FLU VACCINATION PLATFORMS. THESE VACCINE CANDIDATES WILL THEN BE TESTED FOR SAFETY, TOXICITY, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE PROTECTION IN MOUSE CHALLENGE BEFORE BEING USED IN HIGHER ANIMAL MODELS.
