description: OBJECTIVE: THE AIM OF THIS PHASE I CONTRACT IS TO IDENTIFY NOVEL SEROLOGICAL BIOMARKERS FOR VISCERAL LEISHMANIASIS (VL) AND TO OPTIMIZE A DIAGNOSTIC ASSAY FOR DETECTING VL INFECTIONS. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED BY USING SERUM SAMPLES PROVIDED BY DRS. RICHARD WAMAI AND ERMIAS DIRO FROM PREVIOUS STUDIES CONDUCTED IN KENYA AND ETHIOPIA, RESPECTIVELY. DELIVERABLES FOR PHASE I: 1. SERUM SAMPLES FROM KENYA:  A TOTAL OF 130 SERUM SAMPLES WILL BE PROVIDED BY DR. RICHARD WAMAI. O 65 VL-POSITIVE SAMPLES: THESE SAMPLES WILL BE CONFIRMED TO BE VL POSITIVE USING TWO METHODS:  GOLD STANDARD: MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION OF SPLENIC ASPIRATES FOR THE PRESENCE OF AMASTIGOTES.  DIRECT AGGLUTINATION TEST (DAT) AND RK39 TEST FROM GLOBAL ACCESS DIAGNOSTICS. O 65 VL-NEGATIVE SAMPLES: THESE WILL SERVE AS NEGATIVE CONTROLS, COLLECTED FROM REGIONS IN KENYA NON-ENDEMIC TO VL. THE SAMPLES WILL BE IRREVERSIBLY DE-IDENTIFIED BEFORE SHARING AND HAVE BEEN OBTAINED UNDER PRIOR IRB APPROVALS FROM STUDIES CONDUCTED IN KENYA. 2. SERUM SAMPLES FROM ETHIOPIA:  AN ADDITIONAL 130 SERUM SAMPLES WILL BE PROVIDED BY DR. RICHARD WAMAI, SOURCED FROM DR. ERMIAS DIRO, AND COLLECTED FROM INDIVIDUALS RESIDING IN VL-ENDEMIC (POSITIVES) AND VL NON-ENDEMIC (NEGATIVES) REGIONS IN ETHIOPIA. O 65 VL-POSITIVE SAMPLES: THESE SAMPLES WILL BE CONFIRMED TO BE VL POSITIVE USING:  GOLD STANDARD: MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION OF PARASITES IN SPLENIC OR BONE MARROW ASPIRATES. O 65 VL-NEGATIVE SAMPLES: THESE WILL SERVE AS NEGATIVE CONTROLS. THESE SAMPLES WILL BE SOURCED FROM INDIVIDUALS RESIDING IN VL NON-ENDEMIC REGIONS OF ETHIOPIA. THE SAMPLES WILL BE IRREVERSIBLY DE-IDENTIFIED BEFORE SHARING AND HAVE BEEN OBTAINED UNDER PRIOR IRB APPROVALS FROM STUDIES CONDUCTED IN ETHIOPIA. DR. RICHARD WAMAI WILL MEET REGULARLY WITH DR. ANDREW LEVIN (PI) AND THE TEAM FROM KEPHERA DIAGNOSTICS TO DISCUSS THE PROJECT'S PROGRESS. THE SUBCONTRACT BUDGET WILL INCLUDE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH SAMPLE PROVISION AND COLLABORATION EFFORTS BETWEEN DRS. RICHARD WAMAI AND ERMIAS DIRO, WITH ALL SAMPLE-RELATED EXPENSES CONSOLIDATED UNDER DR. WAMAI'S SUBCONTRACT. PAYMENT SCHEDULE WILL BE 50% PAYMENT UPON RECEIPT BY KEPHERA OF 130 SAMPLES AND THE REMAINING 50% UPON RECEIPT BY KEPHERA OF ALL 260 SAMPLES

description: THE OH LAB AT DUKE UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A METAGENOMIC PIPELINE FOR PATHOGEN DETECTION AND MICROBIAL LOAD ESTIMATION. THIS PIPELINE SIMULTANEOUSLY GENERATES DEEP METAGENOMIC DATA THAT MAY CONTAIN RELEVANT INFORMATION ABOUT INFECTION RISK AS WELL AS ACCURATELY DETECT, AT THE STRAIN LEVEL, MOST LIKELY STRAIN LEVELS OF PATHOGENS OF INTEREST. THIS PIPELINE WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY QPCR TO CALCULATE MICROBIAL LOAD, DATA WHICH WILL THEN BE USED TO EXTRAPOLATE BIOBURDEN AS A FUNCTION OF CFUS PER GRAM OF STOOL OR SKIN SWAB. THE OH LAB WILL RETURN 1) A DETAILED WORKFLOW FOR SAMPLE ACQUISITION, PREPARATION, AND ANALYSIS, 2) ALGORITHMS AND DATABASES FOR PATHOGEN DETECTION IN METAGENOMIC DATA, AND 3) BENCHMARK TESTING FOR THIS PIPELINE.

description: OPTION 23C: 0258-A485-4609 OPTION 23D: 0258-A486-4609 THE UNIVERSAL INFLUENZA VACCINE TECHNOLOGY LANDSCAPE IS A UNIQUE, OPEN-ACCESS DATABASE OF INFORMATION ON UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINES, AS DEFINED IN THE INFLUENZA VACCINES R&D ROADMAP, IN CLINICAL AND PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT. AS OF MAY 2024, THE LANDSCAPE PROFILED MORE THAN 200 VACCINE CANDIDATES IN THE R&D PIPELINE IN ACADEMIC, GOVERNMENT, AND INDUSTRY LABORATORIES, INCLUDING COVID-INFLUENZA COMBINATION VACCINES IN CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT, ACROSS SIX DIFFERENT VACCINE PLATFORMS. DATA ON EACH VACCINE CANDIDATE ARE SUMMARIZED BY PHASE, PLATFORM, TECHNICAL APPROACH, GOAL, AND STATUS OF DEVELOPMENT. THE LANDSCAPE IS ONLINE AND OPEN ACCESS, AND THE ENTIRE DATASET CAN BE DOWNLOADED AS A CSV FILE. A SMALL GROUP OF SUBJECT-MATTER EXPERTS IN INFLUENZA VACCINE R&D AND/OR VACCINE DATABASE DEVELOPMENT PROVIDES ADVICE ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE LANDSCAPE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING AND MAINTAINING INFORMATION ON THE LANDSCAPE TO INCLUDE AN UP-TO-DATE, COMPREHENSIVE, AND ACCURATE OVERVIEW OF VACCINE CANDIDATES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FOR UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINES. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES: 1. COLLECT AND CURATE INFORMATION ON UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINES TECHNOLOGIES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FROM A WIDE RANGE OF PUBLICLY AVAILABLE SOURCES. CONTINUE RESEARCH ON UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINE TECHNOLOGIES; MONITOR KEY SOURCES OF INFORMATION FROM THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE, PREPRINT SERVERS, AND INDUSTRY WEBSITES AND NEWS SOURCES; AND CROSSCHECK DATA ON VACCINE TECHNOLOGIES IN THE DATABASE. 2. UPLOAD NEW OR REVISED INFORMATION ON THE IVR LANDSCAPE WEBSITE ON A WEEKLY BASIS, FOR DISPLAY IN THE SNAPSHOT GRAPHIC AND DATABASE TABLE, AND MONITOR DATA FOR COMPLETENESS AND ACCURACY. 3. DISSEMINATE INFORMATION ON R&D OF INFLUENZA CANDIDATE VACCINES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT VIA PRESENTATIONS AND PUBLICATIONS IN THE PEER-REVIEWED LITERATURE; ENCOURAGE FEEDBACK FROM DEVELOPERS, RESEARCHERS, AND FUNDING ORGANIZATIONS. 4. CONSULT WITH ADVISORY WORKING GROUP MEMBERS FOR GUIDANCE AND REVIEW. COMMUNICATE WITH DEVELOPERS TO VERIFY ACTIVITIES AND ACCURACY OF DATA. 5. MODIFY THE ONLINE DATABASE FORMAT AS NEEDED, WITH SUPPORT FROM CIDRAPÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S IT CONSULTANTS, AND IN COMMUNICATION WITH NIAID AND CIVICS-SEM. THE LANDSCAPE WILL PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE, UP-TO-DATE RESOURCE ON THE R&D PIPELINE FOR VACCINE CANDIDATES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FOR RESEARCHERS, DEVELOPERS, AND NIAID LEADERSHIP. THE LANDSCAPE SUPPORTS THE NIAID/CIVICS PROGRAMÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GOAL OF ADVANCING INFLUENZA VACCINE SCIENCE AND IDENTIFYING POTENTIAL VACCINE CANDIDATES THAT MAY OFFER BROAD AND LONG-LASTING PROTECTION AGAINST SEASONAL AND PANDEMIC INFLUENZA.

description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EVALUATE VARIOUS ADJUVANTS AND COMBINATIONS OF THESE ADJUVANTS FOR USE IN MUCOSAL IMMUNOTHERAPY FOR PEANUT ALLERGY. DR. KULIS AND HIS TEAM AT UNC CHAPEL HILL WILL PERFORM IN VIVO MOUSE STUDIES, ASSAY HUMAN PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS, AND QUANTIFY IMMUNOLOGIC RESPONSES TO ADJUVANTS AND PEANUT FROM BOTH MOUSE AND HUMAN BLOOD. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL EVALUATE SIX ADJUVANT FORMULATIONS IN CELL CULTURE ASSAYS WITH HUMAN T AND B CELLS FROM BLOOD, PRIMARILY INVESTIGATING CYTOKINE RESPONSES AND THEN SENDING CELLS FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS TO DUKE FOR OMICS EXPERIMENTS. FOR THE MOUSE STUDIES, WE WILL EVALUATE THE SAME SIX ADJUVANTS PLUS PEANUT BY ADDING THE ADJUVANTS TO SPLEEN AND LYMPH NODE CELLS IN CULTURE. WE WILL ALSO ADMINISTER THE ADJUVANTS AND PEANUT BY THE SUBLINGUAL ROUTE TO LIVE MICE THAT ARE EITHER NOT SENSITIZED TO PEANUT OR IN MICE THAT HAVE AN ESTABLISHED PEANUT ALLERGY. WE WILL PERFORM THESE EXPERIMENTS AT UNC, AND ALSO SAVE VARIOUS SAMPLES (SPLEEN, LYMPH NODE, SERUM, SALIVA, AND FECAL PELLETS) TO SHIP TO DUKE FOR OMICS STUDIES. ULTIMATELY, THE SIX ADJUVANTS WILL BE EVALUATED FOR THEIR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN THE PEANUT ALLERGIC MICE. SINCE THIS PROJECT INVOLVES TEAM MEMBERS AT DUKE AND INIMMUNE, WE WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN BIWEEKLY MEETINGS TO DISCUSS EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN, PROGRESS, AND DATA ANALYSIS. TWO TEAM MEMBERS FROM UNC (DR. KULIS AND DR. SMEEKENS) WILL ATTEND ANNUAL MEETINGS AT NIH IN BETHESDA, MD. WE ANTICIPATE PUBLISHING SEVERAL MANUSCRIPTS BASED ON THE WORK DONE AT UNC IN COLLABORATION WITH DUKE AND INIMMUNE, WHICH THE UNC TEAM WILL BE HEAVILY INVOLVED IN WRITING.

description: THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, PROTEOMICS, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. MEGAPOOL OF M.TB-DERIVED EPITOPES FROM WHICH M72-DERIVED EPITOPES WERE OMITTED (MTB300-M72) A SUMMARY REPORT OF ALL ACTIVITIES AND STANDARDIZED PROTOCOLS FROM THE OPTION 3 PERIOD WILL BE DRAFTED AND SUBMITTED TO NIAID FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. description: STATEMENT OF WORK: DEFINING THE ROLE OF CD8 T CELLS INDUCED BY A NOVEL LIPOSOMAL NANOPARTICLE MRNA VACCINE IN PREVENTING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE GOAL OF IMPAC-TB IS TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS OF PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY AGAINST TB, AND OUR OVERALL STRATEGY FOR THE CASCADE IMPAC-TB ANIMAL PROGRAM IS TO START WITH GOLD-STANDARDS OF VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION (I.E, CMV/TB AND IV BCG IN NHP; BCG IN MICE) AND THEN DISSECT HOW PROTECTION IS MEDIATED. THE AKAGERA MRNA VACCINE REPRESENTS A NEW GOLD STANDARD FOR PREVENTION OF INFECTION Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ THE BEST VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION EVER OBSERVED IN MICE. TO ACHIEVE OUR GOAL OF IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS OF TB IMMUNITY, CASCADE IMPAC-TB WOULD LIKE TO IDENTIFY THE ANTIGENS AND T CELL SUBSETS THAT MEDIATE THE PROTECTION PROVIDED BY THE NEW AKAGERA MRNA VACCINE, WHICH SHOWS THE BEST VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION EVER OBSERVED IN MICE. THE SPECIFIC WORK TO BE PERFORMED IS DETAILED BELOW. UNDER ALL THREE AIMS, AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR CREATING THE MRNA VACCINE CONSTRUCTS REQUIRED FOR EACH EXPERIMENT. IN ADDITION, SCIENTISTS AT AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL ALSO MEET REGULARLY WITH SCIENTISTS AT SCRI TO EVALUATE PROGRESS, DESIGN NEW CONSTRUCTS, AND TROUBLE-SHOOT, AS NECESSARY. AIM 1: IDENTIFY PROTECTIVE ANTIGENS IN THE AKAGERA MRNA VACCINE. AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL PREPARE SEPARATE MRNA VACCINE CONSTRUCTS FOR 4 ORFS (TB10.4, MTB39, AND ESAT-6 WHICH ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC ANTIGENS IN THE MRNA VACCINE, AND MTB32, WHICH ALONG WITH MTB39 IS PART OF THE M72 VACCINE). THESE WILL BE SENT TO SCRI FOR TESTING IN MICE, TO COMPARE THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF THE PARENTAL MRNA VACCINE, EACH OF THESE 4 CONSTRUCTS INDIVIDUALLY, POOLED ADMINISTRATION OF TB10.4, MTB39, ESAT-6 MRNA CONSTRUCTS, AND THAT SAME POOL WITH THE ADDITION OF MTB32. SCRI WILL MEASURE THE THREE METRICS OF IMMUNITY THAT WERE PREVIOUSLY DEFINED IN THE ULD MODEL: REDUCTION OF LUNG BACTERIAL BURDENS, PREVENTION OF DISSEMINATION TO THE CONTRALATERAL LUNG, AND PREVENTION OF DETECTABLE INFECTION. COLONIES WILL BE COLLECTED, DNA ISOLATED, AND BAR-CODES AMPLIFIED AND SEQUENCED TO DETERMINE THE NUMBER OF FOUNDING MTB STRAINS IN EACH LUNG. BECAUSE THE GROUP SIZES WILL HAVE TO BE REDUCED TO 15 MICE (RATHER THAN OUR MORE STANDARD 20) TO ACCOMMODATE THE NUMBER OF VACCINES TESTED SIMULTANEOUSLY, THE EXPERIMENT WILL BE REPEATED FOUR TIMES TO ASSURE REPRODUCIBILITY AND STATISTICAL RIGOR. IF PROTECTION CONFERRED BY THE THREE OR FOUR POOLED ANTIGENS IS NOT SIMILAR TO THAT CONFERRED BY THE PARENT VACCINE, AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL SYNTHESIZE ADDITIONAL ANTIGENS UNTIL A COCKTAIL OF ANTIGENS THAT CONFERS SIMILAR PROTECTION IS FOUND. AIM 2: IDENTIFY AND ELIMINATE CD8 EPITOPES FROM MRNA VACCINE CONSTRUCTS. THIS AIM WILL FOCUS ON EACH ANTIGEN THAT CONFERRED SOME DEGREE OF PROTECTION AGAINST ESTABLISHING SUSTAINED INFECTION IN AIM 1. ANTIGENS THAT DID NOT PREVENT DETECTABLE INFECTION WILL NOT BE EXAMINED FURTHER IN AIM 2. IN PRIOR CD8 EPITOPE MAPPING STUDIES, TB10.4 IS KNOWN TO HAVE TWO EPITOPES, TB10.4 ON THE H-2B BACKGROUND (C57BL/6) AND TB10.4 ON THE H-2D BACKGROUND (BALB/C), AND MTB32A IS KNOWN TO HAVE ONE EPITOPE ON THE H-2B BACKGROUND (C57BL/6) (MTB32). THUS, IF THESE ANTIGENS ARE FOUND TO CONTRIBUTE TO PREVENTION OF INFECTION IN AIM 1, AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL MAKE A TRUNCATED TB10.4 OR MTB32A CONSTRUCT THAT LACKS THE RESPECTIVE CD8 EPITOPES, BUT WHICH WOULD STILL CONTAIN KNOWN CD4 EPITOPES. FOR MTB39 AND ESAT6, THE CD8 EPITOPES HAVE NOT BEEN MAPPED, BUT IF EITHER MTB39 OR ESAT-6 WERE SHOWN IN AIM 1 TO CONTRIBUTE TO PREVENTING INFECTION, AKAGERA WOULD GENERATE OVERLAPPING PEPTIDES FOR EACH ANTIGEN AND MAP THE EPITOPE(S) RESPONSIBLE USING STIMULATIONS ASSAYS WITH SPLENOCYTES FROM IMMUNIZED B6XBALB/C F1 MICE. AFTER IDENTIFYING THE EPITOPES, AKAGERA MEDICINES WOULD GENERATE NEW CONSTRUCTS THAT SPECIFICALLY LACKED THE CD8 EPITOPES, EITHER VIA TRUNCATION OR POINT MUTATION OF AMINO ACID RESIDUES PREDICTED TO BE CRITICAL FOR THE RESPONSE. description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES CAN BE ALTERED BY VACCINATION AND OTHER HOST FACTORS, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING BY VACCINATION AND ITS IMPACT ON THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE AND BACTERIAL CONTROL. THE SUBAWARD WILL ALSO PERFORM A CROSS-SPECIES ANALYSIS OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES BY ANALYZING EPIGENETIC STATES ACROSS MOUSE AND HUMAN SAMPLES AND LINKING MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC STATES TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES. 1) ANALYZE EPIGENETIC PROFILES GENERATED BY ATAC-SEQ AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES GENERATED BY RNA-SEQ FOR UNTREATED VERSUS INTERFERON-TRAINED MURINE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES. 2) PERFORM ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING ON FROZEN HUMAN ADHERENT BAL SAMPLES FROM ACTIVE TB, RESISTER, HEALTHY CONTROLS, AND SUBCLINICAL TB INDIVIDUALS. PROFILING INCLUDES: CELL PREPARATION, TRANSPOSITION REACTION AND PURIFICATION, PCR AMPLIFICATION, LIBRARY PURIFICATION, AND LIBRARY QC. 3) COMPARE AND CONTRAST MOUSE AND HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC PROFILES. 4) GENERATE BULK RNA-SEQUENCING SAMPLES FOR MTB-INFECTED B6 AND C3H ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES FOLLOWING SA161 HIGH DOSE AEROSOL INFECTION. 5) PERFORM IN VITRO MTB INFECTIONS AND IN VIVO AEROSOL INFECTIONS AFTER AM TRANSFER USING WT, SP140-/-, AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MURINE EX VIVO ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE (MEXAM) PRIMARY CELL LINES TO STUDY ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE RESPONSE TO VACCINATION AND INTERFERON EXPOSURES.

PROVIDE UPDATED BENCHMARK DATASETS WITH RESPECT TO THESE TASKS, DTU WILL DEVELOP CODE IN THEIR LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND ENSURE THAT IT CAN BE EXECUTED APPROPRIATELY IN THE IEDB PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT AND WORK WITH THE LJI TEAM TO UPDATE WEB SERVERS EXECUTING THE CODE AS NECESSARY. THIS INCLUDES RETRAINING, BUG FIXES, AND FEATURE ENHANCEMENTS AS THEY OCCUR. FOR ANY NEW TOOL OR SUBSTANTIAL TOOL UPDATE DEVELOPED WITH FUNDING FROM THE IEDB BY DTU, THE PRIMARY PUBLICATION WILL INCLUDE A LINK TO THE WORKING TOOL ON THE IEDB WEBSITE. B. MEETINGS AND REPORTS 1. MEETINGS/TELECONFERENCES/VIDEOCONFERENCES DTU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH LJI AT A MINIMUM OF TWICE PER MONTH, EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA TELECONFERENCE/VIDEOCONFERENCE. THE PURPOSE OF THESE MEETINGS WILL BE TO COORDINATE EFFORTS AND REPORT PROGRESS. DTU WILL ALSO BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN 1-2 US BASED PROGRAM MEETINGS PER CONTRACT YEAR FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING FEEDBACK TO NIH AND FURTHER PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. 2. QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS DTU WILL PROVIDE INPUT FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS ON A TIMELY BASIS SO THEIR CONTENT CAN BE INCORPORATED IN ADVANCE OF THE SPECIFIED DELIVERY DATE TO NIAID.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY OF LEIDOS AS PART OF THE IEDB & AR PROGRAM IS TO MAINTAIN AND IMPROVE THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE AND CURATION SYSTEMS. IN ADDITION, LEIDOS SHALL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC MEETINGS, PROVIDE PROGRESS REPORTS ON THE WORK AND RESPOND TO IEDB HELP DESK TICKETS IF REQUIRED. AN OVERVIEW OF TASKS TO BE ACCOMPLISHED BY LEIDOS ARE LISTED BELOW: A. IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE SYSTEM AND MAKING IT AVAILABLE TO END USERS. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, STORAGE, ANALYSIS, ARCHIVE AND EXCHANGE OF IMMUNE EPITOPE DATA AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. 2. ASSIST LJI IN MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF THE IEDB WEB PORTAL INCLUDING: A. FURTHER OPTIMIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF UNIFORM, INTELLIGENT WEB-BASED INTERFACES FOR MAKING DATA ACCESSIBLE TO END USERS. THE INTERFACE SHALL MINIMALLY INCLUDE COMPLEX QUERY; SEMANTIC QUERY; DOWNLOAD; EPITOPE SUBMISSION; LINKS TO RELATED RESOURCES; AND REPORTS, MANUSCRIPTS, NEWSLETTERS, AND COMPENDIA. B. UPDATE EXISTING FEATURES AND IMPLEMENT NEW FEATURES IN THE IEDB WEB PORTAL AS NEEDED. C. ASSIST IN ESTABLISHING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE METRICS TO DETERMINE UTILIZATION AND UTILITY OF THE WEB PORTAL WITHIN THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. RELEVANT METRICS SHALL FREQUENCY OF DATA DOWNLOADS, CHARACTERIZATION OF USERS AND USER QUERY STATISTICS. AT A MINIMUM, THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE CONDUCTED BI-ANNUALLY (EVERY 2 YEARS). 3. UPON REQUEST, ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE AND UPDATING OF SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION INCLUDING: A. DOCUMENT ALL SYSTEM COMPONENTS, SOFTWARE AND DATABASES IN ACCORDANCE WITH INDUSTRY BEST PRACTICES AND IN A MANNER THAT WILL ALLOW ANOTHER CONTRACTOR OR USER TO UNDERSTAND AND UTILIZE THE SYSTEM. B. PROVIDE A HIGH LEVEL OVERVIEW OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES OF THE SYSTEM, INCLUDING SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DESIGN, DATABASE DESIGN AND DATA MODELS. THIS COMPENDIUM OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES SHALL BE UPDATED SEMI-ANNUALLY OR AS REQUESTED BY THE COTR OR CONTRACTING OFFICER. C. WORK WITH LJI TO ESTABLISH AND DOCUMENT A SCHEDULE OF SYSTEM UPDATES AND RELEASES. 4. COMPLY WITH SECTION 508 OF THE REHABILITATION ACT (29 U.S.C. 794D), (SEE HTTP://WWW.SECTION508.GOV/) IN TERMS OF DATABASE/WEBSITE USE AND DIRECT EPITOPE/DATA SUBMISSION BY THE BROADER RESEARCH COMMUNITY. B. CURATION SYSTEM TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB CURATION SYSTEM. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, TRACKING, AND ASSIGNMENT OF PUBLISHED MANUSCRIPTS AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. C. MEETINGS AND REPORTS PARTICIPATE IN WEEKLY MEETINGS TO COORDINATE SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS. ADDITIONALLY, PROVIDE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS SUMMARIZING WORK PERFORMED. D. COMMUNITY OUTREACH 1. IF REQUESTED, ASSIST WITH ADDRESSING ANY HELP DESK TICKETS RELATED TO ANY IEDB SYSTEMS INFRASTRUCTURE. 2. ASSIST LJI WITH PREPARING A COMPENDIUM OF THE DATA IN THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

SU WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN THE DESIGN, EXECUTION AND DATA ANALYSIS OF IMMUNOLOGICAL STUDIES AND PARTICIPATE IN THE LEADERSHIP TEAM OF Ã¢Â‚¬Å“CASCADE IMPAC-TBÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ CENTER. SU WILL INTERACT AND COORDINATE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WITH THE PI OF THE PROJECT. DR. DU PLESSIS AND DR. WALZL, THE SU CO-PIÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S WILL REVIEW ALL RAW DATA GENERATED BY THE SU TEAM, AND SUPERVISE THE LABORATORY WORK, AND THE RESEARCH TECHNICIANS. SPECIFIC DELIVERABLES FOR YEAR 6 OF THE CONTRACT AT SU INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: A. RECRUITMENT: THE ANTICIPATED SCREENING AND RECRUITMENT GOALS HAVE BEEN ACHIEVED AND EXCEEDED. WHILE THE INITIAL RECRUITMENT TARGET WAS SET AT 20 PARTICIPANTS FOR EACH OF THE 8 CLINICAL GROUPS (N=160 TOTAL), WE EXCEEDED THIS TO ACHIEVE AND ENROLL A TOTAL NUMBER OF 185 STUDY PARTICIPANTS ACROSS ALL GROUPS FOR THE MAIN STUDY. THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC HAS RESULTED IN A REQUEST FOR A SOMEWHAT ALTERED CLASSIFICATION AND ENROLLMENT TARGET OF CLINICAL GROUPS, WHICH WAS APPROVED BY THE NIH IN 2021. THE SU HHC STUDY NOW CONSISTS OF GROUPS STRATIFIED NOT ONLY BY IGRA RESULTS OR PET/CT READOUT, BUT ALSO BY SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGY STATUS. THE BUDGET FOR PERIOD 6 WILL INCLUDE LIMITED PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT AND BRONCHOSCOPIES, AS ORIGINALLY PROPOSED, WHICH WILL INCLUDE ONLY STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM SELECTED Ã¢Â‚¬Å“BIOLOGICALLY INTERESTINGÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ CLINICAL PHENOTYPES FOR FURTHER TARGETED FUNCTIONAL ANALYSES THROUGH GRANULOMA MODEL MANIPULATION. SU HAS BUDGETED FOR N=12 BRONCHOSCOPIES. B. END-ASSAYS: IMMUNOPHENOTYPING EXPERIMENTS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ ONE OF THE DELIVERABLES AT SU IS TO CONDUCT DEEP PHENOTYPING OF PAIRED BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) AND PBMC FROM THE VARIOUS CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY CLINICAL GROUPS. SU HAS EVALUATED THE ASSAY PRIORITY LIST, AS WELL AS THE BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED IN THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, TO ENUMERATE THE NUMBER OF STORED SAMPLES AVAILABLE FOR THE OBJECTIVES RELATED TO THE PROPOSED PLANS FOR THIS END-ASSAY. OF ALL MAIN STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM WHICH PAIRED BAL AND PBMC HAVE BEEN COLLECTED (N=190), SUFFICIENT CELL NUMBERS WERE OBTAINED FROM 88% OF PARTICIPANTS, WHICH INCLUDES MAKING USE OF RESIDUALLY STORED BAL CELLS. THIS ALSO INCLUDES REPLACEMENT OR REPEATING OF BRONCHOSCOPIES FOR N=5 OF THE PARTICIPANTS WITH LOW CELL YIELDS. WHILE THE BAL CELL AUTOFLUORESCENCE IS LIKELY TO RESULT IN A SMALLER NUMBER OF AVAILABLE FLUORESCENT CHANNELS FOR OUR BAL MYELOID FLOW CYTOMETRY IMMUNE PHENOTYPING PANEL, THE OPTIMIZATION OF THE 24 MARKER MYELOID PANEL FOR PBMC HAS BEEN COMPLETED WHILE OPTIMIZATION OF THE 27 MARKER LYMPHOID PANEL FOR PBMC WILL BE FINALIZED IN OCTOBER 2024. SU EXPECTS TO COMPLETE IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF ALL SU HHC PBMC SAMPLES BY JUNE 2025. IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF ALL SU HHC BAL SAMPLES USING THE LYMPHOID FLOW CYTOMETRY PANEL WILL BE COMPLETED BY DECEMBER 2025. GRANULOMA MODEL/KILLING ASSAYS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ SU WILL MAKE USE OF THE IN VITRO GRANULOMA MODEL ALONG WITH PARALLEL ASSESSMENTS IN MONOLAYER CULTURE AND UNFRACTIONATED PBMC AND BAL, TO ASSESS MTB KILLING AMONGST THE VARIOUS CLINICAL GROUPS. INTERESTING FINDINGS RELATED TO MTB CONTROL WILL BE TESTED IN FUTURE IN GRANULOMA MODEL EXPERIMENTS. BY USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PARTICIPANTS NOT ELIGIBLE ACCORDING TO THE CASCADE HHC STUDY CRITERIA, SU HAS OPTIMIZED THE MODEL AND ALSO IMPLEMENTED CHANGES TO STREAMLINE BACTERIAL LOAD ASSESSMENT THROUGH MGIT CULTURE. SU EXPECTS TO COMPLETE THE KILLING ASSAY EXPERIMENTS FOR AT LEAST A QUARTER OF ALL SU HHC SAMPLES BY THE END OF PERIOD 6. description: MPHI IS A NON-PROFIT PUBLIC HEALTH INSTITUTE MADE UP OF RESEARCHERS, EVALUATORS, AND CONTENT DEVELOPERS AIMED AT PROMOTING HEALTH AND WELLBEING. MPHI WILL CONTINUE TO CONTRIBUTE ITS EXPERTISE IN RESEARCH AND PROJECT EVALUATION TO SUPPORT PLANNING AND EVALUATION ACTIVITIES FOR THE S-TAC PROJECT. AS LEAD EVALUATOR FOR THIS PROJECT YEAR, THE GOAL OF THIS PARTNERSHIP IS TO SUPPORT THE S-TAC AND ITS PARTNERS IN CONDUCTING EVALUATION AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACROSS ALL S-TAC TA ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES PROVIDED THROUGHOUT OPTION YEAR 1 OF THE S-TAC'S CONTRACT. CCBHC S-TAC IS FUNDED THROUGH A CONTRACT BY THE SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA), WHICH REQUIRES PROJECT EVALUATION ACTIVITIES AND REPORTING DURING EACH PROJECT YEAR. MPHI IS MADE UP OF OVER 1,000 CONTENT AND PROCESS EXPERTS ACROSS MULTIPLE TOPIC AREAS, BRINGING TOGETHER DIVERSE KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE. EXPERTS FROM MPHI WORK WITH STAKEHOLDERS FROM ACADEMIA, GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS ACROSS TO U.S. TO STRENGTHEN PUBLIC HEALTH AND MENTAL WELLBEING AND INFLUENCE POLICY AND PRACTICE THROUGH RESEARCH, CONTENT DEVELOPMENT, AND EVALUATION ACTIVITIES. IN LINE WITH THEIR EXPERTISE, THE MPHI WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT TASK 4 IN ADDITION TO TASK 2 OF THE CCBHC STAC PROJECT WITH EVALUATION PLAN DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT, INCLUDING WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH KEY STAKEHOLDERS TO ENSURE THE EVALUATION QUESTIONS, METHODOLOGY AND DATA COLLECTED ARE APPLICABLE AND USEFUL IN ASSESSING KEY OUTCOMES OF INTEREST AND INFORMING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS. MPHI IS A CRITICAL PARTNER TO S-TAC IN THIS WORK BECAUSE OF THEIR HISTORICAL INVOLVEMENT IN THIS EFFORT IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL. MPHI IS THE EVALUATION LEAD FOR THE TWO OTHER SAMHSA FUNDED TA CENTERS AT THE NATIONAL COUNCIL, NTTAC AND THE COE-IHS. S-TAC WOULD LIKE TO BUILD THEIR PARTNERSHIP WITH MPHI AS THEIR EVALUATION LEAD ON EFFORTS MOVING FORWARD TO ENSURE BETTER ALIGNMENT IN DATA COLLECTION AND EVALUATION EFFORTS ACROSS ALL THREE TA CENTERS FUNDED BY SAMHSA HOSTED BY THE NATIONAL COUNCIL. TASK 2 – 396 HOURS PROVIDE EVALUATION CONSULTATION AND STRATEGY TO THE NATIONAL COUNCIL STAC EVALUATION TEAM AND SOLIDIFY AN EVALUATION PLAN FOR YEARS 2 AND 3 OF THE STAC PROJECT. – 183 HOURS TASK ORDER 4 – 136 HOURS CONTINUE TO WORK WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL AND THEIR IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE PARTNERS TO SUPPORT THE EVALUATION OF THE EBP IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE PILOT ACTIVITIES. THESE ACTIVITIES MAY INCLUDE ATTENDING MEETINGS AND PROVIDING FEEDBACK, DEVELOPING A DISSEMINATING AND EVALUATION SURVEY TOOL, WORKING WITH NATIONAL COUNCIL AND OTHER KEY PROJECT PARTNERS TO IDENTIFY OTHER KEY EVALUATION QUESTIONS, PARTICIPATE IN AND CONDUCT PRELIMINARY QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS OF LISTENING SESSIONS WITH CCBHC-E GRANTEES AND SUPPORTING THE USE OF DATA TO INFORM FUTURE TTA PROGRAMMING AND ACTIVITIES.

description: THIS STAKEHOLDER RESEARCH WILL SERVE AS A FOUNDATIONAL STEP IN DEVELOPING A COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIC ENGAGEMENT PLAN AND A THEORY OF CHANGE AIMED AT PROMOTING THE ADOPTION OF FAIR DATA MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, ESPECIALLY WITHIN MINORITY SERVING INSTITUTIONS (MSIS) AND HISTORICALLY BLACK COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES (HBCUS). BY DEEPLY ANALYZING THE FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE RESEARCHERSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ DECISIONS TO EITHER SUPPORT, ADOPT, REJECT, OR OVERLOOK FAIR PRINCIPLES, THE RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE BARRIERS AND MOTIVATORS SPECIFIC TO THESE COMMUNITIES. UNDERSTANDING THESE DYNAMICS WILL ALLOW US TO TAILOR ENGAGEMENT STRATEGIES THAT ADDRESS UNIQUE CHALLENGES FACED BY RESEARCHERS AT MSIS AND HBCUS, ENSURING THAT THE INITIATIVES ARE NOT ONLY RELEVANT BUT ALSO CULTURALLY AND CONTEXTUALLY APPROPRIATE. THIS APPROACH WILL HELP FOSTER A MORE INCLUSIVE AND EQUITABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR THE WIDESPREAD ADOPTION OF FAIR DATA MANAGEMENT AND SHARING PRACTICES.

CLINICAL SITES FOR THE UNITED STATES CRITICAL ILLNESS AND INJURY TRIALS GROUP PROGRAM FOR EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (USCIITG-PREP) HAVE BEEN RECRUITED TO PERFORM THIS WORK. THE WORK IS DIVIDED INTO A BASE PERIOD AND 4 ONE-YEAR OPTION PERIODS. BASE PERIOD (YEARS 1-4): THERE ARE FOUR DELIVERABLES IDENTIFIED FOR THE BASE PERIOD: Â€¢ IN YEAR 1, DEVELOP AN INTRAVENOUS ANTIVIRAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL TO ASSESS THE USE OF INTRAVENOUS (IV) ANTIVIRALS (E.G., IV ZANAMIVIR) UNDER AN EXPANDED ACCESS IND FOR CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH CONFIRMED INFLUENZA USING ELECTRONIC CASE REPORT FORMS (ECRFS) AND A DATA ENTRY USER MANUAL. Â€¢ UTILIZE PRE-ESTABLISHED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR BROAD COVERAGE OF CLINICAL TRIAL SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES Â€¢ UTILIZE RAPID DATA COLLECTION TOOL/MECHANISM FOR COLLECTION OF SAFETY (ADVERSE EVENTS) AND EFFECTIVENESS (PERFORMANCE) DATA Â€¢ COLLABORATE WITH BARDA AND BARDA-FUNDED COMPANY SPONSORS OF MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES ON PATHWAY FOR FDA APPROVAL/LICENSURE UNDER THE ANIMAL RULE TO MEET POST-MARKETING REGULATORY COMMITMENTS THE BULK OF THIS WORK WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED IN YEAR 1 OF THE BASE PERIOD; MINOR ITERATIONS OF THE WORK ARE REQUIRED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER. COLLABORATORS IN THE USCIITG-PREP NETWORK ARE TASKED WITH COORDINATING REPORTS AND COMPLETING THE WORK REQUIRED AT THEIR RESPECTIVE SITES. DELIVERABLES SPECIFIC FOR THE BASE PERIOD INCLUDE: 1. MONTHLY - PROGRESS REPORTS TO INCLUDE FINANCIAL INFORMATION AND RESEARCH UPDATES, DUE THE 15TH OF EACH MONTH WITH THE FIRST REPORT DUE ON NOVEMBER 15, 2014 2. YEARLY - PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE PAST YEAR'S WORK TO INCLUDE BOTH RESEARCH FINDINGS, FINANCIAL UPDATE, AND PUBLICATIONS AND SPEAKING ENGAGEMENTS, DUE NOVEMBER 15TH OF EACH YEAR 3. YEARLY - OPERATIONS PLAN FOR THE BARDA-SPONSORED PHASE 4 FIELD STUDIES, DUE SEPTEMBER 30TH OF EACH YEAR IF APPLICABLE 4. JANUARY 31, 2015 - FINAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL FOR TREATING CRITICALLY ILL INFLUENZA PATIENTS WITH IV ZANAMIVIR 5. JULY 30, 2015 - A COPY OF THE ECRF TO BE USED DURING THE 2015-2016 INFLUENZA SEASON

INTERACTION WITH PRACTICES FOR 2 MORE WEEKS ONLINE AFTER THE TRAINING VIA LIST-SERV.

description: "OBJECTIVE 1: DEVELOPMENT AND LAUNCH OF EFFECTIVE BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WORK WITH NCI AND NCI PRIZE ADVISORY COMMITTEE TO DEVELOP AN EFFECTIVE CHALLENGE. THIS WORK WILL INCLUDE PREPARATION OF CHALLENGE DESCRIPTION, RULES, AND EVALUATION CRITERIA. IN ADDITION, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PREPARE THE CHALLENGE HUB USING THE SYNAPSE INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE CHALLENGE, INCLUDING POSTING ALL RULES, DESCRIPTIVE INFORMATION, FAQS, AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR CHALLENGE PARTICIPATION. SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL ALSO PROVIDE DATA SCIENTIST SUPPORT TO WORK WITH THE CHALLENGE LEADER AND OTHER DATA SCIENTISTS AS PART OF THE CHALLENGE ORGANIZATIONAL TEAM. THE SAGE APPOINTED DATA SCIENTIST WILL HELP GUIDE THE TEAM IN CHALLENGE Â€˜BEST PRACTICESÂ€™, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO PRE-CHALLENGE DRY-RUN AND SUPPORT FOR THE SYNAPSE PLATFORM. SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL WORK WITH NCI TO ANNOUNCE LAUNCHING OF THE CHALLENGE. OBJECTIVE 2: MANAGEMENT AND PROMOTION OF BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PERFORM DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES FOR THE CHALLENGE AND POST CHALLENGE ON THE SAGE/SYNAPSE PLATFORM. THEY WILL DEVELOP A CHALLENGE HUB TO FACILITATE PARTICIPATION IN THE CHALLENGE. THIS HUB WILL INCLUDE REGISTRATION AND TRACKING OF CHALLENGE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR DATA ACCESS REQUESTS, SUPPORT FOR PARTICIPANTS REQARDING INQUIRES, TRANSLATION SERVICES, COMMUNITY FORUM AND MANAGEMENT OF SUBMISSIONS OF CHALLENGE SOLUTIONS. OBJECTIVE 3: EVALUATION, AWARD AND DISSEMINATION OF BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE SOLUTIONS. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL MANAGE EVALUATIONS OF CHALLENGE SUBMISSIONS, ANNOUNCE WINNER OF THE PRIZE, PROVIDE THE CHALLENGE AWARD AND PARTICIPATE IN DISSEMINATION OF THE CHALLENG SOLUTION AND NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF THE CHALLENGE PROCESS. FINALLY, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PROVIDE POST-CHALLENGE INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORT BY STORING SUMMARY OF SUBMISSIONS AND SOURCE CODE, AS APPROPRIATE, FOR THE CHALLENGE. "

description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: THE SICKLE CELL DISEASE TREATMENT DEMONSTRATION PROGRAM (SCDTDP) PROVIDES GRANTS TO REGIONAL NETWORKS THAT WILL WORK WITH PRIMARY CARE PRACTICES THAT TREAT SICKLE CELL DISEASE, COMPREHENSIVE SICKLE CELL DISEASE CENTERS, AND COMMUNITY-BASED SUPPORT ORGANIZATIONS TO PROVIDE COORDINATED, COMPREHENSIVE, CULTURALLY COMPETENT, AND FAMILY-CENTERED CARE TO FAMILIES WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE. TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS TO ACCESS TO SICKLE CELL DISEASE CARE, THE MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH BUREAU (MCHB) IS ADJUSTING THE SCDTDP TO A REGIONAL MODEL. THE REGIONAL APPROACH HAS BEEN USED BY MCHB WITH OTHER PROGRAMS AND WILL INCREASE THE REACH OF THE PROGRAM TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO A GREATER NUMBER OF PATIENTS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROCUREMENT FOR THE SCDTDP COORDINATING CENTER IS TO OBTAIN SERVICES TO GATHER DATA FROM AND EVALUATE THE PERFORMANCE OF THE SCDTDP GRANTEES IN ADDRESSING THE THREE GOALS OF THE PROGRAM, INCLUDING: 1) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PROVIDERS TREATING PERSONS FOR SICKLE CELL DISEASE FOR SICKLE CELL RELATED ISSUES; 2) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PROVIDERS PRESCRIBING DISEASE MODIFYING THERAPIES SUCH AS HYDROXYUREA; AND 3) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF SICKLE CELL PATIENTS THAT ARE RECEIVING REGULAR CARE WITH PROVIDERS KNOWLEDGEABLE ABOUT TREATING SICKLE CELL DISEASE. description: THE AMERICAN INSTITUTES FOR RESEARCH (AIR) HAS IN PLACE THE NECESSARY ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE AND EXPERIENCE TO COMPLETE THE WORK ASSIGNED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. WE HAVE BUDGETED HOURS FOR MANAGEMENT OF THE CONTRACT, WHICH INCLUDES TIME FOR MONTHLY MONITORING OF THE PROJECTÂ€™S BUDGET, COORDINATING STAFFING ACROSS PROJECT ACTIVITIES, WEEKLY MEETINGS WITH THE EISENBERG CENTER, AND INTERNAL PROJECT MEETINGS ACROSS TRANSLATION TOPICS. WHILE LEVEL OF EFFORT REMAINS ROUGHLY EQUAL ACROSS ALL YEARS FOR THIS TASK, WE ESTIMATE AN INCREASE OF ABOUT $2,800 PER YEAR FOR AIRÂ€™S ANNUAL COST OF LIVING SALARY INCREASES. CLINICIAN TESTING INCLUDES SEVEN CLINICIAN ONE-HOUR COGNITIVE INTERVIEWS WITH FIVE GENERAL PRACTITIONERS AND TWO SPECIALISTS. BASED ON OUR RECENT EXPERIENCES ON THE PREVIOUS CONTRACT, WE HAVE BUDGETED RECRUITMENT COSTS OF $160 FOR CONSUMERS AND $150 FOR CLINICIANS. DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS. IN YEAR 1, THE EC-BCM WILL RECRUIT 15 CONSUMER AND PATIENT ORGANIZATIONS; DEVELOP PROCESSES FOR MATCHING PATIENT AND CONSUMER REPRESENTATIVES WITH AHRQ AND EHC PROGRAM RESEARCH PROJECTS; ESTABLISH STANDARDIZED APPROACHES AND GUIDANCE ON HOW TO SUCCESSFULLY INVOLVE PATIENT AND CONSUMER PARTICIPANTS; DEVELOP A PASSWORD PROTECTED ONLINE RESOURCE CENTER FOR PATIENTS AND CONSUMERS ENGAGED IN SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES; CREATE AND HOST THREE MULTIMEDIA PRESENTATIONS AND ENSURE THEY ARE 508 COMPLIANT TO POST ON THE EHC WEB SITE; AND DEVELOP FEEDBACK FORMS TO COLLECT FEEDBACK ABOUT THE ENGAGEMENT PROCESS AND OUTCOMES.

description: JOHNS HOPKINS SCOPE OF WORK A. INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES EMERGING INSIGHT INTO TUMOR GENOMES MAKES IT CLEAR THAT CHROMOSOMAL TRANSLOCATIONS OCCUR RELATIVELY COMMONLY AND IN A NON-RANDOM FASHION (1-3). FUSION PROTEINS THAT FORM AS A RESULT OF THESE TRANSLOCATIONS TYPICALLY HAVE ALTERED FUNCTIONS RELATIVE TO THE INDIVIDUAL SOURCE PROTEINS AND, IN SOME CASES, APPEAR TO DRIVE THE MALIGNANT PHENOTYPE. SINCE THE FUSION PROTEINS ARISE DURING TUMOR DEVELOPMENT, AND ARE NOT EXPRESSED IN NORMAL TISSUES, THEY REPRESENT TUMOR-SPECIFIC ANTIGENS AND PROVIDE POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR TUMOR VACCINES. THERAPEUTIC BREAKPOINT PEPTIDE VACCINES WITH EVIDENCE OF CLINICAL ACTIVITY WERE FIRST DEVELOPED AGAINST THE BCRABL FUSIONS OBSERVED IN CML (4-6). WHILE THE SIZE OF THE TRIALS CONDUCTED HAVE BEEN MODEST AND THE EXACT CONTENT OF THE VACCINES VARIABLE, THE BODY OF THE DATA SUPPORTS THE POTENTIAL FOR CLINICAL ACTIVITY OF THE PRODUCTS. MORE MODEST PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE USING THERAPEUTIC BREAKPOINT VACCINES AGAINST CHARACTERISTIC FUSIONS OBSERVED IN SARCOMAS (7-9). GIVEN THAT VACCINATION AGAINST HPV, THE VIRUS THAT INDUCES CERVICAL CANCER, IS CAPABLE OF PROTECTING WOMEN FROM THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERVICAL CANCER WHEN GIVEN PRIOR TO VIRUS EXPOSURE, YET INEFFECTIVE IN THE TREATMENT SETTING AFTER THE CANCER HAS ALREADY DEVELOPED (10), BREAKPOINT VACCINES MAY ALSO BE MORE EFFECTIVE AS A PREVENTATIVE THERAPY. HOWEVER, SO FAR, NO BREAKPOINT-SPECIFIC VACCINES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR CANCER PREVENTION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A MULTIVALENT VACCINE DIRECTED AGAINST FUSION PROTEINS OBSERVED IN SOLID TUMORS COULD GENERATE AN IMMUNE RESPONSE CAPABLE OF PREVENTING SOLID TUMORS IN HIGH-RISK GROUPS OF PATIENTS. IN ADULT SOLID TUMORS, FUSIONS INVOLVING SOME OF THE SAME AND SOME DIFFERENT SOURCE GENES AS THOSE IDENTIFIED IN SARCOMAS HAVE BEEN OBSERVED. SINCE THE SAME SET OF TRANSLOCATIONS AND CORRESPONDING FUSION PROTEINS ARE NOT OBSERVED IN ALL TUMORS OF A GIVEN HISTOLOGIC TYPE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A STRATEGY THAT TARGETS MULTIPLE, FREQUENTLY OBSERVED FUSIONS HAS THE BEST CHANCE OF GENERATING EFFECTIVE ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY AND PROTECTION. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO DEFINE ONE OR MORE PRECLINICAL MODELS TO DEVELOP THIS APPROACH AND EVALUATE ITS POTENTIAL FOR THE PREVENTION OF SOLID TUMORS. OBJECTIVES 1. TO IDENTIFY T CELL TARGETABLE GENE FUSION ANTIGENS EXPRESSED BY THE MURINE LEWIS LUNG CANCER AND MC38 COLON CANCER CELL LINES. 2. TO EVALUATE THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AN EML4-ALK GENE FUSION THAT DRIVES TUMOR DEVELOPMENT IN A TRANSGENIC LUNG CANCER MODEL. 3. TO DEVELOP PEPTIDE AND LISTERIA-BASED IMMUNIZATION STRATEGIES FOR INDUCING ROBUST GENE FUSION-SPECIFIC EFFECTOR T CELL RESPONSES. 4. TO EVALUATE THE PRECLINICAL EFFICACY OF GENE FUSION-SPECIFIC IMMUNIZATION STRATEGIES FOR PREVENTING TUMOR DEVELOPMENT.

description: OPTION 15A (09/15/14-02/29/16): 0258-0516-4609 THE ROLES OF SPECIFIC SIALIC ACID VARIANTS IN INFLUENZA-HOST CELL INTERACTIONS. WE ARE FOCUSING ON BETTER UNDERSTANDING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA VIRUSES AND DIFFERENT HOSTS BY DEFINING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA HA AND NA AND SPECIFICALLY MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS (WITH ADDITIONAL ACETYLATIONS, HYDROXYLATIONS, AND/OR LINKAGES) DISPLAYED ON THE VARIOUS TARGET CELLS AND TISSUES FROM DIFFERENT HOSTS. THESE LIKELY MODIFY THE SPECIFIC PROCESSES OF VIRUS CELL BINDING, INFECTION AND SHEDDING AND WILL THEREFORE ADD TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE VIRUS-HOST INTERACTION, AND PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO POTENTIAL NEW INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. IN THE FIRST PART OF THE PROJECT WE WILL DEVELOP TOOLS FOR DETECTING THE PRESENCE OF MODIFIED FORMS OF SA ON CELLS AND TISSUES. WE WILL PREPARE PROBES FOR QUANTITATIVELY ASSAYING FOR THE PRESENCE OF NEU5AC AND NEU5GC ON CELLS AND TISSUES USING PARVOVIRUS CAPSIDS, ANTIBODIES RECOGNIZING NEU5GC, AND BACTERIAL TOXIN SUBUNITS. PROBES FOR 4-O-ACETYLATED SAS WILL BE DERIVED FROM THE MOUSE HEPATITIS VIRUS (MHV) HEMAGGLUTININ-ESTERASE (HE), AND THE MHV-S HE ESTERASE WOULD BE USED TO REMOVE THE 4-O-ACETYL GROUP FROM THE SA ON CELLS OR TISSUES. PROBES FOR 9-O-ACETYLATED SA WILL BE DERIVED FROM THE BOVINE CORONAVIRUS HE PROTEIN OR INFLUENZA C HE PROTEIN, AND ESTERASE ACTIVE FORMS WOULD BE USED AS MODIFYING ENZYMES. OTHER PROBES THAT WE WILL DEVELOP FOR THIS TESTING INCLUDE SPECIFIC INFLUENZA HA DOMAINS LINKED TO THE FC PORTION OF HUMAN IGG1. IN THE SECOND PART OF THE PROJECT WE WILL DEFINE THE SPECIFIC SA FORMS AND LINKAGES EXPRESSED ON THE RESPIRATORY EPITHELIAL AND OTHER CELLS OF NATURAL HOSTS OF INFLUENZA, SO AS TO UNDERSTAND THE CORRELATIONS BETWEEN HA BINDING AND NA CLEAVAGE AND NATURAL VIRUS SUSCEPTIBILITY. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE THE EXPRESSION OF THE MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS ON CELLS IN TISSUE CULTURE, AND THEN WILL TEST FOR THE EFFECTS OF SA MODIFICATIONS ON VIRUS BINDING, INFECTION, AND RELEASE, OR INTERACTIONS WITH HOST PROTEINS. OPTION 22D (09/10/16-12/09/17): 0258-0578-4609 DR. COLIN R. PARRISH (CORNELL UNIVERSITY) WILL COORDINATE STUDIES TO DEFINE THE ROLES OF MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS (SIAS) IN CONTROLLING THE HOST RANGES AND TROPISMS OF INFLUENZA A VIRUSES. INFLUENZA VIRUSES ALL BIND AND CLEAVE SPECIFIC SIAS DURING MANY INTERACTIONS WITH THEIR HOSTS, AND IN THIS PROPOSAL THE PARRISH LABORATORY WILL DEFINE THE EXPRESSION OF MODIFIED SIA RECEPTORS, AND EXPLAIN THEIR ROLES IN THE CONTROL OF INFLUENZA VIRUS INTERACTIONS WITH HOST CELLS AND TISSUES. PRIMARY GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO PREPARE SPECIFIC PROBES THAT RECOGNIZE THE DIFFERENT MODIFIED FORMS OF SIALIC ACID THAT ARE EXPRESSED ON CELLS, AND THEN TO DEFINE THEIR EFFECTS ON VIRUS INFECTION. THE SPECIFIC PROJECT INVOLVES THE PREPARATION OF A VARIETY OF PROBES BY EXPRESSION OF PROTEINS IN BACULOVIRUS SYSTEMS WHERE THE PROTEIN IS SECRETED AND PURIFIED. THE DIFFERENT PROBES ARE BEING USED TO DETECT THE PRESENCE OF DIFFERENT MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS ON PROTEINS, CELLS, OR TISSUES OBTAINED FROM DIFFERENT HOSTS, USING A VARIETY OF DETECTION METHODS. WE WOULD ALSO USE VARIOUS ENZYMES TO ALTER THE EXPRESSION OF DIFFERENT SIALIC ACIDS, TO MODIFY THE SIALIC ACIDS ON THE SURFACE OF CELLS, AND WOULD USE CRSP/CAS9 EDITING OF GENES IN CELLS TO ALTER THE SIALIC ACID EXPRESSION. THE MODIFIED SIALIC ACID FORMS WOULD THEN BE TESTED FOR THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH INFLUENZA VIRUSES, OR THEIR EXPRESSED PROTEINS. DR. PARRISH WILL OVERSEE THE LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AT CORNELL, AND WILL ASSIST IN THE PREPARATION OF MONTHLY, SEMI-ANNUAL, AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. HE WILL ALSO OVERSEE THE WRITING OF SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS DESCRIBING THE RESULTS OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM. THIS WORK DIRECTLY REFLECTS BOTH THE SPECIFIC AND OVERALL GOALS OF THE CEIRS PROGRAM, AND IS HIGHLY COMPLEMENTARY TO A NUMBER OF PROJECTS WITHIN THE CEIRS NETWORK, PARTICULARLY THOSE EXAMINING THE HOST AND TISSUE TROPISMS OF THE VARIOUS INFLUENZA VIRUSES IN MAMMALS AND IN DIFFERENT AVIAN HOSTS. WE WILL GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA VIRUSES AND THEIR HOSTS BY DEFINING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA HA AND NA AND THE SPECIFICALLY MODIFIED RECEPTORS ON HOST CELLS AND TISSUES, WHICH LIKELY CONTROL THE SPECIFIC PROCESSES OF VIRUS INFECTION OF CELLS AND TISSUES OF DIFFERENT HOSTS, INTERACTIONS WITH MUCUS, AND VIRUS SHEDDING. THE RESULTS WILL ALSO PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO POTENTIAL INTERVENTIONS
